Entry point to SCP-9028 (Live Feed).

CLASS: Maksur..Item has been separated into several anomalous parts which must be kept separate.

CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES: Due to continued tourist and pilgrimage activity, SCP-9028 is to remain open to the public, although efforts to improve accessibility to the cave entrance are to be discouraged discreetly by Foundation operatives in the region. The cave will be monitored at all times by Foundation personnel trained to recognize Protocol Mithra and equipped with Class-B amnestics for any necessary abatement.

SCP-9028-2 is to be detained at Site-14 in standard humanoid confinement quarters indefinitely with four (4) Scranton reality anchors at each corner of the perimeter. Interrogation requests are to be approved by Site Director Izadi.

DESCRIPTION SCP-9028 is an anomalous pir.Zoroastrian Pilgrimage site, translated from Persian (پیر). For clarity, all Persian and Avestan words have been Romanized unless specified. found within the Shekaft-e Yazdan cave near the village Zarju, Iran..Population approx. 70. While not one of the six most holy pilgrimage sites of the Yazd region, Zoroastrian legend holds that Shekaft-e Yazdan was used to hide the sacred flame during various Hellenistic and Sassanian conflicts and is still a popular location for worship. Ingress to the cave which houses SCP-9028 provides some challenge due to altitude and entrance formation, while SCP-9028 itself is only accessible to visitors via ritualistic behaviors hereafter referred to as Protocol Mithra..Visitors to the cave structure who do not correctly execute Protocol Mithra will describe the cave as extraordinarily large, with visible ancient worship sites and traditional Zoroastrian fire altars but no anomalous elements visible or accessible.

Successfully executing Protocol Mithra will result in a spatial and/or temporal distortion.Foundation researchers are divided on the appropriate description of the disruption to reality within SCP-9028. For further reading, see Dokein Sept 2022 edition., during which the roof of the cave will appear to disappear, opening to a clear, moonless night sky, regardless of the time of day in baseline reality..Foundation astronomers are unable to identify any celestial objects visible within SCP-9028. Research is ongoing. In addition to the cave roof, the following features of the cave also undergo change:

  • The floor of the cave transforms from bare limestone to a meadow plateau, overseeing a valley that resembles the Eshkeft valley found in baseline reality geographically, but with significantly more flora and fauna visible. Attempts to explore the valley via drone have provided samples of previously undiscovered plant life. Research is ongoing.
  • The archaeological remnants of the fire altars are replaced with a fully constructed darb-e mehr..Zoroastrian fire temple. Also known as an ātashkade or آتشکده. The building appears to be in excellent condition (although not newly constructed) with a characteristic Sassanian architecture with a centralized domed archway over the primary altar space and four short passageways of approach from each cardinal direction, verified as matching baseline reality after successful completion of Protocol Mithra. As is tradition with most darb-e mehr, the façade has no decoration and heavy curtains on each archway to limit access to the atashgah..Inner-most chamber (trans. 'the place of flame') where the fire altar is constructed and maintained. Traditionally only the temple's high clergy are allowed within the atashgah.
  • Regardless of the number of individuals present for Protocol Mithra, six humanoid entities dressed in traditional white veiled garments.Garments include the kushti or aiwyaongana around their waist, given to Zoroastrian adherents during their sedreh-pushi ceremony of induction to the faith. will be present at various locations around the darb-e mehr. These humanoids (hereafter designated SCP-9028-1) do not have any identifiable individual characteristics and will typically refuse to speak with or interact with observers as they attend to their presumed temple duties.

SCP-9028-1 instances will not interfere with Foundation efforts to explore SCP-9028's outer environs, provided personnel do not attempt to enter the ātashkade. In the event that a person attempts to directly enter the ātashkade when an SCP-9028-1 instance is nearby, said instance will use extraordinary physical strength to bar entry by blocking the archway before the curtain barrier. The instance will not resort to physical violence or further efforts to block ingress should the attempt be continued. Neither human nor drone exploration of the atashgah has proven possible, as human ingress is immediately met with translocation to the entryway of SCP-9028 and the cessation of the effects of Protocol Mithra whilst drone exploration results in an instant loss of recording and transmission as well as the loss of equipment. Other methods of exploration are being considered by Foundation researchers.

UPDATED Following the events of Incident Anahita, all SCP-9028-1 instances present after Protocol Mithra will aggressively pursue any entrants to the space and place their hand upon the intruder's forehead, immediately forcing the cessation of the effects of Protocol Mithra. (Note that on average, the effects of Protocol Mithra have previously lasted for roughly two hours, provided no attempt to enter the atashgah has been made.)

INCIDENT ANAHITA

On 16 October 2033, an unidentified person (hereafter designated SCP-9028-2) approached SCP-9028 via unknown means. Foundation monitoring of the site failed to observe any movement along the mountain path leading towards SCP-9028's entry point nor any attempt at aerial ingress. Investigation is ongoing into how SCP-9028-2 was able to enter the cave and begin Protocol Mithra without notice. SCP-9028-2 was apprehended without incident by Foundation personnel and transferred to Site-14 for interrogation.

SCP-9028-2 is a humanoid standing 213cm.Approx. 6'10". of ambiguous ethnicity with short cropped black hair and dark brown eyes with no notable scarring or other distinguishing characteristics. SCP-9028-2 emits a fluctuating baseline reading of Hume levels just below 0.5, indicating some level of reality distortion ability, possibly unrealized. At the time of his apprehension, SCP-9028-2 was wearing a nondescript black long-sleeved shirt and dark trousers (neither with any identifying branding tags or stamping) with an unbranded black knapsack containing three Grenade brand. Primarily sold in Türkiye. protein bars, a large bottle of water, and a copy of the complete Sasanian Avesta, untranslated from Avestan..It should be noted that the book was bound and printed in 1993 by Denkard Publishing (location unlisted), per the reverse title page. No publisher by this name has been identified, and the complete Sassanian Avesta has been considered lost literature since roughly 800 CE. A possible connection to SCP-7028 is being investigated. No other identifying items or documentation were found on their person. Although cooperative upon initial detainment, SCP-9028-2 refused to answer any questions for a total of twenty-one days after containment.

On 6 November, SCP-9028-2 directly requested to meet with Site Director Nizam Rashid Izadi by name, despite never previously meeting Dir. Izadi nor being told his name by any site personnel. Dir. Izadi agreed to the meeting, which is transcribed below.

Interview Log 9028.1 - 6 November 2033

[ DIR. IZADI sits across a table from SCP-9028-2 in Interrogation Room 2. Both parties have a glass of water, and SCP-9028-2's hands are unrestrained per IZADI's request. The complete Sasanian Avesta sits on the table between the two men. NB: Although both subjects spoke in Farsi, an English translation has been provided for ease of outside researchers. Original Farsi transcripts and recordings are available by request. ]

IZADI: You have me at a disadvantage, as you asked for me by name but I'm afraid that I cannot do the same. I've always disliked the idea of calling a man by a number, so please. Indulge me.

SCP-9028-2: At the risk of sounding cliche, my name is not important. If you must, call me Asha.

IZADI: Very well, Asha. Why have you asked to speak with me today? Thus far, you haven't exactly been talkative.

SCP-9028-2: I have never seen the benefit of speaking when there is nothing to say. Now, there is.

[ IZADI nods, extending his hands in a gesture of encouragement. ]

IZADI: By all means, feel free. I have cleared my schedule and am entirely at your disposal. We have all the time in the world.

[ SCP-9028-2 smiles, shaking their head slightly. ]

SCP-9028-2: You do not, but that is irrelevant. You will allow me to travel to Hara Berezaiti,.In Zoroastrian tradition, the great mountain at the centre of the world and the only place in creation which remained pure and incorruptible by the machinations of the angra mainyu or spirits responsible for chaos and disorder. Director. You will allow me to venerate the flame and recite the Yasna..Zoroastrian holy rite. The time has come and should not be further delayed.

IZADI: Well. Points for optimism, I suppose. I think beginning with an exchange of information would be more helpful for us both. How did you come to know of SCP-9028?

SCP-9028-2: You mean more helpful for you, for this Foundation of yours. I do not see how that is helpful for me in the slightest, but feel free to explain.

IZADI: I am trying to be as plain with you as possible, Asha. You know of the Foundation, which implies that you know of our creed and why we maintain the secrecy that we do. Surely then you know that I cannot just allow you to approach 9028 without understanding why you wish to do so in the first place?

SCP-9028-2: Ah, yes. Research is ongoing. If your Foundation has a creed, there it is. I waver between wondering if you truly believe you can understand everything or if you know that is a lie you tell yourself to go on.

IZADI: If you are attempting to bait my temper, you will have to try much harder than that. I am neither so arrogant to believe that everything can be understood fully nor so weak as to be cowed by that reality. I take no shame in the fact that I am driven to learn, to know what might be known.

[ There is a pause, and SCP-9028-2 puts his hand over the Avesta briefly. ]

SCP-9028-2: I spoke of your Foundation as a monolith, which I see is an error and I beg pardon. Individuals are invariably judged by the company they keep, but such a view can be limiting, wouldn't you agree?

IZADI: I would. It might inform a great deal, and some associations are — well, unforgivable. But I try to see the parts, not just the sum. And right now I am trying to understand what part you wish to play here, without judgment.

SCP-9028-2: I will play the part required of me. But it would seem that this is all required as well, and I am patient enough to wait you out.

IZADI: … I feel that you must realize how ominous that appears to eyes that do not see your aspirations as clearly as you are able to, yes?

SCP-9028-2: I suppose, if one views change as dangerous rather than inevitable.

IZADI: Of course change itself is inevitable, I would never argue that. However, surely you can appreciate that sometimes a little risk analysis is wise, especially to minimize potential suffering?

SCP-9028-2: You are trying to find answers to a question you do not have the language to understand. But I am not the only one who must play a part. Though blind, you serve asha,.Zoroastrian concept of righteousness and truth, with druj as its ontological opposite. that much is clear.

IZADI: One of the more esoteric compliments that I have received, but appreciated none the less.

SCP-9028-2: Which raises the question… Why are you working here?

[ At this point, SCP-9028-2 ceased answering questions and IZADI ended the interview. SCP-9028-2 was escorted back to their quarters. ]

[ END TRANSCRIPT ]

After Interview 9028.1, SCP-9028-2 remained cooperative but non-verbal for variable, extended periods of time before once again requesting to speak to Dir. Izadi directly. In these interviews, SCP-9028-2 would explain at length their understanding of Zoroastrian cosmology, primarily centered around the unseen struggle between the creator god Ahura Mazda and the flawed corruption of his enemy, Angra Mainyu. When pressed for direct information about SCP-9028 or themselves, SCP-9028-2 would redirect the conversation or refuse to continue.

All other attempts to interview SCP-9028-2 have proved ineffective. As SCP-9028 presents a limited (if not yet fully understood) danger to baseline reality, advanced interrogation methods are not approved at this time.

Interview Log 9028.3 - 7 January 2034

[ IZADI sits in the Interrogation Room alone, with the center surface draped with a simple white linen table cloth, brass coal samovar, two glass cups with saucers, and a tray of zoolbia & bamieh sweets. SCP-9028-2 enters, looking briefly confused at the table. ]

IZADI: Ah, Asha. Welcome.

SCP-9028-2: … to what do I owe this level of hospitality?

IZADI: You are a human being, are you not? You have been quite willing to communicate with me thus far and I wish to make it clear that I intend to do the same, even if we cannot allow you your request to enter 9028 at this time. While we talk, I see no reason why we should treat it as anything besides just that. A talk.

SCP-9028-2: A surprisingly civilized view considering the acts of some of your predecessors.

[ IZADI shrugs, pouring the tea and offering SCP-9028-2 one of the sweets. ]

IZADI: I will not hesitate to admit that one of my goals upon appointment was to ensure that Site-14 did not recognize itself in any way within a few years. Change has been slow, but gratifying, I would say. Now, let us begin.

[ Pulling out his notepad, IZADI begins making simple notes whilst drinking his tea with his free hand. ]

IZADI: While I have appreciated your candor about your goal of worshiping at 9028, I was hoping to understand why a bit more clearly. I understand you are unwilling to explain how you know of it, so we won't press that again, but why is worship at this ātashkade so critical? Might you explain that?

SCP-9028-2: Why a forgotten, all but invisible flame when the Great Temple of Yazd is far grander? Make my offering at the Atash Behram.Trans. Victory Fire, considered the most sacred of Zoroastrian Temple Flames. Consecration of such fire requires sixteen different types of fires, sourced by priests to be combined as one and sanctified over a year-long process and resulting in a high holy pilgrimage site for the devout. instead?

IZADI: I don't view this through a lens of grandeur or importance, for what it is worth. But I certainly would think there would be more convenient ātashkade for your offering.

[ There is a long moment of silence, punctuated by quiet sounds of mastication and drinking. ]

SCP-9028-2: You truly want to know these things, don't you?

IZADI: I am asking, aren't I?

SCP-9028-2: The Atash Behram within that cave and its beyond is the most sacred of the fires for it has never gone out. It has burned since the beginning and it will burn until the end, for that has always been its purpose. Now you, Nizam. What is your purpose? Do you have family?

IZADI: Oh, none living, I'm afraid. My maman joon often joked that I was a nightingale who refused to sleep..Persian idiom for one who works often and refuses to take breaks or enjoy life outside of their job. I focused too much on my research to settle down anywhere. The world was large and I was drawn to see as much as I could of it.

[ SCP-9028-2 seems to consider this, chewing on one of the sweetcakes in silence before responding. ]

SCP-9028-2: This '9028' that you call it… I suppose you could say it is the same for me. I am drawn to it, for it is what remains for me to see. We have known before the days of Zarathushtra.Persian spelling for Zoroaster (which is closer to the Greek spelling of the original name). of what can only be called disharmony between what getig.Zoroastrian term for creation as made by Ahura Mazda. was intended to be and what it became. Ahriman worked against Ahura Mazda to corrupt the perfection that was intended for you, for everyone. Like all, I am determined to see the last of these intentions realized and fulfilled.

IZADI: … and then? What happens after you are able to enter the building?

[ There is a long pause as neither man speaks. ]

SCP-9028-2: I think this is where we should end. For now.

[ END TRANSCRIPT ]

On 16 October, 2035 at 2:14 a.m. IST,.Iran Standard Time, GMT+3:30. SCP-9028-2 breached containment through unknown means, disappearing from their containment chamber and reappearing in the Site Kitchens. After reestablishing containment, Dir. Izadi interviewed SCP-9028-2.

Interview Log 9028.7 - 17 October 2035

[ IZADI paces within the containment chamber of SCP-9028-2 who sits in one of the provided armchairs, frowning.

IZADI: There are other ways to get our attention, Asha. You didn't have to go and prove what we've assumed for the better part of a year now.

SCP-9028-2: What exactly did I prove, just so we're on the same page?

IZADI: That we're not doing a damned thing to hold you here, and that you're just toying with us all at this point. Why bother with the game?

[ There is a long pause as neither man speaks. ]

SCP-9028-2: … that was not my intention, although now I can see how it might seem that way. You do not hold me here in one sense of the word, but I am not playing a game either, Nizam.

IZADI: You have to know we can't just trust that, not when 'Type Green' is going to be thrown around with strong evidence supporting it! We have been trusting your cooperation was a mark of good faith, but now —

SCP-9028-2: — now, I have made you look like a naive fool to your superiors? I should have known ambition would blind you in the end.

IZADI: I am the Director of Site-14 and that is all that I have aspired to, all that I have wanted in my career. Stop acting like you understand me so fully because I assure you that you do not. And yes, I have been made to look a trusting fool, which has far more consequences for you than it will for me!

[ At this point, IZADI catches his breath, as his tone had escalated to shouting. There is another long pause. ]

IZADI: I am not worried about my place in the hierarchy, or anything so mundane. Assumptions about your motivations and abilities will no longer do, there will be testing and confirmation, stricter containment procedures to ensure we are not allowing a reality bender to do as he pleases. I had thought we had established some trust and now that trust is broken. What on earth was so important that you would undermine it all with this little jaunt?

SCP-9028-2: … I heard one of those passing in the hallway say that the canteen had faloodeh.Traditional Iranian dessert. on the menu today, but dinner merely had a biscuit. I was just checking to see if perhaps there were leftovers.

IZADI: … you're kidding.

SCP-9028-2: No, I assure you that I am not. I do not really 'kid', which I assumed you know by this point. But I had always enjoyed faloodeh, before. I suppose it just got into my head. … I did not find any, though.

[ IZADI does not reply, seemingly in a state of stunned shock. SCP-9028-2 continues. ]

SCP-9028-2: And while it is true that your Foundation is not holding me here, it is where I am. Where I am meant to be, until it is time for me to be somewhere else. You cannot prevent that, nor can anyone else. In the interim, I will try to help you to find you the answers you seek.

IZADI: … why?

SCP-9028-2: In all truth, I am not sure myself. It is not required to be done by the Saoshyant.Avestan eschatological term, literal translation 'one who brings benefit'. Described in the Younger Avesta as the bringer of Frashokereti, the end-times restoration of the cosmos per Zoroastrian theology. but I wish to, so I will.

IZADI: You speak so casually of cosmic restructuring, of the end times. As if it is a simple thing.

SCP-9028-2: Why would it be anything else?

[ IZADI removes his glasses, rubbing roughly at his eyes before continuing. ]

IZADI: There will be some security measures put in place after today. Just so we're clear.

[ IZADI turns to leave, pausing only at the door with his back to SCP-9028-2. ]

IZADI: … I'll see what I can do about the faloodeh.

[ END TRANSCRIPT ]

After SCP-9028-2's self-identification as the Saoshyant, Site-14 requested additional support from the Department of Tactical Theology for further investigation into the possible connection between SCP-9028 and Frashokereti. Although the link is assumed due to SCP-9028-2's stated purpose upon apprehension by Foundation personnel as well as their self-identification as Saoshyant, further testing has been denied by the O5 Council as inviting unnecessary risks to baseline reality.

Containment procedures were modified to include Scranton anchors as well as other paratechnology used to restrain reality bending anomalies. SCP-9028-2 has either been unable or unwilling to attempt another escape from their quarters and has resumed periodic interviews with Dir. Izadi. Any requests from SCP-9028-2 for additions or items to their quarters must be approved by both Dir. Izadi and Dir. Yossarian Leiner (Head of Tactical Theology)..To date, requests have been varied classical and religious texts as well as Persian poetry, a notebook for journaling, and a hardwood chess set.

Interview Log 9028.20 - 4 March 2051

[ Both IZADI and SCP-9028-2 sit within the latter's quarters, playing chess and sharing tea as well as cardamom biscuits supplied and approved by IZADI and Dr. Leiner (via email). ]

SCP-9028-2: I suppose my good behavior merited this reward? It has been some years since my misbehavior, after all.

IZADI: You say that as if you are a school boy we are scolding for his misdeeds when he returns a man grown. As you were a man grown when you arrived, it doesn't really seem a fair comparison.

SCP-9028-2: Well, your gift is appreciated, regardless of intention.

IZADI: The intention was merely that I wished to bring them to our meeting today, as I saw them at the naanavaya.Persian bakery. this morning and thought you would enjoy them. I recognize you see the Foundation as adversarial but not everything that I do is the means to some cunning, devious end. Sometimes a biscuit is simply a biscuit.

[ They eat in silence for a time, SCP-9028-2 pouring tea for both men. ]

SCP-9028-2: … I do not see your Foundation as an adversary, for the record.

IZADI: Oh? Are we not keeping you from your stated goal of venerating the flame and reciting the Yasna? I certainly thought we were, but I suppose that I might have lost track.

SCP-9028-2: You use dry humor as a deflection. It is not subtle.

IZADI: It isn't really intended to be. But please, continue.

SCP-9028-2: I am where I need to be, not where I am meant to be. I am no fool, Nizam. I know you find me almost maddeningly vague, but imagine if you were to try to explain how one of your satellites or particle accelerators worked to a child who had just learned to speak.

IZADI: That was not exactly a compliment.

SCP-9028-2: It was not intended to be.

[ With a deep sigh, SCP-9028-2 stands up and walks over to look at their small bookshelf, their back to IZADI. ]

SCP-9028-2: It goes back so far, humanity's need to classify and categorize and explain all things, and I continue to marvel at it. I confess, it used to drive me mad, so confusing and ultimately pointless. At this point — I suppose that I find it more endearing than otherwise.

IZADI: You have been watching for some time, haven't you? After all, my eyes might grow cloudy, but not blind.

[ SCP-9028-2 turns around to look at IZADI questioningly. ]

IZADI: It has been years, my friend, and my hair has gone all but silver while you look the same age as you did when we found you in the cave. You do not age, Asha. Whatever you are, it is not made of the same stuff as the rest of us.

SCP-9028-2: I am and I am not, which is what I mean by struggling to explain it all to you. For I understand at least that much — that you want nothing more to understand. So many of you here at this Site-14 of yours want to know, simply for its own sake, even to defend those who you deem innocent. Perhaps for many it might be control, authority, but even that makes a certain amount of sense when grappling with the reality that in the end, nothing can be controlled. Not by you, or any of you.

IZADI: … you can imagine how bleak that might be to accept, on its face.

SCP-9028-2: Of course. Particularly when it is not the divine order demanding it of you, but invaders from beyond your lands, standing upon the earth and demanding authority.

[ IZADI can be seen flexing his hand into a fist beneath the table briefly, taking a few deep breaths, as if to calm himself. ]

IZADI: It goes without saying that your reception at Site-14 would have been very different, should you have arrived roughly a decade earlier. If only you knew how I worried that night you went on your little jaunt about the Site for sweets, that such a little thing might mean my removal and some outsider would be brought in to make 'things right'. Even now, self-determination is sometimes challenging, for who knows the way the future might hold? Yet ever we carry on, as long as we may. Hoping that the future might be brighter for those around you, that it all has been worth it.

SCP-9028-2: 'Be grateful for whoever comes, because each has been sent as a guide from beyond?'

IZADI: I see you've been taking advantage of the Rumi.Jalāl al-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī, 14th Century Persian poet. that I lent you, if a bit on the nose for this particular discussion. Is that who you truly are, Asha? A guide from beyond?

SCP-9028-2: I suppose that title would be as close as any. I am here for one goal, which you have known since I arrived and that I have never attempted to obfuscate. But I will confess that not every reason that I am here has been given to me by others, and along this journey I have found several of my own. Is that enough to suffice for explanation?

[ IZADI pauses, looking up at SCP-9028-2 with an unreadable expression before moving his bishop. ]

IZADI: I suppose it must be. For now.

[ SCP-9028-2 sits back opposite IZADI at the table and moves his queen. ]

SCP-9028-2: Check.

[ END TRANSCRIPT ]

On 16 October 2063, SCP-9028-2 asked to speak to Dir. Izadi and was told that due to illness, he was currently unavailable and that Acting Director Mahdavi would take his place. SCP-9028-2 immediately vanished from their containment quarters.Retroactive checks have indicated that all reality anchors and paratechnology were functioning correctly around the containment chamber. and manifested next to Dir. Izadi's bedside in the medical unit of Site-14 where he was receiving palliative care.

Interview Log 9028.29 - 16 October 2063

[ Immediately after manifesting in IZADI's private hospice room, SCP-9028-2 knelt next to the bed and took the other man's hand in his own. IZADI , still receiving oxygen via nasal cannula opened his eyes, laughing roughly before coughing. ]

IZADI: I knew those Scrantons were a waste of time.

SCP-9028-2: It did not seem beneficial to point it out. The time and money you would have all wasted to try and find something else could be used for greater need.

IZADI: So, Asha — we have come to the end then, I take it?

SCP-9028-2: I did not think you should be alone for it, my friend.

IZADI: No, no. Not that. I mean the end. To Frashokereti.

SCP-9028-2: … we have, yes. It was never yours to stop, for all that you tried.

IZADI: I didn't — well, I suppose I did. But the harm, Asha. The end of everything…

SCP-9028-2: It is not the end, Nizam. It was never intended to be the end, only the inevitable that I tried to explain to you so many times. There is no end, merely change, just as you now are facing. From one place to the next.

IZADI: … 'good prevails over evil, Ahura Mazda conquers Angra Mainyu and all is purified by the molten metal flowing from the peaks of Hara Berezaiti.' Forgive me for not finding much comfort there.

SCP-9028-2: Zarathushtra's revelations became muddled by the words of those who followed him with far louder voices, and thus the believers read terror in the silence. I will not tell you to not fear the unknown, I know that asks too much. I could tell you of the gentle beauty that awaits you, the singing of the larks and the end of suffering, but that would feel like placation to a man like you. So instead, remember, my friend. Remember what the word itself means.

IZADI: … Frashokereti. To be made wonderful, excellent. Beautiful.

SCP-9028-2: You have lived in the darkness for so long, Nizam. At last, walk with me into the light.

[ IZADI takes a deep breath before using his free hand to displace the cannula, disrupting the oxygen flow. SCP-9028-2 presses his lips to IZADI's forehead before kneeling again at the bedside, still clasping IZADI's hand. ]

SCP-9028-2: We look unto thee, Ahura Mazda, for the relief of our grief and comfort of our hearts. Their earthly work is done and they have laid down the burden that pressed heavily on them. Let thy light shine upon them..Traditional Zoroastrian prayer for the dead.

[ END TRANSCRIPT ]

UPDATE: Former Site Director Nizam Rashid Izadi passed away at 9:31 a.m. Site-14 security recordings show SCP-9028-2 vanishing from Izadi's bedside before disappearing from all recordings. SCP-9028-2 remains uncontained to date.

As of 16 October 2073, Protocol Mithra is no longer effective for gaining entry to SCP-9028. Reestablishing access to SCP-9028 is considered the highest of priorities. Research is ongoing.

Special Containment Procedures: Complete containment of SCP-9029 has proven to be impossible. Instead, MTF LAMBDA-12 "Pest control" is to routinely patrol the area surrounding SCP-9029 to monitor its expansion, and prevent unauthorised personnel from reaching SCP-9029. Surveillance of the perimeter walls is to be maintained at all times, through the use of cameras and stationed MTF operatives. On a bi-weekly basis, MTF operatives, equipped with the appropriate ballistic equipment, should advance into the containment zone, following the sustained fire of several artillery pieces stationed 10 kilometres North from the containment zone. MTF operatives involved in this advance should make use of kinetic, incendiary and chemical weapons in order to decrease the population and area of influence of SCP-9029.

Should a member of MTF LAMBDA-12 be lost, their body should immediately be retrieved and incinerated. Following the findings of Addendum 02, the transfer of SCP-9029 to Wilsons Wildlife Solutions is no longer being considered. Caution when advancing into the containment zone is also advised following Incident 01.

Researcher's note: The containment procedures previously displayed are currently under review, and will be subject to change.

- Dr. Keller

Description:The designation 'SCP-9029' refers to an anomalous colony of leafcutter ants, located in a 5km wide forested zone in Southern Texas. While SCP-9029 mostly resembles a mature colony of Atta mexicana, workers of SCP-9029, referred to hereby as SCP-9029-1, have never been seen cutting or consuming any type of leaf. SCP-9029 as a colony also harbours an abnormal ratio of workers to majors1, with over 40 percent of the colonies estimated population being composed of majors.

Image of an SCP-9029 satellite nest, located in the South East quadrant of the containment zone.

Majors of SCP-9029 also display greater polymorphism2, with the largest supermajors reaching over 60mm. The colony of SCP-9029 has also shown to be polygynous3, with the number of queens estimated to be over 50,000. Paired with an exceedingly quick egg to worker development of just under 2 weeks, as well as the ability to inbreed4, SCP-9029 as a colony is able to expand rapidly, should sufficient nutrients be available. SCP-9029-1 instances have also shown to be invulnerable to all forms of common pesticide.

The most dangerous anomalous effects, however, begin to manifest once any vertebrate approaches SCP-9029. The affected subject's bodily systems will begin to gradually fail, with the rate and severity of these failures varying between subjects and species. Below is a list of the organisms tested, with the results attached.

Subject Result
Atta mexicana (Leafcutter Ant) No discernible effect.
Atta texana (Leafcutter Ant) No discernible effect.
Centruoides vittatus (Striped Bark Scorpion) No discernible effect.
Hemidactylus frenatus (Asian House Gecko) Subject immediately started showing signs of distress, with its tail being dropped roughly 5 minutes after being placed into the containment zone of SCP-9029. Approximately 20 minutes after first exposure, skin discolouration could be seen, which rapidly progressed to bleeding from the eyes and mouth. The subject subsequently died from blood loss. Following dissections revealed a high concentration of an unknown hemotoxin in the subject's bloodstream.
Varanus acanthurus (Spiny-Tailed monitor) Subject remained within the containment zone for 16 days before the onset of the first symptoms. The subject died due to the formation of a blood clot in the coronary artery, caused by the presence of the same hemotoxin in the subjects bloodstream. No other symptoms were recorded prior to the subject's death.
Struthio camelus (Common Ostrich) Subject remained in the containment zone for 8 days before the first symptoms developed. The symptoms first manifested in necrosis around the right calf, but quickly progressed into acute, body wide necrosis. The subject later died from blood loss, as well as an infection in the wound. Later dissections also found the same hemotoxin present in the subject's blood stream, however it was found in a much lower concentration.
Pan troglodytes (Chimpanzee) Subject remained inside the containment zone for 2 months without the development of any notable conditions past infrequent nosebleeds. The hemotoxin was not found in the subject's bloodstream, and it is suspected that the exceedingly low concentration of the hemotoxin rendered it undetectable.
Human Subject D-4839 (Measured IQ 105) No discernible effect.
Human Subject D-5017 (Measured IQ 68) No discernible effect.

These results suggest that the severity and lethality of the symptoms are directly linked to the intelligence of the subject affected, with subjects with lower intelligence experiencing the most rapid and severe onset of symptoms. The anomalous abilities of SCP-9029 also do not seem to affect other invertebrates. Finally, the hemotoxin compound present in the bloodstream of every organism affected has since been named Hemotoxin-9029, and research on the effects of this toxin are still ongoing.

Despite the lack of symptoms experienced by humans in the previous tests, it is still recommended that proximity with SCP-9029-1 instances is minimised. Once the death of a subject occurs, a large number of SCP-9029-1 instances will exit the nest and form trails to the newly placed corpse, provided that the corpse is not being visually observed by a primate. SCP-9029-1 instances will then begin to cut and divide the corpse into segments, to be disinfected by chemical compounds stored on the mandibles of SCP-9029-1 instances and carried back into the nest. It should be noted that the pieces of flesh 'harvested' by SCP-9029-1 instances have been drained of blood, due to the presence of Hemotoxin-9029.

The current size and depth of the main nest is unknown, and has been rendered difficult to calculate due to the presence of satellite nests. However, current estimates place it being over 80m deep, and spanning a diameter of 2km. Despite the size and population of SCP-9029, the area in which SCP-9029 inhabits remains biodiverse, and has no notable ecological differences when compared to other forests located in Southern Texas.

As the population of reptiles and mammals monitored was seemingly unaffected, it is theorized that the anomalous effects posed by SCP-9029 are significantly less potent towards reptiles and mammals that were found naturally in the containment zone. This was later confirmed by running parallel tests using reptiles of the same species taken from different ranges.

Further analysis of the rate at which SCP-9029-1 instances naturally 'harvest' has revealed that SCP-9029 does not intake a significant amount of nutrients, despite the size and population of SCP-9029-1 instances. This suggests that SCP-9029 is capable of surviving and expanding with significantly limited nutrients. The method in which SCP-9029-1 instances are able to survive such long periods of time without nutrients is currently unknown.

Discovery: SCP-9029 was discovered following the attempted publishing of a journal titled ‘My Time Spent With Gaia’, which was in the process of publishing on the behalf of the author ‘Alice Pearce’, before her disappearance. The journal details Miss Pearce's experience studying numerous ‘unnatural’ organisms, with some of her descriptions assisting the Foundation in the capture of SCP-████, SCP-████ and SCP-9029.

This journal was found by Foundation agents embedded within the publishing industry, and was seized shortly before publication. Amnestics have since been administered to all civilians that had previously viewed or had knowledge of the journal’s existence.

It should be noted that the final pages relating to SCP-9029 had been torn out prior to Foundation recovery. It should also be noted that Miss Pearce had previously been in Foundation custody for witnessing an SCP-████ event, and was given amnestic treatment before being released.

Image taken of Alice Pearce's final journal entry on site, relating to SCP-9029.

As I continue to scour this forest, I've come across a species of leafcutter that really shouldn't exist. They definitely resemble Atta, but the colony structure is unlike anything I've ever seen before.

I almost only see majors, and their polymorphism is far greater than even Carebara. Some of them reach almost 3cm. I only ever see them venturing outside their nest when forming large trails, and I almost never see them deviate from this.

These trails also seem to never end. I've followed them for hours, but I have yet to see even a single worker harvesting. Come to think of it, I don't see how a colony this large can even survive in a forest this small. By now, there shouldn't even be any plants left.

I just can't quite shake the feeling that maybe they're the reason half of this forest is drenched in blood… This doesn't make any sense.

Still, I haven't ruled out a hemophagic virus yet. Even if it was the leafcutters, I should be finding bodies; even just skeletons…

There's something unnatural in this forest, and I'm going to find out what it is.

Addendum 9029-01: Containment Revision 01

Due to growing resource concerns, it has been decided that the size of the area containing SCP-9029 should be decreased, with the vegetation being cleared to facilitate ease of management, as well as improving the accuracy of monitoring efforts. With this in mind, MTF LAMBDA-12 was sent into the current containment perimeter with heavy machinery to remove significant amounts of vegetation. An artillery barrage was then used to eliminate instances of SCP-9029 outside of the newly designated zone.

Since the first advance, MTF units have been successful in clearing 12.5km²of land containing SCP-9029, with no notable changes in behaviour occurring in SCP-9029-1 instances. Due to this, construction on a wall encircling the perimeter of the area effected by SCP-9029 has begun. Long term containment procedures have also been changed to accommodate the limits in resources.

Addendum 9029-02: Discovery and subsequent analysis of SCP-9029-2

Through further study, it has been found that instances of SCP-9029-1 are sustained through a symbiotic relationship, not dissimilar to non-anomalous leaf cutters. However, instead of cultivating the Leucoagaricus gongylophorus fungus, instances of SCP-9029-1 cultivate what appears to be a constantly growing mass of flesh, hereby referred to as an SCP-9029-2 mass. Samples of SCP-9029-2 were extracted from SCP-9029 quickly following this discovery. These samples were safely contained for a period of three weeks, before these samples were then tested for their effects on various tissue samples and living organisms.

When exsanguinated dead tissue was exposed to an SCP-9029-2 sample, the effects were almost immediate. The dead tissue started warping, quickly being reduced to a semi permeable mass of biological material. Later chemical tests revealed that the proteins stored within the tissue had been broken down into their relative amino acids, along with the lipids being converted into glycerol.

Further examination of this substance revealed that this had been caused by a fungal pathogen, which replicated and processed the tissue through the production of digestive enzymes, creating a nutrient rich blend.

The effects of the pathogen were then tested on a living muscle tissue sample, taken from a lab rat. While the subsequent result was similar to that of the dead tissue, it was found through further testing that this tissue was slowly releasing fungal spores. Samples of the blood stored within the tissue were then tested, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of active SCP-9029-2 instances.

These SCP-9029-2 instances were using nutrients present in the blood to produce fungal spores, which were then being released through the semi permeable membrane. It was also found that the SCP-9029-2 instances had caused the rapid growth of new blood vessels, which were redirecting nutrients present in the muscle tissue to the main bloodstream.

The discovery of fungal spores was made several hours following testing, due to the low concentration of spores being released. This resulted in the infection of junior researcher Jeffrey Anderson, who has since been quarantined. No other researchers were found to be infected by SCP-9029-2, and the effects of SCP-9029-2 on Dr. Anderson are currently being examined.

Dr. Anderson initially began showing flu-like symptoms hours after the first infection with SCP-9029-2, slowly progressing into more severe fevers after several days. It was at this time that various antifungal medications were administered to Dr. Anderson, with no noticeable effect. Shortly after the fevers developed, SCP-9029-2 began to cause rapid and uncontrollable mutations in the body of Dr. Anderson, resulting in a rash forming over Dr Andersons' skin, as well as several health complications. These complications were not dealt with, for fear of the infection spreading to other researchers.

Shortly after the formation of the rash, Dr. Andersons' immune system was completely degraded by SCP-9029-2. It was at this time that the decision was made to cease all interaction with Dr. Anderson to prevent further infection. SCP-9029-2 then deconstructed Dr. Andersons' nervous system shortly after his immune system was compromised, quickly causing paralysis. Dr. Anderson died almost immediately after this due to his brain functions ceasing. It should be noted that while Dr. Anderson suffered complete brain death, Dr. Andersons' heart continued functioning, allowing most of his tissue to continue undergoing aerobic respiration.

Following Dr. Andersons' death, SCP-9029-2 then hijacked his digestive system, using it to dissolve much of his remaining living tissue. Dr. Andersons' bone structure was also broken down in this period. After approximately 24 hours, the body of Dr. Anderson was reduced to a mass of flesh, similar in composition to the tissue sample tested previously. However, Dr. Andersons' heart continued circulating blood throughout this mass, which was aided by the growth of an extensive system of new blood vessels.

Magnified image taken of SCP-9029-2 instances in the bloodstream, during the formation of new blood vessels.

Analysis of the blood showed a substantially high concentration of SCP-9029-2, with a significant amount of fungal spores being emitted from this mass. It is currently estimated that flesh infected with SCP-9029-2 is capable of lasting indefinitely, despite differing climate conditions and exposure to other pathogens. This is due to the tendency of SCP-9029-2 instances to actively locate and engulf other pathogens, destroying them through the production of digestive enzymes. This has so far prevented all contained samples of SCP-9029-2 decomposing, as no tested pathogen has proven to be capable of proliferating within these samples.

The effects of the pathogen have since been tested on multiple different species of mammals and reptiles, consistently resulting in the death of the subject. At this time, there is no known cure to SCP-9029-2. Analysis of SCP-9029-2 spores have shown that they are capable of surviving in the air for upwards of 6 months, and have an infectivity rate close to 100%. To attempt to prevent a potential outbreak, containment efforts should be reinforced.

Resources should immediately be allocated to extract as many instances of SCP-9029-2 as possible, to be prepared for incineration. 20 samples of SCP-9029-2 should also be stored within separate containment chambers in biological storage centre 23 for further testing. This should be done directly following artillery bombardment on the main nest, in which drones should then be used to extract exposed SCP-9029-2 instances.

When conducting tests involving SCP-9029-2, personnel must wear level A hazmat suits, and be routinely checked for any symptom's characteristic of SCP-9029-2. Should Foundation personnel be suspected to be infected with SCP-9029-2, they should undergo immediate quarantine. Should their infection be confirmed, they should be terminated remotely, with their body being incinerated.

Due to the bloodborne nature of SCP-9029-2, it is theorized that SCP-9029-1 has evolved to manifest a hemotoxin in subjects as a way to counter the pathogenic effects of SCP-9029-2, thereby allowing them to cultivate SCP-9029-2 for nutrients. This suggests that SCP-9029-1 and SCP-9029-2 are unlikely to have evolved whilst having a symbiotic relationship, instead suggesting that this relationship is a recent development.

Raymond Warren (SCP-9029 Head Researcher)

Dr. Warren: Ok, let's get this started.

Dr. Warren uses a syringe to inject SCP-9029-2 into a previously prepared lab rat

Dr. Barnes: Shouldn't we be a little more cautious? I mean, last test it immediately caused the tissue to convulse after seconds-

Dr. Anderson: -Relax. It's not like it's going to jump out at you or anything; besides, there are worse ways to go working for the Foundation.

Incident 9029-01:

Approximately 48 hours following the first tests on SCP-9029-2, MTF operatives spotted three trails of SCP-9029-1 instances, primarily composed of majors, heading towards the main walls. MTF operatives continued to stand guard, observing as the three trails merged into one, seemingly heading directly towards a sentry tower. When the trail reached approximately 50m from the sentry tower, MTF operatives were instructed to fire on the trail, destroying thousands of SCP-9029-1 instances. This did not deter the surviving SCP-9029-1 instances, which continued to advance despite the heavy casualties. It was at this time that almost all of the perimeter floodlights stopped functioning, forcing the MTF operatives to use handheld flashlights.

Despite the relatively small advancing force, members of MTF LAMBDA-12 were quickly overpowered and forced to retreat. SCP-9029-1 did not advance past the walls during this advance, with night vision cameras confirming their retreat shortly before sunrise. Later analysis has found several tunnel entrances exiting behind the perimeter wall, each roughly 30cm in diameter. Further investigation through the use of remote-controlled rovers have found that the tunnels have been recently blocked approximately 200m from the source. It has been concluded that these tunnels were constructed quickly following the bombardment of the main nest, and allowed SCP-9029-1 instances to quickly overpower the MTF operatives stationed by the perimeter.

Further analysis of this attack found that the floodlights were disabled due to large numbers of SCP-9029-1 workers entering the light through the seals in the plating, causing the floodlights to short circuit, destroying all SCP-9029-1 instances in the process. Almost all the floodlights were rendered useless within minutes of each other, displaying a great degree of coordination and intelligence. The use of these strategies in tandem also suggests that SCP-9029-1 instances may have some form of collective consciousness, with at least a basic understanding of military strategy.

A total of 14 casualties were sustained during this attack, with the deaths of 5 MTF operatives. Instances of SCP-9029-1 seemingly did not utilise their anomalous abilities to cause these deaths, as evident by the lack of Hemotoxin-9029 in their bloodstream, instead using their mandibles to make small incisions, eventually causing the MTF operatives to die from blood loss. Whilst SCP-9029-1 instances did not 'harvest' these corpses, they continued to make incisions into the corpses flesh, rendering the corpses unidentifiable without DNA confirmation. Instances of SCP-9029-1 were still present on the body when it was recovered, with no signs indicating that they would have stopped 'processing' the corpse. Due to this notable change in behaviour, SCP-9029 is to be reclassified to Keter. Increased caution is advised regarding the containment of SCP-9029.

Update Incident 9029-01:

Approximately one week following Incident 01, all outward communications from biological storage centre 23 ceased. MTF LAMBDA-12 were dispatched quickly following this, and made contact three hours after dispatch. It would seem that during Incident 01, several SCP-9029-1 queens began founding underneath biological storage centre 23, forming an established colony in under a week. This directly conflicts with the egg to worker development seen in SCP-9029 that had been measured previously, suggesting that the speed of brood development is dynamic, and can be altered based on circumstance.

After the satellite nest reached a substantial population, a large number of SCP-9029-1 instances emerged from underneath the storage centre and immediately targeted the communications array, using supermajors to unscrew various panels, allowing smaller SCP-9029-1 instances to enter the circuitry. While many instances of SCP-9029-1 were able to breach biological storage centre 23, it would seem that the SCP-9029-1 instances were attempting to enter the containment chamber of SCP-9029-2. Instances of SCP-9029-1 were unsuccessful in entering this containment chamber before the arrival of MTF LAMBDA-12, due to the chamber being hermetically sealed.

This containment breach was quickly stopped upon the arrival of MTF LAMBDA-12, with MTF operatives destroying the SCP-9029-1 instances on site. The source of the SCP-9029-1 instances was quickly traced back to the satellite nest by following the trails left by these instances. An incendiary explosive was then placed inside the satellite nest, which due to the nest's size, was able to destroy all remaining SCP-9029-1 instances upon detonation.

A total of 3 armed guards were killed during this containment breach, with many others being wounded. Extreme caution has been advised with the containment of SCP-9029, and a containment revision has been deemed necessary.

Addendum 9029-04: SCP-9029-2 Mutation Analysis

Following frequent testing, it has been noted that some of the general conditions required for an SCP-9029-2 infection to develop have changed. This was first noticed following the testing of an infected human tissue sample, taken from D-5487. SCP-9029-2 spores were extracted from this sample, and placed on a sample of exsanguinated human muscle tissue. Whilst the SCP-9029-2 instances initially began breaking down the muscle tissue, they did this at a far lower rate than previously observed.

Researchers involved in this test were immediately quarantined, after the exsanguinated tissue sample failed to show signs of degradation after 2 hours. All researchers involved in this test were found to be infected with SCP-9029-2 shortly after quarantine, and were promptly terminated through incineration. Analysis of the infected tissue sample following the incident has found that the tissue had been producing spores for approximately 1 hour before any change was noticed.

Dissection of the sample revealed that many new blood vessels had grown outwards from a small pulsating mass. This mass seems to be similar in structure to a small human heart, and continues functioning despite the notable lack of pacemaker cells. The blood mixture found in the blood vessels of the tissue sample has also shown to be identical in concentration to standard human blood, and has the same genetic composition as the surrounding muscle tissue. It has been concluded that the growth of a double circulatory system happened shortly after initial infection, and allowed the production of SCP-9029-2 spores at a significantly heightened rate.

It is currently unknown how SCP-9029-2 instances replicated haemoglobin, among other compounds found in human blood, despite no blood being initially present. This notable change in SCP-9029-2 following the presence of a limited supply of hosts suggests that SCP-9029-2 instances are capable of rapid and targeted mutations, allowing them to adapt quickly to different environments.

Following this incident, it has been decided to increase the frequency of testing on SCP-9029-2, to attempt to determine the limits of this adaptive ability.

Addendum 9029-05: Outbreak Mitigation Efforts

Approximately 3 months following the termination of SCP-9029-1, numerous reports of a 'flesh eating disease' from hospitals and the media have surfaced across Texas, Louisiana and Northern Mexico. This corresponded with the containment breach of a developed sample of SCP-9029-2, 2 weeks prior. This occurred due to the development of a mutation that allowed SCP-9029-2 instances to both bypass advanced air filtration systems, as well as allow them to remain undetected in the bloodstream of hosts. Whilst this breach was thought to be contained, the disease responsible for these reports was quickly confirmed to be SCP-9029-2, following Foundation autopsies on infected subjects. While a total death toll is currently unavailable, Foundation estimates place the number infected to be over 200,000.

The Foundation has administered warnings and significant medical aid through government agencies. Media coverage of this fact is to be censored, as to not promote widespread panic. While country wide quarantine has been advised, due to the wide distance that SCP-9029-2 spores are able to travel through the air, this will most likely be ineffective in preventing the spread of SCP-9029-2.

Foundation containment efforts are to be completely focused on the development of a cure for SCP-9029-2 effective immediately. Once the cure has been finalised, it is to be distributed through an established vaccine manufacturer.

After careful consideration, SCP-9029 is to be reclassified as hiemal.

They've got us cornered - these; animals.

I don't know how much longer the door will hold them-

Addendum 9029-10: SCP-9029-3 analysis

It would seem that new strains of SCP-9029-2 are capable of forming animate organisms from infected tissue. These organisms, known hereby as SCP-9029-3, take various forms, seemingly dependent on the levels of armament possessed by the Foundation team sighting them. Instances of SCP-9029-3 have been described by most accounts as bipedal, approximately 3 metres in height and with a vaguely humanoid shape. The size and number of appendages present on instances of SCP-9029-3 vary significantly, with some instances having upwards of 6 armlike limbs. Appendages often end in a brittle pointed structure, theorized to be composed of human keratin.

While instances of SCP-9029-3 are believed to possess a complete double circulatory system, more detailed examinations have shown to be impossible to conduct, due to their tendency to transmute into SCP-9029-2 instances following capture. Providing that the total mass of this SCP-9029-2 instance has not been significantly altered, it is then capable of transmuting back into an instance of SCP-9029-3. This allows SCP-9029-3 instances to effectively 'reanimate', should they be significantly injured, making them significantly more difficult to destroy.

Instances of SCP-9029-3 are extremely hostile, and will attempt to incapacitate and incorporate large organisms into their mass. While most instances of SCP-9029-3 can be significantly slowed through the use of kinetic weapons, incineration is currently the only known method to completely destroy SCP-9029-3 instances, preventing reanimation from taking place. Many Foundation personnel attacked by SCP-9029-3 instances have been found to be infected with SCP-9029-2, despite no physical contact taking place. Due to this, it has been theorized that instances of SCP-9029-3 passively release SCP-9029-2 spores into the surrounding environment, although this has yet to be proven.

Project Aurora progress update:

72% efficacy. Activation of the kill switch causes SCP-9029-2 samples to rapidly degrade on a molecular level. SCP-██████ instances are infrequently transmitted to other SCP-9029-2 instances in close proximity. This rate of transition is significantly affected by the ambient temperature, with infectivity being nullified in temperatures lower than 5 degrees Celsius.

Addendum 9029-11: SCP-9029-3 Revision

Further research suggests that SCP-9029-3 instances will only manifest from SCP-9029-2 if a large organism is nearby, and will de-manifest back into SCP-9029-2 once this organism has been incorporated into their mass. This allows SCP-9029-2 infected zones to be traversed safely through the use of autonomous vehicles.

It has also been found that SCP-9029-3 instances exclusively target individuals that are already infected with SCP-9029-2. For this reason, should instances of SCP-9029-3 manifest near any Foundation team, all Foundation vessels nearby should be immediately relocated away from the coastline until further notice.

Addendum 9029-12: SCP-9029-2 Outbreak

SCP-9029-2 has reached the southern coast of Russia, proliferating across Magadan and Nelkan. The outbreak has so far been limited to only a few hundred cases, and mass scale evacuations across Siberia are underway.

With the consent of the Russian government, tactical nuclear warheads have been utilised to create a dividing line across eastern Siberia, as well as to terminate all instances of SCP-9029-2 in Magadan and Nelkan. It is hoped that this will delay the advance of SCP-9029-2 until project Aurora is completed.

Project Aurora progress update:

89% efficacy. SCP-██████ instances are now far more infective, with instances of SCP-9029-2 being at risk of infection as much as 50 metres away from another infected instance. However, SCP-██████ instances will now often self-destruct before fully eliminating an SCP-9029-2 mass, should the kill switch be activated. As a result, SCP-██████ instances may have to be distributed repeatedly within a region to have a significant effect, significantly slowing termination efforts.

Distribution of this incomplete frequency is currently being considered by the 05 council.

Addendum 9029-13: █████████████████████████

Project Aurora is complete. Millions of SCP-██████ instances set to the Y45 frequency have been replicated within Site-300, and are being stored within hermetically sealed steel containers. This frequency has been found to have a 98% efficacy in both transmitting between and terminating instances of SCP-9029-2. Aerial distribution has begun over large parts of Scandinavia and North America.

Current Foundation estimates suggest approximately 90% of the total mass of SCP-9029-2 will be infected by SCP-██████ within 4 days. The kill switch is not to be activated until authorised by the 05 council.

Researcher's Note:

The time has finally come

It was not long after my transfer that the cure was blessed upon me. I remember how it felt to have the pestilence rid from my flesh. To become something greater than myself. To watch the sun set on that blessed day.

I was fearful. That night I couldn’t sleep. Yet I dreamt. I dreamt of a world devoid of the all-consuming plagues. A world where the elements governed themselves. And then I understood.

So I waited patiently. I fulfilled all the menial tasks given to me, all while the Foundation lost its grip over the new world. But I could only wait so long. I devised a plan. An anomalous weapon, capable of ridding the world of its final plague.

And now it’s over. We won. For all my respect to Gaia… She could never understand. This had to be done. When we wake there will be no more plagues, no more pestilence.

It’s funny, really. I could keep it all going. I have the kill switch right here. But how weak I would have to be to flick it. I must be patient. The time will come. But to you. Well… Your time has run out.

I was naïve then. I thought the 05 indestructible. I even believed that your eyes would see through the façade of my actions, that my very creation would silence the hope for a better world. But following my conversation with 05-8, I realise just how mortal you really are.

You cannot hope to contain us - it was always going to end like this. Your mere attempt was insulting… Still, I am truly grateful that your Foundation set us free. I hope that you will allow me to return the favour.

Samples of the cure have been dispersed in Tokyo, Shanghai, Mumbai and Delhi, among other major metropolitan areas. It is to my greatest regret that tactical nuclear warheads have been used on various military centres and embassies. This didn't need to happen. We just needed more time…

How characteristic of the pestilence, to strive to fight an unwinnable war, even when hope is truly lost. I can only hope their sacrifice will not be in vain.

SCP-610 has been terminated by the cured. Those vile creatures were far beyond saving. Numerous sites have been instructed to detonate their on-site alpha warhead. The Foundation’s structure has allowed us to cull many remaining anomalies with ease. The cured have determined the surviving anomalies to have been rid of the pestilence.

As of writing, the war is nearly over. The cured have been used to crush the last remaining strongholds of humanity. The only people left lie counting their time, living in borrowed tombs.

It’s not long until their need for sustenance brings them to our world. Not long until the pestilence is vanquished. Not long… Until I flick this switch.

Nothing is permanent. There is no structure in this world that will not, one day, return to dust. We can only hope tomorrow will have a brighter sunrise.

See you on the other side.

- Dr. Keller
