Instead, MTF LAMBDA-12 "Pest control" is to routinely patrol the area surrounding SCP-9029 to monitor its expansion, and prevent unauthorised personnel from reaching SCP-9029. Surveillance of the perimeter walls is to be maintained at all times, through the use of cameras and stationed MTF operatives. On a bi-weekly basis, MTF operatives, equipped with the appropriate ballistic equipment, should advance into the containment zone, following the sustained fire of several artillery pieces stationed 10 kilometres North from the containment zone. MTF operatives involved in this advance should make use of kinetic, incendiary and chemical weapons in order to decrease the population and area of influence of SCP-9029. Should a member of MTF LAMBDA-12 be lost, their body should immediately be retrieved and incinerated. Following the findings of Addendum 02, the transfer of SCP-9029 to Wilsons Wildlife Solutions is no longer being considered. Caution when advancing into the containment zone is also advised following Incident 01. [[div class="blockquote"]] **Researcher's note:** The containment procedures previously displayed are currently under review, and will be subject to change. - //Dr. Keller// [[/div]] **Description:**The designation 'SCP-9029' refers to an anomalous colony of leafcutter ants, located in a 5km wide forested zone in Southern Texas. While SCP-9029 mostly resembles a mature colony of //Atta mexicana//, workers of SCP-9029, referred to hereby as SCP-9029-1, have never been seen cutting or consuming any type of leaf. SCP-9029 as a colony also harbours an abnormal ratio of workers to majors [[footnote]]Majors are slightly larger worker ants that have far larger heads and mandibles, allowing them to more easily cut through prey. [[/footnote]], with over 40 percent of the colonies estimated population being composed of majors. [[include component:image-block | name=https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/corpse-cutters/Atta_Mexicana.jpeg | caption=Image of an SCP-9029 satellite nest, located in the South East quadrant of the containment zone. | width=50% | align=right]] Majors of SCP-9029 also display greater polymorphism [[footnote]]This means that workers within casts have varying sizes.[[/footnote]], with the largest supermajors reaching over 60mm. The colony of SCP-9029 has also shown to be polygynous[[footnote]]Have multiple queens. [[/footnote]], with the number of queens estimated to be over 50,000. Paired with an exceedingly quick egg to worker development of just under 2 weeks, as well as the ability to inbreed[[footnote]]This allows the colony to expand indefinitely and exponentially. [[/footnote]], SCP-9029 as a colony is able to expand rapidly, should sufficient nutrients be available. SCP-9029-1 instances have also shown to be invulnerable to all forms of common pesticide. The most dangerous anomalous effects, however, begin to manifest once any vertebrate approaches SCP-9029. The affected subject's bodily systems will begin to gradually fail, with the rate and severity of these failures varying between subjects and species. Below is a list of the organisms tested, with the results attached. [[div class="blockquote"]] ||~ **Subject**||~ **Result**|| || **//Atta mexicana// (Leafcutter Ant)** || No discernible effect. || || **//Atta texana// (Leafcutter Ant)** || No discernible effect. || || **//Centruoides vittatus// (Striped Bark Scorpion)** || No discernible effect. || || **//Hemidactylus frenatus// (Asian House Gecko)** || Subject immediately started showing signs of distress, with its tail being dropped roughly 5 minutes after being placed into the containment zone of SCP-9029. Approximately 20 minutes after first exposure, skin discolouration could be seen, which rapidly progressed to bleeding from the eyes and mouth. The subject subsequently died from blood loss. Following dissections revealed a high concentration of an unknown hemotoxin in the subject's bloodstream. || || **//Varanus acanthurus// (Spiny-Tailed monitor)** || Subject remained within the containment zone for 16 days before the onset of the first symptoms. The subject died due to the formation of a blood clot in the coronary artery, caused by the presence of the same hemotoxin in the subjects bloodstream. No other symptoms were recorded prior to the subject's death. || || **//Struthio camelus// (Common Ostrich)** || Subject remained in the containment zone for 8 days before the first symptoms developed. The symptoms first manifested in necrosis around the right calf, but quickly progressed into acute, body wide necrosis. The subject later died from blood loss, as well as an infection in the wound. Later dissections also found the same hemotoxin present in the subject's blood stream, however it was found in a much lower concentration. || || **//Pan troglodytes// (Chimpanzee)** || Subject remained inside the containment zone for 2 months without the development of any notable conditions past infrequent nosebleeds. The hemotoxin was not found in the subject's bloodstream, and it is suspected that the exceedingly low concentration of the hemotoxin rendered it undetectable. || || **Human Subject D-4839 (Measured IQ 105)** || No discernible effect. || || **Human Subject D-5017 (Measured IQ 68)** || No discernible effect. || These results suggest that the severity and lethality of the symptoms are directly linked to the intelligence of the subject affected, with subjects with lower intelligence experiencing the most rapid and severe onset of symptoms. The anomalous abilities of SCP-9029 also do not seem to affect other invertebrates. Finally, the hemotoxin compound present in the bloodstream of every organism affected has since been named Hemotoxin-9029, and research on the effects of this toxin are still ongoing. [[/div]] Despite the lack of symptoms experienced by humans in the previous tests, it is still recommended that proximity with SCP-9029-1 instances is minimised. Once the death of a subject occurs, a large number of SCP-9029-1 instances will exit the nest and form trails to the newly placed corpse, provided that the corpse is not being visually observed by a primate. SCP-9029-1 instances will then begin to cut and divide the corpse into segments, to be disinfected by chemical compounds stored on the mandibles of SCP-9029-1 instances and carried back into the nest. It should be noted that the pieces of flesh 'harvested' by SCP-9029-1 instances have been drained of blood, due to the presence of Hemotoxin-9029. The current size and depth of the main nest is unknown, and has been rendered difficult to calculate due to the presence of satellite nests. However, current estimates place it being over 80m deep, and spanning a diameter of 2km. Despite the size and population of SCP-9029, the area in which SCP-9029 inhabits remains biodiverse, and has no notable ecological differences when compared to other forests located in Southern Texas. As the population of reptiles and mammals monitored was seemingly unaffected, it is theorized that the anomalous effects posed by SCP-9029 are significantly less potent towards reptiles and mammals that were found naturally in the containment zone. This was later confirmed by running parallel tests using reptiles of the same species taken from different ranges. Further analysis of the rate at which SCP-9029-1 instances naturally 'harvest' has revealed that SCP-9029 does not intake a significant amount of nutrients, despite the size and population of SCP-9029-1 instances. This suggests that SCP-9029 is capable of surviving and expanding with significantly limited nutrients. The method in which SCP-9029-1 instances are able to survive such long periods of time without nutrients is currently unknown. **Discovery:** SCP-9029 was discovered following the attempted publishing of a journal titled ‘My Time Spent With Gaia’, which was in the process of publishing on the behalf of the author ‘Alice Pearce’, before her disappearance. The journal details Miss Pearce's experience studying numerous ‘unnatural’ organisms, with some of her descriptions assisting the Foundation in the capture of SCP-████, SCP-████ and SCP-9029. This journal was found by Foundation agents embedded within the publishing industry, and was seized shortly before publication. Amnestics have since been administered to all civilians that had previously viewed or had knowledge of the journal’s existence. It should be noted that the final pages relating to SCP-9029 had been torn out prior to Foundation recovery. It should also be noted that Miss Pearce had previously been in Foundation custody for witnessing an SCP-████ event, and was given amnestic treatment before being released. [[include component:image-block | name=http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/local--files/corpse-cutters/SCP-9029_Journal_entry.jpeg | caption=Image taken of Alice Pearce's final journal entry on site, relating to SCP-9029. | height=100% | width=100% | align=center]] [[collapsible show="+ Reveal Transcript " hide="- Close Transcript"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] As I continue to scour this forest, I've come across a species of leafcutter that really shouldn't exist. They definitely resemble //Atta//, but the colony structure is unlike anything I've ever seen before. I almost only see majors, and their polymorphism is far greater than even //Carebara//. Some of them reach almost 3cm. I only ever see them venturing outside their nest when forming large trails, and I almost never see them deviate from this. These trails also seem to never end. I've followed them for hours, but I have yet to see even a single worker harvesting. Come to think of it, I don't see how a colony this large can even survive in a forest this small. By now, there shouldn't even be any plants left. I just can't quite shake the feeling that maybe they're the reason half of this forest is drenched in blood... This doesn't make any sense. Still, I haven't ruled out a hemophagic virus yet. Even if it was the leafcutters, I should be finding bodies; even just skeletons... There's something unnatural in this forest, and I'm going to find out what it is. [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-01: Containment Revision 01** ----- Due to growing resource concerns, it has been decided that the size of the area containing SCP-9029 should be decreased, with the vegetation being cleared to facilitate ease of management, as well as improving the accuracy of monitoring efforts. With this in mind, MTF LAMBDA-12 was sent into the current containment perimeter with heavy machinery to remove significant amounts of vegetation. An artillery barrage was then used to eliminate instances of SCP-9029 outside of the newly designated zone. Since the first advance, MTF units have been successful in clearing 12.5km²of land containing SCP-9029, with no notable changes in behaviour occurring in SCP-9029-1 instances. Due to this, construction on a wall encircling the perimeter of the area effected by SCP-9029 has begun. Long term containment procedures have also been changed to accommodate the limits in resources. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-02: Discovery and subsequent analysis of SCP-9029-2** ----- Through further study, it has been found that instances of SCP-9029-1 are sustained through a symbiotic relationship, not dissimilar to non-anomalous leaf cutters. However, instead of cultivating the Leucoagaricus gongylophorus fungus, instances of SCP-9029-1 cultivate what appears to be a constantly growing mass of flesh, hereby referred to as an SCP-9029-2 mass. Samples of SCP-9029-2 were extracted from SCP-9029 quickly following this discovery. These samples were safely contained for a period of three weeks, before these samples were then tested for their effects on various tissue samples and living organisms. ----- When exsanguinated dead tissue was exposed to an SCP-9029-2 sample, the effects were almost immediate. The dead tissue started warping, quickly being reduced to a semi permeable mass of biological material. Later chemical tests revealed that the proteins stored within the tissue had been broken down into their relative amino acids, along with the lipids being converted into glycerol. Further examination of this substance revealed that this had been caused by a fungal pathogen, which replicated and processed the tissue through the production of digestive enzymes, creating a nutrient rich blend. ----- The effects of the pathogen were then tested on a living muscle tissue sample, taken from a lab rat. While the subsequent result was similar to that of the dead tissue, it was found through further testing that this tissue was slowly releasing fungal spores. Samples of the blood stored within the tissue were then tested, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of active SCP-9029-2 instances. These SCP-9029-2 instances were using nutrients present in the blood to produce fungal spores, which were then being released through the semi permeable membrane. It was also found that the SCP-9029-2 instances had caused the rapid growth of new blood vessels, which were redirecting nutrients present in the muscle tissue to the main bloodstream. The discovery of fungal spores was made several hours following testing, due to the low concentration of spores being released. This resulted in the infection of junior researcher Jeffrey Anderson, who has since been quarantined. No other researchers were found to be infected by SCP-9029-2, and the effects of SCP-9029-2 on Dr. Anderson are currently being examined. ----- Dr. Anderson initially began showing flu-like symptoms hours after the first infection with SCP-9029-2, slowly progressing into more severe fevers after several days. It was at this time that various antifungal medications were administered to Dr. Anderson, with no noticeable effect. Shortly after the fevers developed, SCP-9029-2 began to cause rapid and uncontrollable mutations in the body of Dr. Anderson, resulting in a rash forming over Dr Andersons' skin, as well as several health complications. These complications were not dealt with, for fear of the infection spreading to other researchers. Shortly after the formation of the rash, Dr. Andersons' immune system was completely degraded by SCP-9029-2. It was at this time that the decision was made to cease all interaction with Dr. Anderson to prevent further infection. SCP-9029-2 then deconstructed Dr. Andersons' nervous system shortly after his immune system was compromised, quickly causing paralysis. Dr. Anderson died almost immediately after this due to his brain functions ceasing. It should be noted that while Dr. Anderson suffered complete brain death, Dr. Andersons' heart continued functioning, allowing most of his tissue to continue undergoing aerobic respiration. Following Dr. Andersons' death, SCP-9029-2 then hijacked his digestive system, using it to dissolve much of his remaining living tissue. Dr. Andersons' bone structure was also broken down in this period. After approximately 24 hours, the body of Dr. Anderson was reduced to a mass of flesh, similar in composition to the tissue sample tested previously. However, Dr. Andersons' heart continued circulating blood throughout this mass, which was aided by the growth of an extensive system of new blood vessels. [[include component:image-block | name=https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/corpse-cutters/Fibrin_strands_on_blood_smear.jpeg | caption=Magnified image taken of SCP-9029-2 instances in the bloodstream, during the formation of new blood vessels. | width=50% | align=right]] Analysis of the blood showed a substantially high concentration of SCP-9029-2, with a significant amount of fungal spores being emitted from this mass. It is currently estimated that flesh infected with SCP-9029-2 is capable of lasting indefinitely, despite differing climate conditions and exposure to other pathogens. This is due to the tendency of SCP-9029-2 instances to actively locate and engulf other pathogens, destroying them through the production of digestive enzymes. This has so far prevented all contained samples of SCP-9029-2 decomposing, as no tested pathogen has proven to be capable of proliferating within these samples. ----- The effects of the pathogen have since been tested on multiple different species of mammals and reptiles, consistently resulting in the death of the subject. At this time, there is no known cure to SCP-9029-2. Analysis of SCP-9029-2 spores have shown that they are capable of surviving in the air for upwards of 6 months, and have an infectivity rate close to 100%. To attempt to prevent a potential outbreak, containment efforts should be reinforced. Resources should immediately be allocated to extract as many instances of SCP-9029-2 as possible, to be prepared for incineration. 20 samples of SCP-9029-2 should also be stored within separate containment chambers in biological storage centre 23 for further testing. This should be done directly following artillery bombardment on the main nest, in which drones should then be used to extract exposed SCP-9029-2 instances. When conducting tests involving SCP-9029-2, personnel must wear level A hazmat suits, and be routinely checked for any symptom's characteristic of SCP-9029-2. Should Foundation personnel be suspected to be infected with SCP-9029-2, they should undergo immediate quarantine. Should their infection be confirmed, they should be terminated remotely, with their body being incinerated. Due to the bloodborne nature of SCP-9029-2, it is theorized that SCP-9029-1 has evolved to manifest a hemotoxin in subjects as a way to counter the pathogenic effects of SCP-9029-2, thereby allowing them to cultivate SCP-9029-2 for nutrients. This suggests that SCP-9029-1 and SCP-9029-2 are unlikely to have evolved whilst having a symbiotic relationship, instead suggesting that this relationship is a recent development. It was at this time that almost all of the perimeter floodlights stopped functioning, forcing the MTF operatives to use handheld flashlights. Despite the relatively small advancing force, members of MTF LAMBDA-12 were quickly overpowered and forced to retreat. SCP-9029-1 did not advance past the walls during this advance, with night vision cameras confirming their retreat shortly before sunrise. Later analysis has found several tunnel entrances exiting behind the perimeter wall, each roughly 30cm in diameter. Further investigation through the use of remote-controlled rovers have found that the tunnels have been recently blocked approximately 200m from the source. It has been concluded that these tunnels were constructed quickly following the bombardment of the main nest, and allowed SCP-9029-1 instances to quickly overpower the MTF operatives stationed by the perimeter. Further analysis of this attack found that the floodlights were disabled due to large numbers of SCP-9029-1 workers entering the light through the seals in the plating, causing the floodlights to short circuit, destroying all SCP-9029-1 instances in the process. Almost all the floodlights were rendered useless within minutes of each other, displaying a great degree of coordination and intelligence. The use of these strategies in tandem also suggests that SCP-9029-1 instances may have some form of collective consciousness, with at least a basic understanding of military strategy. A total of 14 casualties were sustained during this attack, with the deaths of 5 MTF operatives. Instances of SCP-9029-1 seemingly did not utilise their anomalous abilities to cause these deaths, as evident by the lack of Hemotoxin-9029 in their bloodstream, instead using their mandibles to make small incisions, eventually causing the MTF operatives to die from blood loss. Whilst SCP-9029-1 instances did not 'harvest' these corpses, they continued to make incisions into the corpses flesh, rendering the corpses unidentifiable without DNA confirmation. Instances of SCP-9029-1 were still present on the body when it was recovered, with no signs indicating that they would have stopped 'processing' the corpse. Due to this notable change in behaviour, SCP-9029 is to be reclassified to Keter. Increased caution is advised regarding the containment of SCP-9029. **Update Incident 9029-01:** ----- Approximately one week following Incident 01, all outward communications from biological storage centre 23 ceased. MTF LAMBDA-12 were dispatched quickly following this, and made contact three hours after dispatch. It would seem that during Incident 01, several SCP-9029-1 queens began founding underneath biological storage centre 23, forming an established colony in under a week. An incendiary explosive was then placed inside the satellite nest, which due to the nest's size, was able to destroy all remaining SCP-9029-1 instances upon detonation. A total of 3 armed guards were killed during this containment breach, with many others being wounded. Extreme caution has been advised with the containment of SCP-9029, and a containment revision has been deemed necessary. This was first noticed following the testing of an infected human tissue sample, taken from D-5487. SCP-9029-2 spores were extracted from this sample, and placed on a sample of exsanguinated human muscle tissue. Whilst the SCP-9029-2 instances initially began breaking down the muscle tissue, they did this at a far lower rate than previously observed. Researchers involved in this test were immediately quarantined, after the exsanguinated tissue sample failed to show signs of degradation after 2 hours. All researchers involved in this test were found to be infected with SCP-9029-2 shortly after quarantine, and were promptly terminated through incineration. Analysis of the infected tissue sample following the incident has found that the tissue had been producing spores for approximately 1 hour before any change was noticed. Dissection of the sample revealed that many new blood vessels had grown outwards from a small pulsating mass. This mass seems to be similar in structure to a small human heart, and continues functioning despite the notable lack of pacemaker cells. The blood mixture found in the blood vessels of the tissue sample has also shown to be identical in concentration to standard human blood, and has the same genetic composition as the surrounding muscle tissue. It has been concluded that the growth of a double circulatory system happened shortly after initial infection, and allowed the production of SCP-9029-2 spores at a significantly heightened rate. It is currently unknown how SCP-9029-2 instances replicated haemoglobin, among other compounds found in human blood, despite no blood being initially present. This notable change in SCP-9029-2 following the presence of a limited supply of hosts suggests that SCP-9029-2 instances are capable of rapid and targeted mutations, allowing them to adapt quickly to different environments. Following this incident, it has been decided to increase the frequency of testing on SCP-9029-2, to attempt to determine the limits of this adaptive ability. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-05: Outbreak Mitigation Efforts** ----- Approximately 3 months following the termination of SCP-9029-1, numerous reports of a 'flesh eating disease' from hospitals and the media have surfaced across Texas, Louisiana and Northern Mexico. This corresponded with the containment breach of a developed sample of SCP-9029-2, 2 weeks prior. This occurred due to the development of a mutation that allowed SCP-9029-2 instances to both bypass advanced air filtration systems, as well as allow them to remain undetected in the bloodstream of hosts. Whilst this breach was thought to be contained, the disease responsible for these reports was quickly confirmed to be SCP-9029-2, following Foundation autopsies on infected subjects. While a total death toll is currently unavailable, Foundation estimates place the number infected to be over 200,000. The Foundation has administered warnings and significant medical aid through government agencies. The Foundation has also instructed these agencies to incinerate bodies infected with SCP-9029-2, to decrease the amount of ground that SCP-9029-2 instances are able to cover. Media coverage of this fact is to be censored, as to not promote widespread panic. While country wide quarantine has been advised, due to the wide distance that SCP-9029-2 spores are able to travel through the air, this will most likely be ineffective in preventing the spread of SCP-9029-2. Foundation containment efforts are to be completely focused on the development of a cure for SCP-9029-2 effective immediately. Once the cure has been finalised, it is to be distributed through an established vaccine manufacturer. After careful consideration, SCP-9029 is to be reclassified as hiemal. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-07: SCP-9029 Pandemic Alert** ----- The development of a cure for SCP-9029-2 infections has been significantly slowed due to the rapid mutation observed in SCP-9029-2 instances, across various quarantined sectors. In an attempt to reduce the number of hosts received by SCP-9029-2, the Foundation has taken full control of all remaining US military assets, across all branches. This transfer is known to very few of the remaining members of the US military. Should any members of the greater public be made aware of this, they are to be administered amnestics immediately, with any of their claims being heavily discredited. This has allowed the Foundation to covertly issue a complete lockdown over the entirety of North America, significantly reducing the chance of SCP-9029-2 spreading across continents. Remaining citizens have been instructed to stay inside their homes until the situation is resolved. Large scale sabotage operations have also been conducted on North America's networking infrastructure, cutting off large portions of media coverage. MTF BETA-7 "Maz Hatters" are to work in tandem with these assets in order to establish and maintain a perimeter around the SCP-9029-2 infected zone. Naval convoys have been put in place surrounding much of the American continent. All naval vessels spotted leaving North America are to be destroyed on sight. Propaganda campaigns have already been established, presenting North America as lost. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-08: SCP-9029-2 Containment Revision** ----- The American continent is to be considered lost. Clusters of biological mass infected with SCP-9029-2 have begun growing root systems across large areas of land, connecting many pockets of SCP-9029-2 together. Foundation estimates place the total death toll caused by SCP-9029-2 at approximately 875 million. Remaining populations within the infected zone have fallen into anarchy. Following current rates, the human presence on the American continent is expected to end in under 2 weeks. Further testing on SCP-9029-2 is strictly to be conducted on Foundation naval vessels, positioned over the South Atlantic Ocean. Should communications be lost with any of these vessels, they are to be destroyed remotely with upmost priority. [[/div]] [[collapsible show="+ Insert security clearance level (4) " hide="- Close File"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Overseer Notice:** ----- There has been a significant number of internal sabotage attempts, across multiple branches of the Foundation. These sabotage attempts have resulted in multiple containment breaches, with a total death toll of 32 Foundation personnel. The reason behind the increase in internal sabotage remains unclear, as all currently known culprits have refused to disclose any information. No relation between these culprits has been found. For this reason, Foundation researchers are to be randomly entered for psychological evaluation effective immediately. It is hoped that this may expose the reason for these internal attacks. Personnel suspected to be involved in sabotage attempts are also to be evaluated, by threat of termination. This information is not to be disclosed to personnel under level (4) clearance. [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-09: Project Aurora** ----- The successful development of a cure to SCP-9029-2 has been deemed impossible due to its increasingly volatile genetic composition. After careful consideration, research has begun on the creation of a targeted nano virus, for use against SCP-9029-2, codenamed 'project Aurora'. This is being done through the careful manipulation of receptors present on SCP-██████, allowing their frequency to be altered. Should this be successful, infected instances of SCP-9029-2 could be terminated remotely through the activation of a kill switch, present on SCP-████. The following are currently the most notable frequencies: ||~ **Frequency**||~ **Result**|| || **B7** || **16% efficacy.** Numerous personnel began showing symptoms of infection almost immediately after the test was completed. The vessel was detonated remotely quickly thereafter. Overhead drone footage confirmed no survivors. || || **E73**|| **23% efficacy.** The experiment was conducted in a hermetically sealed metal chamber by multiple D-class personnel. The chamber was immediately disposed into the ocean following the experiment. No efforts were made to extract the D-class personnel. || || **E103**|| **Unknown.** Remote countermeasures did not activate. The vessel is to be considered lost. || || **C21**|| **49% efficacy.** Dr. Jordan Stevens attempted direct sabotage on the vessel's crew and countermeasures, resulting in the infection of three Foundation personnel. All personnel present on this vessel were subsequently terminated remotely using backup incendiary explosives. The reason of Dr. Jordan Stevens's sabotage is currently unknown.|| [[/div]] **Incident 9029-02:** ----- Approximately 20 minutes following the docking of a Foundation frigate on the east coast of Brazil, the following distress call was received:  [[div class="blockquote"]] **Audio Log** **—————————————————————————————————————————** [BEGIN AUDIO LOG] Requesting immediate backup... //The scratching of metal can be heard// They've got us cornered - these;  //animals//. I don't know how much longer the door will hold them- //[SIGNAL LOST]// [END AUDIO LOG] **—————————————————————————————————————————** [[/div]] Research into this incident is currently ongoing. [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-10: SCP-9029-3 analysis** ----- It would seem that new strains of SCP-9029-2 are capable of forming animate organisms from infected tissue. These organisms, known hereby as SCP-9029-3, take various forms, seemingly dependent on the levels of armament possessed by the Foundation team sighting them. Instances of SCP-9029-3 have been described by most accounts as bipedal, approximately 3 metres in height and with a vaguely humanoid shape. The size and number of appendages present on instances of SCP-9029-3 vary significantly, with some instances having upwards of 6 armlike limbs. Appendages often end in a brittle pointed structure, theorized to be composed of human keratin. While instances of SCP-9029-3 are believed to possess a complete double circulatory system, more detailed examinations have shown to be impossible to conduct, due to their tendency to transmute into SCP-9029-2 instances following capture. Providing that the total mass of this SCP-9029-2 instance has not been significantly altered, it is then capable of transmuting back into an instance of SCP-9029-3. This allows SCP-9029-3 instances to effectively 'reanimate', should they be significantly injured, making them significantly more difficult to destroy. Instances of SCP-9029-3 are extremely hostile, and will attempt to incapacitate and incorporate large organisms into their mass. While most instances of SCP-9029-3 can be significantly slowed through the use of kinetic weapons, incineration is currently the only known method to completely destroy SCP-9029-3 instances, preventing reanimation from taking place. Many Foundation personnel attacked by SCP-9029-3 instances have been found to be infected with SCP-9029-2, despite no physical contact taking place. Due to this, it has been theorized that instances of SCP-9029-3 passively release SCP-9029-2 spores into the surrounding environment, although this has yet to be proven. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Project Aurora progress update:** ----- **72% efficacy.** Activation of the kill switch causes SCP-9029-2 samples to rapidly degrade on a molecular level. SCP-██████ instances are infrequently transmitted to other SCP-9029-2 instances in close proximity. This rate of transition is significantly affected by the ambient temperature, with infectivity being nullified in temperatures lower than 5 degrees Celsius. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-11: SCP-9029-3 Revision** ----- Further research suggests that SCP-9029-3 instances will only manifest from SCP-9029-2 if a large organism is nearby, and will de-manifest back into SCP-9029-2 once this organism has been incorporated into their mass. This allows SCP-9029-2 infected zones to be traversed safely through the use of autonomous vehicles. It has also been found that SCP-9029-3 instances exclusively target individuals that are already infected with SCP-9029-2. For this reason, should instances of SCP-9029-3 manifest near any Foundation team, all Foundation vessels nearby should be immediately relocated away from the coastline until further notice. [[/div]] [[collapsible show="+ Insert security clearance level (4) " hide="- Close File"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Overseer Notice:** ----- As of writing, approximately 10% of Foundation personnel have been entered for psychological evaluation over the course of three months, yielding no notable findings. The number of internal attacks has continued rising, resulting in the loss of a further 136 Foundation personnel, as well as the destruction of seven Foundation vessels. Many Foundation researchers have also begun defecting to other groups of interest, such as the Global Occult Coalition and Chaos Insurgency, resulting in the loss of numerous high value anomalies. Due to the stable mental state that defecting researchers have been found in, it is suspected that personnel involved in these attacks may be under the influence of an unknown, mind-altering anomaly. Due to this possibility, MTF ALPHA-1 "Red Right Hand" has been instructed to monitor the activities of all Foundation personnel below level (3) clearance. It is hoped that this may reveal the location and nature of the anomaly responsible. Should this anomaly be found, it is to be destroyed with upmost priority. This information is not to be disclosed to personnel under level (4) clearance. [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-12: SCP-9029-2 Outbreak** ----- SCP-9029-2 has reached the southern coast of Russia, proliferating across Magadan and Nelkan. The outbreak has so far been limited to only a few hundred cases, and mass scale evacuations across Siberia are underway. With the consent of the Russian government, tactical nuclear warheads have been utilised to create a dividing line across eastern Siberia, as well as to terminate all instances of SCP-9029-2 in Magadan and Nelkan. It is hoped that this will delay the advance of SCP-9029-2 until project Aurora is completed. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Project Aurora progress update:** ----- **89% efficacy.** SCP-██████ instances are now far more infective, with instances of SCP-9029-2 being at risk of infection as much as 50 metres away from another infected instance. However, SCP-██████ instances will now often self-destruct before fully eliminating an SCP-9029-2 mass, should the kill switch be activated. As a result, SCP-██████ instances may have to be distributed repeatedly within a region to have a significant effect, significantly slowing termination efforts. Distribution of this incomplete frequency is currently being considered by the 05 council. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Addendum 9029-13:** █████████████████████████ ----- Project Aurora is complete. Millions of SCP-██████ instances set to the Y45 frequency have been replicated within Site-300, and are being stored within hermetically sealed steel containers. This frequency has been found to have a 98% efficacy in both transmitting between and terminating instances of SCP-9029-2. Aerial distribution has begun over large parts of Scandinavia and North America. Current Foundation estimates suggest approximately 90% of the total mass of SCP-9029-2 will be infected by SCP-██████ within 4 days. The kill switch is not to be activated until authorised by the 05 council. [[/div]] [[collapsible show="+ Insert security clearance level (05) " hide="- Close File"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Video/Audio Log** **__In Attendance:__** **Calvin Keller** (SCP-9029 Head Researcher) ████████████████████████████ **—————————————————————————————————————————** [BEGIN VIDEO/AUDIO LOG] **██████████:** I understand you've requested me here. **Dr. Keller:** Yes. Project Aurora is finally complete. Almost all SCP-9029-2 instances are currently at the mercy of the Foundation, save for a few. //Dr. Keller pauses for a moment, surveying ██████████'s indifferent expression// **Dr. Keller:** I was hoping you would allow us to refrain from executing project Aurora. You see, the team hasn't been working well of late. ██████████**:** Continue? **Dr. Keller:** I have reason to suspect that there is sabotage at play. //A faint flicker of shock registers on ██████████'s face, before it is quickly silenced// ██████████**:** What makes you say that? **Dr. Keller:** You see, some things just don't add up. That boat for example - the one that went missing. The boat should've been blown into oblivion, but the countermeasures didn't work. The chance of one malfunctioning is astronomically low - but both? Impossible. **Dr. Keller:** No one on that vessel had any knowledge of the second countermeasure. I doubt anyone would've even had the skill to disarm it. This was an outside job - through and through. //██████████ takes a moment to consider// ██████████**:** What makes you suspect someone on your team? Surely any Foundation member could've sabotaged the experiment. **Dr. Keller:** I'm almost certain that the countermeasures were deactivated remotely. The only terminals with access to those countermeasures are on this site. The only ones with admin are members of our research team. ██████████**:**If a site terminal was used, all of the inputs would have been recorded. Why haven't you already checked through them? **Dr. Keller:** I've had my eyes on Dr. Joe Feron for quite some time now. He's always messing up research, getting mixed up with safety protocols. People have died because of him. But he's also a great technician. Knowledgeable with code. I don't doubt that he could've erased his inputs, and replaced them with the activation code. No one would suspect anything other than mechanical failure. ██████████**:** I see... So, what are you suggesting? **Dr. Keller:** I need you to delay the distribution of SCP-██████ long enough to let me figure out the truth. I understand that we have no time to spare, but those instances could be dangerous. We can't trust the tests anymore. ██████████**:** They've been tested by many different researchers all over the Foundation. No one could've tampered with those findings. **Dr. Keller:** Only ever on small sample sizes. We have no clue of the effects that SCP-██████ could have on the environment //██████████ takes a moment to consider// **██████████:** I can organise an investigation into Dr. Joe Feron. If he's truly the man you think he is, we'll know. But I can't let you delay. We have countless containment sites all over Russia. If we don't put an end to this quickly, we'll lose all the facilities we have left. //Dr. Keller answers in a desperate tone// **Dr. Keller:** What good is distributing the cure if everyone dies starving! You must understand the risk- **██████████:** -If we wait humanity will surely face extinction. I think I'll take the risk. **Dr. Keller:** We don't know what Joe could have done! It could... //Dr. pauses for a moment, as if reconsidering// **Dr. Keller:** This may be your last chance to save humanity. To save yourself. There will be no turning back. **██████████:** I agree. My word is final. //Dr. Keller remains silent, observing ██████████// //██████████ gets up to leave// //Dr. Keller sighs. His tone darkens// [VIDEO FEED IS LOST] //The doorknob can be heard rattling// **Dr. Keller:** That's quite the shame. I wish you could have seen the other side. //Frantic pacing can be heard// **██████████:** What is this!- //The sound of a gunshot resonates through the feed// [END VIDEO/AUDIO LOG] **—————————————————————————————————————————** [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] [[collapsible show="+ Insert security clearance level (05) " hide="- Close File"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **//Researcher's Note://** //The time has finally come// It was not long after my transfer that the cure was blessed upon me. I remember how it felt to have the pestilence rid from my flesh. To become something greater than myself. To watch the sun set on that blessed day. I was fearful. That night I couldn’t sleep. Yet I dreamt. I dreamt of a world devoid of the all-consuming plagues. A world where the elements governed themselves. And then I understood. So I waited patiently. I fulfilled all the menial tasks given to me, all while the Foundation lost its grip over the new world. But I could only wait so long. I devised a plan. An anomalous weapon, capable of ridding the world of its final plague. And now it’s over. We won. For all my respect to Gaia… She could never understand. This had to be done. When we wake there will be no more plagues, no more pestilence. It’s funny, really. I could keep it all going. I have the kill switch right here. But how weak I would have to be to flick it. I must be patient. The time will come. But to you. Well… Your time has run out. I was naïve then. I thought the 05 indestructible. I even believed that your eyes would see through the façade of my actions, that my very creation would silence the hope for a better world. But following my conversation with 05-8, I realise just how mortal you really are. You cannot hope to contain us - it was always going to end like this. Your mere attempt was insulting... Still, I am truly grateful that your Foundation set us free. I hope that you will allow me to return the favour. Samples of the cure have been dispersed in Tokyo, Shanghai, Mumbai and Delhi, among other major metropolitan areas. It is to my greatest regret that tactical nuclear warheads have been used on various military centres and embassies. This didn't need to happen. We just needed more time... How characteristic of the pestilence, to strive to fight an unwinnable war, even when hope is truly lost. I can only hope their sacrifice will not be in vain. SCP-610 has been terminated by the cured. Those vile creatures were far beyond saving. Numerous sites have been instructed to detonate their on-site alpha warhead. The Foundation’s structure has allowed us to cull many remaining anomalies with ease. The cured have determined the surviving anomalies to have been rid of the pestilence. As of writing, the war is nearly over. The cured have been used to crush the last remaining strongholds of humanity. The only people left lie counting their time, living in borrowed tombs. It’s not long until their need for sustenance brings them to our world. Not long until the pestilence is vanquished. Not long… Until I flick this switch. Nothing is permanent. There is no structure in this world that will not, one day, return to dust.                We can only hope tomorrow will have a brighter sunrise. See you on the other side. - //Dr. Keller// [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] [[div class="footer-wikiwalk-nav"]] [[=]] << [[[SCP-9028]]] | SCP-9029 | [[[SCP-9030]]] >> [[/=]] [[/div]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] > **Filename:** Atta_Mexicana.jpeg > **Name:** Atta Mexicana > **Author:** María Eugenia Mendiola González > **License:**CC BY-SA 4.0 > **Source Link:***https://openverse.org/image/916784bb-7d97-4ef7-bc11-e9f4cb6fb342?q=atta+mexicana&p=117 > **Filename:** Fibrin_strands_on_blood_smear.jpeg > **Name:** Fibrin strands on blood smear > **Author:** Spicy > **License:**CC BY-SA 4.0 > **Source Link:***https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=106496712 [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]

SCP-9030.raw_content:
Great television is hard to come by. Take a load off and stay awhile. Ignore the pigs.

Item #: SCP-9030

Object Class: Keter

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9030 is currently uncontainable. Efforts are ongoing to intercept and remove shipments of media infested by SCP-9030.

Selective-memory amnestics are to be administered to every human above the age of 12 in North America and Europe. This is accomplished through an aerosolized compound sprayed over large public areas and the injection of the amnestics in all mandatory vaccines.

The initial vector of the amnestic is to target memories involving the key words “fable”, “fairy tale”, and “fantasy”. The secondary vector is to target the key words "gray", and "tooth".

Description: SCP-9030 is a phenomenon affecting seemingly random pieces of media primarily in North America. SCP-9030 will “infest” a piece of media and change its narrative. These changes largely consist of the additions of pigs and their subsequent deaths. These deaths are usually implied to be incredibly violent, but are rarely described or seen. Characters within the narrative do not react to these deaths or other changes within the narrative in any meaningful way. If changes to the narrative are consistent with the original tone, plot, and characterization, they are reacted to accordingly.

SCP-9030 is believed to have existed within several narratives before becoming anomalous. Though these narratives have been investigated, it is unclear if there was a large-scale memory erasure event or if they have always existed in this state.

Addendum A: Instances of SCP-9030

The following are some of the most notable SCP-9030 infestation events. It is important to note that SCP-9030 infestations, unless stated otherwise, only affect a single copy of the infested media.

INFESTATION POINT TYPE OF MEDIA EVENT DESCRIPTION
Little Red Riding Hood1 Book The wolf is no longer present in the story. When Little Red Riding Hood arrives at her grandmother’s house, she hears chewing sounds from within the bedroom. She does not knock on the door. She spends the majority of the story looking at her shoes. An hour later, when her grandmother leaves the room, they eat pork together. Neither speaks.
Jack and the Beanstalk2 Book Jack plants the bean in his family’s farm and it grows overnight. However, he does not climb it. Pieces of pig viscera fall from above. Jack’s father stands beside him and puts his hand on his shoulder.
Indiana Jones and the Raiders of the Lost Ark3 Film Pigs replace Nazis as the primary antagonists of the film. At the end of the movie, rather than being melted by the opening of the Ark, they are roasted. A large, dark shape can be seen emerging from the Ark before the film cuts to black, but it is too indistinct to make out.
Humpty-Dumpty4 Cartoon The fairy tale is significantly longer than its original version. Humpty-Dumpty is left lying on the ground for a significant, but unspecified length of time. Inside his cracked shell is a piglet. Eventually, one of the King’s men gives him a bandage which he uses to cover up the crack. There are brief descriptions of scratching from within Humpty-Dumpty, but they cease after a brief period of time.
[REDACTED]5 Book Every infested copy of the story contained only the words "No take-backsies". Over 38 instances of [REDACTED] have been infested by SCP-9030.
Braveheart6 Film The movie continues normally throughout the majority of its runtime up until the ending with Wallace's death. Before being drawn and quartered, Wallace screams and says that there is a "great beast within the city walls". His cries are ignored and he is tortured via the Goat's Tongue,7 however the torture is performed by a pig rather than a goat.

Addendum B: Event-9030-A

On September 28th, 2023, an SCP-9030 infestation was detected and intercepted in a recording of the now-defunct late night talk show "Stayin' Up with Joel Bauer". The clip was of an interview between Bauer and three guests from an upcoming theatrical release in 1999.8 The guests in question were actress Maria Lang and actors George Conti and Albert Andersen. This recording has been classified as Event-9030-A due to the numerous unique anomalies present that had not been seen in an SCP-9030 infestation before and have not been seen since.

The full recording has been transcribed below:

BEGIN RECORDING

The footage stutters and flashes on to a bright, blurry display. The zoom is adjusted until the lens focuses on a man standing in front of the camera, standing on a small circular stage, identified as Joel Bauer. He is wearing a navy blue two piece suit and leather shoes. Behind him and to the left are his desk and a long white suede couch. There are dark blue stage curtains in the background with faint halogen lights placed intermittently above. A cramped hallway is set into the back of the stage, presumably for guests to enter through. Bauer looks to someone off screen before looking into the camera, straightening his tie, and smiling.

Bauer: Good evening everyone, I hope you're all having a lovely night. I know I am. To begin tonight's show, we'll be having the main cast of Lupo on to talk about the film and their experience working with Spielberg, and maybe even give us some behind the scenes info.

The audience claps and hollers. Bauer smiles and puts his hands up to quiet them.

Bauer: After that, we'll talk with Tom Waits about his new album "Mule Variations", his first in over five years. Then, to finish off the night, we'll have Jerry Seinfeld on in anticipation of his next tour across North America.

Audience claps again. Bauer speaks over the clapping.

Bauer: Well, I'm glad to see you're excited. Now, if you could get ready for another round of applause, please welcome George, Maria, and Albert, everyone!

The audience continues clapping. "Big Band" jazz music plays as three figures walk onstage from the hallway. The three are identified as Lang, Conti, and Andersen. Lang is wearing an ankle-length red dress, Conti is wearing a wool jacket, jeans, and sunglasses, and Andersen is wearing a bright red jacket and cargo pants. Lang sits on the end of the couch closest to Bauer, Andersen takes the middle seat, and Conti sits at the opposite end. The audience's clapping gradually dies down as Bauer sits at his desk, shaking each of the guests hands.

Bauer: I'm so happy to have you all on the show, it's really such a pleasure. I-I heard you all just got into New York a few days ago, is that true?

Lang: Yeah, we wanted to get in before the show tonight so we could go around and see the sights.

Conti: We got rained out of the plane right when we landed. Made a break for the cab and got to our hotel as fast as possible.

Andersen: Ruined my best sweater.

The audience laughs. Conti begins scratching a hangnail on his left index finger.

Bauer: Well that's quite unfortunate, but how's the city been treating you so far? Besides the sweater, of course.

Audience laughs lightly. The curtains in the background begin to part.

Conti: It's a, uh, a new experience, for sure. I'm used to back roads, farms, fourteen year olds driving tractors down gravel paths.

As the curtains open further, a wall of straw is revealed.

Conti: There's an odd hideousness to it, I guess. Like something's biting your arm, trying to get to the bone, but it's so cold you can't feel it. You just let it keep gnawing, gnawing.

Andersen: The pizza's plenty good. Better than any I've had before. Some New Yorkers like to act like it's God's gift to food, but it's nothing to scoff at, that's for sure.

Bauer: I think you might want to apologize to the audience of New Yorkers in the crowd you just insulted tonight.

Audience laughs. Someone yells out "Best in the world!"

Bauer: Well how about you, Maria? You've been awfully quiet.

Lang: It's been nice. I went to see all the sights, eat all the foods. Just experience everything for the first time.

Conti continues to scratch his hangnail. A small droplet of blood is squeezed out and quickly dries, turning the hangnail dark red.

Lang: My parents called me last night to make sure I hadn't been mugged yet. They specifically said "yet".

Audience laughs. The straw begins to rot.

Conti: Mine called me too. Wanted to tell me that my grandmother thought she'd already seen Lupo and was waiting to congratulate me on a job well done.

Audience laughs again.

Andersen: I thought your grandma died?

Conti: Oh, yeah. It was my grandfather. Slipped my mind.

The straw falls away in clumps until it has rotted beyond usability. There are wooden logs lining the wall behind the straw. Conti continues scratching his hangnail.

Bauer: I'm sorry to hear that George.

Conti: It's nothing. That actually reminds me, I went out to go find a restaurant last night, just some midnight cravings, and I saw this dog. It was in an alleyway, alone.

The audience squeals.

Conti: I went up to it to say hi, and it didn't move an inch. I walked right up next to it, and it wasn't breathing. I nudged his body with my toe, but he just flopped over like a half-empty beanbag. He was starving, I think. When he died, I mean. I wanted to bury him somewhere, but there was only concrete or asphalt everywhere I looked, so I dropped him in the dumpster.

A drop of blood from Conti's hangnail runs down his knuckle.

Bauer: Where did you end up eating? If you don't mind me asking, of course.

Conti: The Topside. Didn't eat.

A loud, hollow bump is heard. Its source cannot be identified.

Lang: I love the Topside, I actually went there most nights. What did you get?

Conti: I didn't get anything.

Andersen: I think I stopped by there once. It was a nice little place. Bit too stuffy for my tastes, but the food was good.

Conti: How many dogs starve in New York, do you think?

Another drop of blood is squeezed from Conti's hangnail. The skin around it is red and puffy.

Bauer: The Topside's a great establishment. I actually, I know the guy who owns it.

Conti: Oh really? You should've gotten me a discount.

Audience squeals and clicks their hooves together.

Lang: Me too.

More squealing. A log falls from the wooden wall behind the guests. The same hollow bump from before is heard as it hits the ground.

Andersen: Anyway, what are we here to talk about again?

Bauer: Right, right, of course. Lupo. Almost forgot.

Lang: Same here.

Several more logs fall down. The focus of the camera shifts to Bauer.

Bauer: Alright then, I imagine you two are just dying to tell all these lovely people here tonight about this movie, and I bet they're ready to hear it.

The audience squeals. As the rest die down, one squeal is heard above the others. It continues for twelve seconds before being abruptly cut off.

Bauer: They certainly sound ready.

The camera cuts back to the guests. In Andersen's seat there is now a pig.

Bauer: Now I know you can't give us everything, especially with opening night so close, October 15th for those who don't know, but I am curious what you can give us.

The Andersen pig drops down onto the floor and walks offstage.

Lang: Is it getting a little cold in here?

Bauer: There is a bit of a draft, now that you mention it.

Squealing is heard from the direction the pig went. A thin line of blood runs down Conti's wrist. He has rubbed the back of his hand raw and is beginning to scratch away the skin.

Lang: I guess we could talk about the uh, the cafe scene?

Conti: Yeah probably.

Lang: You don't seem very certain.

The audience squeals. Conti speaks as they quiet down.

Conti: I could gut you right now.

Lang: It's really getting cold in here.

Bauer: Yeah, maybe we can get some, some uh blankets. I'm sure the crew can get them for us.

Conti: Are you sure you're not trying to freeze us to death, Joel?

The audience squeals and oinks. The logs all fall away from the background, revealing a brick wall.

Bauer: Alright, we have to stop getting off track. I think the viewers at home are probably tired of hearing my voice, so why don't you two talk for a little while? You are the leads, after all.

The camera focuses in on Conti and Lang.

Lang: So, my favorite scene in the movie is this little moment in a cafe. The main characters, George and I, are sitting at a table just chatting. Everything's over, and it's just this little "calm after the storm". And George says "I'm so hungry. I'm starving. Please. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. I need more. Just a little more."

Blood runs down Conti's arm to his elbow. It drips onto the couch and stains the white fabric red.

Lang: It's a lovely scene. I think it really encapsulates everything the film was going for. It's this beautiful look at a person's search for meaning in a world they weren't born into.

Conti: I think it's awful.

Lang: In all honesty, it's been such a pleasure to work with George. He's such a sweet man.

Conti: Why don't you ever respond to me?

Conti has scratched a small hole into his hand near the hangnail. Blood leaks out of it slowly.

Lang: I remember one night when we were finished filming and it was pouring outside. I'd forgotten my umbrella, and he was just, standing there. Waiting for me.

Conti: Why do none of you ever respond to me?

Lang: He walked me out into the rain and asked me how my folks were doing. I hadn't seen them in weeks, but they'd called a few times.

Conti: Are you still feeling cold?

Lang: Oh listen to him, still so concerned over me.

Conti: I'm gonna wring you out.

Lang: Anyway, he walked me all the way out to my car and made my day a little brighter. It was lovely.

The camera cuts back to Bauer's desk. There is now a large pig seated there with its front hooves on the top of the desk. It oinks loudly and, after sniffing the air for a few seconds, begins eating a piece of paper.

A brick falls out of the wall.

Lang: This whole experience has just been amazing. I really couldn't have asked for a better costar than George.

Several lines of blood run down Conti's arm. It has begun pooling on the ground in front of him. There is a large gouge on the back of his hand. The wound is a dark purple color and pus leaks out of it. The hangnail is longer now, and the skin around it is bright red.

Conti: I'm gonna bleed out all over the fucking carpet, Jesus. Does anyone have a towel?

Lang: The wind's louder now.

Conti: Huffing and puffing.

Lang: That's a funny way of putting it.

The Bauer pig falls off its chair and squeals. The audience squeals in reaction.

Lang: Well, do you want to continue the interview?

Conti: Sure.

Grass rapidly grows on the linoleum flooring. A winding gravel path appears and leads up to the back of the stage, presumably going further beyond the wall. More bricks fall out. Conti stands and walks over to Bauer's chair.

Lang: So how's life as a talk show host.

Conti: It's just fucking great.

Lang: That's amazing to hear.

Conti's scratching is now audible. Blood squirts from the gouge.

Conti: Oh god.

Lang: How do you feel about the choices you've made, what they've led you to?

The lighting changes. There are no longer halogen light bulbs. A bright, yellow shine emits from somewhere above.

Conti: I never should have left. I didn't know I could ever be this hungry.

Lang: How does your family feel about it? Your friends?

The brick wall crumbles. The sky is visible beyond Conti and Lang. Fields roll into the distance. On a hill, there are three houses. The camera zooms in on Conti.

Lang: It's a little chilly, isn't it?

Conti grabs the hangnail between thumb and forefinger and pulls. It peels down his arm and reaches his elbow. Gray fur sticks out of the seam.

Conti: I'm so hungry. I'm sorry, I'm so sorry.

Lang: How do you—

Lang's voice is suddenly stopped and replaced by the sound of squealing. The camera zooms out as Conti walks around the desk and kneels down beside the Lang pig. He holds its head in his hands.

Conti: Do you, do you hear me?

The Lang pig squeals. The audience squeals. The Bauer pig and the Andersen pig are approaching the houses on the hill. Conti turns to look at the camera as the sun, suddenly appearing from overhead, rapidly sets.

Conti: Can you hear—

END RECORDING

At the end of Event-9030-A, an empty stomach was ejected from the television used to play it. The words "And they all three lived happily ever after" were etched into the stomach lining.

SCP-9030.raw_source: ===== [[include component:preview text=Great television is hard to come by. Take a load off and stay awhile. Ignore the pigs.]] ===== [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] **Item #:** SCP-9030 **Object Class:** Keter **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9030 is currently uncontainable. Efforts are ongoing to intercept and remove shipments of media infested by SCP-9030. Selective-memory amnestics are to be administered to every human above the age of 12 in North America and Europe. This is accomplished through an aerosolized compound sprayed over large public areas and the injection of the amnestics in all mandatory vaccines. The initial vector of the amnestic is to target memories involving the key words “fable”, “fairy tale”, and “fantasy”. The secondary vector is to target the key words "gray", and "tooth". **Description:** SCP-9030 is a phenomenon affecting seemingly random pieces of media primarily in North America. SCP-9030 will “infest” a piece of media and change its narrative. These changes largely consist of the additions of pigs and their subsequent deaths. These deaths are usually implied to be incredibly violent, but are rarely described or seen. Characters within the narrative do not react to these deaths or other changes within the narrative in any meaningful way. If changes to the narrative are consistent with the original tone, plot, and characterization, they are reacted to accordingly. SCP-9030 is believed to have existed within several narratives before becoming anomalous. Though these narratives have been investigated, it is unclear if there was a large-scale memory erasure event or if they have always existed in this state. **Addendum A:** Instances of SCP-9030 The following are some of the most notable SCP-9030 infestation events. It is important to note that SCP-9030 infestations, unless stated otherwise, only affect a single copy of the infested media. ||~ INFESTATION POINT||~ TYPE OF MEDIA ||~ EVENT DESCRIPTION|| || //Little Red Riding Hood//[[footnote]] Published 1963 [[/footnote]] || Book || The wolf is no longer present in the story. When Little Red Riding Hood arrives at her grandmother’s house, she hears chewing sounds from within the bedroom. She does not knock on the door. She spends the majority of the story looking at her shoes. An hour later, when her grandmother leaves the room, they eat pork together. Neither speaks. || || //Jack and the Beanstalk//[[footnote]] Published 1975[[/footnote]] || Book || Jack plants the bean in his family’s farm and it grows overnight. However, he does not climb it. Pieces of pig viscera fall from above. Jack’s father stands beside him and puts his hand on his shoulder. || || //Indiana Jones and the Raiders of the Lost Ark//[[footnote]]Released 1981[[/footnote]] || Film || Pigs replace Nazis as the primary antagonists of the film. At the end of the movie, rather than being melted by the opening of the Ark, they are roasted. A large, dark shape can be seen emerging from the Ark before the film cuts to black, but it is too indistinct to make out. || || //Humpty-Dumpty//[[footnote]]Published 1992[[/footnote]] || Cartoon || The fairy tale is significantly longer than its original version. Humpty-Dumpty is left lying on the ground for a significant, but unspecified length of time. Inside his cracked shell is a piglet. Eventually, one of the King’s men gives him a bandage which he uses to cover up the crack. There are brief descriptions of scratching from within Humpty-Dumpty, but they cease after a brief period of time.|| || [REDACTED][[footnote]]Publication date varies between infestations. Earliest version is from the 1840's while the latest is from 2025.[[/footnote]] || Book || Every infested copy of the story contained only the words "No take-backsies". Over 38 instances of [REDACTED] have been infested by SCP-9030. || || //Braveheart//[[footnote]]Released 1995[[/footnote]] || Film || The movie continues normally throughout the majority of its runtime up until the ending with Wallace's death. Before being drawn and quartered, Wallace screams and says that there is a "great beast within the city walls". His cries are ignored and he is tortured via the Goat's Tongue, [[footnote]]A method of torture in which salt water is sprayed on the victim's feet and a goat licks it off, removing large amounts of skin in the process.[[/footnote]] however the torture is performed by a pig rather than a goat. || **Addendum B:** Event-9030-A On September 28th, 2023, an SCP-9030 infestation was detected and intercepted in a recording of the now-defunct late night talk show "Stayin' Up with Joel Bauer". The clip was of an interview between Bauer and three guests from an upcoming theatrical release in 1999.[[footnote]]It is referred to as "Lupo" throughout, although research into the film found no evidence of its existence.[[/footnote]] The guests in question were actress Maria Lang and actors George Conti and Albert Andersen. This recording has been classified as Event-9030-A due to the numerous unique anomalies present that had not been seen in an SCP-9030 infestation before and have not been seen since. The full recording has been transcribed below: [[div class="blockquote"]] **BEGIN RECORDING** //The footage stutters and flashes on to a bright, blurry display. The zoom is adjusted until the lens focuses on a man standing in front of the camera, standing on a small circular stage, identified as Joel Bauer. He is wearing a navy blue two piece suit and leather shoes. Behind him and to the left are his desk and a long white suede couch. There are dark blue stage curtains in the background with faint halogen lights placed intermittently above. A cramped hallway is set into the back of the stage, presumably for guests to enter through. Bauer looks to someone off screen before looking into the camera, straightening his tie, and smiling.// **Bauer:** Good evening everyone, I hope you're all having a lovely night. I know I am. To begin tonight's show, we'll be having the main cast of Lupo on to talk about the film and their experience working with Spielberg, and maybe even give us some behind the scenes info. //The audience claps and hollers. Bauer smiles and puts his hands up to quiet them.// **Bauer:** After that, we'll talk with Tom Waits about his new album "Mule Variations", his first in over five years. Then, to finish off the night, we'll have Jerry Seinfeld on in anticipation of his next tour across North America. //Audience claps again. Bauer speaks over the clapping.// **Bauer:** Well, I'm glad to see you're excited. Now, if you could get ready for another round of applause, please welcome George, Maria, and Albert, everyone! //The audience continues clapping. "Big Band" jazz music plays as three figures walk onstage from the hallway. The three are identified as Lang, Conti, and Andersen. Lang is wearing an ankle-length red dress, Conti is wearing a wool jacket, jeans, and sunglasses, and Andersen is wearing a bright red jacket and cargo pants. Lang sits on the end of the couch closest to Bauer, Andersen takes the middle seat, and Conti sits at the opposite end. The audience's clapping gradually dies down as Bauer sits at his desk, shaking each of the guests hands.// **Bauer:** I'm so happy to have you all on the show, it's really such a pleasure. I-I heard you all just got into New York a few days ago, is that true? **Lang:** Yeah, we wanted to get in before the show tonight so we could go around and see the sights. **Conti:** We got rained out of the plane right when we landed. Made a break for the cab and got to our hotel as fast as possible. **Andersen:** Ruined my best sweater. //The audience laughs. Conti begins scratching a hangnail on his left index finger.// **Bauer:** Well that's quite unfortunate, but how's the city been treating you so far? Besides the sweater, of course. //Audience laughs lightly. The curtains in the background begin to part.// **Conti:** It's a, uh, a new experience, for sure. I'm used to back roads, farms, fourteen year olds driving tractors down gravel paths. //As the curtains open further, a wall of straw is revealed.// **Conti:** There's an odd hideousness to it, I guess. Like something's biting your arm, trying to get to the bone, but it's so cold you can't feel it. You just let it keep gnawing, gnawing. **Andersen:** The pizza's plenty good. Better than any I've had before. Some New Yorkers like to act like it's God's gift to food, but it's nothing to scoff at, that's for sure. **Bauer:** I think you might want to apologize to the audience of New Yorkers in the crowd you just insulted tonight. //Audience laughs. Someone yells out "Best in the world!"// **Bauer:** Well how about you, Maria? You've been awfully quiet. **Lang:** It's been nice. I went to see all the sights, eat all the foods. Just experience everything for the first time. //Conti continues to scratch his hangnail. A small droplet of blood is squeezed out and quickly dries, turning the hangnail dark red.// **Lang:** My parents called me last night to make sure I hadn't been mugged yet. They specifically said "yet". //Audience laughs. The straw begins to rot.// **Conti:** Mine called me too. Wanted to tell me that my grandmother thought she'd already seen Lupo and was waiting to congratulate me on a job well done. //Audience laughs again.// **Andersen:** I thought your grandma died? **Conti:** Oh, yeah. It was my grandfather. Slipped my mind. //The straw falls away in clumps until it has rotted beyond usability. There are wooden logs lining the wall behind the straw. Conti continues scratching his hangnail.// **Bauer:** I'm sorry to hear that George. **Conti:** It's nothing. That actually reminds me, I went out to go find a restaurant last night, just some midnight cravings, and I saw this dog. It was in an alleyway, alone. //The audience squeals.// **Conti:** I went up to it to say hi, and it didn't move an inch. I walked right up next to it, and it wasn't breathing. I nudged his body with my toe, but he just flopped over like a half-empty beanbag. He was starving, I think. When he died, I mean. I wanted to bury him somewhere, but there was only concrete or asphalt everywhere I looked, so I dropped him in the dumpster. //A drop of blood from Conti's hangnail runs down his knuckle.// **Bauer:** Where did you end up eating? If you don't mind me asking, of course. **Conti:** The Topside. Didn't eat. //A loud, hollow bump is heard. Its source cannot be identified.// **Lang:** I love the Topside, I actually went there most nights. What did you get? **Conti:** I didn't get anything. **Andersen:** I think I stopped by there once. It was a nice little place. Bit too stuffy for my tastes, but the food was good. **Conti:** How many dogs starve in New York, do you think? //Another drop of blood is squeezed from Conti's hangnail. The skin around it is red and puffy.// **Bauer:** The Topside's a great establishment. I actually, I know the guy who owns it. **Conti:** Oh really? You should've gotten me a discount. //Audience squeals and clicks their hooves together.// **Lang:** Me too. //More squealing. A log falls from the wooden wall behind the guests. The same hollow bump from before is heard as it hits the ground.// **Andersen:** Anyway, what are we here to talk about again? **Bauer:** Right, right, of course. Lupo. Almost forgot. **Lang:** Same here. //Several more logs fall down. The focus of the camera shifts to Bauer.// **Bauer:** Alright then, I imagine you two are just dying to tell all these lovely people here tonight about this movie, and I bet they're ready to hear it. //The audience squeals. As the rest die down, one squeal is heard above the others. It continues for twelve seconds before being abruptly cut off.// **Bauer:** They certainly sound ready. //The camera cuts back to the guests. In Andersen's seat there is now a pig.// **Bauer:** Now I know you can't give us everything, especially with opening night so close, October 15th for those who don't know, but I am curious what you can give us. //The Andersen pig drops down onto the floor and walks offstage.// **Lang:** Is it getting a little cold in here? **Bauer:** There is a bit of a draft, now that you mention it. //Squealing is heard from the direction the pig went. A thin line of blood runs down Conti's wrist. He has rubbed the back of his hand raw and is beginning to scratch away the skin.// **Lang:** I guess we could talk about the uh, the cafe scene? **Conti:** Yeah probably. **Lang:** You don't seem very certain. //The audience squeals. Conti speaks as they quiet down.// **Conti:** I could gut you right now. **Lang:** It's really getting cold in here. **Bauer:** Yeah, maybe we can get some, some uh blankets. I'm sure the crew can get them for us. **Conti:** Are you sure you're not trying to freeze us to death, Joel? //The audience squeals and oinks. The logs all fall away from the background, revealing a brick wall.// **Bauer:** Alright, we have to stop getting off track. I think the viewers at home are probably tired of hearing my voice, so why don't you two talk for a little while? You are the leads, after all. //The camera focuses in on Conti and Lang.// **Lang:** So, my favorite scene in the movie is this little moment in a cafe. The main characters, George and I, are sitting at a table just chatting. Everything's over, and it's just this little "calm after the storm". And George says "I'm so hungry. I'm starving. Please. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. I need more. Just a little more." //Blood runs down Conti's arm to his elbow. It drips onto the couch and stains the white fabric red.// **Lang:** It's a lovely scene. I think it really encapsulates everything the film was going for. It's this beautiful look at a person's search for meaning in a world they weren't born into. **Conti:** I think it's awful. **Lang:** In all honesty, it's been such a pleasure to work with George. He's such a sweet man. **Conti:** Why don't you ever respond to me? //Conti has scratched a small hole into his hand near the hangnail. Blood leaks out of it slowly.// **Lang:** I remember one night when we were finished filming and it was pouring outside. I'd forgotten my umbrella, and he was just, standing there. Waiting for me. **Conti:** Why do none of you ever respond to me? **Lang:** He walked me out into the rain and asked me how my folks were doing. I hadn't seen them in weeks, but they'd called a few times. **Conti:** Are you still feeling cold? **Lang:** Oh listen to him, still so concerned over me. **Conti:** I'm gonna wring you out. **Lang:** Anyway, he walked me all the way out to my car and made my day a little brighter. It was lovely. //The camera cuts back to Bauer's desk. There is now a large pig seated there with its front hooves on the top of the desk. It oinks loudly and, after sniffing the air for a few seconds, begins eating a piece of paper.// //A brick falls out of the wall.// **Lang:** This whole experience has just been amazing. I really couldn't have asked for a better costar than George. //Several lines of blood run down Conti's arm. It has begun pooling on the ground in front of him. There is a large gouge on the back of his hand. The wound is a dark purple color and pus leaks out of it. The hangnail is longer now, and the skin around it is bright red.// **Conti:** I'm gonna bleed out all over the fucking carpet, Jesus. Does anyone have a towel? **Lang:** The wind's louder now. **Conti:** Huffing and puffing. **Lang:** That's a funny way of putting it. //The Bauer pig falls off its chair and squeals. The audience squeals in reaction.// **Lang:** Well, do you want to continue the interview? **Conti:** Sure. //Grass rapidly grows on the linoleum flooring. A winding gravel path appears and leads up to the back of the stage, presumably going further beyond the wall. More bricks fall out. Conti stands and walks over to Bauer's chair.// **Lang:** So how's life as a talk show host. **Conti:** It's just fucking great. **Lang:** That's amazing to hear. //Conti's scratching is now audible. Blood squirts from the gouge.// **Conti:** Oh god. **Lang:** How do you feel about the choices you've made, what they've led you to? //The lighting changes. There are no longer halogen light bulbs. A bright, yellow shine emits from somewhere above.// **Conti:** I never should have left. I didn't know I could ever be this hungry. **Lang:** How does your family feel about it? Your friends? //The brick wall crumbles. The sky is visible beyond Conti and Lang. Fields roll into the distance. On a hill, there are three houses. The camera zooms in on Conti.// **Lang:** It's a little chilly, isn't it? //Conti grabs the hangnail between thumb and forefinger and pulls. It peels down his arm and reaches his elbow. Gray fur sticks out of the seam.// **Conti:** I'm so hungry. I'm sorry, I'm so sorry. **Lang:** How do you-- //Lang's voice is suddenly stopped and replaced by the sound of squealing. The camera zooms out as Conti walks around the desk and kneels down beside the Lang pig. He holds its head in his hands.// **Conti:** Do you, do you hear me? //The Lang pig squeals. The audience squeals. The Bauer pig and the Andersen pig are approaching the houses on the hill. Conti turns to look at the camera as the sun, suddenly appearing from overhead, rapidly sets.// **Conti:** Can you hear-- **END RECORDING** [[/div]] At the end of Event-9030-A, an empty stomach was ejected from the television used to play it. The words "And they all three lived happily ever after" were etched into the stomach lining.
