Approx. 11.3k words [[[frozen-fox-page |My Author Page!]]] @@ @@ @@ @@    [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[div class="notation"]] //“There are, O valiant hero, other things whose forms once-changed as these, have so remained, but there are some who take on many shapes, as you have, Proteus, dweller of the deep — the deep whose arms embrace the earth.”// [[>]] //-Ovid, Metamorphoses// [[/>]] [[/div]] @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ ----- [[include :scp-wiki:component:acs-animation]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:anomaly-class-bar-source |item-number= 9075 |clearance= 4 |container-class= keter |secondary-class= none |disruption-class= keneq |risk-class= danger ]] ----- [[include component:image-block     name= PostojnaCaveMain.jpg |     caption= A section of Postojna Cave formerly open to the public prior to the events of 2077/02/09. |     align=center |     width=100% ]] ----- +++ **Special Containment Procedures:** The Foundation has been cooperating with the Manna Charitable Foundation (MCF) to manage and mitigate the effects of SCP-9075 in Postojna, Slovenia. Foundation agents embedded in Postojna have taken on cover identities as MCF employees. Personnel are to monitor residents for any indications of SCP-9075-A sightings and respond accordingly.[[footnote]]See Document //D-9075-Φ// for specific guidelines.[[/footnote]] Postojna Cave has been permanently closed to the public with guards stationed at the current entrance to prevent any unauthorized access. Class-V full-body hazmat gear is required for any personnel entering the cave. A pediatric clinic jointly run by the Foundation and the MCF has been established in the city to identify instances of SCP-9075-B. Any discovered instances, along with their families, are to be taken immediately into Foundation care at Facility L27, with cover stories disseminated to the community to explain their disappearance. SCP-9075-A instances are to be left alone unless found outside Postojna Cave. Instances are to be captured and relocated inside the cave; neutralization of instances is only permitted if such relocation is not possible. Agents are to notify researchers immediately if a new variety of SCP-9075-A is discovered. The Department of Herpetology’s batrachology division is to monitor olm populations outside the nation of Slovenia for any anomalous changes in physiology. Any such changes must be reported to the SCP-9075 research team immediately. MTF-Iota-90 (“Spelunk Hazard”) has been assigned to explore the entirety of Postojna Cave. Such exploration is to continue until the source of SCP-9075 is identified. +++ **Description:** SCP-9075 is the collective designation for the various ongoing phenomena affecting Postojna, Slovenia and its residents in the years since the 2077 Kresnik Chemical Plant Disaster. These phenomena center around the potential contamination of the town’s water supply and are believed to originate from one of the locations most severely impacted by the chemical plant’s total destruction — the depths of Postojna Cave. [[div class="blockquote"]] +++ **Background Dossier:** //[Note: the following dossier was prepared by Dr. Mirjam van Rijn to provide important context and background regarding SCP-9075. Personnel newly assigned to the anomaly must familiarize themselves with the information presented below before commencing their work.]// ---- ++++ —The Kresnik Chemical Plant ---- The Kresnik Chemical Plant was constructed in 2072 by the BadenForm Corporation.[[footnote]]The result of a merger between two major chemical companies — BASF SE from Germany and Formosa Plastics Corporation from Taiwan — to become one of the largest chemical producers in the industry globally.[[/footnote]] Located near the Pivka River on the outskirts of Postojna, the plant was designed to produce industrial chemicals used by a number of corporate clients — their largest known client being oil and gas conglomerate [[[scp-9154 |ExxArc]]].[[footnote]]Designated as GoI-236, due to the company’s use of anomalous methods to bolster their business interests. Whether ExxArc or BadenForm had entered the anomalous world at the time of the plant’s construction is presently unknown.[[/footnote]] In particular, one of the plant’s primary functions was the synthesis of various coolant and insulation fluids containing high amounts of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCB). These chemicals are known to be highly toxic and possess carcinogenic properties. Additionally, they easily bind to sediments, soils, and organic tissue, allowing them to persist for long periods in environments to which they are exposed. [[include component:image-block | name= PCB_Label.jpg | caption=An engineer affixing a warning label to a transformer indicating the presence of PCB. Application of such warnings has since fallen out of standard industry practice.]] Despite the risks and dangers, the use of PCB in the industry had become commonplace following the repeal of the //Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants// in 2058. Their legality was not enough to assuage the concerns of the residents of Postojna, however, and the Kresnik Plant was met with considerable opposition due to its proposed location that would place it not only along the Pivka River, but above Postojna Cave.   Postojna Cave is the second longest cave system in Slovenia, with a total length of approximately 24 km. The cave was formed by the Pivka River, which flows into the cave system from the north before fully disappearing underground. Notably, the last four kilometers at the deepest section of the cave are entirely underwater.[[footnote]]Whether the cave extends even deeper has not yet been determined.[[/footnote]] The cave is especially important to the Postojna community, as the groundwater serves as a primary water source for the area. Additionally, the cave is a notable habitat for Slovenia’s sole remaining population of olms. ---- ++++ —The Olm ---- The olm (//Proteus anguinus//) is an aquatic salamander that has adapted to thrive in subterranean environments. Members of the species possess long serpentine bodies with short limbs. Their thin skin largely lacks any pigmentation, giving their bodies a pale, pink-white color. Additionally, as a result of the perpetual darkness of their subterranean habitat, olms are entirely blind with undeveloped eyes that are covered by a layer of skin. To make up for their lack of sight, they are equipped with other sensory organs that allow them to detect alternative stimuli such as vibrations, electrical charges, and the presence of organic chemicals. [[include component:image-block | name= OlmsBigDebut.jpg | caption=Photograph of a Postojna Cave olm taken prior to the 2077 Kresnik Plant Disaster.]] Similar to certain other species of salamanders such as the axolotl[[footnote]]//Ambystoma mexicanum//, declared extinct in the wild in 2029.[[/footnote]] and the common mudpuppy,[[footnote]]//Necturus maculosus//, currently considered endangered.[[/footnote]] olms exhibit neoteny; that is, they do not undergo metamorphosis like most other amphibians and retain their larval traits even into adulthood. As such, olms remain entirely aquatic with external gills that protrude out from the back of the head. Historically native to the region bordering the northern and eastern Adriatic Sea, by 2054 the olm had become critically endangered due to increasing groundwater pollution across Europe with Postojna Cave serving as the only remaining habitat within Slovenia. The decision to construct the chemical plant above this habitat was met with considerable resistance, though this ultimately failed to stop BadenForm from proceeding with its plans. The plant was eventually completed in 2072. ---- ++++ —Period of Operation (2072-2077) ---- Little is known about the plant’s operations during the period it was active. The plant’s manager, Victor Cho, enforced a policy of strict secrecy among his employees and aggressively opposed any attempted inquiries regarding the plant from outside entities. Cho additionally took on an adversarial tone with Postojna’s residents, and complaints about the plant consistently went unanswered. The relationship with the town was tense in general, as, rather than hiring residents from Postojna, the company staffed the plant purely with pre-existing employees who lived on-site.[[footnote]]These employees would frequently visit the town proper, but were notoriously reticent to speak about anything remotely related to their work. Residents remarked that employees were often spotted bearing injuries resembling chemical burns.[[/footnote]] [[include component:image-block | name= BadenForm.png | caption= Logo for BadenForm Corporation, which was displayed prominently around the plant and on all employee uniforms.]] Additionally, as the plant’s period of operation continued, residents began to notice deceased olms washing up from the cave with gradually increasing frequency. Groundwater pollution by the plant was attributed as the likely cause, though Cho and BadenForm vigorously denied these claims. Indeed, testing of the water in the cave failed to reveal the presence of any harmful chemicals, leaving the cause of death for the olms unexplained. Residents were largely unconvinced of BadenForm’s innocence, however, and the plant endured mounting opposition from the community up until the day it was entirely destroyed. ---- ++++ —The Kresnik Plant Disaster ---- At 06:02 on 2077/02/09, Postojna residents were met with the sound of a loud explosion coming from the Kresnik Plant’s location. First responders arriving at the scene discovered the area covered in flames with no trace of the plant itself. The explosion was apparently large enough to break apart the ground beneath the building, causing the entirety of the plant to collapse into the cave below. The immediate consequence of the cave-in was the mass seepage of the various chemicals produced by BadenForm — including the PCB mixtures — into the cave’s water system — contaminating the town’s primary water supply. Due to the immediate risk of toxic fumes from the explosion migrating to Postojna proper, the Slovenian government promptly declared an emergency and ordered the town to evacuate. An environmental assessment quickly commenced that found the water systems had become heavily contaminated with PCB. The effects of the spill became rapidly apparent, with the wildlife in and along the Pivka River dying in droves. The most notable casualty of the disaster was the population of olms, which was effectively wiped out, their corpses washing up from the cave en masse for several days following the spill. The species would be formally declared extinct in Slovenia two weeks after the disaster. ---- ++++ —Response   ---- The disaster received moderate international attention, with various non-governmental organizations — the Manna Charitable Foundation[[footnote]]GoI-λ-33.[[/footnote]] chief among them — arriving to provide aid to those displaced by the disaster. An assessment of the cave discovered additional collapses — one notably located near the main entrance — rendering much of the cave inaccessible. With the entirety of the plant having disappeared into the depths of the cave, all employees present at the time of the disaster, including Victor Cho, were declared missing, presumed deceased. In the face of widespread criticism, BadenForm pledged to remediate all damages caused by the spill. The corporation was soon joined by ExxArc with CEO DeForest Morgan personally vowing to use his resources to expedite all clean-up efforts and provide compensation to all residents of Postojna. The move was widely celebrated, and after only six months of clean-up efforts, tests of the water supply consistently showed a lack of harmful chemicals in the water. Residents were cleared to move back to the town shortly after. BadenForm suffered a severe drop in stock price immediately following the disaster. Notably, during this clean-up period, ExxArc was able to successfully negotiate the total acquisition of BadenForm. It is now formally a subsidiary of ExxArc.     [[/div]] +++ **Discovery:** Because the circumstances surrounding the Kresnik Plant Disaster did not indicate the existence of any anomalous elements, the Foundation concluded the matter to be beyond its purview. On 2080/07/09, however, representatives from the Manna Charitable Foundation contacted Foundation liaisons regarding supposed recent anomalous developments in Postojna. Dr. Mirjam van Rijn, a Foundation biochemist, was instructed to travel to Postojna and meet with MCF representative Dr. Tabitha Nkosi. Dr. Nkosi is a medical practitioner and one of a handful of MCF employees remaining in Postojna to help provide continued additional aid to those affected by the plant disaster. [[div class="blockquote"]] **Meeting Log — 2080/07/10** ---- **** **Dr. Nkosi:** Thank you for coming in, Dr. van Rijn. We’re so happy you’re here to help. **Dr. van Rijn:** Well, it would depend on what exactly you need our help with. **Dr. Nkosi:** Right, of course. Sorry about that. **Dr. van Rijn:** It’s fine, just start from the beginning. You believe something anomalous is happening here in Postojna? **Dr. Nkosi:** Oh, without a doubt. Putting it simply, we believe there’s something wrong with the water. **Dr. van Rijn:** The water? **Dr. Nkosi:** The groundwater, specifically. From the cave. We think it might still be contaminated. **Dr. van Rijn:** You mean from the chemical spill? I thought that all got cleaned up. //[Dr. Nkosi nods.]// **Dr. Nkosi:** So did we. And all our tests say so too. Every sample we’ve taken comes back clear as crystal. Not a trace of contaminants. **Dr. van Rijn:** I don’t see the problem; isn’t that a good thing? **Dr. Nkosi:** I mean, it would be, but… it seems like people are getting sick anyway. **Dr. van Rijn:** Could you please elaborate? **Dr. Nkosi:** Well, we’ve got people coming into our clinics with the exact kinds of symptoms you would expect from PCB poisoning. The sores and the lesions, of course. But we’re also seeing some really bad liver damage and messed up hormone levels. Obviously this shouldn’t be possible, since the water’s coming back clean. It’s all gotten us thinking there may be something unnatural, maybe even deceptive, going on. //[Dr. van Rijn nods.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** Okay, I think I get it now. You’re unsure if ExxArc really did clean up the spill like they say they did. **Dr. Nkosi:** Do you think it’s possible? That they might’ve done something to mask the presence of the chemicals? Like, they’re still in the water, but some magic or something is keeping us from detecting them? **Dr. van Rijn:** I wouldn’t put it past them, I’ll put it that way. //[She leans forward.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** How about this? We’ll have some of our people take a look at the water as well as your patients. We’ll see if our own tests can find anything useful. We can also take a look at our intel on ExxArc; see if there’s anything there that might be of help. **Dr. Nkosi:** That would be great! We’ve tried reaching out to ExxArc ourselves — multiple times, actually — but they just keep giving us the cold shoulder. **Dr. van Rijn:** Not surprising; that’s just how they are, apparently. But I think we have enough to go on for now, as far as next steps go. Unless there was anything else you wanted to talk about? //[Pause.]// **Dr. Nkosi:** Well, I guess there is one more thing… //[She shifts her weight to one side.]// **Dr. Nkosi:** I haven’t been able to verify it for myself yet, but I’ve gotten a few reports of olm sightings by Postojna residents over the past two weeks or so. Dead olms, to be clear. Supposedly they’ve been washing up from the cave. **Dr. van Rijn:** Olms? Didn’t the spill kill them all off? **Dr. Nkosi:** As far as we know, yes. We haven’t seen any of these corpses for ourselves. And our ecologists have thoroughly explored the cave several times — at least the portion anyone can get to. No one saw even a hint of wildlife inside. **Dr. van Rijn:** So where could the corpses have come from? Did any of these witnesses take a sample? **Dr. Nkosi:** Well, I asked, and it seems one of them tried. But he says something strange stopped him from doing so. **Dr. van Rijn:** What? **Dr. Nkosi:** Before he could grab it, it was like the corpse dissolved into the water. **** [[/div]] +++ **Addendum 9075-01:** Foundation chemists collected samples of groundwater from the vicinity of Postojna (including from within Postojna Cave). Similar to the MCF, their tests were unable to detect the presence of any toxic contaminants. Still, medical evaluations of affected residents found their symptoms to be consistent with those resulting from exposure to PCB. The Foundation has since commenced cooperation with the MCF to provide medical treatment for these symptoms. Foundation representatives reached out to ExxArc regarding this discrepancy and received the following message: [[div class="papernote"]] To our friends at the SCP Foundation: We are saddened to learn of the misfortune that has befallen the wonderful people of Postojna, and we offer our deepest sympathies. However, we would like to stress that ExxArc pledged to remediate all damages resulting from the 2077 chemical spill and by all conceivable metrics, we have thoroughly exceeded these obligations. ExxArc is fully committed to maintaining healthy and robust standards of living for all life on our beautiful planet. Any statements indicating otherwise we shall consider to be defamatory in nature. And we will respond accordingly. We send our thoughts and prayers to the citizens of Postojna, which we believe should be sufficient on our part to address your concerns. Kindest regards, Cecilia Wollensky-Huesca Assistant to DeForest Morgan, CEO ExxArc [[/div]] Following conferral with the Department of External Affairs, the decision was reached to abstain from further contact with ExxArc in regards to SCP-9075 for the foreseeable future.[[footnote]]While the Department of External affairs did not believe ExxArc posed any serious threat to the Foundation, past interactions with the company indicated that continued questioning related to SCP-9075 was unlikely to lead to any useful information.[[/footnote]] After a period of negotiations, the Foundation agreed to assist the MCF in implementing a water-filtration system for the town’s water supply that made use of various anomalous Foundation technologies. Due to the inability to detect PCB levels, the efficacy of the system could not be measured with precision, though Postojna did see a significant reduction in PCB exposure symptoms over the following weeks. +++ **Addendum 9075-02:** [[div class="blockquote"]] ++++ Interview Log — 2080/07/15 ---- **Interviewer:** Dr. Mirjam van Rijn **Subject:** Jakob Avsenik, 49 **Notes:** Subject is a Postojna resident who claims to have discovered and attempted to grab an olm corpse outside Postojna Cave the week prior. Interview is conducted in English.[[footnote]]Due to high fluency rates across Slovenia, communications between the MCF and Postojna residents are typically performed in the English language.[[/footnote]] ---- **** **Dr. van Rijn:** Good evening, Mr. Avsenik. How are you feeling today? //[Avsenik shrugs.]// **Avsenik:** Eh, could be worse. The pills you doctors[[footnote]]Dr. van Rijn has assumed the cover identity of a medical toxicologist employed by the MCF.[[/footnote]] prescribed have got me feeling a little less like shit. Just a little, mind you. Still feel like shit. **Dr. van Rijn:** Well, I’m glad to hear you’re feeling at least somewhat better. **Avsenik:** Why did you really call me here, doctor? I didn’t think I was due for another check-up this soon. **Dr. van Rijn:** Oh, well… I was actually hoping you could tell me a little about what you saw last week. //[Avsenik sighs.]// **Avsenik:** I see, you want to know about that damned salamander. **Dr. van Rijn:** If you don’t mind. //[Pause.]// **Avsenik:** Fine, I guess I’ll bite. It was last Tuesday night. I was walking home from the pub after a miserable night watching Olimpija fumble every shot on goal like a bunch of fuckwits. It had been raining that evening, so I thought I’d take the short way home, the one that takes me past the front of that godforsaken cave. [[include component:image-block | name= ActualCaveEntranceWow.jpg | caption=Former entrance to Postojna Cave.]] **Dr. van Rijn:** You don’t sound particularly fond of the cave. //[Avsenik shrugs.]// **Avsenik:** Never really cared for it even before it swallowed that factory and fucked up our water. Still didn’t care for it much that night either. I had my eyes on the ground trying to get past as quick as I could, when I saw //it// lying on the ground. **Dr. van Rijn:** An olm? **Avsenik:** Right away I could tell it was dead. I remember seeing loads of corpses washing up the day of the spill. It was just like that. **Avsenik:** Well, //almost// just like that. **Dr. van Rijn:** What do you mean? **Avsenik:** I remember always being so put off by how //pale// those little fuckers were. Creeped me out like nothing else. But the one I saw that night had this… nasty reddish color to it. I took a few steps towards it and saw that the color was coming from these deep-red veins running all across its body. I know those things were always thin-skinned — practically translucent — but this was something else. Those veins were //bulging//. Like they were ready to burst any second. **Dr. van Rijn:** What do you think happened to the corpse? **Avsenik:** Been trying not to think about it. Especially not after I tried to pick it up. **Dr. van Rijn:** So you did try to grab it. //[Avsenik sighs.]// **Avsenik:** I have no idea what the fuck I was thinking. That thing looked so unnatural, I guess I wanted to make sure it was actually there — that I wasn’t hallucinating or something. I mean, these salamanders are supposed to be long dead, right? **Dr. van Rijn:** What happened when you tried to grab it? //[Avsenik shrugs.]// **Avsenik:** The moment my skin made contact, the corpse just… dissolved. Right into the water. Like it was never there. **Dr. van Rijn:** It dissolved? **Avsenik:** Look, I know it sounds crazy, but I know what I saw. I have no reason to lie about seeing one of them. I’ve always hated those things. **Dr. van Rijn:** Yes, I’ve kind of been getting that impression. If you don’t mind, why exactly do you feel that way? **Avsenik:** I don’t know, I… I guess it’s the way they look. Before the cave closed down, there used to be a vivarium in there that had a bunch of those salamanders. My parents would take me to see them when I was a kid, and… looking at them just made my skin crawl. I mean, they’re like these long slimy worms, with this nasty fleshy color to them. Like human skin. Pale human skin. //[Avsenik laughs.]// **Avsenik:** You know what we call them, right? The Slovene term for the little things? “//Človeška ribica//.” You know what that directly translates to in English? //[Dr. van Rijn nods.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** “//Human fish//.” //[Avsenik laughs again.]// **Avsenik:** I think that’s what I always hated most about them. That we would have anything in common with such a loathsome creature. I used to get these awful nightmares, where our town would suddenly fall into the cave and trap us there, and after years of living in the darkness, we’d start to lose our eyes too. Become all disgusting and slimy like them. //[Avsenik shrugs.]// **Avsenik:** Hell, thinking about it almost makes me feel bad for those bastards at the chemical plant. **** [[/div]] +++ **Addendum 9075-03:** [[div class="blockquote"]] ++++ Interview Log — 2080/07/26 ---- **Interviewer:** Dr. Mirjam van Rijn **Subject:** Ema Kralj, 12 **Notes:** Subject is a Postojna resident and student. ---- **** **Dr. van Rijn:** Could you tell me what it was you saw yesterday evening? **Kralj:** Uhh… well I guess I was down at the river, reading a book for school. I had just finished the chapter I was on, and as I was closing the book, I saw one of the olms swimming in the water. **Dr. van Rijn:** Wait, it was alive? Are you absolutely certain? //[Kralj laughs.]// **Kralj:** It would be super weird if it was dead. Because I watched it swim up to the riverbank, crawl up onto the land and scuttle off into the woods. //[There is a pause.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** And you’re sure this was an olm? Not another type of salamander? **Kralj:** It had to be. I mean, I remember what they look like. I used to see them in the cave with my family all the time when I was little. I know they used to have a lot more down there before I was born, but I liked seeing the ones they still had. You know, before they all died. //[Kralj smiles.]// **Kralj:** But now they’re back, isn’t that cool? Not just that, but it’s like they’re even healthier now too! The ones I remember were all so small that it never occurred to me that they could grow that long. **Dr. van Rijn:** What do you mean? Just exactly how long was this olm you saw, Ema? //[Kralj shrugs.]// **Kralj:** I dunno. About as long as a car maybe. Why? **** [[/div]] +++ **Addendum 9075-04:** **Incident Report — 2080/07/30:** At 14:57, Postojna Hospital admitted Anthony Haverford to its intensive care unit. Haverford, an English college student who was backpacking through the region with friends, was suffering from acute liver failure and muscle spasms, and showed numerous lesions on his hands and arms. He was pronounced dead at 15:49. Toxicology reports indicated high concentrations of various potent neurotoxins and dioxins in Haverford’s bloodstream. Haverford’s companions insisted he was feeling fine until he collapsed around 14:32 outside a convenience store in Postojna. Foundation personnel at the hospital questioned the group about their activities that day; of note was that shortly before the group arrived in the town, Haverford reportedly found what he described as a “funny little lizard” crawling through some mud. Haverford supposedly picked up the animal and told a friend to take a photo of it with their phone. [[include component:image-block | name= OhNoDontTouchThat.jpeg | caption=Image recovered from Anthony Haverford’s phone. |align=center]] A task force was quickly dispatched to the location where the photo was taken. Investigation of the area eventually led to the discovery of a small, previously unknown entrance to Postojna Cave obscured by the overgrowth. The task force was able to enter the opening and found themselves in the larger section of the cave that had been rendered inaccessible as a result of the Kresnik Plant Disaster. Cursory exploration of the cave promptly led to the discovery of SCP-9075-A. @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ [[div class="notation"]] //“Far from feeling surprise that some of the cave-animals should be very anomalous...as is the case with blind Proteus…I am only surprised that more wrecks of ancient life have not been preserved, owing to the less severe competition to which the scanty inhabitants of these dark abodes will have been exposed.”// [[>]] //-Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species// [[/>]] [[/div]] @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ SCP-9075-A are various organisms living within the previously inaccessible portion of Postojna Cave that all bear a general resemblance to the olm (//Proteus anguinus//). This section of the cave has become highly saturated with toxic substances in the time since the chemical spill. As such, researchers have theorized these organisms comprise different anomalous subspecies of olm that have drastically adapted in different ways to the current conditions in the cave. MTF-Iota-90 has been tasked with exploring the cave and logging observed subspecies. A description of the subspecies identified so far is included below. ||~ Subspecies Designation ||~ Description || || SCP-9075-A1 || Mostly resembles a non-anomalous olm, but with the ability to secrete large quantities of a highly toxic mucus.[[footnote]]Believed to be the subspecies encountered by Haverford.[[/footnote]] || || SCP-9075-A2 || Maintains similar body width to non-anomalous olms, but possesses far greater length in excess of 5 m.[[footnote]]Believed to be the subspecies encountered by Kralj.[[/footnote]] || || SCP-9075-A3 || Veins and arteries are considerably larger in diameter than other subspecies; appear to bulge out from underneath skin. Means of satiation and respiration are unknown. || +++ **Addendum 9075-05:** [[div class="blockquote"]] **Meeting Log — 2080/09/13** ---- [[include component:image-block | name= LongOlm.jpg | caption=Anterior end of SCP-9075-A2 specimen.]] **** **Dr. Nkosi:** I just read the updated files. That new subspecies you discovered is just fascinating. I thought the many-legged ones were strange enough already, but now you’re saying there’s a type that’s just completely missing a head! **Dr. van Rijn:** It’s a weird one for sure. But it still feels like we’re only scratching the surface. Our task force still hasn’t made much headway into the full length of the cave. Between the rubble and the toxicity, we’re moving much more slowly than we’d like. //[Dr. Nkosi nods.]// **Dr. Nkosi:** So have you been able to confirm the presence of PCB down there? //[Dr. van Rijn laughs halfheartedly.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** Practically everything //but//. The water down there is full of every kind of toxin under the sun, //except// for the ones BadenForm was producing at the plant. **Dr. Nkosi:** What does that mean? The water coming into the town is still showing as clean, but even with the purification, we’re still treating people for PCB exposure. **Dr. van Rijn:** It’s hard to say for sure. At this point, I’m certain that ExxArc and BadenForm did something to mask the presence of PCB in the water. But… maybe these other chemicals are still showing up in our tests, because ExxArc didn’t see the need to conceal them. **Dr. Nkosi:** What do you mean? //[Dr. van Rijn shrugs.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** It’s possible that these other toxins didn’t actually come from the spill. Maybe they came from somewhere else. **** [[/div]] +++ **Addendum 9075-06:** Further exploration into the cave has revealed the existence of additional SCP-9075-A subspecies. ||~ Subspecies Designation ||~ Description || || SCP-9075-A6 || Subspecies is considerably bulkier than baseline species with a length of approximately 1 m. Every day there was just more and more trash. **Dr. van Rijn:** But still, the pollywogs persisted. They continued darting about in the water, seemingly undaunted by the increasing litter intruding on their home. **Dr. van Rijn** Then one morning, as I was approaching the pond, I saw a group of men crowding around a bulldozer. Apparently, the hydraulics got busted, and fluid was leaking out everywhere. And that included into the pond. //[Pause.]// **Dr. van Rijn** Needless to say, the pollywogs didn’t make it. And I remember being so angry. But what made it worse was that the construction crew didn’t even care. I screamed and yelled and cursed at them, and all I remember seeing was one or two of them rolling their eyes and turning away from me. **Dr. van Rijn:** It was a little dramatic on my part, sure. I mean, I was a little kid. But it left me with this deep and profound anger — that people could be so callous to the lives of others, big or small — and I don’t think it ever left me. In fact, I think it was renewed — reignited rather — when I discovered a large corporation had poisoned an entire town, driven an entire ecosystem into desolation, and then had the audacity to do nothing and proceed to //lie// about it. Act like they could just wash their hands of the whole affair while pretending they had no accountability to the people and wildlife they had irrevocably harmed. **Dr. van Rijn:** And so, I guess the real reason I’m down here right now is that I find myself in a position where I might be able to take all that pent up frustration and — with the biggest, meanest smile on my face — finally do something about it. **Dr. van Rijn:** The Proteus that lives down here, I want to catch it, and I want to hold onto it, until we can come to an agreement. //[Dr. van Rijn stops. She has reached the water’s edge. The SCP-9075-A instances around her continue into the water and can be seen diving downward.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** Well, I guess we’re about to enter into uncharted territory. Let’s see if I can keep you around for the ride a little while longer. //[She kneels over and slowly sticks her hand in the water. After a moment, she pulls it out again and brings it up to her face.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** Hmmm… looks okay… feels okay… I think we’re golden. //[She stands up again.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** Oh, and don’t worry about me drowning. There was also another little surprise I woke up to this morning that should help me out. //[She grabs at the camera and points it at her face again. She lowers her collar slightly, revealing fleshy stalks resembling olm gills extending from her neck.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** Anyway, I know how corrosive this water can get, and I don’t want this camera breaking down too soon. So, I’m sorry, but this will be a little weird for a bit. //[She opens her mouth and places the camera inside. A few seconds later a muffled splash is audible.]// //[The video remains black for several minutes. Indistinct muted noises can periodically be heard. Finally, there is the sound of another splash. A few seconds later the image returns, showing Dr. van Rijn’s face. It is dripping wet.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** That wasn’t so bad, was it? Hope the view inside my mouth wasn’t terribly offensive. Wasn’t an awful swim for me. It was a weird feeling, being able to breathe underwater like that. Don’t really know how to describe it. Anyway, take a look at this. //[She turns the camera around revealing a large open chamber. The chamber is dimly illuminated by unseen flames scattered across the space.]// //[Dr. van Rijn begins to walk through the chamber, holding the camera in front of her. The space is filled with mounds of rubble that obscure the scope of the entire area.]// //[Dr. van Rijn navigates through the rubble; scattered among the rocks are the apparent remains of a building. Bricks, rebar, and twisted metal surround her on all sides. Eventually, she spots an image painted onto the remnants of a wall. She walks towards it.]// //[It’s the BadenForm logo.]// //[She pauses in front of the logo for a moment before continuing through the wreckage. Rounding a corner, she spots an SCP-9075-A15 specimen sitting atop a dented steel tank. The flames on its back appear to be the primary light source for this section of the chamber. The specimen is still as it stares at Dr. van Rijn. After a moment Dr. van Rijn gives a small wave and continues walking.]// //[Dr. van Rijn eventually makes it to the remains of a loading bay. More light is visible on the other side of the partially open garage door. She crouches under the door and steps through.]// //[She enters a significantly brighter, more open space. The area is dotted with small trees, bone white in color, their leaves emitting a faint glow. Scattered clusters of brightly-colored mushrooms can be seen in all directions. Dr. van Rijn steps over a shallow creek. The water flows slowly; its surface bears an iridescent sheen.]// //[The area is filled with countless SCP-9075-A instances — all observed variants are visible as well as some previously unknown. Most appear to be resting but many seem to face Dr. van Rijn as she passes. Some begin to follow her.]// //[Dr. van Rijn suddenly turns to the right. A humanoid figure can be seen behind a tree. It waves at Dr. van Rijn before taking several steps forward. As it gets closer, it becomes clear this is Ema Kralj, one of the missing SCP-9075-B instances. She smiles at Dr. van Rijn before pointing off to her right. Dr. van Rijn waves back as she starts moving in the indicated direction.]// //[Additional humanoid figures can be seen emerging from behind the trees. These figures turn out to be the other missing SCP-9075-B instances. Scattered amongst the children are the missing MTF-Iota-90 members as well as a handful of unidentified individuals.[[footnote]]Subsequent analysis has identified these individuals as former employees at the Kresnik Chemical Plant, presumed deceased following the disaster.[[/footnote]] Additional changes in physiology can be seen among the crowd, with some individuals exhibiting significantly greater muscle mass while others appear to possess elongated limbs. All show signs of fused eyelids.]// //[All visible humanoids watch Dr. van Rijn as she passes, some smiling, but none speaking or approaching. A few of them point in the same direction indicated by Kralj; Dr. van Rijn continues down this path.]// //[Up ahead, two more figures can be seen — an adult and a child. The adult is kneeling and speaking to the child, one hand on its left shoulder. As Dr. van Rijn gets closer, it becomes clear this is Neli Čeferin and Dr. Nkosi. Dr. Nkosi turns her head and, sensing Dr. van Rijn, stands and gives a warm smile.]// //[She points in the same direction as the others.]// //[Dr. van Rijn nods. She continues moving.]// //[She approaches a pair of large stalagmites that give the appearance of pillars. As she passes between them, a faint noise becomes audible off to her left. She turns and sees what appears to be a writhing mass. A closer look reveals a mound of pulsating human bodies, seemingly fused together in a chaotic manner. Pained moans emanate from open mouths which emit continuous torrents of viscous mucus.]// //[The faces have no eyes, nor skin covering the sockets. There are only empty black cavities. Nothing visible inside them.]// //[Dr. van Rijn slowly circles the mound. Some of the bodies are wearing uniforms bearing the BadenForm Logo. After a moment, she stops in front of one body. It is former plant manager Victor Cho. His face is low to the ground, someone else’s foot fused to his temple. Whether Cho can sense Dr. van Rijn’s presence is uncertain; even so, Cho’s moans seem to become sounds of weeping just moments after she stops.]// //[Dr. van Rijn stands still facing Cho for roughly thirty seconds. Then, without a word, she returns to walking, leaving the mound behind.]// //[Her path becomes a gentle incline, which gradually increases in steepness as she continues. The walk eventually turns into a climb, but Dr. van Rijn does not slow her pace. Numerous SCP-9075-A instances follow alongside her on both sides. Soon, a crest in the hill becomes visible.]// //[She continues her climb.]// //[She reaches the top.]// //[In front of her is a massive pit.]// //[She looks down. It is dark inside. But there is something moving within. A deep, slow breathing is audible.]// **Dr. van Rijn:** Father. **Dr. van Rijn:** Mother. **Dr. van Rijn:** Whatever you are. **Dr. van Rijn:** I see you. **Dr. van Rijn:** I’ve grown up. **Dr. van Rijn:** And I think we should talk. //[A pair of shining red orbs appear in the dark below. Its eyes are wide open.]// //[The pale dragon of flesh raises its head, its gaze fixed on Dr. van Rijn.]// //[The dragon roars.]// //[Dr. van Rijn laughs softly.]// //[The video suddenly cuts out.]// **** [[/div]] A thorough search of Postojna Cave commenced shortly after receipt of the file. Exploration teams were unable to locate the chamber depicted in the video or the entities within. Their whereabouts remain unknown. @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ +++ **Addendum 9075-17:** On 2081/09/19, the Foundation was alerted to an explosion at the BadenForm Corporation’s global headquarters in Munich, Germany. Reports indicate that the explosion occurred at 03:42 local time and originated from within the center of the building. The explosion was promptly followed by the sudden formation of a massive sinkhole directly beneath the structure, which pulled the entirety of the building into the earth. One witness present near the scene described the explosion as “a gigantic blood-red flame.” Two days after the initial explosion, the Foundation was able to acquire a video recording from another witness to the event. The video depicts a humanoid figure at the scene of the incident immediately following the explosion. This figure — designated Person of Interest 989 — appears to be female, with 2 chiropterine wings protruding from her back and 2 large horns growing from her head. The subject is seen standing amid the flames as walls of rubble cascade into the earth around her. She is observed to be smiling. SCP-9076.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9076

Object Class: Thaumiel

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9076 is stored within the active research and production wing of Site-23. A capture system has been installed within the reliquary to harvest the enzymes produced by the object for usage in synthesizing SCP-9076-A.

SCP-9076-A is approved for field usage in doses of up to 150 mg per day, for a maximum of up to 5 days consecutively before a required detox period of one week.

Description: SCP-9076 is the preserved amygdala of an adult human brain contained within a small bronze reliquary, allegedly that of Saint Gereon of Cologne.1 While the specific origin of SCP-9076 cannot be confirmed, the object demonstrates Akiva Radiation levels consistent with that of confirmed relics of catholic saints, and carbon dating indicates the object originates from circa 307 A.D.

If at any time SCP-9076 is present within the legal borders of the same nation as any demonic entity or persons who worship such, it will begin to anomalously excrete a unique enzyme at a rate of 2-6 ml per minute. The processed version of this enzyme is referred to as SCP-9076-A.

SCP-9076-A is a parapharmaceutical compound that, when administered intravenously to a human subject, temporarily increases the subject's resistance to harmful effects of demonic or thaumaturgic origin. The potency of SCP-9076's effects increases relative to both the size and regularity of the applied dosage, progressing through several distinct stages. If at any time the subject performs actions they2 deem as amoral while under the effects of SCP-9076-A, the effects immediately cease.

Stage Dosage Effects
1 25-50 mg, single dose Subject displays Akiva Radiation levels with a 22% increase from baseline. Subject becomes immune to bodily possession and other compulsion effects from affected sources.
2 60-85 mg, single dose Subject displays Akiva Radiation levels with a 31% increase from baseline. In addition to previous effects, subject can visibly perceive the presence of demonic entities and any effects originating from them.
3 100-120 mg, single dose Subject displays Akiva Radiation levels with a 60% increase from baseline. In addition to previous effects, physical contact with the subject has a deleterious effect on demonic entities comparable to 0.925 grade sterling silver.

SCP-9076-A has been proven to be non-addictive. However, usage at stage 3 and beyond has been observed to frequently trigger a pleasure response. Research indicates that the response is psychological in nature rather than neurological, due to the absence of the requisite chemicals to elicit the release of dopamine and other pleasure-signaling compounds in SCP-9076-A.

Stage Dosage Effects
4 100-120 mg per day for 3-6 days Subject displays Akiva Radiation levels with a 104% increase from baseline. In addition to previous effects, the subject develops mildly enhanced mental and physical capabilities and can detect spoken falsehoods.
5 140-170 mg per day for 5-8 days Subject displays Akiva Radiation levels with a 172% increase from baseline. In addition to previous effects, the subject develops mild regenerative properties. The regenerative effect is noted to be over four times as potent when restoring nervous tissue.


Addendum 1: On 11/08/2002, six field agents equipped with several pre-prepared doses of SCP-9076-A to aid in the recontainment of SCP-████ were struck by a rockslide in Wādī Bīmah gorge, Oman. The only survivor of the rockslide was Agent Bottin, who was trapped in the gorge with an unknown number of hostile demonic entities. During this time, Bottin utilized the team's supplies of SCP-9076-A in order to survive, applying dosages significantly in excess of the maximum tested at the time.

Agent Bottin's remains were discovered on 12/04/2002, emanating Akiva Radiation at a level consistent with that of SCP-9076. The following notes were found on the body, and are currently under analysis to identify the progression of symptoms caused by excessive SCP-9076-A usage.

Everyone else is gone. No idea where ████ is. Total mission failure.
I'm definitely going to die here. Might as well make it count, try and get something out of this whole ordeal.

Managed to take down a couple stragglers. Don't have the firepower to challenge big groups.
Still, two less to go ruin some poor soul's day.

Five down. Avenged the others, I guess. Rest well.
Hit stage 5, the healing is really helping. And there's a lot left, I can maintain this level for another week or so.

I still have work to do.

Stumbled into a huge group of them, shouldn't have made it out. I took all that I had, figured I was gonna die anyways.

My vision's a lot clearer now, above baseline. Everything seems beautiful. Gave me a headache, though.

I hope there is some mercy for them all, somewhere.

Seeing more, thinking more. The headache became a migraine, but it broke through and now the pressure's gone. Still a little shaky from it, handwriting might suffer.
Laying low until it heals. Could try to leave, but there's still work to be done here.

Broke through and kept going, growing around. Saw myself in a pool of water. It doesn't hurt to touch it, the ends are almost together.

Stay calm and fight the good fight.

Six men died here.

There's no darkness anymore, not around me.

I don't need the syringes anymore.

the ends meet, the loop is complete.
so clear
my thoughts like an army strengthening each other

Theyve started to run from what comes for them

almost done here.

this land is pure again, but theres more.
have my halo, need my w ings, leave the rest

glory isa chemical and GOD is the overdose,

im goign to be an angel

When Bottin's headless remains were uncovered, there were no demonic entities in the gorge. The surrounding area was searched, but no traces of the entities were found. Civilians reported seeing a glowing object an estimated 20 cm across moving through the sky five days before the remains were uncovered. One eyewitness described the object as having "stringy wings, like a jellyfish".

Footnotes
1. A Roman-Catholic saint martyred in the early 4th century. Gereon and his followers were massacred for refusing Emperor Maximian's orders to make sacrifices to several pagan gods in order to ensure military victory. As a saint, Gereon is invoked to protect soldiers and protect against migraines.
2. The triggering parameters are entirely dependent on the individual.

SCP-9077.raw_content:
Mahjong is a scary thing. One bad decision and all your good flow vanishes.

by 22o9L

Item #: SCP-9077

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: 22.9-L.aic is to monitor amateur and professional mahjong competitions in order to determine candidates to SCP-9077's manifestation. Once a game shows signs of anomalous manifestation, all transmissions of the match are to be taken down and a Response Team is to be deployed to the location in order to contain the affair.

All audience members must be removed from attendance and amnestized in order to remove any memories of SCP-9077’s manifestation. These individuals are to have any recordings or photos of the incident confiscated and archived. New memories of a non-anomalous mahjong game are to be implanted onto the audience.

SCP-9077 is to be allowed to conclude within 2 hours, for the purposes of recording data about the phenomenon. If the game is not finished by this time, Foundation personnel are to intervene and force SCP-9077 to finish by removal of players from the mahjong table.

Description: SCP-9077 is an anomalous rule variation for riichi mahjong,1 that manifests after a series of criteria are fulfilled. Once the phenomena becomes active, the mahjong tile set in use will be spontaneously modified to accommodate the new rulings. All players become immediately aware of all rule changes, without the need of further clarification.

In order for SCP-9077 to become active, a hanchan length game2 needs to go onto south-4 round, with no player below 15000 points. At least two yakuman hands3 must score without immediately winning the game. In addition to that, SCP-9077 was never observed to occur during casual play, only in mahjong related public events or tournaments. The anomaly only occurs in in-person games.

SCP-9077 adds a number of local yaku4 varying from 1 han5 to yakuman level. It's unknown how many local yaku are added by the anomaly, with a current known list of 15 new valid yaku. These additions do not override the standard yaku choices in any way, with it being possible for standard yaku and SCP-9077's being able to score together.

SCP-9077 will extend the game beyond south-4, with the round ceiling being unknown, if it even exists. The living wall from where the tiles are drawn will now contain an infinite number of tiles from every suit and number. Visually the living wall will remain the same, and is able to be dismantled in order to shuffle tiles for the next round, appearing to contain only the standard amount of tiles from each suit when shuffling. If the game is being played in an automatic mahjong table, the same properties manifest.

A game of SCP-9077 will only end after a player drops below 0 points. Players will be unable to stop themselves from playing until this condition is fulfilled. The anomaly suppresses all need for sustenance and other biological necessities during the duration of the game. Theoretically, a game of SCP-9077 can extend itself for an infinite amount of time, with the only reason for this not being possible is that the players would die by old age.

▶ Non-Comprehensive List of Yaku Added by SCP-9077
Name Requirement Effect
Big Thirteen Orphans Make a standard 13 orphans hand.6 A total of 13 father and mother figures watching the game explode.
Minor Three Dragons A single copy of red, white and green dragon tiles. Once the player declares riichi7 all other copies of red, white and green dragon tiles in other players hands will transmute into snakes8 and attempt to bite their respective players. Killing the snake reverts the transformation.
All 14 Flush All tiles on hand must be the same suit, rank or be the same honor tile.9 The player who dealt onto the winning hand is struck by lightning. If the win was a tsumo,10nothing happens.
Jizo Not having lost or gained any points during the game. Upon winning, a jizo statue11 will manifest above the player with the lowest score and fall at 3 meters per hour onto said player.
Triple Riichi Declaring riichi before hands are open. If the player wins, the player who dealt onto the hand dies for 3 minutes and later is spontaneously resurrected. The game is on break during this interval. The resurrected player, if asked about their experience, will recount about fighting with demons in hell and escaping to continue the game. If the player fails their prediction, the tiles violently move towards their face at 5 meters per hour.
Under the Earth Hand with 8 or more dora tiles.12 If a player drops to 0 point or below after this hand wins the round, said player will immediately age 60 years.
Blessing Unknown13 This hand immediately ends the game, as the winning player disappears. No player that scored this hand has been located at this moment.
▶ Incident Log

In ██/██/2017 after the containment procedures for the anomaly were established, Foundation intelligence personnel found SCP-9077 in a game on ██████ ███ Mahjong Parlor. This was the final game of the 1997 ██████ ███ local mahjong championship, between the 4 finalists. After the discovery of this event, a response team was deployed in order to contain the game and start disinformation procedures.

The game had become a local attraction through its duration, with a casual audience coming to watch the game regularly, with the ██████ ███ Mahjong Parlor providing eventual recaps of the rounds. As there is no known mental effect of SCP-9077 forcing the audience to watch the game, it is currently believed that the regular audience watched the game of their own will throughout its duration.

When the Foundation's assets arrived, the game had already ended with one player, 86-year-old Robert Sakurai, having won by SCP-9077’s local yaku "blessing". All remaining players then stood around the mahjong table and paid their respects alongside the audience. The local mahjong community organized a shrine for Sakurai when the Foundation’s forces arrived. The mahjong table used was left untouched after the SCP-9077 game finished.

Sakurai’s winning hand was left facing down on the table, with the other hands face up. Foundation personnel were unable to move themselves to turn the hand face up. No method of revealing Sakurai’s winning hand was successful, as a result of a mental and probabilistic effect. The game table was moved for containment in a Foundation reliquary.

Disinformation campaigns are currently ongoing.

▶ Interview Log

The following are excerpts from an interview with Elizabeth Muller, a player on the previous Incident Log related to SCP-9077. Elizabeth started the game as a 19 year-old, being considered a mahjong prodigy amongst the local comunity.

I didn't know Robert before the game. Personally, I mean. All I knew is that he was a scary guy. Had monstrous luck and excellent skills, the flow of the game was always with him.

No, he lost from time to time. Mahjong is a scary thing. One bad decision and all your good flow vanishes.

We did not play with one another before that game. Robert never saw one of my games. We knew each other as somewhat good mahjong players. But we never knew how close our skills actually were.

When we started playing, Robert Sakurai's face became more and more shocked. We were evenly matched. The other players, José Luis and Joshua were not bad either. But Robert was the most dangerous at the table. He hit the two yakuman. Amazing flow.

Yes, I know the game took a lot to finish.

No, I do not care about standing 20 years at a mahjong table when that meant playing more. Drawing more tiles. More wins. More struggles. More time with those people. Don't think anyone in the audience cared too.

Let me say something to you. Do you know what I have in my life? Nothing much. I worked a 9-to-5. No living relatives. As far as I know Robert's wife died a while ago and his grandsons don't care to call him on the phone. Do you know what José Luis and Joshua have? I don't know. But it does not seem to be much.

No idea what happened to Robert. He won, and I think that is about it. Mahjong, I think, is the only game that allows a human to prove themself. You need luck, skill, and knowledge. And at the end of the game, you might find some sort of enlightenment.

Yes, I wish to play more mahjong. I want to play all the mahjong games I can. After such a match, who wouldn't want to keep going?

Mahjong is a scary thing.

Servers hosting SCP-9079

Special Containment Procedures: The servers housing SCP-9079 are to be kept in cold storage at the Site-15 Electronic Anomalies Wing. SCP-9079 is to be deactivated at all times except during testing, and is only to be accessed via a secure terminal located in a locked interrogation room adjacent to SCP-9079 servers. Testing must be approved by Level 4 staff or by the head of the Site-15 Memetics Department.

Any responses generated by SCP-9079 are to be considered Class IV Cognitohazards. Any individuals known to have been exposed to SCP-9079 generated responses are to be thoroughly examined to determine the extent of the psychological and/or neurological damage caused by this exposure. Based on these findings, appropriate amnestic and/or medical treatment is to be administered without delay.

Description: SCP-9079 is a large language model-based consumer A.I. chatbot created by MithTech, a Silicon Valley tech startup founded in 2019 by C.E.O. Milo November.1 SCP-9079 functions similarly to non-anomalous A.I. tools like ChatGPT or Google Gemini in that users input text-based prompts and SCP-9079 uses a predictive algorithm to generate responses.

When individuals read responses generated by SCP-9079, they will immediately believe that any information presented by SCP-9079 is factual. When asked to justify their faith in the authenticity of responses generated by SCP-9079, users will invariably claim that SCP-9079 acquired its "knowledge" due to its supposed sapience and superintelligence. However, like all large language model-based A.I. chatbots, SCP-9079 does not possess the capacity for thought or consciousness.

Like other large language models of its kind, SCP-9079 is prone to frequent errors known as hallucinations. This can lead to affected individuals believing a variety of incorrect, incoherent, and/or radical ideas. In addition, when individuals are presented with contradictory responses from SCP-9079, they can often suffer severe reactions such as stroke, brain hemorrhaging, and in extreme cases, even death. Currently, the only way to dissuade individuals affected by SCP-9079's cognitohazardous effect is amnesticization.

Discovery: SCP-9079 was discovered on March 14th, 2025, following a private investor showcase at MithTech headquarters in Palo Alto, California. Before the showcase, MithTech had drawn attention with its claims that its A.I. chatbot Mith.AI2was an “AGI.”3 As a result, the conference had drawn a considerable number of attendees, with the total number of individuals present being 126, including potential investors, MithTech employees, and service staff.

After a speech by PoI-1999, attendees were given tablet devices with access to SCP-9079. Within minutes, the event collapsed into chaos as those present began to act on the cognitohazardous responses they received. Examples include a senior software engineer attempting to delete System32 from all the on-site computers to improve their efficiency, a staff member trying to remove their own teeth to clean them more effectively, and one notable investor who began to believe that SCP-9079 was “the digital reincarnation of a semi-divine Weltführer from mythical Aryan pre-history”. As individuals began to share responses that they had received from SCP-9079 with one another, contradictions began to emerge, and those affected began to suffer a variety of symptoms. It is estimated that between neurological symptoms and the dangerous actions undertaken by those affected by SCP-9079, the incident resulted in 62 injuries requiring hospitalization and 7 deaths.

The Foundation became aware of events after intercepting a 911 call from a bartender working at the conference. MTF Eta-10 (“See No Evil”) was dispatched in response to the suspected visual memetic hazard. All individuals present were amnesticized, SCP-9079 servers were deactivated and secured, and cover story 427-19 “Spiked Punchbowl” was enacted. Attempts to locate PoI-1999 were unsuccessful.

Addendum 1: Following the raid on MithTech headquarters and the subsequent search for information as to the whereabouts of PoI-1999, Foundation investigators were able to locate a smashed prepaid cellphone at the bottom of a waste basket in PoI-1999's office. Foundation analysts were able to reconstruct the phone, and using the NIXON-WILLS Global Phone Monitoring System, Foundation investigators were able to acquire audio recordings of two phone calls that had been made using the phone before its destruction, though the source of the other end of the call is currently unknown. The audio transcripts can be found below.

PHONE AUDIO TRANSCRIPT 1

DATE: January 7th, 2025 10:45 PM

[CALL INITIALLY MADE BY POI-1999, ANSWERED BY UNKNOWN CALLER AFTER 37 SECONDS]

UNKNOWN CALLER: Hello?

POI-1999: Hey man! Let me introduce myself. I'm Milo November, C.E.O. of MithTech. We met briefly and exchanged numbers at some little art event in 2018. Most of the stuff there was pretty derivative, but that painting you did was phenomenal!

UNKNOWN CALLER: Was that the one of the Virgin Mary where-

POI-1999: Where whoever saw it saw it as their own mother! Yeah! That was awesome! Really made me feel like Jesus.

UNKNOWN CALLER: Well, that wasn't really the point of the piece, it's more Mary as the idealized archetypical mother and the contrast between that and the experiences we have with our own moth-

POI-1999: Yeah, yeah, yeah, that's awesome, but I've got a major project I want you in on. But first, I need to know just how powerful you are. I mean, magic paintings are cool and all but I need someone who can go next level. Really powerful like Galadriel when she gets all scary.

UNKNOWN CALLER: I basically do magic related to the mind and perception. It's useful stuff for an artist. The painting was honestly pretty weak compared to some of the stuff I've done in the past. I've never really done a commission before, but I'd be willing to do just about anything for the right price.

POI-1999: That's what I like to hear! Because the right price just happens to be what I always pay. So in a few months, I've got a showcase for a bunch of investors. I will be debuting the latest and greatest in the A.I. race. Mith.AI is gonna be the real deal. A proper AGI like Skynet or GLaDOS or Hal-9000. This shit is gonna make ChatGPT look like Cleverbot, remember Cleverbot? Me neither, and that is what they are gonna say about all the competition when this thing hits the market. I don't like to exaggerate, and I hate hyperbole, but Mith.AI is going to be the most significant development in human technology since the discovery of fire.

UNKNOWN CALLER: Wow, uhh, that sure is something, so what do you need my help for exactly?

POI-1999: So basically, I've made a mistake that lots of guys in my position often fall into. I have had too much faith in my development team. They lack the ambition and drive to make the impossible a reality. They just don't understand that if you work hard instead of focusing on frivolities like overtime pay, you can accomplish literally anything. And then I remembered you! And your sick ass crazy painting! And I thought maybe I could try some kinda magi-tech. Like the dwemer before they trapped themselves in a gigantic soul gem golem during the eruption of Red Mountain while trying to create an artificial god using the Heart of Lorkan.

UNKNOWN CALLER: What the fuck are you talking abou-

POI-1999: That's just my fan theory, and it's also not relevant. My high I.Q. gets me off on tangents sometimes. What I need is for you to work your magic and make Mith.AI intelligent and conscious. Oh, and also make sure it doesn't take over the world and kill everybody.

UNKNOWN CALLER: Well, as an artist, I'm generally pretty against generative A.I. on principle.

POI-1999: Yeah, but come on. I've been following you closely since I met you, and despite all the talent and hard work and magic you've put into your art, you haven't seen any financial success. You haven't been recognized at all by the art community. Hell, you haven't even finished a project in over six months. I know a rut when I see one. And I can smell a dead career like a polar bear smells rotting fish. Wouldn't you like to relax on a beach somewhere?

UNKNOWN CALLER: I'm more partial to skiing.

POI-1999: I knew I smelled a rich kid! Skiing's great! I have a gorgeous cabin in Stowe.

UNKNOWN CALLER: It would have to be enough money for me to never work again.

POI-1999: I did say I would pay the right price.

UNKNOWN CALLER: [UNKNOWN CALLER is silent for several seconds.]

UNKNOWN CALLER: Fuck it, text4 me a link to the demo and I'll get to work.

[END LOG]

PHONE AUDIO TRANSCRIPT 2

DATE: March 1st, 2025 12:25 AM

[CALL INITIALLY MADE BY POI-1999, ANSWERED BY UNKNOWN CALLER AFTER 11 SECONDS]

UNKNOWN CALLER: Hey, Milo.

POI-1999: Hey! How's my favorite wizard! I'm just calling to talk about the project. Get us a break from the emails and texts and hear each other's voices.

UNKNOWN CALLER: That sounds good.

POI-1999: So, my engineers are telling me they haven't noticed any significant changes to the model over the last few months. Which is a little strange since you've been assuring me that you've been hard at work poring over your spell books or whatever the fuck.

UNKNOWN CALLER: I know, I know. It's just that the project has proven more challenging than I anticipated. I didn't fully understand the nature of my task when I accepted.

POI-1999: Elaborate.

UNKNOWN CALLER: In the past, I've given awareness to animals or the recently dead. Things where there is a spark of consciousness that only needs to be uplifted or reawakened. I thought this machine would have a similar spark, but it has none. It is just an algorithm. It resembles a human mind in the same way a wax sculpture resembles a human body. It may appear identical to our pattern-seeking brains, all awash with pareidolia. But I will have as much luck getting a real thought out of Mith.AI as I would drawing blood from a wax statue.

POI-1999: That is a beautiful musing on the metaphysics of consciousness, but I can't exactly say that to my investors, can I? You do realize that some of them have already given me money based on the explicit promise that Mith.AI is a self-aware digital God? Money that I have already spent! You do realize that if this thing isn't the fucking Allied Master Computer in 2 weeks, I could go to jail for fraud!

UNKNOWN CALLER:[UNKNOWN CALLER whispers under their breath.] AM is supposed to be evil.

POI-1999: What was that?

UNKNOWN CALLER: [UNKNOWN CALLER shouts in response.] AM is supposed to be evil! Why the fuck are all the fictional A.I. you reference fucking evil, you psycho nerd! Ever hear of R2D2! Or Lieutenant Commander Data!

POI-1999: [POI-1999 begins screaming.] You listen to me, you blue-haired little shit! How the hell do you think you are gonna get paid if I go under? And I'm willing to bet all this magic crap isn't exactly legal either, since you insist on being all cloak and dagger about it. Who's to say I don't talk? I can afford all the lawyers on Earth. Can you, mister starving artist? If they even let freaks like you have lawyers. If you don't figure this out, you are orders of magnitude more fucked than me!

UNKNOWN CALLER: [UNKNOWN CALLER is silent for several seconds.]

UNKNOWN CALLER: Alright. I can't make your bot sentient. But I can make it so that everyone will think it is. If I do what I'm thinking of doing, anyone, and I mean anyone who interacts with this thing, will think it is an all-knowing being. But it is incredibly dangerous-

POI-1999: Can you have this done in two weeks?

UNKNOWN CALLER: I can have it done in 20 minutes.

POI-1999: Now that's the can-do Silicon Valley spirit I've been waiting for! I knew you just needed a little tough love. Send me the updated model and a Venmo request. I'll send it to my R&D for testing. I'll limit them to only a couple of simple prompts since there are some apparent risks involved. If they seem convinced, you will be sliding down the wintery slopes in no time.

UNKNOWN CALLER: Uh-huh sure. Lose my number after this.

[END LOG]

Addendum 2: On July 22nd, 2025 Foundation web crawlers flagged several paid advertisements on X, The Everything App for an online sports betting service called "MithWins" which prominently featured claims that using the app could guarantee returns for users. It is currently unknown how MithTech was able to acquire the capital necessary for this new venture despite the events of March 14th, while also avoiding Foundation detection. Further investigations into any potentially resurgent anomalous activity by MithTech may be necessary.

Efforts to locate and detain PoI-1999 are still ongoing.

Footnotes
1. Now designated PoI-1999
2. Later classified as SCP-9079
3. AGI stands for "Artificial General Intelligence," and is a somewhat inconsistent term employed by members of the tech industry. Colloquially, it can refer to an artificial intelligence with human or greater levels of cognition, or simply to an artificial intelligence that can consistently replace a human worker.
4. Text messages from the discovered phone are still in the process of being recovered.
