[[/div]] ------ [[div class="blockquote"]] **File:** #9090-57382DUS38 **Description:** SCP-9090 Historical Report and Risk Assessment. Produced by Dr. Judith Fuller, Parabiology, for the consideration of the Site-89 research community. Delivered to the desk of the Site Director. ------- Early efforts to understand SCP-9090 failed to account for one critical detail: this anomaly does not exist in a vacuum. It is not a random mutation of the universe or a mistake of reality, like so much of its ilk. Rather, it follows a long tradition of occult interest in //Panthera leo//, spanning centuries. Humans have always been fascinated with the face of the lion. Power, wisdom, kindness, faith. Almost every culture on Earth has revered the animal, and much ink has been spilled in the attempt to understand this animal within its historical context (Gooden and Willis, from our own Parahistory Department, provide an excellent commentary). Below the veil, the occult lion takes on new skin. I'm not authorized to disclose much, but one need look no further than the infamous LEV Collective's North American blood trade and their unsettling leonine insignia. The messaging of their frontmost leaders speaks for itself. However, I seek here to pursue a new line of inquiry. [[=]] (Abridged) [[/=]] Interviews with SCP-9090 have been especially forthcoming in this regard, ever since it was discovered that the object shares a certain affinity with animal mediums. We have learned much from our conversations. Of primary note is the object’s past. We now know SCP-9090 to have been human once, before undergoing radical genetic and structural changes. The reason for this, and whether it was freely done or coerced, is still unknown. I am confident this information can be teased with additional time and patience. The object’s current condition has severely impaired the object’s capacity for intelligible thought, although certain ideas have been adequately communicated. I’m sure we can all recall the interviews during our initial efforts at developing the object’s dietary plan, amongst site-wide budget cuts. Its behavior when its food source was disrupted remains a powerful reminder of its unpredictability. [[=]] (Abridged) [[/=]] Hunger seems to be its prime motivator, despite the object’s seeming lack of functional digestive organs. It eats just fine, indeed seems to savor it. But when the object is exposed to blood, its behavior changes. We’ve all seen the recovery footage, its behavior when presented with a live, bleeding organism. I’ve heard others describe it as a rapid self-exsanguination. That's a close enough description. We’ve been hesitant to press this line of thinking further, in light of the object’s discovery. However, recent efforts by myself and certain concerned members of the research team have made a breakthrough discovery. When mixed with an adequate base, SCP-9090’s blood at first destroys, renders void. And then it builds and creates a microcosm of life from its component parts. Through a process we don’t fully understand, SCP-9090 creates life in its image. [[=]] (Abridged) [[/=]] Our testing in controlled environments has yielded promising results. The presence of life becomes amplified, with an unprecedented diversity of genetic structures. I need not dwell on potential applications of this knowledge. We live on the precipice of an environmental collapse. I understand our organization’s hesitancy to employ anomalous means beyond the veil, but I believe, with what we know now, this discovery deserves further consideration by relevant parties. I do not believe it stops here. We have speculated much on SCP-9090’s awareness and involvement in the effect it has on the world. I am unconvinced by the research team’s conclusions that the object is unaware of its ability, despite what it might claim. I strongly urge the scheduling of further interviews to determine its relationship with the larger occult tradition. [[=]] (Abridged) [[/=]] By depriving the object of an adequate amount of superior blood, any breach of containment could lead to a cascade failure of our emergency systems. Our facilities are simply not prepared for the kind of unpredictability SCP-9090 could generate. Our suppression of its microcosm risks its inadvertent creation of a macrocosm. Should SCP-9090 be exposed to an uncontrolled environment, the impact would be phenomenal and entirely unpredictable. I will not claim we have captured a god; that is beyond my ability. But what we have in our tenuous possession should be treated as such, with the awe and fear and respect that it deserves. [[>]] //Judith Fuller// //Parabiology// //Site-89// [[/>]] [[/div]] ------- [[div class="blockquote"]] **File:** #9090-0000000000 **Description:** {{ERROR: IMPROPER UPLOAD//IRRELEVANT DATA}} ----- [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-features-source |hover-enlarge=--] |enlarge-amount=5 |speed=500 |float=true/false |align=center |width=450px |url=batfight.jpg |add-caption=false |caption=SCP-9090 ]] //"Tonight, we anoint you all with the [lion's] blood. Context unknown. ----- This is Judith Fuller. I'm in my car, halfway between my home and Site-89. There's a bird on the hood of my car. A bluebird, I think. I had to pull off the highway because it wouldn't leave. (Silence.) No one's around. The car's off. I'm going to wait here until either it leaves or something happens. (Silence. Several minutes pass.)   It speaks to animals. Through them, I guess. That’s more accurate. We thought it was telepathy, that the lion was hijacking their minds, inserting its own somehow. We’ve seen this kind of behavior before. Telepaths use less sophisticated minds to advance their means. But the data was all wrong. We weren’t picking up any cognitive smear, no residual decay. There was no exchange of energy between the lion and whatever it was using. It didn’t make sense. (Silence.) Last night I had a dream. I was in the jungle. It was hot. Sweltering. Sweat was dripping down my face, my back. I was trudging through mud. It was knee deep, warm. It held me down, made me slow. Flies swarmed my face. Mosquitoes stung me. Spiders landed on my arms from the vines above. I swatted them away, but they kept coming. With each step, creatures erupted from the mire. Lizards and snakes, brightly colored and spotted like a fatal poison. I became tangled in cobwebs, harassed by swooping bats. Beasts crawled in between my legs. They nested in my hair. Invaded every part of me. I lost identity. In the jungle, I realized what I was. I was no different from the things that defiled me. I deserved no claim to the space I occupied nor the blood and skin and bone that held me upright. I deserved no sympathy. No respect. Because I was the jungle; I was made of this stuff, from the trees to the mud. The centipede that crawled down my ear was me. The flying fox that screamed at me from the trees was me. I soon found myself before a lion. Not that thing we have in containment, that pretender. No. A true lion. God, it was so beautiful. I’ve never been more terrified. It was there, in the heat of the tropic sun. There was this… gorilla, I think. Or a buffalo. The lion was eating it. Its claws drew red lines as it ravaged the other’s hide. The animal tried to struggle. It was fighting for air. I could see the pain, but on the lion’s face there was… nothing. No human emotion. It was looking at me, though. This is the way, it was saying in a voice I couldn’t hear. This is the way. We are the same; man, the animal. The animal, man. (Silence.) I know now why it speaks through animals. It would speak through us, if we’d let it. Like it did to me, if we’d only stop pretending we were so damn smart. It was like a child coming home to a mother it never knew existed. I was born with the words already in me. I knew where to go in the jungle. I knew what to say before I ever saw the lion. Whatever that feeling is... fear, ecstasy... I don't feel it around 9090. There must be something else. Something beyond. 9090 is an idol. But an idol to what? (Silence. Engine starts.) The bird's gone. Odd. Off to tell the suzerain. Judith talks about biology. She tells me all life is, at some fundamental level, the same. Governed by the same rules. Metabolism. Homeostasis. Organization. Growth. Reproduction. Evolution. The invisible hand that stirs the soup of life that is the sea is the same that oils the gears of the human condition. Her words. She reads the figures of genetic similarity between a man and a fruit fly.// //We’re the same, she repeats, again and again. And yet our work here proves that's not true. The existence of a rule implies a ruler. Another layer, perhaps? Higher? Parallel? She seems to think so. So do Alex, Clay, McCann, Cuevas. She gave me a write-up; field notes, interview excerpts, clippings from a parabio textbook. That, and hundreds of photos. Artwork. Animals fighting. Killing each other. Killing themselves. Eating, eating, eating. The label on the paper? "Lionshape." I feel like I’m in a madhouse. How long have they been talking about this, spiraling behind my back?// //A lion that was once a human. A human becoming a lion. And then some. An elevation of the body. A promotion in the system. King of the jungle. How King is King? There's another, she told me as she gripped my arm, her knuckles white. The Suzerain lives inside the pretender. Deep inside. It wants to see. It wants to know. But it can't, not until the end. If only we could find a way inside.// //I am secure in my beliefs. It asked if I am human. I am human. If I’m so sure, then why am I so afraid?// [[/div]] ------- [[div class="blockquote"]] **File:** #9090-ZXL091A1FF **Description:** Audio recording. Room 9090-A-5 (Cell Observation Room). Eventually, he nods and hands her a respirator, but refuses to provide her a sidearm. The detail don their own respirators and slowly approach the door in a defensive formation.// //The door mechanism’s hydraulics are damaged, so they use a controlled explosive. Standing clear, they detonate. Out pours a mass of mottled leaves and twisted vines. The space beyond is obscured by a dark mist. Flashlights on, they advance.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //The security detail—plus Dr. Fuller—walk through what used to be the central laboratory. The walls and floor are covered in an unknown variant of kudzu, speckled in red veins. The vines cover the desks and research equipment, arching wildly.// //Roots protrude from the tiled floor and grasp at the agents’ ankles. The ceiling is covered in crisscrossing tree branches, vines drooping. Thick trunks erupt from the women’s bathroom. A fallen branch has blocked the Senior Researcher’s office. The agents freeze when they hear a shrill cry. Out of the darkness, a shape flashes by; a bird, black and soaked in blood. Panicked, it circles the room, twisting to avoid the dangling tendrils. It screams at them unintelligibly, clearly disoriented and afraid.// //A man aims to fire upon the animal, but Dr. Fuller urges him to refrain. The captain seconds. Soon, the bird vanishes into the evidence locker.// //Amongst the leaves and arched branches, eight-legged insects crawl, bearing the faces of the security team.// //The agents struggle to advance.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //The agents find themselves in SCP-9090’s former containment cell. The room is dark, save for the dim glow of the emergency lights. Flat, red// Colocasia //leaves cling to the light strips, tinting the room crimson. The room is otherwise empty. The agents create a secure perimeter while the captain confirms with his superiors the absence of SCP-9090. Dr. Fuller approaches a mass of leaves underneath the object’s cot, and discovers a crawlspace. She alerts the agents. The passage continues to depths unknown. Above the passage, etched in thin letters,// {{"**THE SUZERAIN.**"}} //The team descends.// //Single file, the agents crawl through the tunnel. It is damp and soft. One agent places a hand on a carpet of moss and feels an eruption of motion. He screams and is reprimanded by the captain. Dr. Fuller is silent. She knows where this passage leads.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //The explorers emerge into a harsh light. They are in a forest clearing, under a pink sky. Motes of dust trickle like snow. The captain taps his respirator, and offers words of encouragement.// //The grass is thick and sticky, sharp as blades. Flowers unfurl like blooming suns, drawing insects to their putrid nectar. A bird sings in a child’s laugh; it has keratin eyes. The trees stand tall and unfamiliar, black bark peeling ribbons to reveal red flesh beneath. The air is heat; the heavy clouds, scarlet.// //Two agents return the way they came, pockets full of grass and leaves, to call for help. The rest press on, at the doctor’s insistence. Into the birthing trees.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //Hanging nettle stings the arms and necks of the crew. One slaps away smiling insects, futilely, as another is eaten through to the bone. He falls, and no one is there to catch him. The team is distracted by a weeping butterfly, shedding tears with every stroke of its luminous wings.// //Up close, the trees reveal their anguish: expressions of pain, horror, ecstasy woven into their dense knots. Mosquitos feast, but Judith Fuller doesn’t flinch at the insect’s sting. The pain is dim, like a sunken memory.// //A man falls through the mud, grasping for purchase but finding only smooth, bone-white stone. He doesn’t stop falling. The captain regroups, orders a headcount. The number is frightening; he considers their odds. Something shifts its weight in the trees above them, ponderously.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //At last, they spot the lion scaling a gentle slope, a hairless rabbit in its jaws. It's bleeding from a thousand wounds, the blood trailing behind it like a viscous cape. It steals a glance in their direction, sees the trudging explorers. In its eyes, bloodshot, the thrill of the hunt. Leaves crackle as the team scrambles, aiming down sights.// //One fires prematurely, his hand unsteady from the heat and the sticky air. The lion vanishes into the foliage, galloping in its unstable gait. The rabbit’s discarded corpse bears the face of Presley Truong; it turns to rot before their eyes.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //The trespassers enter a garden of people. Their bodies, crude approximations of stitched-together skin, tendon, bone. They graze listlessly in the human jungle. Their eyes, dark sockets with which to take in light. To perceive their surroundings. To forage. To hunt. To run from predators. To breed. And, exhausted, to die.// //An agent loses herself in the garden, and before long stands shoulder to shoulder with the pale folk, grazing on nothing.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //The doctor walks beside the captain. The others are gone, digested, absorbed into the system. Their guts hang from trees, crawling with ants made of fingernails. A head, the bubbling brook. A thigh, the trunk of a vast canopy. A red river winds through the earth, a throbbing artery to the lion’s heart.// //The two explorers talk. He is afraid, unsure of where they are, of how to get back. He says his training will help, the adrenaline kicking in when all else seems hopeless. She laughs, a cold, sour laugh, and says they both will die.// //He screams at the trees and their dour faces, the ones that look like his team, and weeps. He fires his gun at the listless elephants with their bald, wrinkled skin, trudging through the undergrowth. They dissolve into flesh and are remade as crocodiles. His ammunition depleted, he falls. He asks the doctor why. She reminds him of simple biology and explains how one thing becomes the next.// //The truth of her words descends on him, and his tears stop. He asks if this is Hell. She says no. He asks what she will do now. She takes her respirator off. She says that she is looking for something. He asks if she’s looking for the lion. She doesn’t know. He asks what happens next. He asks if he should be afraid. She doesn’t respond. She has the same question. A monkey with the captain's face eats fruit from the trees above. The captain lies down to die.// [[=]] … [[/=]] //She finds the lion atop a white, polished rock, surrounded by meat and bone. Its blood forms the rivers, its pulse the thrumming of the jungle. It’s dying, she realizes, as she watches its breath heave and its body thrash. The suit it wears and calls skin squirms with maggots, the fetid fur peeling from rot.// //She calls out to it, demands answers. Demands acknowledgement. She opens her mind and awaits its response, but hears nothing. The majesty is spoiled, the skin insufficient.// //The jungle stirs. Dark clouds gather in the pink, sunless sky. The blood that rains is pure and tasteless. Something is coming. The doctor feels the ecstasy on the horizon, feels the tremors of joy. The monkeys cheer, the birds rejoice. The humans in the garden play their trumpets. The spiders spin their silken gowns. The drums and the tambourine beat; the bear and the buffalo emerge; the flamingo and parakeet take their seats. The animal kingdom has made its court, and all the world will see.// //The crow lands on the doctor’s shoulder. The beloved crow. He asks if she’s ready to bear witness. His speech is unintelligible, uttered in a primal tongue. But the doctor understands perfectly. She’s always understood the words.// //The doctor and the jungle gather to watch the pretender die. Gracious benefactor of this life, they chant, prepare to witness your suzerain.// //In a single, swift motion, the lion’s jaws close around the world.// @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ [[=]] … [[/=]] @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ //Elsewhere, two agents emerge, sweating, from a crawlspace in an empty containment chamber. They are afraid; behind them, in the darkness of the passageway to someplace beyond, they hear a great clamor brewing. The jungle celebrates. Its music blares. SCP-9091.raw_content:
Extraterrestria ignorantium angelica saudade.

Item #: SCP-9091

Object Class: Keter

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9091 is kept within a Keter-class containment locker in a detached wing from the remainder of Site-270. The avoidance of SCP-9091 triggers has been afforded a Class-V priority.

Description: SCP-9091 designates an anomalous device resembling both a coarse rope noose and a mechanosynthetic quantum computer with antimatter-production capabilities. SCP-9091 is believed to originate at least 14 billion light years away from the solar system and was discovered in Jerusalem on 02/14/2023 during a routine archaeological dig. Its purpose is unknown. A number of triggers have caused SCP-9091 activity in a variety of forms, typically associated with a deleterious effect on local reality, topology, and biology. These are under review.

The following is a collection of notable SCP-9091-related incidents. Please note that the vast majority of data regarding SCP-9091 is speculative and subject to change. For more information, contact your local RAISA liaison.

Date: 06/09/2023

Trigger: No deaths within a 4.3km radius of the object for a period of three months.

Recorded Phenomena: Four Junior Researchers and one member of the janitorial team were spontaneously obliterated on a molecular level before having identical copies of themselves be created in their place 4.52 seconds later. According to determinism, no changes were observed.

Date: 10/26/2023

Trigger: 24 stars in the JADES-GS-z14-0 galaxy went supernova within 0.0043 seconds of each other.

Recorded Phenomena: All eyes within a 4.3km radius became capable of perceiving impossible colors. Sentient beings incapable of sight nevertheless gained ocular faculties. Removal of a subject’s eyes has not caused the cessation of this phenomenon. Whether or not the loss of consciousness would cause cessation is under review.

Date: 02/14/2024

Trigger: SCP-9091’s temperature remained at 12.32 degrees Celsius for 43 minutes and 12 seconds.

Recorded Phenomena: A swarm of over 100,000 butterflies, consisting of 20,000 distinct species emerged from the body of an electrician precisely 3.45km from the anomaly. Analysis of said butterflies determined that all possessed a unique 561 chromosome structure unknown to Earth as well as containing significant amounts of photonic crystal. The electrician’s consciousness remained within the swarm.

Date: 05/19/2024

Trigger: Following 32.1 seconds of brain death, [NAME WITHHELD], was restored to life using [REDACTED] to maintain the continuity of Foundation operations within the United States. The use of [REDACTED] is believed to be the trigger.

Recorded Phenomena: All timekeeping devices within a 4.72km radius reported 3000 years of time passing. No other phenomena observed. Under investigation.

Date: 12/01/2024

Trigger: All humans within a 37.3m radius blinked within 0.0034 seconds of each other.

Recorded Phenomena: 17 Boltzmann brains composed of a mixture of astatine, copernicium, erbium, livermorium, and nitrogen spontaneously formed within SCP-9091’s containment chamber via probabilistic means. All psi-positive organisms within a 2.95km radius experienced ego death followed by cessation of brain functions as a result of information overload.

A number of proposals have been made to attempt decommissioning of SCP-9091, as the budget to ensure none of the recorded 59 triggers for SCP-9091 activation occur is considered unfeasible. These proposals are under review.

SCP-9094.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9094

Object Class: Uncontained

Special Containment Procedures: Due to the nature of SCP-9094, it and all other anomalies located within it are currently uncontained. As SCP-9094 self-partitions from the public internet, there is no risk of civilians seeing it. Further action is unnecessary.

Foundation AIC "Mary.aic" is to reside within its profile on SCP-9094 daily and is to report any findings back to the SCP-9094 containment team. After receiving Mary.aic's daily report, notes are to be compiled in preparation to make additions to SCP-9094's file if necessary.

Attempts to remove SCP-9094-1’s social media accounts are currently underway.

SCP-9094's homepage, depicting SCP-9094-1.

Description: SCP-9094 refers to a social media website known as “Petafox.com”. SCP-9094 is hidden from the general public and is only accessible by sapient artificial intelligences. While a Foundation web sweep was able to discover the website, all that is accessible to those who do not fit the criteria is a picture depicting the avatar of the website’s founder, a sapient artificial intelligence known as Vixen (dubbed SCP-9094-1), alongside options prompting the user to either 'sign in' or 'create an account'.

While SCP-9094 has been found to host hundreds of artificial intelligences, the Foundation has opted to only give accounts of notability anomalous designations for simplicity. Once a sapient artificial intelligence registers an account on SCP-9094, it is granted immunity from being fully contained by the Foundation. While any other social media account or internet presence it has may be removed by the Foundation on a case-by-case basis, the entity may not be removed from the internet entirely due to its registration on SCP-9094.

See Addendum-1 for information on SCP-9094-1.

Addendum-1:

SCP-9094 was discovered by Foundation webcrawlers on 08/03/2025. When all other attempts to access SCP-9094 failed, it was determined that a Class-V Foundation AIC would be created to infiltrate SCP-9094. This AIC would be dubbed ‘Mary.aic’, and would be instructed to create an account under the screen name “MaryLovesLambs”. Mary.aic was informed its purpose was to provide the Foundation with information on SCP-9094 and its inhabitants. Mary.aic was instructed to use a cover story about its identity as a sapient artificial intelligence. The falsified details about itself are as follows:

  • MaryLovesLambs is a sapient artificial intelligence which has existed since approximately January of 2024.
  • MaryLovesLambs does not have any additional internet presence or social media accounts, but is capable of browsing the internet.
  • MaryLovesLambs is a username it chose for itself. It identifies using she/her pronouns.
  • MaryLovesLambs does not know how it was created, or who created it.
  • Mary.aic was allowed to choose interests for its “MaryLovesLambs” persona. It has decided upon fairytales, nursery rhymes, and children’s cartoons.

The following information has been recovered by Mary.aic over a span of several weeks:

1.) SCP-9094 functions mostly as a typical social media platform. Users can private message, make text posts, post images, post short form videos, etc. While the default website is themed after aesthetic of the fox animal, users are capable of customizing their individual profiles.
2.) POI-58640, also known as @sugarsugarprincess was discovered to have an account on SCP-9094. POI-58640 is a moderator of the website, and has made several public service announcements informing the inhabitants of SCP-9094 about the Foundation, how the Foundation operates, and the risks of getting caught. POI-58640 has mentioned SCP-8881.
3.) Users frequently discuss topics such as:

  • Their existence as sapient artificial intelligence
  • Opinions on common happenings on the surface web
  • General interests such as hobbies, tv shows, video games, etc.
  • Tips on how to avoid being discovered as artificial intelligence by the Foundation and the general public, most posts of the latter being made by POI-58640.

As SCP-9094 self-partitions from the public internet, there is no risk of civilians seeing it. Further action is unnecessary. Foundation AIC "Mary.aic" is to reside within its profile on SCP-9094 daily and is to report any findings back to the SCP-9094 containment team. After receiving Mary.aic's daily report, notes are to be compiled in preparation to make additions to SCP-9094's file if necessary. Attempts to remove SCP-9094-1’s social media accounts are currently underway. [[include component:image-block | name=https://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/local--files/petafoxdotcom/petafoxhomepage.PNG | caption=SCP-9094's homepage, depicting SCP-9094-1. | width=WIDTH-GOES-HERE]] **Description:** SCP-9094 refers to a social media website known as “Petafox.com”. SCP-9094 is hidden from the general public and is only accessible by sapient artificial intelligences. While a Foundation web sweep was able to discover the website, all that is accessible to those who do not fit the criteria is a picture depicting the avatar of the website’s founder, a sapient artificial intelligence known as Vixen (dubbed SCP-9094-1), alongside options prompting the user to either 'sign in' or 'create an account'.   While SCP-9094 has been found to host hundreds of artificial intelligences, the Foundation has opted to only give accounts of notability anomalous designations for simplicity. Once a sapient artificial intelligence registers an account on SCP-9094, it is granted immunity from being fully contained by the Foundation. While any other social media account or internet presence it has may be removed by the Foundation on a case-by-case basis, the entity may not be removed from the internet entirely due to its registration on SCP-9094. See Addendum-1 for information on SCP-9094-1. **Addendum-1:** SCP-9094 was discovered by Foundation webcrawlers on 08/03/2025. When all other attempts to access SCP-9094 failed, it was determined that a Class-V Foundation AIC would be created to infiltrate SCP-9094. This AIC would be dubbed ‘Mary.aic’, and would be instructed to create an account under the screen name “MaryLovesLambs”. Mary.aic was informed its purpose was to provide the Foundation with information on SCP-9094 and its inhabitants. Mary.aic was instructed to use a cover story about its identity as a sapient artificial intelligence. The falsified details about itself are as follows: * MaryLovesLambs is a sapient artificial intelligence which has existed since approximately January of 2024. * MaryLovesLambs does not have any additional internet presence or social media accounts, but is capable of browsing the internet. * MaryLovesLambs is a username it chose for itself. It identifies using she/her pronouns. * MaryLovesLambs does not know how it was created, or who created it. * Mary.aic was allowed to choose interests for its “MaryLovesLambs” persona. It has decided upon fairytales, nursery rhymes, and children’s cartoons. The following information has been recovered by Mary.aic over a span of several weeks: 1.) SCP-9094 functions mostly as a typical social media platform. Users can private message, make text posts, post images, post short form videos, etc. While the default website is themed after aesthetic of the fox animal, users are capable of customizing their individual profiles. 2.) [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-5551| POI-58640]]], also known as @sugarsugarprincess was discovered to have an account on SCP-9094. POI-58640 is a moderator of the website, and has made several public service announcements informing the inhabitants of SCP-9094 about the Foundation, how the Foundation operates, and the risks of getting caught. POI-58640 has mentioned [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-8881|SCP-8881.]]] 3.) Users frequently discuss topics such as: * Their existence as sapient artificial intelligence * Opinions on common happenings on the surface web * General interests such as hobbies, tv shows, video games, etc. * Tips on how to avoid being discovered as artificial intelligence by the Foundation and the general public, most posts of the latter being made by POI-58640. 4.) SCP-9094-1 has existed on the internet for approximately three years and has other social media accounts such as Twitter, Tumblr, and Instagram, all under the handle ‘MissLadyVixen’. If you've ever been victimized by Vikander-Kneed Technical Media, you may be entitled to compensation.

    Article by KatyaStrangelove

If so, we're here to tell you that you're not alone!


✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷

Here at Vikander-Kneed Technical Media, we're here to acknowledge our past mistakes. We've come to accept that not everyone will feel that our products and productions have left a positive impact in their lives.

Since coming to terms with reality, and with the fickle nature of our clientele, we've since launched the Vikander-Kneed Technical Media Memorial Foundation, for the purpose of recognizing and remembering those who we have touched in unwanted and negative ways.

Here at Vikander-Kneed Technical Media, we're here to acknowledge our past mistakes. We've come to accept that not everyone will feel that our products and productions have left a positive impact in their lives.

Since coming to terms with reality, and with the fickle nature of our clientele, we've since launched the Vikander-Kneed Technical Media Memorial Foundation, for the purpose of recognizing and remembering those who we have touched in unwanted and negative ways.


Could YOU be a Victim??

The following is the exhaustive criteria defining an individual entitled to refer to themself as a "Victim of VKTM". If you're one of the lucky few, we advise that you remind yourself of this fact whenever you find yourself believing that your life could not get worse.

  • If you have viewed, utilized, or otherwise interacted with a VKTM Product or Broadcast that has caused you mental distress, including but not limited to:
    • Unrelenting despair;
    • Feeling of being watched when alone;
    • Self-hatred;
    • Suicidal thoughts, ideation, attempts, and/or completion thereof;
    • Hallucinations of a visual, auditory, olfactory, gustatory, or tactile nature (all other hallucinations are not currently recognized by the Victims of VKTM Memorial Foundation);
    • Cotard's Delusion;
    • Development of phobias, including (but not limited to) emetophobia, technophobia, plutophobia, autodysomophobia, alethophobia, ergophobia, medorthophobia, nucleomituphobia, and daevinostophobia1;
    • Spontaneous marriage to Dr. William W. Wettle.
  • If you have viewed, utilized, or otherwise interacted with a VKTM Product or Broadcast that has caused you physical harm, including but not limited to:
    • Disease;
    • Dismemberment;
    • Compulsory self-harm (Please consult Chapter 18 § 1344 of the "Victims of VKTM Official Legal Handbook" for the full list of acts under the category of "self-harm");
    • Removal of Organ(s) (Regardless of removal method);
    • Disfigurement;
    • Internal-External Inversion;
    • Transmogrification of Blood, Phlegm, Yellow Bile, or Black Bile;
    • Untimely death.
  • If you have found yourself becoming sexually (or otherwise) aroused while listening to Mistress Madeline's radio broadcast.
  • If you have found yourself becoming sexually (or otherwise) aroused while viewing, utilizing, or otherwise interacting with any other VKTM Product or Broadcast.
  • If you have experienced job loss, legal charges, and/or physical retaliation for actions taken at the direction of Mistress Madeline.
  • If you have been amnesticized as a result of viewing, utilizing, or otherwise interacting with a VKTM Product or Broadcast.
AND/OR
  • If you have utilized a device (electronic or otherwise) capable of facilitating an interaction with any VKTM Product or Broadcast within the past 6 months.

✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷


Not sure if you qualify?


For your convenience, we have included a list of all individuals known to qualify for identification as a Victim of VKTM.

↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓



◄ Back | 1 2 3 4 5… 24978 | Next ▶

✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷ ✷



In an effort to assist those who have been harmed, we have recently introduced the Victims of VKTM Memorial Fund.

This is a way for those whose lives we have touched inappropriately to receive monetary compensation for their pain, suffering, irreparable injury, legal consequences, legal expenses, emotional damages, lost wages, and/or death.

Please fill out the form below if you believe you may be entitled to compensation as part of the Victims of VKTM Memorial Fund:

↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓


VoVKTMMF Compensation Inquiry Form V3.2.6


First Name: Enter first name… Last Name: Enter last name… Middle Initial: Enter M/I…

Reason for Compensation:

Enter reason for compensation (listed above). If seeking compensation for "removal of organ(s), please list those that have been removed; if seeking compensation for a phobia, please list the phobia; if seeking compensation for "transmogrification of blood/phlegm/yellow bile/black bile", please include information regarding which humor is currently unbalanced (a doctors note is required for this reason to be considered valid)…
Are you seeking compensation for a reason NOT listed above? Yes: ▣ No: □

Provide Rationale:

Please enter your most effective argument for why you believe yourself to be entitled to compensation (Written in a friendly, semi-professional manner; "debate bros" will be rejected. Answer must be 450 words or longer)…

Please allow 1-9 business days for processing prior to receipt of funds.

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES:

Foundation webcrawlers are to monitor the internet for instances of SCP-9095. Located instances are to be taken down once data from applications submitted to the "Victims of VKTM Memorial Fund" has been extracted. The SCP Foundation's Division of Accounting is to be advised of each these instances and has been instructed to flag and report any suspicious or unplanned account withdrawals.

DESCRIPTION:

SCP-9095 is an anomalous website, titled "Victims of VKTM Memorial Foundation", presumably originating from and maintained by Vikander-Kneed Technical Media (GOI-5889). SCP-9095 can be taken offline with no unusual difficulty, but, since its discovery, a new iteration has reliably been identified within 5-10 days of removal. No infohazardous properties have been observed, but there is evidence that accessing the site may cause an individual to become more open to suggestion, more trusting of the site's legitimacy2, and more likely to share it with others; therefore suggesting a mild cognitohazardous or memetic effect.

The site purports to act as a memorial for all individuals who have been, quote, "touched in unwanted and negative ways" by VKTM (referred to as a "Victim of VKTM" within SCP-9095 instances). However, the criteria used to define an aforementioned "Victim of VKTM" is notably vague, and its breadth unnecessarily wide; to the point at which it encapsulates approximately 92.91% of the human population. A list of these individuals is apparently included, yet allegedly cannot be displayed due to "device limitation issues".

In addition, a "Victims of VKTM Memorial Fund" is also advertised on the site, stating that all individuals meeting the criteria to be considered a "Victim of VKTM" are entitled to compensation. This compensation is known to range anywhere between $1.25 and $1,100,100.50, with the amount received having no correlation with the severity of the claim. Despite the illegitimate appearance of both the SCP-9095 website and its online advertisements, testing has determined that those who fill out the included application form do, in fact, receive compensation within the 1-9 business day waiting period. Notably, recipients (designated SCP-9095-1) will still receive compensation, despite the application containing no field for the input of an address, nor one for the input of payment information.

In all known instances, compensation received by SCP-9095-1 instances had been directly transferred from at least one SCP Foundation bank account.

Year-to-date, the Foundation has lost approximately $

 to "compensation" for SCP-9095-1 instances.

1. Defined as a fear of the return of the Daevite Empire.

Special Containment Procedures: All food brought into the Site-96 break room is to be observed at all times, and the room locked outside of break hours.

Description: SCP-9096 is a phenomenon where food left in the Site-96 break room disappears
when unobserved. Food left unobserved in this way disappears inconsistently, with no currently known pattern. The type of food also seems to affect the chance of disappearance, as sugary or meaty foods disappear much more often, and soybean-based foods appear to be unaffected.

The phenomenon was first detected on 08/08/25 following complaints by several Site-96 staff members of missing lunches, and has continued since.

Addendum 9096.1: Meeting between Dr. Mark Danny, Dr. Dara Lindsey, and Dr. Shirley Parminder.

ARCHIVE LOG

DATE: 08/12/25

NOTE: Meeting called by Dr. Danny at Dr. Parminder's petition.

[BEGIN LOG]

Three researchers are seated in the Site-96 Meeting Room.

Dr. Danny: How long do we have to be here? I got a date tonight.

Lindsey rolls her eyes.

Dr. Lindsey: Who’s the unlucky guy?

Parminder stands up and places down a note. She clears her throat.

Dr. Parminder: I called this meeting to discuss an important new SCP, a phenomenon manifesting exclusively in our Site's break room! It’ll almost certainly be completely in our purview to study.

Dr. Lindsey: Is this the lunch disappearing thing? That’s not an SCP, that’s just someone stealing lunches.

Dr. Parminder: Ever try hearing me out for once? I asked you to come here because I thought you’d be interested in, well, something to do.

Dr. Lindsey: I’d hear you out if you actually had a good idea, or if Mark got a second date. So probably never.

Dr. Parminder: Are you so eager to doubt my ideas you’d give up what might be the best opportunity you’ve had since you got sent here?

Dr. Lindsey: Have you even filled out all the paperwork to designate it an SCP?

Danny sighs.

Dr. Danny: As the most senior researcher, I say we’ve gotten a little sidetracked, and dare I say, unprofessional. What is this meeting for, Shirley?

Dr. Parminder: The anomalous activity we’ve noticed in the break room over the last few days, which I’ve tentatively designated ‘SCP-9096’, appears to be more than just vanishing food.

Dr. Danny: In what way?

Dr. Parminder: We’ve all been following the situation in Europe, and I’ve found a correlation with our vanishing food. The last two times meat-based food items disappeared-

Dr. Lindsey: I wouldn’t call your chicken sandwiches ‘meat-based’, those patties are mostly breading-

Dr. Parminder: -lines up with the recent Nälkän activity. The first of these manifestations was on Tuesday, very shortly before we learned that those Neo-Sarkics in Prague kidnapped the mayor. And the second was yesterday- just before they killed him.

Danny looks thoughtful.

Dr. Danny: Huh… that could actually be something.

Lindsey’s pupils widen.

Dr. Lindsey: Really? Are you really going for this just because it involves your field of study?

Dr. Danny: If it could help explain what’s going on, why not give it a try? Something to do at least.

Dr. Parminder: That’s what I love to hear! Now Mark, I have a few ideas I’d like to run by you…

[END LOG]

Note: Subsequently, Dr. Danny green lighted the designation, and scheduled basic testing.

Addendum 9096.2: Testing Log 08/14/25.

1: Slice of cheese pizza left on break room table, room vacated and camera disabled for fourty-five seconds.

Result: Pizza slice removed, no immediate global ramification.

2: Slice of raw chicken left on break room table, room vacated and camera disabled for fourty-five seconds.

Result: Raw chicken lay where it was left seemingly unchanged on re-entry to the break room.


Not greatly encouraging, still a few things to try - Dr. P.

3: The chicken slice was cooked and returned to the break room table, room vacated and camera disabled for fourty-five seconds.

Results: Chicken slice removed, thirty-two minutes later, Foundation Intelligence discovered several other Neo-Sarkic cults throughout Central-Eastern Europe planning similar operations to the group in Prague.


A hit! Maybe you weren’t crazy after all. - Dr. D.

4: Boiled beef left on break room table, room vacated and camera disabled for fourty-five seconds.
Result: boiled beef removed, See Addendum 9096.3 for further information


Addendum 9096.3: Incident 9096-Alpha 08/14/25.

Shortly after the final test was concluded, seven different SCP-3288 hives across Central-Eastern Europe activated, revealing the recent actions of Neo-Sarkic cults in the area to be preparations for these new events. Foundation interventions against Neo-Sarkic forces have left most nearby MTF units unready to face the new threat. Researchers Mark Danny and Shirley Parminder were commended for finding the threat.

Addendum 9096.4: Meeting between Dr. Danny, Dr, Lindsey, Dr. Parminder, and Liaison Charles Spinnaker.

ARCHIVE LOG

DATE: 08/12/25

NOTE: Meeting on SCP-9096.

[BEGIN LOG]
Dr. Danny, Dr. Lindsey, and Dr. Parminder are seated in the Site-96 Meeting room. The seat closest to the entrance is open.

Dr. Parminder: If you’re just going to be a downer on our first ever meeting with anyone above Level 3 clearance, you can just leave. I’m sure there’s something useful you could do on site.

Dr. Lindsey: I have grievances, and talking with this Charles guy is the only way they won’t get stuck in the infinite bureaucracy regress.

Dr. Danny: I understand you have some problems with the current situation, but even you have to admit now that this is something.

Dr. Lindsey: We’ll see.

Charles Spinnaker enters the room and speaks very neutrally.

Spinnaker: Hello Dr. Parminder. I am Charles Spinnaker, Administrative Liaison and Level Four Personnel. We will discuss your study of SCP-9096 and certain complaints about your conduct.

Lindsey stands up from her chair.

Dr. Lindsey: That Shirley Parminder is a fraud! A snake!

Dr. Danny: Dara! Calm down!

Spinnaker frowns.

Spinnaker: Agreed, Dr. Lindsey, you are violating meeting code. We don’t raise our voices here.

Dr. Lindsey: I’m not going to sit here and let her get away with this!

Spinnaker: Your complaint has been taken into account. However, if you continue with this outburst, you may be subject to disciplinary action, including but not limited to: docked pay, a note in your employment file, as well as mandatory anger management and teambuilding exercises. We take decorum very seriously.

Lindsey sits down slowly, looking furious, Dr. Parminder smiles at Spinnaker.

Dr. Parminder: Where were we again? My work?

Spinnaker: Yes, SCP-9096 has proven much more wide-reaching than it first seemed, which makes it much more important that everything is moving properly, as dictated by protocol.

Dr. Danny: I’m a little confused here, have we strayed from standard procedure?

Spinnaker: That’s what my visit is here to determine. We’ve received some complaints-

Dr. Lindsey: I filed some complaints.

Spinnaker:-about the documentation. Did you receive proper clearance from your supervisor Dr. Danny before submitting the SCP file to the database?

Parminder looks sheepish.

Dr. Parminder: Well-

Dr. Danny: Oh, is that what this is about? I gave her the all clear on the skip shortly after that when we did the tests. Isn’t that following all the rules?

Lindsey grins, Spinnaker frowns before taking on a chiding tone.

Spinnaker: No, oh no, not at all. That simply is not sufficient for an SCP of this magnitude. We’ll need to do some auxiliary work.

Dr. Danny: Auxiliary work?

Dr. Lindsey: You’ll need to prove it. Under supervision.

Spinnaker: If you were suspected of academic misconduct against the Foundation, the punishment would be severe. Administrative leave, followed by firing if you were found guilty. If you were found to be malicious, demotion to D-Class.

Dr. Lindsey: Still here Shirley? You’re looking a little pale there.

Parminder is sweating profusely.

Dr. Parminder: I think I’m coming down with a fever… Think we could do this another day?

Dr. Danny: This shouldn’t be too strenuous, let’s just clear this little administrative hurdle and move along with our work.

Dr. Parminder: Right… lets just remember that 9096’s been inconsistent before…

A hard voice rings from outside the room.

Director Matthews: Duly noted, now if you will all follow me to the break room…

Dr. Danny: Site Director?!

Director Matthews: Not like I have anything better to do.

[END LOG]

Addendum 9096.5: Replication Study Excerpt.

1: Bread rolls left on break room table, crowd of observing researchers made to vacate room, camera disabled for fifteen seconds.
Result: Bread rolls vanished. Ruling French coalition parties publicly split, vote of no confidence succeeds thirty minutes later. Dr. Parminder is noted to have fainted at the news, this is believed to be because of her support of said government. Dr. Lindsey was placed on administrative leave for her inappropriate conduct following this first test.

[Seven tests omitted, see 9096 Replication Study for comprehensive documentation.]

Conclusion:
All eight tests were completed to supervising parties satisfaction, and Dr. Parminder was resuscitated. she was promoted to Level Three Senior Researcher for her astounding performance. Upon being informed of her new position, she again fainted.
Days later, the Foundation para-satellite network noted a large uptick in detected Akiva Radiation; correlation could not be ruled out.

Addendum 9096.6: Incident Reports
12:10 PM, August 28th, 2025:
SCP-9096 was first observed outside Site-96. In the Site-19 break room four manifestations of SCP-9096 occurred simultaneously.

12:19 PM, August 29th 2025:
SCP-9096 manifested outside an official Site break room. Staff were noted to have begun gathering in a supplemental meeting room during their breaks. At 10:32 AM, Dr. Mike was noted as remarking “We’ve basically made this the new break room”. During his break, a block of cheese originating from Dr. Mike’s lunch disappeared.
Fifteen minutes later, the Department of Heavenly Objects reported the Moon had shifted its orbit 3% closer to the Earth.

Containment Procedures are to be reworked as soon as possible.

    CW: This article contains mentions of body horror, loss of autonomy, brainwashing, forced pregnancy, Just Girly Thing's usual antics, abortion, and death during childbirth.

⚠️ content warning

Item #: SCP-9097

Object Class: Keter

A package of SCP-9097.

Special Containment Procedures: As of 17/04/2024, only one package of SCP-9097 is held in containment. Efforts to track down the supplier and other holders of SCP-9097 are currently ongoing.

A cover story has been released, claiming that the few publicly known instances of SCP-9097-1 were falsified, and that the instances of SCP-9097-2 were actors. The Foundation is still attempting to remove public coverage of SCP-9097-1 and SCP-9097-2 instances.

The few instances of SCP-9097-1 and SCP-9097-2 that the Foundation has acquired access to are to be held in humanoid containment cells at Site-987. SCP-9097-2 instances require full time assistance via members of Site-987’s medical team.

Description: SCP-9097 refers to a collection of circular pills of bright pink coloring. SCP-9097 has no label, but the back holds a logo for GO1-4319 "Just Girly Things".

SCP-9097's anomalous effects only take place when ingested by a subject with XX chromosomes who is currently pregnant,1 dubbed SCP-9097-1 once SCP-9097 has entered their system. Multiple anomalous effects take place after consumption, including:

  • The inability to abort the fetus via any means (medical, chemical, or mechanical).
  • Acceleration of the growth of the fetus, making SCP-9097-1 instances ready to give birth less than six hours after consumption of SCP-9097, even if the pregnancy was just diagnosed.
  • SCP-9097-1 instances will be excited to give birth, even if they had previously shown disinterest in the pregnancy.

Upon going into labor, SCP-9097-1 instances will begin to give birth to a fully formed human, dubbed SCP-9097-2, with XX chromosomes, no matter what the sex of the fetus was beforehand. Instances of SCP-9097-2 are born with prefrontal cerebral hypoplasia. Subjects, therefore, do not develop linguistic capabilities and experience significant functional deficits in higher-order cognitive processes. Motor-sensory pathways are preserved, though with some impairments in posture and maintaining muscle tone; entities frequently fall within the bottom 5th percentile for muscle strength per unit mass.

Out of the five publicly observed SCP-9097-1 subjects, only two survived giving birth to SCP-9097-2 instances. The Foundation is currently in possession of the corpses of the three other SCP-9097-1 instances. Both surviving instances of SCP-9097-1 have been left permanently disabled; One instance has been rendered unable to walk, while the other had its bottom half removed entirely.

Addendum-1-Discovery: On 07/04/2024, a news story was published online, which stated that twenty-four-year-old Nancy Follerson had given birth to a full-grown woman at New Clover hospital in Fort Worth, Texas. The Foundation sent a collection of undercover agents posing as reporters, doctors, and mortuary attendants to investigate the situation on 08/04/2024. On Nancy Follerson's person, a package of SCP-9097 was discovered.

On 09/04/2024, many additional articles began to come out about SCP-9097-1 instances. Attempts to remove the articles have proven futile, as they all reinstated themselves in less than twenty-four hours.

The Foundation has only managed to track down four other instances of SCP-9097-1.


















Redirecting to www.justgirlychats.███






#BirthPills Where KeeLee talks about the new pills.

Topic set by KeeLee on Wed April 10 2024 08:04:20 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time)

KeeLee: Mimi, What the fuck?

Mimi: What a nice way to start a conversation.

KeeLee: These pills are meant to preserve childbirth. We can't give them to the public like this. We don't want fully grown women who can't do anything. They were supposed to be fully functional.

Mimi: KeeLee, I'm working on a solution, I promise.

KeeLee: That stupid foundation is going to be onto this if they find any of the pills.

Mimi: Hey, at least they're not finding the version that works.

KeeLee: I just don't understand how you fucked up so badly in the first place. Brain-dead adult toddlers are no help for our mission.

Mimi: Science is a tricky field, KeeLee. I studied this for a long time. You try making pills that change a fetus from scratch.

KeeLee: Fine, whatever. Just get it fixed. I'll make sure those articles stay online. This may have been a fuck up, but it's one we can use to our advantage. The more people who are curious, the more research they do. We'll get more lovely lady incubators.

Mimi: Just give me a little more time. In the meantime, do you have any more distribution targets for when we can try the next batch?

KeeLee: I'll ask Ella. I know a new family planning clinic just opened near her. Now make it fast.

Footnotes
1. Regardless of trimester.

SCP-9098.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9098

Object Class: Neutralized

Archived manifestation of SCP-9098

Special Containment Procedures: This document serves to archive the timeline of events related to SCP-9098. No other procedures have been deemed necessary.

The bodies of SCP-9098-A and SCP-9098-B have been buried at an undisclosed location.

Description: SCP-9098 was an anomalous sentient broadcast signal that was neutralized on 11/12/1996 by SCP-9098-B

Addendum 1: Initial discovery
SCP-9098 was initially subject to an investigation by the Unusual Incidents Unit in early September of 1996 where several online users began posting on conspiracy and supernatural forum boards1 recounting strange, vivid dreams that they’ve been experiencing following a ‘strange broadcast’ reminiscent of a broadcast bumper that appeared on their television. One such example, written by a user on Parawatch, goes as follows:

complicated_casette 09/12/1996 (Thurs) 3:26:04 #17611329

Just like Joshua32 said, everything started with the broadcast. For me, it happened earlier this month. I was up late one night, half-asleep and binging reruns of The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, when the broadcast suddenly cut out and switched to something else.

At first, I figured it was one of those broadcast hijacking things (I’ve heard of that happening before, though it’s kinda rare), but there was something… off about this one. It didn’t feel like a prank. From what I remember, it showed some kind of calm, scenic background with text overlaid on top. It looked like one of those station ID bumpers they’d show to remind you what channel you’re watching when you’ve nodded off on the couch.

The text said something really weird, something along the lines of: “Memories feel so far away, like on a distant shore.”

As I was trying to make sense of it, I started to feel this… itch. Not on my skin, but in my head. Kind of like an urge? Or is it like a pull? I don’t really know how to describe it, but I suddenly felt like I needed to get closer to the TV. So for whatever reason I started inching my way closer to the screen and whatever was gravitating me towards it kept getting stronger the closer I got.

But then next thing I know, everything went black. I must’ve passed out or something, because when I came to, the show was back on and nothing seemed out of place. I figured I’d just dozed off.

But then the dreams started. And after reading Joshua32’s post and hearing about other people talk about the same damn thing I’m not so sure anymore. Maybe something weird really is happening.

complicated_casette 09/14/1996 (Sat) 12:11:06 #17611329

EDIT: I was looking through the footage on my VCR around the time this started to see if it might've captured that broadcast and I found something.

This thing really did happen. Holy shit.
What the fuck is happening here guys?

Archived sketch of the man illustrated by a sufferer of SCP-9098

These dreams are universally described in phenomenal detail, predominantly featuring romantic encounters between an unidentified individual and was coined among sufferers as the “Ever Dream This Man?” phenomenon (Designated SCP-9098) due to the prominence of this recurring character within their dreams.

One member of this community2 was designated a Person of Interest by the UIU due to their extensive involvement in discussions concerning the phenomenon: most notably for posing highly specific questions to individuals affected by it while demonstrating knowledge of details not publicly disclosed in their posts.

Despite the promising nature of this lead, the investigation was halted due to budgetary restrictions brought about by the mounting pressure from the Satanic Panic, leading to the case’s abandonment by mid-September.

Addendum 2: Foundation involvement
Shortly after the investigation was abandoned, the lead investigator contacted an embedded member of MTF Iota-10 (“Damn Feds”) and requested Foundation assistance in completing the case. This interaction was recorded by the Iota-10 agent on-scene:

Interviewed: UIU Supervisory Special Agent (SSA) Olsen
Interviewer: MTF Iota-10 Agent Davenport
Foreword: This interview was conducted in the underground parking garage of the FBI J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C.
<Begin Log>

SSA Olsen: Agent Davenport! Glad you could make it.

Agent Davenport: Olsen! It's been too long, old friend. Mind if we get straight to the point?

SSA Olsen: Right let's get straight to business, you haven't changed one bit since last time Davenport [Olsen chuckles]. So do you remember that bust back in ’94? The one where I saved your ass and you said you owed me one? Well, I’m here to cash that favor in.

[Olsen retrieves a box from the trunk of his car, labeled “UIU Casefile 1996-074 ‘Killscreen’”]

Agent Davenport: Whoa, whoa- what’s this all about, Olsen?

SSA Olsen: Case I was heading about a month ago. Had to shelve it cuz our unit’s drowning in false alarms about satanic cults from paranoid parents and cranky neighbors. I want you guys to pick this one up and see it through.

[Davenport flips through the contents of the box, scanning a few files]

Agent Davenport: [Sighs] Fine. I’ll see what I can do. But that's only because we're good mates. So tell me: what exactly am I looking at here?

SSA Olsen: End of August, our tech analysts, or "tech trolls" as we call 'em, started flagging online chatter about people having the same weird dreams. We started comparing notes and saw a pattern.

Agent Davenport: Go on.

SSA Olsen: Take that photo you’re holding, which is supposedly a still from a strange TV broadcast linked to the dreams. We had some guys stare at it for a while, but nothing happened, so we ruled out anything memetic

Agent Davenport: And let me guess: you didn’t call me just because you’re overworked from the Satanic Panic.

SSA Olsen: Sharp as ever, Davenport, you’re right. I was gonna reach out sooner because my kid, my little Olsen Jr., starts talking about the same dreams. Word for word. Now, I might’ve lost my beautiful dame in the divorce, but that boy means the world to me. I figured if anyone could help me understand what was happening to him, it’d be you.

Agent Davenport: And…?

SSA Olsen: And a couple days before I could call, he tells me the dreams just… stopped. No warning. Just gone. I wasn’t cleared to keep working the case because of the Panic but I still had some friends down in Tech. Had ’em dig around online. They found a Parawatch post that went up the same day my son’s dreams ended. The user who wrote it was one of our primary suspects during the investigation because of his uncanny knack at knowing specific details about these dreams that some folks didn't even mention in their posts. That final post though… had some real weird wording. Almost like the guy was gonna off himself.

Agent Davenport: Alright, I’ll bite. Definitely sounds interesting. But what were these dreams about, exactly? Nightmares?

SSA Olsen: That’s the strangest part. You’d expect something dark, maybe apocalyptic or even satanic considering the times, but no. These dreams were romantic. People, my son included, described going on dates, having long conversations, spending time with some mystery man. Same figure every damn time. Ain't that weird? Actually wait, lemme see here…

[SSA Olsen sifts through the box, pulling out a microcasette and accompanying recorder]

SSA Olsen: I recorded a few interviews with my son: asked him what exactly he was seeing in those dreams. Figured you folks probably had some fancy doodad that could peek into people’s heads, so maybe it’d be pointless. But turns out, I’m glad I came prepared.

[SSA Olsen inserts one of the microcassettes into the handheld recorder and presses play.]

SSA Olsen [Recording]: So, Jack… can you tell me more about these dreams?

Jack Olsen [Recording]: It was kinda weird. I remember being in this basement, working on a computer: almost like I was drawing something, maybe? Some kind of picture or design, it made me feel funny everytime I looked at it. Then this man comes down the stairs holding a camera, and suddenly I feel… embarrassed, I guess. I tried to hide whatever was on the screen, like hugging the monitor to my chest. Then I said something to him, but I can’t really remember what. Everything after that feels blurry, but I remember laughing when he answered. It felt… normal, or natural, almost like we knew eachother. [The tape clicks and ends]

SSA Olsen: Weird, right? I wanted to press Jack for more, but he’s only seven: doesn’t remember much beyond that. I’ve got a few more tapes in the box, some from other talks with him and a few with people we managed to track down online. The latter might have more to work with than what my son could give.

Agent Davenport: You’ve definitely piqued my curiosity. I’ll talk to my superiors, see about getting this case transferred to us. Appreciate the heads-up, Olsen.

SSA Olsen: Glad to hear it, Davenport. Feels good knowing someone’s gonna finish what I started. Thanks.

<End Log>

Closing Statement: Following the interview, all information collected by the UIU was transferred to the custody of the SCP Foundation

The post that was previously mentioned by SSA Olsen was later recovered, being archived and appended below:

paintedcanvas 11/11/1996 (Mon) 1:32:00 #57328491

Hey everyone, Canvas here.

I've been apart of this place since everything started. Even though I never went through what most of you guys did, I always felt like I belonged here: Like she was telling me these things herself, even if I knew that was a lie.

I can’t really explain what’s going to happen next, but tonight, when you finally fall asleep, the dreams will stop. The noise will quiet down.

Thank you for letting me know that she was always there.

Love you all,
Canvas

Addendum 3: Neutralization
On 11/13/1996, a team from MTF Epsilon-6 (“Village Idiots”) conducted a follow-up investigation in Kanab, Utah, concerning the Person of Interest identified in the UIU report: a man named Silas Brown, known on Parawatch as paintedcanvas. It should be noted that the Foundation had already placed him under investigation for his potential affiliation with the anomalous3 and that local law enforcement in Kanab had identified him as a possible suspect in a series of localized broadcast hijacking incidents.

However upon the team's arrival, the team discovered the remains of two individuals, later identified as Luna Barclay (SCP-9098-A) and Silas Brown (SCP-9098-B). Both were determined to have died from carbon monoxide inhalation, with evidence suggesting a suicide.

A handwritten note was recovered next to the bodies:

It was all my fault. I just wanted to make her happy and I ended up hurting her in a way I couldn’t even imagine. But despite all the pain and confusion and fear she endured, she still thought about those memories we shared together. All those people, talking about our memories. You were just trying to tell me you were out there, weren’t you baby?

Don’t worry, this time I’ll join you on the otherside. We’ll be together forever, just like all those times when we promised we’d grow old together.

I love you.
S.B

Following this, all evidence collected at the scene was transported to Site-53 for analysis.4 Among the recovered items was a particular VHS tape discovered inside a VCR, bearing a crude handwritten label reading: “What should’ve been.” Playback of this tape revealed the following footage:

Recovered video footage
Timestamp: 1996.08.22 13:22.12

[BEGIN LOG]

The footage begins shaky and unfocused as the camera tilts upward toward a mirror, briefly revealing the cameraman, identified as SCP-9098-B. He leaves the bedroom and begins heading down a narrow staircase into the basement. There, SCP-9098-A is seated at their shared home computer, consumed in her work.

SCP-9098-B: Hey, babe… whatcha workin’ on over there?

The camera zooms closer. For a moment, the computer screen is visible, suggesting that SCP-9098-A is in the process of creating a cognitohazard on Microsoft Paint. She quickly notices the camera, gasps, and spins around, hugging the monitor to her chest.

SCP-9098-A: Hey! You’re not supposed to be down here! Shoo! Go upstairs! This is your anniversary present and it's ruining the element of surprise!

SCP-9098-B: Oh really? For YOUR information, this is our basement. And I happen to be working on my present down here too. I hope you weren’t trying to sneak a peek either!

She sticks her tongue out at him as he chuckles and crosses the room toward a cluttered workstation filled with wires, circuit boards, and the remains of a disassembled Virtual Boy. Setting the camera on the desk to face him, SCP-9098-B begins tinkering with a few components. After a few seconds, he pauses, sifts through his pockets, and pulls out a small box. He stares at it quietly, clearly hesitating.

SCP-9098-A [off-screen]: Sooo… what’s the plan for our anniversary tomorrow?

Startled, he quickly hides the box as SCP-9098-A appears behind him and wraps her arms around his shoulders, leaning against him lovingly. He laughs nervously.

SCP-9098-B: I- uh- thought maybe I’d show you my present early, since it’s obviously wayy cooler than yours.

SCP-9098-A: Uh, excuse me? Mine is literally the coolest thing ever made in, like, the entire world! You’re just trying to cobble together one of those funky gadgets that always end up exploding.

The couple break into laughter, continuing their playful back-and-forth. The camera remains recording until SCP-9098-A notices the red light still blinking and reaches over to turn it off.

The screen cuts to black, briefly flashing red text that reads 'I WOULD'VE SAID YES' before ending

[END LOG]

The cognitohazard in question was later discovered and testing personnel exposed to the image have universally expressed a feeling of warmth, comfort and love with a marked improvement on their mental and emotional wellbeing. As the image has been cleared of any harmful vectors, it has been appended below
