One such example, written by a user on [http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/parawatch-hub Parawatch], goes as follows: [[div style="background-color: #262626; font-family: 'PT Mono', monospace; padding: 0.5em;"]] [[div class="parapost"]] > ##purple|**complicated_casette**## 09/12/1996 (Thurs) 3:26:04 #17611329 [[span style="color:white"]] > ------ > Just like ##orange|Joshua32## said, everything started with the broadcast. For me, it happened earlier this month. I was up late one night, half-asleep and binging reruns of //The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air//, when the broadcast suddenly cut out and switched to something else. > > At first, I figured it was one of those broadcast hijacking things (I’ve heard of that happening before, though it’s kinda rare), but there was something… off about this one. It didn’t feel like a prank. From what I remember, it showed some kind of calm, scenic background with text overlaid on top. It looked like one of those station ID bumpers they’d show to remind you what channel you’re watching when you’ve nodded off on the couch. > > The text said something really weird, something along the lines of: “Memories feel so far away, like on a distant shore.” > > As I was trying to make sense of it, I started to feel this… itch. Not on my skin, but in my head. Kind of like an urge? Or is it like a pull? I don’t really know how to describe it, but I suddenly felt like I needed to get closer to the TV. So for whatever reason I started inching my way closer to the screen and whatever was gravitating me towards it kept getting stronger the closer I got. > > But then next thing I know, everything went black. I must’ve passed out or something, because when I came to, the show was back on and nothing seemed out of place. I figured I’d just dozed off. > > But then the dreams started. And after reading ##orange|Joshua32##’s post and hearing about other people talk about the same damn thing I’m not so sure anymore. Maybe something weird really is happening. [[/span]] [[/div]] [[div class="parapost reply1"]] > ##purple|**complicated_casette**## 09/14/1996 (Sat) 12:11:06 #17611329 [[span style="color:white"]] > ------ > > **EDIT:** I was looking through the footage on my VCR around the time this started to see if it might've captured that broadcast and I found something. > [[image memories.png]] > This thing really did happen. Holy shit. > > What the fuck is happening here guys? [[/span]] [[/div]] [[/div]] @@@@ [[include component:image-block name=Silas.png| caption=Archived sketch of the man illustrated by a sufferer of SCP-9098]] These dreams are universally described in phenomenal detail, predominantly featuring romantic encounters between an unidentified individual and was coined among sufferers as the “Ever Dream This Man?” phenomenon (Designated SCP-9098) due to the prominence of this recurring character within their dreams. One member of this community[[footnote]] Known under the username **paintedcanvas** [[/footnote]] was designated a Person of Interest by the UIU due to their extensive involvement in discussions concerning the phenomenon: most notably for posing highly specific questions to individuals affected by it while demonstrating knowledge of details not publicly disclosed in their posts. Despite the promising nature of this lead, the investigation was halted due to budgetary restrictions brought about by the mounting pressure from the Satanic Panic, leading to the case’s abandonment by mid-September. **Addendum 2:** Foundation involvement Shortly after the investigation was abandoned, the lead investigator contacted an embedded member of MTF Iota-10 (“Damn Feds”) and requested Foundation assistance in completing the case. This interaction was recorded by the Iota-10 agent on-scene: > **Interviewed:** UIU Supervisory Special Agent (SSA) Olsen > **Interviewer:** MTF Iota-10 Agent Davenport > **Foreword:** This interview was conducted in the underground parking garage of the FBI J. Edgar Hoover Building in Washington, D.C. > > **** > > **SSA Olsen:** Agent Davenport! Glad you could make it. > > **Agent Davenport:** Olsen! It's been too long, old friend. Mind if we get straight to the point? > > **SSA Olsen:** Right let's get straight to business, you haven't changed one bit since last time Davenport //[Olsen chuckles]//. So do you remember that bust back in ’94? The one where I saved your ass and you said you owed me one? Well, I’m here to cash that favor in. > > //[Olsen retrieves a box from the trunk of his car, labeled “UIU Casefile 1996-074 ‘Killscreen’”]// > > **Agent Davenport:** Whoa, whoa- what’s this all about, Olsen? > > **SSA Olsen:** Case I was heading about a month ago. Had to shelve it cuz our unit’s drowning in false alarms about satanic cults from paranoid parents and cranky neighbors. I want you guys to pick this one up and see it through. > > //[Davenport flips through the contents of the box, scanning a few files]// > > **Agent Davenport:** //[Sighs]// Fine. I’ll see what I can do. But that's only because we're good mates. So tell me: what exactly am I looking at here? > > **SSA Olsen:** End of August, our tech analysts, or "tech trolls" as we call 'em, started flagging online chatter about people having the same weird dreams. We started comparing notes and saw a pattern. > > **Agent Davenport:** Go on. > > **SSA Olsen:** Take that photo you’re holding, which is supposedly a still from a strange TV broadcast linked to the dreams. We had some guys stare at it for a while, but nothing happened, so we ruled out anything memetic > > **Agent Davenport:** And let me guess: you didn’t call me just because you’re overworked from the Satanic Panic. > > **SSA Olsen:** Sharp as ever, Davenport, you’re right. I was gonna reach out sooner because my kid, my little Olsen Jr., starts talking about the same dreams. Word for word. Now, I might’ve lost my beautiful dame in the divorce, but that boy means the world to me. I figured if anyone could help me understand what was happening to him, it’d be you. > > **Agent Davenport:** And...? > > **SSA Olsen:** And a couple days before I could call, he tells me the dreams just… stopped. No warning. Just gone. I wasn’t cleared to keep working the case because of the Panic but I still had some friends down in Tech. Had ’em dig around online. They found a Parawatch post that went up the same day my son’s dreams ended. The user who wrote it was one of our primary suspects during the investigation because of his uncanny knack at knowing specific details about these dreams that some folks didn't even mention in their posts. That final post though... had some real weird wording. Almost like the guy was gonna off himself. > > **Agent Davenport:** Alright, I’ll bite. Definitely sounds interesting. But what were these dreams about, exactly? Nightmares? > > **SSA Olsen:** That’s the strangest part. You’d expect something dark, maybe apocalyptic or even satanic considering the times, but no. These dreams were romantic. People, my son included, described going on dates, having long conversations, spending time with some mystery man. Same figure every damn time. Ain't that weird? Actually wait, lemme see here... > > //[SSA Olsen sifts through the box, pulling out a microcasette and accompanying recorder]// > > **SSA Olsen:** I recorded a few interviews with my son: asked him what exactly he was seeing in those dreams. Figured you folks probably had some fancy doodad that could peek into people’s heads, so maybe it’d be pointless. But turns out, I’m glad I came prepared. > > //[SSA Olsen inserts one of the microcassettes into the handheld recorder and presses play.]// > > **SSA Olsen [Recording]:** //So, Jack… can you tell me more about these dreams?// > > **Jack Olsen [Recording]:** //It was kinda weird. I remember being in this basement, working on a computer: almost like I was drawing something, maybe? Some kind of picture or design, it made me feel funny everytime I looked at it. Then this man comes down the stairs holding a camera, and suddenly I feel… embarrassed, I guess. I tried to hide whatever was on the screen, like hugging the monitor to my chest. Then I said something to him, but I can’t really remember what. Everything after that feels blurry, but I remember laughing when he answered. It felt… normal, or natural, almost like we knew eachother. [The tape clicks and ends]// > > **SSA Olsen:** Weird, right? I wanted to press Jack for more, but he’s only seven: doesn’t remember much beyond that. I’ve got a few more tapes in the box, some from other talks with him and a few with people we managed to track down online. The latter might have more to work with than what my son could give. > > **Agent Davenport:** You’ve definitely piqued my curiosity. I’ll talk to my superiors, see about getting this case transferred to us. Appreciate the heads-up, Olsen. > > **SSA Olsen:** Glad to hear it, Davenport. Feels good knowing someone’s gonna finish what I started. Thanks. > > **** > > **Closing Statement:** Following the interview, all information collected by the UIU was transferred to the custody of the SCP Foundation The post that was previously mentioned by SSA Olsen was later recovered, being archived and appended below: [[div style="background-color: #262626; font-family: 'PT Mono', monospace; padding: 0.5em;"]] [[div class="parapost"]] > ##blue|**paintedcanvas**## 11/11/1996 (Mon) 1:32:00 #57328491 [[span style="color:white"]] > ------ > Hey everyone, Canvas here. > > I've been apart of this place since everything started. Even though I never went through what most of you guys did, I always felt like I belonged here: Like she was telling me these things herself, even if I knew that was a lie. > > I can’t really explain what’s going to happen next, but tonight, when you finally fall asleep, the dreams will stop. The noise will quiet down. > > Thank you for letting me know that she was always there. > > Love you all, > Canvas [[/span]] [[/div]] [[/div]] **Addendum 3:** Neutralization On 11/13/1996, a team from MTF Epsilon-6 (“Village Idiots”) conducted a follow-up investigation in Kanab, Utah, concerning the Person of Interest identified in the UIU report: a man named Silas Brown, known on Parawatch as paintedcanvas. It should be noted that the Foundation had already placed him under investigation for his potential affiliation with the anomalous[[footnote]] Such examples include their collusion with the anartist community known as Are We Cool Yet? [[/footnote]] and that local law enforcement in Kanab had identified him as a possible suspect in a series of localized broadcast hijacking incidents. However upon the team's arrival, the team discovered the remains of two individuals, later identified as Luna Barclay (SCP-9098-A) and Silas Brown (SCP-9098-B). Both were determined to have died from carbon monoxide inhalation, with evidence suggesting a suicide. A handwritten note was recovered next to the bodies: [[div class="page"]] //It was all my fault. I just wanted to make her happy and I ended up hurting her in a way I couldn’t even imagine. But despite all the pain and confusion and fear she endured, she still thought about those memories we shared together. All those people, talking about our memories. You were just trying to tell me you were out there, weren’t you baby?// @@ @@ //Don’t worry, this time I’ll join you on the otherside. We’ll be together forever, just like all those times when we promised we’d grow old together.// @@ @@ [[>]] //I love you.// //S.B// [[/>]] [[/div]] Following this, all evidence collected at the scene was transported to Site-53 for analysis.[[footnote]]A full list is available upon request.[[/footnote]] Among the recovered items was a particular VHS tape discovered inside a VCR, bearing a crude handwritten label reading: “//What should’ve been//.” Playback of this tape revealed the following footage: [[div class="blockquote" style="border-radius: 10px; margin: 10px"]] **Recovered video footage** **Timestamp:** 1996.08.22 13:22.12 ----- [BEGIN LOG] //The footage begins shaky and unfocused as the camera tilts upward toward a mirror, briefly revealing the cameraman, identified as SCP-9098-B. He leaves the bedroom and begins heading down a narrow staircase into the basement. There, SCP-9098-A is seated at their shared home computer, consumed in her work.// **SCP-9098-B:** Hey, babe… whatcha workin’ on over there? //The camera zooms closer. For a moment, the computer screen is visible, suggesting that SCP-9098-A is in the process of creating a cognitohazard on Microsoft Paint. She quickly notices the camera, gasps, and spins around, hugging the monitor to her chest.// **SCP-9098-A:** Hey! You’re not supposed to be down here! Shoo! Go upstairs! This is your anniversary present and it's ruining the element of surprise! **SCP-9098-B:** Oh really? For YOUR information, this is our basement. And I happen to be working on my present down here too. I hope you weren’t trying to sneak a peek either! //She sticks her tongue out at him as he chuckles and crosses the room toward a cluttered workstation filled with wires, circuit boards, and the remains of a disassembled Virtual Boy. Setting the camera on the desk to face him, SCP-9098-B begins tinkering with a few components. After a few seconds, he pauses, sifts through his pockets, and pulls out a small box. He stares at it quietly, clearly hesitating.// **SCP-9098-A [//off-screen//]:** Sooo… what’s the plan for our anniversary tomorrow? //Startled, he quickly hides the box as SCP-9098-A appears behind him and wraps her arms around his shoulders, leaning against him lovingly. He laughs nervously.// **SCP-9098-B:** I- uh- thought maybe I’d show you my present early, since it’s obviously wayy cooler than yours. **SCP-9098-A:** Uh, excuse me? Mine is literally the coolest thing ever made in, like, the entire world! You’re just trying to cobble together one of those funky gadgets that always end up exploding. //The couple  break into laughter, continuing their playful back-and-forth. The camera remains recording until SCP-9098-A notices the red light still blinking and reaches over to turn it off.// //The screen cuts to black, briefly flashing red text that reads 'I WOULD'VE SAID YES' before ending// [[image iloveu.png]] [END LOG] [[/div]] The cognitohazard in question was later discovered and testing personnel exposed to the image have universally expressed a feeling of warmth, comfort and love with a marked improvement on their mental and emotional wellbeing. As the image has been cleared of any harmful vectors, it has been appended below [[collapsible show="+ View Image? SCP-9099.raw_content:
Item#: 9099
Level3
Containment Class:
euclid
Secondary Class:
thaumiel
Disruption Class:
keneq
Risk Class:
caution
link to memo

Special Containment Procedures: Due to SCP-9099’s remote location, monitoring the surrounding area for trespassers and maintaining a standard controlled entry perimeter is sufficient on-site containment. Satellite and aerial imagery depicting SCP-9099 with enough detail to confirm its size are to be expunged from public sources, with any and all public records indicating that it is a Soviet-era storage silo of unremarkable scale.

Only D-Class personnel with no prior contact with other SCPs or access to any sensitive information may be assigned observation platform duty within SCP-9099. Under no circumstances should personnel not meeting these criteria enter SCP-9099, and no activity other than observation should be undertaken while in SCP-9099. No electronic recording or storage equipment is permitted within SCP-9099. All items brought into SCP-9099 must be directly approved by the head researcher, and D-Class must be checked for contraband before each shift to ensure compliance.

Standard equipment for observation duty includes:

• Pen and journal
• Mechanical timepiece
• Mechanical depth gauge
• Bottled water
• Field rations
• Emergency kit
• Portable latrine

All other items are at the discretion of the head researcher.

At least one D-Class personnel, and preferably up to three when resources permit, are to staff SCP-9099’s observation platform during each rotation cycle. If three or more consecutive rotation cycles are missed, an on-site containment breach should be considered to be in progress. In this instance, SCP-9099 should be sealed, its ladder retracted, and its singular point of egress defended by an aerial assault squad who are to maintain a minimal distance of ten meters from the top of the structure. The structure itself is to be flooded with fatal concentrations of carbon monoxide. The carbon monoxide should not be pumped out until appropriate D-Class personnel are on standby, with testing resumed as quickly as possible.

Update 05/03/████: A petition by former Head Researcher Vogle to keep SCP-9099 permanently flooded with fatal concentrations of carbon monoxide and discontinue active research has been officially denied by an O5 vote of 9 to 3, as this only neutralizes SCP-9099-A instances. The full capabilities of SCP-9099 itself are not yet sufficiently understood to justify passive containment procedures.

Update 05/09/████: As of Incident 9099-108, preference for D-Class is to be given to individuals with below-average intelligence, reasoning, insightfulness, and visual acuity, even when such traits may detract from the quality of test results. D-Class personnel are to be instructed to refrain from looking down in order to avoid vertigo.

Description: SCP-9099 is a concrete silo approximately seventy-five meters in diameter and two hundred and twenty-five meters in height, located approximately seventy kilometers northeast of ████████, Siberia. Though it came under Foundation control after the fall of the Soviet Union, it is not known if it was originally created by the Soviets, as all pertinent GRU-P records were destroyed prior to their dissolution.

Though its brutalist style is consistent with mid-20th-century Soviet architecture, dating methods to confirm its age have all proven inconclusive, and there is otherwise nothing about SCP-9099 itself to suggest a Soviet origin. It is possible that the exterior of SCP-9099 was constructed around a much older structure.

There is no ground-level access to SCP-9099, as SCP-9099 does not possess a ground level. An exterior ladder must be climbed to reach the only entrance at the top of the structure. The interior perimeter of SCP-9099 is ringed by ninety-nine levels of ninety-nine two-meter-wide containment cells, nearly all of which are sealed by a five-centimetre-thick sheet of one-way glass. When the lights inside these cells are off, occupants are not visible to outside observers.

Note that SCP-9099 does not possess any source of electricity or electrical wiring, and each of the caged light fixtures within SCP-9099 contains anomalously piezoluminescent salt crystals. Light emission is stimulated by a continuous, gentle vibration throughout SCP-9099, and terminated by detaching the fixtures from the walls.

The overall design of SCP-9099 is highly suggestive of a panopticon-style prison, and the prevailing hypothesis is that this was its original purpose. In the center of SCP-9099 is an observation platform suspended between three rails. The observation platform will ascend and descend these rails at a rate of one meter per minute, remaining stationary for two separate fifteen-minute periods, causing a full cycle to take eight hours. There is no known method of stopping or altering this cycle, and further attempts to do so are no longer permitted.

The first of the fifteen-minute rest periods is always at the top of the structure, allowing personnel to embark on and disembark from the platform. The second rest period will occur at a random point during the eight-hour cycle. Approximately once every two months on average, this will occur when the observation platform is at ground level. Since SCP-9099 does not possess a ground level, Foundation personnel who disembark from the observation platform during this time are considered irretrievable.

Approximately thirty percent of the time during a typical cycle, at least one cell visible from the observation platform will have its lights on, revealing its occupants. There does not appear to be any obvious patterns as to which cells are illuminated or when. Visible occupants almost invariably take extreme interest in the occupants of the observation platform, maintaining line-of-sight for as long as possible.

It is generally presumed that the same applies to non-visible occupants, as well.

Occupants of SCP-9099 (henceforth SCP-9099-A), are generally humanoid, though typically gaunt, pallid, and hairless with noticeably elongated nails and teeth. Instances of SCP-9099-A universally possess a singular, cyclopean orifice in the center of their foreheads of unclear purpose and origin. Clothing is generally simple, dark linens of premodern but otherwise uncertain make.

The majority of the time, SCP-9099-A are content to simply watch the observer, but they frequently also make threatening or lewd gestures, bang at the glass to get attention, etc. Occassionally, they will even hold up signs or write messages on the glass for observers to read. These messages are typically succinct and cryptic, and observers are instructed to record but otherwise ignore them. Written messages are always in the observer’s native language, and to date, all tests with illiterate D-Class subjects have not produced any written messages.

The current, unconfirmed hypothesis is that some form of quantum observer effect allows SCP-9099-A to gain access to information regarding any entity observing them, and that the one-way glass doors were put in place to mitigate this effect. The seemingly random activation of cell lights within SCP-9099 is presumed to be an unintended development.

If an instance of SCP-9099-A in an illuminated cell is not viewed by a human observer within a rotation cycle, it will remain illuminated for the next cycle, and the total number of new illuminated cells will increase by the square of the previous number of illuminated cells. This compounds quickly, and it appears that the strength of the hypothetical observer effect increases non-linearly. When this effect reaches a critical threshold, capable of occurring in as little as three unobserved cycles with optimal starting conditions, all cells within SCP-9099 will open, and all instances of SCP-9099-A will attempt to breach containment. Raising CO2 within SCP-9099 to fatal levels has proven to be an effective means of reestablishing containment without exposing Foundation personnel to the effects of SCP-9099-A.

Upon resuming observation of SCP-9099, SCP-9099 appears to effectively reset, with all instances of SCP-9099-A being both alive and back within their cells. To date, no cadavers of SCP-9099-A after a containment breach have been recovered. While it is not yet clear precisely what is occurring, the aforementioned quantum observer effects are believed to be involved, with SCP-9099’s wavefunction returning to a stable state to prevent the loss of all conscious observers within it.

It should be noted that several of the messages written by SCP-9099-A at least imply that they recall past asphyxiation.

Addendum: The following is a journal entry taken from D-14409, the most recent D-Class to reach the ground floor of SCP-9099.

+ CLEARANCE REQUIRED
- ACCESS GRANTED

Selected Journal Entry

09:15 ~ The platform has begun to descend as scheduled. At least I’m pretty sure it has. A meter a minute isn’t exactly noticeable. No visible SCP-9099-A instances as of yet, but I would like to personally thank the Ethics Committee Liaison who made sure the portable latrine has a privacy tent. Not sure how I’d feel about taking a leak in front of an audience this size.

I guess I should probably thank you for the safety harness, too. It’s a long drop to the bottom, and anomalous or not, the fact that this platform receives absolutely zero maintenance is far from reassuring.

I wasn’t sure what the file meant when it said there was no ground level, but now I can see that there’s no frickin’ ground. It’s just a big black hole at the bottom of the shaft. Why couldn’t you have said that instead of making it sound so cryptic and ominous? I can’t tell how deep it goes, and hopefully I’m not going to find out. And if I do, that’ll be my secret, since you sure as hell aren’t going to send anyone after me.

10:10 ~ Finally got my first instance of SCP-9099-A after nearly an hour. If I’m reading the depth gauge you guys gave me correctly, he’s on Level 77, Cell 32. He’s looking straight up at me, but nothing else. There’s nothing really to distinguish his appearance from the description I was given. I’ll keep an eye on him until either he’s out of sight or he creeps me out too much. If we’re taking bets on which one of us can win a staring contest, my money’s on him.

10:35 ~ I’ve got another one. Level 68, Cell 82. This one’s smiling at me, and rapping his fingers against the glass. I actually heard that before I saw him. Every little noise echoes like hell in here. It’s a constant rat-a-tat-tat. No pauses, no variations in rhythm. I asked him if he wanted something, but he didn’t respond.

Speaking of rhythm, I think the vibrations are getting stronger. I can’t say for sure, but the slow, constant thrumming feels like it’s getting more intense little by little, and I think the salt lamps are just a little bit brighter. Is that normal? It wasn’t mentioned in the briefing.

11:08 ~This one appeared straight ahead of me when I came out of the latrine. Level-56, Cell 93. Scared the crap out of me, and I think it was on purpose. I know it’s irrational, since I have no control over this platform, but them gradually coming into view as I descended made it feel like I was the one sneaking up on them.

Has anyone ever caught the exact moment the lights in the cells come on? Anyway, this guy slowly waved at me when I first saw him, but has otherwise done nothing remarkable. I can still hear rat-at-tat-tat guy up there, though the echo’s so strong I can hardly tell he’s above me at all.

11:20 ~ No sighting, but I’ve been staring down into the hole at the bottom of the shaft. I know there are dash-A instances watching all around me, whether I can see them or not, but I can’t shake the feeling that something down there is watching me. I’m worried that if I take my eyes off it, something might come flying up at me or maybe climb up the rails, but also that by staring at it, I’m just pissing it off.

Damnit, why couldn’t you guys have just told me what you know? I know you know more than you’re saying. If it was just a hole, then you would have said that. What did you mean when you said there was no ground level?

11:38 ~ Another one. Level 45, Cell 44. This one looked angry, and he had a sign. The sign said “A fall from this height wouldn’t kill you. Unfortunately,”. I lost the staring contest with him pretty quickly.

12:01 ~ Something just happened. The shaft shook and there was a sudden upswell of air, accompanied by a deep bellowing sound. The platform was rocked back and forth, enough that if I had been near the edge and not harnessed in, I’d have been at risk of falling off.

The lights in the shaft went off for a few seconds, and all of the lights in the cells turned on. Some of the SCP-9099-A instances were definitely holding up signs, but it was over too quickly for me to read any of them.

I’m not sure what that was or if it’s happened before, but if it has, no one ever briefed me on it. If that last sign was anything to go by though, that guy in cell 45-44 knew it was coming. The platform’s still descending at the same rate though, so that hasn’t changed, but the vibration is getting stronger. I’m sure of it now.

12:35 ~ Level 22, Cell 81. This is the first one who isn’t standing. They’re huddled in a kind of fetal position, rocking back and forth, but still looking at me. They look a little skinnier and smaller than most of the others. Definitely the least threatening and most pathetic-looking. I can’t help but wonder how long she’s been in that cell.

12:49 ~ Another message. Level 9, Cell 03. No sign this time, just written on the glass. I’m not going to guess with what. It said, “You See, We See, He Sees. Know; it’s why the rails move so slow,”. The instance itself looks deranged with its face pushed right up against the glass, like it was anticipating something. I can only hope it will be disappointed when I ride past it again in an hour.

13:00 ~ Just staring down again. I think I understand.

13:15 ~ I’ve hit the ground level, the one you said didn’t exist. It’s not a pit at all. There’s a transparent, concave covering over it, with a yellowish-green rim all around the perimeter.

It’s an eye, and it sees me.

It’s seen me this whole time, and now I see it. I can see a little into its mind as it peers into mine. It’s not just an eye; it has a body. I’m sure of it. Some kind of colossal cyclops. Not necessarily a giant from Greek mythology Cyclops, but that eye is attached to something.

The vibration through the structure is its pulse, or its breathing, or some kind of vital rhythm. The more I saw it, the more I understood what it was, the more alive it became. It’s telling me this because the more information it gives me, the more it can take from me.

They, whoever they were, tried to cover up the eye and failed, so they built around it instead. They did what the Foundation is doing, and what the Soviets did before them; they sent in only their most expendable people in the hopes of not losing anyone important or letting crucial information slip.

But it didn’t work then, and it’s not working now.

Every bit of information that they got on this thing, that you’re getting on this thing, came at the cost of it learning about them. To look upon the eye is to be seen by the eye. And once you are seen by the eye, you can’t be unseen. Directing your conscious attention away from a thing is as much an act of observation as looking at it, once you know it’s there. If we look, we make it stronger. If we look away, we still make it stronger, so we might as well look, right?

That’s why all these things, all these people, are still here. And it’s why I’m still here. I’m not going back now. There’s a cell with the glass broken down here on the bottom level, a cell you never mentioned. At first, I was terrified that something was going to come out and attack me, but now I understand that that cell is for me. The eye will be watching me forever now, no matter where I am. If I go back to you guys now, I’ll end up locked up in a cell like that anyway. I know what you’ll do to me. I’m better off becoming a proper dash-A instance now. Can’t say I’m looking forward to you guys gassing me every time you miss a day of testing, but it still beats the alternative. I’d be the eye’s slave over yours any day.

This place isn’t a panopticon; it’s an observatory, and you’re not the ones doing the observing.

See you soon.
SCP-9099.raw_source: [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:black-highlighter-theme]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:jakstyle]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:anomaly-class-bar-source |item-number= 9099 |clearance= 3 |container-class= euclid |secondary-class=thaumiel |secondary-icon= https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/component:anomaly-class-bar/thaumiel-icon.svg |disruption-class= keneq |risk-class= caution ]] **Special Containment Procedures:** Due to SCP-9099’s remote location, monitoring the surrounding area for trespassers and maintaining a standard controlled entry perimeter is sufficient on-site containment. Satellite and aerial imagery depicting SCP-9099 with enough detail to confirm its size are to be expunged from public sources, with any and all public records indicating that it is a Soviet-era storage silo of unremarkable scale. Only D-Class personnel with no prior contact with other SCPs or access to any sensitive information may be assigned observation platform duty within SCP-9099. Under no circumstances should personnel not meeting these criteria enter SCP-9099, and no activity other than observation should be undertaken while in SCP-9099. No electronic recording or storage equipment is permitted within SCP-9099. All items brought into SCP-9099 must be directly approved by the head researcher, and D-Class must be checked for contraband before each shift to ensure compliance. Standard equipment for observation duty includes: • Pen and journal • Mechanical timepiece • Mechanical depth gauge • Bottled water • Field rations • Emergency kit • Portable latrine All other items are at the discretion of the head researcher. At least one D-Class personnel, and preferably up to three when resources permit, are to staff SCP-9099’s observation platform during each rotation cycle. If three or more consecutive rotation cycles are missed, an on-site containment breach should be considered to be in progress. In this instance, SCP-9099 should be sealed, its ladder retracted, and its singular point of egress defended by an aerial assault squad who are to maintain a minimal distance of ten meters from the top of the structure. The structure itself is to be flooded with fatal concentrations of carbon monoxide. The carbon monoxide should not be pumped out until appropriate D-Class personnel are on standby, with testing resumed as quickly as possible. **Update 05/03/████:** A petition by former Head Researcher Vogle to keep SCP-9099 permanently flooded with fatal concentrations of carbon monoxide and discontinue active research has been officially denied by an O5 vote of 9 to 3, as this only neutralizes SCP-9099-A instances. The full capabilities of SCP-9099 itself are not yet sufficiently understood to justify passive containment procedures. **Update 05/09/████:** As of Incident 9099-108, preference for D-Class is to be given to individuals with below-average intelligence, reasoning, insightfulness, and visual acuity, even when such traits may detract from the quality of test results. D-Class personnel are to be instructed to refrain from looking down in order to avoid vertigo. **Description:** SCP-9099 is a concrete silo approximately seventy-five meters in diameter and two hundred and twenty-five meters in height, located approximately seventy kilometers northeast of ████████, Siberia. Though it came under Foundation control after the fall of the Soviet Union, it is not known if it was originally created by the Soviets, as all pertinent GRU-P records were destroyed prior to their dissolution. Though its brutalist style is consistent with mid-20th-century Soviet architecture, dating methods to confirm its age have all proven inconclusive, and there is otherwise nothing about SCP-9099 itself to suggest a Soviet origin. It is possible that the exterior of SCP-9099 was constructed around a much older structure. There is no ground-level access to SCP-9099, as SCP-9099 does not possess a ground level. An exterior ladder must be climbed to reach the only entrance at the top of the structure. The interior perimeter of SCP-9099 is ringed by ninety-nine levels of ninety-nine two-meter-wide containment cells, nearly all of which are sealed by a five-centimetre-thick sheet of one-way glass. When the lights inside these cells are off, occupants are not visible to outside observers. Note that SCP-9099 does not possess any source of electricity or electrical wiring, and each of the caged light fixtures within SCP-9099 contains anomalously piezoluminescent salt crystals. Light emission is stimulated by a continuous, gentle vibration throughout SCP-9099, and terminated by detaching the fixtures from the walls. The overall design of SCP-9099 is highly suggestive of a panopticon-style prison, and the prevailing hypothesis is that this was its original purpose. In the center of SCP-9099 is an observation platform suspended between three rails. The observation platform will ascend and descend these rails at a rate of one meter per minute, remaining stationary for two separate fifteen-minute periods, causing a full cycle to take eight hours. There is no known method of stopping or altering this cycle, and further attempts to do so are no longer permitted. The first of the fifteen-minute rest periods is always at the top of the structure, allowing personnel to embark on and disembark from the platform. The second rest period will occur at a random point during the eight-hour cycle. Approximately once every two months on average, this will occur when the observation platform is at ground level. Since SCP-9099 does not possess a ground level, Foundation personnel who disembark from the observation platform during this time are considered irretrievable. Approximately thirty percent of the time during a typical cycle, at least one cell visible from the observation platform will have its lights on, revealing its occupants. There does not appear to be any obvious patterns as to which cells are illuminated or when. Visible occupants almost invariably take extreme interest in the occupants of the observation platform, maintaining line-of-sight for as long as possible. It is generally presumed that the same applies to non-visible occupants, as well. Occupants of SCP-9099 (henceforth SCP-9099-A), are generally humanoid, though typically gaunt, pallid, and hairless with noticeably elongated nails and teeth. Instances of SCP-9099-A universally possess a singular, cyclopean orifice in the center of their foreheads of unclear purpose and origin. Clothing is generally simple, dark linens of premodern but otherwise uncertain make. The majority of the time, SCP-9099-A are content to simply watch the observer, but they frequently also make threatening or lewd gestures, bang at the glass to get attention, etc. Occassionally, they will even hold up signs or write messages on the glass for observers to read. These messages are typically succinct and cryptic, and observers are instructed to record but otherwise ignore them. Written messages are always in the observer’s native language, and to date, all tests with illiterate D-Class subjects have not produced any written messages. The current, unconfirmed hypothesis is that some form of quantum observer effect allows SCP-9099-A to gain access to information regarding any entity observing them, and that the one-way glass doors were put in place to mitigate this effect. The seemingly random activation of cell lights within SCP-9099 is presumed to be an unintended development. If an instance of SCP-9099-A in an illuminated cell is not viewed by a human observer within a rotation cycle, it will remain illuminated for the next cycle, and the total number of new illuminated cells will increase by the square of the previous number of illuminated cells. This compounds quickly, and it appears that the strength of the hypothetical observer effect increases non-linearly. When this effect reaches a critical threshold, capable of occurring in as little as three unobserved cycles with optimal starting conditions, all cells within SCP-9099 will open, and all instances of SCP-9099-A will attempt to breach containment. Raising CO2 within SCP-9099 to fatal levels has proven to be an effective means of reestablishing containment without exposing Foundation personnel to the effects of SCP-9099-A. Upon resuming observation of SCP-9099, SCP-9099 appears to effectively reset, with all instances of SCP-9099-A being both alive and back within their cells. To date, no cadavers of SCP-9099-A after a containment breach have been recovered. While it is not yet clear precisely what is occurring, the aforementioned quantum observer effects are believed to be involved, with SCP-9099’s wavefunction returning to a stable state to prevent the loss of all conscious observers within it. It should be noted that several of the messages written by SCP-9099-A at least imply that they recall past asphyxiation. **Addendum:** The following is a journal entry taken from D-14409, the most recent D-Class to reach the ground floor of SCP-9099. [[collapsible show="+ CLEARANCE REQUIRED" hide="- ACCESS GRANTED"]] [[div class="blockquote" style="border-radius: 10px; margin: 10px"]] [[=]] **Selected Journal Entry** [[/=]] ----- **//09:15 ~//** The platform has begun to descend as scheduled. At least I’m pretty sure it has. A meter a minute isn’t exactly noticeable. No visible SCP-9099-A instances as of yet, but I would like to personally thank the Ethics Committee Liaison who made sure the portable latrine has a privacy tent. Not sure how I’d feel about taking a leak in front of an audience this size. I guess I should probably thank you for the safety harness, too. It’s a long drop to the bottom, and anomalous or not, the fact that this platform receives absolutely zero maintenance is far from reassuring. I wasn’t sure what the file meant when it said there was no ground level, but now I can see that there’s no frickin’ ground. It’s just a big black hole at the bottom of the shaft. Why couldn’t you have said that instead of making it sound so cryptic and ominous? I can’t tell how deep it goes, and hopefully I’m not going to find out. And if I do, that’ll be my secret, since you sure as hell aren’t going to send anyone after me. //**10:10 ~**// Finally got my first instance of SCP-9099-A after nearly an hour. If I’m reading the depth gauge you guys gave me correctly, he’s on Level 77, Cell 32. He’s looking straight up at me, but nothing else. There’s nothing really to distinguish his appearance from the description I was given. I’ll keep an eye on him until either he’s out of sight or he creeps me out too much. If we’re taking bets on which one of us can win a staring contest, my money’s on him. //**10:35 ~**// I’ve got another one. Level 68, Cell 82. This one’s smiling at me, and rapping his fingers against the glass. I actually heard that before I saw him. Every little noise echoes like hell in here. It’s a constant //rat-a-tat-tat//. No pauses, no variations in rhythm. I asked him if he wanted something, but he didn’t respond. Speaking of rhythm, I think the vibrations are getting stronger. I can’t say for sure, but the slow, constant thrumming feels like it’s getting more intense little by little, and I think the salt lamps are just a little bit brighter. Is that normal? It wasn’t mentioned in the briefing. //**11:08 ~**//This one appeared straight ahead of me when I came out of the latrine. Level-56, Cell 93. Scared the crap out of me, and I think it was on purpose. I know it’s irrational, since I have no control over this platform, but them gradually coming into view as I descended made it feel like I was the one sneaking up on them. Has anyone ever caught the exact moment the lights in the cells come on? Anyway, this guy slowly waved at me when I first saw him, but has otherwise done nothing remarkable. I can still hear //rat-at-tat-tat// guy up there, though the echo’s so strong I can hardly tell he’s above me at all. //**11:20 ~**// No sighting, but I’ve been staring down into the hole at the bottom of the shaft. I know there are dash-A instances watching all around me, whether I can see them or not, but I can’t shake the feeling that something down there is watching me. I’m worried that if I take my eyes off it, something might come flying up at me or maybe climb up the rails, but also that by staring at it, I’m just pissing it off. Damnit, why couldn’t you guys have just told me what you know? I know you know more than you’re saying. If it was just a hole, then you would have said that. What did you mean when you said there was no ground level? //**11:38 ~**// Another one. Level 45, Cell 44. This one looked angry, and he had a sign. The sign said “A fall from this height wouldn’t kill you. Unfortunately,”. I lost the staring contest with him pretty quickly. //**12:01 ~**// Something just happened. The shaft shook and there was a sudden upswell of air, accompanied by a deep bellowing sound. The platform was rocked back and forth, enough that if I had been near the edge and not harnessed in, I’d have been at risk of falling off. The lights in the shaft went off for a few seconds, and all of the lights in the cells turned on. Some of the SCP-9099-A instances were definitely holding up signs, but it was over too quickly for me to read any of them. I’m not sure what that was or if it’s happened before, but if it has, no one ever briefed me on it. If that last sign was anything to go by though, that guy in cell 45-44 knew it was coming. The platform’s still descending at the same rate though, so that hasn’t changed, but the vibration is getting stronger. I’m sure of it now. //**12:35 ~**// Level 22, Cell 81. This is the first one who isn’t standing. They’re huddled in a kind of fetal position, rocking back and forth, but still looking at me. They look a little skinnier and smaller than most of the others. Definitely the least threatening and most pathetic-looking.  I can’t help but wonder how long she’s been in that cell. //**12:49 ~**// Another message. Level 9, Cell 03. No sign this time, just written on the glass. I’m not going to guess with what. It said, “You See, We See, He Sees. Know; it’s why the rails move so slow,”. The instance itself looks deranged with its face pushed right up against the glass, like it was anticipating something. I can only hope it will be disappointed when I ride past it again in an hour. //**13:00 ~**// Just staring down again. I think I understand. //**13:15 ~**// I’ve hit the ground level, the one you said didn’t exist. It’s not a pit at all. There’s a transparent, concave covering over it, with a yellowish-green rim all around the perimeter. It’s an eye, and it sees me. It’s seen me this whole time, and now I see it. I can see a little into its mind as it peers into mine. It’s not just an eye; it has a body. I’m sure of it. Some kind of colossal cyclops. Not necessarily a giant from Greek mythology Cyclops, but that eye is attached to something. The vibration through the structure is its pulse, or its breathing, or some kind of vital rhythm. The more I saw it, the more I understood what it was, the more alive it became. It’s telling me this because the more information it gives me, the more it can take from me. They, whoever they were, tried to cover up the eye and failed, so they built around it instead. They did what the Foundation is doing, and what the Soviets did before them; they sent in only their most expendable people in the hopes of not losing anyone important or letting crucial information slip. But it didn’t work then, and it’s not working now. Every bit of information that they got on this thing, that you’re getting on this thing, came at the cost of it learning about them. To look upon the eye is to be seen by the eye. And once you are seen by the eye, you can’t be unseen. Directing your conscious attention away from a thing is as much an act of observation as looking at it, once you know it’s there. If we look, we make it stronger. If we look away, we still make it stronger, so we might as well look, right? That’s why all these things, all these people, are still here. And it’s why I’m still here. I’m not going back now. There’s a cell with the glass broken down here on the bottom level, a cell you never mentioned. At first, I was terrified that something was going to come out and attack me, but now I understand that that cell is for me. The eye will be watching me forever now, no matter where I am. If I go back to you guys now, I’ll end up locked up in a cell like that anyway. I know what you’ll do to me. I’m better off becoming a proper dash-A instance now. Can’t say I’m looking forward to you guys gassing me every time you miss a day of testing, but it still beats the alternative. I’d be the eye’s slave over yours any day. This place isn’t a panopticon; it’s an observatory, and you’re not the ones doing the observing. See you soon. SCP-9100.raw_content:
Junior Researcher Vo struggles with a life-stealing anomaly, hostile bureaucracy, and her own conscience in this decade-spanning psychological thriller.

  • 

    close

    Info

    X

    Author: Jezixo

    Preview: Junior Researcher Vo struggles with a life-stealing anomaly, hostile bureaucracy, and her own conscience in this decade-spanning psychological thriller.

    ⚠️ Content warning: strong language, time anxiety, mentions of a plane crash, self harm, suicide, trauma, mental illness, memory loss, regret, medical investigations, and implied (non-graphic depictions of) torture.

⚠️ content warning

by Jezixo

Audit: A12.86.2026

User: AU-350

Greetings, auditor.

The committee requests you determine how actions at the Minor Anomalies Unit at Site-86 led to the expenditure of $890 million in Foundation emergency funds and $1.9 billion in estimated losses.

Relevant documents and events have been collected for your review.

Kindly submit your recommendations at least 24 hours prior to the A12 hearing.

2/9100 LEVEL 2/9100
CLASSIFIED
Item #: SCP-9100
pending

Akron, OH.

Special Containment Procedures

SCP-9100 is the subject of an ongoing investigation. Field operatives will monitor local news, social media, and assisted living facilities in Akron, propagating a cover story attributing all symptoms to age-related cognitive decline and/or post-traumatic stress disorder.

Description

SCP-9100 is an anomaly speculated to account for rapid mental health decline in a subset of the Akron, OH population immediately following the 2014 Akron mid-air disaster. Affected individuals, primarily senior citizens, become convinced they have "skipped" several decades of their life, with no memory of the intervening years.

  • The duration of missing time varies between subjects, averaging 35 years.
  • The whereabouts of every subject during the relevant time periods are accounted for.
  • With prompting, subjects are eventually able to recall the missing memories, albeit with a lower fidelity commonly described as a “dream”.
  • Most subjects express dissociation from their own appearance, with deprecating comments about the state of their hands, skin, or teeth.
  • Subjects affected by SCP-9100 exhibit a drastically increased likelihood of compounding comorbid mental health disorders, such as depression, anxiety, self-harm and suicidal tendencies.

Discovery

On 3.1.2014, a Boeing 737-200 collided mid-air with a McDonnell Douglas MD-80 ascending from Akron-Fulton Airport. The 737 crashed in East Akron and the MD-80 in Goodyear Heights, killing all 112 aboard the two aircraft and 29 people on the ground. Scattered wreckage from the two planes set fire to several buildings and caused significant property damage.

During cleanup operations, Foundation personnel embedded with first responders became aware of a developing rumor that older members of the population had been unusually affected by the disaster. The extreme similarity of reported symptoms suggested anomalous phenomena.

28 Persons of Interest (PoI) have been identified with complaints matching the description of SCP-9100. All PoI were personally affected by the air crash, either by witnessing the event, suffering property loss, losing family members, or being directly injured by falling debris and resultant fires. SCP-9100-related complaints started immediately after these stressors occurred. Support networks (friends/family/caregivers) commonly reported this change as a sudden and unexplained shift in personality.

As SCP-9100 is presumed to pose a low risk to the public, it was assigned to the Minor Anomalies Unit at Site-86 in Medina County, OH.

Research Updates

4.2.2014: Site–86 initiated an investigation to identify SCP-9100’s cause and mechanisms of action, and if possible, develop a means to treat affected individuals or protect the public from future occurences.

[+2 DAYS]

4.4.2014: Head of Research Dr. Stuart Finlay was assigned by Site Director Harry Talbot. This was Finlay’s first case at Site–86 following his transfer from Site–210 in Dover, UK.

  • To assist in the investigation, Finlay requisitioned a seven-person team of statistics and parapsychology experts.
  • Finlay was assigned Junior Researcher Dr. Marissa Vo.

[+5 DAYS]

4.9.2014 – Interview 12 of 28 – Rhonda Barnes (PoI-12)

FACILITATORS: Drs Finlay and Vo

SUBJECT: Rhonda Barnes (76 y/o)

<Excerpt begins>

Barnes: I dropped my fork.

Vo: I’m sorry?

Barnes: My fork fell under the table, and I bent over to pick it up. That’s when it happened – that must have caused it, somehow.

Vo: Maybe we can start at the beginning, what–

Barnes: [Interrupting] We were at dinner. A friend's house – Owen Parsons – for dinner. It was Andy – my husband, and Owen, and Lauren – that’s Owen’s wife – and his kids…

Vo: [Interrupting] That’s okay ma’am, we don’t need everyone’s names. Just tell us what happened.

Barnes: We finished dinner, and we were talking about… football. I dropped my fork, I bent over to pick it up, and when I looked up there was a man, in a nurse uniform, in front of me. He was explaining that my husband had died. I thought, “that's not possible, he’s sitting right here.” And I looked around and realized I wasn't at dinner anymore. I was here.

[Subject gestures around the room.]

Barnes: I asked where I was, and they said this was… well I don’t remember what they called it, but it’s a nursing home, isn't it? They tried to tell me I'd been here a while.

Vo: Yes, we were told you’ve been at Sunrise Crossing for a few years. But you’re saying that, for you, this change was instantaneous?

Barnes: Instantaneous. That's a good word for it. Yes. Like… walking through a door.

Vo: Ma'am, I’d like you to think carefully for a moment – do you remember anything, between grabbing the fork and waking up here?

Barnes: No. I…

[Silence on recording.]

Barnes: Well, there is something. It was a dream. Some… long, complicated dream and there were… faces.

[Silence on recording, lasting over a minute. Indistinct conversations are audible from the corridor outside.]

Barnes: I suppose I do remember… people. That nurse, I remember him from my dream. So… what, I’ve been asleep, this whole time?

Vo: That’s what we hope to find out, Mrs. Barnes.

Barnes: And then you’ll fix it?

Vo: Well, we–

Barnes: [Interrupting] You have to. You can't leave me here. Look, this is all wrong– we only just moved in. Andy's going to paint the nursery… I can't be old already, it's not– well it isn't fair. I have to go back. How can I get back?

<Excerpt ends>

[+1 WEEK]

4.14.2014 – Voice Memo – Dr. Stuart Finlay

Finlay: I request a team of stats and parapsych, and Talbot gives me one – junior – researcher. Marissa Vo, practically an intern.

Ha. All these years, and Talbot's still pissed. Nursing his wrath to keep it warm, and all that. Well. He's the one who fucked up – I just found it. It's his own fault they buried him here.

Site-86. Minor anomalies. The knackers yard.

Put myself here now, I suppose. Making trouble, as per. Well, teach me for giving a fuck.

Course, they always make out like it's a promotion. “In light of your years of stalwart service, you have been reassigned… to the middle of fucking nowhere."

But what are the chances I should land in the same shitheap as Talbot? He was fair beaming at the door when I arrived, still the same black dye-job and Buddy Holly glasses. Aye, no doubt that toffee-nosed git had something to do with it.

Here's the thing though – Vo is quality.

First thing she says – "How come they call you Wee Rasputin?" Pure gallus1.

I told her it's on account of my shaggy beard and short stature.

Instincts are sound, though. Fourteen interviews in one week, and she led half of them – knows when to push, when to hush. Carries a wee notepad everywhere – good sign.

And she listens. Not just to them, but to me. Doesnae care for my language, but she doesnae moan about it either. Asks my advice, says she wants to be like me one day. Fuck's sake.

Vo: [Distant] Sorry Doctor – did you call me over?

Finlay: Oh, eh – no that's alright there, Vo. All good for now. Back to it.

Vo: [Distant] Will do.

[Silence.]

Finlay: [Whispered] She wants to get into Parapsych, and they stuck her in the dump with us. This case will do her good though – fine chance to earn her stripes, do some proper science and help people who need it – that's what we're about.

Talbot didn't have a clue when he sent her to me – his kind of sick joke. Well, the jokes on you Talbot, you fucking bawbag2.

[+1 WEEK]

4.23.2014 – Study – Biographical Review of Persons of Interest

METHODOLOGY: Retrospective longitudinal study of 28 subjects, noting each subject’s “onset date”: the last day they could clearly remember before experiencing an apparent time skip and “waking up” in 2014.

KEY RESULTS: Life histories varied widely, but following their onset date all subjects led average, unremarkable lives with no distinguishing successes:

  • Despite decades of employment, all subjects uniformly failed to achieve positions of significant responsibility or authority, nor did they achieve distinction in any particular field.
  • Performance reviews (where available) frequently contained descriptors signifying compliance, punctuality, and/or inconspicuousness.
  • Subjects scored within 3 points of the 50th percentile on standardized tests taken after their onset dates (where available), including:
    • Iowa Test of Basic Skills (ITBS)
    • Aptitude Testing (ASVAB, DOT)
    • Military performance (DD214)
    • SAT, ACT, GED scores
    • Presidential Fitness Test
  • The events surrounding the 2014 mid-air disaster constituted the first significantly traumatic event any of the subjects had experienced since their onset date.

Looking at the lives of 28 people, what stands out is how little they stood out. Average in every way. About what you'd expect of someone stuck in a daydream, away with the faeries. But their friends and family didn't notice anything strange, so whatever this thing is, it's subtle.

–F

[+2 DAYS]

4.25.2014: Vo completed an archival review, identifying several historical cases matching the description of SCP-9100:

  • On May 15, 1916, William Zachery survived the collapse of the Crystal Restaurant in downton Akron, but was later hospitalized with psychatric concerns. Doctor’s notes remarked: "Patient exhibits confusional state, believing it to be the year 1874, despite no prior history of mental disturbance".
  • On April 11, 1965, after an F4 tornado struck Pittsfield, OH, four people were admitted to psychiatric care with symptoms matching SCP-9100. One of these, Adrianne Sunderland, was the granddaughter of William Zachery.
  • On February 18, 1991, a story in The Akron Beacon Journal reported that suicide rates among Akron’s senior population were roughly 10x the national average.

[+3 DAYS]

4.28.2014: Finlay and Vo hypothesized that the Persons of Interest had been under the influence of an as-yet unknown anomaly for most of their lives, and that psychological stress (a collapsing building, tornado, and events surrounding the air crash) had somehow released them.

  • The revised research objective was to identify and study a member of the public who was still under this influence (speculatively designated SCP-9100-A), if such a person existed.

[+5 DAYS]

5.3.2014 – Voice Memo – Dr. Stuart Finlay

Finlay: Vo broke yesterday. The last PoI interview – old lady, Samantha Morris – it got under her skin.

She tried to hide it, but she'd stopped taking notes, hands were shaking. Soon as the interview's over, she belts it to the ladies room. Comes out half an hour later, barely keeping it together. She was pissed about it, angry at herself and all.

She’ll be fine.

NAPEAGUE is a set of decontamination methodologies for SCP-9100, organized into seven stages of escalating intensity. NAPEAGUE is to be enacted only by trained research staff, to ensure fidelity to the procedure and the wellbeing of the subject.

The procedure begins at Stage 1, with a methodology selected randomly from the collection. If decontamination fails at the first stage, practitioners proceed to the next, and so on until decontamination is achieved.

The methodologies in each stage are designed to arouse a psychological stress response in the subject, with the goal of heightening their awareness via sympathetic nervous system response to such a degree that the effect of SCP-9100 is nullified. NAPEAGUE currently maintains a 100% success rate, though the precise means by which this response nullifies SCP-9100 is still unknown.

Awareness of specific NAPEAGUE methodologies has been demonstrated to increase resistance to them. As such, it is imperative no single individual be made aware of all of the potential methodologies. To date, over 150 methodologies have been approved for NAPEAGUE, contributed by eight staff members.

It is hypothesized that, in some cases, prior knowledge of the existence of NAPEAGUE, combined with deliberately vague public documentation of its methodologies, may be sufficient to cause spontaneous decontamination.

Following successful decontamination, all subjects are to receive rigorous psychological aftercare to minimize the likelihood or severity of post-traumatic stress disorder.

NAPEAGUE Stages

Stage 1 consists of informational stress, in which the subject is given information that should be highly distressing.

Stage 2 entails enhanced informational and sensory distress. The subject is given information combined with sensory stimuli (visual, auditory and olfactory) sufficient to cause significant mental stress.

Note: During application of NAPEAGUE, researchers are temporarily excused from stipulations in the ethical code of conduct which prohibit lying to a contained subject.

Stage 3 involves the application of cognitohazardous information18 of sufficiently low intensity as to avoid long-term psychological damage. This stipulation greatly reduces the number of viable cognitohazards available.

Note: Due to the extreme risk posed to the subject, Stages 4 and 5 require the express approval of the relevant Site Director.

Stage 4 introduces physical stress on the subject through a variety of means, including the application of force.

Stage 5 enhances the techniques used in Stage 4 by combining them with methods of psychological manipulation, prolonged deprivation, and sensory assault.

Note: Stages 6 and 7 require express approval of the O4 Council.

Stage 6 intensifies the methods introduced in Stage 5 via use of anomalous tools, materials, and effects to impart psychological stresses that would not be possible in standard euclidean geometries and/or linear time.

Stage 7 is without description.

Note: Additional experimentation is required to validate these approaches.

[…] Consciousness is not vital for bodily operations, yet it is fundamental to the brain's nature; a healthy brain lacking consciousness will continually attempt to reinitialize it, for reasons that are currently unknown. […]

Visualization of SCP-9100's propagation pattern.

9. D-Class are volunteer test participants sourced from prison populations, assisting the Foundation in exchange for reduced sentences.
10. Scots: to feel disgust or strong dislike.
11. Scots idiom, pejorative: “Has a superficially positive appearance that is belied by the reality.”
12. The Special Commendation for Outstanding Dedication and Achievement (SCODA) is the Foundation’s highest merit award, conferring a $5,000 prize and commemorative plaque. Neither Finlay nor Talbot had received this honor in their career.
13. Scots: angry.
14. Scots: physically assault.
15. Terminal narrative refers to the intense final desire of the originating human at the moment of their death. Fulfilling this will typically neutralize the spectre.
16. Scots: be quiet.
17. Scots idiom: to be in a state of confusion.
18. Information that is impossible for the human mind to process safely.
19. The O5 council is the Foundation’s highest authority. The members are known only by their designation, numbered O5-1 through O5-13.
20. To ensure participation, Dr. Vo informed staff their compliance would be monitored and that a $50 lunch voucher would be offered to whomever used it most often. At the conclusion of the experiment, an employee was selected at random to receive the prize.
21. Scots idiom: lit. “Many littles make a large.”
