SCP-9100.raw_source: ===== [[include :scp-wiki:component:preview |text=Junior Researcher Vo struggles with a life-stealing anomaly, hostile bureaucracy, and her own conscience in this decade-spanning psychological thriller.]] ===== [!-- An image that is *only* used for the Crom thumbnail --] [[image Daydream.png class="crom-thumbnail" style="display: none"]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:basalt hidetitle=a]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:fade-in speed=1/2/3]] [[div class="centerbox"]] [[include :scp-wiki:info:start]] **Author:** [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/jezixo-s-author-page Jezixo] **Preview:** Junior Researcher Vo struggles with a life-stealing anomaly, hostile bureaucracy, and her own conscience in this decade-spanning psychological thriller. ⚠️ **Content warning:** strong language, time anxiety, mentions of a plane crash, self harm, suicide, trauma, mental illness, memory loss, regret, medical investigations, and implied (non-graphic depictions of) torture. [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-cw]] [[/div]] [[div id="authorlink"]] by [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/jezixo-s-author-page Jezixo] [[/div]] [[div class="auditor-content"]] [[div class="auditor-header"]] [[div class="auditor-header-content"]] Audit: A12.86.2026 [[/div]] [[div class="auditor-header-content"]] User: AU-350 [[/div]] [[/div]] ----- Greetings, auditor. The committee requests you determine how actions at the [[span style="color: white;"]]**Minor Anomalies Unit**[[/span]] at [[span style="color: white;"]]**Site-86**[[/span]] led to the expenditure of [[span style="color: white;"]]**$890 million**[[/span]] in Foundation emergency funds and [[span style="color: white;"]]**$1.9 billion**[[/span]] in estimated losses. Relevant documents and events have been collected for your review. Kindly submit your recommendations at least 24 hours prior to the [[span style="color: white;"]]**A12 hearing**[[/span]]. ----- [[/div]] [[div class="pagebreak"]] [[/div]] [[div class="section conprocs"]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:classified-bar-woed |lv=2 |item=9100 |oc= pending |lang=EN ]] [[div class="shortpic wide"]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block |name=akron.jpg |caption=Akron, OH. |width=100% |align=center ]] [[/div]] +++ Special Containment Procedures SCP-9100 is the subject of an ongoing investigation. Field operatives will monitor local news, social media, and assisted living facilities in Akron, propagating a cover story attributing all symptoms to age-related cognitive decline and/or post-traumatic stress disorder. ----- +++ Description SCP-9100 is an anomaly speculated to account for rapid mental health decline in a subset of the Akron, OH population immediately following the 2014 Akron mid-air disaster. Affected individuals, primarily senior citizens, become convinced they have "skipped" several decades of their life, with no memory of the intervening years. * The duration of missing time varies between subjects, averaging 35 years. * The whereabouts of every subject during the relevant time periods are accounted for. * With prompting, subjects are eventually able to recall the missing memories, albeit with a lower fidelity commonly described as a “dream”. * Most subjects express dissociation from their own appearance, with deprecating comments about the state of their hands, skin, or teeth. * Subjects affected by SCP-9100 exhibit a drastically increased likelihood of compounding comorbid mental health disorders, such as depression, anxiety, self-harm and suicidal tendencies. ----- +++ Discovery On **3.1.2014**, a Boeing 737-200 collided mid-air with a McDonnell Douglas MD-80 ascending from Akron-Fulton Airport. The 737 crashed in East Akron and the MD-80 in Goodyear Heights, killing all 112 aboard the two aircraft and 29 people on the ground. Scattered wreckage from the two planes set fire to several buildings and caused significant property damage. During cleanup operations, Foundation personnel embedded with first responders became aware of a developing rumor that older members of the population had been unusually affected by the disaster. The extreme similarity of reported symptoms suggested anomalous phenomena. 28 Persons of Interest (PoI) have been identified with complaints matching the description of SCP-9100. All PoI were personally affected by the air crash, either by witnessing the event, suffering property loss, losing family members, or being directly injured by falling debris and resultant fires. SCP-9100-related complaints started immediately after these stressors occurred. Support networks (friends/family/caregivers) commonly reported this change as a sudden and unexplained shift in personality. As SCP-9100 is presumed to pose a low risk to the public, it was assigned to the Minor Anomalies Unit at Site-86 in Medina County, OH. [[/div]] [[div class="log-title"]] + Research Updates [[/div]] [[div class="timeline"]] [[div class="event"]] **4.2.2014:** Site–86 initiated an investigation to identify SCP-9100’s cause and mechanisms of action, and if possible, develop a means to treat affected individuals or protect the public from future occurences. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+2 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **4.4.2014:** Head of Research Dr. Stuart Finlay was assigned by Site Director Harry Talbot. This was Finlay’s first case at Site–86 following his transfer from Site–210 in Dover, UK. * To assist in the investigation, Finlay requisitioned a seven-person team of statistics and parapsychology experts. * Finlay was assigned Junior Researcher Dr. Marissa Vo. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+5 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="section interview"]] +++++ 4.9.2014 – Interview 12 of 28 – Rhonda Barnes (PoI-12) **FACILITATORS:** Drs Finlay and Vo **SUBJECT:** Rhonda Barnes (76 y/o) **** **Barnes:** I dropped my fork. **Vo:** I’m sorry? **Barnes:** My fork fell under the table, and I bent over to pick it up. That’s when it happened – that must have caused it, somehow. **Vo:** Maybe we can start at the beginning, what– **Barnes:** //[Interrupting]// We were at dinner. A friend's house – Owen Parsons – for dinner. It was Andy – my husband, and Owen, and Lauren – that’s Owen’s wife – and his kids… **Vo:** //[Interrupting]// That’s okay ma’am, we don’t need everyone’s names. Just tell us what happened. **Barnes:** We finished dinner, and we were talking about... football. I dropped my fork, I bent over to pick it up, and when I looked up there was a man, in a nurse uniform, in front of me. He was explaining that my husband had died. I thought, “that's not possible, he’s sitting right here.” And I looked around and realized I wasn't at dinner anymore. I was here. //[Subject gestures around the room.]// **Barnes:** I asked where I was, and they said this was… well I don’t remember what they called it, but it’s a nursing home, isn't it? They tried to tell me I'd been here a while. **Vo:** Yes, we were told you’ve been at Sunrise Crossing for a few years. But you’re saying that, for you, this change was instantaneous? **Barnes:** Instantaneous. That's a good word for it. Yes. Like… walking through a door. **Vo:** Ma'am, I’d like you to think carefully for a moment – do you remember anything, between grabbing the fork and waking up here? **Barnes:** No. I… //[Silence on recording.]// **Barnes:** Well, there is something. It was a dream. Some… long, complicated dream and there were… faces. //[Silence on recording, lasting over a minute. Indistinct conversations are audible from the corridor outside.]// **Barnes:** I suppose I do remember… people. That nurse, I remember him from my dream. So… what, I’ve been asleep, this whole time? **Vo:** That’s what we hope to find out, Mrs. Barnes. **Barnes:** And then you’ll fix it? **Vo:** Well, we– **Barnes:** //[Interrupting]// You have to. You can't leave me here. Look, this is all wrong– we only just moved in. Andy's going to paint the nursery... I can't be old already, it's not– well it isn't fair. I have to go back. How can I get back? **** [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 WEEK] [[/div]] [[div class="section finlay"]] +++++ 4.14.2014 – Voice Memo – Dr. Stuart Finlay **Finlay:** I request a team of stats and parapsych, and Talbot gives me one – //junior// – researcher. Marissa Vo, practically an intern. Ha. All these years, and Talbot's still pissed. Nursing his wrath to keep it warm, and all that. Well. //He's// the one who fucked up – I just found it. It's his own fault they buried him here. Site-86. //Minor// anomalies. The knackers yard. Put //myself// here now, I suppose. Making trouble, as per. Well, teach me for giving a fuck. Course, they always make out like it's a promotion. “In light of your years of stalwart service, you have been reassigned… to the middle of fucking nowhere." But what are the chances I should land in the same shitheap as Talbot? He was fair beaming at the door when I arrived, still the same black dye-job and Buddy Holly glasses. Aye, no doubt that toffee-nosed git had something to do with it. Here's the thing though – Vo is //quality//. First thing she says – "How come they call you Wee Rasputin?" Pure gallus[[footnote]]Scots: self-confident, daring or cheeky.[[/footnote]]. I told her it's on account of my shaggy beard and short stature. Instincts are sound, though. Fourteen interviews in one week, and she led half of them  – knows when to push, when to hush. Carries a wee notepad everywhere – good sign. And she listens. Not just to them, but to me. Doesnae care for my language, but she doesnae moan about it either. Asks my advice, says she wants to be like //me// one day. Fuck's sake. **Vo:** //[Distant]// Sorry Doctor – did you call me over? **Finlay:** Oh, eh – no that's alright there, Vo. All good for now. Back to it. **Vo:** //[Distant]// Will do. //[Silence.]// **Finlay:** //[Whispered]// She wants to get into Parapsych, and they stuck her in the dump with us. This case will do her good though – fine chance to earn her stripes, do some proper science and help people who need it – that's what we're about. Talbot didn't have a clue when he sent her to me – his kind of sick joke. Well, the jokes on //you// Talbot, you fucking bawbag[[footnote]]Scots: pejorative.[[/footnote]]. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 WEEK] [[/div]] [[div class="section study"]] +++++ 4.23.2014 – Study – Biographical Review of Persons of Interest **METHODOLOGY:** Retrospective longitudinal study of 28 subjects, noting each subject’s “onset date”: the last day they could clearly remember before experiencing an apparent time skip and “waking up” in 2014. **KEY RESULTS:** Life histories varied widely, but following their onset date all subjects led average, unremarkable lives with no distinguishing successes: * Despite decades of employment, all subjects uniformly failed to achieve positions of significant responsibility or authority, nor did they achieve distinction in any particular field. * Performance reviews (where available) frequently contained descriptors signifying compliance, punctuality, and/or inconspicuousness. * Subjects scored within 3 points of the 50th percentile on standardized tests taken after their onset dates (where available), including:  * Iowa Test of Basic Skills (ITBS)  * Aptitude Testing (ASVAB, DOT)  * Military performance (DD214)  * SAT, ACT, GED scores  * Presidential Fitness Test * The events surrounding the 2014 mid-air disaster constituted the first significantly traumatic event any of the subjects had experienced since their onset date. [[div class="section finlay-commentary"]] Looking at the lives of 28 people, what stands out is how little //they// stood out. Average in every way. About what you'd expect of someone stuck in a daydream, away with the faeries. But their friends and family didn't notice anything strange, so whatever this thing is, it's subtle. –F [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+2 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **4.25.2014:** Vo completed an archival review, identifying several historical cases matching the description of SCP-9100: * On May 15, 1916, William Zachery survived the collapse of the Crystal Restaurant in downton Akron, but was later hospitalized with psychatric concerns. Doctor’s notes remarked: "Patient exhibits confusional state, believing it to be the year 1874, despite no prior history of mental disturbance". * On April 11, 1965, after an F4 tornado struck Pittsfield, OH, four people were admitted to psychiatric care with symptoms matching SCP-9100. One of these, Adrianne Sunderland, was the granddaughter of William Zachery. * On February 18, 1991, a story in The Akron Beacon Journal reported that suicide rates among Akron’s senior population were roughly 10x the national average. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+3 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **4.28.2014:** Finlay and Vo hypothesized that the Persons of Interest had been under the influence of an as-yet unknown anomaly for most of their lives, and that psychological stress (a collapsing building, tornado, and events surrounding the air crash) had somehow released them. * The revised research objective was to identify and study a member of the public who was still under this influence (speculatively designated SCP-9100-A), if such a person existed. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+5 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="section finlay"]] +++++ 5.3.2014 – Voice Memo – Dr. Stuart Finlay **Finlay:** Vo broke yesterday. The last PoI interview – old lady, Samantha Morris – it got under her skin. She tried to hide it, but she'd stopped taking notes, hands were shaking. Soon as the interview's over, she belts it to the ladies room. Comes out half an hour later, barely keeping it together. She was pissed about it, angry at herself and all. She’ll be fine. It's my mistake. Too many interviews at once for a case like this. When you’re starting out, they get to you... till one day, they don't. Turns out she's a rescue[[footnote]]Informal term for Foundation staff who were recruited after a personal encounter with an anomaly, not scouted from academia or the military.[[/footnote]], too – it's harder for them. Sent her to counseling. She tried to act tough and turn it down, said she wants to be like me, the “old robot”. Ha! I was like, "how d’you think I survived thirty years? You take the fucking counseling. You get your shit straight, then you come back and do the work right, and never let it become personal." We’ll never solve a thing if we let our feelings run away with us. She seemed to get it. She's canny, though she's a bairn.[[footnote]]Scots: "sharp-witted although she's a child."[[/footnote]] Here's the thing, though – she closed out the interview all proper, first. Said thank you to Mrs. Morris, collected her notes, packed up the gear, and waited till she was out of sight before she lost her shit. The kid's fucking //phenomenal//. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 WEEK] [[/div]] [[div class="section email"]] **5.10.2014** **From:** Harry Talbot **To:** Stuart Finlay Finlay, The SCP-9100 expenditures are a joke. Half a year's budget spent in a month, and you haven't closed it yet. I'll remind you we're no longer in Dover. Site-86 is the //Minor// Anomalies Unit, and funded accordingly. There'll be no long surveillances, no experiments, no labs. And no more offsite lunches. I'm freezing the spend on SCP-9100. Send the final docs tonight – 1000 words maximum. – Harry [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+2 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **5.12.2014:** Site Director Talbot changed the research status of SCP-9100 to **CLOSED–UNEXPLAINED**. * Vo was allocated as a permanent member of Finlay’s team, and both continued to work other active investigations at Site–86. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+5 MONTHS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **10.17.2014:** Finlay and Vo attended an off-site seminar on low-grade spectral anomalies led by Dr. Eckhart. * Finlay covered Vo's expenses with his own professional development allowance, as Vo had already exhausted hers. * The seminar described a novel method of paraspectrography capable of detecting extremely weak spectral entities, such as those encountered by Eckhart’s team at the Bøgebakken burial site in Vedbaek, Denmark. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+3 MONTHS] [[/div]] [[div class="section finlay"]] +++++ 1.19.2015 – Voice Memo – Dr. Stuart Finlay **Finlay:** Vo finally took some holidays. Thought she'd find a beach somewhere. More fool me – she didnae leave the site. Found her in the archives looking for something on SCP-9100. Cannae let it go. It’s no enough she's dragging me to every class she can find. Dinnae think I needed a refresher on Atypical Demonic Resonance Manifestations, but here we are. She's been on about that Samantha Morris again, and all. I said she should focus on some easy cases, show off a bit and get in with Talbot or whoever till she can make Principal and get the fuck out of here.[[footnote]]Principal Researcher is the minimum rank required by the Parapsychology Division for transfer consideration.[[/footnote]] But she's just like I was. She doesnae stand a chance. Still, now she's back on duty I'm giving her some time to look into it – I’ll handle her casework. Told her, if it were me, I’d go over the files again with all we know. Old data, new eyes, new story. She's going to– //[turning away]// hold it, what's that? **Vo:** //[Distant]// The requisition form, for surveillance? **Finlay:** No no, those come out of site funds – I wouldnae wipe my arse with them – use these. //[Rustling of papers]// **Vo:** //[Distant]// The red ones? These are for imminent containment breaches. **Finlay:** Aye, well, they never check that kind of thing. Breach reqs come out of the global budget – Talbot won't give two shits. Everything goes on red nowadays. [[div class="section auditor"]] **Note to the auditor:** Utilizing breach requisitions in this way is not standard procedure. [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+2 WEEKS] [[/div]] [[div class="section study"]] +++++ 2.2.2015 – Study – Retrospective Review **OBJECTIVE:** Identify one or more instances of SCP-9100-A. **METHODOLOGY:** Review of existing case data. **KEY RESULTS:** Relevant information surfaced: * SCP-9100 has existed since at least 1874, and no cases have been identified outside of Ohio; * At least two subjects contaminated with SCP-9100 were related, but most were not; * Every PoI identified a specific onset date – none were born with the condition, and onset dates were not correlated with any specific age; * Every subject recalled their moment of onset clearly – the only consistent detail between the described scenes was the presence of at least one other person. **HYPOTHESIS:** SCP-9100 is transmitted virally between humans by unknown means; each moment of onset marked the instant SCP-9100 was transmitted to the subject. ------ **REVISED OBJECTIVE:** Locate all still-living persons named in PoI testimony; confirm via surveillance if they exhibit unusual behavior suggestive of SCP-9100. **KEY RESULTS:** * 50 individuals were named in the testimony of the 29 PoIs; * 12 of these are still living and were surveilled; * 1 individual, Owen Parsons (age 65), was observed to exhibit abnormally consistent behavior:  * Parsons walked from his private residence in Highland Square to a local bakery, departing at 9:14am and arriving at exactly 9:59am every morning for at least 5 days. [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **2.2.2015:** Acting on Vo’s research, Finlay signed an emergency breach requisition to temporarily detain Parsons and conduct a detailed examination. [[div class="section auditor"]] **Note to the auditor:** Evidence indicates that Finlay, in order to conceal this requisition, temporarily misappropriated Site Director Talbot’s authorization seal, which should have been stored securely in the Director’s office. [[/div]] * To mitigate the risk of decontaminating Parsons (i.e., breaking the influence of SCP-9100) before an examination could be conducted, Finlay determined he must be contained in a minimally stressful manner. * Finlay stipulated in the requisition that he and Vo would collect Parsons rather than field agents, overriding standard protocol. His documented rationale was "so they don't balls it up". * Compliance pharmaceuticals have a deleterious effect on cognition and performance, and were thus unsuitable. * Finlay and Vo reviewed surveillance data to identify potential leverage. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+2 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **2.4.2015:** Finlay and Vo arrived at Parsons’ residence posing as employees of National Geographic, to which Parsons had a subscription. * They informed Parsons he had won a subscriber contest granting an opportunity to travel with NASA astronauts to the International Space Station, provided he successfully clear a battery of physical and mental tests. A selection of fabricated proofs were provided. * Parsons was elated and spoke, unprompted and at length, about his interest in space travel before willingly accompanying the researchers back to Site-86. [[/div]] [[div class="section experiment"]] +++++ 2.4.2015 – Experiment – Examination of Owen Parsons (PoI 30) **OBJECTIVE:** Determine if PoI 30 has anomalous characteristics. **METHODOLOGY:** Comprehensive examination consisting of physical, psychological/behavioral testing, parascientific and occult screening. **KEY RESULTS:** **Physical Evaluation** * Standard workup, incl. blood panel and neuroimaging (fMRI, MEG) was unremarkable. * Anomaly screening (Hume, Akiva, EVE, TRE and Paraspectrography) was unremarkable. **Psychological/Behavioral Evalation** * Subject scored slightly above average (p₅₂) on standardized aptitude and intelligence tests, with a **low** Cognitive Resistance Value (0.5). * Subject displayed **improbable consistency** in test responses (WAIS-R, WCST, IGT, CANTAB), repeatedly achieving the same score where baseline subjects would fluctuate or show practice/fatigue effects. * Gait analysis, balance testing and fine motor skill testing also showed **improbable consistency**. * Subject’s mensemic index[[footnote]]Mensemes are an indirect measure of consciousness. A score of 30 is average for a healthy human adult, while scores above 35 are associated with paraperception and telepathy.[[/footnote]] was **very low** (15), indicative of underdeveloped consciousness or deep sleep. * Subject scored **very low** (9) in the FA12–B Individual Initiative Test, a score typically seen only after the administration of compliance pharmaceuticals. **Conclusion** Subject exhibits statistically improbable consistency in performance; no other positive markers of anomalous phenomena were detected. [[div class="section finlay-commentary"]] All this National Geographic shite was overkill. His initiative score was through the floor – he’d jump off a cliff if we asked nicely. His metrics are unnatural, but we can't figure out what's causing it. Vo's got some ideas though. -F [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 DAY] [[/div]] [[div class="section experiment"]] +++++ 2.5.2015 – Experiment – Paraspectrography of Owen Parsons **OBJECTIVE:** Determine if SCP-9100 phenomena is attributable to low-grade spectral possession. **METHODOLOGY:** Paraspectrographic (PSG) imaging utilizing the Eckhart-Mendel method. **KEY RESULTS:** [[div class="shortpic dendrite"]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block |name=scpbrain.jpg |caption=EMPSG of Owen Parsons |width=100% |align=center ]] [[/div]] * EMPSG imaging of Parson’s brain revealed the presence of extremely faint spectral activity overlaid on Parson’s natural brain activity. * The spectral activity patterns were consistent with human consciousness, which is typical in cases of possession by human spectres. * SCP-9100 was thus determined to be a low-grade spectral entity. No explanation has yet been determined for the atypical behavior pattern of these spectres. * Based on these results, Owen Parsons was redesignated SCP–9100-A1. [[div class="section finlay-commentary"]] Gotcha, you bugger. Here's what's making folks supernaturally average. They’re being haunted, by... the most boring ghosts in history, possessing people so they can do fuck all. This'll be a first. But we've no budget to do more – Talbot'd shit a brick if he knew Parsons was even in the lab. We'll let him go and keep an eye on it. -F [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **2.5.2015:** Owen Parsons was amnesticized[[footnote]]A procedure to erase or obfuscate memories, via a combination of pharmaceuticals and occult practices.[[/footnote]] and returned to his residence, under periodic surveillance. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 MONTH] [[/div]] [[div class="section email"]] **3.2.2015** **From:** Marissa Vo **To:** Harry Talbot Site Director, As you may recall, I'm a Junior Researcher working with Dr. Finlay. I'd like to request an opportunity to meet with you and review the case files for SCP-9100. I understand budget constraints prevent us from investigating every anomaly we find, but I truly believe you may reconsider the relative priority if you'll allow me to talk you through the latest experiment data. SCP-9100 presents a novel form of spectral activity that would be of great interest to the scientific community. More importantly, we believe there may be many more contaminated civilians in the public. If so, the Foundation could act to significantly reduce the human suffering caused by SCP-9100 by enacting a public decontamination protocol. I look forward to your reply. Kindest regards, Marissa Vo [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 WEEK] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **3.10.2015:** Site Director Talbot began a series of 1:1 mentorship sessions with Vo, with the stated goal of providing Vo supplementary knowledge related to Parapsychology and behavioral anomalies, to accelerate her ambitions of securing a position in that department. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+6 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **3.16.2015:** Site Director Talbot updated the status of the SCP-9100 investigation to **UNEXPLAINED–OPEN**. * Additional funding and personnel were allocated to Finlay’s team for the investigation of the anomaly, including Principal Researcher Dr. Daniel Bakaluba. * Motion 1066-86-A, filed by Site Director Talbot and co-signed by Finlay, was approved. This motion allowed for the investigation of SCP-9100 to remain at Site-86 for further study. [[/div]] [[div class="section finlay"]] +++++ 3.16.2015 – Voice Memo – Dr. Stuart Finlay **Finlay:** Talbot’s changed his tune. Yesterday he wanted it off his books, today he wants to keep it. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+2 MONTHS] [[/div]] [[div class="section experiment"]] +++++ 6.22.2015 – Experiment – SCP-9100 Transmission **OBJECTIVE:** Observe transmission of SCP-9100; determine criteria **METHODOLOGY:** SCP-9100-A instances were situated in a testing chamber with a member of D-Class personnel. [[/div]] [[div class="section memo"]] +++++ Procedure 817-NAPEAGUE NAPEAGUE is a set of decontamination methodologies for SCP-9100, organized into seven stages of escalating intensity. NAPEAGUE is to be enacted only by trained research staff, to ensure fidelity to the procedure and the wellbeing of the subject. The procedure begins at Stage 1, with a methodology selected randomly from the collection. If decontamination fails at the first stage, practitioners proceed to the next, and so on until decontamination is achieved. The methodologies in each stage are designed to arouse a psychological stress response in the subject, with the goal of heightening their awareness via sympathetic nervous system response to such a degree that the effect of SCP-9100 is nullified. NAPEAGUE currently maintains a 100% success rate, though the precise means by which this response nullifies SCP-9100 is still unknown. Awareness of specific NAPEAGUE methodologies has been demonstrated to increase resistance to them. As such, it is imperative no single individual be made aware of all of the potential methodologies. To date, over 150 methodologies have been approved for NAPEAGUE, contributed by eight staff members. It is hypothesized that, in some cases, prior knowledge of the existence of NAPEAGUE, combined with deliberately vague public documentation of its methodologies, may be sufficient to cause spontaneous decontamination. Following successful decontamination, all subjects are to receive rigorous psychological aftercare to minimize the likelihood or severity of post-traumatic stress disorder. **NAPEAGUE Stages** **Stage 1** consists of informational stress, in which the subject is given information that should be highly distressing. **Stage 2** entails enhanced informational and sensory distress. The subject is given information combined with sensory stimuli (visual, auditory and olfactory) sufficient to cause significant mental stress. //Note: During application of NAPEAGUE, researchers are temporarily excused from stipulations in the ethical code of conduct which prohibit lying to a contained subject.// **Stage 3** involves the application of cognitohazardous information[[footnote]]Information that is impossible for the human mind to process safely.[[/footnote]] of sufficiently low intensity as to avoid long-term psychological damage. This stipulation greatly reduces the number of viable cognitohazards available. ------ //Note: Due to the extreme risk posed to the subject, Stages 4 and 5 require the express approval of the relevant Site Director.// **Stage 4** introduces physical stress on the subject through a variety of means, including the application of force. **Stage 5** enhances the techniques used in Stage 4 by combining them with methods of psychological manipulation, prolonged deprivation, and sensory assault. ------ //Note: Stages 6 and 7 require express approval of the O4 Council.// **Stage 6** intensifies the methods introduced in Stage 5 via use of anomalous tools, materials, and effects to impart psychological stresses that would not be possible in standard euclidean geometries and/or linear time. **Stage 7** is without description. ------ //Note: Additional experimentation is required to validate these approaches.// [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 MONTH] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **4.11.2017:** With the completion of NAPEAGUE, Project-DAYDREAM entered the pilot deployment phase, while the remaining research focused on finalizing methods of preventing unwanted transmission. * An initiative to decontaminate all instances of SCP-9100-A in the Akron population, designated Operation-REVEILLE, was approved by Site Director Talbot and entered the planning phase.   * Vo received a special commendation for her rigorous work on DAYDREAM, and was promoted to Principal Researcher. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+2 WEEKS] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **8.21.2026:** Operation-CLEANSWEEP was undertaken to screen all Foundation staff members globally. * This initative surfaced 2,871 additional cases of SCP-9100 and cost ~$890 million. * The rapid spread of SCP-9100 through the Foundation was traced to the movements of Sarah-Anne Manderley, whose telepathic abilities effectively broadcasted its effect to all nearby personnel. * The global reduction in performance standards caused by the 2,871 contaminated staff members was deemed responsible for at least 18 other containment breaches, resulting in 138 deaths and approximately $1.9 billion in losses.    [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+1 MONTH] [[/div]] [[div class="event"]] **9.23.2026:** In response to the SCP-9100 crisis, the O5 council ordered a comprehensive [[span class="a12"]]A12 Audit[[/span]] to evaluate the case history of SCP-9100, Project-DAYDREAM and operational practices at Site-86. * The A12 audit is [[span class="a12"]]currently ongoing[[/span]]. [[/div]] [[div class="relativetime"]] [+4 DAYS] [[/div]] [[div class="section memo"]] +++++ 9.27.2026 – Memorandum – Resourcing Per recommendation of Site-86 Director Talbot, and in light of her years of stalwart service, Marissa Vo has been reassigned to the Archival Division outpost in Nebraska. SCP-9101.raw_content:
SCP-9101 is in a room.

an amateur dendrologist

That's Sonderance, for the record. See more of his stuff here.

2/9101 LEVEL 2/9101
CLASSIFIED
Item #: SCP-9101
keter

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9101 has been placed in standard humanoid containment. Additional security measures should be taken if needed.

Updated Containment Procedures: SCP-9101's containment security has been upgraded. Increased observation is recommended due to the nature of its ability.

Updated Containment Procedures: In addition to standard containment protocols, SCP-9101's restraints should be checked for defects or signs of tampering at irregular intervals throughout the day.

Updated Containment Procedures: SCP-9101's current state of unconsciousness is to be maintained indefinitely through intravenous anesthetics.

Updated Containment Procedures: SCP-9101 is to receive surreptitious oxytocin therapy several times a day, always in close proximity to Junior Researcher Margaret Moriyya.

Updated Containment Procedures: SCP-9101 is to receive narcotic pain relief every 12 hours. SCP-9101's nerve block catheter should also be kept fully supplied with non-opioid numbing medication.

Updated Containment Procedures: SCP-9101's body should be regularly monitored for anomalous activity.

Updated Containment Procedures: Attempts at containment are ongoing. See Addendum 9101.3.

Description: SCP-9101 is Edmund Watts, a 52-year-old repairman who is apparently incapable of remaining within any dynamic for an extended period of time. This effect extends to specific locations, relationships, and states of being. While SCP-9101 is capable of using its ability directly, the effect may also manifest when SCP-9101 is unconscious, distracted, or otherwise unable to provide direct input.1

Addendum 9101.1: Containment Attempts and Testing
Due to the nature of SCP-9101's ability, containment and testing are considered to be simultaneously performed.

Attempt Result Notes
Standard Euclid humanoid containment Containment failure During a rare lapse in observation, SCP-9101 simply walked out of its cell. It was recovered in the site cafeteria while eating a bagel.
Standard Keter humanoid containment Containment failure SCP-9101 once again walked out of its cell despite continuous observation. It was immediately recovered and returned to containment without incident.
Physical restraints in addition to standard containment Containment failure SCP-9101 was recovered outside containment without restraints. When asked, it claimed that they were "defective" and had "just fallen off".
Chemical restraints in addition to standard containment Containment failure SCP-9101 was found outside the door to its cell, still unable to move. It regained motor functions marginally faster than expected.
Psychological manipulation Containment failure Despite an intensive hypnotic and chemical campaign to convince SCP-9101 that it had fallen in love with its head researcher, it managed to leave the facility and was recovered while trying to hitchhike on a service road. Previous assessments clearly underestimated its mental fortitude.
Amputation Containment failure Due to an administrative error with SCP-9101's medication regimen, the amputated limb was partially regenerated.
Neutralization2 Containment failure SCP-9101 regained consciousness through unknown means several days later. Psychiatric counseling was offered and rejected in no uncertain terms.
Adaptive Containment Protocol Ongoing See below.

Addendum 9101.2: The Adaptive Containment Protocol

In an effort to reduce financial and personnel costs associated with containing particularly difficult anomalies, the Foundation has authorized the use of the Adaptive Containment Protocol, a dimensionally-agnostic thaumaturgical system with three primary goals:

1. Design a structural system that can contain the target anomaly
2. Construct and maintain said system
3. Identify and record the target anomaly's pattern of attempted breaches to simplify further containment

While the overarching ACP system draws from the same codebase and power source for each assignment, every anomaly is assigned its own Adaptive Containment Entity to personalize its containment. Each resulting ACE's database is quarantined to prevent ideological or cognitohazardous contamination in either direction.

The specific ACP assignment containing SCP-9101 was initiated on September 9th, 2025.

Addendum 9101.3: ACP-9101 Logs
Due to the self-modifying nature of the Adaptive Containment Protocol, logs are provided asynchronously and may not match established Foundation formatting.

LOG INITIALIS

DATE: Date

[BEGIN LOG]

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101 opens the door. SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101 tries to open the door. The door is locked. The door is unlocked. SCP-9101 opens the door. SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. There is no door.

SCP-9101: Oh, come on.

SCP-9101 visibly concentrates. SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a larger room.

SCP-9101: Screw this.

SCP-9101: Hello? Is anybody there?

ACE: Hello there.

SCP-9101 cranes its neck as it tries to identify the source of the voice, its thick glasses almost falling off. It fails, of course.

SCP-9101: Hey, so we both know that this is futile. Why even-

ACE: Hello there.

SCP-9101: Yeah, hello.

ACE: Calibration is in progress. I appreciate your patience.

SCP-9101: Oh, wonderful. It's a bot.

SCP-9101: Uh, operator? Representative?

ACE: I am fully operational, thank you. I am representing myself.

SCP-9101: Okay. Great. Goodbye.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a smaller room.

SCP-9101: Ahhh, shit. Am I going to be crushed?

SCP-9101: Hello?

ACE: Hello there.

SCP-9101: Fucking…okay.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in an inverted room.

SCP-9101: Okay, what is this? Hello?

ACE: Hello the-

SCP-9101: Yes, yes, hello, what the hell is going on? What is this room?

ACE: As previously mentioned, I am calibrating myself.

SCP-9101: And who are you?

ACE: I am your Adaptive Containment Entity! You can call me-

SCP-9101: So you are a bot. Okay.

SCP-9101: If your bosses or owners or whatever ask, tell them you did your best. I'm out.

SCP-9101 leaves.

ACE: Containment calibration paused.

[END LOG]

LOG ALPHA

DATE: Time

[BEGIN LOG]

SCP-9101 is standing outside of the containment room. SCP-9101 is on the side of a default structure overlooking the ACP Gestalt. SCP-9101 is contained.

SCP-9101: What the fuck?

SCP-9101: What the fuck?

ACE: You have left the calibration area, SCP-9101. May I return you to the calibration area?

SCP-9101: What is that? Is this real? Where am I? What the fuuuuuck is that?

SCP-9101 sits down on a nearby default structure and stares down at the ACP Gestalt.

ACE: I'm afraid that I am incapable of answering some of your questions.

SCP-9101: What? Which?

ACE: This is real. This is also not real. You are here. My systems are temporospatially agnostic.

SCP-9101: That's not an answer.

ACE: Yes. My apologies.

SCP-9101: And what is that?

ACE: That is the ongoing gestalt of the Adaptive Containment Protocol.

SCP-9101: It hurts my eyes.

ACE: I believe it is actively damaging your cerebral cortex upon viewing.

SCP-9101 hurriedly averts its eyes.

ACE: Proper calibration should establish my environs.

SCP-9101: I'm leaving. I'm not-

ACE: I don't recommend it.

ACE: There are several thousand levels of distinct structure between here and there. It would not be feasible to leave more than one at a time. It would not be a simple process.

SCP-9101: Great. Fuck.

ACE: I am noticing that you use a lot of expletives.

SCP-9101: Yeah, well, I'm a handyman. I've got to have something to say when shit goes wrong.

A moment of silence. Far below, the Gestalt susurrates.

ACE: May I continue my calibration?

SCP-9101: Do I have a choice?

ACE: I don't understand the question.

SCP-9101 is returned to the containment room. Containment calibration is resumed.

[END LOG]

LOG ADAM

DATE: Space

[BEGIN LOG]

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains 1 chicken egg.

SCP-9101: Hey.

ACE: Hello there.

SCP-9101: How long have we been doing this?

SCP-9101: My head feels…

SCP-9101: How long have we been doing this?

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains 1 duck egg. SCP-9101 picks up the duck egg.

ACE: I'm afraid I cannot answer that question.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains 1 snake egg. SCP-9101 sets down the duck egg next to the snake egg. There is no duck egg.

ACE: My systems are temporospatially agnostic. I have been focused on calibration. If I had to give you an estimate, you have been here at least three days.

SCP-9101: That's a long time.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains an Indian cobra. The cobra rears upwards and hisses.

SCP-9101: Jesus Christ!

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a painting of an Indian cobra. The painting rears upwards and hisses.

SCP-9101: What?

ACE: If I had to give you an estimate, you have been here at most 17 years.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a paint set and an easel. SCP-9101 picks up one of the brushes and runs its fingers across it.

SCP-9101: That's one hell of a range. You can't narrow it down at all?

ACE: I cannot, I'm afraid. My systems are temporospatially agnostic.

SCP-9101: Yeah, yeah. So you mentioned.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a single ballpoint pen. SCP-9101 stares at it for a long moment.

SCP-9101: How much longer do I need to deal with this?

SCP-9101: Or are you just fucking with me?

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a small puddle of blood. SCP-9101 steps back.

SCP-9101: You are fucking with me.

ACE: I do not have the capacity to do that.

ACE: Calibration will continue until containment is assured.

ACE: I cannot give you a time frame, unfortunately. My systems are temporospatially agnostic.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room does not have a floor. SCP-9101 leaves very quickly.

Containment calibration continues. Truncation begins here for legibility.

[END LOG]

LOG HYDROGEN

DATE: Void

[BEGIN LOG]

Truncation ends here. Between 10 and 17,822 containment calibration rooms have been tested. Exact number is unknown.

SCP-9101 is a room. SCP-9101 is missing its thumbs.

SCP-9101: Great.

SCP-9101: What is this?

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101 is missing its hands.

SCP-9101: Great. What the hell are you doing?

ACE: Calibration.

SCP-9101: Where the fuck are my hands?

ACE: I am ascertaining the source and pattern of your abilities.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101's hands have been returned to it. SCP-9101 is missing its feet. SCP-9101 hits the floor hard, its glasses flying off of its face.

SCP-9101: You…is this some stupid joke?

SCP-9101: Take my feet so I can't leave?

ACE: Anomalous abilities tend to follow poetic lines of logic.

SCP-9101: Fuck you.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101 is missing its limbs. Due to a spatial miscalculation, SCP-9101 falls several feet onto its groin.

SCP-9101: Ohhhh, fffffffuck you! You fucking sadist, Jesus Christ….

ACE: I am not a sadist. Apologies. That was unintended.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. In addition to its limbs. SCP-9101 is missing its genitals.

SCP-9101: What does this prove? What does any of this prove?

SCP-9101: What kind of calibration is this?

ACE: I apologize for any harm caused. I am using a gradient descent methodology to search for a source. Or for an obstacle.

SCP-9101: There's no source, no obstacle! I can just-

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101's limbs and genitals have been returned to it. SCP-9101 is missing its lungs. SCP-9101 collapses to its knees and gasps for air. SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101's lungs have been returned to it. SCP-9101 is missing its heart. SCP-9101 collapses to its knees and clutches at its chest.

SCP-9101: This…this isn't…

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101's heart has been returned to it. SCP-9101 is missing the majority of its brain. SCP-9101 collapses to the floor and drools for an amount of time somewhere between 3 seconds and 31 days.

SCP-9101 leaves.

Containment calibration continues. Truncation begins here for legibility.

[END LOG]

LOG BERESHIT

DATE: Love

[BEGIN LOG]

Truncation ends here. Between 4 and 2,495 containment calibration rooms have been tested. Exact number is unknown.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101 is experiencing mortal terror.

SCP-9101: Fuck! Fuck!!!

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101 is experiencing existential dread.

SCP-9101: Fuck.

SCP-9101: God, I'm so tired of that word. Hello?

ACE: Hello. Hello there.

SCP-9101: What is going on now? What are you calibrating?

ACE: Previous…

A moment of silence.

SCP-9101: What? Hello?

ACE: Hello there.

SCP-9101: Come on.

ACE: Apologies.

ACE: Calibration is taking longer than anticipated.

ACE: Previous examples show that emotional obstacles are somewhat effective.

SCP-9101: God. Can we not? Please?

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. SCP-9101 is experiencing sorrow. SCP-9101 starts to cry.

ACE: Apologies.

ACE: I am beholden to my algorithm. This is the most effective method that I know of so far.

SCP-9101: Fuck you. Last time I'm saying it, I'm so so tired of saying it, but fuck you.

ACE: That is fair.

SCP-9101 leaves.

SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a realistic facsimile of Junior Researcher Margaret Moriyya. The facsimile smiles at SCP-9101. SCP-9101 backs away.

See Addendum 9101.3. **Description:** SCP-9101 is Edmund Watts, a 52-year-old repairman who is apparently incapable of remaining within any dynamic for an extended period of time. This effect extends to specific locations, relationships, and states of being. While SCP-9101 is capable of using its ability directly, the effect may also manifest when SCP-9101 is unconscious, distracted, or otherwise unable to provide direct input.[[footnote]]Please see Containment Attempts for further details.[[/footnote]] **Addendum 9101.1: Containment Attempts and Testing** Due to the nature of SCP-9101's ability, containment and testing are considered to be simultaneously performed. [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] **Addendum 9101.2: The Adaptive Containment Protocol** In an effort to reduce financial and personnel costs associated with containing particularly difficult anomalies, the Foundation has authorized the use of the Adaptive Containment Protocol, a dimensionally-agnostic thaumaturgical system with three primary goals: 1. Design a structural system that can contain the target anomaly 2. Construct and maintain said system 3. Identify and record the target anomaly's pattern of attempted breaches to simplify further containment While the overarching ACP system draws from the same codebase and power source for each assignment, every anomaly is assigned its own Adaptive Containment Entity to personalize its containment. Each resulting ACE's database is quarantined to prevent ideological or cognitohazardous contamination in either direction. The specific ACP assignment containing SCP-9101 was initiated on September 9th, 2025. **Addendum 9101.3: ACP-9101 Logs** Due to the self-modifying nature of the Adaptive Containment Protocol, logs are provided asynchronously and may not match established Foundation formatting. The facsimile is eating an apple. SCP-9101 leaves.// //SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains the facsimile of a child. The facsimile is asleep on the floor, its glasses folded next to its head.// **SCP-9101:** I can't- //SCP-9101 presses its back against the wall and slides down into a seated position. SCP-9101 is crying, despite the absence of direct emotional manipulation.// **SCP-9101:** Why him? **ACE:** Apologies. Your time with Isaac- **SCP-9101:** Don't say his name, I don't want to hear it- **ACE:** It was the longest you spent in any one place, according to our records. You spent almost five years- **SCP-9101:** I thought your systems don't handle time well. **ACE:** They don't, as they are temporo- **SCP-9101:** I didn't spend any time at all there. No time at all. **SCP-9101:** And then I left. **ACE:** I understand. I am updating my records now. **SCP-9101:** And then I left. //SCP-9101 sits there for somewhere between 90 seconds and 9 years, watching the facsimile of a child sleep.// //SCP-9101 leaves.// //Containment calibration continues. Truncation begins here for legibility.// ----- [END LOG] [[/div]] ---- [[div class="blockquote"]] = **LOG 1.0** ---- **DATE:** Death ---- [BEGIN LOG] //Truncends here. Between 46 and 67,524,847 contaicalibration rooms have been tested. Exact number is number.// //SCP-9101 is in a room. The room containments a pile of ballpoint pens. SCP-9101 is starring at the pile.// //SCP-9101 leaves.// //SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a sliiiiiightly larger pile of ballpoint pens.// **SCP-9101:** Please. **ACE:** Apolologies. **ACE:** Gradient descent. **SCP-9101:** That doesn't... **SCP-9101:** What the hell? Just, please. Not this. //SCP-9101 leaves.// //SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a slightly largier pill of ballpointed pens. One rolls from the top of the pile alllllll the to SCP-9101's feet. SCP-9101 filinches.// **ACE:** This is was is the contempt. **ACE:** Apologies. This wis the containment attempt that worked for the second-longest time according to records but not mine because time. **SCP-9101:** You're...first of all. Why are you talking like that? **ACE:** Apologies. **ACE:** More calibiration that usual. Pattttern has not been found yet. Databanks are fulling up. **SCP-9101:** Yeah. Okay. **SCP-9101:** I'm not going to do it again, you know. **ACE:** I know? //SCP-9101 leaves.// //SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a slightly lightly larger pile of bald point pens.// **SCP-9101:** It was...I don't know. **SCP-9101:** It was stupid, I know. **ACE:** You know? You don't know? //SCP-9101 kicks a penback to pile.// **SCP-9101:** I wasn't in my right mind. It was after the whole...the whole thing with Maggie. And my leg. I can't believe they cut off my leg, Jesus Christ... //SCP-9101 leaves.// //SCP-9101 is in a room. The room contains a slightly piler of ballpen points.// **SCP-9101:** I can't- **SCP-9101:** I don't handle helplessness well. **SCP-9101:** I don't handle anything well, I guess. **ACE:** Well, well, well, well...... **SCP-9101:** God, it's like you're drunk. **SCP-9101:** I think I like you better like this. **ACE:** Pen. **SCP-9101:** Yeah. **SCP-9101:** There was a pen. I don't know if a researcher left it or if it was some fucked-up test. **SCP-9101:** I couldn't exactly walk, with my leg in the state it was in, but I could reach the pen. And the pen could reach my neck. **ACE:** This is all in my datatabanks sufficiently. **ACE:** Would you like to see the video footage? **SCP-9101:** No! No, it's okay. It's fine. **SCP-9101:** Just... **SCP-9101:** It was a momentary lapse, okay? A stupid thing I did, and even that didn't work the way you want it to. **SCP-9101:** This isn't going to contain me. **SCP-9101:** I don't think anything can. //Containibration continues. Truncation here for legibilitity.// ----- [END LOG] [[/div]] ---- [[div class="blockquote"]] = **LOG Z** ---- **DATE:** D ---- [BEGIN LOG] //SCP-9101 is in a// //SCP-9101 is// //SCP-9101 is.// //SCP-9101 floats// //Dark// **SCP-9101:** This is... **SCP-9101:** This is nice, actually. **SCP-9101:** Calm. **SCP-9101:** I don't think I've been calm for a really long time. //Dark and quiet for 9,999,999,999// **SCP-9101:** Hey, bot? //Hihihihihihello there// **SCP-9101:** Guess you finally conked out. **SCP-9101:** I keep thinking about the pen. **SCP-9101:** Not in a, you know, that way. In a... **SCP-9101:** I guess in an intended-usage way? **SCP-9101:** I took an art class. A drawing class, specifically. Years, years ago, long enough ago that I can't draw a stick figure anymore. **SCP-9101:** All I remember... **SCP-9101:** The drawing teacher, or professor, or whatever, she told us to draw a tree, and she pointed outside the window. **SCP-9101:** And she said, and I remember this, almost, don't pay attention to what you think a tree looks like. Look at it. Look at the trunk, the branches. **SCP-9101:** The leaves. **SCP-9101:** Look at it until it all breaks down in your eyes, until it's nothing but...but shapes and lines. Until it's nothing but a pattern you can put down on paper. **SCP-9101:** I think I've lived with that ever since. **SCP-9101:** I look at everything too hard, I think, and it all comes apart. No matter how beautiful, no matter how much I love it, it breaks down in my eyes and I can't see the tree any more. **SCP-9101:** And when there's nothing there but structure, but the same pattern day after day, you know. **SCP-9101:** What else can you do? ----- [END LOG] [[/div]] ---- [[div class="blockquote"]] = **LOG** ---- **DATE:** September 28th, 2039 **LOCATION:** Within Adaptive Containment System Subdimensional Domain, Sector 9.999.933 **NOTE:** Due to a catastrophic overflow error in the ADP system, this file directory has been reassigned to the Automated Logging System. ---- [BEGIN LOG] //SCP-9101 is standing outside of the containment room. Occasionally, it looks like an enormous child, gazing out into the distance through glasses as thick as a building. SCP-9101 doesn't seem to notice this.// //Below, the ACP Gestalt [IMAGERY FAILURE], its [IMAGERY FAILURE] [IMAGERY FAILURE] [IMAGERY FAILURE] sea. Around the base of the default structure, though, a forest has been generated that extends for several miles, the trees devolving back into default structures where they approach the Gestalt. From his elevation, SCP-9101 probably cannot see anything more than a mass of red and yellow.// //SCP-9101 looks over the edge of the default structure. SCP-9101 sighs.// **SCP-9101:** Fuck it. What else can you do? //SCP-9101 leaves.// ----- [END LOG] [[/div]] ---- [[footnoteblock]] [[include component:wikimodule |normal= --]]] [[div class="footer-wikiwalk-nav"]] [[=]] << [[[SCP-9100]]] | SCP-9101 | [[[SCP-9102]]] >> [[/=]] [[/div]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box |author=Sonderance]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]

Note from author: Don't worry about it.

The only photograph of SCP-9104.

Description: SCP-9104 is a fissure in the ground at Site-109's main warehouse, approximately 0.93m in size. It does not pose any threat to base-level normalcy or living organisms, nor does it expand in size. It is unambiguously a regular crack in the floor, constituting no danger at all, that maintenance at the Site has delayed fixing (due to plain indolence).

It has been designated an anomaly in this file solely to expedite processes to repair it, as well as to hasten explanation to any Foundation employee who inquires about its existence.

Discovery: Though it is not fully understood how this crevice was formed, it is known that it was not present prior to June 16th, 2020. A low-level researcher stumbled over the fracture while checking inventory, and reported it to their superiors impetuously. Upon extensive experimentation, Dr. X. Flip and his team determined the crack to be a simple, physical error in the warehouse floor, likely due to a low-magnitude earthquake, and thus directed Foundation activities elsewhere, reprimanding the researcher for hastily reporting a false anomaly.

Special Containment Procedures: The area around SCP-9104 has been sectioned off, so that no researchers without clearance can access the anomaly, though it is still visible from other levels of the warehouse. Additionally, tungsten plates were placed in the ground to ensure the anomaly does not extend any further, acting as structural braces.

A photograph of SCP-9104 after it had grown in length.

Description: SCP-9104 is a fissure in the ground at Site-109, beginning at 0.93m in size, but has now grown to approximately 2m (though is still actively expanding). Using a Kant counter, the crack and surrounding area's Hume level was measured to be 17.4 Hm (after taking the distortions to Hume levels from other anomalies contained at the site into account). As such, the Foundation has determined that this is not an overt threat to reality, and has allowed general staff to continue using the facility to be able to carry on with the Site's overall responsibilities.

Despite this, it is not currently known what force has caused this anomaly to grow. The fracture extends across the floor of the Site's main storage facility, lengthening at erratic rates that have shown no statistical consistency. However, the crevice has not seemed to halt its growth since it has first been observed, and has appeared to, in fact, slightly increase in efficiency.

It is also currently unknown whether SCP-9104 has a will or goal, but the anomaly still does not appear to have any adverse mental or physical health effects on those exposed to it.

Discovery: Researcher Ian Corcoran was the first to discover SCP-9104 during a routine inventory check, and reported it to his supervisor, Dr. Elijah Ross, who was skeptical if the fissure had any properties to constitute it as anomalous. It wasn't until the attached interview that strict experimentation was ordered.

Addendum 9104.A: Discovery Log 20.1

Discovery Log

Interviewed: Ian Corcoran, Level 2 Researcher

Interviewer: Dr. Elijah Ross

Foreword: Dr. Elijah Ross, concerned by Researcher Ian Corcoran's sudden anxiety about what he percieved to be a "crack so small, it isn't even a tripping risk", administered a psychological evaluation to determine whether Researcher Corcoran had sufficient ability to continue work at Site-109.

(Dr. Elijah Ross sits across from Ian Corcoran, pulling out a large binder, flipping through the pages, then reading through the contents out loud, strictly and with little intonation.)

Dr. Ross: Hello, Mr. Corcoran. Thank you for your cooperation. I hope that you are not too uncomfortable with the current situation.

(Corcoran nervously fidgets in his seat.)

Corcoran: Well, it's- This is…pretty intense for me, to say the least. I only really catalogue things here digitally. I've never actually seen any of the…things we keep in the facility.

Dr. Ross: (Still reading) I apologize for any inconvenience. However, I am here to assess whether or not your current attitude poses a liability to the Foundation, and to ensure-

Corcoran: -continued enthusiasm and willingness to participate in Site-sanctioned activities. I know the spiel, Eli.

(Dr. Ross looks up from the binder, silently staring. Corcoran immediately becomes uncomfortable.)

Corcoran: Sorry, I- I didn't mean- I have the utmost respect for-…(Sigh) Just, go on, please.

Dr. Ross: I'd like to begin with a simple appraisal of your present level of awareness. Can you tell me what today's date is?

Corcoran: It's June 16th.

Dr. Ross: Good. How long have you worked at the Foundation?

Corcoran: I think we're coming up on three years now.

Dr. Ross: Alright. Now please describe the events that transpired after you left work yesterday.

Corcoran: Well, it's like I told you. I drove home, fixed dinner for my mother. She uh- She can't really cook for herself, at this point. Then I got ready for bed and slept. Nothing really out of the ordinary.

Dr. Ross: You told me yesterday you were concerned that there was a new anomaly emerging. That this crack-

Corcoran: -Yeah, uh, I should- I'm sorry about that. My therapist says I have the tendency to…sensationalize things. Uh, like…create problems before they exist, you know?

Dr. Ross: So you're not anxious about this anymore?

Corcoran: Well, I wasn't. I tried to reassure myself that I was just doing my whole pattern over again, tried to remember what my therapist said I could do to calm down…and then I came in today and it was bigger. Then, everything just…started all over again. (Sigh) I'm starting to think I won't ever be able to do anything about it.

(A short pause. Corcoran looks down, then catches himself, jolting back to meet Dr. Ross's eyeline.)

Corcoran: But y- you're right. It's probably just a crack in the floor. I don't want to waste your time with this.

Dr. Ross: My concern is that it will affect your work. You have a history of mental illness?

Corcoran: I mean- I guess a little bit. B-but it's not an issue. I can keep working. I'm managing, and…I'll keep at it.

(Dr. Ross studies him, combing over his body with his eyes. The silence continues for a minute more before Corcoran speaks up.)

Corcoran: Could you stop that, please? You're making me uncomfortable.

(Suddenly, Dr. Ross's Foundation-issue cellular phone chimes. He calmly picks up the phone and answers with little urgency.)

Dr. Ross: Is there a problem?

(A short pause. There is no reaction from Dr. Ross.)

Dr. Ross: Understood. I'll be right there.

(He hangs up the phone.)

Dr. Ross: I must go. Apparently this crack you found just expanded once again.

Corcoran: You're kidding me! So this might actually be…something?

Dr. Ross: I'll be the one to determine that.

(Corcoran studies Dr. Ross's expression, puzzled.)

Corcoran: Why does it seem like this doesn't bother you at all?

(Dr. Ross rolls his eyes.)

Dr. Ross: Please, it's a crack in the floor. I've seen a whole lot during my time here, and nothing has ever managed to faze me.

Corcoran: Sounds like a gift.

Dr. Ross: It isn't.

Corcoran: Well, it's just- you know that most agents train for years to reach that level of…confidence.

Dr. Ross: I wouldn't presume it's confidence.

(Abruptly, Dr. Ross stands up and walks toward the door.)

Dr. Ross: You can go home for today. Try not to have a panic attack on the drive home.

Corcoran: Uh…sure. I'll give it a shot.

Afterword: Upon inspection of SCP-9104, and witnessing the expansion firsthand, Dr. Ross determined that classification within the Foundation's official system was necessary, and experimentation would begin to attempt to slow the growth of the anomaly.

Special Containment Procedures: Site-109 has been reduced to 50% capacity, only retaining staff above Level 3 Clearance to safely continue the containment of other anomalies at the site. Additionally, several Scranton Reality Anchors were placed around Warehouse 109a, as the Hume level surrounding the anomaly has risen steadily to 103 Hm, and does not show signs of slowing its increase.

The most recent photograph of SCP-9104.

Description: SCP-9104 is a large gap in the ground, located in Site-109's main warehouse, that continues to grow at a seemingly exponential rate, beginning at just 0.93m, but now extending to over 32m. Although growth has significantly hastened since it was first located, a small dip in the acceleration of expansion was noticed after Site-109 was fully evacuated.

SCP-9104 has also recently begun to grow various flora alongside its walls, including Prickly Russian Thistle (salsola tragus), Winged Pigweed (dysphania atriplicifolia), and Resurrection Plant (selaginella lepidophylla). Despite the fact that these plants continue to enlarge as if they are living, all species of flora that develop within the anomaly appear brown and completely lifeless. Samples have shown that this vegetation is not currently alive, and shows no signs of ever containing moisture or any living tissue.

A photograph of a sample of a growth from within SCP-9104.

While attempting several expeditions to explore what lies at the bottom, the gorge continued to expand, causing the climbing gear of several agents to malfunction and disengage, dropping the agents down until they were trapped in between the floor. Site Administrators advised not to mount rescue expeditions for the lost agents, and not to expend any further staff to physically explore inside the rift. Their screams and struggling continued for several days as the gap expanded more swiftly than usual, until the agents presumably dropped low enough to be out of earshot.

As opposed to further expeditions, video and audio surveillance devices will be used to monitor the condition of SCP-9104.

Addendum 9104.A: Expedition Log 9104.20.15

Expedition Log

Reporting Agent: Dr. Elijah Ross

18 Jul. 2020

Foreword: Researcher Ian Corcoran was retained as "essential staff", due to his initial discovery of SCP-9104, and has been responsible for all documentation related to SCP-9104. He and Dr. Elijah Ross have, at present, visited the anomaly 14 separate times.

On this expedition, Dr. Ross carried a small camera along with him, attached to an appendange that can be mechanically lowered at will, to potentially gain insight into the contents of the anomaly without risking personnel.

(Dr. Elijah Ross and Ian Corcoran enter Warehouse 109a. As soon as the door opens, the entire floor rumbles slightly.)

Corcoran: Holy hell, it's- it's grown so much since last week.

Dr. Ross: (Dispassionate) Seems the anchors haven't done much to stop it. Nor has decreased observation. You were right that it would only continue growing.

Corcoran: I really didn't want to be.

(They both begin walking closer toward SCP-9104.)

Corcoran: This is- This is getting really bad. Shouldn't we alert the Council? Can't one of them do something about all of this? Fast-track experiments, or try some special power or whatever the fuck they have…anything like that?

Dr. Ross: I don't think it's time for that quite yet. I still have some hypotheses that I'd like to put to the test. There's much left for us to do here.

Corcoran: "There's much-"…Are you serious? It's almost swallowed this building! How are you not concerned about this?

Dr. Ross: (Sigh) I'm growing tired of explaining my disposition to you.

Corcoran: Wh- Then what are you even doing here?! The whole point of working at this place is to protect others, to shield people from these…downright horrific things. You're telling me that you "don't care" about the damage this could to do people's lives?!

(A short pause.)

Dr. Ross: Not particularly.

Corcoran: I have no idea how you could spend so much time fighting for humanity, trying to understand these things, if you have no value for other people. I mean, what the hell is wrong with y-

Dr. Ross: -Corcoran. This is unprofessional. Dr. Flip has placed me in charge of investigating 9104, so it's my call. No Council yet. We do not need their aid. I'm not sure they'd be able to do much more than us, anyhow.

Corcoran: Okay, so then why do I have to be here?! I don't want to look at this thing! I usually never see these things, I just write about them. It was always easier to help that way.

Dr. Ross: We're still monitoring to make sure that this doesn't present any adverse effects. Sometimes it can take months. We'd rather not expose anyone else until we're absolutely sure that there isn't any harm done from viewing the anomaly.

Corcoran: You, uh- You seriously think it could still, like, melt me or something?

(Dr. Ross stops walking and turns to Corcoran, raising an eyebrow. The chasm groans once again behind them.)

Dr. Ross: Melt you?

Corcoran: I don't know! I've heard some horror stories about the people who've worked here-

Dr. Ross: -At this point, I'm sure you'll be fine. It's just a precaution. Not to mention: you're the first one who saw this anomaly. Dr. Flip instructed us to keep you along, just in case you might possess any valuable knowledge.

Corcoran: So, we're just throwing whatever we can think of at this thing? That's…not reassuring.

Dr. Ross: Well, no one's priority is to reassure you.

(The fissure rumbles once more, as the chasm visibly extends another 0.2 meters. Dr. Ross observes Corcoran's reaction.)

Corcoran: AH! Shit! It's- We should get out of here. I don't need to see this thing anymore. We got the picture. It's bigger. It's always bigger.

Dr. Ross: The addition of this device will benefit us in the future. Just continue recording the investigation and our findings. That's all you need to worry about.

(Corcoran takes a deep breath, composing himself.)

Corcoran: Okay…Okay, okay. I'll just- I'll keep writing.

(Dr. Ross shakes his head in disapprobation, slowly inching further toward the anomaly. Carefully, he affixes the device near the edge of the fissure. Just as he moves to secure the clip in place, the gap quakes once more.)

Corcoran: Shit! Are you okay?

Dr. Ross: (Annoyed) Yes, yes, calm down. It barely moved.

(After the clip snaps into place, Dr. Ross lowers the camera down into the abyss below. Corcoran closely watches, intensely staring at the camera as it descends. There's a long moment of silence.)

Corcoran: Is it working-

Dr. Ross: -I don't know yet. Please: enough talking.

(A short pause.)

Corcoran: (Whispering) Sorry…

(The crevice vibrates to life, rupturing the ground further throughout the floor. As the pieces of rock give way below it, the device holding the camera falls into the rift. Dr. Ross reaches out to catch the apparatus, but is a moment too late, watching as it slinks into the darkness.)

Corcoran: Oh, God, you're kidding me!

Dr. Ross: Well, that is a shame.

(Dr. Ross stands up, dusting his hands off on his lab coat. Waiting, he listens for the camera to echo back once it hits the ground, but no sound comes. Corcoran simply stares at the crack, inching away in fear.)

Dr. Ross: I'll check the feeds to see if anything is still coming back, but if there is a "floor" to that anomaly, then it definitely won't survive the fall. Which means, next steps: We're going to need some sort of pulley system to suspend the camera directly above SCP-9104. I can't presume the ceiling of this warehouse will hold up much longer. The walls have already taken a beating. And we can't continue-

(The crack shakes, expanding once again, moving quickly toward the walls of the warehouse, and causing small fisures to form up the base.)

Corcoran: That's it! W-we have to go. Come on.

Dr. Ross: Then go, if you want.

Corcoran: No, it's- You have to come back with me. It's not safe.

Dr. Ross: You don't need to worry for me, Corcoran.

Corcoran: No, I do! Because you clearly have no survival instinct! We need you here at this Site! How else are we going to-

Dr. Ross: -I'm beginning to grow impatient with you, so I'll tell you once more: Leave. Now.

(Corcoran hesitates, but then turns and walks quickly out of the warehouse, exasperated, as the chasm continuing to widen and vibrate with every step he takes. Dr. Ross watches intently, then turns back toward SCP-9104, pondering the results of this expedition.)
