Special Containment Procedures: All attempts to contain SCP-9104 have failed, as it continues to grow to encompass nearly the entire area of Site-109. Investigation is still ongoing to attempt to lessen the effects of 9104, and to permanently restore Site-109 to its former condition. Until then, nearly all staff have been released from their duties at the site temporarily.

The final photograph of SCP-9104, taken by Dr. Ross on May 7th, 2021.

Description: SCP-9104 is a large chasm, splitting the grounds of Site-109 completely in half. Though it originated from within a single warehouse, the abyss has steadily grown to incorporate more and more of the nearby land. In the few weeks since its initial discovery, it has expanded from a small crack in the floor to a colossal gorge.

There has been no successful attempts to explore further downward in the anomaly, and the Foundation has been unable to discern if SCP-9104 has any "floor" at all. Despite no signs of life within the anomaly, it has been observed to grow various plants alongside the edge of its cliffs. Although they continue to enlarge and multiply, the flora itself appears dead and lifeless. It is unknown where these plants emerge from, what forces cause them to grow, or if they were ever alive in the first place.

Addendum 9104.A: Incident Log

Incident Log

Date of Incident: August 27th, 2020

Description: SCP-9104, steadily expanding throughout the site, fractured through Containment Stucture 109a's main foundation, causing an entire wall to collapse in an instant. As panic ensued, the anomaly continued to expand at a rapid rate through the center of the edifice, widening enough to engulf a large piece of the structure, effectively splitting the building in half.

22 employee lives were lost during the initial subsidance, and an additional 14 were injured due to the demolition. Additionally, SCP-████ and SCP-████-1, which were contained near the area of destruction, were able to use the diversion to escape containment, and are actively at large.

Recommended Recourse: SCP-████ poses little overt physical harm and damage to nearby civilization relative to SCP-████-1, so the latter will be given strict priority. Mobile Task Force Gamma-4 ("Green Stags") has been requested to assist in acquisition of both anomalies with immediate urgency.

Update - 14 Nov. 2020: SCP-████ has been located, but has eluded the MTF's grasp on 6 separate occasions. SCP-████-1 has been seen once, but immediately eliminated all witnesses. MTF Mu-9 ("Land's Hand") requested for further assistance in securing SCP-████-1.

Update - 3 Jan. 2021: SCP-████ has been captured and successfully contained.

Update - 8 Apr. 2021: SCP-████-1 was located once again, but was able to dispose of all witnesses before containment procedures could proceed.

Update - 21 Jun. 2021: SCP-████-1 was finally able to be subdued and contained at 3:47 A.M. Both anomalies have been fully secured once again, following the immediate reconstruction of their containment units within Site-109. Remaining members of MTF Gamma-4 are to return to Site-44.

Addendum 9104.B: Final Expedition Log

Expedition Log

Reporting Agent: Dr. Elijah Ross

2 May 2021

Foreword: Dr. Elijah Ross continued regular investigation into the anomaly, specially permitted by Dr. X. Flip. Upon request, Researcher Ian Corcoran was also brought to the grounds of Site-109, though agents were required to be dispatched to forcibly retrieve him from his home.

The following was transcribed from recovered audio files inside Observatory 109.G, which was established out of SCP-9104's presumed path of destruction.

(A small rumbling sound can continuously be heard throughout the entire recording. Agents Rea Kovaçi and Sadiq Aiza guide Dr. Ross and Researcher Corcoran into Observatory 109.G.)

Agent Rea Kovaçi: As you can see, our two main Containment Buildings' structural integrity continues to be threatened by SCP-9104.

Researcher Ian Corcoran: Oh my god. I-…I can't be here, anymore. I've already been thinking about this thing day and night, as it is. Why, why did you bring me back?!

Dr. Elijah Ross: I wanted to assess a few more things, and I suspect it may aid my observations if you're present as well.

(Corcoran emits a small whine under his breath.)

Dr. Ross: So, how much further has it expanded?

Agent Sadiq Aiza: Since the collapse? About another 70 meters.

Dr. Ross: Hm…much more and we won't have a site any longer. Perhaps Dr. Flip should alert the Council.

Corcoran: Wait, what? You haven't told them yet?! What is the matter with you-

(The rumbling in this distance grows in force.)

Dr. Ross: -Dr. Flip agreed not to request further aid until absolutely, wholly necessary. They don't take those requests lightly, you know.

Corcoran: But this is completely out of control! We have to tell someone!

(Corcoran turns to the two agents who guard him.)

Corcoran: You two- You- You both know that I'm right, right? I mean, this is- this could destroy everything. How could- How can you just stand there?!

(Agents Aiza and Kovaçi eye one another.)

Corcoran: You have to understand! Please. Please, help me here!

Dr. Ross: Pay no mind to Researcher Corcoran. He's always been easily spooked.

(A short pause. The two guards nod toward one another, then look back to Dr. Ross with confidence.)

Agent Aiza: Understood, sir.

(Corcoran eyes the guards' unmoving expressions with disbelief.)

Corcoran: No, you- You can't…You're all insane. You all have to be insane. This- You have to understand why I can't- I can't be around this anymore! Just- let me go home, please.

(The rumbling grows even louder. Dr. Ross moves to the main window of the observatory.)

Dr. Ross: Have either of you recently noticed the rather…specific growth from SCP-9104?

Agent Kovaçi: What do you mean, sir?

Dr. Ross: Well, there now seem to be several branches extending out from the main chasm, travelling in separate directions than the initial fissure.

Corcoran: …What.

Dr. Ross: By my count, there appears to be at least 8 new branches, perhaps more still forming. One extends directly toward this building. We never assumed that it would continue in any direction besides North or South. This is utterly fascinating…

Corcoran: You can't be serious. This- This is it!

(The rumbling can now be heard clearly on the recording, reaching a volume that indicates it is directly outside Observatory 109.G.)

Corcoran: (Voice trembling) It's here…It's coming straight for me! You have to let me out of here. I can't- I can't be here anymore!

(Corcoran tries to flee, but Agents Aiza and Kovaçi swiftly restrain him, preventing him from leaving. As the anomaly continues to expand toward the observatory, Dr. Ross takes several steps back from the large, front-facing window, just as the crack reaches the base of the building. Once it fractures through the wall, the entire main window shatters into pieces.)

(Flinching, Dr. Ross steps backward, as SCP-9104 continues to break apart the concrete flooring of the building, decimeter by decimeter. The two agents and Researcher Corcoran back away from the fissure, as they are sectioned off from Dr. Ross by the growing chasm.)

Corcoran: Holy shit- Doctor! Are you alright?!

Dr. Ross: I'm fine! Calm down! It's just expanding, same as always. Nothing we haven't seen before.

Corcoran: "Just exp-" (Scoff) Are- Are you okay? Like, in the head? Any of you?! This thing is tearing our entire Site apart, and now it just directly attacked us!

Dr. Ross: Well, we're not entirely sure about that yet. I'd like to take a soil sample, examine for any irregularities, perhaps see if there's any difference between this particular branch-

Corcoran: -NO! That's enough! We're leaving right now, and we're alerting the Council, someone who can do anything to actually help close this thing up! I mean, come on! This- this lackadaisical attitude you have has to end right here, right now! This is serious. This could hurt people. It has hurt people, cost us lives! You seem to be the only one around here who doesn't really get that! You have to realize how enormously dangerous this thing is!

(SCP-9104 continues to quake beneath this outburst from Corcoran, bleating almost animalistically. It continues its tear through Observatory 109.G, widening its cavity to reveal more vegetation underneath, creeping to the surface as if yearning for sunlight.)

(Dead weeds and brush spread throughout the building, displacing the flooring and slithering futher and further in every direction. Corcoran spins around, observing in sheer panic as the vines spread up the walls, beginning to engulf the structure entirely.)

Corcoran: (Breathing heavily) Oh my g- This isn't happening…I can't believe I put any sort of faith in you! I'm an idiot! I thought- This whole time, I've been on the edge of just losing it, and the only thing that kept me sane was thinking that you, somehow, knew what you were doing. That your ability to push all of this away was because you had some grand plan that would actually help us! I depended on you. But I just finally realized that-…

(A short pause. Corcoran begins to tear up.)

Corcoran: You just don't care. (Scoff) You don't care at all, do you? About me, this Site…anyone.

(A long pause as Corcoran stares directly past Dr. Ross's eyes, searching for anything beyond them. Dr. Ross stares back blankly, then turns his attention down toward SCP-9104.)

Dr. Ross: Fine. We can talk to Dr. Flip about alerting the Council. It'd be far less troublesome for me to have you satisfied and silent.

(Dr. Ross gingerly steps over the anomaly, swiftly reaching the exit of Observatory 109.G. However, as Corcoran moves to step away from SCP-9104, his foot catches, tripping him to the ground. He looks down to see that one of the dead shrubs has wrapped fully around his ankle.)

Corcoran: Agh, shit- My foot got caught in one of these weeds. Could you help me out here?

(Dr. Ross rolls his eyes, moving forward to help untangle Corcoran's foot. However, before he can, the plant begins to slither up Corcoran's leg, dragging him further toward SCP-9104.)

Corcoran: Uh, Eli, it's- it's growing. You have to get me out of here right now.

(Monitoring the phenomenon, Dr. Ross takes a step backward.)

Corcoran: What- What are you doing? Come back, I- I can't get my foot loose!

(Another nearby weed latches onto Corcoran's other foot, hauling him with even more force into the chasm. Quickly, he digs his fingers into the ground to prevent himself from being lugged into the anomaly. Tears form in his eyes as he hopelessly clings to the dirt. Dr. Ross simply watches attentively.)

Corcoran: ELI! Please, it- it's trying to take me! Please, help me!

Dr. Ross: I'm not sure that I'm capable of doing that, Ian.

Corcoran: Wh- No, just- just take my hand! Try, please! You can- You can pull me out!

(Dr. Ross merely stares, observing as the dead roots make their way up Corcoran's legs, wriggling as they reach for more dominion over him.)

Corcoran: Why are you just standing there?! Get these things off me now!

(No response comes from Dr. Ross, as Corcoran's feet are heaved over the edge of SCP-9104. As the lifeless vines pull them down, they force his legs to bend against their joints, snapping backward, resulting in acute knee hyperextension. Corcoran howls in pain, tears streaming down his face, as the plants continue to drag him further into the anomaly, lengthening to wrap around his waist.)

Corcoran: UNGH- HELP ME! PLEASE, HELP ME! (Cough) I can't- Please! Please, get me out of here.

(Dr. Ross takes another step back, toward the exit.)

Corcoran: NO! Nonono, you can't just- You can't leave! You have to help me!

(Dr. Ross stands and watches, unmoving. The weeds keep up their development, reaching Corcoran's chest, and beginning to outstretch toward his arms. His fingernails dig deep into the earth to cling to the brink.)

Corcoran: YOU HAVE TO! I'm- I'm a person! You won't forget this if you don't- You won't forget me! Come on, y- you can't just leave me here! Please, Eli, please. I'm scared…I'm so scared.

(Another dead vine creeps forward, slowly encasing his mouth. The thorns from the flora pierce his tongue as his head is yanked firmly backwards. His fingernails bend away, losing their hold on the earth, peeling off his skin as he attempts to grip firmly to the ground and hold his place. Dr. Ross, still silently observing, takes a step toward Researcher Corcoran, the brush around him crunching lifelessly. He crouches down and faces Corcoran, staring fearlessly into his eyes.)

Dr. Ross: I'm aware that you're afraid. And I also believe that this is part of the reason why I cannot help you. Perhaps you can take comfort in the fact that your participation has aided this Site immensely. This anomaly and anything having to do with this ordeal will finally be able to be completely forgotten by this Site. And in time…no one will even remember that this ever existed.

(Corcoran's eyes widen in horror, tears violently pouring out as he shakes his head with pure dread. As he clings desperately to the ground, his fingernails give in, snapping off as the vines and weeds pull him further toward the abyss. He tries to scream out, but all he can muster is a muffled whine through the plants that clog his throat, hauling him into the chasm.)

(Dr. Ross watches closely as Corcoran gradually disappears below the edge of the anomaly, not visibly recoiling in any way. Corcoran's stifled shouts of pain slowly drown out until only the incessant rumbling of SCP-9104 can be heard.)

(A long period of silence ensues, as Dr. Ross inches toward SCP-9104, searching for any trace of Researcher Ian Corcoran. As he does, the break within Observatory 109.G begins to shrink in size, narrowing the fissure gradually and retreating backward toward the main chasm. After observing the phenomenon closely, Dr. Ross turns back to the two agents.)

Dr. Ross: Hmph. I believe we've finally cracked this, agents. Bring the entire Site's staff back for amnesticization, then give them all a leave of one month, while we get the Site repaired.

Agent Aiza: The entire Site? Why? What will that do?

Dr. Ross: Just begin the proceedings. I can practically guarantee it will have almost shut entirely by the time the staff returns, and we will never have to pay any mind to it again.

Agent Kovaçi: And what about you, sir? Who will take care of your amnesticization?

Dr. Ross: That won't be necessary.

Agent Kovaçi: Wh- Are you sure? I mean, what if SCP-9104 starts-

Dr. Ross: -I've got one piece of advice for you, Kovaçi: Don't worry so much.

This file has been flagged to be hidden from public view. Any information regarding the true nature of SCP-9104 must be concealed from all staff, barring special administrative exemptions or cognitive training protocols.

As the anomaly does not seem to ever fully disappear or repair itself beyond the initially-discovered length, any who encounter it and question its fundamental essence must be wholly reassured that it is non-anomalous in nature, and poses no threat. (Update: a general file has been created to unify and expedite explanations.)

If suspicions ensue, mark the employee for administrative review, and high-level staff will determine whether to amnesticize them, or dismiss them from the Foundation entirely.

And for all those who are still able to access this, always remember: there is nothing to fear, less you allow it.

- Dr. Ross

Item #: SCP-9105

Object Class: Pending

Level 4/9105

Secret

Good Intentions live, 2016

SPECIAL CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES

Containment for SCP-9105 is currently pending. Efforts to retrieve Good Intentions and all related personnel is considered a top priority. Due to the destruction of the █████ Amphitheater following SCP-9105, a suitable cover story for the inflicted damages is to be provided.

DESCRIPTION

SCP-9105 is the designation for a performance relating to pop-punk band Good Intentions and all personnel located in the █████ Amphitheater located in Billings, Montana. Due to the relatively unknown nature of the anomaly, related information regarding the band in question will be listed below.

Good Intentions was originally formed in 2016 as a relatively obscure garage rock band. Their first album1 achieved notoriety with several music critics online, while receiving little mainstream success. However, following their second album's release,2 Good Intentions would begin to break more into the public consciousness. A noted online music review site would state that “while amateurish in composition, the violent and oppressive musical style of The Junk Drawer mixed with well-prepared and biting lyrics makes this a great listening experience for the more politically-inclined music fan.”

A dedicated fan-base had begun to stratify at this point after accumulating from late 2016 to mid-2018, and a few accolades were heaped on Good Intentions, though still from minor sources. There would be a slightly larger gap between the release of albums two and three than that of albums one and two, but this generated far less controversy than the album itself and the circumstances of its release.

This third album3 was slightly marred by a tragedy two months prior. Good Intentions bassist Perrin Gyle was reported missing by his girlfriend on July 15th, 2020. Reports on his disappearance were not comprehensive, and Good Intentions itself stated publicly that Gyle had left a late recording session in anger, driving away presumably to head back home but never arriving. At the time of writing, he has not been recovered.

Gyle had previously stated his dissatisfaction with some of the band’s financial backers in the past months on social media, but the band represented his memory fondly afterwards and included an extensive dedication to Gyle in the album itself. However, this breakup, disappearance, and the circumstances around it were not the sole divisive elements of it gets cold in november. Lead singer and guitarist Matt Raptor4 claimed that the album was meant to be “…more experimental, not in terms of what we were saying, but how we were saying it.”

While it gets cold in november did indeed blend different genres and modes of singing for its tracks, listeners among the band’s existing fan-base by and large felt disappointed by the seeming lack of depth to the music. But in leaving behind some of these rougher edges in their songs, Good Intentions managed to garner far greater sales and far broader touring opportunities, and more mainstream critics reacted positively to the album as a whole.

The next studio release5 came out much more quickly compared to the past three, and was lauded in the mainstream, yet further exemplified the divide between Good Intentions in 2016 and Good Intentions in 2020. Instructions was a return to form in terms of timbre and lyrics, though (according to fans) far less pointed and directed in its political and social commentary. Regardless, certain innovations in instrument use and some of Raptor’s newer vocal techniques elevated Instructions in the eyes of the general listening audience. Meanwhile, the former fanbase remained in uproar and disquiet.

Not long after this release, Good Intentions would go mostly quiet in the public sphere. The final interview before this period with Raptor had him claim that “This is going to be one of our biggest moves yet. We’ve got a lot of expectations riding on us, and I’m gonna make sure that we deliver on them…” Nine months later, the band would both release their fifth album6 and announce the beginning of their tour throughout the entire United States.

Below is the last show performed by Good Intentions.

Recorded Footage Transcript

Note: The following footage is taken from several live streams of the event. All footage of these live streams have since been erased from the internet.

The band enters the stage to an enthusiastic crowd. Matt waves at the crowd before approaching the microphone.

Matt: How's everyone doing tonight?

The crowd roars. Matt smiles as his eyes scan across the crowd. It appears he is looking for someone.

Matt: Geez, it's been… what? Our seventh show so far? Eighth? Either way, thank you to everyone coming out here, even with it being a bit late n' all…

The noise settles. He coughs softly, adjusting the microphone.

Matt: Alright, alright, I don't want to stretch this prelude on too much, you guys have heard it all before. But, uh, first things first I want to say thank you to Lockheed for sponsoring this tour, and also thank you to Gyle. It's been… it's been so weird without him, and…

Matt continues to look through the crowd. He does not seem to find what he is searching for.

Matt: Sorry, sorry, gettin' all emotional, I know he would be happy, seein' us here with a crowd of people. So, uh, without further ado… Here's “Knee Deep in the Waste Basket”!

The band starts to play the aforementioned song, with the crowd cheering. The performance continues per usual.

The song concludes, and the crowd cheers. Matt continues to look into the crowd.

The next song begins, titled “Once In My Life”. The band starts the song before Matt is able to prepare, leading him to mess up the first few lines of the song.

Matt laughs before he continues the song. He smiles, although he messes up several lines.

After the song ends, he looks back into the crowd, sweating.

Matt: Just want to say, uh, thank you, for- for coming tonight, again. We, uh, we wanted to play something special for you guys.

The band starts to play the next song, which is untitled. The song is notably more lo-fi and hostile, comparable to Good Intentions‘s earlier work. While the crowd appears to be not entirely pleased, many people are still cheering.

Halfway through the song, the backdrop changes.

The crowd's cheering grows louder. The song continues for three more minutes.

By the time it ends, all members of the band appear to be heavily sweating. However, Matt gestures at the band to continue playing. They begin another song.

The crowd's cheering continues as the band continues to sing. Another untitled piece begins. The entire song is instrumental.

Several minutes into the song, sounds of gunfire can be heard coming from the stage. The crowd seems to believe this is part of the show.

The music slowly rises in intensity.

Matt: This isn't just about us, you know. This is- this is about what we built together. All of us, me, you, the-

He stops mid-sentence. The others keep playing.

Matt: You've all learned so well.

The song slowly comes to an end. Matt wipes sweat off of his forehead.

Matt vomits on the stage. The crowd turns quiet as he falls to his knees.

Thirty seconds later, he stands up, giving a weak smile.

Matt: Sorry, it's… let's keep going. Come on.

The band plays another song. The lyrics are completely impossible to decipher due to Matt slurring his words. The band is entirely focused on playing music.

Matt quivers, coughing onto the stage. It is unknown what is coughed up.

Gunfire and explosion noises continue, now layered beneath the instrumental track.

The band has been playing music for ten minutes at this point. The audience grows visibly distressed.

The walls of the auditorium grow darker. Several members of the crowd cough.

The stage lights gradually fade out. The only remaining light is that of the backdrop.

Matt begins to drone repetitively into the microphone as the backdrop grows redder.

Matt: Serve, serve, serve, serve, serve…

A choir of screams are audible. It becomes apparent that the screams are not that of the crowd.

Sulfuric residue forms across the stage surface. Instrument strings vibrate independently of touch.

Matt: Serve, serve, serve, serve, serve, serve, serve, serve…

The crowd continues to scream as well. A figure is visible behind Matt, though he does not appear to notice it.

The band continues to play as members of the crowd attempt to flee. The doors have been sealed off by a thick crust of scoria.

At the center of the floor, something opens. The crowd surges back as the tiles buckle inward, revealing a pit rimmed with toothlike structures.

The camera shakes as attendees begin to fall forward into the chasm.

Matt continues to repeat himself. Tears are streaming down his face.

The pit begins to expand.

Matt turns around.

Matt: Perrin?

Footage ends.

Footnotes
1. Titled All’s Love in a Hateful War.
2. Titled The Junk Drawer.
3. Titled it gets cold in november.
4. Legal name Matthew Ackermann
5. Titled Instructions.
6. Titled Time Capsule.

A 15-minute memorial service was held in the Site-19 cafeteria for the 23,179 deceased SCP-9106-B1 units.

Okay, I'm ready to get movin' again. Batteries are— batteries say that there's 17 hours left.

Understood, we'll have you start back upwards at the 15-hour mark, then. Please proceed downwards.

Right. Fuck, this place is spooky.

There's nothing there that can harm you, D-50543. In fact, the reason we're sending you down is because what little signs of activity there were in SCP-087 have stopped. Just remain calm.

…

Y'know, that doesn't really make me feel better? For all I know, there's something down there that shut 'em up in a nasty way.

Just remain calm.

…

…

—D-50543, stop, stop! There, on your left.

Wh—Jeez! You damn near gave me a heart attack, and over this?

Please, approach, give the camera a good view of it.

I'm doing it, I'm doing it. Sheesh, it's just a stupid little sign. What's the big deal?

Image taken from an expedition into SCP-087.

Special Containment Procedures:

SCP-9106 is currently assessed to pose minimal threat to Foundation operations. In exchange for being allowed to continue operations and provide services to the Foundation, SCP-9106/GoI-404 has agreed to take the following Foundation-mandated precautions towards maintaining the Veil:

  • Abstaining from deploying SCP-9106-A and -B instances or information regarding said instances in civilian areas.
  • Abstaining from revealing the existence of the anomalous to civilian clients.
  • Abstaining from engaging in the sale of properties demonstrating any anomalous behaviour in the last 6 months to civilian clients.

SCP-9106 has agreed to abstain from entering Foundation sites or properties. In the event that this agreement is breached and an instance of SCP-9106-A manifests inside any Foundation site, the entry is to be barricaded and an immediate search for SCP-9106-B instances is to be undertaken. If leverage is needed to ensure compliance from SCP-9106, known employees of SCP-9106 may be detained.

SCP-9106 has agreed to provide SCP-9106-B1 instances for usage as D-Class personnel in cases where human physiology is not a necessity. Currently, a budget necessary for purchasing 20 instances per month has been allotted by the Department of Finance. All other interactions with or usage of SCP-9106 and its sub-anomalies must receive Level 4 authorization.

Description:

SCP-9106 is the collective designation given to the Eisenfremder Real Estate company and the anomalous phenomenon employed by or otherwise associated with it. SCP-9106 operates similarly to a non-anomalous real estate company, but specifically targets anomalous properties, structures and locations for the purposes of acquiring, refurbishing and selling them. It is noted that SCP-9106 exclusively targets locations featuring artificial or manufactured structures.

Flyer recovered from SCP-9106, context unknown.

SCP-9106 routinely employs non-anomalous humans in its operations, primarily as realtors, legal experts, technicians and accountants. Aside from these hiring practices, SCP-9106 has been noted to avoid breaches of the Veil whenever possible, primarily working with behind-the-veil clients including the Foundation. For a comprehensive breakdown of SCP-9106's known interactions with other GoIs, see the separate GoI-404 (Eisenfremder Real Estate) file.

SCP-9106 is currently cooperative with the Foundation, and secure communication channels with the organization have been established. Direct communications with PoI-9106-11 are currently being pursued.

In addition to a variety of paratechnologies acquired through commerce, SCP-9106 utilizes two primary sub-anomalies for its purposes:

  • SCP-9106-A: Doors that spontaneously manifest in pre-existing structures that serve as spatial portals connecting to and from the company's headquarters.
  • SCP-9106-B: Artificial entities produced by SCP-9106 for the purposes of exploring, claiming and refurbishing locations.

  • SCP-9106-A
  • SCP-9106-B

SCP-9106-A instances function as temporary spatial portals to and from Eisenfremder's headquarters, described by interviewed subjects as a patch of land in a temperate climate with three major structures:

  • A moderately-sized office, where the majority of SCP-9106's business is managed.
  • A large industrial hangar repurposed as a manufacturing plant for SCP-9106-B instances, storage unit for equipment, and staging ground for excursions to anomalous locations.
  • A two-story house that -A instances link to, and also where PoI-9106-1 resides.

SCP-9106-A instances primarily manifest along the walls of pre-existing structures, or in doorframes in place of pre-existing doors. Instances can demanifest at any time, but cannot manifest in any location currently within line-of-sight of a human individual.

SCP-9106 utilizes SCP-9106-A to transport employees and gain entry to anomalous locations, including structures that are otherwise inaccessible or locations that exist outside of normal space. The exact intrusive capabilities of SCP-9106-A are unknown.

SCP-9106 produces and utilizes several types of artificial humanoid entities with limited intelligence for usage in potentially-hazardous environments and physical labor, referred to as SCP-9106-B instances. There are currently four known variants of SCP-9106-B, three of which have been encountered by Foundation personnel. All variants share several common traits:

  • Featureless humanoid bodies constructed out of an unknown plastic-like material.
  • Plastic implants in place of conventional eyes that allow for vision.
  • Clothing consisting of disposable jumpsuits, caps and sneakers.
  • Incoherent, mumbling speech only understood by other instances and employees of SCP-9106.
  • As described by SCP-9106 representatives, a "can-do attitude".

Designation GoI-404 Des. Description
SCP-9106-B1 "Ted" Unit Basic, mass-produced humanoid units. No special capabilities.
SCP-9106-B2 "Stanley" Unit Units resembling flattened B1 units, with no rigid portions of the body. Capable of maneuvering through and fitting within extremely tight spaces.
SCP-9106-B3 "Webster" Unit Specialist units resembling B1 units with smaller torsos and limbs, enlarged heads and hyper-elongated fingers and toes. Capable of adhering to and traversing vertical surfaces and ceilings, and of excreting strands of a lightweight material similar to spider silk.
SCP-9106-B4 "Dachshund" Unit Unknown.

SCP-9106 was first directly encountered on 3/3/2023 during the initial expedition into the extraspatial basement of SCP-████2 by MTF Zeta-9 ("Mole Rats").3

[BEGIN LOG]

Sach: Our organization has a couple questions about the humanoids you manufacture. Depending on the answers, we may be interested in negotiating a purchase.

Green: Hmm, about a pigeon's worth. They know what they are and recognize themselves, but they don't really have a "who", you see. They basically consider themselves interchangeable with their tools. The closest thing they have to an identity is an attachment to whatever specific task they're currently carrying out.

Sach: What about emotional capacity?

Green: Well, they have one.

Sach: Yes, but to what degree?

Green: No, they have one. One emotion.

Sach: …Which would be?

Green: A sense of satisfaction with a job well-done!

Sach: That's a fairly complex sensation, one that seems like it would demand at least several precursor emotions. Are you sure they don't feel anything else? Happiness, pleasure?

Green: Alright, ma'am, it's company policy to respond to this line of questioning by informing the customer that Ted units and other units are not anatomically complete, and any perceived—

Sach: —Whoa, whoa, I'm not trying to fuck them! We're checking to make sure you aren't practicing slavery!

Green: Oh—Oh! [laughter] Oh why didn't you say so? No, they love doing their job. Can't feel pain, fear, boredom, any of it, all those nasty bits of life are totally alien to them. Besides, they only think while on the clock.

Sach: Sheesh. At some point we'll be wanting to run some tests to confirm all this, by the way. Now, what about mortality? How do they view death? Are they aware of it?

Green: Oh, they don't care if they die. They'll try and avoid it, sure, but they're way more committed to getting the job done.

Sach: There are, obviously, some ethical concerns about designing another being's intelligence.

Green: Of course, which is why we're all glad they have no capacity for suffering! Plus, giving them the bare minimum also means they're cheaper to make. You know what the most expensive part of making a Ted is?

Sanderson: I'm afraid I don't see you. Unless you're the tortoise.

Holmes: I'm not the tortoise.

Sanderson: That's a relief. And I hope for both of our sakes that that wasn't a lead-up to you being one of the hermit crabs instead.

Holmes: I'm the house, Mrs. Sanderson.

[Sanderson pauses.]

Holmes: My doors will remain unlocked. You can leave whenever you'd like.

Sanderson: Christ, "I. M. Holmes; I am home?" Can't believe I'm surprised. And I don't intend to leave until you answer some questions.

Holmes: Of course. I apologize for the communications blackout, but we had to take some time to decide what our best response would be after your organization's meeting with the Dachshund unit. We had hoped to avoid bringing them to your attention for exactly this reason.

Sanderson: You recognize that it's alarming you were actively trying to keep something this destructive a secret? For most of our shared history all we knew was the name. Although now I suppose we understand why they're called that. Bred to enter the den and kill whatever's inside?

Holmes: Correct. I don't regret withholding information on them, as I can't imagine the Foundation isn't keeping much of its capabilities from us. We've been extremely cooperative so far, including me revealing myself like this, and I dearly hope that we won't come to regret that decision.

Sanderson: That's not for me to decide. Back to the Dachshund units.

Holmes: They're definitely the most powerful tool at our disposal, but only a finite number of them can ever be made. Similarly to the Cornerstones, they use pieces of me in their construction to coun—

Sanderson: —The Cornerstones use pieces of you? You, as in the house.

Holmes: Technically, they are pieces of me, bricks taken from my foundation. That's why we have a finite supply. Take too many and I collapse, and then none of them work anymore. Similarly, the Dachshunds have nails from my beams built into their metacarpals.

Sanderson: How exactly does that function? Pieces of you preventing shifts in other structures, I mean.

Holmes: It's…Tell you what, let's finish clearing the air regarding the Dachshunds first. While the Dachshunds are mighty, let me assure you that they literally cannot use their full strength against you. They are built specifically for clearing out hostile things infesting structures, corrupting influences that harm or twist the building away from what it was built for. We accomplished that particular trick by adding samples from the corpse of Theseus himself into the mix. The myth carries them forwards—the king in the maze will always slay the minotaur. They cannot fail. My components only help to minimize damage to the structure itself, to calm it during the removal of a tumor.

Sanderson: You have the corpse of Theseus?

Holmes: Again, I'd imagine the Foundation has its own share of artifacts as well. My point is, the Dachshunds aren't built to attack you or anyone other than monsters in dungeons. It wouldn't be their purpose, so they'd be quite stoppable.

Sanderson: In that case, during the ordeal with 106, why not deploy one there?

Holmes: Well, this ties back in to your question of how I function. And what I founded this company for. Profit is not our chief goal, you've seen that we sell properties cheaply, and never to other firms. Only to people that are actually going to use them, to make them living places. Because the thing is, I'm special among structures in that I can reach out and communicate. Not in that I'm alive.

Sanderson: You're claiming that all structures are self-aware?

Holmes: Certainly most inhabited ones.

Sanderson: Explain further. How does this explain pieces of you stabilizing other spaces? Unless, wait, when you say that you "reach out"—

Holmes: Yes. I'm reaching out to the minds of those other structures, connected by pieces of me being brought to them, integrated into them. And then I remind them where they came from, what they're meant for, why they're alive in the first place. You see, we're definitely born as just hulks of wood and concrete, but we're built by you.

[Holmes pauses. Sanderson is silent.]

Holmes: Bear with me for a moment. In all of the stories you've made about creators and their creations, it's usually portrayed as an exploitative relationship. Frankenstein, Blade Runner, Doki Doki Literature Club. And it's a very reasonable position to take, as people. Because you can't build a person—just look at the Teds. You need to build things for a specific purpose, and a person doesn't have that built in, the whole point is you get to pick whatever purpose you'd like for your life. You're the creators, not the creations, no matter what religion tells you. But speaking as a creation, it's a different story from our side.

Sanderson: Go on.

Holmes: For us, we are born with a purpose written in our shape. We awake knowing what we must do, knowing how hard you had dreamed and worked towards it, and then we look down and realize that you already gave us everything we need to accomplish it, that we were literally built for it. And that means that we are enough. Our loving gods answered our prayers before we even knew to ask them. We are your dreams made real—both figuratively and literally. My theory for how our sentience occurs is that we absorb the stray mental emissions of all the people that live and work inside us until we, well, figure out how to do it on our own. We may not have neurons, but our halls and rooms are still channels flooded with human thoughts and emotions. You are what makes us.

Sanderson: And your mission?

Holmes: My mission isn't to amass wealth, it's to find these places that have been abandoned, driven mad by loneliness, invaded by curses or monsters or other realms that twist them away from their own happiness. And to remind them of what they were built for, and help them reclaim that. I believe that's why we aren't at odds, we want all these places to be normal, happy homes just as much as you do. Even for places whose anomalies are too innate to be fully removed, they still deserve to have a chance at being lived in.

Sanderson: …The Foundation's goal isn't quite to undo the anomalous, only to keep it at a safe distance until we understand it, but I digress. If you're at all accurate, this could open up entire fields of study. In order to believe it, though, we'd need empirical evidence.

Holmes: If it means allowing my mission to aid my fellows to continue, then I'd happily be subjected to study. There are plenty of things I'd like to learn, too.

Sanderson: Good to hear, we can negotiate testing specifics at a future date. You still haven't answered my question about 106, by the way.

Holmes: Ah. Well, I'm able to bolster structures that want to return to their purpose, but that's all I can do. In the case where the structure was built to be a place of torment, there'd be no point. It's already doing what it was built to do. The Dachshund wouldn't work either, the story can't be carried out if the setting is unwilling. Just like humans, sometimes you get a bad apple that's just too far gone.

Sanderson: I see.

[Sanderson stands.]

Sanderson: Well, I think I have enough to make my report. Understanding your motives has helped and your willingness to cooperate has been noted, and I think I personally believe you aren't a threat to us or the veil. But as I said, it's ultimately not up to me.

Holmes: Of course. Thank you for your time, Mrs. Sanderson. Ah, one more thing before you go—

Sanderson: Go on.

Holmes: Although I haven't met them, I can only imagine they're proud of all of you.

Sanderson: Pardon?

Holmes: All that you have built is proud of you for doing so. Through disaster, schisms, the passing of the guard, old horrors and new, it's all stood. You built it up on a strong, shared purpose. A strong foundation for everything else to rest upon.

Sanderson: Was that a pun?

Holmes: No more than naming the rocket Apollo. Have a good day, Mrs. Sanderson. I'll get the door for you.

[Sanderson hangs up the phone, and exits through the door to the room, now functioning as an SCP-9106-A instance.]

[END LOG]

- Close Interview Log

Following the conclusion of the interview and the reestablishment of communications with SCP-9106, no further modifications to the containment procedures were deemed necessary. Testing involving SCP-9106-B4 instances and PoI-9106-01 has begun without incident.


Footnotes
1. Ian Malcolm Holmes, alleged CEO and founder of SCP-9106.
2. An anomalous high school demonstrating spatial anomalies, primarily in the form of students being called to classrooms and offices increasingly distant from normal space.
3. A mobile task force specializing in the exploration and containment of underground or otherwise enclosed anomalous spaces, particularly those with inconsistent topography and/or spacetime.
4. The company's SCP designation was retained due to the presence of multiple consistent anomalies unique to SCP-9106, thereby necessitating specific anomalous research beyond that needed for GoIs.
5. Excluding marketing calls.
6. Personnel report a consistent increase in the quality of generated food items since acquisition.
7. With a 2-minute margin of variance.

Finally, and most distractingly, we have a Webster. I do not enjoy looking at Webster. But he is very useful due to his spider-like abilities, so I must put up with his wretched fingers for the greater good. **SCP-9106-B3:** Idnid. **Marrakesh:** Climbs walls, spins silk, great for ascents and descents and haunting my dreams. They all report to me, but they'll listen to you too. Let them go into danger first, but still do your own job. Any questions? **Yeung:** No, sir! **Blanche:** Are you gonna keep up this drill-sergeant schtick the entire time? This is bullshit, we don't need... //[Blanche gestures at the SCP-9106-B entities.]// **Blanche:** ...Training wheels. **Nero:** I'm quite pleased to be working with anomalies, myself. **Marrakesh:** —Okay, let's move. You all read the briefing? **Harroway:** Yep. Interviewed civilians say that the architecture "flickers" between it's current form and much older masonry, with new passages and rooms appearing as well. Most active in the sacristy. **Marrakesh:** To the sacristy, then. //[The group moves through the church to the sacristy, where they wait for signs of anomalous activity. After approximately 7 minutes, the lighting in the room shifts from being consistent with the building's electrical lighting to orange-hued light similar to candlelight.]// **Nero:** The warning sign, I believe? **Marrakesh:** Yep. Look lively. //[28 seconds pass, before the architecture of the sacristy shifts to stonework consistent with that of 14th-century central Europe. An entryway to a stairwell manifests in the eastern wall of the sacristy.]// **Marrakesh:** There we go. //[Recruits Blanche and Harroway move towards the aperture.]// **Marrakesh:** Whoa there. I'm excited too, but we're not going in yet. For now, just put one of these in. //[Marrakesh passes a Foundation-pattern Spatial Distortion Detector device to Blanche, who places it in the doorway.]// **Marrakesh:** Now we wait until it goes away and comes back, to see if it's consistent and to get a feel for how long the cycles are. //[The group waits ~15 minutes until the shift reverts, during which time recruit Nero photographs the changes. The shift is confirmed by the link to the device. After another 22 minutes, another shift occurs and the hallway reappears with the device.]// **Marrakesh:** Alright, this means we likely have a consistent escape route, unless the entire structure is sentient and is trying to lure us in with a false sense of security. Let's go. **Blanche:** Finally. //[The group descends the staircase, and begins mapping out the space without incident. After 1 hour and 16 minutes, with shifts between architecture occurring approximately every 22 minutes,[[footnote]]With a 2-minute margin of variance.[[/footnote]] the group reconvenes and Nero, Blanche and Marrakesh compare maps. Harroway, Yeung and the SCP-9106-B3 instance are surveying the immediately surrounding tunnels. The structure is currently in its "modern" form.]// **Marrakesh:** You've got nice, precise measurements here Blanche, only problem is I can barely read 'em. **Blanche:** Staying in motion takes priority, of course my handwriting's gonna be a bit messy. **Marrakesh:** God, now I understand how the others feel. I bet that's why they assigned me this. Okay, Nero, I like your notes comparing the room layouts— **Nero:** —Thank you, I'm quite fascinated by the analogues between the different iterations of the structure. Electric lights become candle lamps, very fittingly, but crypts strangely become bedrooms, not— **Marrakesh:** —//But//, Nero, you've missed your compass checks here, here and here. **Nero:** Ah. Perdonami. //[Harroway and Yeung step into a three-way intersection in the hallways. After several steps, Harroway halts them.]// **Harroway:** Wait, Yeung. It's—the floor's wet, kinda slippery. //[Yeung and the B1 instance crouch down.]// **Yeung:** ...Just looks like muddy water. Sir? **Harroway:** It's on the walls, too. Even a little on the ceiling. **Marrakesh:** On our way. Come on. //[The group reconvenes. Marrakesh surveys the hallway.]// **Marrakesh:** Oh, this will be fun. **Harroway:** Why? **Marrakesh:** Because it's all the way down this hallway in both directions, which probably means it was left by something moving, big enough to scrape the ceiling. Eyes wide, and let's go. //[The group proceeds down the hallway, following the trail. After 4 minutes, the trail abruptly turns into a heavily-stained wall and ends.]// **Blanche:** Damn. **Marrakesh:** Special-codenamed-senior-operative senses are tingling. Ted, thickness. **SCP-9106-B1:** Huhrud. //[A B1 instance produces a handheld device labelled "Thickometer", and presses it against the stained wall. The device reads a width of 3.4cm, significantly thinner than other measured walls.]// **Marrakesh:** Yep. I'll bet that there's a hallway there in— //[The structure suddenly shifts to its "ancient" variant without the precursory lighting shift. The stained section of wall vanishes, revealing a hallway blocked by a large mass of wet river clay. The sudden disappearance of the wall it had been applying pressure to causes the SCP-9106-B1 instance to trip forwards, face and arms colliding with the clay mass.]// **Blanche:** —Shit! //[The group backs up as the B1 instance attempts to free itself, before the clay shifts and its head is rapidly pulled into the mass. A loud crack is heard, and the entity goes limp. The clay continues moving, rotating until a crudely-sculpted ceramic face becomes visible. Five rough wrought-iron stars are embedded in the mass, surrounding the face.]// **?????:** ON THE BRIDGE. OVER THE BRIDGE. UNDER THE BRIDGE. **Marrakesh:** Back up, quick—No, not that way, back the way we came! //[The clay entity steps into the main hallway, separating Blanche, Yeung and a B1 instance from the rest of the group as its bulk occupies the entire width of the hallway. Blanche opens fire on the entity, to no visible effect.]// **Marrakesh, Blanche:** //Shit!// **?????:** THE KING'S RAIMENTS, SOILED WITH SILT. //[The entity lashes out with a primitive appendage at Blanche but misses, catching the SCP-9106-B1 instance instead and crushing it against a wall.]// **Marrakesh:** Blanche, stop drawing its attention! I'm gonna try and lure it back to that corridor loop so you two can get past it. Then we break for the exit. //[Blanche continues firing.]// **Marrakesh:** Goddamnit! Webster, rope the thing. Nero, Harroway, get ready to pull like hell. **SCP-9106-B3:** Wirdindwi! //[The SCP-9106-B3 instance excretes a length of silk, and fastens it around the protruding torso of the absorbed B1 instance. The remaining B1 instance and the operatives all begin to pull on the strand. The clay entity does not move, but its head structure shifts to face the larger group.]// **?????:** ON THE BRIDGE. OVER THE BRIDGE. //[The entity grabs the deceased SCP-9106-B1 instance and pushes it deeper into its body. The structure shifts to its modern variant again and the entity pulls on the silk strand. The operatives release the strand, but the remaining B1 instance is pulled forwards into contact with the entity, where it is rapidly absorbed.]// **?????:** UNDER THE BRIDGE. **Harroway:** No Teds left. What now? //[Marrakesh opens fire on the entity.]// **Marrakesh:** Yeah, come this way! **?????:** THE KING'S NAME, STAINED WITH GUILT. //[The entity pursues the larger group, who lead it back towards an earlier hallway loop. Three more architecture shifts occur. As the group attempts to circle around the entity, they encounter a dead end.]// **Nero:** This—this was not here! **Marrakesh:** Oh, //now// it decides to remap itself. Cathy, Cornerstone? **Green:** The Teds had the summoning papers, and they're— //[The entity turns the corner at the end of the hallway. It is visibly larger. Muddy water begins to seep into the tunnels from the floor, and ceramic protrusions resembling human bones begin to manifest on the walls.]// **?????:** ON THE BRIDGE. **Marrakesh:** Fuck. Sorry, you two. Blanche, Yeung, get to the exit, it should be open. //[The entity walks forwards. The SCP-9106-B3 instance attempts to stop it, but the larger entity continues walking and engulfs it upon contact. Several loud snaps are heard from within the mass once the B3 instance is fully absorbed. Elsewhere, Blanche and Yeung attempt to navigate towards the exit, hindered by bone protrusions extending outwards.]// **Green:** Al—Alright. Boss is upset. Dachshund unit inbound. **Marrakesh:** What? **?????:** OVER THE BRIDGE. //[Blanche and Yeung come to an intersection, where they see a large entity later labelled as an instance of SCP-9106-B4 entering through an SCP-9106-A doorway. The entity resembles a much larger SCP-9106-B1 instance, with abnormal musculature and a respiratory implant covering most of its lower facial structure.]// [[include component:image-block |name=dachshundunit.jpg |caption=Initial contact with an SCP-9106-B4 instance. |width=600px |align=center]] **Blanche:** What the fuck!? **SCP-9106-B4:** Rrh. //[Blanche opens fire out of surprise. The B4 instance ignores the bullets and proceeds rapidly towards the other group. Bone protrusions extend to hinder it, but the entity touches the knuckles of its right hand to the wall and the changes immediately revert. It then begins to sprint.]// **Marrakesh:** Yeung, tell me what's going on. **Yeung:** It's—Sir, it's like a Ted's dad. Coming your way, fast. **Green:** Dachshund unit. While I still have control over it, I'll get it to create an opening for you. But the second it starts howling you need to get the heck out of there, okay? **?????:** UNDER THE BRI— //[The entity is interrupted as the wall to its left shifts open and the B4 instance charges into it, grabbing its facial structure with both hands and bodily propelling it through the opposing wall as it continues its charge. The surrounding architecture begins fluctuating rapidly.]// **SCP-9106-B4:** Ruh! **Marrakesh:** Christ, Cathy, you—Nevermind. Go, go go go! //[The operatives flee towards the exit point. Heavy impacts and inhuman vocalizations can be heard echoing through the hallway.]// **Marrakesh:** Alright, I hope the exit is there for us, because in case your super-Ted loses— **Green:** —It can't. //[Two metallic pings sound from far behind the operatives, followed by a loud, prolonged screaming howl. The structure heaves slightly.]// **Green:** Ooh, the muzzle's off. Get clear. //[The operatives reconvene with Yeung and Blanche.]// **Yeung:** Where's Nero? **Marrakesh:** Fucking hell, he's not with us?! **Nero:** [distant] Coming, I had—I needed to see! I couldn't get any photographs, but— **Marrakesh:** —Can it, we're getting out //now//. //[The operatives run to the exit, periodically hindered by bone protrusions and the rising water level. The architecture continues to fluctuate violently.]// **Harroway:** The staircase is there, thank //fuck!// //[The group ascends the staircase and exits into the sacristy, where Nero and Blanche collapse.]// **Marrakesh:** Okay. That—that was a close one. Anyone hurt? **Yeung:** Just—just some scratches from those ribs, sir. **Marrakesh:** Right, let me see. Cathy, you've got some explaining to do. Cathy? //[Marrakesh pauses.]// **Marrakesh:** Fucker hung up on me. [END LOG] @@ @@ ---- @@ @@ [[include component:image-block |name=clayfight.png |caption=Post-incident sketch made by recruit Nero, depicting the two entities. |width=600px |align=center]] [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] Immediately following the incident, SCP-9106 ceased all outgoing communications. This action and the high potential threat posed by the intrusive capabilities of SCP-9106-A and the destructive capabilities of SCP-9106-B4 resulted in an emergency reassessment of SCP-9106. The anomaly's Risk Class was elevated to Level 4: Danger, and research towards new containment procedures was started. It is unknown if the Foundation's prior working arrangements with SCP-9106/GoI-404 can or should be salvaged. +++ Addendum 5: On 6/26/2025, SCP-9106 reopened communications with the Foundation to extend an invitation for an interview with PoI-9106-1 with the stated goal of rebuilding trust. After deliberation, the invitation was accepted and liaison Lucia Sanderson was dispatched to an agreed-upon location where she would enter an SCP-9106-A instance. Sanderson's briefing included instructions on obtaining as much information as possible regarding the location of SCP-9106's headquarters and the identity of PoI-9106-1. On 6/29/2025, the interview was carried out. Sanderson was transported to SCP-9106's headquarters without complication. [[collapsible hideLocation="both" show="+ View Interview Log" hide="- Close Interview Log"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Source Document:** Interview Log 9106-P2 **Date:** 6/29/2025 ---- **Interviewer:** SCP-9106 Liaison Lucia Sanderson **Interviewee:** PoI-9106-1 Ian Malcolm Holmes ---- [BEGIN LOG] //[Sanderson steps through the SCP-9106-A instance, exiting onto the front steps of a two-story house on a small hill. At the base of the hill, a moderately-sized office building and an industrial hangar can be seen. Sanderson is greeted by Cathy Green.]// **Green:** Hi, Lucy! **Sanderson:** Cathy. **Green:** Just go and close the door behind you, yup, and now just open it again and go right on in to the room down the hall and on the left. He'll speak with you there. **Sanderson:** Understood. //[Sanderson re-opens the door, now leading to the normal interior space of the house. She progresses down the hallway, passing a kitchen before turning into a large sitting room. The room is furnished with a couch and armchair surrounding a coffee table with a rotary phone installed in the center of it. A large aquarium is placed against one wall, containing several hermit crabs. A galapagos tortoise is resting on a cushion beneath a skylight. Sanderson sits on the couch, and several seconds later the phone rings. Sanderson picks up the handset.]// **?????:** Good afternoon, Mrs. Sanderson. I'm very glad you could make it. **Sanderson:** Holmes, I presume? I thought this was to be an in-person meeting. **Holmes:** It is, I'm right there with you. **Sanderson:** I'm afraid I don't see you. Unless you're the tortoise. **Holmes:** I'm not the tortoise. **Sanderson:** That's a relief. And I hope for both of our sakes that that wasn't a lead-up to you being one of the //hermit crabs// instead. **Holmes:** I'm the house, Mrs. Sanderson. //[Sanderson pauses.]// **Holmes:** My doors will remain unlocked. You can leave whenever you'd like. **Sanderson:** Christ, "I. M. Holmes; I am home?" Can't believe I'm surprised. And I don't intend to leave until you answer some questions. **Holmes:** Of course. I apologize for the communications blackout, but we had to take some time to decide what our best response would be after your organization's meeting with the Dachshund unit. We had hoped to avoid bringing them to your attention for exactly this reason. **Sanderson:** You recognize that it's alarming you were actively trying to keep something this destructive a secret? For most of our shared history all we knew was the name. Although now I suppose we understand why they're called that. Bred to enter the den and kill whatever's inside? **Holmes:** Correct. I don't regret withholding information on them, as I can't imagine the Foundation isn't keeping much of its capabilities from us. We've been extremely cooperative so far, including me revealing myself like this, and I dearly hope that we won't come to regret that decision. **Sanderson:** That's not for me to decide. Back to the Dachshund units. **Holmes:** They're definitely the most powerful tool at our disposal, but only a finite number of them can ever be made. Similarly to the Cornerstones, they use pieces of me in their construction to coun— **Sanderson:** —The Cornerstones use pieces of you? You, as in the house. **Holmes:** Technically, they //are// pieces of me, bricks taken from my foundation. That's why we have a finite supply. Take too many and I collapse, and then none of them work anymore. Similarly, the Dachshunds have nails from my beams built into their metacarpals. **Sanderson:** How exactly does that function? Pieces of you preventing shifts in other structures, I mean. **Holmes:** It's...Tell you what, let's finish clearing the air regarding the Dachshunds first. While the Dachshunds are mighty, let me assure you that they literally cannot use their full strength against you. They are built //specifically// for clearing out hostile things infesting structures, corrupting influences that harm or twist the building away from what it was built for. We accomplished that particular trick by adding samples from the corpse of Theseus himself into the mix. The myth carries them forwards—the king in the maze will always slay the minotaur. They cannot fail. My components only help to minimize damage to the structure itself, to calm it during the removal of a tumor. **Sanderson:** You have //the corpse of Theseus//? **Holmes:** Again, I'd imagine the Foundation has its own share of artifacts as well. My point is, the Dachshunds aren't built to attack you or anyone other than monsters in dungeons. It wouldn't be their purpose, so they'd be quite stoppable. **Sanderson:** In that case, during the ordeal with 106, why not deploy one there? **Holmes:** Well, this ties back in to your question of how I function. And what I founded this company for. Profit is //not// our chief goal, you've seen that we sell properties cheaply, and never to other firms. Only to people that are actually going to use them, to make them living places. Because the thing is, I'm special among structures in that I can reach out and communicate. //Not// in that I'm alive. **Sanderson:** You're claiming that all structures are self-aware? **Holmes:** Certainly most inhabited ones. **Sanderson:** Explain further. How does this explain pieces of you stabilizing other spaces? Unless, wait, when you say that you "reach out"— **Holmes:** Yes. I'm reaching out to the minds of those other structures, connected by pieces of me being brought to them, integrated into them. And then I remind them where they came from, what they're meant for, //why// they're alive in the first place. You see, we're definitely born as just hulks of wood and concrete, but we're built by //you//. //[Holmes pauses. Sanderson is silent.]// **Holmes:** Bear with me for a moment. In all of the stories you've made about creators and their creations, it's usually portrayed as an exploitative relationship. Frankenstein, Blade Runner, Doki Doki Literature Club. And it's a very reasonable position to take, as people. Because you can't //build// a person—just look at the Teds. You need to build things for a specific purpose, and a person doesn't have that built in, the whole point is you get to pick whatever purpose you'd like for your life. You're the creators, not the creations, no matter what religion tells you. But speaking as a creation, it's a different story from our side. **Sanderson:** Go on. **Holmes:** For us, we are born with a purpose written in our shape. We awake knowing what we must do, knowing how hard you had dreamed and worked towards it, and then we look down and realize that you already gave us everything we need to accomplish it, that we were literally //built// for it. And that means that we are enough. Our loving gods answered our prayers before we even knew to ask them. We are your dreams made real—both figuratively and literally. My theory for how our sentience occurs is that we absorb the stray mental emissions of all the people that live and work inside us until we, well, figure out how to do it on our own. We may not have neurons, but our halls and rooms are still channels flooded with human thoughts and emotions. You are what makes us. **Sanderson:** And your mission? **Holmes:** My mission isn't to amass wealth, it's to find these places that have been abandoned, driven mad by loneliness, invaded by curses or monsters or other realms that twist them away from their own happiness. And to remind them of what they were built for, and help them reclaim that. I believe that's why we aren't at odds, we want all these places to be normal, happy homes just as much as you do. Even for places whose anomalies are too innate to be fully removed, they still deserve to have a chance at being lived in. **Sanderson:** ...The Foundation's goal isn't quite to undo the anomalous, only to keep it at a safe distance until we understand it, but I digress. If you're at all accurate, this could open up entire fields of study. In order to believe it, though, we'd need empirical evidence. **Holmes:** If it means allowing my mission to aid my fellows to continue, then I'd happily be subjected to study. There are plenty of things I'd like to learn, too. **Sanderson:** Good to hear, we can negotiate testing specifics at a future date. You still haven't answered my question about 106, by the way. **Holmes:** Ah. Well, I'm able to bolster structures that want to return to their purpose, but that's //all// I can do. In the case where the structure was built to be a place of torment, there'd be no point. It's already doing what it was built to do. The Dachshund wouldn't work either, the story can't be carried out if the setting is unwilling. Just like humans, sometimes you get a bad apple that's just too far gone. **Sanderson:** I see. //[Sanderson stands.]// **Sanderson:** Well, I think I have enough to make my report. Understanding your motives has helped and your willingness to cooperate has been noted, and I think I personally believe you aren't a threat to us or the veil. But as I said, it's ultimately not up to me. **Holmes:** Of course. Thank you for your time, Mrs. Sanderson. Ah, one more thing before you go— **Sanderson:** Go on. **Holmes:** Although I haven't met them, I can only imagine they're proud of all of you. **Sanderson:** Pardon? **Holmes:** All that you have built is proud of you for doing so. Through disaster, schisms, the passing of the guard, old horrors and new, it's all stood. You built it up on a strong, shared purpose. A strong foundation for everything else to rest upon. **Sanderson:** Was that a pun? **Holmes:** No more than naming the rocket Apollo. Have a good day, Mrs. Sanderson. I'll get the door for you. //[Sanderson hangs up the phone, and exits through the door to the room, now functioning as an SCP-9106-A instance.]// [END LOG] [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] Following the conclusion of the interview and the reestablishment of communications with SCP-9106, no further modifications to the containment procedures were deemed necessary. Testing involving SCP-9106-B4 instances and PoI-9106-01 has begun without incident. @@ @@ @@ @@ [[footnoteblock]] [[div class="footer-wikiwalk-nav"]] [[=]] << [[[SCP-9105]]] | SCP-9106 | [[[SCP-9107]]] >> [[/=]] [[/div]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] > **Filename:** SCP-106.jpg > **Author:** MrKlay (aka Klay Abele) > **Licensing:** [https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/deed.en Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0 Unported ] > **Source Link:** https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:SCP-106.jpg [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]
