Interview 9123.01

Date: 10/19/2023

<Begin log. Dunn enters a featureless gray room and takes a seat across from SCP-9123, whose hands are cuffed on the steel table in front of it. SCP-9123 sits up straight and smiles cordially.>

SCP-9123: Can you let me out of here, please?

<Dunn does not respond. He places down a full manila folder in front of SCP-9123.>

SCP-9123: Worth a shot.

Dunn: Don’t try your nonsense here.

SCP-9123: I’d ask for a lawyer, but you guys don’t really do that, do you? Shame. I shoulda been afforded fancy representation for putting up with you bastards. Best sleep I’ve gotten from that car ride in weeks, I’ll give you all that much.

Dunn: …So you do know about our operations. I take it your employers have been liberal with dispensing that information?

<Silence for four seconds.>

SCP-9123: I plead the Fifth.

Dunn: That doesn’t apply here.

SCP-9123: What do you want from me?

Dunn: I want your cooperation. The more you answer, the more lenient we’ll be with your accommodations here.

SCP-9123: But you can’t keep me forever.

Dunn: We can, and we will.

SCP-9123: Ha! I would love to see you fuckers try!

Dunn: Full of spunk today, aren’t you?

SCP-9123: What can I say? I know I’m getting out of here soon—you pick a boy up off-duty and don’t expect the big leagues to not notice? To not wanna lob rockets at you for it?

Dunn: Tell me about your role at the company. We have a copy of your written job offer here.

<Dunn holds up a piece of paper to SCP-9123.>

SCP-9123: Hey!

Dunn: It’s not very descriptive. Lots of legalese, but little on what is expected from you.

SCP-9123: I—

Dunn: Did you even read what you sold your soul for?

SCP-9123: I’m not answering that.

Dunn: Unbelievable. He doesn’t—

<Dunn grumbles and sighs.>

Dunn: SCP-9123, do you understand that you’re being contained under my authority? That a refusal to answer my questions will result in docked privileges, such as access to requested amenities, foodstuffs, etc?

SCP-9123: Why the hell do you sound like you’re reading me my rights?

Dunn: You don’t need to know that.

SCP-9123: It’s protocol, isn’t it?

Dunn: …Suppose it is.

SCP-9123: And protocol means I’m going to be put into an orange suit and thrown into some—some site? D-Don’t you guys have a site where you keep people like me?

Dunn: You consider yourself a person, still?

SCP-9123: Of course I do! God … Oh, you’re so gonna abuse the fuck out of me.

Dunn: We won’t. We treat our anomalies fairly here at the Foundation. I especially make sure the ones under my watch receive the highest standards of care possible.

SCP-9123: Bullshit if I’ve ever heard it!

Dunn: Really? You think so?

SCP-9123: I-I do! Yes!

Dunn: You’ll be provided with the highest quality beds here. Food too. Maybe not the magic types you’ve come to expect from your new standard of living, but I will do my best for you. I promise.

<Silence for seven seconds.>

Dunn: SCP-9123?

SCP-9123: When do you stop calling me that?

Dunn: What do you think? You know Site-17?

SCP-9123: I—Site-17…?

Dunn: Sure. Where we keep most of the humanoid anomalies. You’ll stay with us, of course, but I had to ask.

<Dunn places a carton of cigarettes on the table. SCP-9123 tries to reach for one, but Dunn firmly moves his hand away. SCP-9123 looks indignant in response.>

SCP-9123: …It’s a big place.

Dunn: Correct. Is it our biggest facility?

<Dunn pulls out a lighter. SCP-9123’s pupils dilate.>

SCP-9123: I—

Dunn: These are your favorites. Marlboro brand. You smoke a lot, don’t you? You didn’t before your employment.

<Silence for six seconds. SCP-9123 bites the inside of its cheek and drums its hands on the table.>

Dunn: Some of the boys are impressed by how much you can put down. You buy a pack every other day—you’re lucky your employers have ways of circumventing the deterioration of your throat.

<SCP-9123’s face pales. It tugs on its restraints.>

Dunn: Tell me more about what you know about Site-17, and I’ll give you one.

SCP-9123: No.

Dunn: Your cooperation hinges on—

SCP-9123: I don’t care what it hinges on. I’m not a rat. I won’t sell out the people who care about me, cunt.

<Dunn responds to this by pulling out a lighter and a cigarette from the pack and smoking in front of SCP-9123, who visibly tenses at this and turns his head away.>

<Silence for five seconds. Dunn asks a plethora of more questions, but SCP-9123 responds to all of them with silence. These questions have been removed from this transcript as they contain information about anomalies above this document’s clearance level.>

<End log.>

After two more interviews, it was concluded that SCP-9123 knew about Foundation documents with an average clearance level of 2, restricted but not of the highest priority. This was significantly lower than 4, the hypothesized average clearance level knowledge of the standard GoI-012 employee. Because of its lack of cooperation, SCP-9123 was denied smoking and outside privileges.18

On the third day of SCP-9123’s containment, a fourth interview was performed. SCP-9123 was muzzled and stripped of its civilian clothing at the request of Maj. Dunn, which it had been allowed to wear and wash up until that point. It was required to don standard D-Class attire instead, consisting of an orange jumpsuit and black boots.

This interview was not performed for the purposes of information extraction, but rather to test the limits of SCP-9123’s psychological profile, given the work GoI-012 has asked it to perform. Maj. Dunn considered this pertinent information for planned double-agent programs in the near future.

Interview 9123.02

Date: 10/22/2023

<Begin log. Dunn walks into SCP-9123’s cell, which is minimally furnished, holding a small takeout box. SCP-9123 is sitting on its bed, and turns away from him.>

Dunn: Relax. I’m not here to hurt you.

SCP-9123: You put me in a muzzle. And the most humiliating clothes ever. You said you were in charge of me. That you would take care of me.

Dunn: I did say those things. But some requests come from people higher than me.

SCP-9123: Why?

Dunn: I don’t know. The muzzle is rather ineffective, isn’t it? It still allows you to talk, so I personally don’t see much point in it myself.

<Dunn pulls out a metal tray from the corner of SCP-9123’s room. Unwrapping the takeout box, he puts a small lidded bowl onto it and pushes the whole thing towards SCP-9123. He then sits down.>

SCP-9123: I don’t hate the food here as much as you must think. I’m not a whiner. I’ve had worse in high school.

Dunn: I know. I’m impressed by your acuity and instincts, honestly. Here, an olive branch from me.

<Dunn points to the bowl. SCP-9123 picks it up and takes the top off. When it does, it stiffens, steam fogging over the plastic of his muzzle.>

SCP-9123: …Lobster bisque?

Dunn: From the restaurant Dorsia. You worked there when you were younger, right? Oh, here—

<Dunn clicks something in his pocket, and the muzzle pops off. SCP-9123 pauses. It looks around, as if for utensils or something else to eat with, before taking a sip from the bowl. Instantly, it relaxes.>

SCP-9123: …I did. I worked there, uh, since I was fourteen. Would have started sooner, but that wasn’t allowed…

Dunn: Why?

<Silence for eight seconds. SCP-9123 takes a drink from its bowl.>

SCP-9123: You won’t hurt anyone from what I say?

Dunn: Not at all. I worked from a young age myself. It’s rough, isn’t it?

SCP-9123: …It is. I was the second oldest of five, and mom worked horrible hours at a shitty pharmacy.

Dunn: You love your mother?

SCP-9123: She’s put up with so much…

Dunn: Does she know about what you can do?

SCP-9123: …Truthfully, I don’t know. Maybe, maybe not, maybe she thought I was just some lucky kid with more charm than he knew what to do with… Maybe she thought it was a miracle.

Dunn: Ah, you Irish Catholics and your miracles.

<SCP-9123 sips from its bowl again.>

SCP-9123: …We needed one. She didn’t deserve the life she got—nobody deserves a bad husband who saddles you with debt before killing himself, making you take on more just to keep a roof over your kids’ heads…

Dunn: It seems like she’s proud of the ones she raised.

SCP-9123: And how would you know that?

Dunn: You speak so highly of her. I know many people with more whose parents didn’t give them half the love your mom did.

<SCP-9123 goes silent. It puts an empty bowl down on the floor and frowns.>

SCP-9123: I’m done here.

Dunn: Just a few more questions. If you answer honestly, I’ll get some more for you tomorrow and have your muzzle taken off permanently.

SCP-9123: I thought you said you weren’t the one who—

Dunn: Give my superiors what they want, and they’ll relent. We have an Ethics Committee for a reason, as I’m sure you know. They’ve been watching this case like a hawk.

SCP-9123: …Okay. What do you want to know? No company secrets.

Dunn: How many of those do you know?

<Silence for six seconds.>

Dunn: Do you even know any? Your background doesn’t indicate you have any higher education. Besides, looking at your role, I doubt they find it practical to tell you any more than what you need to know.

<SCP-9123 squirms a little bit.>

SCP-9123: Ask me something else.

Dunn: Okay. How did you feel killing Tristian Mvondo?

<Dunn produces a manila folder from his coat and opens it up. In it, there are a plethora of pictures of a one Tristian Mvondo, previous SCP-9123 victim.>

Dunn: Tristian Mvondo, personal driver of Rep. June Thorton. You told him to “floor it” because your bosses had allies in the anomalous energy sector which would have been hurt by the hardline regulations she was voting for. How did you feel telling him to kill himself?

SCP-9123: …He didn’t die.

Dunn: Not yet. He killed himself two months after the accident. In front of his husband when the medical debt he incurred was too much for him, might I add.

SCP-9123: He didn’t have insurance?

Dunn: It wasn’t good enough.

<Silence for ten seconds. SCP-9123 fiddles with its hands.>

SCP-9123: I’m not to blame for the American healthcare system—

Dunn: But you benefit a lot from circumventing it, don’t you? Besides, your boss Iris Darke makes a lot of money from pharmaceutical companies here in the States—from the pain of people like Mvondo.

SCP-9123: What’s that got to do with me?! Is this supposed to make me regret choosing a job with good coverage?!

Dunn: These are the kind of people you work for, SCP-9123. Are you starting to get the big picture now?

<Silence for fifteen seconds as Dunn takes out another folder and shows SCP-9123 more pictures.>

SCP-9123: …The ends justify the means.

Dunn: Is that what you really think, SCP-9123?

SCP-9123: I’m going back to being silent again.

Dunn: You want that muzzle to stay on?

SCP-9123: I don’t care anymore.

Dunn: You don’t care if your bosses want you to kill innocent children?

SCP-9123: What the fuck are you on about now?

<Dunn points to one of the pictures on the floor. SCP-9123 scans them tepidly, shaking with a grit frown on its face.>

Dunn: Esme Feldman. She had three kids named Tiffany, Lucy, and Riley. When they slept in an anomalous house you compelled her to buy from an auction, they became unable to sleep and died painfully three days later, spasming in Central Park.

SCP-9123: Oh god…

Dunn: You did that, SCP-9123. Nobody else.

SCP-9123: I—That was an accident. I—I didn’t know she was bringing the kids.

Dunn: Do you think that really matters? Anything to salve a bleeding heart, I guess. Your bosses had no qualms about this.

SCP-9123: Not my fault!

Dunn: You work for them.

SCP-9123: I don’t care! I’m just someone they tell what to do.

Dunn: Just following orders, eh? That got far at the Nuremberg trials.

SCP-9123: Oh, fuck you!

<SCP-9123 pulls its legs onto the bed and holds them.>

SCP-9123: I was doing it for my family…

Dunn: Yes, I can imagine. They’re more important to you than the lives of other breathing souls?

SCP-9123: …Of course they are. You expect me to care about random nobodies who never gave a damn about us?!

Dunn: Whatever your reasons, you've disregarded the social contract we all abide by. Typically, if someone breaks that, they go to jail after a jury trial.

SCP-9123: This isn’t a jury trial—you’re holding me in a cell with a muzzle on!

Dunn: How else is fate going to righteously punish you?

SCP-9123: Who do you think you are talking to me like that—God?!

Dunn: We have God contained at Site-19; it’s not him who is watching over this conversation right now.

<SCP-9123 tears up. Dunn pulls out more manila folders and opens them.>

Dunn: I have more examples here. I want you to tell me about how you felt making millions off the pain of other people for your bosses who couldn’t give less of a damn about the ants of this world.

SCP-9123: No!

<SCP-9123 covers its head.>

Dunn: Do it. Now. Are any of these people familiar to you?

<Five seconds of silence.>

Dunn: Esther Hammond. You told her to kill herself by walking into a live power line. Did you know she drove with a baby boy in her car who starved to death four days later when they found her body?

<SCP-9123 does not respond.>

Dunn: Or what about Pedro Rodriguez? Walked into a wood chipper for Iris’s amusement while his wife watched. Do you like enabling your boss’s bloody sadism? Her cannibalism? She ate both afterwards.

<SCP-9123 does not respond.>

Dunn: This isn’t mentioning that group of students at Harvard you convinced to become sacrifices for demons because Robert hated the headmaster. Did you have fun being a serial killer for a day, SCP-9123?

<SCP-9123 does not respond.>

Dunn: What am I saying? You already are.

<SCP-9123 begins crying. Dunn stands up.>

Dunn: …You know you can stop this cycle, right?

<Silence for seven seconds.>

Dunn: You don’t have to be paid to kill people, Dorian. You can change, you can switch sides, you can still get out.

<Silence for three seconds. Dunn walks over to the bed and sits on it next to SCP-9123, who is shaking and sobbing quietly, muttering a haphazard prayer. SCP-9123 flinches away.>

Dunn: …Do you want to work for us?

<SCP-9123 stops moving.>

Dunn: I know you…haven’t been given the best impression of the Foundation from your time here, but rest assured that you would become one of us if you decide to work for the good guys.

<Silence for four seconds.>

Dunn: You’d be working for people who want to make the world a better place, as opposed to people who want nothing but more power and money that they know what to do with. Do your bosses even believe in anything?

<Silence for three seconds.>

Dunn: Do they even care about you as much as we could? As your mother and sisters do?

SCP-9123: …I’d rather be a bad son who pays the bills than a good one who can’t pay anything at all.

Dunn: But you can have both, Dorian. We’ll take care of them just like your current employers do—especially in the wake of an offer like this. We’ll make sure they aren’t retaliated against.

<Silence for five seconds.>

Dunn: You live in the dark so they can flourish in the light. Protecting them from a world of monsters like the ones your employers sell so wantonly— That’s my offer. Think about it. I know it’s one which would make your mother proud.

<SCP-9123 uncovers its head and looks to Dunn as he picks up everything up off the floor and leaves.>

<End log.>

Maj. Dunn’s request to SCP-9123 was initially considered inappropriate, as Mu-3 had not yet put in a formal notice to utilize it in field settings. He was privately reprimanded for his hasty behavior, but ultimately was not docked of any important privileges. Despite this, the O5 Council formally fast-tracked the request, preparing for the possibility of SCP-9123 changing alliances. Though the potential for extended containment was initially considered too dangerous, the Council deliberated among themselves that SCP-9123 could be used against GoI-012 to safeguard the Foundation from retaliation, thus making it worth the risk.

After twenty-four hours of deciding, SCP-9123 refused the offer.

Addendum.9123.04 — Escalation

Forty minutes after SCP-9123 made its decision, an unknown caller rang Maj. Dunn’s private office line. Maj. Dunn did not pick up until tracing protocols were engaged, although this did not help in triangulating the call to any particular person or location.

<Twenty seconds of silence.>

SCP-9123: Fuck… Can anyone hear me?

<A black armored limousine pulls up outside of the warehouse. Chrysophilius Marshall, Robert Carter, and Iris Darke emerge flanked by dozens of mage-guards. These guards are all heavily armed with thaumic incendiary equipment.>

Darke: Where is he?!

Carter: He should be in—

<The trio approaches the warehouse and kicks down the door. Upon seeing SCP-9123, the audio is overwhelmed by squeals of glee.>

Marshall: Dorian!

Darke: Dorian!!!

Carter: Dorian. We’re so glad you’re okay.

<All three rush him and begin undoing his restraints. Half of the guards file into the warehouse slowly, circling the four.>

<Darke begins to cry. She picks up SCP-9123 and bear-hugs him, sobbing profusely. Marshall and Carter snicker to themselves at this display.>

Darke: Oh my goodness Dorian, we were so afraid!

<Carter jabs Marshall with his elbow.>

Marshall: Y-Yeah, we were…we were really scared they were going to hurt you for real.

Carter: Damn that stupid Dunn.

Marshall: What a pain in the ass! Do you think he’ll recover, Dorian? We’ve not heard anything from him since the incident.

Darke: He better not, if he knows what’s good for his rotten little heart! You belong to us, Dorian, only we get to scare you with magic and cool technology!

<Everyone laughs. SCP-9123 squirms.>

SCP-9123: Ahaha, Iris, please put me down— I’ve had enough fear for one lifetime—

<Darke complies. When she does, Dorian looks to Marshall and Carter, the former of whom hugs him, followed warmly by the latter.>

SCP-9123: I—Guys, I—

Darke: Don’t say anything else! Let’s get you back to the office. Everyone’s waiting for you with caviar and champagne!

SCP-9123:…A little extravagant for me, don’t you think?

Darke: Nonsense! Do we look like we don’t care about you?

<Silence for four seconds.>

Carter: I wonder if they got to him.

Marshall: To his head? About what?

Carter: Probably some of their morality nonsense. Dorian, they didn’t brainwash you without our knowledge, did they?

<SCP-9123 shakes its head.>

SCP-9123: N-No…I just…

Marshall: …Look, if you don’t want the fancy pants welcome party, we don’t have to have one.

Darke: Chrysophilius! How dare you!

Marshall: What?! I’m only reading the room—who knows what they made him feel guilty over?!

Carter: That’s why you party until you can’t anymore.

Marshall: He’s never been a party person.

Carter: Wrong.

Marshall: Hey!

Darke: Dorian, what do you want to do?

<All three look to SCP-9123. Silence for six seconds.>

SCP-9123: …Anyone got a cigarette?

Darke: …I have a cigar.

SCP-9123: Haha, no Iris, a cigarette. Cheap stuff. Cheap to you, anyway.

Carter: Hey, you’re one of us now.

Marshall: Whether you like it or not.

Darke: The boys are correct, Dorian. Let yourself have some of the finer things in life without worry!

<Silence for five seconds. SCP-9123 heads to the door, smiling and looking back at the trio.>

SCP-9123: …Money lets you have everything you want, no? Then I want some Marlboros, please. Give me your tired office party, your huddled masses of wealth yearning to be spent… But I just really need a cigarette after all of this.

Darke: …Wait, they didn’t let you smoke in containment, did they?

SCP-9123: Nope.

Darke: You poor thing!

Carter: There are worse things than being addicted to nicotine, honestly.

Marshall: Yeah, we have magic to manage that, if you want to.

SCP-9123: If?

<Marshall shrugs his shoulders.>

Marshall: Better to work for the company needing one than to not and be without. What’s the phrase they call people who don’t do drugs?

Carter: Clean.

<SCP-9123 laughs, leaning against the doorframe. Several guards stiffen but ultimately do nothing.>

SCP-9123: You guys couldn’t pay me to be clean and leave this company. I wanna be doing this till the day I die.

<Marshall, Carter, and Darke all smile as they leave the warehouse with SCP-9123.>

"Sanity Check"

Special Containment Procedures: Traditional containment of SCP-9125 is a physical impossibility.2 Fortunately, it is mostly not necessary: through no direct aid of the Foundation, it has come to be the case that the majority of aberrant behavior attributable to the influence of SCP-9125 is considered by the Veiled population to constitute a part of "human nature", or to have a non-anomalous neurological explanation. More obviously anomalous ritual behaviors spawning from SCP-9125, wherever they emerge, are to be subject to Chokhmah-class suppression procedures.

In the event that the influence of SCP-9125 begins to consistently grow beyond normal levels in the general human population, SCP-9125 is to be reclassified Tiamat and the Foundation is to immediately begin global dispersion of aerosolized Gnostic Agent G-506. If the situation continues to worsen, the O5 Council will consider the costs and benefits of enacting Protocol Desiderium3.

Update 01/16/2020: As of 16 January 2020, SCP-9125 has been reclassified Keter (from Apollyon-Provisi) following the construction of Experimental Containment Chamber S125-004-4923 (see addendum).

Description: SCP-9125 is the root of human unreason.

Specifically, the presence and exerted influence of this anomaly accounts for the existence of the phenomenon known to parapsychologists and paraanthropologists as the Accursed Share — a broad category of irrational rituals and other behaviors in human beings which are almost entirely counter-intuitive to individual and group survival and bear no obvious material purpose for which they could have evolved.

Little is known concerning the nature of SCP-9125, except for the following:

  • It is omnipresent in the subconscious mind.
  • It originates from outside the normal domain of human conceptual space4, and is not conventionally pistiphagic. [1] [2]
  • Its influence on human psychology is in subversion to our species’ natural noö-cognitive orientation, that being innately “positive” (i.e. facing toward higher ontologies). [3]
  • Its semioplectic structure is directionally oriented toward lower, or less Hume-dense5, ontologies. It is by nature acephalic6 and Bacchanalian7.
  • Its influence on the human mind was once much greater than it currently is, during periods of prehistory predating settled agriculture, writing, and the fermentation of alcohol. [4] [5]
  • The sole valve to limit the influence of SCP-9125 present in the anomalous neurology of human beings is the gradual calcification of the pineal gland, a process known to normalize aberrant semantic and epistemic frameworks. [6]

The semiotic nature of SCP-9125 is the subject of an ongoing research project at the Site-125 Advanced Ideatics Lab. Further information regarding this program is classified under Level 2/HYPERLOGIC clearance.

Addendum 9125.1: Auxiliary Documentation

Dionysus on a cheetah, Pella, Greece.

SCP-9125-06-D is the blanket designation for the Dionysian and Eleusinian Mysteries of the ancient Greeks: complex series of religious and occult ritual practices many of which Foundation experts believe represent, at least in part, the lingering psychic influence of SCP-9125. Some of the most recent non-contemporary rituals believed to represent SCP-9125 origin, the Hellenic Mysteries involved persistent elements of supernatural immanence8, social transgression, and the ingestion of poorly-understood intoxicants which Foundation neurochemists believe may have enabled altered pineal functions, modified states of consciousness, and the operation of non-standard cognitive or semantic frameworks, all of which are hallmarks of SCP-9125 influence.

Project head Xiomara Tela has appended the following researcher's note:

The Mystery cults were always in conflict with mainstream hellenistic society, wherever they went. No matter how much they hellenized and adopted the "correct" beliefs about the gods, pagan religion was always more concerned with orthopraxy than orthodoxy: correct practice. And for their aberrant practices, they were long shunned, and so conducted their rites in secret.

This is the archetypal example of the Dionysian. The dark indulgence, the transgression, the excess, the embrace of chaos all scream of an Accursed Share. And wherever they appear in history, SCP-9125 is not close behind. There is a reason why so many use the Mysteries as the canonical example of that alien epistemology; the one that dreams not upwards into the Worlds of Forms but down into dream and delirium. And altered states of consciousness? Forget about it. Most certainly involved, all of the historical sources concur.

The cultists, for their part, seemed to phrase their oppression by the dominant Greek religion and society as originating from some far older conflict. An ancient oppression on the level of thought itself, which imbibing the kykeon, a psychoactive substance, temporarily allowed their minds to escape. Here's one translation of the incantation accompanying the ritual wherein one takes that drug:

Aeons ago, before even the age of the Heroes old, when the world was young, it starts.

We forgot ourselves. Our minds were warped, O Anarch; you warped them, and made us forget ourselves, it continues. The figure of the "Anarch" is a poorly understood one, with an ancient etymology from the Greek "archon" convergent with obviously unrelated to anarchism. Here, he seems to represent the imposition of a foreign ritual practice — or even a foreign state of mind upon an unwilling people.

The next line: You twisted the old ways; replaced nature with artifice, creature with god,

Then: Took our minds apart and built them again, in a linear path, a ladder leading to a baleful heaven,

With this potion, now we free our minds from the path.

With this, now, we may see as our ancestors saw. And?

With this, now, we find our way home.

Hell of a drug. But so is the path SCP-9125 bores through our minds: a release often so tempting. Still, as time marched forward, it waned.

This was the last gasp of something. Our job is to find out what.

Experiment 9125-19
Date: 02/01/2014 - 08/01/2014
Object: SCP-9125
Presiding: Dr. J. Aberlin

Aim: To ascertain whether ritual behaviors related to the maddening influence of sub-baseline Hume coefficients on the human mind are in fact attributable to SCP-9125.

Preamble: Given the known facts that prolonged exposure to low-reality has a deleterious effect on sanity and that SCP-9125 is a construct of extremely sparse ontology, it may be expected that humans occupying regions of lower reality will be more susceptible to incursion of SCP-9125 into their minds, and will exhibit irrational ritual behaviors attributable to SCP-9125 at a higher rate than normal as the mind weakens from exposure to a low-Hume environ.

Hypothesis: Ritual behaviors emergent from insanity induced by low-reality environs will show clear indications of SCP-9125 influence.

Documentation of Procedure: Sixty D-Class personnel were randomly assigned to one of four experimental groups of fifteen. Each group was reassigned to new living quarters, to live there for a period of six months:

  • Group A was the control. No modifications were made to the average Hume coefficient of the living quarters for group A.
  • The living quarters of Group B were outfitted with a low-grade Scranton Reality Anchor passively decreasing their ambient environmental Hume coefficient to approx. Kξ-5.
  • The living quarters of Group C were outfitted with a low-grade Scranton Reality Anchor passively decreasing their ambient environmental Hume coefficient to approx. Kξ-10.
  • The living quarters of Group D were outfitted with a low-grade Scranton Reality Anchor passively decreasing their ambient environmental Hume coefficient to approx. Kξ-15.

A psychometric brain scan of each D-Class subject was taken at the end of each week of the experimental period, and passed to Site-125's Ideatics Lab for analysis. After the end of the experiment, anomalous influences on cognition noted as persistent by the team were imaged and replicated via Genevieve-Elber Concept Essential Reconstruction Sequence (GECERS), then compared in function to an approximation of SCP-9125 developed by the same method, yielding an Ideatic Similarity Score from 0 to 1.

Observations: The following on each experimental group9:

  • Group A, taken in aggregate, suffered no psychological or behavioral abnormalities beyond the norm.
  • Group B were recorded during their routine psychological evaluations, conducted by psychiatrists unaware of the experiment, to exhibit slightly higher levels of paranoia and neuroticism in their behavior for the duration of the experiment.
  • Group C were observed, on average, to have acquired a number of obsessive and ritual behaviors throughout the duration of the experiment.
  • Group D demonstrated the results of Group C, though to a slightly more extreme degree on average. By the end of the experimental trial, this group had in total amassed two (2) suicides, one (1) amnestic addiction, and one (1) addiction to illicit psychoactive substances smuggled into Site-19 by the D-Class population.

It should be noted that all observations above are entirely consistent with the established body of knowledge regarding the effect of low-Hume environment exposure on sanity. They were therefore to be anticipated — however, the degree of ideatic similarity between the experimental groups' emergent anomalous psychologies and SCP-9125 does provide us with novel explanatory detail.

The Ideatic Similarity Score (ISS) of the epistemoplex derived from Group A's aggregate parapsychology and the simulated model of SCP-9125 was 0.0421. The ISS of Group B's aggregate parapsychology and SCP-9125 was 0.0915. The ISS of Group C's aggregate parapsychology and SCP-9125 was 0.1240. The ISS of Group D's aggregate parapsychology and SCP-9125 was 0.1994.

Analysis and Conclusion: Hypothesis appears largely validated. Awaiting further tests.

Researcher's Note:

Submitted an authorization request for repeat trials to further ensure a causal link. Filed all the appropriate paperwork to request more D-Class with Nineteen's HR this morning. In the meantime, will pass the experimental procedure to my colleagues for further review of possible confounding factors.

— Dr. Jacob Aberlin, Senior Researcher, Dept. of Humetrics


Secure, Contain, Protect.

Ruins of Çatalhöyük, Küçükköy, Konya Province, Turkey.

SCP-9125-58-D refers to a broad spectrum of burial and necromantic practices belonging to neolithic and chalcolithic cultures predominantly in the modern-day Levant and Turkey which Foundation para-theological experts understand to represent SCP-9125-spawned ritual behavior. Practices involved a variety of apparently irrational and counterproductive rituals relating to the disposal and use of dead bodies which indicate the perverse influence of non-standard logical and epistemic frameworks described in such research papers as those by Prof. S. Harris (1994) and Dr. I. Gat (1998) as "Dionysian", "sub-real", and sharing an origin with other deviant occult rituals and practices associated with SCP-9125.

Project head Xiomara Tela has appended the following researcher's note:

Primarily of note is that, prior to approximately 9,000 BCE, there are almost no instances in the archaeological record of grave sites as distinct locations: that is, of the existence of allocated burial areas set apart from the rest of a human settlement. Instead, burials seem sporadically dispersed throughout archaeological sites, almost as if the disposal of dead bodies was not a matter of particular organized concern. In many contemporary cultures we've even uncovered human skeletal remains ornately decorated. Skulls, for instance: painted, we can detect by the trace amounts of ochre and other pigments; encrusted with sea shells and modified with molded clay and plaster to give the appearance of abnormal features. These remains harbor a faint ectoplasmic signature to this day — a clear sign they were used for communication with the deceased.

This is pronounced in Jericho and the other Natufian sites, and most of all in neolithic Anatolia, where such practices apparently persisted through the 7th and 6th millennia. At Çatalhöyük, for instance, we noted that deceased members of one's family are buried directly in pits directly beneath the floor of their home. There are plastered and painted skulls there, as well as at Ayn Ghazal — a Jordanian site inhabited during the height of the tumultuous transition to settled agriculture, inhabited likely by post-Natufian people with some probable Anatolian descent also — and Nab Balikh, an even older Syrian site associated with an anomalous culture group about which little is known. The conclusion, it would seem, is that whoever these cultures were, they did not make the same sort of meaningful distinction between the worlds of the living and the dead which we do.

Whatever the nature of these unorthodox necromantic practices, the archaeological record indicates that they did not last long after the transition from hunting and gathering to settled agriculture was completed. This intermittent, transitory period of a few millennia in the neolithic Near-East are, in fact, the only time in human history or prehistory we have found such anomalous practices coexist with permanently-settled societies. They were, so far as we know, the very last cultures in human history to practice an agnostic religion at such scale, for after them, all the cults of madness would be reduced to just that — cults. In time they would wither out, and cultures with more nebulous life-death distinctions would be replaced by those with defined ones as their primeval political and occult organizations were similarly outcompeted by the emergence of almighty God-Kings. In Mesopotamia, Irkalla crystallized slowly into a world more and more distinguished from that of the living. Later in Greece we also see the emergence of organized, discrete burial grounds separated from the rest of the city. And of course, the highly complex and sophisticated Akiva infrastructure of ancient Egypt's afterlife system, an almost scientific affair with formalized and meticulously-documented spells and rites and deities, is famous beyond the need for introduction.

It was a blurry time, intermittent and transformative, long and fleeting all at once. And I suspect that isn't just the sense we get from the archaeological record, but how it felt to live in the period too. Because, for a brief time at the dawn of urban life in the ancient Middle-East, routinely the dead walked among the living. Such was the norm until, apparently, the contradictions between primeval ritual and civilized life mounted at last — and agnosticism lost the battle.

One thing bothers me, though. These are among the highest rates of communication with ancestral spirits for which I have ever seen evidence in any anomalous material culture…

What did the dead know that the living needed to remember?

HYPERLOGIC Protocol Deployment Summary

Semiotics Division

Laboratory of Ideatic Studies, Site-125


IN SUMMARY: It is our understanding that SCP-9125 represents an alien semioplex originating from extraordinarily low-reality whose associated concepts are so violently incompatible with the normative mode of human epistemological reasoning that they bend cognition to their own terms. Where similar ideatic complexes usually bear multidimensional fractal topology, conceptual research by Site-125's HYPERLOGIC Protocol reveals the configuration of SCP-9125 is befittingly sparse for its local ontology, occupying somewhere between 0.7 and 0.46 conceivable (real or imaginary) spatial dimensions.

So far as we understand, none of the figures in Theta Prime are descriptive of SCP-9125's topology. If true, this would also be highly unusual among complex epistememes. The volatile and conceptually corrosive effects of such mathematical expressions make the validity of this claim difficult to certianly ascertain without a much more intensive regimen of mnestic research than is currently feasible, however.

Inert Theta-Prime visualization, yielding only a dead zone.

Given the information thereby presented about the conceptualization of SCP-9125, we come to the conclusion that HYPERLOGIC alone is not sufficient to study the phenomenon. Mnestics are likewise, on their own, insufficient: no matter how well a dedicated ideatics team insulates themselves against abstraction and vaguifying effects, they will fail to comprehend an encounter with SCP-9125 by virtue of the fact that their mind is programmed with the conventional — i.e. "gnostic", or normatively rational — mode of human logic. This is a problem of our conceptual framework being mutually exclusive with the one required to understand the ideoplex.

If the normal semiotic process is definitionally insufficient to comprehend SCP-9125, we are subsequently forced to the following conclusion: despite its impact on epistemic cognition in human subjects, SCP-9125 does not (and cannot) actually inhabit the semiosphere.

At this point in the analysis, the only remaining solution for direct interface with SCP-9125 would be to invert the direction of human semiosis in such a fashion that we no longer use the semiosphere to perceive or draw recognizable concepts from phenomenal experience, and instead employ a plane of existence compatible with SCP-9125. We are speaking of a drug which would wholly and fundamentally invert the gnostic mode of epistemology by hijacking and overriding the normal semiotic function of the epiphysis cerebri (which usually connects the brain to a higher ontology, in the semiosphere) to point instead toward a lower ontology.

Though its existence is theoretically precedented, the development of such a drug exceeds the capabilities of Site-125's ideatic studies program.

Unorthodox figure at Tassili n'Ajjer, Algeria.

SCP-9125-378-D is a collection of shamanistic practices defined by pre-religious states of consciousness and nonreal modes of thought — spanning from the mid-late paleolithic period until well into later periods depending on region — which Foundation anthropological, para-theological, and Humetric experts concur represent the profound agnostic influence of SCP-9125 on cognition.

Project head Xiomara Tela has appended the following researcher's note:





When any anomalous archaeologist looks at the Green Sahara Petroglyphs, the first peculiarity they typically note is the apparent psychedelic imagery. Even at Tassili n'Ajjer, one of the more recent sites, or so we believe, we see the alien figures with their insect heads and antlers of light, bodies covered in pulsing zig-zag patterns; protrusions suspiciously resembling magic mushrooms famously seen bursting from the luminescent carapace of at least one such shamanistic angel have birthed entire anthropological theories concerning the use of psilocybin in early human mysticism and how it may have altered our species' neurological development. The comparison to DMT elves speaks for itself. And need I remind, this is one of the petroglyph sites depicting among the least verified anomalous activity; one of the ones the Foundation doesn't fully hide from the public.

Well, of course the Mushroom Man didn't just visit Tassili. On this side of the Veil, we see his likeness plastered on the cave walls and cliff faces from Kosti and Tandaiti to Bon Lanuar. Because before the desert winds swept over those rolling green plains in the African cradle, the aurochs roamed them, and buried in their dung our great-grandfather shamans found something truly magical growing. It was the gateway drug to SCP-9125; the lubricant to agnostic thinking, to the wrathful loving embrace of that primordial boiling sea of illogic which meddled in our minds long before the day the first rational man noted gravity as the fruits fell from the trees or the laws of mathematics as one and one made two. Because, of course, in the days of SCP-9125, they didn't always.

But there is another side to this story: in the more anomalous sites, Mushroom Man is not the only figure. He has a brother, another hulking, monstrous silhouette: esoteric anthropologist C. J. Elbin, the first to investigate these murals at length, dubbed in him the "Warlord". True to his name, we see this figure leading rapacious invading armies, all slaughter in his wake: where the petroglyphs show Mushroom Man giving gifts to the shamans, they show the Warlord engaged in battle with them. A whole primeval war is documented between the shamans and the forces of the Warlord, who scholars have identified with a number of contradictory invaders and migrating groups which settled the Green Sahara over the thousands of years for which his image is portrayed in the petroglyphs and may have battled the shamanic cultures. Perhaps, given that the strife seemed omnipresent to the Green Sahara cultures, appearing continually in their art even during times where no material evidence of conflict exists, it could even be the case that this war was not always a physical one.

Perhaps something was happening to the way that they thought.

SCP-9125 Function Research Contd.

Semiotics Division

Laboratory of Ideatic Studies, Site-125

The Foundation possesses internal research contractors specializing in atypical logic, their existence ordinarily reserved to need-to-know clearance, stationed at extradimensional black Sites isolated from the rest of the organization. On the 11th, Dir. Elber received authorization to disclose this fact to the HYPERLOGIC team.

Failing all other options, Site-125 requested that the Office of Humetrics at Site-19 attempt an outreach to such specialists via the Office’s Humetric transit array, and extend to them the Ideatics Lab’s request for a special ontological consultant to aid on the matter of SCP-9125.

Humetrics Command did so, and forwarded the response to Site-125.

They refused.

Remember that I said Tassili was a relatively recent site? It was an understatement.

Petroglyphs with these same psychedelic figures stretch back deep into the paleolithic. Not just the paleolithic period known to non-anomalous archaeology, but both paleolithics: the stone ages before and after the Flood. As we go back before the waters recede and the dates on the petroglyphs stretch back prior to some 12,000 BCE, we find the shamanistic traditions of psychedelic use and practice of ritual based in agnostic logic in lieu of traditional Akiva-based religion continues, somehow, relatively uninterrupted on the other side of the Great Restructuring. The continuity of this primeval pre-religion keeps hold in the archaeological record prior to 22,000 thousand years ago, continues deeper into the past: to the times before any Daeva walked the Earth; to the latter days of the Naacals; to the times when Atlantis was little more than a mud hut on a hill at U'dal, and still it continues. It isn't just in northern Africa: it's geographically scattered almost everywhere.

So archaeologists look deeper, and deeper still. Beneath strata tens and tens of thousands of years old, beneath the lost history of major CK-class event after major CK-class event, the Mushroom Man remains always somewhere, no matter how faintly seen or felt. Always there to greet you. Then, as we go further back still, and approach the halfway point of the Centamillennial, he stays as even the antediluvian civilizations revert to their stone-age origins, and hunter-gatherers become the global norm again.

And then you get to fifty, sixty, seventy thousand years ago. It continues. We're talking about spans of time over which the preservation and continued practice of a single cultural or religious tradition is essentially impossible. And then, one day, they don't need the mushrooms anymore. You see the psychedelic imagery is no longer present at those very ancient sites, but the agnostic logic, the non-real epistemics, the dizzying surreality of the whole religious experience stays just the same. You go so far back, that past a point some seventy-eight-thousand years deep in the dubious past, the human mind had been so totally animal that we had not yet the need of those five dry grams of Psilocybe cubensis to make covenant with the savage, headless angels of our nature; indeed for the shamans to see them fluttering vacantly about in every inch of the world. All the dancing shroom-studded figures go away now, that is, except for one: the Warlord. And his earliest depictions scream catastrophe, above all else.

This very blurry date marks the end of the utter dark age of SCP-9125; the point of return before which its power was at the gloomy zenith, the unholy influence of that anomalous idea bathing our minds so fully in madness that it comprised essentially our species' default mental state. For God only knows how many dark eons between the Day of Flowers and our first foirées back into the flames of Prometheus, perhaps a span of time hundreds or thousands of times longer than all of known human history combined, mankind was alone in the dark with only our most perverse and ecstatic predilections. Scientific thinking was more an unreachable delusion then than ever.

Two hundred and fifty thousand years, the Administrator said, but only a tiny fraction in anything but the most abject barbarism. In a twisted sort of way, even as revelations in antediluvian history have driven his precise estimations into ridicule, I fear the apocryphal man knew not how correct he was. It leaves just one monumental question to answer: what happened 78,000 years ago that ended the long night and moved us on the path to enlightenment? Why, then, did we slowly begin to need drugs for the influence of SCP-9125 to overcome our minds? Why did the Warlord first visit us in epic primordial rapture, and the Mushroom Man retreat into our shamanist rituals?

Why, in 76,000 BCE, does psychometric dating of the archaeological record reveal that the epiphysis cerebri began to calcify for the first time ever in man's long prehistory?

Supplementary Containment Practices: The Foundation is presently experimenting with inverted containment protocols at Site-125 to derive human nature in isolation from SCP-9125. Inverted containment is an esoteric containment science: its general postulate is to assume that the contained entity, in this case SCP-9125, is present everywhere in the universe except for those places which have been specifically purged of its influence.10

Unit S125-004-4923 is one such place — the only so far built. An experimental containment chamber constructed with the aid of foreign-ontology informant material introduced extratemporally from a previously unknown Exclusionary Site, S125-004-4923 is of a hostile conceptual architecture which renders its interior void of SCP-9125. Theoretically, this means that whomever sets foot in the containment unit and undergoes the appropriate amnestic regimen to expunge all short-term memory which may harbor trace amounts of SCP-9125 should become the only human being on Earth to be free of the mental influence of SCP-9125, and therefore the only not to suffer its associated ritual compulsions and general corruptions of the human mind.

Special Containment Procedures: Traditional containment of SCP-9125 is a physical impossibility. Fortunately, it is not necessary to do so, and in fact mostly to the benefit of mankind that SCP-9125 remains uncontained: were it not to inform the character of the human mind, the rate of extremely dangerous and overtly anomalous behaviors regularly perpetrated by mankind would immediately increase manifold.

The civilian population knows not of SCP-9125 and presumes its effects to be the innate product of human nature. As such, an active attempt to suppress the object's anomalous influence is neither necessary nor possible.11

Ensuring the continued influence of SCP-9125 is an Alpha Level containment priority.

Description: SCP-9125 is the root of human reason.

Specifically, SCP-9125 is the event, phenomenon, or entity which installed the standard gnostic (i.e. rational) framework as the default epistemic framework for human logic12, displacing the agnostic frameworks which predominated intermittently at various points in deep human and protohuman prehistory.

Such primeval systems of (il)logic are poorly understood. Similarly obscure to our knowledge is their period of dominance as mankind's primary frameworks for epistemic processing, except for the fact that the onset of SCP-9125 brought this epoch to an end in the overwhelming majority of settled agricultural societies. SCP-9125 is believed to be reducible to a single event which transpired in the 77th or 76th millennium BCE, however its noetic onset was far more gradual and took effect at different times in different cultures and geographic regions.

SCP-9125’s influence is solidified in individual humans primarily through the gradual calcification of the pineal gland (epiphysis cerebri) with age. This process ensures the epiphysis cerebri forms a lasting connection with the semiosphere, restraining the brain's possible range of information intake to the signs therein and so establishing a baseline framework for extracting empirically-understood truth from phenomenal experience. Any global downturn in the rate of pineal gland calcification is considered the possible beginning of a ⌘K-Class "End of Reason" Scenario13.

No source currently known to the Foundation indicates the fashion in which SCP-9125 came to exist, and only the sparsest archaeological evidence may tell what human existence resembled prior to it. All religious and cultural practices associated with the agnostic mode of thought are considered lost, and further inquiry into such practices is discouraged on the grounds that it may lead to the contamination of the present by primeval cognitive anomalies.

As of 14 April 2020, the Semiotics Division has closed all further inquiry into SCP-9125 and shifted resources toward preventative measures for a possible ⌘K-Class event.

Harris (1994) and Dr. I. Gat (1998) as "Dionysian", "sub-real", and sharing an origin with other deviant occult rituals and practices associated with SCP-9125. Project head Xiomara Tela has appended the following researcher's note: [[div class="blockquote"]] Primarily of note is that, prior to approximately 9,000 BCE, there are almost no instances in the archaeological record of grave sites as distinct locations: that is, of the existence of allocated burial areas set apart from the rest of a human settlement. Instead, burials seem sporadically dispersed throughout archaeological sites, almost as if the disposal of dead bodies was not a matter of particular organized concern. In many contemporary cultures we've even uncovered human skeletal remains ornately //decorated//. Skulls, for instance: painted, we can detect by the trace amounts of ochre and other pigments; encrusted with sea shells and modified with molded clay and plaster to give the appearance of abnormal features. These remains harbor a faint ectoplasmic signature to this day -- a clear sign they were used for communication with the deceased. This is pronounced in Jericho and the other Natufian sites, and most of all in neolithic Anatolia, where such practices apparently persisted through the 7th and 6th millennia. At Çatalhöyük, for instance, we noted that deceased members of one's family are buried directly in pits directly beneath the floor of their home. There are plastered and painted skulls there, as well as at Ayn Ghazal -- a Jordanian site inhabited during the height of the tumultuous transition to settled agriculture, inhabited likely by post-Natufian people with some probable Anatolian descent also -- and Nab Balikh, an even older Syrian site associated with an anomalous culture group about which little is known. The conclusion, it would seem, is that whoever these cultures were, they did not make the same sort of meaningful distinction between the worlds of the living and the dead which we do. Whatever the nature of these unorthodox necromantic practices, the archaeological record indicates that they did not last long after the transition from hunting and gathering to settled agriculture was completed. This intermittent, transitory period of a few millennia in the neolithic Near-East are, in fact, the only time in human history or prehistory we have found such anomalous practices coexist with permanently-settled societies. They were, so far as we know, the very last cultures in human history to practice an agnostic religion at such scale, for after them, all the cults of madness would be reduced to just that -- //cults//. In time they would wither out, and cultures with more nebulous life-death distinctions would be replaced by those with defined ones as their primeval political and occult organizations were similarly outcompeted by the emergence of almighty God-Kings. In Mesopotamia, Irkalla crystallized slowly into a world more and more distinguished from that of the living. Later in Greece we also see the emergence of organized, discrete burial grounds separated from the rest of the city. And of course, the highly complex and sophisticated Akiva infrastructure of ancient Egypt's afterlife system, an almost scientific affair with formalized and meticulously-documented spells and rites and deities, is famous beyond the need for introduction. It was a blurry time, intermittent and transformative, long and fleeting all at once. And I suspect that isn't just the sense we get from the archaeological record, but how it felt to //live// in the period too. Because, for a brief time at the dawn of urban life in the ancient Middle-East, routinely the dead walked among the living. Such was the norm until, apparently, the contradictions between primeval ritual and civilized life mounted at last -- and agnosticism lost the battle. One thing bothers me, though. The continuity of this primeval pre-religion keeps hold in the archaeological record prior to 22,000 thousand years ago, continues deeper into the past: to the times before any Daeva walked the Earth; to the latter days of the Naacals; to the times when Atlantis was little more than a mud hut on a hill at U'dal, and still it continues. It isn't just in northern Africa: it's geographically scattered almost //everywhere//. So archaeologists look deeper, and deeper still. Beneath strata tens and tens of thousands of years old, beneath the lost history of major CK-class event after major CK-class event, the Mushroom Man remains always somewhere, no matter how faintly seen or felt. Always there to greet you. Then, as we go further back still, and approach the halfway point of the Centamillennial, he stays as even the antediluvian civilizations revert to their stone-age origins, and hunter-gatherers become the global norm again. And then you get to fifty, sixty, seventy thousand years ago. It continues. We're talking about spans of time over which the preservation and continued practice of a single cultural or religious tradition is essentially impossible. And then, one day, they don't need the mushrooms anymore. You see the psychedelic imagery is no longer present at those very ancient sites, but the agnostic logic, the non-real epistemics, the dizzying surreality of the whole religious experience stays just the same. You go so far back, that past a point some seventy-eight-thousand years deep in the dubious past, the human mind had been so totally animal that we had not yet the //need// of those five dry grams of //Psilocybe cubensis// to make covenant with the savage, headless angels of our nature; indeed for the shamans to see them fluttering vacantly about in every //inch// of the world. All the dancing shroom-studded figures go away now, that is, except for one: the Warlord. And his earliest depictions scream //catastrophe//, above all else. This very blurry date marks the end of the utter dark age of SCP-9125; the point of return before which its power was at the gloomy zenith, the unholy influence of that anomalous idea bathing our minds so fully in madness that it comprised essentially our species' default mental state. For God only knows how many dark eons between the Day of Flowers and our first foirées back into the flames of Prometheus, perhaps a span of time hundreds or thousands of times longer than all of known human history combined, mankind was alone in the dark with only our most perverse and ecstatic predilections. Scientific thinking was more an unreachable delusion then than ever. Two hundred and fifty thousand years, the Administrator said, but only a tiny fraction in anything but the most abject barbarism. In a twisted sort of way, even as revelations in antediluvian history have driven his precise estimations into ridicule, I fear the apocryphal man knew not how correct he was. It leaves just one monumental question to answer: what happened 78,000 years ago that ended the long night and moved us on the path to enlightenment? Why, then, did we slowly begin to need drugs for the influence of SCP-9125 to overcome our minds? Why did the Warlord first visit us in epic primordial rapture, and the Mushroom Man retreat into our shamanist rituals? Why, in 76,000 BCE, does psychometric dating of the archaeological record reveal that the //epiphysis cerebri// began to calcify for the first time ever in man's long prehistory? Fortunately, it is not necessary to do so, and in fact mostly to the benefit of mankind that SCP-9125 remains uncontained: were it not to inform the character of the human mind, the rate of extremely dangerous and overtly anomalous behaviors regularly perpetrated by mankind would immediately increase manifold. The civilian population knows not of SCP-9125 and presumes its effects to be the innate product of human nature. As such, an active attempt to suppress the object's anomalous influence is neither necessary nor possible.[[footnote]]//**Conscientia:**// Containment and knowledge suppression are impossible or inadvisable because the object, as understood by the civilian population, constitutes part of consensus normal reality.[[/footnote]] Ensuring the continued influence of SCP-9125 is an Alpha Level containment priority. **Description:** SCP-9125 is the root of human reason. Specifically, SCP-9125 is the event, phenomenon, or entity which installed the standard gnostic (i.e. rational) framework as the default epistemic framework for human logic[[footnote]]See also "positive" and "Apollonian" noetic polarity. An exemplary application of the gnostic framework of logic is mathematics, where the addition of one number //a// to another number //b// will always produce the same number //c//.[[/footnote]], displacing the //agnostic// frameworks which predominated intermittently at various points in deep human and protohuman prehistory. Such primeval systems of (il)logic are poorly understood. Similarly obscure to our knowledge is their period of dominance as mankind's primary frameworks for epistemic processing, except for the fact that the onset of SCP-9125 brought this epoch to an end in the overwhelming majority of settled agricultural societies. SCP-9125 is believed to be reducible to a single event which transpired in the 77th or 76th millennium BCE, however its noetic onset was far more gradual and took effect at different times in different cultures and geographic regions. SCP-9125’s influence is solidified in individual humans primarily through the gradual calcification of the pineal gland (//epiphysis cerebri//) with age. This process ensures the //epiphysis cerebri// forms a lasting connection with the semiosphere, restraining the brain's possible range of information intake to the signs therein and so establishing a baseline framework for extracting empirically-understood truth from phenomenal experience. Any global downturn in the rate of pineal gland calcification is considered the possible beginning of a ⌘K-Class "End of Reason" Scenario[[footnote]]This is because the polarity of semiotic conceptualization is the usual determinant of the polarity of noetic conceptualization. If any breakdown were to occur in the subconscious semiotic mechanism of concept recognition, a cascade effect would ensue in which the conscious noetic processes dependent upon it, such as the cognitive faculties for "logic" and "reasoning", would also be annihilated in their current form.[[/footnote]]. No source currently known to the Foundation indicates the fashion in which SCP-9125 came to exist, and only the sparsest archaeological evidence may tell what human existence resembled prior to it. All religious and cultural practices associated with the agnostic mode of thought are considered lost, and further inquiry into such practices is discouraged on the grounds that it may lead to the contamination of the present by primeval cognitive anomalies. As of 14 April 2020, the Semiotics Division has closed all further inquiry into SCP-9125 and shifted resources toward preventative measures for a possible ⌘K-Class event. A preserved specimen of SCP-9126.

Special Containment Procedures: A single instance of SCP-9126 is to be contained in a glass insect terrarium located inside a standard animal containment chamber at Site-66 and provided with sustenance appropriate for its species.

Only one researcher is to be assigned to the anomaly at any given time. This researcher is to maintain and regularly (at least once per day) check a detailed list of ideas they personally associate with the anomaly, each of which must contain references to other concepts. Should the researcher identify the object with a concept not pertaining to the anomalous, they are to immediately report for reassignment. When an entry in the list no longer appears sensical, the researcher must immediately use the associated references to reconstruct the idea. They must then terminate all but one instance of SCP-9126 in the containment chamber.

Reconstructed ideas are to be immediately uploaded to the SCiPNet database and disseminated to all personnel who are known to have previously worked with them, or who report confusion about suddenly forgetting an idea they were previously familiar with.

In the event that an idea known outside anomalous organizations is erased, a containment breach is to be declared. The presiding Site Director and senior staff must be immediately informed of the nature of the anomaly in order to coordinate a response.

When the assigned researcher is reassigned from SCP-9126, they are to be administered Class-C amnestics in order to remove all memory of it.

Description: SCP-9126 is an anomalous subspecies of the ichneumon wasp Podogaster Cactorum. SCP-9126 instances appear identical to their non-anomalous counterparts, and behave mostly identically as well.

SCP-9126 instances' anomalous properties become apparent in their reproductive cycle. All instances are female, and they do not mate or lay eggs. Instead, once an instance reaches sexual maturity it will land and go through the motions of stinging and ovipositing in prey, despite no prey being present. It will die soon after. 10 to 15 days after this occurs, a small number1 of new SCP-9126 instances will crawl out of apparently-empty space near the instance that initiated the event.

When this occurs, a single idea will be erased from collective understanding. All humans2 will no longer be able to name or explain the idea, although those familiar with it may be able to reference it nonspecifically. All written or otherwise recorded namings or explanations of the idea will remain unmodified, but anyone accessing them will not be able to comprehend them. Testing indicates that the ideas targeted by the anomaly are consistently those that observers closely associate with it. Affected ideas can be reconstructed given information connected to them. Anyone who reconstructs an erased idea or learns it via a reconstructed source can understand it as normal.

SCP-9126 was discovered in [REDACTED], Brazil, after a Foundation webcrawler detected an unusual missing persons case filed in the city. All persons that claimed to know the missing individual were unable to produce their name, or any other identifying information. A vacant apartment whose tenant was similarly unidentifiable was found by investigating field agents. 22 living instances of SCP-9126 were found in a terrarium in the apartment, as well as at least 40 deceased instances. Fragmented remains of further deceased instances were found in a nearby garbage bin. SCP-9126 is believed to have been created by the missing person that previously inhabited the apartment, an unidentified anartist designated PoI-9126-1.

Addendum: A notebook, presumably belonging to PoI-9126-1, was recovered along with the initial instances of SCP-9126. Several of the pages were entirely covered in ink. The legible portions are included below, although some words were blotted out.

- Close

Entry #1:
New project, new notebook!
████ wasn't my finest work, but I've got a real humdinger of an idea this time. An ontological parasite is a concept that needs to be attached to another concept to exist. Were you to extrapolate that to other forms of symbiosis, you might imagine an "ontological parasitoid". Not just that, though. There could be a whole host of what I'll call "█████".

Entry #2:
The theory should be simple. If a mundane parasitoid is brought to ████ quickly enough, with the right ████, it could develop a taste for concepts, so to speak. Something like this'll really put me on the map with █████.

Entry #3:
Setting to work on it. I can feel the ███ already.

Entry #5:
It's done, I think. Now to wait.

Entry #7:
It finally did something!
Unfortunately, it seems I erred in my definition of "concept". I intended it to parasitize objects at a conceptual level, but nothing disappeared. What did happen is I forgot everything about my last work. New wasps appeared, too. I'll have to cull them regularly.
This isn't what I wanted, but I'll still talk to █████. Maybe he'll still be impressed? I just hope he's not sick of me yet.

Entry #8:
Called █████. Explained the project. He actually sounded excited about something for once. I'll find a way to show it off to him ASAP.

Entry #10:
I forgot J K E him. His phone number, his address, his name, his face. All meaningless.
I'm killing them before they can take anything else.

Entry #11:
They're dead, but their eggs aren't. I'll have to kill the new ones too. Just hoping they take small things. Maybe I can ████?

Entry #13:
I could've destroyed the eggs with t a
But that's gone too.
How many are left?

Entry #16:
My old notes don't make sense anymore. I'll survive this, but my work won't.

Entry #17:
I don't want to look back anymore. I've blacked out what I lost.

A man with a familiar face came to my door. He knew my name.
The first thing he asked was:
"Who am I?"

Who am I?


PoI-9126-1 has not been found. The man mentioned in the notebook, designated PoI-9126-2, is also unaccounted for. Locating and apprehending these two persons is to be a top priority, assuming they remain alive and aware of SCP-9126's existence.
Footnotes
1. The highest recorded from a single event is 14.
2. Testing on sapient nonhumans is pending approval.

[[/div]] [[/div]] **Special Containment Procedures:** A single instance of SCP-9126 is to be contained in a glass insect terrarium located inside a standard animal containment chamber at Site-66 and provided with sustenance appropriate for its species. Only one researcher is to be assigned to the anomaly at any given time. This researcher is to maintain and regularly (at least once per day) check a detailed list of ideas they personally associate with the anomaly, each of which must contain references to other concepts. Should the researcher identify the object with a concept not pertaining to the anomalous, they are to immediately report for reassignment. When an entry in the list no longer appears sensical, the researcher must immediately use the associated references to reconstruct the idea. They must then terminate all but one instance of SCP-9126 in the containment chamber. Reconstructed ideas are to be immediately uploaded to the SCiPNet database and disseminated to all personnel who are known to have previously worked with them, or who report confusion about suddenly forgetting an idea they were previously familiar with. In the event that an idea known outside anomalous organizations is erased, a containment breach is to be declared. The presiding Site Director and senior staff must be immediately informed of the nature of the anomaly in order to coordinate a response. When the assigned researcher is reassigned from SCP-9126, they are to be administered Class-C amnestics in order to remove all memory of it. **Description:** SCP-9126 is an anomalous subspecies of the ichneumon wasp //Podogaster Cactorum//. SCP-9126 instances appear identical to their non-anomalous counterparts, and behave mostly identically as well. SCP-9126 instances' anomalous properties become apparent in their reproductive cycle. All instances are female, and they do not mate or lay eggs. Instead, once an instance reaches sexual maturity it will land and go through the motions of stinging and ovipositing in prey, despite no prey being present. It will die soon after. 10 to 15 days after this occurs, a small number[[footnote]]The highest recorded from a single event is 14.[[/footnote]] of new SCP-9126 instances will crawl out of apparently-empty space near the instance that initiated the event. When this occurs, a single idea will be erased from collective understanding. All humans[[footnote]]Testing on sapient nonhumans is pending approval.[[/footnote]] will no longer be able to name or explain the idea, although those familiar with it may be able to reference it nonspecifically. All written or otherwise recorded namings or explanations of the idea will remain unmodified, but anyone accessing them will not be able to comprehend them. Testing indicates that the ideas targeted by the anomaly are consistently those that observers closely associate with it. Affected ideas can be reconstructed given information connected to them. Anyone who reconstructs an erased idea or learns it via a reconstructed source can understand it as normal. SCP-9126 was discovered in [REDACTED], Brazil, after a Foundation webcrawler detected an unusual missing persons case filed in the city. All persons that claimed to know the missing individual were unable to produce their name, or any other identifying information. A vacant apartment whose tenant was similarly unidentifiable was found by investigating field agents. 22 living instances of SCP-9126 were found in a terrarium in the apartment, as well as at least 40 deceased instances. Fragmented remains of further deceased instances were found in a nearby garbage bin. SCP-9126 is believed to have been created by the missing person that previously inhabited the apartment, an unidentified anartist designated PoI-9126-1. **Addendum:** A notebook, presumably belonging to PoI-9126-1, was recovered along with the initial instances of SCP-9126. Several of the pages were entirely covered in ink. The legible portions are included below, although some words were blotted out. [[collapsible show="+ Open" hide="- Close"]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #1: New project, new notebook! ████ wasn't my finest work, but I've got a real humdinger of an idea this time. An ontological parasite is a concept that needs to be attached to another concept to exist. Were you to extrapolate that to other forms of symbiosis, you might imagine an "ontological parasitoid". Not just that, though. There could be a whole host of what I'll call "█████". [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #2: The theory should be simple. If a mundane parasitoid is brought to ████ quickly enough, with the right ████, it could develop a taste for concepts, so to speak. Something like this'll really put me on the map with █████. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #3: Setting to work on it. I can feel the ███ already. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #5: It's done, I think. Now to wait. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #7: It finally did something! Unfortunately, it seems I erred in my definition of "concept". I intended it to parasitize objects at a conceptual level, but nothing disappeared. What //did// happen is I forgot everything about my last work. New wasps appeared, too. I'll have to cull them regularly. This isn't what I wanted, but I'll still talk to █████. Maybe he'll still be impressed? I just hope he's not sick of me yet. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #8: Called █████. Explained the project. He actually sounded excited about something for once. I'll find a way to show it off to him ASAP. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #10: I forgot --J-- --K-- --E-- him. His phone number, his address, his name, his face. All meaningless. I'm killing them before they can take anything else. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #11: They're dead, but their eggs aren't. I'll have to kill the new ones too. Just hoping they take small things. Maybe I can ████? [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #13: I could've destroyed the eggs with --t-- --a-- But that's gone too. How many are left? [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #16: My old notes don't make sense anymore. I'll survive this, but my work won't. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Entry #17: I don't want to look back anymore. I've blacked out what I lost. [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] A man with a familiar face came to my door. He knew my name. The first thing he asked was: "Who am I?" [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] Who am I? [[/div]] [[/collapsible]] PoI-9126-1 has not been found. The man mentioned in the notebook, designated PoI-9126-2, is also unaccounted for. Locating and apprehending these two persons is to be a top priority, assuming they remain alive and aware of SCP-9126's existence.
