Special Containment Procedures:

Note: Due to the scale and circumstances surrounding SCP-9130’s containment, SCP-9130’s Special Containment Procedures, as well as access to certain related files, are split between Site-103 and Site-130 respectively.


Site-103 Procedures:
Living specimens of SCP-9130-1 are to be contained within Anomalous Greenhouse C. Anomalous Greenhouse C is to be outfitted with 5 SRAs1 covering the whole area to lessen the effects of SCP-9130 on staff.

Each specimen's differing needs are to be met as closely as possible. In the event that a specimen of SCP-9130-1 dies, all resultant SCP-9130-A material is to be carefully collected and shipped to Site-130 for containment. Under no circumstances is any staff member of Site-103 to damage or alter any SCP-9130-A material during collection or transport.

Staff working with or around living SCP-9130-1 specimens must be rotated out every 2 weeks to reduce mental strain.

Satellites equipped with long-range Kant counters are to continuously monitor for potential SCP-9130 activity. (Footnote: due to the unreliability of Kant counters at long range, these satellites are tuned specifically and solely to detect SCP-9130 activity.) When SCP-9130 activity is confirmed, MTF Theta-4 “Gardeners” are to be sent to retrieve any SCP-9130-1 instances. If the SCP-9130-1 instance is small enough, enact protocol BONSAI upon return to Site-103. If the specimen is too large or too risky to safely transplant, the SCP-9130-1 instance is to be killed and 9130-A material collected. In special circumstances, a separate containment site may be constructed around individual 9130-1 instances.

In the case of the discovery or creation of any SCP-9130-2 instances, MTF Psi-7 “Home Improvement” is to capture or destroy the instance. If successfully captured, SCP-9130-2 instances are to be immediately transported to Site-130.

Site-130 Procedures:
SCP-9130-A material is to be stored in a cool and dry environment in Warehouse Building 304. Under approved testing, SCP-9130-A material may be tested on or worked with to facilitate the creation of SCP-9130-2 instances. All SCP-9130-2 instances are to be processed separately and assigned containment procedures if required. Otherwise, all SCP-9130-2 instances are to be stored in Warehouse Building 207.

Foundation webcrawlers are to investigate online woodworking and antiques communities for signs of SCP-9130-2 instances. If discovered, instances are to be tracked down and contained. In the case of a instance that is dangerous or containment is deemed infeasible, it is to be incinerated.

To: Researcher Rin Moor
From: Researcher Rin Moor
Subject: notes

Dear Myself…

I need somewhere to vent. A plastic fern. A fucking plastic fern. Years of study into anomalous flora, fighting through the mental strain of working with SCP-9130, making a breakthrough…. And my reward is being sent to the middle of the fucking desert. There is not a single living green thing here other than the single saddest cactus I've ever seen 30 meters away from my window. Site-130 is supposed to be one of the biggest Sites by pure number of anomalies. I guess it makes sense that it is simply a giant complex of offices and warehouses surrounded by miles and miles of dust, and the only thing I have to comfort me is a fucking plastic fern.

Ok, I’m calming down a bit now. Work here is just as important as the work the Foundation does all over the world. Apparently the senior researcher I'm now working under… Tubas? Apparently he lost his legs to doors?

At least here I can fully focus on my work with SCP-9130. It may be the only thing to focus on…

Description:

SCP-9130 is an effect that transforms members of the Coniferous and Deciduous2 groups of trees into SCP-9130-1 instances. 9130-1 instances have an increased metabolism and growth rate, which appear at first to be ectoentropic in nature, but actually drains from the surrounding reality for nutrition. SCP-9130-1 instances measurably have a lower Hume reading than baseline, indicating that they are acting as a constant reality sink. It is currently unknown how SCP-9130-1 instances convert reality to nutrition or otherwise store it, and research is being done into SCP-9130-1’s effect on surrounding reality. It has been recently discovered that the rate of a SCP-9130-1's reality sink is directly proportional to the volume of the instance, and as such protocol BONSAI was created to contain instances in the smallest state possible.

Instances of SCP-9130-1 increase levels of Pareidolia3 in humans in a 50 meter radius, with effect severity increasing with closer proximity to the instance. SRAs placed in this area stabilize the Hume levels, drastically decreasing the effect by providing a source of reality for the 9130-1 instances.

Due to the increased metabolisms of SCP-9130-1 instances, they are much more susceptible to negative environmental effects, which can cause the rapid deterioration of health, leading to death. When an instance of SCP-9130-1 dies, two things happen. First, the tree emits a Hume wave that is theorized to be responsible for the creation of new SCP-9130-1 instances. The secondary effect is the heavily decreased Hume level of the lumber material left behind compared to baseline reality. This material is designated SCP-9130-A.

Due to the inverse reality bending effects of SCP-9130-A material, any object constructed4 using it will gain some anomalous properties before stabilizing. These new anomalies are designated SCP-9130-2 instances, however some have required unique SCP designation. These properties have lead to the esoteric classification Embla.5

Addendum 9130.3, Interview Log 9130/2:

Interviewed: POI-9130-4

Interviewer: Researcher █████ G████6

Foreword: Original Context for interview lost on transfer from physical file to digital storage. Interview estimated to be conducted around March 1929.

<Begin Log>

Interviewer G: Can you tell me again what you saw?

POI-9130-4: Really? I've been here for hours it feels like!

Interviewer G: Yes.

POI-9130-4: Well I told that other guy, the trees, they just starting hollering!

Interviewer G: Can you describe the noise?

POI-9130-4: N-no, as I said there weren't no noise, but their faces… they were all twisted, twisted up and hollering at me!

Interviewer G: Their… faces.

POI-9130-4: Thats what I said! I noticed it about 10 minutes in my walk, faces on, well everything! The trunks, the branches, hell even the leaves. All of 'em staring at me. Like they wished me death.

Interviewer G: What happened then?

POI-9130-4: Well I ran! I'm not normally one for all that paranormal ghosts 'nd shit. But, those faces. I just wanted to get out of there.

Interviewer G: And did the faces follow you?

POI-9130-4: I didn't look back much, but uh, if they did it wasn't for long, as I got away I saw less of 'em, and they are cleared out by the time I got back to the clearing.

Interviewer G: Okay, that is all I need from you for now.

<End Log>

Addendum 9130.7, Incident Report SCP-9130-A7:

On 9/28/2025, a record breaking SCP-9130-1 instance was detected in Sequoia National Park. Due to its immense size, the reality consuming effect of this instance threatened local reality, so a SRA was approved to be installed on site. The SRA was installed on 10/3/2025.

The following events took place on 10/3/2025 starting at 7:41:12

[BEGIN LOG]

3 members of MTF Theta-4 "Gardeners"9 finish hauling the SRA off the back of a flatbed truck and begin to connect it up to a generator. They are standing 30 meters away from the 9130-1 instance due to the severity of its effects.

Agent Taroko: Man, I'm so sick of seeing these faces all the time. Can't wait to get this thing up and running.

Agent Ernst detaches a large wire from the generator and begins to pull it over to the SRA

Agent Ernst: You can say that about 3 more times. How's the connection point?

Agent Strachey: Almost there… with the faces appearing all over the wires here its hard to tell what is what.

Agent Taroko moves to the other side of the SRA, pulling up a control panel.

Agent Strachey finishes opening up the connection panel on the SRA, and stands back so Worker 2 can insert the power cable.

Agent Ernst: Ok, all systems go.

Agent Taroko: Booting up the SRA… Strachey, we got a Kant counter? Given the size of this one, I think it's worth keeping an eye on the Hume levels for a bit.

Agent Strachey: Gotcha.

Agent Strachey heads over the the flatbed truck and begins rummaging around. As they do this, the SRA whirs to life.

Agent Ernst: (sigh) I am ready for this week to be done-

Agent Ernst is interrupted by a series of screeching metal noises coming from inside the SRA, raising in intensity as the machine begins to shake.

Out of view of the workers, the instance of SCP-9130-1 rumbles, as its needles and branches start to rapidly grow.

Agent Taroko: That cannot be good. Turning the SRA off now.

Agent Strachey: Looks like Hume levels are raising at least. Wait no, they're lower- they're moving up and down erratically!

The instance of SCP-9130-1 begins to show signs of cracking and stress along its main trunk as its needles grow and fall off in droves, piling on the surrounding ground.

Agent Taroko furiously types at her control panel.

Agent Taroko: It's not turning off!

Agent Ernst: I'm noticing an irregularity over at the tree as well. We need to call this in immediately.

An incredibly loud creaking sound emanates out from the SCP-9130-1 instance, sending birds flying. The SCP-9130-1 instance is noticeably leaning towards the direction of the SRA work site.

Agent Strachey drops their Kant detector and begins to work at the cord powering the SRA, attempting to forcefully disconnect it.

Agent Taroko: Uh. UH. I think we need to clear, NOW.

A deafening boom can be heard as the SCP-9130-1 instance cracks, falling with irregular speed towards the SRA. Upon impact, an explosion occurs, knocking out connection.

[END LOG]

After incident 9130-A7, the resultant 9130-A material was collected. Agent Ernst survived with serious injuries. Agents Taroko and Strachey died in the initial explosion. The tree falling and subsequent explosion was blamed on a freak lightning strike.

Addendum 9130.9, Report on Potential Multiversal Cause of SCP-9130 and Suggestions for Containment Adjustments:

Report on Potential Multiversal Cause of SCP-9130 and Suggestions for Containment Adjustments

By Researcher Rin Moor & Senior Researcher Derek Tubas

Abstract
A direct correlation between the amount of SRA's employed by the Foundation and number of SCP-9130-1 instances has been discovered. After doing research into incident 9130-A7, our team firmly believes that 9130-1 instances siphon reality from our universe into a "Dead" universe from which we draw reality from in turn. Due to the recent increase in using SRAs for the containment of SCP-9130 and other SCPs, the near exponential increase in SCP-9130-1 instances can be explained.

This paper will go into the details of our argument and further posit a method of deciphering which universe SCP-9130-1 may come from so that our SRAs can stop siphoning from their reality, as well as a means to establish communication.

…

…as such it is proposed that SCP-9130-A material be used in the creation of any potential communication device, as recommended by the Department of Multiversal Affairs. The contents of the message are currently being worked on by a joint team of linguists and arborists in Site-103. If this report is approved, said message will be sent to universe 9130 simultaneously with the rewiring of any SRAs siphoning from universe 9130.

…

Request Approved.

Dear Myself,

Well. I am back at Site-103. The reunion was great, but I’m a bit overwhelmed at all the increased attention from the paper. I visited the SCP-9130 greenhouse again and the effect of the Pareidolia seems to have… loosened. I always saw the faces as screaming and in anguish. But now? They seem almost… relieved.

You know? I don’t think I’d turn down another research assignment to Site-130.

9. Due to the scale of SCP-9130's containment, there are divisions of MTF Theta-4 specially trained in the deployment of SRA technologies
10. includes SRA-like technologies otherwise used for the containment of objects by the foundation

Anomalous Greenhouse C is to be outfitted with 5 SRAs[[footnote]]Scranton Reality Anchor. Siphons reality from "dead" universes to stabilize local reality.[[/footnote]] covering the whole area to lessen the effects of SCP-9130 on staff. Each specimen's differing needs are to be met as closely as possible. In the event that a specimen of SCP-9130-1 dies, all resultant SCP-9130-A material is to be carefully collected and shipped to Site-130 for containment. Under no circumstances is any staff member of Site-103 to damage or alter any SCP-9130-A material during collection or transport. Staff working with or around living SCP-9130-1 specimens must be rotated out every 2 weeks to reduce mental strain. Satellites equipped with long-range Kant counters are to continuously monitor for potential SCP-9130 activity. (Footnote: due to the unreliability of Kant counters at long range, these satellites are tuned specifically and solely to detect SCP-9130 activity.) When SCP-9130 activity is confirmed, MTF Theta-4 “Gardeners” are to be sent to retrieve any SCP-9130-1 instances. If the SCP-9130-1 instance is small enough, enact protocol BONSAI upon return to Site-103. If the specimen is too large or too risky to safely transplant, the SCP-9130-1 instance is to be killed and 9130-A material collected. In special circumstances, a separate containment site may be constructed around individual 9130-1 instances. In the case of the discovery or creation of any SCP-9130-2 instances, MTF Psi-7 “Home Improvement” is to capture or destroy the instance. If successfully captured, SCP-9130-2 instances are to be immediately transported to Site-130. ----- **Site-130 Procedures:** SCP-9130-A material is to be stored in a cool and dry environment in Warehouse Building 304. Under approved testing, SCP-9130-A material may be tested on or worked with to facilitate the creation of SCP-9130-2 instances. All SCP-9130-2 instances are to be processed separately and assigned containment procedures if required. Otherwise, all SCP-9130-2 instances are to be stored in Warehouse Building 207. Foundation webcrawlers are to investigate online woodworking and antiques communities for signs of SCP-9130-2 instances. If discovered, instances are to be tracked down and contained. In the case of a instance that is dangerous or containment is deemed infeasible, it is to be incinerated. ----- [[div class="email-example"]] [[=]] [[<]] [[div class="email"]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **To:** Researcher Rin Moor **From:** Researcher Rin Moor **Subject:** notes [[/div]] ------ Dear Myself…     I need somewhere to vent. A plastic fern. A fucking plastic fern. Years of study into anomalous flora, fighting through the mental strain of working with SCP-9130, making a breakthrough…. And my reward is being sent to the middle of the fucking desert. There is not a single living green thing here other than the single saddest cactus I've ever seen 30 meters away from my window. Site-130 is supposed to be one of the biggest Sites by pure number of anomalies. I guess it makes sense that it is simply a giant complex of offices and warehouses surrounded by miles and miles of dust, and the only thing I have to comfort me is a fucking plastic fern. Ok, I’m calming down a bit now. Work here is just as important as the work the Foundation does all over the world. Apparently the senior researcher I'm now working under… Tubas? Apparently he lost his legs to [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-8839 doors]? At least here I can fully focus on my work with SCP-9130. It may be the only thing to focus on… [[/div]] [[/<]] [[/=]] [[/div]] ----- **Description:** SCP-9130 is an effect that transforms members of the Coniferous and Deciduous[[footnote]]Conifer trees are a subset of families under the Clade //Gymnospermae//, while Deciduous trees are under the Clade //Angiospermae//[[/footnote]] groups of trees into SCP-9130-1 instances. 9130-1 instances have an increased metabolism and growth rate, which appear at first to be ectoentropic in nature, but actually drains from the surrounding reality for nutrition. SCP-9130-1 instances measurably have a lower Hume reading than baseline, indicating that they are acting as a constant reality sink. It is currently unknown how SCP-9130-1 instances convert reality to nutrition or otherwise store it, and research is being done into SCP-9130-1’s effect on surrounding reality. It has been recently discovered that the rate of a SCP-9130-1's reality sink is directly proportional to the volume of the instance, and as such protocol BONSAI was created to contain instances in the smallest state possible. Instances of SCP-9130-1 increase levels of Pareidolia[[footnote]]Pareidolia is the human tendency to see patterns, especially faces in objects.[[/footnote]] in humans in a 50 meter radius, with effect severity increasing with closer proximity to the instance. SRAs placed in this area stabilize the Hume levels, drastically decreasing the effect by providing a source of reality for the 9130-1 instances. Due to the increased metabolisms of SCP-9130-1 instances, they are much more susceptible to negative environmental effects, which can cause the rapid deterioration of health, leading to death. When an instance of SCP-9130-1 dies, two things happen. First, the tree emits a Hume wave that is theorized to be responsible for the creation of new SCP-9130-1 instances. The secondary effect is the heavily decreased Hume level of the lumber material left behind compared to baseline reality. This material is designated SCP-9130-A. Due to the inverse reality bending effects of SCP-9130-A material, any object constructed[[footnote]]Objects fully automated do not gain anomalous traits. Recent theory suggests that some level of "Intent" during the construction of the object is required[[/footnote]] using it will gain some anomalous properties before stabilizing. These new anomalies are designated SCP-9130-2 instances, however some have required unique SCP designation. THE DAMN MAP. I should not have printed it out. I have stared so long at that paper, trying to make any sense of the patterns. Heck, I'm going to give //myself// pareidolia at this point. At one point I even mapped the chemical structure of cis-3-hexenol onto it. The fact that cis-3-hexenol is one of the main "alarm" systems for plants is definitely intriguing, and I feel like there should be some connection, but in what world would the smell of fresh cut grass be made by that many trees over that long of a period of time. Well its in my notes anyway. Maybe I should take Tubas up on his offer to assist with the 9130-A studies. I really can't keep isolating forever. [[/div]] [[/<]] [[/=]] [[/div]] **Addendum 6, Further Testing on SCP-9130-A Material:** > Forward: For the upcoming tests, researchers Moor and Tubas gave subjects SCP-9130-A material and ample tools. D-Class subjects were directed to craft something of their own volition. Before they started, they wrote down the goal of the object that they would make on a piece of paper which would be used for comparison later. Upon skin contact, the structure grew rapidly, twisting and turning at right angles around D-053493's arm. D-053493 screamed and tried to shake it off, but within 10 seconds the object had spread fully around D-053493, mangling him beyond recognizability. The growth slowed after D-053493 was swallowed, stabilizing in the shape of a tree with twisted branches. D-053493 could not be extracted and passed away. I am surprised you contacted me first, your stay at 130 must be going a lot better than you made it out to be as you were leaving 103. Wish you could come back soon though. SCP-9130 sure is trouble for an anomaly we've been containing for nearly a century. The constant discovery every few months of new 9130-1 instances all over the globe is really stretching resources thin over here, and while the BONSAI protocol is definitely helping, I really feel like we are on the edge. Hope the desert is treating you well,                                                         Isabella [[/div]] [[/<]] [[/=]] [[/div]] **Addendum 9130.7, Incident Report SCP-9130-A7:** On 9/28/2025, a record breaking SCP-9130-1 instance was detected in Sequoia National Park. Due to its immense size, the reality consuming effect of this instance threatened local reality, so a SRA was approved to be installed on site. The SRA was installed on 10/3/2025. [[div class="blockquote"]] **{{The following events took place on 10/3/2025 starting at 7:41:12}}** ----- [BEGIN LOG] //3 members of MTF Theta-4 "Gardeners"[[footnote]]Due to the scale of SCP-9130's containment, there are divisions of MTF Theta-4 specially trained in the deployment of SRA technologies[[/footnote]] finish hauling the SRA off the back of a flatbed truck and begin to connect it up to a generator. They are standing 30 meters away from the 9130-1 instance due to the severity of its effects.// **Agent Taroko:** Man, I'm so sick of seeing these faces all the time. Can't wait to get this thing up and running. //Agent Ernst detaches a large wire from the generator and begins to pull it over to the SRA// **Agent Ernst:** You can say that about 3 more times. How's the connection point? **Agent Strachey:** Almost there... with the faces appearing all over the wires here its hard to tell what is what. //Agent Taroko moves to the other side of the SRA, pulling up a control panel.// //Agent Strachey finishes opening up the connection panel on the SRA, and stands back so Worker 2 can insert the power cable.// **Agent Ernst:** Ok, all systems go. **Agent Taroko:** Booting up the SRA... Strachey, we got a Kant counter? Given the size of this one, I think it's worth keeping an eye on the Hume levels for a bit. **Agent Strachey:** Gotcha. //Agent Strachey heads over the the flatbed truck and begins rummaging around. As they do this, the SRA whirs to life.// **Agent Ernst:** //(sigh)// I am ready for this week to be done- //Agent Ernst is interrupted by a series of screeching metal noises coming from inside the SRA, raising in intensity as the machine begins to shake.// //Out of view of the workers, the instance of SCP-9130-1 rumbles, as its needles and branches start to rapidly grow.// **Agent Taroko:** That cannot be good. Turning the SRA off now. **Agent Strachey:** Looks like Hume levels are raising at least. Wait no, they're lower- they're moving up and down erratically! //The instance of SCP-9130-1 begins to show signs of cracking and stress along its main trunk as its needles grow and fall off in droves, piling on the surrounding ground.// //Agent Taroko furiously types at her control panel.// **Agent Taroko:** It's not turning off! **Agent Ernst:** I'm noticing an irregularity over at the tree as well. We need to call this in immediately. //An incredibly loud creaking sound emanates out from the SCP-9130-1 instance, sending birds flying. The SCP-9130-1 instance is noticeably leaning towards the direction of the SRA work site.// //Agent Strachey drops their Kant detector and begins to work at the cord powering the SRA, attempting to forcefully disconnect it.// **Agent Taroko:** Uh. UH. I think we need to clear, NOW. //A deafening boom can be heard as the SCP-9130-1 instance cracks, falling with irregular speed towards the SRA. Upon impact, an explosion occurs, knocking out connection.// [END LOG] ---- After incident 9130-A7, the resultant 9130-A material was collected. Agent Ernst survived with serious injuries. Agents Taroko and Strachey died in the initial explosion. The tree falling and subsequent explosion was blamed on a freak lightning strike. [[/div]] [[div class="email-example"]] [[=]] ------ [[<]] [[div class="email"]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **To:** Researcher Rin Moor **From:** Senior Researcher Derek Tubas **Subject:** File Access [[/div]] ------ Sure, I can send you those. Files on SRAs, huh? I guess everyone is worried after incident 9130-A7. Hopefully this will help with your research! ~ Tubas [[/div]] [[/<]] [[/=]] [[/div]] **Addendum 9130.8, Foundation Use of SRA Technology Over Time** [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block name=http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/local--files/coccolithophor-pareidolia/sragraph.png| caption=Foundation Use of SRA Technology Over Time[[footnote]]includes SRA-like technologies otherwise used for the containment of objects by the foundation [[/footnote]]| align=center | width=100% ]] [[div class="email-example"]] [[=]] ------ [[<]] [[div class="email"]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **To:** Researcher Rin Moor **From:** Researcher Rin Moor **Subject:** notes [[/div]] ------ Dear Myself,            I keep thinking about Tubas' theory of Intent. What is the intent of this? Why reality sinks? Why did it react so violently to that specific SRA? Wait [[/div]] [[/<]] [[/=]] [[/div]] [[div class="email-example"]] [[=]] [[<]] [[div class="email"]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **To:** Researcher Rin Moor **From:** Senior Researcher Derek Tubas **Subject:** Potential Breakthrough [[/div]] ------ oh. oh god. wait wait if this is correct then there is probably some intelligence behind it right? one does not simply end up with specific targeting reality siphoning technology out of nowhere! on my way over right now. ~ Tubas [[/div]] [[/<]] [[/=]] [[/div]] **Addendum 9130.9, Report on Potential Multiversal Cause of SCP-9130 and Suggestions for Containment Adjustments:** [[div class="blockquote"]] = [[size larger]]**Report on Potential Multiversal Cause of SCP-9130 and Suggestions for Containment Adjustments**[[/size]] = **By Researcher Rin Moor & Senior Researcher Derek Tubas** **Abstract** A direct correlation between the amount of SRA's employed by the Foundation and number of SCP-9130-1 instances has been discovered. After doing research into incident 9130-A7, our team firmly believes that 9130-1 instances siphon reality from our universe into a "Dead" universe from which we draw reality from in turn. Due to the recent increase in using SRAs for the containment of SCP-9130 and other SCPs, the near exponential increase in SCP-9130-1 instances can be explained. This paper will go into the details of our argument and further posit a method of deciphering which universe SCP-9130-1 may come from so that our SRAs can stop siphoning from their reality, as well as a means to establish communication. ... ...as such it is proposed that SCP-9130-A material be used in the creation of any potential communication device, as recommended by the Department of Multiversal Affairs. The contents of the message are currently being worked on by a joint team of linguists and arborists in Site-103. If this report is approved, said message will be sent to universe 9130 simultaneously with the rewiring of any SRAs siphoning from universe 9130. ... [[include :scp-wiki:component:responsive-tables-source |cell-end= --] ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:responsive-tables-source |cell-start= --] |cell-header=Designation ]] 9130-2-99999 [[include :scp-wiki:component:responsive-tables-source |cell-end= --] ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:responsive-tables-source |cell-start= --] |cell-header=Result ]] Upon typing on 9130-2-99999's keyboard, equivalent text will appear on the back of the box. When the box is touched to any plant matter, a series of smells and chemicals will be produced. One identified chemical is cis-3-hexenol. [[include :scp-wiki:component:responsive-tables-source |cell-end= --] ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:responsive-tables-source |row-end= --] ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:responsive-tables-source |responsive-table-end= --] ]] [[div class="email-example"]] [[=]] ------ [[<]] [[div class="email"]] [[div class="tofrom"]] **To:** Researcher Rin Moor **From:** Researcher Rin Moor **Subject:** notes [[/div]] ------ Dear Myself,     Well. I am back at Site-103. The reunion was great, but I’m a bit overwhelmed at all the increased attention from the paper. I visited the SCP-9130 greenhouse again and the effect of the Pareidolia seems to have… loosened. I always saw the faces as screaming and in anguish. But now? They seem almost… relieved.     You know? I don’t think I’d turn down another research assignment to Site-130. Item #: SCP-9138

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: The honoured dead are to be exhumed and disposed of in ritually unclean locations1 as available. Oracles, sibyls, mediums, and other classes of necromancer are to be amnesticised in order to maintain informational security.

Furthermore, Foundation front agencies are to promote deurbanisation and lower population density, as to minimise the impact of necrogenic emotional pollution on living human society.

Description: SCP-9138 is the newly dominant moral framework of the universe as of 25/06/1950. It selects sapient souls considered exceptional by their peers, distinguishing them primarily by their tomb decorations and grave-goods. Souls so recognised by their community are sorted into a variety of paradisiacal afterlives which reflect their actions while living. These afterlives embody SCP-9138-A’s ethical and aesthetic values, and are structured to reward and further perpetuate such behaviour.

SCP-9138-A are an alien species which is known to have constructed SCP-9138. Little else can be said about them, other than that they must possess enormous thaumatological capacity in order to have engineered a universal eschatological field. By making inferences from testimonies of heavenbound individuals, it has been deduced that SCP-9138-A greatly value physical and psychological closeness, selflessness, and effective child-rearing. As a result, SCP-9138 disproportionately selects altruistic individuals and prolific mothers. It is estimated SCP-9138 affects approximately 1.3% of the human dead, primarily of the lattermost demographic.

SCP-9138-B are the sympathetic and psychic impressions left by selected souls on the material world. These occur primarily around sites of interment, such as graves, holy rivers, and shrines. Particularly sensitive individuals around these areas can receive empathic imprints of the thoughts and sensations of these souls in their destinations. The location and nature of these impressions has been both the primary source of knowledge about SCP-9138 and the primary threat it presents to Normalcy.

Listed below are some examples of SCP-9138-B testimonies from attuned Foundation staff, attempting to describe their feelings as accurately as possible.

Source Individual Presumed Reason for Selection by SCP-9138 Subject Testimony
Dmitri Volkov Parish priest who provided spiritual comfort to his community during wartime. It’s nice not to worry about being alone. I was so scared for so long. They’re close.
Rosa Delgado Midwife who delivered ~2,000 babies in her rural community. Every one I lost stuck with me. They all live, up here. We are always full to bursting.
Margaret Adler Mother of nine children. Advocated for natural birth practices and homesteading. There's enough. There's more coming. (Notably, subject seemed to struggle to breathe as they spoke).
Yuki Tanaka Donated over 40 litres of blood during her lifetime. They’re so sweet. Better them than me.
Satya Ramakrishnan Spent large portions of her free time voluntarily providing charitable services to the local urban homeless population. Butterflies in my stomach. Butterflies in my heart. Butterflies in my lungs.

SCP-9138-B manifestations grow more intense as SCP-9138 continues to increase in scope. It is expected humans of median psionic sensitivity will become able to perceive them clearly around the year 2030.



ADDENDUM 17/02/2026: ASTRONOMICAL SURVEY

As a result of recent breakthroughs in esoteric astronomy, the Foundation has located the homeworld of SCP-9138-A. Preliminary observations are below:

+ LEVEL 4 EYES ONLY
- VERIFIED

SCP-9138-A are the intelligent denizens of Kepler-138c, a water-covered world some 219 lightyears from Earth. A species of pisciform obligate filial cannibals that spawn in broods of around 80,000, SCP-9138-A typically fed on native meiofauna. For most of their history, lack of sufficient prey and relatively heavy parasitism (the average historical SCP-9138-A instance was composed of only 40% parasites by mass, but could sustain little more) kept their numbers low. They coped with these conditions by placing great emphasis on the glory and pleasure of sacrificial parasitisation, and the holiness of maternal filicide.

However, on 14/06/1950, an anomalous technique was discovered by their priestly classes that allowed instances to filterfeed across alternate universes. This immediately flooded the ecological cycles of Kepler-138c with an enormous amount of biomass, which was mostly monopolised by SCP-9138-A. The vast number of new souls created thereby lent the species sufficient metaphysical weight to instantiate their ideal afterlives. They now saturate every body of water on the planet, and though density varies cyclically (often by orders of magnitude), never does it fall below 1 SCP-9138-A instance per cubic metre.

Footnotes
1. e.g. middens, industrial crematoria, or meatpacking plants

Listed below are some examples of SCP-9138-B testimonies from attuned Foundation staff, attempting to describe their feelings as accurately as possible. ||~ Source Individual ||~ Presumed Reason for Selection by SCP-9138 ||~ Subject Testimony|| || Dmitri Volkov || Parish priest who provided spiritual comfort to his community during wartime.|| {{It’s nice not to worry about being alone. I was so scared for so long. They’re close.}} || || Rosa Delgado || Midwife who delivered ~2,000 babies in her rural community. || {{Every one I lost stuck with me. They all live, up here. We are always full to bursting.}} || || Margaret Adler || Mother of nine children. Advocated for natural birth practices and homesteading. || {{There's enough. There's more coming.}} (Notably, subject seemed to struggle to breathe as they spoke). || || Yuki Tanaka || Donated over 40 litres of blood during her lifetime. || {{They’re so sweet. Better them than me.}} || || Satya Ramakrishnan || Spent large portions of her free time voluntarily providing charitable services to the local urban homeless population.|| {{Butterflies in my stomach. Butterflies in my heart. Butterflies in my lungs.}} || SCP-9138-B manifestations grow more intense as SCP-9138 continues to increase in scope. It is expected humans of median psionic sensitivity will become able to perceive them clearly around the year 2030. @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ @@ **ADDENDUM 17/02/2026: ASTRONOMICAL SURVEY** As a result of recent breakthroughs in esoteric astronomy, the Foundation has located the homeworld of SCP-9138-A. Preliminary observations are below: [[collapsible show="+ LEVEL 4 EYES ONLY" hide="- VERIFIED"]] SCP-9138-A are the intelligent denizens of Kepler-138c, a water-covered world some 219 lightyears from Earth. A species of pisciform obligate filial cannibals that spawn in broods of around 80,000, SCP-9138-A typically fed on native meiofauna. For most of their history, lack of sufficient prey and relatively heavy parasitism (the average historical SCP-9138-A instance was composed of only 40% parasites by mass, but could sustain little more) kept their numbers low. They coped with these conditions by placing great emphasis on the glory and pleasure of sacrificial parasitisation, and the holiness of maternal filicide. However, on 14/06/1950, an anomalous technique was discovered by their priestly classes that allowed instances to filterfeed across alternate universes. This immediately flooded the ecological cycles of Kepler-138c with an enormous amount of biomass, which was mostly monopolised by SCP-9138-A. The vast number of new souls created thereby lent the species sufficient metaphysical weight to instantiate their ideal afterlives. They now saturate every body of water on the planet, and though density varies cyclically (often by orders of magnitude), never does it fall below 1 SCP-9138-A instance per cubic metre. Special Containment Procedures

Use of SCP-9140 for its intended purpose is strictly prohibited by Ethics Committee mandate1. All component parts are to be stored in a secure containment locker at Site-76, and may only be removed for archeological study.

Moving forward, a modified version of the Containment Onion2 is to be applied to SCP-9140-A instances:

➣ If they do not currently exist, do not create them.
➣ If they currently exist, do not inform them of their status.
➣ If they are aware of their status, Conversion Protocol RETROVERT is to be enacted prior to non-essential interaction.
➣ If they have been subject to Conversion, weekly examination by medical staff is required to identify and treat adverse health effects.

Description

SCP-9140 is a set of Daevite ritual objects, referred to in translated primary sources as the Imperial Bloodsieve. Its principal component (designated SCP-9140-1) is a carved stone statue, measuring 12.5cm in height. The statue resembles the figure of a pregnant woman, with glyphs carved around its circumference. Above the carvings, there is a groove carved into the stone, measuring 0.7cm in width and 0.5cm in depth.


An artistic representation of SCP-9140.

In addition to the main statue, SCP-9140 also refers to six smaller stone statues (designated SCP-9140-2-1 through SCP-9140-2-6). These smaller statues, each measuring 7.7cm in height, resemble young children. Each is carved with a distinct ritual glyph and a groove of similar dimensions and placement to the one found on SCP-9140-1. These artifacts are intended to be used in conjunction; each must be tied together in a prescribed order using 100% natural twine prior to use.

SCP-9140 was used by Daevite matriarchs and priestesses in the performance of a thaumaturgical fertility ritual, with most documented cases taking place in southern Siberia between 200 BC and 300 AD. During the ritual, SCP-9140 is tied around the waist of a newly pregnant human (Homo sapiens), after which, three female practitioners of thaumaturgy3 perform a rite involving dance and incantation. It ends with each practitioner drawing a sigil on the subject's stomach in blood. If the rite is performed correctly, the pregnant subject will give birth to a child of the subspecies Homo sapiens daeva. Individuals born following the ritual's successful execution are designated as instances of SCP-9140-A.

UPDATE (October 1995): The Foundation Species of Interest (SoI) database now includes H. sapiens daeva (Daevite) under the designation SoI-140:

Department of Xenobiology - SoI Database Change



As of October 18th, 1995, the Daevite subspecies has been added as an entry to the SCP Foundation Species of Interest Database. Further study of SCP-9140-A-0 is in progress.
Scientific Nomenclature: Homo sapiens daeva HTE Classification: TYPE BLUE (Gifted)

Excerpts from the SoI-140 bulletin have been included at relevant points within this file.

For more information, please contact your Department of Xenobiology Liaison.


Recovery

On 11-26-1991, SCP-9140 was recovered from GRU-P Liquidated Site VIII4, located 75 kilometers outside of Pokrovskoye, Russia; a small village in southern Siberia. The object was discovered by Foundation agents associated with Operation: Curtain Cascade5 in a sector of the site designated for the storage of anomalies not being tested or utilized. Within its locker, agents also located a file of relevant documents and a spool of jute twine.

After recovery, SCP-9140 was placed as one of the lowest priority objects obtained by O:CC. At the time, the existence of the Daevite subspecies was unconfirmed, and its legitimacy was doubted by researchers, informing their decision to shelve the anomaly.

Its associated files were catalogued, and the names of the H. sapiens daeva individuals born through the use of SCP-9140 were cross-checked with the Persons of Interest Database. The search yielded no results, as Junior Researcher ░░░░░░░░░ ░░░░░░░░ had not yet been scouted by the Foundation.

Confirmation of Anomalous Nature

On ░░-░░-1995, Junior Researcher ░░░░░░░░░ ░░░░░░░░, then stationed at Site-░░ was subjected to a DNA test, as it was suspected that an anomalous pathogen capable of gene editing had spread within the area. While the test did not confirm an infection, it did indicate significant genetic irregularities. After a more thorough investigation, it was determined on ░░-░░-1995 that Junior Researcher ░░░░░░░░ was a member of the previously unconfirmed subspecies, H. sapiens daeva.

SCP-9143.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9143

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: All pathways that lead to SCP-9143 must be closed off utilizing palisade fencing. Caution signage is to be posted along each pathway warning of toxic chemicals in the region. All staff stationed within SCP-9143's surveillance outpost are to identify themselves as a local cleanup crew working with city hall to restore the area for public usage after a chemical spill. Communication with Mayor Eastman is to be solely handled by Dr J. Andrews.

Surveillance cameras installed at each entrance as well as those placed within the vicinity of SCP-9143 are set to alert security staff of any captured motion. Individuals that attempt to enter the site must be interviewed and interrogated as to their personal feelings and relations to SCP-9143.

Due to SCP-9143's declining state and public perception believing it to merely be a hoax or local urban legend, no Amnestics are necessary for individuals having witnessed its effects.

Description: SCP-9143, also known as Lake Love, is a lake in Tennessee measured to be 6400m², located in the south-eastern region of the rural mining town "██████."

SCP-9143 produces auditory hallucinations intermittently of music incapable of being recorded using any known form of audio capturing. Conflicting reports given by detained individuals suggest that the type of music produced by SCP-9143 varies from each subject.

Examples of the music heard are as follows:

Classical Music, Alternative Rock, Jazz, and natural soundscapes harmonizing to create melodic symphonies.

At least forty-six individuals to date living in ██████ claim to have witnessed the anomaly. Sixteen have attempted to breach SCP-9143's perimeter multiple times. Public perception primarily views SCP-9143 and its effects to be that of a local urban legend. Between 1980 and 1991, local politicians began using SCP-9143 as a tourist attraction. The marketing scheme proved to be an effective economic boost holding positive influence throughout the town. Though SCP-9143 has not yet been proven to hold any physical effects on observers, those who have come in contact with SCP-9143 seem to all have formative experiences involving the landmark.

Whether or not this is the result of SCP-9143's anomalous effect is yet to be determined.

Discovery: Though first dismissed by the Foundation to be a local hoax in 1981, a renewed interest in SCP-9143 was found when a Facebook group (Lake Love Experiencers) was created in 2011 by local senior citizen 'Denise Grant.'

The group had garnered a dedicated following of town residents sharing their experiences with the landmark. Foundation webcrawlers monitoring the site picked up on a sudden uptick in the groups following, with many members openly sharing their experiences with SCP-9143's anomalous effect. Many of whom encouraging others to visit SCP-9143 and experience it for themselves. The group also called attention to SCP-9143's gradually weakening state, producing music at a far less frequent rate over the years.

Researcher J. Andrews was assigned to investigate the uptick in anomalous reports. After several nights of interviewing locals and stationing within SCP-9143's perimeter, it was officially classified as anomalous after the effects could not be explained away using any scientific reasoning.

+ Interview Log 9143-A-1
- Close

Interviewed: Lacia Evergreen

Interviewer: Dr J. Andrews

<Begin Log>

Dr J. Andrews: May you state your name and age for the record, please?

Lacia: Am I in trouble…?

Dr J. Andrews: We're just going to ask you some questions if that's alright.

Lacia: Um, for sure, yeah.

Dr J. Andrews: Name and age?

Lacia: Lacia Evergreen. I'm 24.

Dr J. Andrews: Alright Miss Evergreen. Or, is Lacia preferable?

Lacia: Lacia is fine, yeah…

Dr J. Andrews: So I'm told you were on your way to Lake Love when security found you, is that correct?

Lacia: I didn't notice the uh, signs. But I was on my way there, yes.

Dr J. Andrews: Could you please provide a verbal statement explaining why you were attempting to visit the Lake, Miss Lacia?

Lacia: Is this for like… The police?

Dr J. Andrews: As we've stated you're not in trouble today Miss Lacia. We're just looking for some clarification is all.

Lacia: Right… Um. I just haven't been to the lake in a long while, so I thought I'd stop by.

Dr J. Andrews: You've visited before then? When was the last time you'd visited Lake Love?

Lacia: It's been a few years… When I was Seventeen, I think.

Dr J. Andrews: And the purpose of the visit?

Lacia: Excuse me…?

Dr J. Andrews: When you last visited Lake Love, was it for any particular reason? Seeing a loved one, an exchange of finances, looking for lost-

Lacia: Um… No, it wasn't anything like that. It's silly, but… There's the town rumor about that place, and-

Dr J. Andrews: Love's Call?

Lacia: Yeah. I was curious. About whether or not it was real.

Dr J. Andrews: Did you come to any conclusions?

Lacia: I did.

Dr J. Andrews: And you were just visiting tonight, correct?

Lacia: Well, I was actually trying to look into the uh… Other rumor. People saying the music is going away. That it's not as easy to hear anymore.

Dr J. Andrews: Is that what you believe?

Lacia: No. I mean, I don't see why it would be… It's been a thing forever now. Since I was a kid, since my dad was a kid… Something as crazy as that wouldn't just up and disappear one day.

Dr J. Andrews: Did anything happen the last night you visited? Before you went to the lake?

Lacia: Why are you asking?

Dr J. Andrews: It's just for the record, Miss Lacia.

Lacia: Um… My… Family. There was a bit of a fight, I don't really remember. I was trying to clear my head.

Dr J. Andrews: Your parents. Are they still together?

Lacia: No. Not since I was… Seventeen.

Dr J. Andrews: I see. My apologies.

Lacia: It's been a long time, it's okay.

Dr J. Andrews: Alright then. Miss Lacia, that's all we needed. You're free to go.

Lacia: Do you think the cleanup will be finished soon…? With the lake…?

Dr J. Andrews: Soon enough. Good day Miss Lacia.

<End Log>

Closing Statement: Subject released without incident.

+ Interview Log 9143-A-2
- Close

Interviewed: Richard Stevens

Interviewer: Dr J. Andrews

<Begin Log>

Stevens: Can we get this the hell over with?

Dr J. Andrews: We're just going to ask you some questions, Richard.

Stevens: Like that'll do ya any fuckin' good.

Dr J. Andrews: So as you know, this is the thi-

Stevens: Third time you assholes grabbed me, I know.

Dr J. Andrews: Yes… And the previous two times you refused to take questions.

Stevens: I gave you all the answers, a perfect fucking score.

Dr J. Andrews: Well that is what we thought the first time, yes. Until we did our own private investigation and discovered you had been lying, very convincingly I might add. Which we brought up in your second detainment before asking you those very same questions again.

Stevens: Oh so you didn't like those ones either?

Dr J. Andrews: After conducting another investigation, we found that again you weren't being entirely truthful. Your name-

Stevens: Richard Stevens is my fucking name.

Dr J. Andrews: Yes, from what we found that is correct. But it's the only thing that was correct. So we're going to be asking you some questions again, and I'm going to ask once more that you answer truthfully. To your best possible capabilities. Or we'll be forced to report your continued trespassing to the local authorities.

Stevens: Fucking stupid.

Dr J. Andrews: Alright so, again. What is your name?

Stevens: Richard Stevens.

Dr J. Andrews: Age?

Stevens: 46.

Dr J. Andrews: Okay… And what was the purpose of todays trip to Lake Love?

Stevens: Screwing your mother.

Dr J. Andrews: You won't be getting another chance at this, Mr Stevens.

Stevens: And whats it the fuck to you anyway? To ANY of you? You fuckin *people.*

Dr J. Andrews: Mr Stevens-

Stevens: Everything was just fine until you all came along. Until you started poking around, with your fuckin' hazmat suits, and your fuckin' lab coats. It was every week that I used to go there.

[Stevens rises from his chair.]

Stevens: The one fuckin' thing I could count on in this miserable existence. The one thing my daughter and I got left to remember. To remember all the times we'd spent together listenin' to that fuckin' music. To remember meeting her mother back in high school and running off there just to get away from it all. And what do you do? Sit around and ask WHY? Why something, anything in this world, could possibly be good? And I'll tell you another thing-

Dr J. Andrews: I think we're done here Mr. Stevens.

Stevens: NO, we're done when I sa-

<End Log>

Closing Statement: Subject removed from the premises by local authorities. Legal fines dealt to discourage further trespassing.

+ Communications Log 9143-3-6
- Close

Incoming: Jonathan Eastman [Mayor of ██████]

Outgoing: Dr J. Andrews

<Begin Log>

Eastman: So you got it then, right? It's all good?

Dr J. Andrews: Unfortunately Mr. Eastman. no… It's not.

Eastman: Oh come the hell on…

Dr J. Andrews: We've looked at the situation from many, many different angles. Despite our best efforts, the chemical spill isn't going to be an overnight fix.

Eastman: That's what, the third time you've told me that? What the hell is it that coulda got dumped in that lake that's so awful, that nobody can even go near it!

Dr J. Andrews: Unfortunately it's classified.

Eastman: I know… God, I know.

Dr J. Andrews: Is that all Mr Eastman?

Eastman: Look I know you guys are trying your best out there, and I appreciate that. But please for the love of god can you guys hurry it up?

Dr J. Andrews: Is this about the upcoming election?
Eastman: It's about the town, for christ sake! Everythings going great, but-… People are leaving. And other people- tourists- They're not even stopping by anymore.

Dr J. Andrews: Do you believe our work with the lake is the reasoning behind this?
Eastman: I don't know WHAT I believe. All I know is the lake- It means a helluva lot to people. They don't talk about it, but things were rough here for a very long time. Everybody was shut in, wouldn't even say hello to you walking down the street. They could hardly buy a decent meal, let alone take care of their family. But the more people found out about that lake- Things just… Changed. For the better. God knows it changed things for me.

Dr J. Andrews: Are you afraid of things changing again?

Eastman: I uh… I just need you all to get your shit together. Can you do that?

Dr J. Andrews: We'll do our best.

<End Log>

+ Video Log 9143-B-3
- Close

Interviewed: Jake Reeds

Interviewer: H. Lionel

<Lionel activates body camera.>

H. Lionel: Alright I've got a few questions here I need to ask before I can let you go, is that alright sir?

Reeds: Yeah I'm good, I'm good.

H. Lionel: Alright, may I get your name and age please?

Reeds: Jake.

H. Lionel: Okay, last name and age?

Reeds: Oh I'm sorry man uh, Reeds. R-E-E-D-S. I'm twenty.

H. Lionel: And what're you doing out here so late at night Jake?

Reeds: Yeah I'm really sorry, I wanted to see the lake is all it was stupid.

H. Lionel: You wanted to see the lake?

Reeds: Yeah.

H. Lionel: Have you been to the lake before? Any time recent?

Reeds: No I haven't since I was a kid.

H. Lionel: Since you were a kid? Okay… What was it that led you to going out to the lake that day?

Reeds: I was bummed out over some stuff at school, getting bullied. My mom took me there and said it'd make me feel better.

H. Lionel: And is that why you're here tonight, you feeling bummed out?

Reeds: Yeah it's not good man.

H. Lionel: What's got you feeling down?

Reeds: Honestly dude… Everything at this point.

H. Lionel: Everything?

Reeds: Yeah. Stuffs been going good but like, you ever get the feeling you don't know how long it's gonna last? Like someone can just take it from you at any point and it's back to square one?

H. Lionel: Something in particular got you feeling that way?

Reeds: I mean the lakes part of it. Can't even go there anymore, apparently. Now I gotta just face my problems myself I guess.

H. Lionel: Well we've got folks working hard on cleaning up the place. It shouldn't be too long before you can come back around.

Reeds: Yeah but I wanna go now. While I still can. Before some fucked up shit happens for no reason at all.

H. Lionel: Is it that important to you?

Reeds: Of course it is…! When you're a kid man, everything feels like it's gonna last forever. And you take stupid shit for granted, and you don't even realize until it's gone and you've already screwed everything up! I just don't see the fucking point… It's bullshit. It's all just… Bullshit.

H. Lionel: Well let's just take a breath for a second here and relax for a second okay? I've got some people that're gonna come take care of you.

Reeds: Okay…

<End Log>

Closing Statement: Subject was examined by on-site psychiatrist and deemed safe for release.

+ Interview Log 9143-A-3
- Close

Interviewed: Denise Grant

Interviewer: Dr J. Andrews

<Begin Log>

Dr J. Andrews: Okay ma'am, I've got a list of questions I'm going to ask you before you're free to go. Is that alright?

Grant: Oh yes, please go ahead!

Dr J. Andrews: May we start with your name and age please?

Grant: I'm Denise, Denise Grant. I turn 76 this coming April.

Dr J. Andrews: That's a lovely name Mrs Grant. Could you tell me the reasoning behind your visit today?

Grant: Oh I was just hoping to hear the music just one last time before it's gone.

Dr J. Andrews: That old rumor about the lakes got your attention?

Grant: Rumor? Ha! Oh it's no rumor I promise you that. And another thing, neither is the rumor going around saying that the musics going away…

Dr J. Andrews: What makes you say that, Ms Grant?

Grant: Oh dear, we ALL lose the music that's in us sooner or later. Lord knows how much longer I got left to let it play myself!

Dr J. Andrews: Let's hope both our songs are still playing a long long time from now.

Grant: What's the next question, sweetie?

Dr J. Andrews: When was the last time you visited Lake Love?

Grant: The last time… Oh I couldn't tell you. I've been there so many times over the years it's all just a big mess in my old head.

Dr J. Andrews: Are there any notable instances? Anything important that prompted the visits?

Grant: Oh well, me and my husband John would go there for our honeymoons. He proposed to me a long, long time ago there. He got down on one knee, with the most handsome face you'd ever saw. And I remember just how happy I was when he asked me… "Denise, dear? In a world where nothing lasts forever, would you do me the honors of making sure our love is the one thing that does?" [Laughs]

Grant: I still remember the music too. It was the first time we'd heard it. Maybe the first time *anybody* heard it. To me, it sounded like the most beautiful set of strings I'd ever heard… But he always told me he heard horns, [Laughs]

<Andrews writes in notes>

Grant: The Music, It just picked us up, and swept us away. All we could think about was how *good* we felt. How all our troubles just melted away. As if for just a moment, there was SOMETHING in this world that would last forever.

<Ms Grant sniffles as she wipes away a tear>

Grant: He passed away, just a few winters ago. Kept me smiling the whole time, never wanted a frown on this face he told me. And I learned something in the weeks after.

Dr J. Andrews: What did you learn Mrs Grant?

Grant: Well… I learned that miracles don't last forever. Whether it's love, money, or people. No matter how good something is, it really does all go away in the end…

But… For however brief a miracle it is. That miracle can bring just enough peace into somebodys world, that just being there to see it was worth being alive. And though some miracles may come and go for us older folks, there'll always be another miracle that comes along to bring light into someone elses life. Weeks from now, or years from now.

The best we can do to honor those miracles, is by holding them near and dear to our hearts. Putting them in a special place in our memory called nostalgia, and letting them go when it's time. Even if it hurts, you can smile through the tears and love the beauty that comes with having gotten to know this life is filled with such amazing wonders.

Dr J. Andrews: Thank you, Ms Grant. That will be all.

<End Log>

Closing Statement: Subject released without incident.

>

Addendum: On 03/12/20██, Denise Grant passed away as result of congestive heart failure. There has since been expedited decrease in SCP-9143's activity. Currently it is projected that the anomalous effects may be rendered completely dormant within ten to twenty years.

SCP-9143's connection to the residents of ██████ is yet to be fully understood, if there is any connection at all. Further research is still underway.

SCP-9143.raw_source: [[include :scp-wiki:theme:black-highlighter-theme]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:midnight-rush]] [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] **Item #:** SCP-9143 **Object Class:** Safe **Special Containment Procedures:** All pathways that lead to SCP-9143 must be closed off utilizing palisade fencing. Caution signage is to be posted along each pathway warning of toxic chemicals in the region. All staff stationed within SCP-9143's surveillance outpost are to identify themselves as a local cleanup crew working with city hall to restore the area for public usage after a chemical spill. Communication with Mayor Eastman is to be solely handled by Dr J. Andrews. Surveillance cameras installed at each entrance as well as those placed within the vicinity of SCP-9143 are set to alert security staff of any captured motion. Individuals that attempt to enter the site must be interviewed and interrogated as to their personal feelings and relations to SCP-9143. Due to SCP-9143's declining state and public perception believing it to merely be a hoax or local urban legend, no Amnestics are necessary for individuals having witnessed its effects. **Description:** SCP-9143, also known as Lake Love, is a lake in Tennessee measured to be 6400m², located in the south-eastern region of the rural mining town "██████."   SCP-9143 produces auditory hallucinations intermittently of music incapable of being recorded using any known form of audio capturing. Conflicting reports given by detained individuals suggest that the type of music produced by SCP-9143 varies from each subject. Examples of the music heard are as follows: Classical Music, Alternative Rock, Jazz, and natural soundscapes harmonizing to create melodic symphonies. At least forty-six individuals to date living in ██████ claim to have witnessed the anomaly. Sixteen have attempted to breach SCP-9143's perimeter multiple times. Public perception primarily views SCP-9143 and its effects to be that of a local urban legend. Between 1980 and 1991, local politicians began using SCP-9143 as a tourist attraction. The marketing scheme proved to be an effective economic boost holding positive influence throughout the town. Though SCP-9143 has not yet been proven to hold any physical effects on observers, those who have come in contact with SCP-9143 seem to all have formative experiences involving the landmark. Whether or not this is the result of SCP-9143's anomalous effect is yet to be determined. **Discovery:** Though first dismissed by the Foundation to be a local hoax in 1981, a renewed interest in SCP-9143 was found when a Facebook group (Lake Love Experiencers) was created in 2011 by local senior citizen 'Denise Grant.' The group had garnered a dedicated following of town residents sharing their experiences with the landmark. Foundation webcrawlers monitoring the site picked up on a sudden uptick in the groups following, with many members openly sharing their experiences with SCP-9143's anomalous effect. Many of whom encouraging others to visit SCP-9143 and experience it for themselves. The group also called attention to SCP-9143's gradually weakening state, producing music at a far less frequent rate over the years. Researcher J. Andrews was assigned to investigate the uptick in anomalous reports. After several nights of interviewing locals and stationing within SCP-9143's perimeter, it was officially classified as anomalous after the effects could not be explained away using any scientific reasoning. Item #: SCP-9148

Object Class: Thaumiel

Level 1/9148

Confidential

Special Containment Procedures

SCP-9148.

When not in use, SCP-9148 shall be kept in High-Security Artifact Storage at Site-157.

The Overseer Council has delegated the power to authorize deployment of SCP-9148 to the ad hoc SCP-9148 Targeting Committee, consisting of Site-157 Director Miami Ventura, Department of Analytics Director Simon Pietrykau, and Overseer 5. All requests for use of SCP-9148 must be submitted to the Targeting Committee for review and approval. Denied requests may not be resubmitted for 30 days.

Description

SCP-9148 is a prototype paraweapon developed in the 1970s by the Soviet Union's Main Intelligence Directorate, Psychotronics Division (GRU-P) for use in assassinations. The device superficially resembles a pistol, but kills through the use of psychokinetic force, rather than projectiles.

The core of SCP-9148 is a cylinder of an unknown metal alloy, similar in composition to the "telekill" alloy developed by Prometheus Labs. This cylinder is encased in beryllium-bronze. Approximately one meter of copper wiring is tightly wound around the cylinder. The wiring connects the cylinder to the dehydrated frontal lobe of a rat brain. The entire assemblage is powered by a Soviet Type A343 battery.

When the trigger is depressed, the device emits a burst of telekinetic force with a range of 185 meters and a magnitude of 1.7 nanonewtons. This force is insufficient to cause immediate physical harm. Instead, SCP-9148 targets neural tissues to induce a protein misfold, creating a prion infection in the victim which resembles fatal familial insomnia. With few exceptions, victims of SCP-9148 die within a year.

While effective, SCP-9148 saw limited use by the Soviet Union, and no additional copies were manufactured. It is believed that the average time-to-kill was too long for the weapon's intended purpose; additionally, multiple attempts by various parties to replicate the weapon have uniformly failed, suggesting that its manufacturing process was too complex to allow for mass production.

In 1991, the KGB Division of Special Circumstances went rogue, absconding with large quantities of Soviet paraweaponry, SCP-9148 among them. The former Division of Special Circumstances used SCP-9148 to eliminate high-profile targets that posed a hindrance to their criminal operations, including Deputy Director Alex Paszek of the Joint Occult Venture of Europe and Russian State Duma Deputy Dmitri Antonovich Volkogonov.

SCP-9148 was recovered alongside several other pieces of paraweaponry during a joint GRU-P/Foundation raid in 1997. Three Mobile Task Force agents involved in the operation subsequently died from prion diseases believed to be the result of SCP-9148.

Targeting Committee Records — Notable Proposals

Upon initial containment, SCP-9148 was provisionally classified as Safe. However, in light of the utility offered by its ability to untraceably kill targets through seemingly natural causes, SCP-9148 was reclassified as a Thaumiel object and approved for use in Veil-support operations. Per Ethics Committee Recommendation 99-Foxglove, lethal deployments of Thaumiel objects must be approved by a committee of at least three L4 or higher personnel. The SCP-9148 Targeting Committee has been assembled for this purpose.

Attached are the records of the Targeting Committee regarding proposed deployments of SCP-9148. Only the most notable proposals are included.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 1999-06-01
Target: SCP-682
Reason: It's worth a shot.
Status: APPROVED

No observable effect. Target remains alive.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2001-10-10
Target: Bertram Rowles
Reason: Former Prometheus Labs researcher who has attempted to sell knowledge regarding eigenweapon operating principles.
Status: APPROVED

Target died in an unrelated vehicular collision two days after SCP-9148 deployment. Pentagram involvement is suspected but remains unconfirmed.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2003-11-08
Target: James Brown
Reason: Major American musician, singer, and record producer important in the development of soul and funk music, as well as [REDACTED] as a result of non-anomalous legal issues.
Status: APPROVED

Target expired nearly a full 3 years after deployment of SCP-9148, on December 25, 2006. Target kept up a grueling performance schedule despite development of fatal insomnia, which was covered up as diabetes and prostate cancer. Internal research suggests that, as a result of the strike, American popular music will continue to decline in melodic diversity for a period of over 15 years, as per proposed best case scenario.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2005-05-01
Target: Larry F. Walker
Reason: Target is a claims adjuster from Sudbury, Ontario, Canada, who is seemingly non-anomalous but has an aetheric signature consistent with a minor deific entity. Attempting containment or overt termination may trigger unrealized ontokinetic abilities, to the detriment of the Veil.
Status: APPROVED

Target expired 5 months after deployment of SCP-9148. Post-mortem aetheric signature of target is consistent with that of a baseline human. Target's 3 children are currently under long-term observation to monitor for potential anomalous properties.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2006-08-01
Target: Fidel Castro
Reason: Ongoing opposition to SCP-8352 containment.
Status: DENIED

Risk/reward calculus does not support SCP-9148 deployment. Target is aware of the Foundation and is demonstrably well-shielded against both conventional and anomalous attacks — all previous assassination attempts by the Foundation and by other agencies have failed. Target poses only minimal threat to SCP-8352 containment.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2011-04-01
Target: Gideon Sturgis
Reason: Target is a board member of the Manna Charitable Foundation with suspected ties to elements of the Chaos Insurgency and the Serpent's Hand. Target has violated Veil protocols on multiple occasions for supposedly humanitarian reasons. Target has mild regenerative abilities that render conventional termination methods unreliable.
Status: APPROVED

Target expired 9 months after SCP-9148 deployment. Target's habit of using his regenerative abilities to routinely donate blood and organs resulted in secondary infections of over 100 other individuals before the target died of fatal insomnia. This collateral damage is considered to be within acceptable limits. Upon consideration, the Overseer Council has declined to pay reparations for the secondary casualties.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2012-12-13
Target: Undersecretary-General D.C. al Fine
Reason: Target represents the single greatest threat to the Foundation's continuity of operations. The chaos of selecting a new Undersecretary-General would enable the Foundation to increase the scale and scope of our operations.
Status: DENIED

The Targeting Committee has provided the following comment on this proposal: "Absolutely the fuck not."

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2015-11-12
Target: Lu Zhang
Reason: Target is the owner of Zhejiang EmblemNorth Co., Ltd, a large agricultural and fishery conglomerate based out of Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China, controversial for its use of Uyghur slave labor and massive illegal overfishing practices. Target is a reality bender suffering from paranoid and narcissistic personality disorder. Target has repeatedly used his abilities to manipulate other individuals for his own entertainment, and to sabotage potential competitors. Target has rendered conventional weaponry non-functional within his area of effect.
Status: APPROVED

SCP-9148 was successfully deployed against target. Onset of prion disease symptoms worsened target's existing psychological disorders and rendered his ontokinetic abilities highly unstable. Target was terminated by GOC Strike Team 4321 ("Black Swan Hypothesis") using experimental paraweaponry. The full extent of collateral damage and civilian casualties is unknown, but estimated to total almost 300 million dollars in property damage and reparations paid by the GOC to survivors. Population of whale sharks in the vicinity of the Galápagos Islands still remains in steady decline.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2019-05-01
Target: Iris Dark
Reason: Target has increased the profitability of Marshall, Carter, and Dark by an order of magnitude since assuming leadership of the company, massively increasing the threat posed to normalcy by the group's operations.
Status: APPROVED

Target made eye contact with the agent carrying SCP-9148 at the moment she fired the device. The agent later died of fatal insomnia. Target remains alive. Investigation into the target's apparent immunity is ongoing. The current leading theory is that since becoming CEO of Marshall, Carter, and Dark, the target is no longer human. Aetheric observation of the target has shown that her aura more closely resembles that of the New York Stock Exchange than that of a baseline human.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2021-02-28
Target: SCP-008-A137
Reason: SCP-008 is an anomalous prion infection; maybe a competing prion infection will neutralize it.
Status: APPROVED

SCP-9148 was deployed against an SCP-008 infectee. After several months, target showed no traces of SCP-008 infection and displayed normal life signs. An unexpected interaction between SCP-008 and SCP-9148 appears to cause a reversal of the effects of SCP-008, without producing a fatal prion infection from SCP-9148. SCP-9148 prions appear to have hostile anti-misfolding properties towards other prions, which leads to mutual neutralization of both prion infections. Neutralization via SCP-9148 deemed successful, but too slow for practical applications.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2022-03-30
Target: SCP-008-A137
Reason: Test to see if former SCP-008 infectees cured via SCP-9148 possess immunity to subsequent uses of SCP-9148.
Status: APPROVED

Target died from fatal insomnia 6 months after SCP-9148 deployment.

PROPOSAL FOR USE

Date: 2024-07-14
Target: Meghan McCain
Reason: Target has recently been nominated as a candidate for President of the United States. An Atlantean cannot be allowed to become President.
Status: DENIED

All operations against the United States government are currently suspended.

The Overseer Council has delegated the power to authorize deployment of SCP-9148 to the //ad hoc// SCP-9148 Targeting Committee, consisting of Site-157 Director Miami Ventura, Department of Analytics Director Simon Pietrykau, and Overseer 5. All requests for use of SCP-9148 must be submitted to the Targeting Committee for review and approval. Denied requests may not be resubmitted for 30 days. [[/div]] [[div style="padding-bottom: -1em; border-bottom: solid 1px #444;"]] ++ **Description** SCP-9148 is a prototype paraweapon developed in the 1970s by the Soviet Union's Main Intelligence Directorate, Psychotronics Division (GRU-P) for use in assassinations. The device superficially resembles a pistol, but kills through the use of psychokinetic force, rather than projectiles. The core of SCP-9148 is a cylinder of an unknown metal alloy, similar in composition to the [[[SCP-148|"telekill"]]] alloy developed by Prometheus Labs. This cylinder is encased in beryllium-bronze. Approximately one meter of copper wiring is tightly wound around the cylinder. The wiring connects the cylinder to the dehydrated frontal lobe of a rat brain. The entire assemblage is powered by a Soviet Type A343 battery. When the trigger is depressed, the device emits a burst of telekinetic force with a range of 185 meters and a magnitude of 1.7 nanonewtons. This force is insufficient to cause immediate physical harm. Instead, SCP-9148 targets neural tissues to induce a protein misfold, creating a prion infection in the victim which resembles fatal familial insomnia. With few exceptions, victims of SCP-9148 die within a year. While effective, SCP-9148 saw limited use by the Soviet Union, and no additional copies were manufactured. It is believed that the average time-to-kill was too long for the weapon's intended purpose; additionally, multiple attempts by various parties to replicate the weapon have uniformly failed, suggesting that its manufacturing process was too complex to allow for mass production. In 1991, the KGB Division of Special Circumstances went rogue, absconding with large quantities of Soviet paraweaponry, SCP-9148 among them. The former Division of Special Circumstances used SCP-9148 to eliminate high-profile targets that posed a hindrance to their criminal operations, including Deputy Director Alex Paszek of the Joint Occult Venture of Europe and Russian State Duma Deputy Dmitri Antonovich Volkogonov. SCP-9148 was recovered alongside several other pieces of paraweaponry during a joint GRU-P/Foundation raid in 1997. Three Mobile Task Force agents involved in the operation subsequently died from prion diseases believed to be the result of SCP-9148. [[/div]] ++ **Targeting Committee Records -- Notable Proposals** Upon initial containment, SCP-9148 was provisionally classified as Safe. However, in light of the utility offered by its ability to untraceably kill targets through seemingly natural causes, SCP-9148 was reclassified as a Thaumiel object and approved for use in Veil-support operations. Per Ethics Committee Recommendation {{99-Foxglove}}, lethal deployments of Thaumiel objects must be approved by a committee of at least three L4 or higher personnel. The SCP-9148 Targeting Committee has been assembled for this purpose. Attached are the records of the Targeting Committee regarding proposed deployments of SCP-9148. Only the most notable proposals are included.
