Special Containment Procedures: Samples of SCP-9149 are to be kept in a secure biological containment unit in the medium-risk biological containment wing, located on floor 16 of Site-19's Heavy Containment Zone.
Standard haz-mat suits have proven sufficient in preventing SCP-9149 infection, personnel must undergo standard decontamination procedures after leaving SCP-9149's containment unit.

In the event of an SCP-9149 outbreak, MTF Epsilon-37 ("Holiday Antibiotics") are to be deployed to the outbreak site, to discern the scale and severity of the outbreak. Infected subjects are to be quarantined and transported to the nearest Foundation facility equipped for the containment of bio-hazardous anomalies, subjects are to be sedated while they progress through the stages of infection. Infected subjects are to be incinerated after expiration.

All testing with SCP-9149 must be approved by the project lead,1 3 Level 3 Researchers or the Containment Manager of the medium-risk biological containment wing.

Description: SCP-9149 is a virus of unknown composition, the structure of which appears snowflake-shaped when viewed under a microscope. Subjects infected with SCP-9149 become obsessed with celebrating the Christmas holiday and will alter their behavior and routines to center completely around activities associated with Christmas, even if they do not celebrate the holiday or possess Christian beliefs.

SCP-9149 is spread through contact with infected bodily fluids, SCP-9149 is primarily concentrated in the saliva and mucus of infected subjects. Due to the method of infection, SCP-9149 has a low rate of infection as it does not spread through airborne or waterborne vectors.
SCP-9149 is most commonly spread by infected individuals serving food and drink items tainted with their saliva to non-infected individuals, tainted items tend to include but are not limited to cookies, eggnog, cakes and hot chocolate.
SCP-9149 is invariably lethal to all infected subjects; there is no known cure for SCP-9149 at this time.

SCP-9149 progresses in 5 stages of infection:

Stage 1: SCP-9149 incubates within the host for a 24-hour period before active infection begins.

Stage 2: Active infection begins; infected subjects will begin to purchase Christmas decorations in bulk and will decorate their domicile. Subjects will become more sociable, inviting friends and family to participate in social gatherings. During these gatherings infected subjects will serve guests tainted food and drink items that will spread SCP-9149 further.

Stage 3: Infected subjects will begin donating significant amounts of money to any nearby charities that are considered reputable, this as well as increased gift buying and the purchasing of further decorations, will commonly result in financial difficulties for infected individuals.
Subjects will develop an indifference towards violence.

Stage 4: Infected subjects will attack any individuals that do not celebrate Christmas or individuals that do not possess "adequate Christmas spirit" and force them to participate in Christmas related activities, if these individuals do not comply, then infected subjects will attempt to kill the individual, usually via blunt force trauma to the head.

Stage 5: After approximately 2 weeks after initial infection, infected subjects will begin to bleed from every orifice, before exclaiming "Merry Christmas, Happy New Year", and finally, expiring via spontaneous cranial eruption.

Discovery: SCP-9149 was discovered in Cleveland, OH on 23/12/2016 after an infected individual expired during an interview with a local news station. Carl Keller, a 37-year-old stockbroker who won a neighborhood Christmas light contest, despite displaying no Christian beliefs and having previously denounced the Christmas holiday.
During the interview, Keller succumbed to Stage-5 infection and expired. Foundation Agents embedded in the network that conducted the interview, confiscated the interview footage and Keller's body, before administering amnestics to witnesses.
After SCP-9149 was identified, Agents screened the civilians that had come into contact with Keller in the days before his death, the investigation uncovered that Keller had served tainted gingerbread cookies to the news team, 5 members of the news team had been infected and were transported to Area-12 for end-of-life care.
The source of SCP-9149 was determined to be a gift basket containing several gingerbread cookies, that was delivered to Keller by his neighbor Alan Doherty.2 Foundation Agents conducted a raid on the Doherty residence and discovered the body of Mr. Doherty on the floor of the living room, bound with rope, with his hands nailed into the floor.
Cause of death was determined to be a .9mm gunshot to the head.

Two notable items were recovered from the Doherty residence; they are as follows:

1: A medical vial containing samples of SCP-9149.

2: Alan Doherty's personal journal. (See below)

+ Interview Log 9149-01
- ACCESS GRANTED

Interviewed: Emily Morrow

Interviewer: Dr. Richard Bernard

Foreword: Ms. Morrow was a field reporter for ████ News, a local network in the Cleveland area. Ms. Morrow was interviewing Carl Keller at the time of his death due to Stage-5 infection. She was determined to be infected with SCP-9149 by Foundation Agents and was transported to Site-19.

[BEGIN LOG]

Dr. Bernard: Good afternoon Ms. Morrow, I'm Dr. Bernard. I'm here to see how you're feeling.

Emily Morrow: I feel great, never been better. Honestly, I don't know why I'm here, I really do need get going. The season's got me busy.

Dr. Bernard: Ms. Morrow, you're here because we need to know more about what occurred during your last interview.

Emily Morrow: What? Oh yes. Was it some kind of sniper? I mean his head just exploded.

Dr. Bernard: Yes, we believe it was disgruntled former client. You don't seem very upset about this.

Emily Morrow: I mean, it was awful thing, but I can't let it ruin the season, Christmas is in three days! I've been so busy with work, there's still decorations to put up, cookies to bake and I still need to shop for my mom, Lord knows she's always so hesitant to ask for something. You'd think I was pulling teeth.

Dr. Bernard: Did Mr. Keller give you anything to eat or drink, during the interview?

Emily Morrow: Yeah, some sugar cookies, reminded me of my grandma's. They kind of tasted like peppermint… when he… died, I smelled peppermint. Is that going to happen to me?

Dr. Bernard: Ms. Morrow, I need you to remain-

Emily Morrow: It is, isn't it. I'm going to die. Let me the fuck out of here you Scrooges, you pathetic holiday haters!

Dr. Bernard: Ms. morrow calm down-

<Subject begins striking the wall of her biohazardous containment unit>

[END LOG]

Closing Statement: Subject entered Stage-4 infection during interview. Dr. Bernard ended the interview early and Ms. Morrow was sedated. She expired from stage-5 infection and her remains were incinerated.

+ Abridged Testing Log

Abridged Testing Log 9149-01

Test-01:
Date: 17/02/2017
Subject: D-87612
Test Description: D-87612 was infected with SCP-9149 and placed in a standard Bio-hazardous Humanoid Containment Cell for the duration of testing. During Stage-2 infection, D-87612 was provided with an artificial Christmas tree, ornaments, garland, and a surplus of Christmas lights.
Results: D-87612 proceeded to assemble the tree and decorate it with the provided materials, before using the remaining lights to decorate its bed and the walls of its cell. Upon completion of decorating, D-87612 requested more lights and garland to decorate further. The request was approved, and it continued to request more materials until expiration.

Test-05:
Date: 28/02/2017
Subject: D-09965
Test Description: D-09965 was infected with SCP-9149 and placed in a standard Bio-hazardous Humanoid Containment Cell for the duration of testing. During Stage-2 infection, D-09965 was provided with 6 paint cans of various colors and 3 different paint brushes.
Results: D-09965 painted large murals on the walls of its cell, until it's expiration during stage-5 infection. The mural on the north wall depicted Santa Claus waving while consuming a gingerbread cookie. The mural on the east wall depicted two reindeer playing in a snow-covered forest. The mural on the west wall depicted a family seated at a large dining table for what appears to be a Christmas dinner. The mural on the south wall depicted D-09965 as a child standing next to a snowman. D-09965 displayed no painting experience prior to testing.

Test-10:
Date: 06/03/2017
Subject: D-13348
Test Description: D-13348 was infected with SCP-9149 and placed in a standard Bio-hazardous Humanoid Containment Cell for the duration of testing. During stage 2-infection, D-13348 was not provided any materials for testing.
Results: D-13348 demanded access to Christmas decorations and appeared severely agitated, request was denied. D-13348 spent the rest of Stage-2 and Stage-3 laying on its bed or pacing around its cell, muttering to itself. During Stage-4 subject's agitation increased, subject demanded access to Christmas decorations, request was denied. D-13348 began slamming its head against the northern wall of its cell. D-13348 expired from severe blunt force trauma.
<End Log>

Recovered Journal of Alan Doherty

Forward: The following are journal entries written by Poi-98763, regarding the creation of SCP-9149. Investigation into details mentioned within the entries is currently being performed by MTF Epsilon-37.
Poi-98763 was a 46-year-old male named Alan Doherty, employed at the Hayworth Mall as a Santa Claus actor. Poi-98763 was generally well liked by friends and co-workers and possessed a strong love of the Christmas holiday, Poi-98763 has no known living family members.
Poi-98763 was previously involved in the containment of SCP-████, on 02/11/1987. Subject was administered Class-B amnestics and released from foundation custody.

27 November 2016
Another Ok day at work, not as bad as yesterday. I could actually stand Greg today, it's a Christmas miracle. Though I guess compared to some managers I've had, Greg isn't too bad. The kids seemed excited for the season, unlike their parents, they seemed so tired, worn out. Like they'd drop dead any minute. One little girl wanted to see me so bad, but her mother just pulled her along like some animal. The poor girl was crying all the way to the parking lot. I've worked retail long enough that I know better than to get upset with the customers, but something about the way that woman treated her daughter, just made me so angry. People just don't have the Christmas spirit anymore.

3 December 2016
Bad day today, Greg jumped down my throat about my line not being orderly enough, how am I supposed to control these people? I lost my cool and told him to shove it. I'm the best Santa this mall has ever seen, so I deserve a little respect. He didn't take it very well, he didn't say anything, but he didn't have to, his face said it all. I don't think he's used to people standing up for themselves around him. As for the shoppers, they were savages! Honestly, I couldn't believe it, they were fighting over toys, and useless decorations, it was unbelievable. Christmas used to be about giving, about peace and love. Now it's about consuming, about buying the trendiest bullshit, about donating to charity, not out of the goodness of your heart, but to brag about it on social media! Christmas wasn't supposed to be like this…

5 December 2016
I got fired today, I should have known. Greg is such a petty little shit, he's everything wrong with corporate Christmas. I've been thinking of a way to bring more Christmas cheer to people and get them in the holiday spirit. My buddy Stevie knows some people who make stuff, weird stuff. Evidently, they bought that weird glowing stone that me and Stevie found back in high school off of him, and he's kept in touch with them over the years. I'll call him up and see if he can reach out to them for me.

9 December 2016

Stevie came through, turns out he does some work for that group he knows, so he's real close with them. They make paranormal shit, I'd think it ridiculous but then there's that stone me and Stevie found, I wonder what they did with it? Anywho, they came back with, what I think is a good answer to my problems. It's a virus that makes people want to celebrate Christmas! Pretty ingenious, I think. I've got a vial of the stuff, I know what I'll do. I think I'll start with Carl from down the street, he's always been a real Scrooge.

23 December 2016

Oh God what have I done? It was going so well, Carl really got into the spirit of the season. His light set up is fantastic and he was giving to charity. I saw him.. on the news. His fucking head exploded, it just blew up. God there was so much blood. I was so stupid to trust those shady motherfuckers, and poor Carl paid for it. He was never the nicest guy, but he didn't deserve that, no one does. I'm going to the police, they won't believe me but if I show them the vial, they'll have to believe. Those bastards will pay for what they did. I gotta call Stevie and tell him what happened.

Stevie told those fuckers that I was going to the police, the idiot! He said that I should let them handle damage control, I won't let Stanton just sweep it under the rung. Stanton will be coming for us, I gotta hurry. If I don't make it then go to the warehouse on Clarkson oh fuck I just heard someone in the living room

+Addendum 9149-01
- ACCESS GRANTED

Addendum 9149-01 The individual mentioned by Poi-98763's journal was identified as Steven Trevino3 by investigating Agents.
MTF Epsilon-37 discovered Trevino bound to the radiator in the corner of his living room, he was completely nude and showed signs of undergoing advanced interrogation techniques.
Cause of death was determined to be a .44 gunshot to the head.
On 26/12/2016, MTF Iota-10 conducted a raid on a warehouse belonging to the Crimson Consumer Products Corporation. The warehouse was believed to be the one mentioned in
Mr. Doherty's journal. Agents engaged several Crimson Consumer Products security personnel, resulting in the loss of 1 agent and the termination of 7 Crimson Consumer Products personnel, 8 personnel were taken into Foundation custody. 4 anomalous objects were recovered from the warehouse and were transported to Site-19 for containment.
Crimson Consumer Products is believed to be a front for a previously unknown paracriminal organization. Investigation is ongoing.
A handwritten note was discovered inside the manager's office. (See Below)

Hey Rylie, word just came in, those Foundation bastards are poking around, and Mr. Stanton wants your place liquidated. Burn the records, take the items to Emersons, and kill whoever you think will snitch. I can't believe you let Doc make that virus for those idiots and believe me Mr. Stanton is pissed. Expect a thrashing.
Reginal Supervisor Davey Gibbs.

[[include :scp-wiki:component:ratio-bar base=--  |ex=--]] [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include theme:black-highlighter-theme]] [[include theme:xmas |xmas-header-bhl= --] |xmas-snow-bhl= --]]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:acs-animation]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:anomaly-class-bar-source |item-number= 9149 |clearance= 3 |container-class= euclid |secondary-class= none |disruption-class= vlam |risk-class= danger ]] @@@@ @@@@ **Special Containment Procedures:** Samples of SCP-9149 are to be kept in a secure biological containment unit in the medium-risk biological containment wing, located on floor 16 of Site-19's Heavy Containment Zone. Standard haz-mat suits have proven sufficient in preventing SCP-9149 infection, personnel must undergo standard decontamination procedures after leaving SCP-9149's containment unit. In the event of an SCP-9149 outbreak, MTF Epsilon-37 ("Holiday Antibiotics") are to be deployed to the outbreak site, to discern the scale and severity of the outbreak. Infected subjects are to be quarantined and transported to the nearest Foundation facility equipped for the containment of bio-hazardous anomalies, subjects are to be sedated while they progress through the stages of infection. Infected subjects are to be incinerated after expiration. All testing with SCP-9149 must be approved by the project lead, [[footnote]]Currently Dr. Richard Bernard[[/footnote]] 3 Level 3 Researchers or the Containment Manager of the medium-risk biological containment wing. **Description:** SCP-9149 is a virus of unknown composition, the structure of which appears snowflake-shaped when viewed under a microscope. Subjects infected with SCP-9149 become obsessed with celebrating the Christmas holiday and will alter their behavior and routines to center completely around activities associated with Christmas, even if they do not celebrate the holiday or possess Christian beliefs. SCP-9149 is spread through contact with infected bodily fluids, SCP-9149 is primarily concentrated in the saliva and mucus of infected subjects. Due to the method of infection, SCP-9149 has a low rate of infection as it does not spread through airborne or waterborne vectors. SCP-9149 is most commonly spread by infected individuals serving food and drink items tainted with their saliva to non-infected individuals, tainted items tend to include but are not limited to cookies, eggnog, cakes and hot chocolate. SCP-9149 is invariably lethal to all infected subjects; there is no known cure for SCP-9149 at this time. SCP-9149 progresses in 5 stages of infection: Stage 1: SCP-9149 incubates within the host for a 24-hour period before active infection begins. Stage 2: Active infection begins; infected subjects will begin to purchase Christmas decorations in bulk and will decorate their domicile. Subjects will become more sociable, inviting friends and family to participate in social gatherings. During these gatherings infected subjects will serve guests tainted food and drink items that will spread SCP-9149 further. Stage 3: Infected subjects will begin donating significant amounts of money to any nearby charities that are considered reputable, this as well as increased gift buying and the purchasing of further decorations, will commonly result in financial difficulties for infected individuals. Subjects will develop an indifference towards violence.    Stage 4: Infected subjects will attack any individuals that do not celebrate Christmas or individuals that do not possess "adequate Christmas spirit" and force them to participate in Christmas related activities, if these individuals do not comply, then infected subjects will attempt to kill the individual, usually via blunt force trauma to the head. Stage 5: After approximately 2 weeks after initial infection, infected subjects will begin to bleed from every orifice, before exclaiming "Merry Christmas, Happy New Year", and finally, expiring via spontaneous cranial eruption. **Discovery:** SCP-9149 was discovered in Cleveland, OH on 23/12/2016 after an infected individual expired during an interview with a local news station. Carl Keller, a 37-year-old stockbroker who won a neighborhood Christmas light contest, despite displaying no Christian beliefs and having previously denounced the Christmas holiday. During the interview, Keller succumbed to Stage-5 infection and expired. Foundation Agents embedded in the network that conducted the interview, confiscated the interview footage and Keller's body, before administering amnestics to witnesses. After SCP-9149 was identified, Agents screened the civilians that had come into contact with Keller in the days before his death, the investigation uncovered that Keller had served tainted gingerbread cookies to the news team, 5 members of the news team had been infected and were transported to Area-12 for end-of-life care. The source of SCP-9149 was determined to be a gift basket containing several gingerbread cookies, that was delivered to Keller by his neighbor Alan Doherty. [[footnote]]Designated Poi-98763[[/footnote]] Foundation Agents conducted a raid on the Doherty residence and discovered the body of Mr. Doherty on the floor of the living room, bound with rope, with his hands nailed into the floor. Cause of death was determined to be a .9mm gunshot to the head. Two notable items were recovered from the Doherty residence; they are as follows: 1: A medical vial containing samples of SCP-9149. 2: Alan Doherty's personal journal. (See below) [[collapsible show="+ Interview Log 9149-01" hide="- ACCESS GRANTED"]] [[div class="blockquote"]]  **Interviewed:** Emily Morrow  **Interviewer:** Dr. Richard Bernard  **Foreword:** Ms. Morrow was a field reporter for ████ News, a local network in the Cleveland area. Ms. Morrow was interviewing Carl Keller at the time of his death due to Stage-5 infection.     She was determined to be infected with SCP-9149 by Foundation Agents and was transported to Site-19. **[BEGIN LOG]**  **Dr. Bernard:** Good afternoon Ms. Morrow, I'm Dr. Bernard. I'm here to see how you're feeling.  **Emily Morrow:** I feel great, never been better. Honestly, I don't know why I'm here, I really do need get going. The season's got me busy.    **Dr. Bernard:** Ms. Morrow, you're here because we need to know more about what occurred during your last interview.    **Emily Morrow:** What? Oh yes. Was it some kind of sniper? I mean his head just exploded.  **Dr. Bernard:** Yes, we believe it was disgruntled former client. You don't seem very upset about this.  **Emily Morrow:** I mean, it was awful thing, but I can't let it ruin the season, Christmas is in three days!  I've been so busy with work, there's still decorations to put up, cookies to bake and I still need to shop for my mom, Lord knows she's always so hesitant to ask for something. You'd think I was pulling teeth.  **Dr. Bernard:** Did Mr. Keller give you anything to eat or drink, during the interview?  **Emily Morrow:** Yeah, some sugar cookies, reminded me of my grandma's. They kind of tasted like peppermint... when he... died, I smelled peppermint. Is that going to happen to me?  **Dr. Bernard:** Ms. Morrow, I need you to remain-  **Emily Morrow:** It is, isn't it. I'm going to die. Let me the fuck out of here you Scrooges, you pathetic holiday haters!  **Dr. Bernard:** Ms. morrow calm down-  //// **[END LOG]**  **Closing Statement:** Subject entered Stage-4 infection during interview. Dr. Bernard ended the interview early and Ms. Morrow was sedated. She expired from stage-5 infection and her remains were incinerated. The request was approved, and it continued to request more materials until expiration. > ------ > **Test-05:** > **Date:** 28/02/2017 > **Subject:** D-09965 > **Test Description:** D-09965 was infected with SCP-9149 and placed in a standard Bio-hazardous Humanoid Containment Cell for the duration of testing. During Stage-2 infection, D-09965 was provided with 6 paint cans of various colors and 3 different paint brushes. > **Results:** D-09965 painted large murals on the walls of its cell, until it's expiration during stage-5 infection. The mural on the north wall depicted Santa Claus waving while consuming a gingerbread cookie. The mural on the east wall depicted two reindeer playing in a snow-covered forest.  The mural on the west wall depicted a family seated at a large dining table for what appears to be a Christmas dinner. The mural on the south wall depicted D-09965 as a child standing next to a snowman. D-09965 displayed no painting experience prior to testing. > ------ > **Test-10:** > **Date:** 06/03/2017 > **Subject:** D-13348 > **Test Description:** D-13348 was infected with SCP-9149 and placed in a standard Bio-hazardous Humanoid Containment Cell for the duration of testing. During stage 2-infection, D-13348 was not provided any materials for testing. > **Results:** D-13348 demanded access to Christmas decorations and appeared severely agitated, request was denied. D-13348 spent the rest of Stage-2 and Stage-3 laying on its bed or pacing around its cell, muttering to itself.  During Stage-4 subject's agitation increased, subject demanded access to Christmas decorations, request was denied. D-13348 began slamming its head against the northern wall of its cell. SCP-9150.raw_content:
NOTICE FROM THE PARAPHARMACOLOGY DIVISION

This document is Level 3/9150 Classified. Any requests for Treatment-R9KL is to be forwarded to the Department of Pharmacology, Parapharmacology Division, and/or Senior Researcher Stephanie Allen, alongside all necessary documents.

— Jason L. Graham, Director, Department of Pharmacology.

Item#: 9150
Level3
Containment Class:
esoteric
Secondary Class:
archon
Disruption Class:
dark
Risk Class:
warning
link to memo

Department of Pharmacology

Special Containment Procedures: Ongoing research is being conducted by the Department of Pharmacology in order to find a potential cure to SCP-9150. Foundation staff affected by the anomaly must undergo mandated therapy until the anomalous effect is no longer present.

Treatment-R9KL is to be synthesized and sold at Foundation-owned pharmacies under the common name of ██████ ████.

SCP-9150 is to be left uncontained. Treatment-R9KL is available for all Foundation staff on request. (See Addendum 9150.1)

Description: SCP-9150 refers to an anomaly that is present in the mind of every living Homo sapiens.

The anomalous effects of SCP-9150 are triggered when a person experiences a high concentration of negative emotions, and the anomaly will last until the individual has fully recovered from the trigger event. During SCP-9150, the individual will progressively lose a specific memory or concept, with the effect intensifying when the individual speak, thinks, or otherwise directly acknowledge the concept. The effects of SCP-9150 can be categorized into 4 5 distinct stages, and a single affected individual can inhabit multiple stages of SCP-9150 for different memories. An advancement of the anomaly will also be accompanied by a specific activation event.

Stage # Effect Activation Event
1 Individual starts experiencing difficulty in remembering minor details of the memory. Individual freezes in place and stares forward.
2 Individual begins to lose long term memories that are related to the core concept. Individual crouches down and lies flat on the ground. If the ground is not appropriate for the action, the individual will wander around in search of an appropriate surface.
3 Individual have great difficulty in recalling the concept, requiring intense concentration. Individual stares to the ceiling for a few seconds before whispering the phrase "Don't forget."1
4 Individual completely loses all memory of the concept. However, the lost concept can still be retaught from scratch, and memories can be artificially replanted. Individual will continuously scream before passing out. Affected individuals have been recorded to take from five seconds up to three months to awaken.
5 Individual loses ability to observe and comprehend the affected concept. Currently known to be permanent. Unknown2

From various Foundation records, there exists numerous evidence to SCP-9150 having been present in the human history for an indeterminate amount of time, presumably since the first emergence of Homo sapiens. The fact that the anomaly was only recently classified as SCP-9150 by the Foundation suggests that the anomaly was retroactively introduced into the collective noosphere.

To date, there has been a total of 1 4 12 63 221 recorded instances of individuals progressing to Stage 5 of the anomaly.

Discovery: The Foundation became aware of SCP-9150 on 5/7/2020 when Junior Researcher Sasha F. Hiller reported having problems with remembering specific details about their assigned research. Hiller was initially prescribed countertop medications, which were ineffective. After reports of similar symptoms in Foundation personnel, and reports from various Foundation-owned public hospitals of the same illness being present in the general populace, the anomaly was designated as SCP-9150, and the Paramedical Department was assigned for further research on the anomaly and its effects.

Experiment Log-9150.α
[FILE OPENED]

During experimentation, various Foundation employees that have reported symptoms attributed to SCP-9150 were interviewed in order to learn more about its effects. This protocol was further extended to also include civilians who were admitted in Foundation-owned hospitals for similar symptoms.

Subject3 Background Results Notes
Junior Researcher Sasha F. Hiller Subject's pet hamster died of complications. Subject have some difficulty in remembering what rodents normally look like. Subject was assigned in the research team for an anomaly related to rats and other similar rodents.
Janitor Jane Owen Subject engaged in physical violence with Researcher Ulysses Boom. Subject have slight difficulty recalling details about the incident. Subject also reported to have, "spent way too much money on useless crap these pasts few days." After the incident, Subject's pay was cut for 2 months as disciplinary action.
Junior Researcher Steven Allen Subject's mother was killed in a car accident. Subject lost almost all memory of the incident. When questioned about their deceased mother, subject said that the only thing they remember was that "she's no longer here." Subject requested Foundation therapy and a paid leave for 1 month. Request was partially accepted.
D-12993 Subject was present during another anomaly's containment breach on 7/7/2007. Subject lost all memory of the incident. Subject was also reported to have become more calm and collected. The containment breach resulted in 12 casualties and 29 injuries, 21 of which are D-classes.
Researcher Ulysses Boom Subject engaged in physical violence with Janitor Jane Owen. Subject have major difficulty recalling details about the incident, reporting that they only "know it was a horrible mistake." When questioned about Janitor Owen, Subject stared blankly with confusion. After the incident, Subject was put on suspension for 1 month as disciplinary action.
O-█ [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED]
PoI-9150-1 Subject was a witness to Incident-8232-Alpha. Subject lost all memory of Incident-8232-Alpha. Subject had recovered fully from SCP-9150 prior to the interview.
34 ENTRIES OMITTED FOR BREVITY
PoI-9150-23 Subject was a witness to Incident-8232-Alpha. Subject can no longer comprehend Incident-8232-Alpha, among other related concepts. Subject was the first recorded instance of the Stage 5 effects of SCP-9150.
145 ENTRIES OMITTED FOR BREVITY

Addendum-9150.1
Treatment-R9KL is an anomalous drug synthesized by the Parapharmacology Division, having the ability to permanently cure SCP-9150 in an individual, with a success rate of 100% in all recorded instances. However, Treatment-R9KL cannot recover memories and concepts lost during the anomaly, only removing the anomaly itself from the individual.

More information on the components and synthesis of Treatment-R9KL is strictly classified. If necessary, contact Senior Researcher Stephanie Allen for requesting access to Document-R9KL-1 and Document-R9KL-2.

Addendum-9150.2
PoI-9150-1 was the first civilian to be interviewed by the Paramedical Department as part of Experiment-9150.A, under the guise of a therapy session. PoI-9150-1 was a witness in Incident-8232-Alpha, the containment breach of an anomaly that lead to approximately 253 civilian casualties during the time period between 3/9/1988 to 11/3/2011 before the anomaly was eventually contained by the Foundation on 12/3/2011.

More information on the anomaly and Incident-8232-Alpha is strictly classified. If necessary, contact the Cryptozoology Division and/or Division Director Whittaker for requesting access to the SCP document.

Interview Log-9150.A
[FILE OPENED]

INTERVIEW LOG

Date: 6/8/2022

Interviewed: PoI-9150-1

Interviewer: Field Agent Sophie S. Smitten

Foreword: The interview was conducted in ███████ Clinic, Surrey, England. Field Agent Smitten was substituted in place of PoI-9150-1's assigned therapist.

<Begin Log, [13:23]>

Field Agent Smitten: Ahem. Good afternoon, Mr. Pedro Ivor.

PoI-9150-1: Oh um, hi!

PoI-9150-1: Uh, sorry. I just thought I would be meeting my usual today. You know, Miss Guinness? Did something ha-

Field Agent Smitten: Oh right. Apologies for the sudden change. She couldn't come to work today for personal reasons. At least that's what she told me.

PoI-9150-1: Oh… that's a bummer.

Field Agent Smitten: But don't worry! She already gave me all the relevant information I need for this session, and she said she'll be able to return next session. And we can end it early or find a different substitute if you don't feel comfortable talkin-

PoI-9150-1: No no no it's fine! I just…

PoI-9150-1: …

PoI-9150-1: …Never mind. Anyway, um, you can start…?

Field Agent Smitten: Of course, let's go over some basic things first. How have your daily life been, lately?

PoI-9150-1: It's actually quite great lately! I just got a new job at the local Mcdonalds and my first shift will start around next Monday. And I think that-

…4

PoI-9150-1: -well, I mean… Sigh.

PoI-9150-1: I still think about it from time to time…

Field Agent Smitten: Hm? What do you mean by that?

PoI-9150-1: Oh, you know… that day…

PoI-9150-1: It's just, something is missing from my head! I know something happened on that day, but I just… I just can't remember it! Why can't I remember it? Why can't I remember… him?

Field Agent Smitten: "Him"? Could you perhaps elaborate?

PoI-9150-1: I… well… I. I can't. I don't know.

…

Field Agent Smitten: To you, too.

<End Log, [15:32]>

Proposal: Due SCP-9150's effects potential to completely cripple any and all Foundation research. Treatment-R9KL is to be administered to every Foundation personnel; as a preemptive measure against SCP-9150.

Although tempting, due to the cost and time needed to synthesize Treatment-R9KL, wide application across the whole Foundation is neither feasible with our current resources, nor worth the effort. — Jason L. Graham, Director, Department of Pharmacology.

Proposal-10KLL.2
[FILE OPENED]

Proposal: Due SCP-9150's effects potential to completely cripple any and all Foundation research. Treatment-R9KL is to be administered to every researcher and Foundation personnel assigned to high-importance duties who are prone to encountering potentially traumatic events during work; as a preemptive measure against SCP-9150.

The anomalous effects of SCP-9150 poses a sizable risk to our most important personnel, therefore, many of our important duties, which can further lead to potentially catastrophic consequences later down the line. — O5-█

Foundation staff affected by the anomaly must undergo mandated therapy until the anomalous effect is no longer present.-- --Treatment-R9KL is to be synthesized and sold at Foundation-owned pharmacies under the common name of ██████ ████.-- SCP-9150 is to be left uncontained. Treatment-R9KL is available for all Foundation staff on request. (See Addendum 9150.1) **Description:** SCP-9150 refers to an anomaly that is present in the mind of every living //Homo sapiens//. The anomalous effects of SCP-9150 are triggered when a person experiences a high concentration of negative emotions, and the anomaly will last until the individual has fully recovered from the trigger event. During SCP-9150, the individual will progressively lose a specific memory or concept, with the effect intensifying when the individual speak, thinks, or otherwise directly acknowledge the concept. The effects of SCP-9150 can be categorized into --4-- 5 distinct stages, and a single affected individual can inhabit multiple stages of SCP-9150 for different memories. An advancement of the anomaly will also be accompanied by a specific activation event. ||~ Stage # ||~ Effect ||~ Activation Event || || 1 || Individual starts experiencing difficulty in remembering minor details of the memory. || Individual freezes in place and stares forward. || || 2 || Individual begins to lose long term memories that are related to the core concept. || Individual crouches down and lies flat on the ground. If the ground is not appropriate for the action, the individual will wander around in search of an appropriate surface. || || 3 || Individual have great difficulty in recalling the concept, requiring intense concentration. || Individual stares to the ceiling for a few seconds before whispering the phrase "Don't forget."[[footnote]]All affected individuals during this event will speak the phrase in English regardless of their fluency or skill with the English language.[[/footnote]] || || 4 || Individual completely loses all memory of the concept. However, the lost concept can still be retaught from scratch, and memories can be artificially replanted. || Individual will continuously scream before passing out. Affected individuals have been recorded to take from five seconds up to three months to awaken. || || 5 || Individual loses ability to observe and comprehend the affected concept. Currently known to be permanent. || Unknown[[footnote]]It is currently debated whether a definitive Stage 5 Activation Event exist or not.[[/footnote]] || From various Foundation records, there exists numerous evidence to SCP-9150 having been present in the human history for an indeterminate amount of time, presumably since the first emergence of //Homo sapiens//. The fact that the anomaly was only recently classified as SCP-9150 by the Foundation suggests that the anomaly was retroactively introduced into the collective noosphere. To date, there has been a total of --1-- --4-- --12-- --63-- 221 recorded instances of individuals progressing to Stage 5 of the anomaly. **Discovery:** The Foundation became aware of SCP-9150 on 5/7/2020 when Junior Researcher Sasha F. Hiller reported having problems with remembering specific details about their assigned research. Hiller was initially prescribed countertop medications, which were ineffective. After reports of similar symptoms in Foundation personnel, and reports from various Foundation-owned public hospitals of the same illness being present in the general populace, the anomaly was designated as SCP-9150, and the Paramedical Department was assigned for further research on the anomaly and its effects. However, Treatment-R9KL cannot recover memories and concepts lost during the anomaly, only removing the anomaly itself from the individual. More information on the components and synthesis of Treatment-R9KL is strictly classified. If necessary, contact Senior Researcher Stephanie Allen for requesting access to Document-R9KL-1 and Document-R9KL-2. [[size 150%]]**Addendum-9150.2**[[/size]] PoI-9150-1 was the first civilian to be interviewed by the Paramedical Department as part of Experiment-9150.A, under the guise of a therapy session. PoI-9150-1 was a witness in Incident-8232-Alpha, the containment breach of an anomaly that lead to approximately 253 civilian casualties during the time period between 3/9/1988 to 11/3/2011 before the anomaly was eventually contained by the Foundation on 12/3/2011. More information on the anomaly and Incident-8232-Alpha is strictly classified. If necessary, contact the Cryptozoology Division and/or Division Director Whittaker for requesting access to the SCP document. SCP-9153: The Missing Infinity

Researchers Helen Dang and Jade Huynh study an anomaly pertaining to the vast infinities of mathematics while navigating a burgeoning romantic relationship and its hardships.

More By Badooga

Incident Notice: SCP-9153-α-0

Instead of recognizing the threat, triggering the containment breach alarm, and notifying relevant security personnel, the alpha version of Myrmex.aic employed for the study of SCP-9153 silently observed the events of Incident 9153-α-0 without intervening and erroneously uploaded its unabridged transcription as a normal research addendum. If you're reading this, this file is in the process of being quarantined, and you're one of the ones quarantining it; as such, the transcript in question (which doesn't seem to be infohazardous, at least for the time being) has been preserved in Addendum 9153.07 for your further review. —Bhaumik

Special Containment Procedures: Mathematics conferences, research publications, and educational institution communication channels are to be monitored by Site-Σ staff for any work involving the continuum hypothesis. Any evidence of a developing SCP-9153-α instance is to be manually reviewed by Researchers Helen Dang and Jade Huynh of the Department of Esoteric Mathematics; if flagged, Mobile Task Force Psi-18 ("Tenure Trackers") is to intervene by preventing knowledge of the instance from spreading, disseminating disinformation that leads to incorrect study of the hypothesis that yields no anomalous effects, and retrieving the anomalous material for further analysis.

The creation and storage of SCP-9153-α instances is to be handled by Site-Σ staff of Level 3 clearance or higher. Any instance is to be kept at least 30 meters from all other mathematics material and digital systems. Instances may be developed on analog surfaces in the presence of a Scranton Reality Anchor, but these surfaces must be destroyed once this work is concluded; permanent copies are to be recorded by and stored on a Numsafe RGU-𝕐1 terminal.

Description: SCP-9153 is the hypothetical solution to the continuum hypothesis2: an open problem in mathematics surrounding the possible sizes of infinite sets. In set theory, rather than a singular label for the cardinality (size) of an infinite set, it is understood that there exists an endless sequence of infinite cardinalities, each one bigger than the last. The continuum hypothesis then posits that there is no infinite cardinality that lies between that of the integers, which are the first infinity in the sequence, and that of the real numbers, the alleged second infinity in the sequence. Since being advanced in 1878, the hypothesis has received considerable attention and development within the wider mathematics community; however, no conclusive proof confirming or denying the existence of this "missing infinity"—tentatively designated SCP-9153-ℵ3—has been verified to date. For further supplementation on the relevant mathematical background, see Document M-HU-11.25.10.

While neither research into the hypothesis nor the hypothesis itself carry any inherent anomalous properties, recent discoveries suggest that any significant mathematical evidence that progresses towards a proof or refutation of its claim, designated SCP-9153-α, must involve anomalous mathematics and thus introduce math-erosion: the gradual structural degradation of any nonanomalous mathematical or digital system it comes in contact with4. Unlike SCP-0335, SCP-9153's degradation also extends to the laws of physics immediately surrounding an SCP-9153-α instance, leading to reductions in Hume levels within the same vicinity (see Discovery).

Research and experimentation involving SCP-9153 is currently headed by Researchers Helen Dang and Jade Huynh from the Department of Esoteric Mathematics, whose contributions are described in the addenda in the form of video recording transcripts automatically uploaded by Myrmex.aic6.

Discovery: Between 12/28/2017 and 01/07/2018, mathematics professor ██████ ████████ from the National University of Singapore generated an SCP-9153-α instance (designated SCP-9153-α-1) during novel research on the continuum hypothesis. The professor then emailed a ZIP file containing SCP-9153-α-1 to four of their colleagues on 01/08/2018. On 01/15/2018, students reported the professor's absence from the first day of classes, which led to a missing person's report. Automated systems embedded in Singaporean law enforcement then triggered a Foundation webcrawler sweep that discovered the anomaly-containing email.

MTF Psi-18 was deployed and found the corpse of Professor ████████ locked in their office soon after. Standard-issue Kant counters read concentrations of 0.57(3) Hm within the area. Professor ████████ was found to have died of strangulation, although there were no signs of forced entrance, a back-and-forth struggle, or any other forensic evidence suggesting the nature of the attacker. SCP-9153-α-1 was safely recovered, leading to the restabilization of local Hume levels, and its digital copy was wiped from the professor's computer and the university's mail servers; as none of the professors had checked their email since at least 12/02/2017, no further containment was required.

Addendum 9153.01: Initial Research Direction

On 01/19/2018, Researchers Dang and Huynh convened to discuss the initial discovery of SCP-9153 and plan their approach for studying the anomaly.

[BEGIN LOG]

Dang opens the door, carrying a heavy bag of overflowing notes and papers, only to discover that Huynh has already situated herself.

Dang: Oh! You're already here… am I—?

Huynh: No worries, I'm just early.

Dang sighs in relief and fully enters the room. She struggles against the weight of her bag, but Huynh steps in and grabs it for her, carrying it in one hand with ease.

Dang: Thank you… that bag nearly killed me when I was coming up the stairs.

Huynh: What have you got in there, cinder blocks?

Dang: A printed copy of every research paper I thought could come in handy. Although, perhaps I went a bit overboard…

Huynh chuckles. After placing down the bag, she outstretches her hand towards Dang.

Huynh: I know we've technically met a few times before, but I figured a formal introduction might be in order now that we're working together. The name's Jade Huynh. I work under Professor Bhaumik on infohazard containment.

Dang returns the handshake.

Dang: Helen Dang. I'm one of Professor Hutchinson's set theorists. Nice to properly meet you, Ms. Huynh.

Huynh: Likewise.

Dang: Say, have you grown even taller since the last time I saw you?

Huynh breaks the handshake and points down at her boots, which she clacks together.

Huynh: No, but these bad boys do net me a few extra inches. They're rather bulky, but hey, that's never stopped me before.

Dang: Oh. They… I'd say they look good on you. In any case, give me a moment to…

Dang rummages through her bag until she acquires two copies of SCP-9153's file, one of which she hands to Huynh.

Dang: Here we are. Complete documentation of SCP-9153, including its initial discovery. I assume you've read this all already, but I left a few annotations on the margins that are deserving of your attention.

Huynh takes her time reading through the entirety of the file and its annotations; once finished, she puts it to the side and stares intently at Dang.

Huynh: So Helen, you think the hypothesis is false?

Dang: I… well, obviously we don't know for sure yet, but I can't fathom a scenario where research on the hypothesis causes anomalous effects without some form of $\aleph_{\text{CH}}$ being the source of it.

Huynh: Anomalous effects don't necessitate mathematical existence. Nonexistence works just as well, especially when we're dealing with reductions in Hume levels.

Dang: Nonexistent mathematical objects don't strangle university professors to death, Ms. Huynh.

Huynh: Neither do ones that do exist. Well, most of the time, anyway. But for all we know, that could have been an unrelated incident. An unfortunate one, of course, but unrelated nonetheless.

Dang: I'm not hedging my bets on that.

Huynh: Fair. Well, if something does come at us, know that I'll fight them all off for you. (She grins.) Hopefully, though, the Reality Anchor here will be an effective first line of defense.

Dang: Hopefully. Back to the task at hand, you'll find that Professor ████████'s notes don't lean towards one solution or another. All they have is a proof is that the hypothesis is solvable, as well as a rough outline for a potential method of anomalous set-forcing that could lead to a solution.

Huynh: Anomalous set-forcing, you say? What sort of change makes the method anomalous?

Dang sits at the RGU-𝕐 terminal beside her and pulls up the file for SCP-9153-α-1. Huynh peers over Dang's shoulder to read it along with her.

Dang: Two separate changes, actually. Normal set-forcing expands our normal set-theoretical universe by introducing a new generic set to the mix, which lets us circumvent the limitations of the normal set-universe that prevent us from solving it there. But this paper describes two modes of anomalous set-forcing: one where the set being forced in is anomalous, and one where an otherwise-incompatible set is forced in anyway through anomalous means. Either approach gives an anomalous set-universe that could contain $\aleph_{\text{CH}}$… or confirm its nonexistence.

Huynh: And from what it says right there, the two approaches can be combined…

Dang: …which means we effectively have three avenues we need to explore here.

Huynh: We're going to be at this for a while, aren't we?

Dang: It would appear so.

Huynh breaks away from the screen, sits backwards in the nearest chair, and sighs loudly.

Dang: Finding a fair distribution of work for this project might be challenging, but there are few options that might—

Huynh: I read through all of your papers, Helen. Between my expertise and yours, there's only one real way to go about this.

Dang: And that is?

Huynh: We make it an assembly line. I pick a set and the type of forcing used to shove it in, and you explore the new set-universe that creates and see if CH can hold there in a way that also holds in our own universe. If it gives good results, or if the Reality Anchor starts beeping like crazy, then we continue from there. If it doesn't work, I'll already have three new options at the ready for you.

Dang: I suppose that is a fair arrangement.

Huynh: Any additions or amendments?

Dang stands up, peering down at Huynh and making direct eye contact with a stern glare.

Dang: I've read through your works too, Jade. I know you're quite the stickler, but I won't let you bog me down with complaints about supposedly-subpar rigor or pointless minutia. You'll have your half of the work, and I'll have mine—unless one of us asks the other for assistance, of course. Is that understood?

Huynh laughs boisterously. She then stands up from her chair, towering over Dang with ease, and grins widely.

Huynh: Very well. Whatever you say, princess.

[END LOG]

With their workflow established, Researchers Dang and Huynh carried out their first batch of set-forcing trials. Of them, only two attempts were notable.

Attempt #: 7
Forced Set: A variant of the real numbers $\mathbb{R}$, designated $\mathbb{R}^{**}$, that is shifted by a generic infinitesimal7.
Forcing Axioms: An anomalous bounding axiom that allows for multiple continua to exist so long as they remain finitely separated.

Results: A model that corresponds to a three-dimensional fluid; differences in depth correspond to different multiples of the aforementioned infinitesimal. Notably, the (non)existence and potential value of Dash Aleph must remain constant regardless of depth.

Notes: This confirms our suspicion that the solution to the continuum hypothesis is definitive and self-consistent. Looks like we're on the right track after all. —J.H.

Attempt #: 23
Forced Set: A generic class of anomalous "hyperangle" sets used by the Foundation to construct containment areas that use non-Euclidean geometries to their advantage8.
Forcing Axioms: A variant of the "Martin's maximum" forcing axiom that filters out most standard classes of anomalous sets.

Results: A normal, albeit smaller than normal set-universe where most mathematical anomalies cannot exist. Notably, the continuum hypothesis is undecidable here.

Notes: This once more confirms that the continuum hypothesis cannot be solved without the use of esoteric mathematics. Curiously, the anti-anomalous filter didn't pick it up—so either Dash Aleph doesn't exist at all, or it's something out of the ordinary even for this department. —J.H.

Addendum 9153.02: Narrowing the Search Band

The next ten months of exploration into the anomaly yielded no significant progress. During their regularly scheduled meeting on 11/24/2018, Researchers Dang and Huynh sought to narrow the scope of their search by finding constraints on the methodology used.

[BEGIN LOG]

Dang: Okay, now it's recording. Sorry about that.

Huynh: Damn. It's alright though. Let's take it from the top.

Dang: Can't we just leave it at "we've found nothing and know nothing"?

Huynh: Gotta stick to the rules.

Dang: Fine. (She sighs.) Over the course of the last ten months, Jade and I have made 66 failed attempts at using forcing to find a set-universe where proving CH is within the realm of possibility. These 66 attempts can be divided into three groups of 22, each one using a different method of set-forcing: mundanely forcing an anomalous set, which Jade has called the "corkscrew" method; anomalously forcing a mundane set, labeled the "can opener" approach by Jade; and a hybrid of both, which a certain someone has designated—

Huynh: —The "power drill" procedure!

Dang: You really are proud of that one, hm?

Huynh: I am, actually! Don't act like you don't find it funny.

Dang: Endearing at best, annoying at worst. In any case—

Huynh: You wound me, Helen. But since you brought me tea today, I'll let it slide… for now.

Dang: As I was saying, I've been calling for us to change our approach after the first six months, while Jade here thought it wise to finish her backlog of ideas first. From the date on this addendum, you can see which one of us won that argument.

Huynh: We had to try, Helen. It's not my fault it didn't work.

Dang: We need to figure out a different approach, or at least determine which of our current approaches are irredeemably flawed, or else we'll be at this forever.

Huynh: Any suggestions, then? Because I'm down to keep trying it my way 'till the end of the year.

Dang: You've been excitedly talking about the departmental holiday celebration in December for the past three weeks. Do you plan to attend that and continue working on this simultaneously?

Huynh: Well, not at the same time, obviously. But if I must, I'll pull an all nighter… or two.

Dang furrows her brow. Huynh shrugs it off.

Huynh: Don't act surprised. I drink black tea for a reason.

Dang: (She sighs in defeat.) Again, is there anything that could help make this process less of a blind search?

Huynh: Let me take a look at your current notes.

Huynh organizes Dang's scattered notes into three neat sections—one for each of the three methods—and scans their contents.

Huynh: So, most of our attempts at corkscrewing have led to… what, a bunch of disjoint sets?

Dang: It effectively shatters the set-universe into several pieces, yes. If I had to eliminate one of our methods, it would be this one.

Huynh: Got it. What about the can opener?

Dang: That one is… well, a can of worms. The results seem fine at first, but then they tend to… I don't know, shift into something else? It's not the type of math-erosion I'm used to, to be sure. I've been calling it "axiomatic drift".

Huynh: Yikes. So then power drilling it… yeesh, how many papers do you have there?

Dang: At least twice the other two combined. This hybrid approach has yielded the most varied results, but they take a lot more work to map out fully. Thus, this one's a bit of a "wild card".

Huynh: No wonder why we've been going so slowly as of late, then… hm. So if we eliminate pure corkscrewing—I doubt a shattered set-universe can do us any good—then we're down to either using a can opener or busting out the power drill. Any thoughts?

Dang: I think we ought to double down on the hybrid approach.

Huynh: The power drill? Really?

Dang: It's provided the largest variety of results so far. Surely that's worth something?

Huynh: I'm glad you've enjoyed exploring that thus far, but clearly it's a huge bottleneck for our current workflow. I can't see it working out anytime soon—not until Myrmex.aic reaches the point in development where it's fast enough to do it for us.

Dang: I am not waiting half a decade just for some machine to verify the futility of our efforts. We need to use the—ugh—"power drill" method.

Huynh: (She laughs.) That's my girl.

Dang exhales unsteadily, turning away quickly to face her sprawled out notes. After a few seconds of peering over them, Dang's face lights up, and the Scranton Reality Anchor emits a single loud beep.

Dang: …What if a shattered set-universe can do us some good?

Huynh: Pardon?

Dang grabs a wad of notes and rushes to the chalkboard.

Dang: This whole time, we've considered this project to be a normal, static set-theory problem.

Huynh: I mean… yeah. Sets are sets. Anomalous ones might erode the math around them, but that's not the same thing as an actual time-evolving system.

Dang: But what if the axiomatic drift is a feature of our set-universes, not a bug? What if time evolution is in fact an emergent property any set-universe that's useful for our search must have? And what if we could claim some control over where this drift takes us?

Huynh: …Go on.

Dang begins mapping out her thoughts on the chalkboard.

In spite of this, Dang suddenly turns to face it; before she can scream, an unseen force grabs her by the throat and lifts her into the air. As Dang flails around helplessly, Huynh springs into action, returning to her feet and swinging a broken desk leg at the assailant with reckless abandon. Her attacks hit only air, so she instead attempts to pull Dang away, which also proves to be futile; all the while, the grip on Dang's throat leaves dark bruising that grows and intensifies by the second.

Huynh: Dammit dammit dammit dammit—

In a flash of inspiration, Huynh grabs Dang's bag of notes and papers as it flies across the room and successfully redirects its trajectory to slam it into the assailant. Dang drops to the floor and coughs violently as she regains the ability to breathe; merely one second later, Dang and Huynh cover their ears and wince in pain despite the absence of new audio stimuli.

Huynh: Helen, are you okay?!

Dang: (She continues coughing.) Jade, you were right—

Distortions in reality ripple out from the nonexistent area where the Reality Anchor once sat, twisting space itself into warped, unrecognizable forms; another quake soon follows.

Huynh: What?

Dang: Jade, it's set-forcing. Something forced concepts into our Noösphere, and that carried $\aleph_{\text{CH}}$ into our mathematics. The moment it took shape in my mind, it… oh God…

Huynh: Shit, so this is Dash Aleph?

Dang: Dash Aleph doesn't exist. You were right all along, it shouldn't exist, it can't exist, but something injected it here anyway, or maybe it is the injection…? I… I don't know, I don't know, I'm so—

Huynh: It's a rift. A small one, but it grows bigger the more you look at it—comprehend it? A literal gap in mathematics and reality, one that lets infohazardous monsters like that squeeze their way in. Does that cover it?

Huynh gestures towards a spot on the floor that contains nothing of note. Dang reluctantly nods in agreement.

Huynh: I understand. Now, how do we stop it?

Dang: We can't. I don't… the Reality Anchor is feeding it. Who knows what that'll do?

Huynh: We can't shut it off from out here. How are we supposed to—?

Both of them are hit with a realization; Huynh's eyes widen in fear, while Dang's well up with tears.

Huynh: No. That is not an option.

Dang: It's the only way.

Huynh: Fuck you. We'll find another way.

Dang: I don't think we can. The screaming, it… it's so loud, I can barely breathe, I need—

Huynh: We need to get out of here. Surely a task force is coming to extract us?

Dang: Through what door? They won't make it in time. It's just us in here, my love. Always has been, always will be.

Huynh grits her teeth; tears stream down Dang's face. The spatial distortions intensify, causing the walls, floors, and ceilings to develop deep cracks.

Dang: If I don't go in there now, this anomaly is bound to tear the whole site apart—and you along with it.

Huynh: Who gives a shit?! And hell, how do you even know this will work?

Dang: I don't. But I have to try, don't I?

Dang stands up, grabs her bag of papers, and walks unsteadily to the threshold of the non-existent region.

Dang: It's like you said: sooner or later, everything comes to an end.

Huynh reaches out to embrace her. They kiss, briefly and poignantly, until Dang breaks away and takes another step towards the threshold.

Huynh: Helen, please. Just… stay with me.

Dang: …I wish I could, Jade. But you can't make this choice for me. Not this time.

Dang crosses the threshold and thus ceases to exist. Despite this, Huynh attempts to continue conversing with her.

Huynh: I'm so sorry…

No response.

Huynh: You… you really shouldn't. I—

No response.

Huynh: (She chuckles.) You know me. I always try my damnedest.

No response.

Huynh: Do you think I'll ever see you again?

No response.

Huynh: …I love you.

No response.

Five seconds later, the anomaly is quelled: the swirling office materials fall to the floor; the spatial distortions and quakes vanish; the region where the Reality Anchor once existed returns to reality; the doors and windows reappear. Huynh collapses to her knees, and then to the floor, falling fully unconscious just as security personnel break through the door and enter the room.

[END LOG]

STOAT NEWS 24/7


Why the de-extinction of coral is bad for the economy

Greg Nielsen
16th of June, 2086

The reintroduction of corals to the Caribbean Sea has had a number of undesirable effects. In the past month, hundreds of employees at ExxArc have lost their jobs as oil platforms in the region have been forced to close due to a phenomenon that has been dubbed 'coral clogging'.

After two decades of reckless genetic engineering, an international team of careless scientists with backing from the European Union, African Union, and a number of governments has unleashed genetically engineered species in the Caribbean Sea as part of a project aiming to restore the oceans of the early 21st century. These include a variety of species ranging from corals and sponges to whale sharks and cuttlefish, which have been extinct in the wild since the 2060s.

This has given rise a new phenomenon dubbed 'coral clogging' where corals, and sometimes sponges, grow inside boreholes as well as on equipment, resulting in clogging and structural damage. Due to these species being classed as 'critically endangered' following their reintroduction to the wild, measures to remove them from oil platforms have been deemed illegal. However, ExxArc has announced a research project aiming to discover a way to repel them from yet unaffected rigs.

"It's unbelievable. I took this job so I could pay for my kids' college tuition, and I'm just not ready to tell them that only one of them might be able to go now," says Steve Bennett, a technical diver who recently found himself unemployed after ExxArc's recent layoffs.

ExxArc CEO DeForest Morgan has accused the scientists behind the project of inserting genes in the corals to make them seek out hydrocarbons in a deliberate move to sabotage the industry, which a representative of the project has 'unsubstantiated'.

At the current rate of spread, 'coral clogging' is estimated to cause damages upwards of 100 000 000 000€ and the loss of up to 20 000 jobs before the end of July.

Item#: 9154
Level2
Containment Class:
archon
Secondary Class:
baldr
Disruption Class:
