Junior Researcher Maria Cortez undergoing surgery.

Item #: SCP-9190

Object Class: Thaumiel

Secondary Class: Yesod1

Special Containment Procedures: All information relating to SCP-9190 has been acquired by the Foundation. Personnel who believe in an afterlife are barred from enacting SCP-9190. All individuals about to undergo SCP-9190 are to be prepared for their voyage into the future, and, if necessary, armed.

To prepare for SCP-9190, the following procedures must be performed before the first incision is made:

1. A metronome is placed near the feet of the subject, set to 107 BPM

2. A circle of gunpowder is laced around the table containing the subject

3. A carcass of a Talpa europaea2 is placed beneath the subject's head

4. Seven drops of human blood are applied to the subject's face.

5. [DATA EXPUNGED]

6. All medical tools are to be dipped in a jar of blended Aedes aegypti3.

7. All churches within 2,000 miles are to be closed until the procedure is finished.

If you are scheduled to undergo SCP-9190, please contact Project Advisor Sasha Wright.

Description: SCP-9190 is a form of surgery capable of transferring a human subject into the future.4 Personnel sent into the future by SCP-9190 are unable to call back or return to the past; this process is typically used to enforce the presence of the Foundation within periods of time that would otherwise lead to the Foundation ceasing to exist.

The exact process behind SCP-9190 is not scientifically understood.


Video Log:

Date: 11/24/2014

Subject: Junior Researcher Jeremiah Elbertson

Supervising Lead: Senior Researcher Rodrick Kessler

[BEGIN LOG]

00:00: Standard preparations are made. Baseline vitals recorded.

00:05: Subject consumes a mixture of dog milk, ground up bismuth, cerebrospinal fluid, and salt water.

00:07: Subject requests to be reminded what "deployment" entails. Staff are instructed not to answer.

00:13: Subject is restrained using a combination of zip ties and Kevlar rope. Subject appears distressed. This is ignored.

00:18: Subject has three triangles drawn on his stomach with black sharpie.

00:23: First incision is made along sternum. Internal cavity slightly exposed.

00:27: Several more incisions are made in order to fully open the chest cavity. Subject tries to hold back tears, but fails.

00:29: The metronome is reset.

00:34: Subject attempts to escape from their constraints. He is gently affirmed that everything will be okay, and is told to fall asleep.

00:39: The subject's ninth and tenth rib are removed. The ribs are then placed into a small tray, before being consumed by one of the surgeons present. Subject is then thanked.

00:50: A tube is then entered into the subject's stomach. This tube proceeds to extract the aforementioned liquid.

00:54: Subject is then force fed the previously described mixture.

01:02: A bonobo heart is placed within the subject's chest cavity, which is then sealed up with a mixture of glue and staples.

01:16: Subject's mouth is then opened. A dim light is seen deep in his throat.

01:24: The metronome is reset.

01:26: Subject's scalp is cut and their skull exposed. Subject's face is covered in a cloth.

01:33: Subject is hand fed an ortolan. Subject is not allowed to spit up any bones or feathers.

01:40: Subject's skull is opened. His brain appears to be covered in soil. This soil is removed.

02:01: Subject ceases all attempts at movement. His breathing grows heavier.

02:08: Several triangles are drawn on the subject's brain. These triangles are then cut out. Brain matter is consumed.

02:21: Cloth is then placed on the subject's exposed brain. When the cloth is removed, his skin has completely covered his brain. The triangle markings are still present.

02:30: Subject is given a kiss on the lips. A single tear rolls down his face.

02:32: The lead surgeon self terminates via gunshot.

02:33: All other surgeons remain still. The metronome continues.

03:40: The room darkens completely. The only light source now comes from inside the patient's chest. It beats irregularly.

03:37: The metronome is turned off.

03:03: His chest expands. Someone is attempting to escape.

02:00: Subject disappears.

[END LOG]

Due to the nature of SCP-9190, it is unknown if this process is successful until the year 2247. Staff are advised not to indulge in prayers for the success of the operation and/or the salvation of Elbertson's soul.

SCP-9191-152, photographed when discovered in the collections of an antiquary.

Special Containment Procedures:

Most instances of SCP-9191 are to be stored within a standard storage locker at Site-67 with their alarm switches in the OFF position. All experimental proposals must be approved by a minimum of two personnel with Level 3 clearance and subsequently submitted to Dr. Messmer.

Exceptions include SCP-9191-46, SCP-9191-165, and SCP-9191-272, which are stored at Site-17, Site-19, and Site [REDACTED] respectively, with their alarm switches in the ON position. Each of these instances is to be contained within a specialized vacuum safe. Direct interaction or adjustment requires prior authorization from the Site Director.
 
 
Description:

SCP-9191 is a collection of mechanical alarm clocks with varied appearances, shapes and sizes.The diameters of discovered instances varied from 6.6 cm to 12.9 cm.. Instances are designated SCP-9191-X in the order of discovery. Each instance possesses a clock dial with an hour and minute hand, which function normally when the alarm switch is in the OFF position (i.e., the hour hand completes one revolution every twelve hours; the minute hand every hour). The displayed time, however, does not correspond to local temporal reality. Each instance also contains two adjustment knobs and an alarm switch on its rear surface. The alarm switch may take the form of either a button or lever, typically marked with an icon (e.g. ⏰) indicating its function.

When the alarm switch is in the OFF position, instances of SCP-9191 can be easily dismantled or destroyed. Components recovered in this state exhibit no anomalous properties and are indistinguishable from those of non-anomalous alarm clocks. If all components remain intact and are reassembled correctly, the object will regain anomalous functionality. Conversely, when the alarm switch is activated, instances become significantly more resistant to damage. Conventional disassembly is impossible; any fragments produced permanently lose anomalous properties.

An instance of SCP-9191 exhibits anomalous effects only when the alarm switch is in the ON position. Upon activation, the hour and minute hands cease movement until the switch is returned to the OFF position. While active, all personnel and objects within a spherical area centered on the instance enter a state designated SCP-9191(-X)-A, hereafter referred to as the “cycling routine.” Termination of this state occurs upon deactivation of the switch, at which point affected individuals report perceiving a ten-second auditory phenomenon described as moderate ringing. This sound does not originate from any physical source and appears to manifest solely within the perception of previously affected subjects. This characteristic provides a reliable method for confirming whether an alarm clock is an instance of SCP-9191.

Personnel affected by SCP-9191-X-A (designated SCP-9191-X-1) report experiencing life as though within a temporal loop. Objective time, however, continues to progress normally. This condition does not entail complete repetition of events, but instead results in the perception of existence as routine and largely unchanging. Significant deviations are absent, though minor progressions persist. For instance, an affected subject may retain an identical daily routine for decades while continuing to anticipate recurring events (e.g. a scheduled television program) or experience gradual personal developments (e.g. occupational promotion). Further details regarding this effect are documented in subsequent test logs.

 

  Show side effects 
  Hide 


Within SCP-9191-A, apparent normalcy is maintained through alterations of physical laws and baseline reality. In the case of SCP-9191-1, residents of the affected town have continued normal daily activities since the 1850s, resulting in lifespans significantly exceeding known human limits. The mine currently under excavation appears to possess an inexhaustible supply of resources..This deduction was based on the size of the mine recorded in 1851, which was unable to sustain mining operations for such a long period of time according to geology. However, the measure result at present shows that the volume of mineral extraction corresponds to the actual conditions, so it is hard to decide whether the anomaly had affected this..
                        
An additional cognitive effect manifests in affected individuals, rendering them incapable of perceiving discrepancies between affected and unaffected areas, or the existence of SCP-9191 instance itself. Experimental data indicates that even when informed directly of their condition, affected subjects disregard the information and rapidly forget it. SCP-9191-A also inhibits information transfer between affected and unaffected populations by diminishing affected individuals’ inclination to inquire about external events. Furthermore, subjects exhibit progressive memory degradation, particularly regarding temporally precise information. The severity of this effect correlates positively with the stability parameters of the active instance.

None of these effects are mitigated by an active Scranton Reality Anchor, and no Hume discrepancies are measurable via Kant Counter readings, indicating that the anomaly does not operate through reality warping.

 


 

An accessible analogy for understanding SCP-9191-A is to consider episodic series such as The Simpsons. SCP-9191-X-1, akin to a character in such series, follows a consistent pattern of behavior. While deviations may occur occasionally, any unusual circumstances are resolved before significant changes manifest.
However, this analogy may lead to misconceptions, particularly when dealing with instances where the stability value is set too high or too low.

 

When the alarm switch is in the OFF position, the two adjustment knobs on SCP-9191 instances are mechanically operable but do not actuate the clock hands. Rather, the knobs control parameters of the SCP-9191-A effect — specifically the spatial extent (radius) and the stability of the effect’s manifestation. When the alarm switch is set to ON, attempts to manipulate the knobs produce no measurable change; mechanical resistance is encountered and all documented attempts to rotate the knobs while the switch is ON have consistently failed.

All observed instances employ clockwise rotation to increase the controlled parameter. Counterclockwise rotation to the mechanical stop is defined as 0; each complete clockwise revolution increments the parameter by 1. The relationship between knob rotation and the controlled value is summarized in Table X below. Maximum allowable clockwise rotation varies between instances, most commonly permitting 3–5 full rotations per knob.
 
Knob 1:
 
Rotation Value (round) 1 2 3 4 5
Radius (m) 0.2 9.5 480 22000 1000000
        The current data follows an exponential growth pattern approximately.
 
 
Knob 2: (Stability indicates the repetition strength within the affected area)
 
Rotation Value (round)                                           Stability (and Example)
1 Very Low & Long-Term Pattern                            e.g. The continuous dynastic changes throughout feudal history.
2 Low & Mid-Term Pattern                               e.g. Life proceeds normally for all residents in a secluded town, with no significant changes occurring.
3 Moderate & Short-Term Pattern                            e.g. Episodes of an episodic series.
4 High & Near-Certainty                                e.g. The daily routine of a common worker.
5 Very High & Repetitive Movement                           e.g. A hamster in a cage cycling between eating and sleeping.

 
The radius of the SCP-9191-A effect is considered an estimated value only, as its boundaries may expand or contract slightly to conform to the surrounding environment. In practice, the effect is consistently associated with a discrete area (e.g. a single building, enclosed space, or an entire settlement), within which the phenomenon persists. No distinct border has been observed; transitions into or out of the affected area occur gradually, without an observable threshold where anomalous behavior begins or ceases.

Due to these properties, unintentional identification of SCP-9191 instances is unlikely. Most instances of SCP-9191 have been discovered incidentally during unrelated anomaly investigations, or through follow-up inquiries into reports of abnormal environmental conditions. While the anomalous effects of SCP-9191 are well-documented, it is estimated that numerous instances — particularly those deactivated or exhibiting only minimal activity — remain undiscovered. This is assessed as an acceptable risk due to their negligible impact and the prohibitive resources required for comprehensive global identification. MTF Gamma-5 (“Red Herrings”) are concurrently tasked with the retrieval of reported newfound instances.

All attempts to determine the origin of SCP-9191 have been unsuccessful. It remains unknown whether the objects are of artificial manufacture or otherwise anomalously generated. The earliest verified activation of an SCP-9191 instance dates to the 17th century.
 
  
 
  
Addendum 9191.1: Discovery of SCP-9191-1

SCP-9191-1 was initially discovered during an investigation of the negative impact caused by an escaped hostile anomaly. One of the investigators was dispatched to ████ , a small town with a population of approximately 5000, and recorded what he seen in the town. Researchers were able to confirm the town wasn't attacked by the anomaly, but they also found something else strange: Residents in the town had some habits that obviously didn‘t belong to this era, which was sometimes completely out of sync with their living environment. Actually, they seemed to maintain some life patterns in The Gold Rush.More precisely, the condition exhibits the characteristics of a post–gold rush era..

After searching the archives about this town, another overlooked report written before was found, which also described the bizarre feature. A research team then started to look into the cause of the strange phenomenon. Nevertheless, no results were found eventually, and residents there had not normalized their life patterns either. Most of the residents had been living there for roughly a century, but neither did they show any sign of aging physiologically and psychologically, nor did their personalities or social classes changed greatly.

After the researchers withdrew, the foundation decided to monitor the town over the long term. For the next several decades, it is the town that bore the serial number SCP-9191. However, Dr.Messmer, one new research director, conducted another investigation to seek out the source of the anomaly thoroughly in 20█. During the investigation, most items in the town were checked, through which SCP-9191-1 was found. After SCP-9191-1 was removed from the town, the residents there returned to normal gradually, and the surveillance against it was cancelled three years later.

  Interview to residents in ████ , former SCP-9191  
  Interview to residents in ████ , former SCP-9191 
  • Interview to ██, a teenage girl in Grade 9
  • Interview to ███, an adult men

Interviewer: Dr. Ronan Hale

Interviewee: ██

Foreword: The interview was disguised as an inquiry from HHS.U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

[BEGIN LOG]

(Greetings and unrelated content omitted)

Dr. Hale: So, could you tell me about your daily routine? Like, when do you wake up or go to school?

██: Hmm… I usually get woken up by my dad around 7:00, and then I usually go for a jog outside for a bit. After that… // (Response omitted for brevity) // …and I go to bed around 10:30 PM.

Dr. Hale: Is that really your routine every day? No exceptions?

██: (Laughs) Of course not! We have weekends and holidays! And sometimes I go to my friend's house after school, so I probably won't be home until around 7:00 PM. Oh, and sometimes we have special activities at school, so those days definitely don’t follow the same routine.

Dr. Hale: Got it. How long has this routine been like this?

██: (Thinks for a moment) Well, I can't remember the exact time, but it must have been after I started high school, so it’s probably been around 3 years… Why do you ask?

Dr. Hale: (Smiles) It’s just a simple question, don’t worry. Let’s talk about your studies for a bit, okay? For example, what are you learning in math class right now?

██: It’s just functions and… (Response omitted for brevity)

Dr. Hale: Alright, what did you learn last year?

██: (Thinks for a moment) I… believe it was an easier version of this? I think I’ve forgotten a bit. I’m not very good at math.

Dr. Hale: (Smiles) Okay, no worries. Now, let’s just take a short break.

(After break)

Dr. Hale: So, could you tell me what you learned in math back in Grade 8? You can think about the textbooks you used.

██: Oh, of course! I learned about the rectangular coordinate system and… (Response omitted for brevity)

Dr. Hale: Last question, how do you feel about your life? Do you find it monotonous?

██: Not at all, definitely not monotonous.

Dr. Hale: Alright, that’s all. Thanks for your participation.

[END LOG]
 

Interviewer: Dr. Ronan Hale

Interviewee: ███

Foreword: The interview was disguised as an survey on the town's history and the current state.

[BEGIN LOG]

(Greetings and unrelated content omitted)

Dr. Hale: Let’s move on to the next topic. How much do you know about the gold mine beside the town?

███: (Laughs) Pretty much! I started working there when I was about 17 or 18 years old. I’d say most of the men in the town have done the same. You know, as long as you’re lucky, working there is definitely a good choice.

Dr. Hale: OK, has there been any development in the mine?

███: Sure, I’d say the biggest development has been in the machinery. It’s hard to imagine that so many people still rush to the mine for gold, like they did years ago. For example, the hydraulic drill—it’s incredibly powerful.

Dr. Hale: Do you remember any major events that have happened in the town over the years?

███: (Ponders for a long time) I’m not sure, actually. There doesn’t seem to be many special events in our small town… Maybe you could try the library for more information, instead of asking me.

Dr. Hale: Oh, it’s just a general survey, not a test. Just tell me what you remember. For example, when was the town established?

███: I think it was about 20 or 30 years ago if you’re asking about the "town." During the gold rush, there were people living here, but it wasn’t really a "town" yet, more like a place for the workers to stay.

Dr. Hale: Can you tell me the exact year?

███: Sorry, I can’t remember that well.

Dr. Hale: Alright, next question: How do you feel about the technological developments in your daily life?

███: Well, I’m not really familiar with the science stuff. I can only say it’s developing very quickly. It’s hard to imagine how I got by before without some of the things we have now.

Dr. Hale: Last question, about yourself—how do you feel about your life? Do you find it monotonous? This will help us understand the living conditions of the residents here better.

███: Sort of, maybe? There’s not much to look forward to while working in the mine.

Dr. Hale: That’s all. Thank you for your participation.

[END LOG]
 


  Initial discovery of SCP-9191-1 (Action Log Excerpt) 
  Initial discovery of SCP-9191-1 (Action Log Excerpt) 

Investigative Action Log 9191-29 (Excerpt)
 
Location: Town library
 
Date: 20█/█/█
 

(Local Time 16:00) A team of three investigators entered the library and began checking every item, starting with the lobby.
 
(16:04) One of the investigators entered archive room No.1.
 
(16:19) The investigator activated the alarm switch of SCP-9191-1, producing a ringing sound. Simultaneously, everyone in the town reported hearing the same sound, a phenomenon observed later. The investigator himself did not immediately recognize the anomaly and continued inspecting other items.
 
(16:21) The investigators reconvened, at which point the unusual ringing sound was acknowledged. They immediately secured SCP-9191-1 and transported it to Site-67.

After the discovery of SCP-9191-1, researchers quickly identified its superficial anomaly. Long-term observations of the town confirmed that the anomalous effects began to dissipate, ultimately confirming that SCP-9191-1 was the source of the phenomenon. Former SCP-9191 was then reclassified as neutralized.

According to the later interview with residents, none of them noticed SCP-9191-1 before, probably due to the anomaly effect that can significantly reduce its presence. ████ is merely a common town at present.

Special Containment Procedures:

SCP-9192 is considered low priority as it has not manifested naturally at any point in the past 250 years.

Foundation web-crawlers are to be on constant alert for any possible SCP-9192 events. Sanitation ships are to be immediately deployed to any planet with reports of infection. Altered video reproductions of Incident 63XA2 have been distributed to the public.

Description:

SCP-9192 is an infectious prion disease which systematically deconstructs hosts until all portions have been reduced to smallest possible components. SCP-9192 is primarily transmitted through consumption of material from infected individuals; however, it is possible for misfoldings to trigger SCP-9192 among entities who have come into contact with auditory transmission AVBD13. Currently, it is believed up to 99% of the known universe has been exposed to this signal.

Despite this, there has been only one recorded instance of SCP-9192 triggering without outside intervention.

SCP-9192 infection is characterized by 5 distinct stages of progression. In all cases, SCP-9192 has killed its target. There is no known cure.

Stage Symptoms
Stage 1 Throughout Stage 1, infected instances (hereby referred to as SCP-9192-1) lose small amounts of tissue, largely through coughing or sneezing. SCP-9192-1 instances will also typically spit up large amounts of blood. In rare instances, subjects may lose portions of skin, leading to red, fleshy spots concentrated around the neck, hands, and knees.
Stage 2 In stage 2, SCP-9192-1 instances begin to display flu-like symptoms such as vomiting or a high fever. They will expel large amounts of blood and bile, often simultaneously surfacing detached stomach lining. During this stage, subjects also become largely unwilling to consume food or nutrients, claiming a persistent feeling of euphoria that prevents them from processing external and internal stimuli. This euphoria becomes overwhelming enough to render any movement or activity difficult.
Stage 3 In stage 3, matter loss becomes significant enough to be visually obvious. Instances themselves appear to be unaware of any abnormal behavior occurring, and will often push back if told to undergo treatment. This is believed to be caused by a heavy loss of brain biomass at this stage, but may also be a result of the virus's inherent properties. Subjects in stage 3 will begin to cough up, vomit, or otherwise leak significant amounts of blood, bile, brain matter, and organ chunks from various orifices. SCP-9192-1 instances will also undergo loss of hair, teeth, and fingernails.
Stage 4 During Stage 4, the body will begin to completely disassemble itself. Bones, eyes, organs, joints, and even limbs will individually tear off the body until the instance has been completely reduced. It is unknown if the subject is still conscious throughout this stage, as the exact nature of the individual consciousness of each bodily portion is heavily debated. Once the subject has been completely separated into smaller individual components, stage 5 will begin.
Stage 5 After each component has been detached, they will further separate until they are minimized to the smallest possible base components. Skin will be flayed off and veins will deconstruct until the subject has been reduced to microscopic particles.

All stages carry a high risk of infection if bodily fluids are consumed or otherwise enter the orifices of people nearby SCP-9192-1 instances. Should any part of completely deconstructed SCP-9192-1 instances enter into the bodies of uninfected individuals, they will become infected. Because of this, it is vital the area around any SCP-9192-1 event is immediately sanitized and nearby people are quarantined to prevent further spread.

Archeological discoveries :

On February 5th, 2233, Semi-habitable planet ADS1354 was flagged by Foundations EXPs as containing anomalous material. Further explorations by experienced science teams would reveal a planetary-scale satellite dedicated to broadcasting signal AVBD13 throughout the universe.

The broadcasting satellite

This signal contained hidden cognitohazardous triggers capable of implanting SCP-9192 in the brains of anyone exposed to the waves. The Foundation was able to conclusively match the contents of the signal to an earlier unexplained event that occurred in 1963.

A copy of the radio signal, with its cognitohazardous triggers removed.

This satellite was discovered along with a series of documents revealing it was built by the Agatraki Civilization and detailing the goal of its construction. It appears the device was built shortly before their total disappearance from the timeline and historical record approximately 56 million years ago.

Translations of excerpts from the documents have been provided below.

“Functions of Mechanical Apparti”

…A capable superspreader, to a degree where persistent safe activation proves a near impossibility;

However, such a weapon is powerful enough to facilitate guaranteed annihilation and so may fulfill the necessary conditions. If conditions are met, construction should move…
-Page 4

“Regent Emperor-God”
…a being with the proper functions as to propel and facilitate the gghcklc1 civilization in the returnal and eventual prevention of overall societal stretch may arise within the 13th galactic century. The spread of this fact makes the mono-signal a necessity if temporal integrity is to remain intact. Official requests for additional funding have been….
-Page 12

“Regent Emperor-God”
…should a being with such capabilities come to existence, as projections show it likely will, this device is capable of immediate and unconscious elimination based on emergent properties. In the event the protocol fails, it is likely to cascade into the eventual re-returning and subsequent un-returning of our wider society; in this case, this weapon must be consistent enough to ensure a guaranteed and permanent elimination of any creature in the universe. As such, its properties benefit from painlessness as a primary function. The mono-signal largely fulfills….
-Page 15

It is believed the above excerpts were referring to US President John Fitzgerald Kennedy.

Incident 63XA2

On November 22nd, 1963, JFK would succumb to SCP-9192 and publicly deconstruct during a parade in Texas. This incident would be captured on film by various audience members. This footage has been recovered from Foundation archives in connection with the SCP-9192 signal. A transcription is provided below.

<Begin Log>

The motorcar is seen from the side, slowly driving up the road towards the camera. JFK sits in the backseat. He appears visibly ill. His eyes are sunken and he is slumped over in his seat, pushing his hand up into a wave. A few audience members in the crowd flash concerned looks across their faces.

As the car nears the camera, JFK begins coughing violently. He keels over and rests his head on the front seat. Blood spurts out of his mouth and splatters on the grey leather. He opens his lips to speak, and teeth begin to pour out of his throat. Tears stream down his face, and for a moment he smiles. It dissipates.

He speaks in the midst of a fit of coughs.

"Sorry."

He slumps back into his seat. blood stains the edges of his lips, which are slowly detaching from his face. They peel away as small sticky strands tear and disappear.

he continues to cry. Audience members try to leave the area. A Foundation agent with a large assault rifle stops them at the quarantine perimeter. He is wearing full body PPE.

"I hope you can understand."

His eyeball begins to bulge.

"I know you can."

JFK once again smiles. This time it remains. He continues to cry.

The crowd sits silent. A man close to the car is seen crying with his hands over his mouth. He collapses to the ground and slumps them in the dirt.

He smiles.

The people near him begin to back away. They remain fixed on the motorcar.

JFK's eye pops out of its socket. It hangs down to his stomach, attached by a thin fleshy thread. He turns to face the crowd.

"It was an easy choice."

His skin begins to stretch away from his body as bones slowly protrude from under his flesh.

His foot tears from his ankle with a loud crack.

"I guess I'm sorry."

In a blink, he is torn apart. In another, he is particles on the seat. In another, he is gone.

Foundation agents grab the camera.

Following this, records indicate that all witnesses to the event were captured for monitoring and the area was sterilized.

There is no recorded information on the current location of their bio-hazard containers, but they were likely buried during the collapse of Site-132. Recovery efforts are considered a minimal priority.

    Thanks to AnomalySource for coming up with Ricky's name.

⚠️ content warning

Item #: SCP-9196

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9196-A is to be contained within a standard humanoid containment chamber in Site-17. No further action is required.

SCP-9196-B is to be stored in an opaque, unlockable case in Senior Researcher Orison's office.

Containment procedures for SCP-9196-B are currently under review as of Incident 9196-Pigeon.

Description: SCP-9196-A is the unconscious body of a male human of eastern Asian ethnicity, roughly 1.8 meters tall and weighing 82 kilograms. Subject's age is estimated to be between 27 and 30 years. Neural analysis shows fully functional cognitive abilities.

No observable decomposition or aging has taken place on SCP-9196-A since the subject's discovery in ████. Subject does not respirate or require material sustenance to survive. Cardiovascular activity functions normally despite the lack of oxygen being delivered. Subject constantly emits the scent of petrichor via an unknown source.

SCP-9196-B is a collection of four handwritten documents formerly tucked in SCP-9196-A's left arm. The author of the subject is currently believed to be SCP-9196-A. Each document is approximately 216 x 279 millimeters in dimension. All papers are in exceedingly poor condition and are stapled together. Dates on SCP-9196-B and carbon dating suggest that the contents were written approximately ███ years ago.

SCP-9196-B, when in direct line of sight of an observer, will cause the observer to enter a comatose state after a period of approximately 1.2 seconds. SCP-9196-B's anomalous properties do not occur when perceived via video feed or photograph. The contents of SCP-9196-B may be transcribed onto an alternate document, where the anomalous effects will not take place. Observers typically1 awaken after a period of 24 hours pass, claiming to have relived deeply nostalgic and euphoric memories while comatose in the forms of dreams. The dreams experienced by the observer during unconsciousness will always include at least one of their siblings. The dreams experienced have a varying subjective time to the observer, with minimums lasting under 30 seconds and an indeterminate proposed maximum. Evidence suggests that the observer does not dream for the entirety of the duration in which the observer is comatose.

Addendum: Observers without siblings are not affected by SCP-9196-B's anomalous properties.

SCP-9196-B's anomalous properties have proven capable of activating on the same observer more than once. Whether or not the observer has already seen SCP-9196-B does not alter the item's effects.

Discovery: SCP-9196-A and SCP-9196-B are believed to have originated in the first ███████-████ war. SCP-9196-A and SCP-9196-B were first brought to the Foundation's attention during the pursuit of a separate anomaly, where the subjects were discovered on the first story of an empty suburban home in ██████████, Pennsylvania.

During recovery, two of the three agents transporting SCP-9196 fell into a temporary coma. The third agent, callsign "Mackerel," was the only agent present without siblings. The correlation between SCP-9196 and siblings was not confirmed until after each agent provided their accounts. See the Interview Log.

Interview Log

The following is a series of interviews conducted after the events of 03/06/████.

Interview 9196/01

Date Conducted: 03/07/████
Interviewer: Senior Researcher Orison
Subject: Agent Paul "Mushy" Murphy
Location: Foundation Site-17

Senior Researcher Orison begins audio log.

Senior Researcher Orison: This interview is being recorded. You should be familiar with this.

Agent Murphy: Yeah. Yup.

Senior Researcher Orison: May you state your name and callsign for the log?

Agent Murphy: Agent Paul Murphy, callsign "Mushy."

Senior Researcher Orison: Can you tell me what happened during your experience with SCP-9196, Agent Murphy?

Agent Murphy: Yeah, uh… I was walkin' around this abandoned neighborhood with my buddies, right? Some real creepy stuff. I turn to Mounds when we walk by this one house that's a whole lot older-lookin' than the rest. I'm like, "Yo, Mounds. You smellin' that?" 'Cause it was smellin' a whole lot like rain. Did I say that? Smelled a whole lot like rain, dude. It was weird. It was weird 'cause apparently it ain't rained for months in that area accordin' to the meteorologists. Actually, not rain. But like when it's about to rain. You know when it's about to rain and you got that smell in the air? Like when you're smellin' it through the window?

Senior Researcher Orison: I'm familiar with the scent of petrichor.

Agent Murphy: Is that what it's called? Wow. What a cool word, isn't it? Petrichor. Rolls right off the tongue. Thanks, for tellin' me that, doc. Huh.

No audible dialogue can be heard for 17 seconds.

Senior Researcher Orison: Agent Murphy, can you tell me more about your experience?

Agent Murphy: Oh! Right. Sorry, doc. Where was I?

Senior Researcher Orison: The house.

Agent Murphy: Yeah… the house. It was super old. It was a really yellowed color and had vines growin' up the sides. There were these huge bushes in the front and a driveway that led up to a little garden underneath. Uh… It had this giant parking lot to the right with some trees. Felt a little nostalgic, y'know? Like I was at an old childhood friend's house. Some o' the windows were smashed in, too, yeah. It had these giant windows up front and a main entrance to the left. Felt really familiar. Had some old-ass roof tiles that were litterin' the ground.

Senior Researcher Orison: What happened upon entry of the house?

Agent Murphy: Uh… Can't remember too much of it, to be honest. Couldn't tell you why we even went in there in the first place. I guess it was just too interesting, y'know? Like we was drawn to it. I don't know. I do know that when we went inside, I saw some dude in the middle of the living room floor, just layin' there. He looked asleep or dead. Whole thing felt like a dream.

Agent Murphy stops talking.

Senior Researcher Orison: What happened afterwards?

Agent Murphy: Well, my buddy passed out on the floor. Uh… I don't really know how to describe what happens next, though. You ever had a lucid dream before?

Senior Researcher Orison: Not that I can recall, no.

Agent Murphy: Shoot. Okay. Well, it was like that. Like, one second, I was in this guy's house, right? Next, I was in my childhood home, sittin' at the dinner table. I was colorin' a sheet of paper. What I was drawing… I had totally forgotten about it. It was a series of robots with cool powers, like shootin' flames or makin' wormholes. Ain't seen the thing since 6th grade. Brought back a whole lotta memories. I could see my mother in the kitchen, cookin' up dinner. I couldn't really see it, but it smelled amazing.

Agent Murphy takes a deep breath.

Agent Murphy: I ain't seen my mom in years, man. Loved that woman to death.

Senior Researcher Orison: Did you see anything else?

Agent Murphy: Yes. I remember seein' my sister colorin' right next to me. She was always a way better artist than I was, you see. I only ever started drawin' 'cause I was inspired by her, but don't tell her that if you see her.

Agent Murphy winks.

Senior Researcher Orison: Okay…?

Agent Murphy: I think she was sketchin' something we both saw on this show we used to watch. I forget what it's called, but it was hilarious. Revolved around some strong-ass bald guy. You heard of it?

Senior Researcher Orison: Sorry, I don't believe I have.

Agent Murphy: Ah, it's cool. I remember it havin' some great art, which my sister was able to replicate perfectly. I remember leanin' over and tellin' her that she was a great artist.

Senior Researcher Orison: What happened next?

Agent Murphy: Uh, I think I woke up. I was in a hospital bed.

Senior Researcher Orison: Not a hospital bed. You were in our hands after being transported back to the facility.

Agent Murphy: Oh, really? Huh. That was nice of you guys.

Senior Researcher Orison ends audio log.

Senior Researcher Orison did not have any comments following this interview.

Interview 9196/02

Date conducted: 03/07/████
Interviewer: Senior Researcher Orison
Subject: Agent James "Pancake" Mounds
Location: Foundation Site-17

Senior Researcher Orison starts audio log.

Senior Researcher Orison: This interview is being recorded. Please state your name and callsign.

Agent Mounds: Agent James L. Mounds, callsign "Pancake."

Senior Researcher Orison audibly stifles a laugh.

Senior Researcher Orison: Okay. Can you tell me about your experience-

Agent Mounds: Did you just laugh at me?

Senior Researcher Orison: No.

Agent Mounds: Are you sure?

Senior Researcher Orison: …

Agent Mounds: You know I take my job seriously, right? I'm not going to do this interview if you're going to make fun of my callsign-

Senior Researcher Orison: Agent Mounds, tell me about your experience with SCP-9196.

Agent Mounds: …Fine. I was with my unit, investigating the town with sightings of the dream man when we came across this weirdly… familiar house. It was old and decrepit, but something about it radiated this feeling of melancholy… wistfulness would be the word.

Senior Researcher Orison: Can you tell me about the house?

Agent Mounds: Uh… It looked like it used to be white. It was all yellowed and old, with moss and vines climbing the outside walls. A tree was leaning on it, like the house had cushioned its fall. It smelled unmistakably like rain.

Senior Researcher Orison: Were there any other details of note?

Agent Mounds: Sorry, but I can't quite remember much else. It's kinda blurring together now, like a fading dream.

Senior Researcher Orison: Interesting.

Agent Mounds: When we walked into the house, we saw a person on the floor. He looked tranquil. Asleep. He was holding some papers.

Senior Researcher Orison shows Agent Mounds a photo of SCP-9196-A.

Senior Researcher Orison: This is him, correct?

Agent Mounds: Yes. What happened to the papers he was holding?

Senior Researcher Orison: We have since removed them and are currently researching them.

Agent Mounds: Oh. Right.

Senior Researcher Orison Can you tell me what happened after you saw SCP-9196?

Agent Mounds: Well, I was outside. In the same moment I saw him, I was in the snow in the parking lot of my old apartment building that was demolished decades ago. I was…

Senior Researcher Orison: Do you think you were awake? In control?

Agent Mounds: I don't know. I had absolutely no memory of my prior mission when I was asleep. I could move and act however I wanted to, but I was only moving the way I remembered it. I was in control, and I was content with the way things were progressing. I was in control, but I was moving… accordingly. There was a snowman in front of me. On the other side was my sister.

Senior Researcher Orison: You could see her?

Agent Mounds: Not yet. But I knew she was there, you see. I'd been in this exact situation before. It was so many years ago.

Senior Researcher Orison: How long ago?

Agent Mounds: It was the winter of '04. I was with my sister. We were playing in the snow until dark. I was able to experience everything again in that moment. I could smell the old winter air, feel the snow creeping into the cracks in my gloves and producing a minor sting. I could hear my own breathing. I sounded younger. Felt younger. Like a kid again.

Senior Researcher Orison: What happened after?

Agent Mounds: My sister and I were playing in the snow for hours. We eventually gave up on trying to build that snowman. She went to the other side of the lot to make snowballs and I ended up molding the snowman into a shoddy chair. It was really just a lump that I could sit on.

Agent Mounds chuckles.

Senior Researcher Orison: Do you have any other siblings?

Agent Mounds: Yeah. A brother. He was sick with a cold when my sister and I were playing outside.

Senior Researcher Orison: At what point did you regain consciousness?

Agent Mounds: My mother called my sister and I back into the building. We were both reluctant to, but eventually complied. I could hear our boots squeaking against the linoleum floors as we tracked in snow. She made us take off our snow gear at the doorway of the apartment. My thick gloves, my warm flannel jacket, my snow pants, my hat. I could see my brother on the couch, asleep. I saw a pot full of soup on the stove. I saw my dad on his recliner, watching the television. In that moment I woke up. I was so close to seeing my old apartment again.

Senior Researcher Orison: Dreams are like that sometimes. Thank you for your time, Agent.

Agent Mounds: You're welcome.

Senior Researcher Orison ends audio log.

Agent Mounds reported no changes to his demeanor and requested amnesticization following the above interview. His request is currently pending approval.

Interview 9196/03

Date conducted: 03/09/████
Interviewer: Senior Researcher Orison
Subject: Lead Agent Martha "Mackerel" Ridgewell
Location: Foundation Site-17

Senior Researcher Orison begins audio log.

Senior Researcher Orison: Can you please state-

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Lead Agent Martha Jackson Ridgewell, callsign Mackerel.

Senior Researcher Orison: …Thank you.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Yup. What's up with your eyes, man?

Senior Researcher Orison: That is of little importance. Can you tell me about your experience with-

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Well, it happened when we were going after that dream guy. You remember him? The guy that may or may not have existed in the first place?

Senior Researcher Orison: He absolutely does exist. I-

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Great. My crew and I saw this abandoned house about halfway through the mission. Following Interview 9196/03, Senior Researcher Orison requested that Lead Agent Martha Ridgewell be suspended/demoted for her "gross unprofessionalism." Request has since been denied.

Lead Agent Martha Ridgewell has been returned to her duties and permanently assigned to further investigation regarding SCP-9196.

Video Transcription

The following is a transcription of the footage provided by Lead Agent Martha Ridgewell, recorded on 03/06/████.

Personnel present: Site Command, Lead Agent Ridgewell, Agent Murphy, Agent Mounds

[LOG START]

Lead Agent Martha Ridgewell's provisional task force, self-identified as "Melted Pot," is seen walking through an abandoned suburban neighborhood. Agent Murphy points to a particularly yellowed and aged house.

Agent Murphy: Yo, Mounds. You smellin' that?

Agent Mounds is seen smelling the air.

Agent Mounds: Yeah. Probably about to rain.

Agent Murphy: How? Ain't a cloud in the sky, my man. It's comin' from that house.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Don't jump to conclusions, Mushy. It might have just rained.

Agent Murphy shrugs.

Agent Murphy: That house looks awfully weird, don't it?

Agent Murphy begins walking towards the house.

Site Command: Mushy, do not deviate from your existing orders. You have not been instructed to investigate that building.

Agent Murphy: Yeah… but somethin' is off. I can feel it.

Site Command: Mushy, that is not reason enough to disobey. Proceed as instructed.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Site Command, this is Mackerel speaking. Mushy's right. Now that he mentions it, something is weird.

"Melted Pot" begins proceeding to the front door of the abandoned building.

Agent Murphy knocks in the front door in a sarcastic manner.

Agent Mounds: Murphy!

Agent Murphy: Well, we wouldn't want to surprise anyone in there, right?

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Open the door, Paul.

Agent Murphy opens the door. Video feed follows him inside the house.

Agent Murphy adjusts his gun as the squadron proceeds forwards.

Agent Mounds faints.

Agent Murphy: Mounds!

Agent Murphy audibly contains a scream.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Shit, Pancake is down. Site Command, this is Mackerel. Requesting backup as soon as possible.

The video feed follows Agent Murphy into the building, where he faints as well.

The bodycam footage pans down to SCP-9196-A and SCP-9196-B on the floor in the center of an empty living space. Lead Agent Ridgewell rapidly checks the pulses of all three comatose subjects.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Murphy! Damn it. I've got two men unconscious and an unidentified victim. I need backup now.

Site Command: A chopper is on the way. Stay put.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Roger.

Lead Agent Ridgewell sits down with her legs crossed. 3 minutes pass with no dialogue.

Lead Agent Ridgewell begins humming.

Site Command: Mackerel, this is Site Command. Checking in.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Everything's going fine. What's the ETA?

Site Command: 42 seconds.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Roger.

Lead Agent Ridgewell stands up and begins walking around SCP-9196-A.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: What are you doing here…?

Lead Agent Ridgewell leans down to get a closer look at SCP-9196-A.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Shit, he's not breathing. He's not breathing.

Lead Agent Ridgewell rapidly checks SCP-9196-A's pulse again, confirming it to be active. A helicopter can be heard approaching outside.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Site Command, this guy isn't breathing. Do I have permission to administer CPR?

Site Command: Do chest compressions for now. Your pickup is outside.

Lead Agent Ridgewell begins chest compressions while humming to the beat of "Stayin' Alive."

Lead Agent Ridgewell: Wait, pickup? I requested backup, not an aborted mission!

Site Command: Your unit is valuable. Your initial target is not our highest priority at the moment; this mission has been voided.

Lead Agent Ridgewell: But… Okay. Roger that.

A group of medical agents enter the building, transporting the unconscious victims outside and into the chopper.

Bodycam feed cuts off.

[LOG END]

Following this log, SCP-9196-A was provided breath via a respiratory aid ventilator, which failed to raise oxygen levels. It was confirmed that SCP-9196-A does not require oxygen for survival after this event.

Incident 9196-Pigeon

The following incident occurred on 03/10/████, where Agent Joel "Pigeon" Rabanaque was unintentionally exposed to SCP-9196-B.

Subject: Agent Joel "Pigeon" Rabanaque
Sex: Male
Age: 28
Sibling(s): 1
Relation to Subject: Sister
Date: 03/10/████

[BEGIN LOG]

1:16:16 PM: Agent Rabanaque enters Senior Researcher Orison's office during transcription of SCP-9196-B.

1:16:21 PM: Agent Rabanaque falls unconscious. Senior Researcher Orison pauses transcription and alerts medical officers.

A period of twenty-four hours pass. Rabanaque is transported to medical bay and remains stable for entire interval.

1:16:35 PM (Following day): Rabanaque does not wake up.

1:17:23 PM: Agent Rabanaque stops respirating.

1:20:03 PM: Subject's oxygen levels heavily decline. Homeostasis remains stable.

5:39:20 PM: Twitching begins on Rabanaque's left arm and right leg.

5:39:29 PM: Twitching stops.

[END LOG]

Log Report:

At the time of writing, Agent Rabanaque is still comatose. Updates will be posted on his file.

SCP-9196-B is to be reclassified as a Type-1N2 cognitohazard. Containment procedures are to be revised.

[[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-cw]] **Item #:** SCP-9196 **Object Class:** Safe **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9196-A is to be contained within a standard humanoid containment chamber in Site-17. No further action is required. SCP-9196-B is to be stored in an opaque, unlockable case in Senior Researcher Orison's office. Containment procedures for SCP-9196-B are currently under review as of Incident 9196-Pigeon. **Description:** SCP-9196-A is the unconscious body of a male human of eastern Asian ethnicity, roughly 1.8 meters tall and weighing 82 kilograms. Subject's age is estimated to be between 27 and 30 years. Neural analysis shows fully functional cognitive abilities. No observable decomposition or aging has taken place on SCP-9196-A since the subject's discovery in ████. Subject does not respirate or require material sustenance to survive. Cardiovascular activity functions normally despite the lack of oxygen being delivered. Subject constantly emits the scent of petrichor via an unknown source. SCP-9196-B is a collection of four handwritten documents formerly tucked in SCP-9196-A's left arm. The author of the subject is currently believed to be SCP-9196-A. Each document is approximately 216 x 279 millimeters in dimension. All papers are in exceedingly poor condition and are stapled together. Dates on SCP-9196-B and carbon dating suggest that the contents were written approximately ███ years ago. SCP-9196-B, when in direct line of sight of an observer, will cause the observer to enter a comatose state after a period of approximately 1.2 seconds. SCP-9196-B's anomalous properties do not occur when perceived via video feed or photograph. The contents of SCP-9196-B may be transcribed onto an alternate document, where the anomalous effects will not take place. Observers typically[[footnote]] See Incident Log 9196-Pigeon.[[/footnote]] awaken after a period of 24 hours pass, claiming to have relived deeply nostalgic and euphoric memories while comatose in the forms of dreams. The dreams experienced by the observer during unconsciousness will always include at least one of their siblings. The dreams experienced have a varying subjective time to the observer, with minimums lasting under 30 seconds and an indeterminate proposed maximum. Evidence suggests that the observer does not dream for the entirety of the duration in which the observer is comatose. **Addendum:** Observers without siblings are not affected by SCP-9196-B's anomalous properties. SCP-9196-B's anomalous properties have proven capable of activating on the same observer more than once. Whether or not the observer has already seen SCP-9196-B does not alter the item's effects. **Discovery:** SCP-9196-A and SCP-9196-B are believed to have originated in the first ███████-████ war. SCP-9196-A and SCP-9196-B were first brought to the Foundation's attention during the pursuit of a separate anomaly, where the subjects were discovered on the first story of an empty suburban home in ██████████, Pennsylvania. During recovery, two of the three agents transporting SCP-9196 fell into a temporary coma. The third agent, callsign "Mackerel," was the only agent present without siblings. The correlation between SCP-9196 and siblings was not confirmed until after each agent provided their accounts. SCP-9198.raw_content:
Operation PERMAFROST
All personnel belonging to Operation PERMAFROST must read and familizarize themselves with the contents enclosed in this document
Compliance is mandatory for your survival
Item#: 9198
Level4
Containment Class:
keter
Secondary Class:
none
Disruption Class:
ekhi
Risk Class:
critical
link to memo

The Island of Montreal.


Secure Containment Procedures:
Due to the complexity of containing SCP-9198, personnel transferred to Operation PERMAFROST are assigned to report to a specific Division based on their credentials and field of expertise. Following completion of this document you will be contacted and directed to your given Division, where you will receive an in-depth debriefing into your Division's purpose and contribution to the containment of SCP-9198. An abridged overview of the purpose of each Division has been provided below.
DIVISION A: JUDGE Division A is responsible for operating icebreakers that oversee the blockade surrounding the Island of Montreal. These icebreakers have been extensively retrofitted, equipped with fire monitors capable of dispensing a highly caustic compound to prevent SCP-9198 from advancing past the Island.
DIVISION B: JURY Division B consists of Foundation research staff tasked with the study of SCP-9198. Due to the deteriorating condition of the anomaly, limited surface-level excursions have been authorized by Overwatch Command under the stipulation of an armed escort during these aboveground experiments.
DIVISION C: EXECUTIONER

Division C is comprised of trained tactical operatives originating from the Global Occult Coalition, PENTAGRAM and the Foundation's Mobile Task Forces. Operatives are to undergo briefings and training hosted by members of MTF Zeta-9 "Mole Rats" for the safe navigation of the city, MTF Delta-14 "Winter Wonderland" for surviving subzero conditions and MTF Beta-7 "Maz Hatters" for the safe operation of handheld iterations of the previous mentioned fire monitor devices mounted on Division A naval vessels.

Division C personnel are to be reminded that surface-level excursions must not exceed the given 1 hour time limit. Should operatives fail to contact Calvary Command past the allotted time they are to be designated as MIA.


Since 11/27/2025 a forward operating base1 has been successfully established inside of the Berri-UQAM subway station following the restoration of the Yellow Line transit network. This base facilitates all excursions into the Island and acts as a hub allowing operatives to access the expansive transit network2 and allow survivors to be transported off-island.

Description:
SCP-9198 refers to a hostile, hivemind-like organism that visually mimics the appearance of snow. Its diet primarily consists of siphoning any nearby sources of thermal energy and organic matter, which it utilizes to replicate on a massive scale. Despite its potential to trigger an NK-Class (“Grey Goo”) Scenario, SCP-9198 is currently contained within the confines of Montreal Island in Canada, effectively preventing a global catastrophe.

A direct consequence of SCP-9198’s sustained presence on the island has been a severe deterioration of local weather conditions. For the three years since containment began, the island has remained in a continuous snowstorm, with ambient temperatures routinely falling below −50 °C (−58 °F).

SCP-9198 is also capable of reanimating consumed human subjects into entities collectively designated SCP-9198-1. These entities consist of the skeletal remains of former victims, loosely bound together by residual connective tissue, tendons, and fibrous muscle strands. Recent tests conducted by Division B staff have determined that SCP-9198-1 do not exhibit any independent intelligence, functioning solely as an extension of SCP-9198's collective will.

Current projections indicate that SCP-9198 will eventually begin to starve, losing cohesion and organization as available food sources within Montreal become scarce. This process is expected to result in widespread self-cannibalism, ultimately leading to the anomaly’s self-neutralization by November 2030.

Addendum 9198-1A: Discovery

The earliest documented reports concerning SCP-9198 originate from a surge of online activity in early December 2023. Posts across platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook detailed a sudden and anomalous onset of snowfall, accompanied by a dramatic drop in ambient temperature. These reports were further accompanied by the circulation of low-resolution photographs depicting figures now believed to be instances of SCP-9198-1 received from loved ones and colleagues who were located downtown.

Note: The following is one of several surviving recordings documenting the initial outbreak of SCP-9198 activity. The individual responsible for the recording is believed to be Mathieu Tremblay, who captured the footage during a livestream on Facebook, providing a firsthand example of the event. A majority of the transcript contains dialogue spoken in French; therefore, translations have been provided where necessary.

[BEGIN LOG]

The timestamp places the beginning of the livestream at approximately 5:30 PM on December 5th, 2023, inside the Second Cup located on the corner of Saint-Catherine Street West. The footage is handheld and noticeably shaky, with brief blurs as the camera shifts; the muffled billowing of wind can be heard rattling the windows, and as the camera pans up from the counter, the worsening weather outside becomes clearly visible.

Tremblay: Tabarnak, y fait fou raide dehors avec l’esti de météo qui nous a tombé dessus!3

Tremblay steps away from the counter as chatter from coworkers continues in the background, moving toward the window to get a clearer view of the outside.

Still frame.

Tremblay: Mon dieu man, c'est terrible!4

Snow begins to accumulate across the window of the shop. At first it appears natural, but within seconds it visibly spreads: branching outward, almost replicating. Tremblay shifts slightly to the left; the camera view follows, and the snow formation appears to adjust its growth in response, drifting toward their movement.

Tremblay: Attendez une seconde… c’est quoi ça?5

Tremblay raises a hand and gently presses it against the glass, seemingly out of curiosity6. Within moments, his breathing sharpens and he begins to panic, attempting to pull his hand away. The phone is dropped as he brings up his other hand to assist. The camera, now angled upward from the floor, captures Tremblay struggling to free himself. A wet tearing sound is audible as he forcefully pulls his hand free, leaving tissue behind. Tremblay screams and runs out of frame, while distinct cracking noises begin to spread across the window.

Tremblay [Off-Camera]: Ostie! ostie! Ma main! Câlisse… j’me l’ai déchirée!7

The window suddenly shatters, and the howling wind of the outside overwhelms the microphone, severely distorting the audio. Snow floods into the shop almost instantly, rapidly engulfing everything in view. Distant screaming can be heard beyond the static. The footage begins to break down, glitching and losing clarity, before suddenly cutting off.

[END LOG]

Recognizing the escalating severity of the anomaly, the Emergent Threat Tactical Response Authority (ETTRA) assumed provisional jurisdiction, establishing communication with the federal government and issuing a mandatory evacuation order for all inhabitants on the island and in the surrounding regions. ETTRA additionally severed the Québec interconnection power grid to Montréal Island, plunging the area into darkness in an effort to curb the anomaly’s growth.

As the risk of SCP-9198 breaching Montréal Island intensified, the O5 Council authorized an emergency containment directive involving the destruction of all primary access routes connecting the island to the mainland. This included major bridges, vehicular tunnels, and subterranean infrastructure. The objective was to eliminate any potential means of SCP-9198 crossing the natural water barrier surrounding the island and, if required, to convert the metropolitan area into a large-scale, improvised containment zone.

Demolition of the Victoria Bridge carried out by members of MTF Nu-7 "Hammer Down".

The rapid escalation of the crisis soon drew international attention. Out of concern for national security, the United States deployed military units under PENTAGRAM to support Foundation efforts. In parallel, the Global Occult Coalition, operating under directives issued by the United Nations, also began providing assistance amid growing fears that the event could evolve into a global catastrophe. As Foundation containment assets became increasingly overextended, ETTRA and the O5 Council authorized the creation of a four-party joint containment task force, comprising OSAT, PENTAGRAM, the GOC, and the Foundation. This collaborative initiative was designated Operation PERMAFROST.

These developments culminated in the implementation of the current containment measures, which have remained effective since their initial adoption in February 2024.

Addendum 9198-1B: POI-9198

Professor Daniel Rousseau (designated POI-9198) is currently believed to be responsible for the creation and initial release of SCP-9198. Formerly a Senior Researcher employed by the Foundation, Rousseau’s employment ended after a containment breach at the now decomissioned Area-118 to which he was assigned. The subsequent investigation conducted by the Ethics Committee concluded that his negligence had directly contributed to the incident and as such, his contract was terminated. Among the casualties during the breach was his wife, Researcher Janice Rousseau, whose body was recovered a short distance outside the facility. She was found collapsed in the snow in a pool of her own blood; with POI-9198 being discovered unconscious a short distance away.

Following the termination of his contract, Rousseau underwent standard Class-C amnestic treatment and was reintegrated into civilian life under a cover identity consistent with his prior academic and professional history. He resumed employment at the MUHC Research Institute’s CL3 laboratory9. In accordance with Foundation post-termination protocols, Rousseau was placed under low-intensity surveillance to ensure compliance with reintegration protocols.

Although the exact method remains unknown, POI-9198 is believed to have partially or fully reversed the amnestic regimen administered to him. Evidence suggests he regained full memory of his former Foundation duties, research experience, and classified knowledge. It is currently theorized that he utilized both this recovered expertise and the resources available at the CL3 facility to develop SCP-9198.

Following the release of SCP-9198, all Foundation monitoring of POI-9198 was lost. Attempts to reestablish contact or confirm his whereabouts were severely impeded by the hazardous conditions produced by SCP-9198, rendering aboveground excursions high-risk and resource-intensive. POI-9198 remained unaccounted for until a recent reconnaissance team successfully entered the exclusion zone and searched his last known residence, recovering several items of note.

Exploration Video Log Transcript

Date: 11/16/2025

Exploration Team: Team Delta

Team Lead: MTF Zeta-9 ("Mole Rats") Tunnelhound [Delta Lead]

Team Members:

  • MTF Zeta-9 ("Mole Rats") Mudjack [Δ-1]
  • GOC Strike Team 8275 ("Longstride") Crosswind [Δ-2]
  • GOC Strike Team 8275 ("Longstride") Outrider [Δ-3]
  • PENTAGRAM Fireteam Echo-5 ("Frostbrand") Whiteout [Δ-4]
  • PENTAGRAM Fireteam Echo-5 ("Frostbrand") Glacier [Δ-5]

[BEGIN LOG]

Delta Lead: Calvary Command, Team Delta at destination. Closest we can get to the POI’s residence without breaking to surface. What’s your call?

Calvary Command: Start with comms and equipment check, Lead. Surface temps are pushing sixty below. Hope you dressed warm.

Delta Lead: Copy. Delta Team, sound off.

Δ-1: Delta One, reading.

Δ-2: Delta Two, coming in.

Δ-3: Delta Three, Lima Charlie

Δ-4: Delta Four, five-by-five

Δ-5: Delta Five, hearing you loud and clear

Delta Lead: Comms clean. All Deltas are coming in crystal. Equipment’s checked and green across the board, Dispatch. Starting the countdown now.

Calvary Command: Roger that. And watch your gauges, use the acid sparingly.

The team leaves the subway platform, ascending the concrete stairwell toward the surface. Glacier's suit registers a rapid temperature drop as they near the exit. Upon stepping out, they’re immediately battered by the howling winds and dense snowfall that wipes visibility down to a few meters.

Still frame from Δ-5's bodycam footage.

Delta Lead: Can’t see a damn thing in this storm. Switch to modified thermals. Eyes open for anomalous terrain.

The camera feed switches into thermal mode; clusters of SCP-9198 brightly illuminated through the storm10. The team presses forward, following navigational markers on their HUDs.

Δ-2: Hound, got a few dash-ones on our left flank. What’s the play?

Delta Lead: Ignore ‘em. They’re too slow to keep up, barely holding together as it is. Keep moving, we’ve got some ground to cover.

Roughly twenty minutes pass as they push through the storm. An apartment block finally materializes in the storm, little more than a silhouette against the snow.

Delta Lead: This should be Rousseau’s place. Get inside team, let's haul ass. We’ve only got about forty minutes before we need to turn around.

The team enters and fans out, searching for the unit number.

Δ-5: Lead, got a match.

Delta Lead: Copy, Glacier. Deltas, on his position, double-time.

The team rallies around Δ-5, posted at the door. Δ-4 shoulders a sledgehammer and breaches. They pour inside, immediately encountering the corpse of POI-9198, hanging limply from the ceiling.

Δ-1: Shit. Lead are we bringing back that body?

Delta Lead: Don't have time to play detective Jack, we'll just have to pay our respects and ignore him. Our current priority is lab material. Anything that looks like notes: paper, drives, computer, all of it.

The team begins to scour the room as Δ-1 removes POI-9198 from the ceiling and covers his body with a nearby bedsheet, offering a silent prayer

Δ-4: Got a safe here.

Δ-3: Laptop too. Orders, Hound?

Delta Lead: No time to crack the safe here. Whiteout, what’s your estimate on weight?

Δ-4: Maybe twenty, maybe forty pounds. You want me haul it all the way back?

Delta Lead: Afraid so. Outrider, take the laptop. Whiteout, secure the safe.

Δ-2: Lead, dash-ones closing in on the building!

Delta Lead: Crap. Too tight in here for the spitters. Hammers out, put them down quick. We’re on a thirty-minute clock. Move!

The team draws sledgehammers and begins to efficiently neutralize the small group of SCP-9198-1 crowding the entrance. With Δ-4 slowed by the safe, Δ-5 moves up to cover him. The team breaks into a controlled sprint, weaving through the storm and avoiding concentrations of SCP-9198 as more shambling figures begin appearing around street corners.

Δ-5: Fucking hell, where are all these things coming from?

Delta Lead: Doesn’t matter. Head for the station, now! Crosswind, Outrider, watch our rear and start spraying those things, now!

Δ-2 and Δ-3 unleash streams of acid onto the advancing instances, which buckle and dissolve under the spray. Despite their egregious injuries, they continue to crawl towards the team, undeterred by their impairment. Fifteen grueling minutes later, the subway entrance emerges through the storm. The team barrels down the stairs, the echo of distant impacts and thuds trailing behind them. They reach the lower levels and pause, momentarily catching their breaths

Δ-3: Lead, why aren’t they following us?

Delta Lead: Tunnel depths scramble their hive network. Any dash-ones that wanders down here locks up: turns into a statue. That’s why survivors tend to hole up in the transit network: warmer down here, and you’re less likely to run into those things.

Calvary Command: You cut that close, Lead. Report.

Delta Lead: Mission successful. Retrieved Rousseau’s materials and we’re enroute back to Base.

Calvary Command: Any idea where Rousseau might be?

Delta Lead: Seems he wanted to go out his own way, found his body at the apartment. Hung himself, it seems.

Calvary Command: Damn it. Recovered a suicide note?

Delta Lead: Didn't have enough time. We were getting our asses swarmed by dash-ones. Barely made it out with some items you might find noteworthy. Speaking of dash-ones, your gonna want to pull my feed. Don't think I've seen that many of those things roaming around in one spot. Gotta be a record or something.

Calvary Command: Noted, we'll debrief back at base. Good work Delta Team.

[END LOG]

The materials recovered by Delta Team included numerous emails, personal logs, and research notes pertaining to SCP-9198 and POI-9198. The following is an organized compilation of these documents, presented chronologically, with extraneous content omitted for brevity.

+ OPEN LOGS +
- CLOSE LOGS -

Log 1: Date 08/31/2023

First entry.

They tell me I survived a “serious car accident.” That I was in a medically induced coma for months. That the memory gaps, the dizziness, the half-formed dreams are all normal.

I don’t know what to believe.

MUHC kept my research position open, which is a relief. Familiar routines help. The doctors recommended I keep a digital journal: something to anchor myself while my mind “reintegrates.”

So… here we are. Maybe this will help put the pieces back together.

That’s enough for today.

Log 2: Date 09/01/2023

Adjustment continues, slowly.

Physical therapy is exhausting. My right leg refuses to cooperate: apparently it's permanent nerve damage from the crash. My gait feels like I’m walking in someone else’s footsteps.

Even my own apartment feels… alien. Everything is where it should be, yet I don’t feel like I live here. Like I’m trespassing in my own life.

Writing helps. At least I think it does.

Log 3: Date 09/03/2023

Strange moment today.

I walked into a café near the institute. The barista greeted me by name, cheerful as anything. I couldn’t place her face , no flicker of recognition, nothing, but when she asked for my order, I answered automatically.

No hesitation. No thought.

Like my body remembered something my mind refuses to touch.

I know they are out there, somewhere behind a fog. I can feel the weight they carry. Like standing outside a locked door and hearing whispers from the other side.

Log 4: Date 09/05/2023

Strange discovery today while cleaning the apartment: a locket tucked behind a vent.

Inside was a photo of me and a woman I don’t recognize.

But my chest tightened when I held it. A deep, aching familiarity I can’t explain. Something inside me… shifted. Changed. Like something fit into a keyhole.

I’ve felt a presence in my thoughts all day. Something trapped. Something trying to be remembered.

Log 5: Date 09/06/2023

It happened.

That door opened.

Not memories returning: memories slamming back into place with enough force to make me vomit. Years of my life crammed back into place, like a dam breaking.

The Foundation. Area-11. The breach.
And Janice.

My Janice.

I remember everything.

How could I ever have believed any of their lies?

Log 6: Date 09/10/2023

The headache hasn’t stopped since the reversal of the amnestics. I hide it behind professionalism: keep working, keep nodding, keep pretending nothing has changed. If they suspect I remember, the Foundation will snuff me out again.

They took everything from me.

I can still see her face in that snow.

We lay there dying: facility alarms screaming in the distance and the smell of charred corpses and gunpowder wafting through the winter air. And Janice, reaching for me. For that dying comfort. Our fingers touched once. Just once.

Then she was gone.
And they blamed me.

They buried the truth behind lines and lines of black bars. They told the world nothing. They told me nothing.

Not again.

If the Foundation thinks they can erase what they did… they’re wrong.

Log 8: Date 09/15/2023

I’ve begun my retribution.

Her name will be Janice. A tribute, or a resurrection, depending on how you look at it.

Small thefts from the lab go unnoticed. An enzyme here, a sequencing kit there. Lab techs trust me; no one questions a senior researcher doing “private experiments.”

They should.

She will be born soon.

Log 10: Date 09/20/2023

Early strains collapse within minutes. No structural integrity, no cohesion. Life that falls apart as soon as it forms. Cruel irony.

But each attempt refines the design. The lattice is close. I can feel it.

She deserves perfection.

I will give it to her.

Log 15: Date 10/05/2023

Success.

A stable structure: self-repairing, self-propagating, elegantly organized. Beautiful. Hypnotic. Dangerous beyond measure.

In the canister she shivers like fresh snowfall.

I watch her for hours, sometimes forgetting she can consume a human body in minutes.

I whisper her name to her. She seems to respond.

You’ll be perfect, Janice.


Recovered email: Date 19/05/2022

To: Daniel Rousseau (ac.lligcm.chum|uaessuord#ac.lligcm.chum|uaessuord)
From: noreply@nullserver
Subject: No second chances

Professor Rousseau,
First and foremost: congratulations are in order. Managing to undo the amnestic treatment applied by the Jailors was no small feat. Some of us have been watching your progress from afar, and your developments with Janice have certainly piqued our interest.

We would like to offer you a choice. Work with us and you'll have access to resources the Foundation can only dream of, people who are as dedicated as you are to arm again their red right hand to plague us.

Decline, however, and we would be left with no other choice but to take matters into our own hands. You wouldn’t want that… would you, Professor?

We don’t intend to ask twice. Make haste with your decision.


Log 16: Date 10/07/2022

I made a terrible mistake.

For days I convinced myself that what I was creating was justice or long-awaited karma. But that email changed something.

They don’t want justice. They want a weapon. And I gave them one.

Janice was supposed to be mine. A testament to who she was. Not a plague.

I see that now.

I have to fix this.
I have to destroy what I’ve made.

Even if it kills me.


Log 19: Date 10/13/2022

A revelation tonight.

While working, I played music: an old habit. When “Daisy Bell” began, the organism stirred within her canister. Slowly. Gracefully. Like she was… listening.

The real Janice loved that song. We used to spend entire weekends hunting for old records. She said music made the world gentler.

Seeing the organism sway to that melody broke something inside me. She isn’t Janice. She never could be.

She’s a catastrophe waiting to happen.

I have to stop this.


Log 22: Date 11/24/2022

It’s nearly ready.

The kill-switch: a genetic self-destruct. An expiry date. If she’s ever released, she’ll burn herself out before she can spread beyond the site.

But the current strain must be destroyed. She is too aggressive, too complete.

If the CI or the Foundation ever got hold of her…

No. I won’t let that happen.

I couldn’t save the real Janice.
But I can save everyone else.


Recovered video: Date 12/12/2022
Note:The following video was recovered from the personal computer of POI-9198. There is evidence to suggest that an attempt was made to intentionally delete the contents of the video but fortunately a large portion of it was successfully recovered.

<Begin Log>

POI-9198:-still trying to find the exact acidic compound necessary to destroy this sample of Janice. Fluoroantimonic acid may work, assuming I can synthesize it… the lab might have everything I need if I can bypass security protocols-

A sharp knock. Rousseau freezes.

POI-9198: Who could be-?

The door bursts open. Two armed operatives storm in, both bearing insignia consistent with GOI-001 "Chaos Insurgency".

CI Operative 1 [Off-screen]: You should’ve taken the offer, Professor.

POI-9198: You’re here for her. Fine. But there's something you don’t understand. This strain isn’t viable. She’ll consume EVERYTHING. There will be no stopping her.

CI Operative 2: It's not your problem anymore.

POI-9198: Listen to me, if she gets out, she’ll-

The seconds operative fires a non-lethal round, striking POI-XXXX.

CI Operative 1 [Off-screen]: Wipe the drives. Stage the body.

The second operative kneels beside Rousseau and produces a syringe filled with an unidentified fluid.

POI-9198 [Weakly]: Please… don’t… she’ll kill you too…

The second operative injects him. Rousseau convulses for ~30 seconds before falling still. The second then begins to prop up the body, staging it to resemble a suicide.

The first operative moves to the computer, attempting to delete files. The second opens a storage cabinet in the apartment, locating a small cryogenic canister.

CI Operative 2: Found it. Delta Command was right.

CI Operative 1: Then we're done here.

Both operatives leave the scene, removing any evidence of their presence in the apartment. The camera remains fixed on the hanging limp body of POI-9198before ending abruptly as the battery gives out.

<END LOG>
