    SCP-9201: ACID
    Alternative Title: Rollback
    Author: aismallard (Author Page)

    Thanks to stormbreath Yossipossi and Tufto for their feedback.

In database design, ACID is an acronym which refers to a system obeying certain capabilities: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

  • Atomicity: All changes to the database take place within transactions. A transaction must succeed completely or not at all. If it fails, it must be entirely rolled back. It must not be possible for the system to write incomplete data.
  • Consistency: All data must obey the constraints and restrictions described by the database's schema. For instance, if a field is marked as unique, no two items may have the same value for that field.
  • Isolation: The system must be able to handle many transactions occurring at the same time. Uncommitted transaction effects must not be "visible" to other operations occurring within the database.
  • Durability: Once a transaction has been successfully written, the data must be durable. At that point, even a system crash should not prevent data from being recoverable.

For mundane forms of information, designing systems which exhibit these properties can be challenging enough. However, here at the Foundation we deal with self-modifying data, retroactive anomalies, and all manner of infohazards, which makes ACID compliance seem impossible.

This is not to say, of course, that we have not succeeded.

— Introduction to RAISA Database Systems, Ninth Edition

Item #: SCP-9201

Object Class: Thaumiel

Special Containment Procedures: Access to SCP-9201-A units is restricted per the Foundation Paratechnology Equipment Policy. Field agents who are Level-3 and above are eligible for access, as are anomaly researchers when overseen by Level-4 oversight staff.

Use of SCP-9201-A is governed by Foundation Containment Policy. As a piece of standard equipment, approval of containment actions is managed by the Containment Command System (CCS).

Installation and management of SCP-9201-B units is overseen by the RAISA Records & Archival Office.

Description: SCP-9201 is the Foundation Reality Transaction Manager (FRTM), a piece of paratechnology which enables ACID transaction processing on a piece of local reality. Due to its immense power requirements and the difficulty of properly determining conceptual parameters, effective use for Foundation operations is challenging.

The primary use of the FRTM is in SCP-9201-A, the Foundation Field Anomaly Analyzer (FFAA). This 47 kilogram device interfaces with an internally-installed limited-use SCP-9201 instance. The FFAA has been programmed to accept nearby spatial coordinates and generic conceptual information, or alternatively, an SCP database number.

When provided input data and activated, the device initializes a transaction on the specified parameters: any changes to reality proceed as expected, until SCP-9201-A closes the transaction with one of two possible actions:

  • Commit — If committed, then any changes made within the region are preserved. This "accepts" the changes to reality since the start of the transaction.
  • Rollback — If rolled back, then reality within the inputted parameter region is reset to the state it was at the time the transaction was initiated. However, note that only the reality captured by the transaction is rolled back. For instance, if a transaction is programmed to capture only biological entities and metals, then any destruction to nearby non-metallic infrastructure will remain after rollback.

Partial commits and rollbacks are not possible due to the atomicity guarantee of SCP-9201. Instead, operators should fine-tune which aspects of reality are captured (and thus, resettable) and which are unaffected through use of precise parameter specification.

Oh, you've never seen a debugger in-person before now, huh? Nah, nobody calls it the "Field Anomaly Analyzer", and "FAA" is too confusing with that one agency.

Have you used one before? No I mean the normal kind, for computers. I guess it makes sense, seeing as you studied memetics. Well, uh let's see, how to explain it…

It's kind of like this, right? You're studying a car crash. Something in the design of the vehicle was flawed or insufficient as it went over this particular road.

So what a debugger does is it lets you replay the car crash, but in slow motion. You can pause it, look around, change stuff: see how hot the engine's burning, tweak the axle strength, and oh hey you found it! One instant where there's too much weight on a slightly deflated tire.

Now unfortunately we don't have any gizmo you can just point out a skip that tells you about its guts, let alone change it however you want. But by capturing it in a transaction and retrying again and again, crashing that car over and over, we can learn an awful lot.

SCP-9201's transactional capture ability also applies to itself. If an SCP-9201-A unit is present within a conceptual capture at the time of transaction start, then any actions taken by that unit (including the creation of sub-transactions) can themselves be committed or reverted.

Due to its isolation guarantee, the events from one transaction are not able to affect events in an unrelated, non-intersecting transaction. The way this will manifest for observers outside both transactions can be difficult to predict and can lead to anomalous manifestations or bodily harm. For this reason, such configurations are not recommended.

When utilized properly, SCP-9201-A is useful for a variety of containment-related tasks. Common tasks include initial containment operations, performing extended experimentation, and limiting or negating the effects of containment breaches.

Initial containment is a motherfuck, that's for sure. All we get are vague reports, mostly-useless sensor readings, and if we're lucky, maybe a decent picture or audio snip. But I've survived a lot of them and I'll tell you we wouldn't contain half the shit we do without these things.

Here's how it's usually laid out. We have a wide net, covering everything in the spacetime region. This transaction is only rolled back if things go really south. Then there's the outer inner one, just inside the main cordon. Then the inner inner one. This gets the suspect scene but also all the agents who are going to go into the danger area.

So you're saying — I mean that sounds like a good idea but it doesn't work. If you put the agents in their own transaction, separate from the transaction holding the skip, and reset them if they get fucked up by it. Bad idea. They might not be able to see the anomaly. Or maybe they can but they create a "different version" of it in their little world. Or other weird stuff. Don't mess with anomalies like that. It's just not good unless you want a second, even more complicated skip to clean up.

To facilitate determination of an anomaly's full properties, stationary versions of SCP-9201-A units have been installed in many containment and research chambers, with pre-tuning for the anomaly being studied. Through use of the Keppler-Gray methodology, 43% of SCP items and 98% of miscellaneous anomalous objects have known SCP-9201 conceptual parameters.

Once an anomaly's loose conceptual parameter space is known, comprehensive testing can be performed at much lower risk than without SCP-9201 use. A contained object can be exposed to a variety of stimuli, forms of sapient interaction, and other tests within the Foundation's extensive test battery and reset after each experiment. For more social anomalies, rollbacks might occur less frequently, to determine how its behavior varies with its treatment and containment conditions.

You know, I'm thinking, your point about resetting people — not like that but it's actually pretty normal for a lot of task forces, including ours. We got these perfect conceptual definitions for regular humans, non-anomalous materials, and most of the Foundation's standard equipment. So sometimes we've got these live fire exercises where everyone is put inside a transaction, we blow each other up, and it all gets reset at the end. Except for memories, because those can be excluded. More experience.

Yeah. It's why most agents are jaded fucks.

Permanent SCP-9201-A installations are also invaluable for avoiding and analyzing containment breaches. With a precise conceptual capture, escaped anomalies can simply be rolled back to their pre-breach state, leaving only facility damage. In situations where a looser capture is maintained, some anomalous residue may be left, which can be studied during the cleanup process. Occasionally, such study yields insights on determining more precise conceptual bounds on the SCP object.

However, note that improper bounding is often worse than no transactional containment at all. Most conceptual specifications for SCP-9201 are incredibly complex and their myriad interactions even more so. Capturing an anomaly using an incomplete definition means that, when rolled back or committed, any of its effects on reality may be uncompensated for or doubly-compensated for. This can cause objects to become inaccessible, duplicated, split, imperceivable, excessively-perceivable, and risks outright containment breaches or the formation of new anomalies.

God, yeah, I remember that incident. No you're exactly right — if you ask me, this is the most important thing to understand about our debuggers. Finding out the exact parameters is a pain in the ass, and in some cases we just can't.

Like we've given up trying to use 'em on Daevite stuff. Maybe because it's retroactive like 9201 is, or maybe it's something else we don't know yet, but it never goes well. They also aren't super great for memetics too, which is why I'm glad you're joining the team. They can reset people just like amnestics reset their memories, but that's mostly it.

Oh yeah, here's the handbook. It actually has a huge-ass list of prohibited anomalies and concepts. Includes some weird ones too, like a few brands of natto and dreams about Neptune's moons. Those require site director approval.

Anyways. Welcome to the force. You seem like a good kid, I look forward to seeing where you end up in twenty years.

For comprehensive information on proper operation of SCP-9201-A, see the Foundation Containment Operations Handbook.

+ INFORMATION RESTRICTED TO CLEARANCE LEVEL 5/9201
Welcome, O5-10.

SCP-9201-B is the Foundation Global Anomaly Analyzer (FGAA). Its effective range is not known to be limited.

When activated, it is capable of resetting all known reality (or any subset thereof, as specified by its input parameters) to any saved checkpoint, as stored within the SCP database.

Invocation requires one of the following:

  • O5 Council majority vote.
  • Site Directors' Executive Committee of the Whole (SDECotW) supermajority vote, if the O5 Council is compromised or incapacitated.
  • LASTRESORT.aic, when the SDECotW-approved automatic activation conditions are met.

To date, SCP-9201-B has successfully reverted 807 K-class events and 525,931,281 severe containment breaches.

SCP-9201.raw_source: ===== [[include component:preview text=Reality is the biggest database there is.]] ===== [[include theme:black-highlighter-theme]] [[module CSS]] div.explainer {     background-color: #dbdbdb; } .explainer li {     list-style: none; } .explainer li:not(:last-child) {     margin-bottom: 0.5em; } .explainer img {     width: 2em; } [[/module]] [[include info:start]] **SCP-9201:** ACID **Alternative Title:** Rollback **Author:** [[*user aismallard]] ([[[aismallard|Author Page]]]) Thanks to [[*user stormbreath]] [[*user yossipossi]] and [[*user Tufto]] for their feedback. [[include info:end]] [[div class="blockquote explainer"]] In database design, **ACID** is an acronym which refers to a system obeying certain capabilities: **atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability**. * [[image https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/scp-9201/atomicity.svg]] **Atomicity:** All changes to the database take place within //transactions//. A transaction must succeed completely or not at all. If it fails, it must be entirely rolled back. It must not be possible for the system to write incomplete data. * [[image https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/scp-9201/consistency.svg]] **Consistency:** All data must obey the constraints and restrictions described by the database's schema. For instance, if a field is marked as //unique//, no two items may have the same value for that field. * [[image https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/scp-9201/isolation.svg]] **Isolation:** The system must be able to handle many transactions occurring at the same time. Uncommitted transaction effects must not be "visible" to other operations occurring within the database. * [[image https://scp-wiki.wdfiles.com/local--files/scp-9201/durability.svg]] **Durability:** Once a transaction has been successfully written, the data must be //durable//. At that point, even a system crash should not prevent data from being recoverable. For mundane forms of information, designing systems which exhibit these properties can be challenging enough. However, here at the Foundation we deal with self-modifying data, retroactive anomalies, and all manner of infohazards, which makes ACID compliance seem impossible. This is not to say, of course, that we have not succeeded. //-- Introduction to RAISA Database Systems, Ninth Edition// [[/div]] **Item #:** SCP-9201 **Object Class:** Thaumiel **Special Containment Procedures:** Access to SCP-9201-A units is restricted per the Foundation Paratechnology Equipment Policy. Field agents who are Level-3 and above are eligible for access, as are anomaly researchers when overseen by Level-4 oversight staff. Use of SCP-9201-A is governed by Foundation Containment Policy. As a piece of standard equipment, approval of containment actions is managed by the Containment Command System (CCS). Installation and management of SCP-9201-B units is overseen by the [[[secure-facility-dossier-site-7 | RAISA Records & Archival Office]]]. **Description:** SCP-9201 is the Foundation Reality Transaction Manager (FRTM), a piece of paratechnology which enables ACID transaction processing on a piece of local reality. Due to its immense power requirements and the difficulty of properly determining conceptual parameters, effective use for Foundation operations is challenging. The primary use of the FRTM is in SCP-9201-A, the Foundation Field Anomaly Analyzer (FFAA). This 47 kilogram device interfaces with an internally-installed limited-use SCP-9201 instance. The FFAA has been programmed to accept nearby spatial coordinates and generic conceptual information, or alternatively, an SCP database number. When provided input data and activated, the device initializes a transaction on the specified parameters: any changes to reality proceed as expected, until SCP-9201-A closes the transaction with one of two possible actions: * **Commit** -- If committed, then any changes made within the region are preserved. This "accepts" the changes to reality since the start of the transaction. * **Rollback** -- If rolled back, then reality within the inputted parameter region is reset to the state it was at the time the transaction was initiated. However, note that //only// the reality captured by the transaction is rolled back. For instance, if a transaction is programmed to capture only biological entities and metals, then any destruction to nearby non-metallic infrastructure will remain after rollback. Partial commits and rollbacks are not possible due to the atomicity guarantee of SCP-9201. Instead, operators should fine-tune which aspects of reality are captured (and thus, resettable) and which are unaffected through use of precise parameter specification. > Oh, you've never seen a debugger in-person before now, huh? Nah, nobody calls it the "Field Anomaly Analyzer", and "FAA" is too confusing with that one agency. > > Have you used one before? No I mean the normal kind, for computers. I guess it makes sense, seeing as you studied memetics. Well, uh let's see, how to explain it... > > It's kind of like this, right? You're studying a car crash. Something in the design of the vehicle was flawed or insufficient as it went over this particular road. > > So what a debugger does is it lets you replay the car crash, but in slow motion. You can pause it, look around, change stuff: see how hot the engine's burning, tweak the axle strength, and oh hey you found it! One instant where there's too much weight on a slightly deflated tire. > > Now unfortunately we don't have any gizmo you can just point out a skip that tells you about its guts, let alone change it however you want. But by capturing it in a transaction and retrying again and again, crashing that car over and over, we can learn an awful lot. SCP-9201's transactional capture ability also applies to itself. If an SCP-9201-A unit is present within a conceptual capture at the time of transaction start, then any actions taken by that unit (including the creation of sub-transactions) can themselves be committed or reverted. Due to its isolation guarantee, the events from one transaction are not able to affect events in an unrelated, non-intersecting transaction. The way this will manifest for observers outside both transactions can be difficult to predict and can lead to anomalous manifestations or bodily harm. For this reason, such configurations are not recommended. When utilized properly, SCP-9201-A is useful for a variety of containment-related tasks. Common tasks include initial containment operations, performing extended experimentation, and limiting or negating the effects of containment breaches. > Initial containment is a motherfuck, that's for sure. All we get are vague reports, mostly-useless sensor readings, and if we're lucky, //maybe// a decent picture or audio snip. But I've survived a lot of them and I'll tell you we wouldn't contain half the shit we do without these things. > > Here's how it's usually laid out. We have a wide net, covering everything in the spacetime region. This transaction is only rolled back if things go //really// south. Then there's the outer inner one, just inside the main cordon. Then the inner inner one. This gets the suspect scene but also all the agents who are going to go into the danger area. > > So you're saying -- I mean that sounds like a good idea but it doesn't work. If you put the agents in their own transaction, separate from the transaction holding the skip, and reset them if they get fucked up by it. Bad idea. They might not be able to see the anomaly. Or maybe they can but they create a "different version" of it in their little world. Or other weird stuff. Don't mess with anomalies like that. It's just not good unless you want a second, even more complicated skip to clean up. To facilitate determination of an anomaly's full properties, stationary versions of SCP-9201-A units have been installed in many containment and research chambers, with pre-tuning for the anomaly being studied. Through use of the Keppler-Gray methodology, 43% of SCP items and 98% of [[[log-of-anomalous-items | miscellaneous anomalous objects]]] have known SCP-9201 conceptual parameters. Once an anomaly's loose conceptual parameter space is known, comprehensive testing can be performed at much lower risk than without SCP-9201 use. A contained object can be exposed to a variety of stimuli, forms of sapient interaction, and other tests within the Foundation's extensive test battery and reset after each experiment. For more social anomalies, rollbacks might occur less frequently, to determine how its behavior varies with its treatment and containment conditions. > You know, I'm thinking, your point about resetting people -- not like that but it's actually pretty normal for a lot of task forces, including ours. We got these perfect conceptual definitions for regular humans, non-anomalous materials, and most of the Foundation's standard equipment. So sometimes we've got these live fire exercises where everyone is put inside a transaction, we blow each other up, and it all gets reset at the end. Except for memories, because those can be excluded. More experience. > > Yeah. It's why most agents are jaded fucks. Permanent SCP-9201-A installations are also invaluable for avoiding and analyzing containment breaches. With a precise conceptual capture, escaped anomalies can simply be rolled back to their pre-breach state, leaving only facility damage. In situations where a looser capture is maintained, some anomalous residue may be left, which can be studied during the cleanup process. Occasionally, such study yields insights on determining more precise conceptual bounds on the SCP object. However, note that improper bounding is often worse than no transactional containment at all. Most conceptual specifications for SCP-9201 are incredibly complex and their myriad interactions even more so. Capturing an anomaly using an incomplete definition means that, when rolled back or committed, any of its effects on reality may be uncompensated for or doubly-compensated for. This can cause objects to become inaccessible, duplicated, split, imperceivable, excessively-perceivable, and risks outright containment breaches or the formation of new anomalies. > God, yeah, I remember that incident. No you're exactly right -- if you ask me, this is the most important thing to understand about our debuggers. Finding out the exact parameters is a pain in the ass, and in some cases we just can't. > > Like we've given up trying to use 'em on Daevite stuff. Maybe because it's retroactive like 9201 is, or [[[scp-6140|maybe it's something else we don't know yet]]], but it never goes well. They also aren't super great for memetics too, which is why I'm glad you're joining the team. They can reset people just like amnestics reset their memories, but that's mostly it. > > Oh yeah, here's the handbook. It actually has a huge-ass list of prohibited anomalies and concepts. Includes some weird ones too, like a few brands of natto and dreams about Neptune's moons. Those require site director approval. > > Anyways. Welcome to the force. You seem like a good kid, I look forward to seeing where you end up in twenty years. For comprehensive information on proper operation of SCP-9201-A, see the Foundation Containment Operations Handbook. [[collapsible show="+ INFORMATION RESTRICTED TO CLEARANCE LEVEL 5/9201" hide="Welcome, O5-10."]] SCP-9201-B is the Foundation Global Anomaly Analyzer (FGAA). Its effective range is not known to be limited. When activated, it is capable of resetting all known reality (or any subset thereof, as specified by its input parameters) to any saved checkpoint, as stored within the SCP database. Invocation requires one of the following: * O5 Council majority vote. * Site Directors' Executive Committee of the Whole (SDECotW) supermajority vote, if the O5 Council is compromised or incapacitated. * LASTRESORT.aic, when the SDECotW-approved automatic activation conditions are met. To date, SCP-9201-B has successfully reverted 807 K-class events and 525,931,281 severe containment breaches. SCP-9202.raw_content:
This document has been modified into an order best suited for full comprehension. Interviews with head researcher Dr. Natasha Atacama have been interspersed for clarification. Due to the nature of SCP-9202, addendums 2 and 3 have been redacted to Level 4, as well as the entirety of PROJECT INDIVIDUAL.

Item#: 9202
Level3
Containment Class:
euclid
Secondary Class:
archon
Disruption Class:
amida
Risk Class:
notice
link to memo

Special Containment Procedures: The SCP-9202 network is to be monitored at all times for instances of SCP-9202-γ. Any detected instances of SCP-9202-γ should be downregulated to instances of SCP-9202-β. Twenty satellites equipped with xenoton-photon conversion lenses (XPC lenses1) should be in orbit such that all areas on the planet accessible via satellite imagery are scanned every two hours for an SCP-9202-β upregulation event. Any SCP-9202-γ instance showing hostility or cognitohazardous or infohazardous speech should be immediately terminated.

A telekill alloy chamber with an internal xenoton sink is to be constructed to capture and house any SCP-9202-ẟ instances that may emerge. The chamber is to have windows with xenoton-resistant glass2 so ẟ instances can be observed but effects are still contained. A system of double doors, where both are controlled solely from outside the chamber, is to be constructed. All information leaving the chamber is to be scanned for info- or cognitohazardous effects.

Other than during testing, only SCP-9202-isolated robots are to be allowed inside the chamber for interaction when a subject either will not or is unable to comply with instructions.3 No person with a clearance level above 1 is to be allowed inside the chamber. Any person who has entered the chamber is to be considered lost and is not to be allowed outside while still living. A persuasion harness is to be installed on all SCP-9202-δ instances in case of aggression or hostility.

[Interviewer]: State your name and station for the record, please.
[Dr. Atacama]: I am Natasha Atacama, doctor of the Foundation and current research head of SCP-9202.
[Interviewer]: Can you describe the containment procedures for SCP-9202 for me?
[Dr. Atacama]: Isn't it already in the file?
[Interviewer]: We would like your perspective.
[Dr. Atacama]: Of course.
[Interviewer]: The first thing I'd like to go over would be the containment procedures for SCP-9202-γ instances. Why terminate them immediately?
[Dr. Atacama]: We call them puppet masters, or just pups for short, because of the way they can control people. You just fall to their will. If one of them manages to figure out their powers and exert them, it can go south very quickly. We only barely took out Pearson and that was mid-stage. A late-stage pup would probably require a full MTF to take out, with xenoproof suits and infohazard scanning.
[Interviewer]: What is the "downregulation" talked about in the file?
[Dr. Atacama]: Do you know what xenos are?
[Interviewer]: That was something I was meaning to ask you about later, but if it's important now, go ahead.
[Dr. Atacama]: Xenos are particles emitted by the 9202 network connections. The word itself comes from the Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, the word xeno meaning the smallest unit of human connection. The typical human emits twelve kiloxenos per second [12 kXe/s]. A typical pup emits around a half thousand megaxenos per second [520 MXe/s], which shows up as a bright spot on our cameras. Downregulation is a technique by which we decrease the capacity of a pup by about seven orders of magnitude using a thaumaturgic ritual that's classified even to me now. The downregulation triggers a reaction in the pup that converts it back down to an aver [sic].
[Interviewer]: Sorry, a what? I would prefer if you used proper abbreviations for instances.
[Dr. Atacama]: I— A -β instance. Aver is short for average.
[Interviewer]: I see. In your file, I remember seeing you were against the immediate termination of δ instances.
[Dr. Atacama]: Yes. I was the one who got -δ instances removed from the kill-list. The Foundation can be a bit trigger-happy sometimes.
[Interviewer]: I would think deltas would be the most dangerous.
[Dr. Atacama]: They would be the most useful is what they would be. A created delta, by simulation, would immediately start teleporting all over the place. That's why we have the attraction telekill chamber, after all. To capture any deltas for research.
[Interviewer]: So it wasn't a moral question, then?
[Dr. Atacama]: … No, I don't think so. Those people that turn into deltas and gammas are too far gone to qualify as human anymore. Nobody with that level of power over others can be seen as human.

Any and all research into the human brain is to be delayed and erroneous papers are to be released to delay that research further. Alternative explanations for autism, other than SCP-9202, are to be proposed. A list of appropriate causes has been drafted. Research into neural coupling, colloquially known as telepathic communication, is to be dismissed as pseudoscience.

Description:

SCP-9202 is a worldwide network, thaumaturgic in nature, that allows for parsing and transmission of emotion and subconscious intent at a higher rate than would be normally possible. SCP-9202 is responsible for the level of advanced reasoning and coordination required for modern civilization. SCP-9202 originates from thaumochemical reactions inside of the human brain.

[Interviewer]: Remind me, your file says you went to Deer College, correct?
[Dr. Atacama]: Yes. I got my doctorate in thaumochemistry there. It was a relatively new field at the time; I specifically published the founding paper on resonance structure glyphs.
[Interviewer]: How has your degree specifically helped with the development of the SCP-9202 protocols and the research that is still being performed?
[Dr. Atacama]: I made the first xenoconversion lens on accident and published it to the Foundation Journal of Chemistry, give or take a year and a half ago? It was the first thing I did at the Foundation that really got attention. I was doing thaumochemistry research for SCP-0000 when I actually made the thing. It wasn't even supposed to be that thaumoactive; it was just for enhancing the impenetrability of the glass. Apparently that triggered the conversion effect, and for a while, that was the anomaly. Where is the energy coming from to make these photons? And then we figured out the thaumoactive chemicals in the human brain elsewhere, and the Foundation called on me to figure it out since I was the expert on thaumoactive resonance structures. I took a sample of the material as a curiosity (with permission, of course) and then realized, Oh, this is the same thing! which led to the discovery of the 9202 network. Then Pearson happened, and the ΨK, and now look where we are today.

SCP-9202-A is the designation for a class of sub-networks contained within SCP-9202. SCP-9202-A instances are characterized by geographic significance, large size, and cultural or religious identity. The creation of new SCP-9202-A instances is rare, but it is typically denoted by the creation of new national, state, or religious identities. Typically, a person can only be a part of two SCP-9202-A networks, one denoting religious ideology (SCP-9202-Aa) and one denoting national ideology or political stance (SCP-9202-Ab).

SCP-9202-B is the designation for a class of sub-networks contained within SCP-9202. SCP-9202-B instances are characterized by sparse occupation, smaller size, tighter connections, and less "realistically meaningful" culture (examples include art movements, online "fandoms", large-scale community projects, etc.). SCP-9202-B instances do not seem to be affected by the-ongoing-ΨK-class-Psychic-Reversion-scenario, unlike SCP-9202-A instances.

SCP-9202-α to SCP-9202-δ are designations for different levels of xenoton emission observed in humans. Interestingly, apart from the α band, each band is neatly separated by several orders of magnitude, with SCP-9202-α instances within the 100 to 8000Xe/s range, SCP-9202-β in the 8 to 15kXe/s band, SCP-9202-γ in the 230 to 800MXe/s band, and SCP-9202-δ theoretically existing in the 94-530GXe/s band. SCP-9202-α and SCP-9202-β, while not as directly separated as -γ or -δ instances, have two separate peaks within their ranges, at 400 Xe/s and 12 kXe/s respectively.

Addendum 1 (Report on the Pearson incident):

Incident Report on the Pearson Atacama MTF Engagement


Document ID Code: XKJ77139-44a
Incident Type: Open Combat
Assigned MTF: Omicron-63

The following transcript was recovered from Agent Samson's bodycam following the execution of Pearson Atacama.

[Transcript Start]

A siren is heard in the background.

[MTF Captain Stevenson]: Testing, testing, one, two. Is this thing [radio] working? Yeah — Good. Okay. We're entering the blast zone soon. Activate the chemical-protection-thingys now if you don't wanna get cooked by the Entity, whatever it is.

[Agent Stravelli]: Entering area now.

[Agent Marx] Seriously? Nothing?

[Agent Samson]: What did you expect? An explosio—

A series of gunshots is heard.

[Unidentified male voice 1]: Get out of the car! NOW! We know who you are!

[Agent Marx]: [through radio] Exit the van by the side door and approach from both sides. If he continues to be hostile, we take him out. On my mark… three, two, one…

The sound of a van door opening is heard.

[Stevenson]: Go, go, go!

A body is heard being slammed against the side of the van.

[Agent Marx]: Okay. Now. We have you up against the wall, and —

1

[Voice 1]: [Infohazard removed]. [Cognitohazard vector removed], fuckers!

[Agent Marx]: These helmets are autoprocessing for indirect hazards. You won't get us—

[Voice 1]: [Infohazard removed]. I am the [Cognitohazard removed], [Infohazard removed] fucking [Infohazard removed]. [Cognitohazard removed]! I will NOT BE SILENCED!

[Agent Stravelli]: I don't think it would be wise to keep this one around.

[Captain Stevenson] Copy that. Terminating.

[Agent Samson]: Jesus. And it's like this for two city blocks?

A gunshot is heard.

Several minutes have been removed for brevity. At the 20-minute mark, video became recoverable.

The MTF team approaches the inner levels of the breach area. As they turn a corner, the obvious epicenter becomes clear. The walls of buildings have been sprayed with slogans, such as "Live, Laugh, Learn", "No Connection Without Correction", and [Infohazard removed]. A large thaumaturgic ritual circle is seen, approx. 10 meters in diameter, with a (7,2) pentagram inscribed in the center and a ring of glyphs inscribed on the outside. A series of twenty-one smaller thaumaturgic ritual circles surrounds the outer one, approx. 0.5 meters in diameter. A person stands in each circle except for three, which are positioned in an equilateral triangle surrounding the first which are noticeably larger. A network of lines connect them.

The woman within the center circle , identified as Pearson Atacama, turns to face them.

[Pearson]: I expected you'd come. Here, have a seat.

Each of the agents continues to have their gun trained on Pearson.

[Pearson]: Or don't. It doesn't matter to me. You can't shoot me and I can't hurt you while I'm in this circle. Physically, of course. I also know you won't risk any more civilian casualties, since none of these people are active aggressors. I invite you to try to shoot me, actually.

2

[Captain Stevenson]: I'll take you up on that challenge.

Captain Stevenson shoots 20 times. A faint dome suddenly appears intersecting the central magic circle, and each of the shots becomes a white dot on the dome.

[Agent Stravelli]: How can we be sure that you can't hurt us?

[Pearson]: You aren't, but I haven't yet, so you'll just have to trust me. You got here early, by the way — we weren't expecting you to get here this fast. Bravo!

[Agent Marx]: Why aren't they attacking us? What have you done to them?

Pearson motions to the people surrounding the circle, who are milling about amicably. Some are chatting amongst each other. Many return the gesture with a wave of their own.

[Pearson]: If they really didn't want to be here, they would go. I planted the idea in their head and it grew into a tree. I told them there was a better way to love, that I could help them connect with each other. And I can! I need your help to do it, though. As for attacking you, well, I wanted to delay you, but I can't just be throwing bodies at the wall like the Foundation that I'm trying to move away from.

[Agent Marx]: How do we know you're not lying?

[Pearson]: Marx. You have never been accepted for who you were, have you?

[Agent Marx]: I got here. Not many people do that.

[Pearson]: Are you really happy, though? I doubt you are. The Foundation told you that they would accept you and pay you and give you a family, but they never let you support the one you already had. No contact form, right?

[Agent Marx]: No contact is necessary to —

[Pearson]: No contact isn't ever necessary. You could have "worked a job" in private security to them, not die and it would be the same effect. You were never treated right, and they never even gave you their promise. Never let you pursue that job in the occult sciences.

3

[Agent Marx]: I was better off here.

[Pearson]: Stop lying to yourself. I can give you the knowledge you need. I can help you. I can [Targeted infohazard removed].

[Agent Marx]: What do I have to do?

It is unknown why other agents did not intervene at this point.

[Pearson]: All you have to do is help me. Step in the circle. You haven't been trained like my apostles here, but you're special. Serve as my conduit. [Targeted infohazard removed].

Marx approaches the indicated circle. He enters it and sits down. A translucent barrier appears.

[Pearson]: Good. Stevenson, this is the job you always wanted?

[Stevenson]: Don't go all therapist mode on me, it's —

[Pearson]: Answer the question.

[Stevenson]: I… yes. This was the job I wanted, but…

[Pearson]: But what?

[Captain Stevenson]: I wanted a bigger team. Nobody was supposed to die— they were supposed to help him but they couldn't come… I didn't understand why. Acceptable losses my ass! He was a good agent, I don't understand why they would…

Stevenson begins to cry. It is unknown why such a strong emotional effect was observed, as simulations suggested this memory had been successfully suppressed through amnestic therapy.

[Pearson]: Now, now. I can give you a team. There are still anomalies to contain. There are still people to protect, and unlike the Foundation, I care about their well-being, not just the greater good. All you have to do is help me, this one time.

Stevenson stands up and takes his place in the indicated circle.

4

[Pearson]: And Stravelli. They gave you a new name and wouldn't let you change it. Prohibited you speaking your own language because it wasn't the standard in America. Pero yo puede entiende tu.4 I can give you a place where you will be understood, accepted by the people around you. Considered normal. I can [Targeted infohazard removed].

Stravelli takes his place in the circle.

[Agent Samson]: What have you done to them?

[Pearson]: Made them understand. It's unfortunate that you sealed your suit correctly or I could make you understand, too. I still have a place for you, though. You can be witness.

[Agent Samson]: Witness to what?

[Pearson]: Witness to my ascension.

The people who were previously milling about suddenly stop and turn to face Pearson. The eighteen people in the smaller circles link themselves to Stravelli, Marx, and Stevenson through the chalk lines. Each of the three begins to glow brightly with xenoton radiation, with the people throughout the town square dimming by several orders of magnitude. The people on the inside begin chanting as Samson begins to pound on the central circle, shouting incoherently. The radiation saturates the cameras before dimming significantly. Pearson is visibly glowing as Samson finally breaches the barrier, firing off several shots in Pearson's general direction. One of the shots appears to hit Pearson in the neck before she disappears entirely. All of the people in the town square fall to the ground, dead. The feed then cuts to static.

[Transcript End]

Stravelli, Marx, and Stevenson were found dead by sub-veil first responders. Each of their heads were carbonized as far as five centimeters into the organic tissue around their head. Samson was found alive but in critical condition, with second to third-degree burns in the facial area. Samson is currently recovering but still comatose, pending reassignment. Pearson was found dead in Sacramento, California, with the cause of death determined as a gunshot wound to the neck.

It is theorized that the burns seen on Stravelli, Marx, Stevenson, and Samson are due to extremely high levels of xenoton downconverson, resulting in severe radiation burns.

Containment Procedures: SCP-9202-Ψ is not to be contained. All documentation pertaining to SCP-9202-Ψ is to be classified to at least Level 3/9202 to prevent mass panic within the Foundation.

In lieu of containment of SCP-9202-Ψ, SCP-9202-B instances are to be encouraged to grow in all ways possible, including the dissemination of infohazardous anart throughout social media platforms to implant the desire to be inside of niche communities. A list has been drafted of potential SCP-9202-B instances and an agreement has been entered with GOI-2979 "Are We Cool Yet?" for assistance in the production and dissemination of anart5 in exchange for certain allowances with the distribution of other anart. Foundation funds are to be diverted for the funding of conventions.

[Interviewer]: What was your experience during initial containment efforts of SCP-9202-Ψ?
[Dr. Atacama]: Probably the worst part of my tenure at the Foundation.
[Interviewer]: I doubt it was the worst —
[Dr. Atacama]: Have you ever had to stay up to 3 A.M. making anart with an AWCY teenager because apparently your three-year-old degree in anart made you the most qualified person on the team, and then fall prey to your own anart and find yourself looking for fursuits on Etsy at four in the morning, on your fourth cup of double-shot espresso? No? I thought not.

Internally, Foundation group-building exercises should be practiced so that, if possible, the Foundation can become a -B instance. Until such time as that is possible, external containment efforts should also be spread internally, in the form of posters, memos, announcements, and embedded infohazards throughout the database. Resources are to be provided to employees for their hobbies for the purpose of making entry into SCP-9202-B instances easier.

Description: SCP-9202-Ψ is the designation for the ongoing ΨK-Class Psychic Reversion Scenario. SCP-9202-Ψ currently affects 4% of people worldwide. SCP-9202-Ψ was caused by the momentary upregulation of SCP-9202-δ-1 from a -γ instance to a -δ instance, which overloaded the network.

Individuals affected by SCP-9202-Ψ are unable to connect with other individuals simply based on geological proximity. Instead, they must share a SCP-9202-B network with the other individual. Projections forecast that 99.99% of people will be affected by SCP-9202-B by 2049.

Currently, the three largest SCP-9202-B groups targeted for the use of containing knowledge of SCP-9202-Ψ are: the 'furry fandom', the LGBTQ+ community, and the cosplay community.

[Dr. Atacama]: Xenos are particles emitted by the 9202 network connections. It comes from the Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, the word xeno meaning the smallest unit of human connection. [Dr. Atacama]: I— A -β instance. Aver is short for average.

[Dr. Atacama]: Yes. I was the one who got -δ instances removed from the kill-list. The Foundation can be a bit trigger-happy sometimes.

SCP-9205.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9205

Object Class: Euclid (Formerly Safe)

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9205 is to be contained in a secure storage locker at Site 76. Personnel assigned to study or handle it are to undergo full psychological evaluations every month: those with misgivings concerning their age, health, and appearance are to be immediately reassigned.

All captive instances of SCP-9205-A are to be held in separate humanoid containment cells. If removed for exercise or testing, instances must be fitted with handcuffs, weighted manacles, and restraint masks. If any instance deploys its nictitating membranes, personnel are to retreat to a safe distance until it is fed, sedated, or terminated, depending on the circumstances.

Meals for SCP-9205-A instances must consist solely of raw meat and bone, delivered twice daily. Though they cannot derive nutrition from fruit, vegetables, or cooked meat, they still enjoy the taste and can be given food from the cafeteria as a reward for good behaviour.

Description: SCP-9205 is a cylindrical jar made of polished black marble, 14 cm in height and 6 cm in diameter, undecorated except for the Latin words carved into the lid: Male parta male dilabuntur.1 The jar is capable of self-repair, having survived multiple gunshots during attempts to acquire it, and it is not known if it can be permanently damaged or destroyed.

The contents of the jar consist of an opaque grey gel, which cannot be completely extracted or exhausted, as SCP-9205 automatically generates more to replace it. This substance is chemically identical to cold cream and exhibits no anomalous traits until exposed to the skin of a human being of at least forty years of age. If used on any other individual, animal, or object, or held in any container other than SCP-9205, it will harmlessly dissolve.

Once applied to the face of an individual of the minimum age, SCP-9205's gel produces an immediate and irreversible rejuvenating effect across the entire body within one minute of application. Regardless of the quantity used, users will be regressed to approximately 20-30 years of age, experiencing a full restoration of physical health and mental acuity in the process.

Twenty-four hours after application, users begin manifesting negative symptoms, including patches of discoloured skin, hair loss, loose teeth, and intramuscular pain, all of which escalate over time, often prompting users to make use of SCP-9205 again in the erroneous belief that they are now aging at an accelerated rate.

SCP-9205 is the only means of treating these symptoms, restoring the subject's initial state of rejuvenation within one minute of application regardless of symptom severity; drugs, surgeries, or even other anomalous items have proved ineffectual. However, the efficacy of SCP-9205 diminishes with repeated uses, progressively halving the time in which positive symptoms are exhibited2, often forcing users to apply more over shorter periods until they cannot meet the accelerated demands and enter the final stage of transformation.

Those who do not reuse SCP-9205 continue to degenerate over the next twenty-four hours following the initial manifestation of negative symptoms, ultimately escalating from mutation to transformation in the final minutes. This process cannot be reversed or undone in any way, making the metamorphosis into an instance of SCP-9205-A inevitable and permanent as soon as a compatible user is exposed.

SCP-9205-A instances are similar in appearance to human children between 5-11 years of age. All specimens are completely bald and exhibit translucent grey skin prominently marked with black-tinted veins, which they disguise with makeup and wigs in public.

SCP-9205-A instances also sport nictitating membranes that deploy in response to fear, hunger, or anger as an instinctive defence mechanism, being dense enough to shield the eyes from bludgeoning, stabbing, and even chemical weapons.3 When these membranes are in use, their eyes appear to turn opaque black, possibly as a threat display to potential enemies.

SCP-9205-A instances possess enhanced regenerative capabilities and though they cannot survive decapitation or perforating head injuries, research indicates that they can fully regenerate amputated limbs and even fractured spines over the course of a month. Because of this, instances no longer physically age: several captive specimens were reportedly converted during the 1920s and have not exhibited any signs of senescence or even basic maturation.

Though they demonstrate no enhanced strength, anomalous mutations to the nerves, muscles, joints, and cardiovascular system make SCP-9205-A instances notably faster and more agile than the human norm. Top speed varies between instances, though most instances can reach speeds in excess of 70 kph with very little effort.

SCP-9205-A instances exhibit anomalously powerful jaws capable of exerting a bite-force in excess of 2000 PSI, with two additional rows of incisors and molars hidden behind their human front teeth. Unusually elastic muscles and tendons allow instances to distend their jaws to more than quadruple their normal size, often resulting in their bites being mistaken for the results of animal attacks.

All instances are obligate predators subsisting entirely on raw meat and bone. Those lacking the funds to buy meat survive on livestock, pets, carrion, and human beings.

Discovery Log: SCP-9205 was first brought to the Foundation's attention in 1987, following several unexplained disappearances among Los Angeles' wealthier inhabitants. Initially attributed to kidnappings, anomalous commonalities in police reports and a lack of ransom demands eventually led to the Foundation being notified.

According to witnesses, the missing individuals had all undergone major cosmetic surgery in the days prior to their disappearance and appeared significantly younger than their chronological age. This was not considered unusual, as the victims had expressed frustration with aging and were often described as “vain”, but none of them would admit the name of the clinic or professional responsible for the surgery. All the victims had been keeping a black marble jar in their home, though none admitted where they had acquired it, and in all cases, the jar had been removed by the time police arrived to investigate the disappearances.

Though the Foundation was able to determine that the jar was responsible for the rejuvenating effects of the “surgeries”, the reason for the disappearances remained unknown, and the identity of the vendor could not be determined through mundane forensic accounting.

On 15/10/1987, wiretaps of witnesses revealed that that the brother of one of the victims had observed the initial effects of the object in action and decided to purchase it after his sister’s disappearance, intending to use it once he had “worked up the nerve." Two hours later, Foundation agents successfully confiscated the item shortly after the owner had applied his first dose. Following a brief analysis by a field researcher to determine that it was safe to handle, it was given the formal designation of SCP-9205 and prepared for transportation.

However, while SCP-9205 was being removed, the team was attacked by seven individuals now recognized as SCP-9205-A instances. Five Foundation agents were killed in the attack, and though the two remaining agents were able to terminate three of their assailants, the surviving instances and their apparent ringleader were able to escape with SCP-9205.

In the aftermath, fingerprint analysis revealed that the attackers had all been individuals listed among the missing, with the ringleader identified as the sister of SCP-9205's previous owner. Upon being transformed, all prior owners had been hired by the vendor's organization as security guards, with available evidence suggesting that the vendor had deliberately withheld information on SCP-9205's long-term effects from their clients in order to guarantee their eventual metamorphosis and recruitment.

Combined with the previous owner's interrogation, transformation, and subsequent containment, SCP-9205's anomalous attributes were finally documented and understood.

Addendum 05/04/2014): Subsequent research has found that SCP-9205-A instances are not recent developments, with obscure references to “grey cannibal brats with the jaws of sharks” found in rare archives of anomalous activity dating back to 1920, though their connection to SCP-9205 was not understood at the time, with any missing persons associated with them believed to have been eaten rather than converted.

It is also believed that the distinctive appearance of hungry SCP-9205-A instances may have led to the urban legend of the “black-eyed children"4.

However, SCP-9205’s vendor has continued to elude the Foundation. Investigation has revealed that this was initially because the stock market crash of 19/10/1987 discouraged further sales, allowing the vendor and their staff of SCP-9205-A instances time to move their base of operations. Afterwards, it is believed the vendor was able to avoid detection by restricting sales to more discreet clientele who avoided public life wherever possible5, all of whom could be more easily exploited, defrauded, converted, and subsequently recruited into the vendor's organization without drawing significant attention.

No evidence has been found to confirm that SCP-9205 is being smuggled internationally through mundane methods, suggesting that the vendor is employing a thaumaturge or some other anomalous means of transportation.

On the rare occasions Foundation agents have been able to find and intercept a courier believed to be carrying SCP-9205, a security team of SCP-9205-A instances was able to retrieve the objective and escape before Foundation backup could arrive.

At present, it is still not known why the vendor's former clients willingly become employees of the organization that defrauded and transformed them.

> Operation GREY METAMORPHOSIS Preliminary Stage: October 2024
- Close

Following a tip-off from Marshall, Carter, & Dark, webcrawlers uncovered a Dark Web forum for prospective SCP-9205 users. Known as “The Society of Iðunn's Orchard,” the forum’s membership had been pooling resources to pay for access to the “Vessel of Eternity."

This forum also confirmed that the vendor, now known as "Imperial Purple Imports," was leasing the item instead of selling it, allowing temporary access to SCP-9205 upon payment and removing it after a single use.6

Foundation strategists agreed this represented an unprecedented opportunity to infiltrate the Society and finally acquire the item. However, given the difficulty in securing the mission objective from Imperial Purple Imports' security personnel, the only reliable method for the infiltrator to escape with the mission objective would be to use SCP-9205 and undergo the transformation themselves.

The agent selected for this mission was Senior Agent William Shadfly. Agent Shadfly had been diagnosed with Stage 4 lung cancer three months prior to selection and chemotherapy had proved ineffective in treating his condition, leaving him with a projected life expectancy of less than a year; combined with his lack of personal connections outside the Foundation, it was believed that he would be the ideal candidate. Upon being approached for this role, Agent Shadfly accepted the offer, agreeing to be contained upon the successful completion of the mission in exchange for privileges normally denied to SCP-9205-A instances.

Agent Shadfly then contacted the Society under the name of "Bill Ambrosian", agreeing to provide the remaining funds needed to access to SCP-9205 in exchange for membership7. In return, he was provided with the address of a hotel in Manhattan where the Society was due to meet with IPI's courier.

On 27/10/24, Agent Shadfly was fitted with a subdermal tracking device, provided with forged documents, multiple sets of replacement clothing8, a wig, a jar of makeup, an emergency signaling device (concealed in Agent Shadfly's wristwatch), and a cufflink dictaphone to ensure mission documentation, before being dispatched to New York City to commence the mission.

- Close


> Mission Documentation: Part 1
- Close

AUDIO LOG TRANSCRIPT

DATE: 27/10/24, 4:00 PM

[BEGIN LOG]

This is Agent William Shadfly, reporting from the Bellingwalsh Hotel, Manhattan.

I’ve met with the Society, all twelve of them, not counting the guards and private nurses. Membership is as expected: aging heiresses turned plastic surgery addicts, sagging corpocrats too limp for the boardroom hookers, rich mummies chasing eternal life… and now me. (coughs) The oldest of them’s in his late nineties. The youngest is fifty-five, so I don’t feel too out of place. (chuckles weakly, coughs)

I can confirm that they’re not pooling their funds because they’re poor: I recognize a few suspected members of Marshall, Carter & Dark’s client list here, along with real estate moguls, Wall Street wizards, business dynasty scions, Hollywood studio execs, and even the odd crime boss. Twelve of the biggest cheapskates in the West, and all of them too proud to accept the notion of growing old and dying like everyone else.

Bit more public than IPI's usual clientele, though. Odd, that.

The head of this little secret society is Patrick Thule, the political megadonor. No surprises there, given his interests. I’m assuming Thule’s used his own company to do some digging on me, but the Foundation’s forgeries are holding up for now… or maybe it's just money talking louder than sense.

Thanks to my donation, I’ve now been officially accepted as the thirteenth and final member of the Society of Iðunn's Orchard. (cough) Thule's bought out the entire fifteenth floor for our use, so we've settled in to wait for IPI's payment to be accepted.

It's deathly quiet up here. Dark, too: all the shutters have been lowered for secrecy's sake. None of the Society members are friends, so no socialization. There’s a boardroom with a huge media suite on this floor, but nobody’s used it. Instead, we're alone in our rooms, wasting time. Most of this crew are glued to their iPads, watching the markets. Me, I'm taking advantage of the lull to survey the floor, work out exit routes, calculate threat levels… and maybe finish reading Fatal Beauty if there's still time.

Hopefully, I won’t have to wait too long. (cough)

Shadfly out.

[END LOG]



AUDIO LOG TRANSCRIPT

DATE: 28/10/24, 7:00 PM

[BEGIN LOG]

(cough) Payment’s been accepted. Thule gathered us in the boardroom to tell us that Imperial Purple Imports are sending a courier tomorrow.

Incident Report (31/10/24):

At 7:35 AM, Agent Shadfly activated his emergency beacon, prompting SCP agents remotely observing the Bellingwalsh Hotel to call for backup.

Upon arriving on the 15th floor, agents found the bodies of three members of the Society of Iðunn's Orchards, the IPI courier, two private nurses employed by Society members, and all twenty-seven of the Society's guards. Analysis revealed that only 40% of the fatalities were due to gunshot wounds, the rest being due to bites from SCP-9205-A instances.

The only survivors of the massacre still at the scene were two partially transformed Society members, who were immediately contained. Agent Shadfly, the remaining seven members, and SCP-9205 could not be located.

According to the two witnesses, after noticing their negative symptoms returning for the second time, the Society had correctly assumed that they were being defrauded by IPI. Soon after, they became convinced (erroneously) that the only way to make SCP-9205's effects permanent was to claim sole full-time ownership of it.

When the IPI courier arrived at the boardroom for the third and final time, numerous Society members drew concealed firearms and attempted to steal SCP-9205 at gunpoint, resulting in a standoff that only ended when Agent Shadfly dropped from a ventilation shaft and successfully dislodged the item from Patrick Thule's grip.

In the ensuing gun battle, all parties involved tried to seize SCP-9205 for themselves or stop the others from claiming it, resulting in numerous fatalities and injuries. In the confusion, Mrs Imelda Waldington was able to escape with SCP-9205.

As soon as this was noticed, the combatants left the area in an attempt to pursue Mrs Waldington, with the surviving Society members exiting via the elevator, Agent Shadfly descending the stairwell at top speed, and the IPI guards leaping out the nearest window and onto the neighbouring rooftops. The two witnesses, having suffered immobilizing injuries during the fight, were left behind.

As Foundation agents arrived to contain the survivors and prevent media exposure, Operation Control received an emergency call from Agent Shadfly with a request for tracking services.

> MISSION DEBRIEFING
- Close

Thirty minutes after Agent Shadfly triggered his signaling device for the second time, Foundation backup arrived at the IPI safehouse in force.

Covertly introduced tear gas proved effective in nullifying the combat potential of SCP-9205-A instances: since none of the instances were alerted to the threat, their nictitating membranes did not deploy in time to protect their eyes from the gas, making it difficult for any of them to retaliate when Foundation operatives were authorized to break down the doors and attack.

As a result, though five of the twenty-three SCP-9205-A instances were able to escape through thaumaturgical means, twelve instances were successfully apprehended, along with three of the ten hired security guards on site. The remainder were terminated in battle, with no Foundation casualties resulting.

Following the cessation of hostilities, agents were able to cut their way through the loft's door with oxyacetylene torches: inside, they found the caged members of the Society of Iðunn's Orchards, Agent Shadfly, and SCP-9205.

With Imelda Waldington fully transformed, and Patrick Thule and the other surviving Society members completing their own metamorphoses over the course of the following hours, all were subsequently contained. Given the level of financial influence wielded by the Society members, the O5 Council has authorized operations to replace all transformed or deceased VIPs with body doubles loyal to the Foundation, both to ensure the preservation of the Veil and the reduction of any potential economic instability triggered by the disappearances.

Agent Shadfly was unconscious when located and did not awaken until he had been rehoused at Site 76 along with SCP-9205 and the other transformed Society members.

Interviewed: Agent William Shadfly

Interviewer: Dr Phillipa Percival

Foreword: The following log constitutes the remainder of Agent Shadfly's mission debriefing, with the events of the mission itself having already been reported. Interview took place in his new quarters.

<Begin Log, 05:00 PM, 31/10/24)>

Dr Percival: …All in all, I'd say this constitutes a successful mission. You've done exceptionally well.

Agent Shadfly: Let's not make mountains out of molehills; I only managed this because the brokers were complacent and greedy.

Dr Percival: Come on, you secured an artefact that's been eluding us since Black Monday and you helped take down Imperial Purple's New York branch. That's got to be worth a celebration, right?

pause

Dr Percival: Will?

Agent Shadfly: You're not supposed to call me that anymore, Philly.

Dr Percival: You're not supposed to be calling me that either. Look, could you just tell me what's wrong? Please? It's hard enough getting Agents to accept therapy, and damn near impossible to secure it for SCPs. Just tell me what's on your mind.

Agent Shadfly: Well, about the only thing we can be thankful for is that this wasn't another apocalypse waiting to happen. I mean, Imperial Purple Imports barely qualifies as a Group of Interest: they spend more time on rugpulls and loansharking than anomalous items. Small potatoes, really.

Dr Percival: Surely you can at least take pride in-

Agent Shadfly: We only found out about IPI because they got greedy and broke their own rules blatantly enough for MC&D to find out. We couldn't find their board of directors, we don't know where the other branches are, we couldn't seize their other artefacts, and we can't stop their clients from buying shit that's guaranteed to turn them into monsters. Not exactly a worthwhile end to my career.

Dr Percival: That's not the only reason why you're in a bad mood, though, is it?

Agent Shadfly: (sighs) No. When I touched SCP-9205 at the warehouse, I saw something. It might have just been a hallucination but… I think I'm beginning to understand.

Dr Percival: …understand what? Your whaling dreams?

Agent Shadfly: Male parta male dilabuntur. The IPI board of directors screwed up when they were making the Vessel, let a little too much of what it once was seep through to the finished article. Essence was stolen from it to replenish their beauty and their lives, so their beauty and their lives were stolen from them. The transformation was meant as an insult.

Dr Percival: You mean-

Agent Shadfly: I said the damn thing was warm to the touch. Like a butchered whale in the ice, carved open, innards smoking… but somehow just alive enough to dream.

pause

Agent Shadfly: Not that it matters.

Dr Percival: Why not?

Agent Shadfly: You heard what Bingham said. You know how many of the victims ended up working for IPI even after everything the company did to them. And I'm betting that Imelda's the only Society member with an ounce of regret for what they've become. Every bastard that shelled out for eternal life and beauty saw the Vessel's insult, and eventually said "yep, that's who I am! Let's have fun with it!"

Dr Percival: So what? It's not like they'd be the first altered individuals to embrace their change-

Agent Shadfly: Embracing the change isn't the point! They sank to new lows. The transformation was meant to show them how petty and childish and monstrous they really were… and they liked it. That's why I'm feeling down, Philly. Because everything about the Vessel - its creation, IPI, the Society, my mission… it's all been a waste of time. (sighs) All in vain, if you like.

pause

Dr Percival: …Do you want me to bring you that bottle of scotch you asked for earlier this week?

Agent Shadfly: I don't need to drown my sorrows, Philly, I need sleep. When I wake, maybe I'll feel better about this whole pointless mess, maybe even enough to enjoy my retirement. Until then, I just want to sleep… and try to forget.

Agent Shadfly lies down on his bunk and closes his eyes.

Agent Shadfly: That's all for now, Dr Percival.

Dr Percival: (sadly) Very well then. Thank you for your time, A-1.

**Item #:** SCP-9205



**Object Class:** Euclid (Formerly Safe)



**Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9205 is to be contained in a secure storage locker at Site 76. Personnel assigned to study or handle it are to undergo full psychological evaluations every month: those with misgivings concerning their age, health, and appearance are to be immediately reassigned.



All captive instances of SCP-9205-A are to be held in separate humanoid containment cells. If removed for exercise or testing, instances must be fitted with handcuffs, weighted manacles, and restraint masks. If any instance deploys its nictitating membranes, personnel are to retreat to a safe distance until it is fed, sedated, or terminated, depending on the circumstances.



Meals for SCP-9205-A instances must consist solely of raw meat and bone, delivered twice daily. Though they cannot derive nutrition from fruit, vegetables, or cooked meat, they still enjoy the taste and can be given food from the cafeteria as a reward for good behaviour.



**Description:** SCP-9205 is a cylindrical jar made of polished black marble, 14 cm in height and 6 cm in diameter, undecorated except for the Latin words carved into the lid: //Male parta male dilabuntur.// [[footnote]] “What has been wrongly gained is wrongly lost," a quote attributed to Marcus Tullius Cicero.[[/footnote]] The jar is capable of self-repair, having survived multiple gunshots during attempts to acquire it, and it is not known if it can be permanently damaged or destroyed.



The contents of the jar consist of an opaque grey gel, which cannot be completely extracted or exhausted, as SCP-9205 automatically generates more to replace it. This substance is chemically identical to cold cream and exhibits no anomalous traits until exposed to the skin of a human being of at least forty years of age. If used on any other individual, animal, or object, or held in any container other than SCP-9205, it will harmlessly dissolve.



Once applied to the face of an individual of the minimum age, SCP-9205's gel produces an immediate and irreversible rejuvenating effect across the entire body within one minute of application. Regardless of the quantity used, users will be regressed to approximately 20-30 years of age, experiencing a full restoration of physical health and mental acuity in the process.



Twenty-four hours after application, users begin manifesting negative symptoms, including patches of discoloured skin, hair loss, loose teeth, and intramuscular pain, all of which escalate over time, often prompting users to make use of SCP-9205 again in the erroneous belief that they are now aging at an accelerated rate. 



SCP-9205 is the only means of treating these symptoms, restoring the subject's initial state of rejuvenation within one minute of application regardless of symptom severity; drugs, surgeries, or even other anomalous items have proved ineffectual. However, the efficacy of SCP-9205 diminishes with repeated uses, progressively halving the time in which positive symptoms are exhibited [[footnote]]Twenty-four hours of positive symptoms being divided into twelve, then six, then three, then ninety minutes, then forty-five minutes, etc. This same reduction applies to the period of negative symptoms prior to transformation. [[/footnote]], often forcing users to apply more over shorter periods until they cannot meet the accelerated demands and enter the final stage of transformation.



Those who do not reuse SCP-9205 continue to degenerate over the next twenty-four hours following the initial manifestation of negative symptoms, ultimately escalating from mutation to transformation in the final minutes. This process cannot be reversed or undone in any way, making the metamorphosis into an instance of SCP-9205-A inevitable and permanent as soon as a compatible user is exposed.



**SCP-9205-A** instances are similar in appearance to human children between 5-11 years of age. All specimens are completely bald and exhibit translucent grey skin prominently marked with black-tinted veins, which they disguise with makeup and wigs in public.



 SCP-9205-A instances also sport nictitating membranes that deploy in response to fear, hunger, or anger as an instinctive defence mechanism, being dense enough to shield the eyes from bludgeoning, stabbing, and even chemical weapons. [[footnote]]Current analysis indicates that SCP-9205-A instances are largely sight-oriented, have no enhanced sense of smell or hearing, and require time to regenerate before recovering from impaired vision, making these membranes essential for guaranteeing their effectiveness as hunters.[[/footnote]] When these membranes are in use, their eyes appear to turn opaque black, possibly as a threat display to potential enemies.



SCP-9205-A instances possess enhanced regenerative capabilities and though they cannot survive decapitation or perforating head injuries, research indicates that they can fully regenerate amputated limbs and even fractured spines over the course of a month. Because of this, instances no longer physically age: several captive specimens were reportedly converted during the 1920s and have not exhibited any signs of senescence or even basic maturation.



Though they demonstrate no enhanced strength, anomalous mutations to the nerves, muscles, joints, and cardiovascular system make SCP-9205-A instances notably faster and more agile than the human norm. Top speed varies between instances, though most instances can reach speeds in excess of 70 kph with very little effort.



SCP-9205-A instances exhibit anomalously powerful jaws capable of exerting a bite-force in excess of 2000 PSI, with two additional rows of incisors and molars hidden behind their human front teeth. Unusually elastic muscles and tendons allow instances to distend their jaws to more than quadruple their normal size, often resulting in their bites being mistaken for the results of animal attacks.



All instances are obligate predators subsisting entirely on raw meat and bone. Those lacking the funds to buy meat survive on livestock, pets, carrion, and human beings.



**Discovery Log**: SCP-9205 was first brought to the Foundation's attention in 1987, following several unexplained disappearances among Los Angeles' wealthier inhabitants. Initially attributed to kidnappings, anomalous commonalities in police reports and a lack of ransom demands eventually led to the Foundation being notified.



According to witnesses, the missing individuals had all undergone major cosmetic surgery in the days prior to their disappearance and appeared significantly younger than their chronological age. This was not considered unusual, as the victims had expressed frustration with aging and were often described as “vain”, but none of them would admit the name of the clinic or professional responsible for the surgery. All the victims had been keeping a black marble jar in their home, though none admitted where they had acquired it, and in all cases, the jar had been removed by the time police arrived to investigate the disappearances.



Though the Foundation was able to determine that the jar was responsible for the rejuvenating effects of the “surgeries”, the reason for the disappearances remained unknown, and the identity of the vendor could not be determined through mundane forensic accounting.



On 15/10/1987, wiretaps of witnesses revealed that that the brother of one of the victims had observed the initial effects of the object in action and decided to purchase it after his sister’s disappearance, intending to use it once he had “worked up the nerve." Two hours later, Foundation agents successfully confiscated the item shortly after the owner had applied his first dose. Following a brief analysis by a field researcher to determine that it was safe to handle, it was given the formal designation of SCP-9205 and prepared for transportation.



However, while SCP-9205 was being removed, the team was attacked by seven individuals now recognized as SCP-9205-A instances. Five Foundation agents were killed in the attack, and though the two remaining agents were able to terminate three of their assailants, the surviving instances and their apparent ringleader were able to escape with SCP-9205.



In the aftermath, fingerprint analysis revealed that the attackers had all been individuals listed among the missing, with the ringleader identified as the sister of SCP-9205's previous owner. Upon being transformed, all prior owners had been hired by the vendor's organization as security guards, with available evidence suggesting that the vendor had deliberately withheld information on SCP-9205's long-term effects from their clients in order to guarantee their eventual metamorphosis and recruitment.

 

Combined with the previous owner's interrogation, transformation, and subsequent containment, SCP-9205's anomalous attributes were finally documented and understood.



**Addendum 05/04/2014):** Subsequent research has found that SCP-9205-A instances are not recent developments, with obscure references to “grey cannibal brats with the jaws of sharks” found in rare archives of anomalous activity dating back to 1920, though their connection to SCP-9205 was not understood at the time, with any missing persons associated with them believed to have been eaten rather than converted.



It is also believed that the distinctive appearance of hungry SCP-9205-A instances may have led to the urban legend of the “black-eyed children"[[footnote]]A cryptid taking the form of a child with black eyes, commonly encountered trying to manipulate civilians into allowing them into their homes or cars.[[/footnote]].



However, SCP-9205’s vendor has continued to elude the Foundation. Investigation has revealed that this was initially because the stock market crash of 19/10/1987 discouraged further sales, allowing the vendor and their staff of SCP-9205-A instances time to move their base of operations. Afterwards, it is believed the vendor was able to avoid detection by restricting sales to more discreet clientele who avoided public life wherever possible[[footnote]]Numerous documented SCP-9205-A instances were formerly recluses, agoraphobes, political exiles, and even wealthy fugitives living under assumed identities.[[/footnote]], all of whom could be more easily exploited, defrauded, converted, and subsequently recruited into the vendor's organization without drawing significant attention. 



No evidence has been found to confirm that SCP-9205 is being smuggled internationally through mundane methods, suggesting that the vendor is employing a thaumaturge or some other anomalous means of transportation.



On the rare occasions Foundation agents have been able to find and intercept a courier believed to be carrying SCP-9205, a security team of SCP-9205-A instances was able to retrieve the objective and escape before Foundation backup could arrive.



At present, it is still not known why the vendor's former clients willingly become employees of the organization that defrauded and transformed them.

Following a tip-off from Marshall, Carter, & Dark, webcrawlers uncovered a Dark Web forum for prospective SCP-9205 users. Known as “The Society of Iðunn's Orchard,” the forum’s membership had been pooling resources to pay for access to the “Vessel of Eternity."



This forum also confirmed that the vendor, now known as "Imperial Purple Imports," was leasing the item instead of selling it, allowing temporary access to SCP-9205 upon payment and removing it after a single use. [[footnote]]Combined with the failure to mention SCP-9205's negative symptoms, it can be presumed that the leasing system was intended to defraud IPI's clients of additional money once they began manifesting said symptoms.[[/footnote]]



Foundation strategists agreed this represented an unprecedented opportunity to infiltrate the Society and finally acquire the item. However, given the difficulty in securing the mission objective from Imperial Purple Imports' security personnel, the only reliable method for the infiltrator to escape with the mission objective would be to use SCP-9205 and undergo the transformation themselves. 



The agent selected for this mission was Senior Agent William Shadfly. Agent Shadfly had been diagnosed with Stage 4 lung cancer three months prior to selection and chemotherapy had proved ineffective in treating his condition, leaving him with a projected life expectancy of less than a year; combined with his lack of personal connections outside the Foundation, it was believed that he would be the ideal candidate. Upon being approached for this role, Agent Shadfly accepted the offer, agreeing to be contained upon the successful completion of the mission in exchange for privileges normally denied to SCP-9205-A instances.



Agent Shadfly then contacted the Society under the name of "Bill Ambrosian", agreeing to provide the remaining funds needed to access to SCP-9205 in exchange for membership[[footnote]]The majority of these funds were garnered from the liquidation of Agent Shadfly’s home, cars, and bank account.[[/footnote]]. In return, he was provided with the address of a hotel in Manhattan where the Society was due to meet with IPI's courier.



On 27/10/24, Agent Shadfly was fitted with a subdermal tracking device, provided with forged documents, multiple sets of replacement clothing[[footnote]]In sizes projected to fit him post-transformation.[[/footnote]], a wig, a jar of makeup, an emergency signaling device (concealed in Agent Shadfly's wristwatch), and a cufflink dictaphone to ensure mission documentation, before being dispatched to New York City to commence the mission.
