[BEGIN LOG]



This is Agent William Shadfly, reporting from the Bellingwalsh Hotel, Manhattan.



I’ve met with the Society, all twelve of them, not counting the guards and private nurses. Membership is as expected: aging heiresses turned plastic surgery addicts, sagging corpocrats too limp for the boardroom hookers, rich mummies chasing eternal life… and now me. (//coughs//) The oldest of them’s in his late nineties. The youngest is fifty-five, so I don’t feel too out of place. (//chuckles weakly, coughs//)



I can confirm that they’re //not// pooling their funds because they’re poor: I recognize a few suspected members of Marshall, Carter & Dark’s client list here, along with real estate moguls, Wall Street wizards, business dynasty scions, Hollywood studio execs, and even the odd crime boss. Twelve of the biggest cheapskates in the West, and all of them too proud to accept the notion of growing old and dying like everyone else.



Bit more public than IPI's usual clientele, though. Odd, that.



The head of this little secret society is Patrick Thule, the political megadonor. No surprises there, given his interests. I’m assuming Thule’s used his own company to do some digging on me, but the Foundation’s forgeries are holding up for now... or maybe it's just money talking louder than sense.



Thanks to my donation, I’ve now been officially accepted as the thirteenth and final member of the Society of Iðunn's Orchard. (//cough//) Thule's bought out the entire fifteenth floor for our use, so we've settled in to wait for IPI's payment to be accepted.



It's deathly quiet up here. Dark, too: all the shutters have been lowered for secrecy's sake. None of the Society members are friends, so no socialization. There’s a boardroom with a huge media suite on this floor, but nobody’s used it. Instead, we're alone in our rooms, wasting time. Most of this crew are glued to their iPads, watching the markets. Me, I'm taking advantage of the lull to survey the floor, work out exit routes, calculate threat levels... and maybe finish reading //Fatal Beauty// if there's still time.



Hopefully, I won’t have to wait too long. (//cough//)



Shadfly out.

(//cough//) Payment’s been accepted. Thule gathered us in the boardroom to tell us that Imperial Purple Imports are sending a courier tomorrow.



Celebratory drinks were passed around. With my throat coughed raw, it was like drinking lye, so I didn't bother with most of mine. I don’t think that rubber plant will ever recover. 



Everyone else got drunk and let their guards down, so I listened. Pretty dull stuff: stocks, crypto, rivalries, politics, the state of their spouses’ genitals, what they’ll do once they’re young again…



Thule was gloating, going on about how he’ll still be young, handsome, and doing business when the presidents he crowned are “ashes in forgotten urns”. He's got his gimlet eyes set on Imperial Purple Imports next: supposedly, IPI's got a board of directors hidden away somewhere in Cardiff, and Thule wants them on his side as fellow megadonors for his next political coup, even claims that they've all used the Vessel themselves and been immortal for almost a century.



Of course, that'd imply that the IPI directors are all SCP-9205-A instances by now. I'd ask why they'd want to spread the madness further if they've experienced what their Vessel does firsthand, but then again, I remember how much the Society paid for a single use of the goddamn thing. Greed can explain an awful lot.



Interesting detail: Thule also claims that the Vessel isn’t the only anomalous item IPI have on offer, even says the board //created// SCP-9205 and the rest of their collection from scratch.



Yeah, it’s not hard to see why Marshall, Carter & Dark tipped us off about IPI's deal with the Society: they’re hoping we’ll wipe out a competitor while they swoop in and steal their inventory. 



As for how they found out... well, Thule has a long-standing beef with MC&D over stiffing him in some deal back in the early 2010s, so as soon as he got a sniff of eternal life, the prick called them just to rub it in their noses. Evidently, money can't buy you brain cells.



The only other Society member of any interest was Imelda Waldington, the mining magnate. She's easily the most distinctive member of this little club: plastic surgery addict, eighty years old by now, and the work she's had done hasn't aged well. She's had her face swathed in bandages since day one here.



Anyway, she mentioned seeing homeless children watching her on the way over, weird shadows following her limo through the underground parking lot, and some //very// young messengers loitering in the foyer.



Imperial Purple are keeping tabs on us. No surprises there. Hopefully, they haven’t figured out who I am, otherwise they'd have called off the deal… but there’s no way of being sure until tomorrow morning.



Shadfly out.

**DATE:** 29/10/24 (2:00 PM):

[BEGIN LOG]



(//music can be heard playing in the background. When Shadfly speaks, his voice is noticeably smoother and younger//)



It worked. Ceremonial bullshit aside, it was so simple: once Thule was done fondling SCP-9205 like his mistress’s tits, one of the guards passed it around the table, all of us took a handful of the gel, and by the time the jar had done a full circuit, the effects had set in.



It’s one thing to know the effects, but it’s another thing to see them for yourself. To see the skin go taut like a drumhead, the hair //erupting// out of the scalp, the shape of the body changing under the clothes… it’s the sort of thing you can’t do justice to by describing it. People were shedding pounds on the spot, gaining new muscle, standing up straighter, becoming //new//...



Once it was over, none of them could resist the mirrors. A few of them even stripped just to show off their bodies. Especially Waldington - practically ripped her bandages off just so she could admire herself minus fifty-five years of plastic surgery.



Even I couldn’t help taking a good look at myself. I didn’t realize it before, but back in my mid-twenties, I looked pretty damn good. And as for the cancer… well, I’m no oncologist, but I can tell it's gone: the coughing, the pain, the breathlessness, even the lingering effects of the chemo, all gone.



Of course, while we were busy admiring ourselves, the courier fucked off and took SCP-9205 with him. The guards didn't see them leave and none of Thule's flunkies downstairs saw them exiting via the lobby, so IPI definitely have a thaumaturge on the payroll. 



Still, all part of the plan: once the side-effects show up, the Society will try to rent it again. The third try will probably be my cue to steal it. By then, hopefully I'll be fully transformed.



(//pause//)



Funny thing: I couldn't help noticing how //warm// the Vessel felt while I was holding it, almost like it was...



(//Music changes, switching to louder, more upbeat song; Society members can be heard attempting to sing along with it//)



...Anyway, Thule's decided it's time to party, and the Society haven’t stopped for the last six hours. They’ve called in room service, drug dealers, hookers, even rented a karaoke machine: the entire floor is jumping. Even the guards are getting shitfaced.

**Incident Report (31/10/24):**



At 7:35 AM, Agent Shadfly activated his emergency beacon, prompting SCP agents remotely observing the Bellingwalsh Hotel to call for backup. 



Upon arriving on the 15th floor, agents found the bodies of three members of the Society of Iðunn's Orchards, the IPI courier, two private nurses employed by Society members, and all twenty-seven of the Society's guards. Analysis revealed that only 40% of the fatalities were due to gunshot wounds, the rest being due to bites from SCP-9205-A instances. 



The only survivors of the massacre still at the scene were two partially transformed Society members, who were immediately contained. Agent Shadfly, the remaining seven members, and SCP-9205 could not be located.



According to the two witnesses, after noticing their negative symptoms returning for the second time, the Society had correctly assumed that they were being defrauded by IPI. Soon after, they became convinced (erroneously) that the only way to make SCP-9205's effects permanent was to claim sole full-time ownership of it. 



When the IPI courier arrived at the boardroom for the third and final time, numerous Society members drew concealed firearms and attempted to steal SCP-9205 at gunpoint, resulting in a standoff that only ended when Agent Shadfly dropped from a ventilation shaft and successfully dislodged the item from Patrick Thule's grip.



In the ensuing gun battle, all parties involved tried to seize SCP-9205 for themselves or stop the others from claiming it, resulting in numerous fatalities and injuries. In the confusion, Mrs Imelda Waldington was able to escape with SCP-9205.



As soon as this was noticed, the combatants left the area in an attempt to pursue Mrs Waldington, with the surviving Society members exiting via the elevator, Agent Shadfly descending the stairwell at top speed, and the IPI guards leaping out the nearest window and onto the neighbouring rooftops. The two witnesses, having suffered immobilizing injuries during the fight, were left behind.



As Foundation agents arrived to contain the survivors and prevent media exposure, Operation Control received an emergency call from Agent Shadfly with a request for tracking services.

Thirty minutes after Agent Shadfly triggered his signaling device for the second time, Foundation backup arrived at the IPI safehouse in force.



Covertly introduced tear gas proved effective in nullifying the combat potential of SCP-9205-A instances: since none of the instances were alerted to the threat, their nictitating membranes did not deploy in time to protect their eyes from the gas, making it difficult for any of them to retaliate when Foundation operatives were authorized to break down the doors and attack.



As a result, though five of the twenty-three SCP-9205-A instances were able to escape through thaumaturgical means, twelve instances were successfully apprehended, along with three of the ten hired security guards on site. The remainder were terminated in battle, with no Foundation casualties resulting.



Following the cessation of hostilities, agents were able to cut their way through the loft's door with oxyacetylene torches: inside, they found the caged members of the Society of Iðunn's Orchards, Agent Shadfly, and SCP-9205.



With Imelda Waldington fully transformed, and Patrick Thule and the other surviving Society members completing their own metamorphoses over the course of the following hours, all were subsequently contained. Given the level of financial influence wielded by the Society members, the O5 Council has authorized operations to replace all transformed or deceased VIPs with body doubles loyal to the Foundation, both to ensure the preservation of the Veil and the reduction of any potential economic instability triggered by the disappearances.



Agent Shadfly was unconscious when located and did not awaken until he had been rehoused at Site 76 along with SCP-9205 and the other transformed Society members.

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** We only found out about IPI because they got greedy and broke their own rules blatantly enough for MC&D to find out. We couldn't find their board of directors, we don't know where the other branches are, we couldn't seize their other artefacts, and we can't stop their clients from buying shit that's //guaranteed// to turn them into monsters. Not exactly a worthwhile end to my career.

> 

> **Dr Percival:** That's not the only reason why you're in a bad mood, though, is it?

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** (//sighs//) No. When I touched SCP-9205 at the warehouse, I saw something. It might have just been a hallucination but... I think I'm beginning to understand.

> 

> **Dr Percival:** ...understand what? Your whaling dreams?

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** //Male parta male dilabuntur//. The IPI board of directors screwed up when they were making the Vessel, let a little too much of what it //once was// seep through to the finished article. Essence was stolen from it to replenish their beauty and their lives, so their beauty and their lives were stolen from them. The transformation was meant as an insult.

> 

> **Dr Percival:** You mean-

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** I //said// the damn thing was warm to the touch. Like a butchered whale in the ice, carved open, innards smoking... but somehow just alive enough to dream. 

> 

> //pause//

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** Not that it matters.

>  

> **Dr Percival:** Why not?

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** You heard what Bingham said. You //know// how many of the victims ended up working for IPI even after everything the company did to them. And I'm betting that Imelda's the only Society member with an ounce of regret for what they've become. Every bastard that shelled out for eternal life and beauty saw the Vessel's insult, and eventually said "yep, that's who I am! Let's have fun with it!"

> 

> **Dr Percival:** So what? It's not like they'd be the first altered individuals to embrace their change-

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** Embracing the change isn't the point! //They sank to new lows//. The transformation was meant to show them how petty and childish and monstrous they really were... //and they liked it.// That's why I'm feeling down, Philly. Because everything about the Vessel - its creation, IPI, the Society, my mission... it's all been a waste of time. (//sighs//) All in vain, if you like.

> 

> //pause//

> 

> **Dr Percival:** ...Do you want me to bring you that bottle of scotch you asked for earlier this week?

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** I don't need to drown my sorrows, Philly, I need //sleep//. When I wake, maybe I'll feel better about this whole pointless mess, maybe even enough to enjoy my retirement. Until then, I just want to sleep... and try to forget.

> 

> //Agent Shadfly lies down on his bunk and closes his eyes.//

> 

> **Agent Shadfly:** That's all for now, Dr Percival.

> 

> **Dr Percival:** (//sadly//) Very well then. Thank you for your time, A-1.

> 

> **<End Log>**

> 

> **Closing Statement:** Agent William Shadfly (retired) has been redesignated SCP-9205-A-1 and is no longer to be treated as a human being.

> 

> As per SCP-9205-A-1's testimony, SCP-9205 has been reclassified from Safe to Euclid in accordance with its possible status as a sentient object.

    X

    No more pencils, no more books
    No more teachers, dirty looks
    Out for summer, out 'til fall
    We might not come back at all
    ( School's Out - Alice Cooper )

    SCP-9210 - [HOMESCHOOLING]

    Troutmaskreplica's author page
    Popsioak's author page

Item Designation: SCP-9210

Classification: Keter

Special Containment Procedures: Foundation contacts in the United States Department of Education and similar agencies at the state, county, and local levels have implemented enrollment limits to avoid triggering SCP-9210. This has been successful in preventing JACK events for the past 25 years, though uncertainty as to whether or not SCP-9210 persists means that reclassification to Neutralized is denied.

In the event SCP-9210 does occur, any buildings in a 100 meter radius are to be demolished. Witnesses are to be amnesticized.

Cover stories are to be disseminated for both affected buildings and individuals, including Zeta-314 "Witness Protection," Beta-9818 "New Mall," and Gamma-871 "Sinkhole," among others. Field personnel will determine the appropriate cover story to use.

Description: SCP-9210 are anomalous zones in the continental United States mapping to enrollment boundaries1 of public elementary schools that enroll over 10 times the number of students as the next most populated.

After unknown criteria are fulfilled, homes that have at least one student enrolled in a school within SCP-9210 will spontaneously have an exact copy of the school building containing their child's class manifest 1 kilometer above their home. This results in total destruction of the home. The drop occurs in a way such that any inhabitants are left unharmed, though resulting debris may still cause injury. Copies created by SCP-9210 appear to be perfect replicas with all classroom supplies intact, and display little to no anomalous characteristics.2

This effect (designated a JACK event) affects suburban single-family homes, with apartments and homes in urban environments being unaffected. This effect typically occurs once per student. Repeat events are uncommon, but allow time for victims to evacuate.3

[Notice]

SCP-9210 was discovered following Foundation employee Dr. Lulu Kidd's home located in Nantucket, Massachusetts was destroyed in a JACK event. Dr. Kidd's child, age 5, was sick at home with mild influenza and was talking with his mother. Standard Foundation listening software installed in all employee homes recorded the following audio:

"But mooooooom, I can't miss class. Show-and-tell was today!"

At conclusion of this statement, a JACK event triggered, manifesting an exact copy of Nantucket Elementary School over Dr. Kidd's home, completely obliterating it.

The child was unharmed, but asked if a JACK event meant that school was cancelled. Low-dose amnestics were administered, and Dr. Kidd's family relocated closer to Site-23.

SCP-9216.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9216

Object Class: Thaumiel

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9216 is to be contained in standard humanoid living quarters at Field Site W-8, and provided with a Foundation computing station with level 3 privileges. Any requests it makes for amenities are to be reviewed and potentially approved by Head Researcher Mary Vollard. Any researcher on site may contact Doctor Vollard to request SCP-9216's assistance with their current case file.

Description: SCP-9216 is a sapient organic biomass. The individual tissues and cells that make up SCP-9216 resemble those of a human, and it often maintains a nearly human figure. Its actual anatomy is highly fluid, such that its organs, their number, and their relative placement around its body are highly variable; it is not uncommon for fully-formed facial features to emerge from the dermal layers of SCP-9216 over the course of several minutes, move across the surface of its skin, and then disappear in a similar manner. SCP-9216 is able to influence these "fluctuations" to some degree, and it is usually able to maintain at least one matching pair of eyes, one nose, and one mouth on its face.

SCP-9216 is a strong supporter of the Foundation and its mission, and has been contributing to the containment of other SCP objects since it was first brought to Field Site W-8, leading to its current Thaumiel designation. As Field Site W-8 is a "first destination" site for many objects of interest after being acquired by the Foundation, it is not uncommon to discover that new research subjects harbor lethal threats during initial testing. SCP-9216, with its redundant anatomy and willingness to serve the Foundation, makes an ideal examiner for new objects processed at the site, and has saved countless lives with its service.

A full list of the SCP objects that SCP-9216 assisted with is available upon request from Site Director Graham.

Addendum 1: Biological test logs
Basic format:

Test performed
Observations
Dr. Vollard's notes

Test 1:

Dermal tissue collection
Organic matter was collected by Dr. Vollard via cutting a 0.72g piece of flesh off the subject's arm with a scalpel. No bleeding was observed from the wound, which quickly widened and converted into a nostril-like aperture in the subject's flesh. The collected sample was semi-solid, deforming readily like soft putty. Under a microscope, the cells making up the sample resembled malignant cancer cells.
There do not appear to be any of the more nasty pathogens that I might worry about from a Sarkic anomaly, which is a relief.

Test 2:

Cohabitation
In order to test if the subject has any deleterious effects on other organisms, a series of cohabitation trials were held, in which SCP-9216 shared its living quarters with various creatures of increasing similarity to humans. The creatures which SCP-9216 cohabited with (and their span of cohabitation) were, in order:
-Five lab mice. Time: 2 weeks.
-One rooster, one hen, and all eggs produced over the cohabitation period. Time: 2 weeks.
-D-3469. Time: 1 month.
After each trial, the cohabiting creature(s) were quarantined for a month. No creature displayed any negative effects from the cohabitation trials.
All creatures panicked like mad the first day. I can't say I think that is an anomalous effect. The D class, especially, did not like the idea of sharing a cell with a monster, but they calmed down when they realized it was a month of leave from regular testing. At the end, they even said they'd miss SCP-9216 — apparently, it was the best cellmate they've had at the Foundation. Hah!

Test 3:

Malleability
The subject was presented with a square wire mesh, with holes approximately 1cm to a side, and was asked to press their hand through the mesh. The subject complied, and was able to pass the mesh through the flesh of their hand. Then, the subject was given a wooden dowel, 0.2m long, and 3cm in diameter. They were asked to pass the dowel through the midpoint of their forearm, as a means to probe the rigidity of their internal structure. The subject attempted to pass the dowel through their forearm, but this caused their arm to detach from their body past the dowel. The wad of flesh immediately lost its shape upon contact with the table, "splattering" in a viscous, semi-fluid manner, and causing the subject visible discomfort. The mass of flesh surged back towards the subject after a moment, rejoining the arm and reforming the missing appendage. The test was aborted due to the emotional response of the subject.
The subject was unused to parts of their flesh separating, and quickly panicked. The test did establish that we have a subject who can pass through fine meshes, and it suggested they are malleable enough to squeeze into small gaps as well. If we want to keep this subject contained, it may serve us to earn compliance from them. That is likely cheaper than sealing off every crack in their cell so they can't slither out.



[Automated alert: This file has been randomly selected for routine auditing by RAISA. This message will be automatically cleared once the audit concludes.]

[Automated alert: RAISA has determined this file needs further review. Edits have been locked, and a RAISA case specialist has been dispatched to resolve any issues. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.]

You are accessing this file from a privileged device, and are cleared to view the current RAISA investigation log for this file.

Open RAISA investigation log 9216-A
Welcome, Agent Ambrose.

NOTICE FROM THE FOUNDATION RECORDS AND INFORMATION SECURITY ADMINISTRATION

This file has been heavily tampered with, with almost all supplementary files displaying some signs of forgery, dissembly, or post-facto alteration of important details.

This investigation is no longer just an audit. It concerns the ability of RAISA to maintain the integrity of Foundation records in the face of a malicious internal actor, and as such, is both core to our mission statement, and a display of our skills as a department.

To the newcomers to this case: read through the items below, in their entirety, before reporting for duty to Agent Ambrose. Pay particular intention to item 0, which was recovered from Field Site W-8's security systems. It should make clear the nature of this investigation.

— Maria Jones, Director, RAISA

ITEM 0: Inciting evidence
Surveillance from Theory Room 3, Field Site W-8.

Video Log Transcript

Start time: 20:36:53, 12 Mar 2018

[BEGIN LOG]

The room is a modified break room, with several blackboards covering the walls, and a central conference table. The blackboards are full of writing, and there are papers spread across the table. There are two entities in the room, seated at the table a few chairs apart, each near a different stack of papers. The first is Sr. Researcher Angela Heinz, while the second is SCP-9216. Both are dressed in standard issue attire for researchers. Such attire is forbidden for SCP objects.

At the beginning of the recording, Heinz is scribbling on a piece of paper, while SCP-9216 is reading a printout. SCP-9216 maintains the components of a general facial expression on the front of its head for the entire recording, and appears to display the same amount of focus as Researcher Heinz. After some time, SCP-9216 crumples up their paper and tosses it at Heinz, making a frustrated grunt. Its voice is roughly human.

SCP-9216: Heinz, that's another dud. I'm telling you that this won't be on SCiPNET. It's conventional science.

Heinz looks up, scowling.

HEINZ: Already? We usually finish the internal review before you start moaning.

SCP-9216: Internal review is for nonstandard science. This is plastics. I think they use plastics out in the real world.

Heinz snorts, and looks back at her scratchwork, muttering.

HEINZ: Fine, if you want to trawl civilian journals, then do it. I feel like I'm on to something here.

SCP-9216 looks at them for a moment, before getting up and exiting theory room 3. It returns roughly thirty seconds later, carrying a Foundation-issue laptop. Heinz does not look up as it sits back down, instead staring at her own page. SCP-9216 opens the laptop, and begins tapping the table impatiently as it starts up. After several minutes, it glances at Heinz.

SCP-9216: Your approach is working, you said?

HEINZ tosses her pencil down the table.

HEINZ: I said I thought I was on to something.

SCP-9216: Something changed, then?

HEINZ: Fine. Fine! I'll get my laptop, Vollard.

[END LOG]

Item 1: AIC alert to Maria Jones

From:
To:
CC:
Subject:
wilbur.aic@scp.int
jones@scp.int
none
ALERT: Compromised documentation, SCP-9216

Director Jones,

A routine audit of footage at Field Site W-8 has revealed evidence that documentation related to SCP-9216, an anomalous humanoid contained at the site, is of questionable integrity. I recommend RAISA personnel be sent to the site immediately. To re-establish the integrity of documents surrounding SCP-9216, I suggest agents be directed to answer the resolve the following issues I have found during my audit:

  1. The subject is designated as Thaumiel, but the only listed reason for this in extant documentation is that the subject is cooperative, and has somewhat unusual physiology. This does not meet the standard 'Three-Step' Thaumiel criteria, and is at best a major error in classification by the subject's head researcher.
  2. The supplementary files available to me are missing any record of the anomaly's acquisition. While some older anomalies simply have not digitized the physical paperwork and the Foundation allows physical copies to suffice, in this particular case I would like the copies digitized.
  3. While there are abundant logs of SCP-9216's efforts in helping to contain other anomalous objects, tests of its own safety are minimal, which raises concerns when given the amount of exposure it has to other researchers, as well as to other anomalous objects. Were such tests ever done?
  4. In footage from 12 March 2018, an employee, Senior Researcher Heinz, was observed referring to SCP-9216 as "Vollard." This is the surname of Senior Researcher Mary Vollard, who is also the head researcher on file for SCP-9216. In the same footage, SCP-9216 is seen to exit and re-enter theory room 3 using a Foundation key card at time 20:41:15. Site security logs confirm that SCP-9216 did so using Senior Researcher Mary Vollard's keycard. Why was SCP-9216 referred to with this surname, and why did a Foundation researcher permit an anomalous object to use a Level 3 keycard?
Wilbur.aic
RAISA automated search construct
Secure, Contain, Protect

Item 2: Field Site W-8, new researcher Q&A
Agent Will Ambrose arrived at Field Site W-8 on 14 March 2018, with a microphone and camera concealed on his person. His visit was unannounced, and was meant to gather information without alerting anyone to the active investigation. When he arrived, he found the site was holding an orientation for new employees, and opted to attend in order to learn more about the work culture on-site. When the various personnel were split into groups, Agent Ambrose chose to follow the session for new research staff.

Video Log Transcript

Start time: 10:03:22, 14 Mar 2018

[BEGIN LOG]

The room is clearly meant for presentations, and at least fifty people are seated in rows before a projector. Agent Ambrose is standing by the rear door to the auditorium, and has a vantage of the whole room. He is facing the projector screen, which rolls up as people politely clap at the end of the "Site Clearances and You" presentation. Director Graham, a portly, balding man in his fifties, approaches the podium. He beams at the audience.

GRAHAM: Alright, everyone, we are coming up on the end of our orientation, and tomorrow you'll all be receiving your lab assignments. I know many of you are recent hires, and maybe you are nervous about jumping into lab work with the Foundation. Maybe you are curious about some of the differences I mentioned in how a field site is different from regular sites they taught you about in onboarding. Maybe you just have a question about site culture here.

Well, whatever it is, we have this last hour reserved for a "no stupid questions" Q&A. I mean it. I'll explain the Foundation handbook if you want. We want you comfortable with the general stuff, because you would not believe the specifics you have to deal with at a Field Site.

A hand rises near the front of the room. Graham calls out to them.

GRAHAM: You, there. Speak up, now!

ATTENDEE: Um, during the tours, our guide told us we can test dangerous stuff on an SCP we have here. Is that true? I thought cross-testing SCPs was banned.

Graham laughs, and turns to an agent by the front door. Graham motions at them, and the agent exits the room.

GRAHAM: Oh boy, that's the first question… five years running now! So, no, we do not test on an SCP, although, SCP-9216 is one of our most treasured containment assets at this site, and they are involved in testing here. Not tested on, though!

The agent returns to the room, and there are scattered gasps as SCP-9216 enters the room behind them. As before, it is dressed in standard Foundation researcher attire. It walks up to Graham's side, hands thrust in its pockets.

GRAHAM: Everyone, this is SCP-9216. She has assisted with more files than some of you will see in your entire careers here. Do you have anything you want to say to them?

SCP-9216: Eh, hello everyone. I'm SCP-9216. You can call me that, it's fine, and yes, I tested, you can't catch… whatever I've got. I have been here a long time, doing research work, and I really don't want to see anyone get hurt. If you get something strange in your lab, or you just want some extra help, Director Graham put me on the site directory, somehow, and you can just message me there to ask if I can collaborate. Don't be shy. Is that good?

GRAHAM: It's perfect. I'd recommend every one of you to consider her offer, there are a lot of researchers that owe their careers here to SCP-9216. Does anyone have any questions for her? … no? Well, alright, you can go. Thank you for coming.

SCP-9216: Of course. I'm sure I'll see some of you around.

[END LOG]

Item 3: Excerpt from the personnel file of Sr. Researcher Mary Vollard, Director Graham's comments

Annual review, 2010
Another year of exemplary output from M. Vollard. She celebrated her 25th anniversary with the Foundation this past October, and it took some urging to get her to take a week off to enjoy the milestone. I am thankful she came back so quickly, though; one of the new hires had improperly stored what he failed to recognize as some Maxwellist tech in an unsecured server room, and M. Vollard caught it in her first hour back. Poor kid got his ear shouted off, but I can't say I can blame her. That's a good segue:

We received three workplace complaints about M. Vollard since last year, down significantly from the seven we received when we lost H. Vollard in 2002. Two of the complaints came from younger, more inexperienced researchers, new enough to the site to get blindsided by her temper, and one came from A. Heinz. The latter was resolved with a third-party mediator, but I suspect it was just a stunt from A. Heinz to get under M. Vollard's skin, as per usual. Both parties declared the issue resolved, though, and the mediator signed off, so no disciplinary action was taken.

M. Vollard also completed a training course on stewardship of sentient anomalous objects, as mandated by the Ethics Committee, following the loss of object B-2332 in a breach due to what the investigators termed "an overzealous containment response." I will not comment on the appropriateness of her response, but I stand behind M. Vollard as one of our most senior and trusted researchers, and stress to the committee the need for rapid action at a Field Site. I have faith she will continue to uphold Foundation principles going forward.

Item 4: Interview 1 with Director Graham
Prior to this interview, Agent Ambrose had flagged a small assortment of files related to Field Site W-8 for review in order to conceal his interest in SCP-9216 specifically. Agent Ambrose claimed the files were flagged automatically by an outdated .AIC, and said he wished to confirm several details of the files with the director as a bureaucratic formality. The only relevant portion of the interview relates to SCP-9216 itself, which is excerpted below.

Video Log Transcript

Start time: 1:23:57, 14 Mar 2018

[BEGIN LOG]

AMBROSE: … very good. Thank you for your patience so far, Director Graham. Now, next, I see… SCP-9216. Oh, yes, the Thaumiel. Between you and me, the file was probably just fine, but admin recently pushed out some new regulations, and now Wilbur is flagging anything that doesn't comply with a two-week old code.

GRAHAM: Again? That must be on us, really sorry. We have been running lean for some time now, so it must have slipped by some of the researchers. I'll need to—

AMBROSE: It's fine, Director Graham. I'm here now, so why don't we step through the checklist together, and see what needs to be corrected?

GRAHAM: By all means.

AMBROSE: Wonderful. Now, let's see… First, Wilbur seems to have a problem with the Thaumiel designation itself, says it does not meet the Three-Step criterion. Are you familiar with that?

GRAHAM: Can't say I am. Back when I was in the lab, I never did work on anything above Euclid.

AMBROSE: That's quite alright. It just means that there is not enough information in the file about why SCP-9216 should be Thaumiel. It seems like the object has a talent for containment, but it isn't anomalous, and Thaumiels need to be anomalously good at containment, if that makes sense.

GRAHAM: Oh, oh, yes, I see.

AMBROSE: So, what is the anomalous skill SCP-9216 has for containment? It is fine if there is none, it just means the object was filed back when we were more lax, and we can reevaluate it as needed, so—

GRAHAM: Oh, no, doesn't it say, in the file? It's very good, very good at Sarkic anomalies, you see.

AMBROSE: Good at?

GRAHAM: Oh, sorry, good at handling. I mean that, well, the anomaly is Sarkic itself — perfectly safe of course, that should be in the logs —

AMBROSE: It is, yes.

GRAHAM: — and that makes it very resilient to other Sarkic anomalies. If you're already made out of putty, they can't really, ah, warp you more.

AMBROSE: I see. Is there a reason this is not in the file?

GRAHAM: It isn't? I'll have a word with the head researcher after this.

AMBROSE: Senior Researcher Mary Vollard?

GRAHAM: Yes, her. Excellent, wonderful employee, but not the best at administrative work. Some of the other files you asked me about are hers as well. She must have been getting worn out lately. I should have her workload lightened.

AMBROSE: That would be a good idea. That aside, Wilbur also flagged the file as missing an acquisition record. He is being rather stubborn with it, so would it be possible for you to upload a copy of it?

GRAHAM: Of course, it should be in storage somewhere. I'll ask Mary to handle that too.

Item 9: Summary of chemical findings

After the preceding interview, SCP-9216's cell was examined. It contains several metal surfaces with which SCP-9216 makes frequent contact. Each displayed signs of chemical etching consistent with exposure to a weak acid, such as dilute hydrogen chloride. The site employs metal door handles, and in areas which SCP-9216 frequents, the same signs of etching were visible.

Security footage from the interview was scoured, and it was verified that the table had no visible defects before the interview. The damage incurred was very shallow, only stripping the top layer of metal, but was still visible to the naked eye. Environmental testing determined this to be the result of a dilute solution of hydrochloric acid, with some organic compounds found in the human stomach mixed in.

There are no mentions of chemical excretions in SCP-9216's file.

AMBROSE: Sounds reasonable. Well, that's the last box I needed to check to conclude the investigation. Thank you very much for you cooperation.

Ambrose begins to stand.

SCP-9216: What is going to happen to me?

AMBROSE: Hm? Isn't that obvious? You'll be reclassified properly, and recontained somewhere else. Likely with restricted privileges.

SCP-9216: Is there any chance I can remain here, and keep working?

AMBROSE: Someone with as much experience as yourself should know better than to ask that. Besides, it is not Foundation policy to explain our containment protocols to the objects we contain.

SCP-9216: After all I've been through, can't you humor me?

Ambrose sits back down.

AMBROSE: After all you've been through? Do you mean transgressing for eight years against Foundation codes that you yourself once followed? Or, do you mean creating a tangled mess that I have spent the past week teasing apart? If you wanted preferential treatment, you should not have falsified your file.

SCP-9216: You really think that would have made any difference?

AMBROSE: Pardon?

SCP-9216: I really doubt the Foundation would have treated me any different if I had surrendered at the start. I think they would've boxed me up and shipped me off just the same. There's an old Ethics Committee guideline about that: attacking staff should be punished, but the Committee recommended forgiveness, and lighter sentences, when there's a peaceful containment breach.

AMBROSE: … I have, perhaps, read that guideline.

SCP-9216: So, if you're saying it's not worth even thinking about me staying here now… there was never a hope. In fact, my chances should be better, since I've proven that I can still do the work like this, but you still think it's not going to happen.

AMBROSE: That was only my opinion. My involvement with your future is only to file this report.

SCP-9216: You could make a recommendation, couldn't you?

AMBROSE: Why should I? If I may be direct, you selfishly put this entire facility at risk because you wanted to pretend your life was the same as before. You compromised a slew of Foundation documents, and through this investigation, are wasting resources on cleaning up your mess. You seem like a drain on the Foundation, not an asset.

SCP-9216: You fucking worm.

AMBROSE: Again, you are not endearing yourself to the —

SCP-9216: You have the gall to say I'm a drain on the Foundation? I gave more to the Foundation than you ever will! No, I let the Foundation take more from me than you ever will, because I believed in it! My youth, my— my family, my chance at kids, no hobbies, no more love, no more sun on my skin, even the… the face in the mirror. Gone. All because I wanted to spare others. Because I wanted to keep them from what I had to face. I was locking up monsters, and because the Foundation made a mistake, and let some poor kid in a room with something scary, now I get caged up too? You don't think they should have shame? You wretched sack of shit. I gave more than my life to this place, and even when that life was gone, I kept giving, and giving, and giving!

AMBROSE: You compromised the entire site.

SCP-9216: What the hell does that even mean? I bet the Foundation won't change a single word of what I put in all those files I made, because it's damn good work and they know it! They'll just try and paper over me, so they can pretend they didn't just throw me away like a fucking candy wrapper when I needed them!

AMBROSE: SCP-9216, you are out of line! Be quiet!

SCP-9216 glares at Agent Ambrose, but goes silent. He stares back at her.

AMBROSE: The Foundation is not a storefront. It does not trade labor for recognition, or respect. It trades it for money, as every employer does. You tell me that you "gave" many things to the Foundation? That's called a job. You were compensated for everything you gave. In fact, you will be compensated one more time, as your Foundation life insurance policy will pay out to your next of kin as soon as the investigation concludes.

SCP-9216: You, you—!

SCP-9216 grimaces, and clenches its misshapen hands. It trembles, and pulls them close to its chest.

SCP-9216: Oh, this is pointless, isn't it?

AMBROSE: Pardon?

SCP-9216: Fighting. I really should know better. I know what I did when objects resisted like I just did: more bars, less amenities. Never more freedom.

AMBROSE: Treating anomalous objects like that sounds like a violation of Foundation guidelines. Thankfully for you, the Foundation will not punish you over transgressions from when you were in Foundation employ. Is that reassuring?

SCP-9216: You know, Agent Ambrose, you really are a model employee. Ah…

SCP-9216 looks down, placing its hands on the table. It fiddles with its digits; it has eleven, at the time of the recording.

SCP-9216: … this reminds me of when Henry died. I inherited all his projects, you know. It was a lot of paperwork, getting the names changed on everything. At the end, I had to meet with a RAISA agent to certify everything, and get the new cards. I remember he acted a lot like you. When I told him I was sorry for taking so long to finish, since I was handling the funeral, he just said, "it's fine." Not a word more about me, not sorry for my loss, nothing. I think I understand him now. He was just there to complete his job, and it didn't need him to understand or feel a thing about me. To him, there may as well have been nothing there in the chair opposite him.

Agent Ambrose shifts in his chair.

AMBROSE: He was likely from accounting, not investigations. A different department.

SCP-9216: He's probably been promoted by now. He seemed like a good worker, focused on the job. The kind the Foundation likes.

AMBROSE: I think we're done here.

Ambrose stands, pausing when he sees SCP-9216 is crying. It is staring at him.

SCP-9216: Agent Ambrose, I bet you'll be up for promotion soon. This investigation, you've managed it so well. I really had no chance. It'll reflect well on you.

AMBROSE: Perhaps. There's no way of knowing.

SCP-9216: Other people will ask you about this case, at least.

AMBROSE: Likely. Why do you mention it?

SCP-9216: Well, I just wanted to ask a stupid favor. If someone asks what the case was about, please don't tell them it was about SCP-9216. Just… say it was about Mary Vollard.

AMBROSE: I don't think I can—

SCP-9216: Please.

AMBROSE: … once it is revised, I will leave a note on your file about how you prefer to be addressed. Goodbye, SCP-9216.

Agent Ambrose exits the room. SCP-9216 remains seated, staring at the door, until site security arrive to take it away.

[END LOG]

SUBMITTED TO RAISA DIRECTOR MARIA JONES ON 22 MARCH 2018
PENDING RECLASSIFICATION
SCP-9216.raw_source: [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:dynamic-emails code=--]] **Item #:** SCP-9216 **Object Class:** Thaumiel **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9216 is to be contained in standard humanoid living quarters at Field Site W-8, and provided with a Foundation computing station with level 3 privileges. Any requests it makes for amenities are to be reviewed and potentially approved by Head Researcher Mary Vollard. Any researcher on site may contact Doctor Vollard to request SCP-9216's assistance with their current case file. **Description:** SCP-9216 is a sapient organic biomass. The individual tissues and cells that make up SCP-9216 resemble those of a human, and it often maintains a nearly human figure. Its actual anatomy is highly fluid, such that its organs, their number, and their relative placement around its body are highly variable; it is not uncommon for fully-formed facial features to emerge from the dermal layers of SCP-9216 over the course of several minutes, move across the surface of its skin, and then disappear in a similar manner. SCP-9216 is able to influence these "fluctuations" to some degree, and it is usually able to maintain at least one matching pair of eyes, one nose, and one mouth on its face. SCP-9216 is a strong supporter of the Foundation and its mission, and has been contributing to the containment of other SCP objects since it was first brought to Field Site W-8, leading to its current Thaumiel designation. As Field Site W-8 is a "first destination" site for many objects of interest after being acquired by the Foundation, it is not uncommon to discover that new research subjects harbor lethal threats during initial testing. SCP-9216, with its redundant anatomy and willingness to serve the Foundation, makes an ideal examiner for new objects processed at the site, and has saved countless lives with its service. A full list of the SCP objects that SCP-9216 assisted with is available upon request from Site Director Graham. **Addendum 1: Biological test logs** Basic format: [[table  style="border-collapse:collapse; max-width: 800px;"]] [[row]] [[cell style="font-weight:bold;padding: .3em .7em; text-align: center; border: 1px solid black; background-color: silver; width: 20%;"]] Test performed [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] Observations [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] //Dr. Vollard's notes// [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] **Test 1:** [[table  style="border-collapse:collapse; max-width: 800px;"]] [[row]] [[cell style="font-weight:bold;padding: .3em .7em; text-align: center; border: 1px solid black; background-color: silver; width: 20%;"]] Dermal tissue collection [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] Organic matter was collected by Dr. Vollard via cutting a 0.72g piece of flesh off the subject's arm with a scalpel. No bleeding was observed from the wound, which quickly widened and converted into a nostril-like aperture in the subject's flesh. The collected sample was semi-solid, deforming readily like soft putty. Under a microscope, the cells making up the sample resembled malignant cancer cells. [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] //There do not appear to be any of the more nasty pathogens that I might worry about from a Sarkic anomaly, which is a relief.// [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] **Test 2:** [[table  style="border-collapse:collapse; max-width: 800px;"]] [[row]] [[cell style="font-weight:bold;padding: .3em .7em; text-align: center; border: 1px solid black; background-color: silver; width: 20%;"]] Cohabitation [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] In order to test if the subject has any deleterious effects on other organisms, a series of cohabitation trials were held, in which SCP-9216 shared its living quarters with various creatures of increasing similarity to humans. The creatures which SCP-9216 cohabited with (and their span of cohabitation) were, in order: -Five lab mice. Time: 2 weeks. -One rooster, one hen, and all eggs produced over the cohabitation period. Time: 2 weeks. -D-3469. Time: 1 month. After each trial, the cohabiting creature(s) were quarantined for a month. No creature displayed any negative effects from the cohabitation trials. [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] //All creatures panicked like mad the first day. I can't say I think that is an anomalous effect. The D class, especially, did not like the idea of sharing a cell with a monster, but they calmed down when they realized it was a month of leave from regular testing. At the end, they even said they'd miss SCP-9216 -- apparently, it was the best cellmate they've had at the Foundation. Hah!// [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] **Test 3:** [[table  style="border-collapse:collapse; max-width: 800px;"]] [[row]] [[cell style="font-weight:bold;padding: .3em .7em; text-align: center; border: 1px solid black; background-color: silver; width: 20%;"]] Malleability [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] The subject was presented with a square wire mesh, with holes approximately 1cm to a side, and was asked to press their hand through the mesh. The subject complied, and was able to pass the mesh through the flesh of their hand. Then, the subject was given a wooden dowel, 0.2m long, and 3cm in diameter. They were asked to pass the dowel through the midpoint of their forearm, as a means to probe the rigidity of their internal structure. The subject attempted to pass the dowel through their forearm, but this caused their arm to detach from their body past the dowel. The wad of flesh immediately lost its shape upon contact with the table, "splattering" in a viscous, semi-fluid manner, and causing the subject visible discomfort. The mass of flesh surged back towards the subject after a moment, rejoining the arm and reforming the missing appendage. The test was aborted due to the emotional response of the subject. [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row]] [[cell style="text-align: left; padding: .3em .7em; border: 1px solid black"]] //The subject was unused to parts of their flesh separating, and quickly panicked. The test did establish that we have a subject who can pass through fine meshes, and it suggested they are malleable enough to squeeze into small gaps as well. If we want to keep this subject contained, it may serve us to earn compliance from them. That is likely cheaper than sealing off every crack in their cell so they can't slither out.// [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] _ **[Automated alert: This file has been randomly selected for routine auditing by RAISA. This investigation is no longer just an audit. It concerns the ability of RAISA to maintain the integrity of Foundation records in the face of a malicious internal actor, and as such, is both core to our mission statement, and a display of our skills as a department.
