For whom he nearly shattered the world. ]] ===== [[include :scp-wiki:info:start]] By [[*user CrazyCat25]] and [[*user AgentCheese]] ⚠️ **Content warning:** Contains themes of physician-assisted suicide [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:info-cw]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:sigma-plus]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:space]] [[include :scp-wiki:theme:cosmos]] [[module CSS]] #main-content {     background-color: rgb(var(--space-void)); } :root {     --header-title: "Secure Contain Protect";     --header-subtitle: "The Lady in the Lake"; [[/module]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:anomaly-class-bar-source |item-number= 9230 |clearance= 4 |container-class= euclid |disruption-class= vlam |risk-class= danger ]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:acs-animation]] ----- [[include component:image-block | name=https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/collab%3Acrazycat25-and-agentcheese/moonlit%20lake.jpg | caption=Photo taken of SCP-9230 | width=WIDTH-GOES-HERE]] **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9230 and SCP-9230-2 are surrounded by a perimeter fence, equipped with six SRAs[[footnote]]Devices that prevent changes to local baseline reality[[/footnote]], and monitored by drones. No personnel are allowed within 100 meters of SCP-9230. In case of unauthorized entry, MTF PSI-8 (The Silencers) is to be dispatched to terminate them. --Instances of SCP-9230-2 are to be denied access to SCP-9230.-- Instances of SCP-9230-2 are not to be interacted with without direct permission from site command. **Description:** SCP-9230 refers to a lake in western Bulgaria. Temporal displacement in the location around the anomaly causes the immediate area to maintain a consistent state of what would constitute midnight anywhere else. SCP-9230-1 is a humanoid entity inhabiting SCP-9230. SCP-9230-1 appears as a human female, with height of approximately 10 meters, blue skin and red eyes. Unidentified luminescent white matter serves as both hair (approximately 8 meters long) and dress of SCP-9230-1.  DNA samples are yet to be acquired. The entity possesses a high level of ontokinetic abilities, potential telepathic capabilities, and above average intellect. Individuals who come into contact with SCP-9230-1 have developed an immunity to amnestics. SCP-9230-2 refers to any individual residing in close proximity to SCP-9230. SCP-9230-2 instances display an above average lifespan. An unnamed village, inhabited by multiple SCP-9230-2 instances, has been built 200 meters away from SCP-9230. It is yet to be determined when the village emerged. **Discovery:** SCP-9230 was discovered on 27.03.2025. Two field agents, embedded within public society, overheard a group of hikers discussing their encounter with SCP-9230-1 and multiple instances of SCP-9230-2. --Subjects were administered Class-A amnestics.-- Subjects were terminated due to inefficiency of amnestics. A quarantine zone has been set up around SCP-9230, consisting of an on-site containment facility and six SRAs deployed in a hexagon around SCP-9230. **Addendum 9230-1:** [[div class="blockquote"]] **Date**: 8.04.2025 **Interviewer**: Dr. Alexander Ivanov **Interviewee**: POI-9230-1 **Notes:** The following is a transcript of an interview carried out by head of research on SCP-9230, Dr. Alexander Ivanov in the village near SCP-9230. A small platoon of guards was stationed nearby. The interviewee, an SCP-9230-2 instance, has been identified as Magdalena Tatianova, an elder and leader in SCP-9230-2 society ----- **Dr. Ivanov:** Good, uh, evening, ma'am. **POI-9230-1:** Evening, outsider. She warned us of your coming. Her sight does not end in the lake or our home. **Dr. Ivanov:** The anomaly's? **POI-9230-1:** Who else do you believe it would be? **Dr. Ivanov:** My apologies, ma'am. I am not acquainted with your culture, but I do wish to learn. **POI-9230-1:** Spare me your feigned interest. The only reason you wish to learn is because your masters told you to. Masters that would cage, torture and break us, were we not under her protection. **Dr. Ivanov:** I cannot speak for what site command and the O5 will do. I only need you to answer some questions and then I'll be gone for good. **POI-9230-1:** Very well, cold faced conqueror. Ask what you will and begone. **Dr. Ivanov:** I reckon given your isolation and circumstance you have developed a rather unique culture. Could you tell me about your people's beliefs and traditions? **POI-9230-1:** We have many a tale, most told to us by The Lady. She loves to tell us of her past when we are gathered around campfires.  I can hardly remember half the stories, but we have written them down.  Please wait a minute. //POI-9230-1 goes to the village. Several moments later she returns with a heavy book labeled "Tales of The Lady: Of the Primordium, the Abyss and the First Empire of Man".// **POI-9230-1:** Consider it an invitation to learn if you truly wish to. //Dr. Ivanov turns to a nearby guard and hands him the book to a guard.// **Dr. Ivanov:** Have this scanned for any cognitohazards and get the junior staff decompiling its contents. //Security guard nods and leaves.// **Dr. Ivanov:** Can you tell me about your traditions? Any holidays? Special occasions? **POI-9230-1:** For us each day is as special as the rest. We have no formal religion either. The Lady hates being worshipped, despises seeing people think of her as anything more than a friend and guide. That is not to say we don't have traditions. Every full moon the children aged from five to thirteen go to the lake and personally talk with The Lady. **Dr. Ivanov:** What do the entity and children talk about? **POI-9230-1:** The Lady refuses to tell us and the children swear an oath of secrecy before going to talk with her. **Dr. Ivanov:** You've been a child too and I doubt you're older than your goddess, so you should have done that and know, right? **POI-9230-1:** Yes. **Dr. Ivanov:** And you won't tell me? **POI-9230-1:** The oath still binds me and you are not dear enough to me to break it. **Dr. Ivanov:** I won't press into personal details. Gonna assume your lifestyle is a lot different. Can you describe it to me? **POI-9230-1:** Not as different as you think, except that we aren't slaves to overlords and get to live longer and healthier than anyone else. We do still toil and work, The Lady says that the greatest joy comes from personally creating new things, but we don't need to. She provides us with what we need and want. The most unusual thing is the place and that we get to visit her. **Dr. Ivanov:** How long do you live on average? **POI-9230-1:** I can't say there is an average. We can get ill, but The Lady always heals us. We don't age at all past adulthood. When we are sick of living and want to go live in The Lady's realm proper we just go. It's always a tearful goodbye. //Dr. Ivanov sighs.// **Dr. Ivanov:** That's the hardest part isn't it. "If you love someone you're gonna let them go." I've heard that a lot recently, yet I keep thinking "If that somebody loves me, why would she leave me?" //POI-9230-1 gives Dr. Ivanov a surprised look.// **Dr Ivanov:** Ah fuck, I am gonna ge- anyways, how did your people come here? **POI-9230-1:**  Our ancestors discovered the lake at least many millennia before your people had a kingdom, before any people had a kingdom, yet The Lady is far older still. **Dr. Ivanov:** Before any kingdom? How has nobody else stumbled upon it? **POI-9230-1:** None "stumble" upon it. They are drawn here by her grace. If she hadn't permitted your entry, you would have never found this place. **Dr. Ivanov:** And you aren't pleased by it, are you? **POI-9230-1:** I wasn't, but it seems I might have been wrong. How did you come to that conclusion? Who did you say goodbye to? **Dr. Ivanov:** It wouldn't be very professional of me to share personal details, ma'am. Let's stick to the topic. How has the entity helped you? **POI-9230-1:** The way only a true deity can: When plague came upon us, she made it beg for its own end. When we were without food, she grew silver trees with fruit that could fill your stomach for centuries with a single bite. When I was stillborn she took my spirit and gave it a body that could sustain it. **Dr. Ivanov:** This goddess of yours brought you back from the dead? Why did she make this exception? **POI-9230-1:** She did not make an exception. That is her greatest gift. We are all given life, even if the world would try to deny it to us. We know joy even as the rest of our home knows calamity and suffering. //Dr. Ivanov goes silent for a long time.// **Dr. Ivanov:** Are you certain this wasn't a dream? Some near death experience? **POI-9230-1:** As certain as can be, for I have seen it done to others. Not just newborns. Men and women recently fallen to illness, unable to go to her in time, have received new bodies for their souls. **Dr. Ivanov:** Then could I - No. No that's - ugh. Is there a chance I can see he-it. This goddess of yours? **POI-9230-1**: Follow me. //POI-9230-1 gets up and leads Dr. Ivanov into the village, when they are stopped by two security guards. Dr. Ivanov is escorted out of SCP-9230.// Note from Director Anesia: Dr. Ivanov is to be placed on temporary leave. Interviews with residents of SCP-9230's village are suspended until further notice. [[/div]] **Incident Report-9230-1:** [[div class="blockquote"]]] **Date:** 13.04.2025 **Location:** Containment site of SCP-9230 ----- Several SCP-9230-2 instances were observed approaching the containment site, carrying what was identified as an unhealthy SCP-9230-2 specimen. Video showed specimens being turned away, but was abruptly cut off. Hume readings showed unprecedented changes in local baseline reality. All traces of containment have disappeared from baseline reality. Security personnel stationed at SCP-9230's containment site have deserted the Foundation. MTF PSI-8 has been dispatched to deal with the deserters. ----- **Update:** On 16:04:2025 One of the deserters (now designated POI-9230-2) was captured. Subject scheduled for interview. ----- **Date:** 20:04:2025 **Interviewer:** Site Director Lena Anesia **Interviewee:** POI-9230-2 ----- **Director Anesia:** Good morning, Mister Shumaro. I hope the accommodations have not been too unpleasant. **POI-9230-2:** To be perfectly honest with you, it's better than I expected. I was ready to be tossed in with the D-class. Lord only knows I rubbed them the wrong way on a few occasions. **Director Anesia:** Glad to hear it, sir. Can you please tell me what happened at the containment site that made our recently promoted chief of security leave? **POI-9230-2:** After the site went into the astral plane the thing that lives in the lake came to us. We opened fire, but the bullets didn't even seem to faze it. We were sure these were our last moments, but that thing didn't kill us. It started talking with us. Asking about us. **Director Anesia:** What did you tell it? **POI-9230-2:** We didn't need to tell it a thing, but it wanted to hear us describe ourselves. It knew every fear, every hope and every wish we had. It reminded me of my father and mother. It reminded all of us of what we love the most. It reminded us that we are people and we can choose the cause we fight for. **Director Anesia:** You feel like the Foundation isn't a cause worth fighting for? Were it not for us this world would be gone by now. **POI 9230-2:** Not saying we aren't doing good work, but we are going about it the wrong way. What is the point of keeping the things that go bump in the night locked up, if we kill even more people than they do? **Director Anesia:** The only reason they haven't killed more is because they are safely locked up. **POI-9230-2:** The lesser of two evils is still an evil though. I know changing things this far in is a risk, but nothing ventured, nothing gained, right? **Director Anesia:** Pardon my saying so Mister Shumaro, but I find this idea to be incredibly selfish. You realize that such a drastic change is gambling the world itself right? If we are forced to abide the strictly moral choice it could lead to an uncontainable containment breach, not to mention the philosophical questions that would need to be answered before an action. **POI-9230-2:** Sure you can't always make the right call but we can at least try. Would it really put everything at risk if we don't kill or amnesticize anyone who gets in the way? The world may be safe the way things are, but should we really settle for being killers? Don't you always say our mission is to protect those who can't protect themselves? //Director Anesia goes silent and looks around.// **Director Anesia:** That is not up to me to decide. Thank you for cooperating and answering my questions, however. Now I think there's a matter we still need to discuss. **POI-9230-2:** If you have any humanity in you make it quick. **Director Anesia:** Make what quick? **POI-9230-2:** We both know you're gonna make me bite the bullet. **Director Anesia:** There's a saying: "History isn't what happened. It's what is believed to have happened." The way I see it there are two things that could have happened. One, as you said, you bite the bullet. Two - via some miracle the amnestic worked. You are an amnesiac ex-military and figure out your life from there. //POI-9230-2 goes silent for half a minute.// **POI-9230-2:** What's the catch? **Director Anesia:** Consider it a favor from a friend. //Director Anesia hands POI-9230-2 a syringe and a new ID card. POI-9230-2 hands over his credentials and records of the Foundation// **POI-9230-2:** Thanks boss. **Director Anesia:** I am not your boss any longer. **POI-9230-2:** Then consider this advice from a friend. Nothing ventured, nothing gained. What's the point of protecting the bodies of thousands if we stain our hearts and minds with the blood of hundreds. There's always a better way, ma'am. Sorry it took me so long to learn it. **Director Anesia:** Noted. Thank you for your years of service, Mister Shumaro. Consider yourself honorably discharged. //Director Anesia salutes. POI-9230-2 salutes back.// //Director Anesia turns off the recording// ---- **Note from Director Anesia:** I don't know if this creature really is benevolent, nor does it matter. Its manipulations could compromise the Foundation. The possibility of more desertions is highly likely under the current circumstances and considering the entity's capabilities it would be a needless waste of lives to send people there. The anomaly's clearance level will be raised to 4. [[/div]] **Addendum-9230-2:** [[div class="blockquote"]] The following footage comes from the security camera in Director Anesia's office **Date:** 26:04:2025 ----- //Director Anesia looks up from a document.// **Director Anesia:** Doctor, not only has this been discussed at length, it could be argued you are  the reason for the new security measures. Your interview with POI-9230-1 gives me a good reason to suspect you were compromised. **Dr. Ivanov:** I get that I was less than professional, but if we just shut down any and all research on the anomaly, we're potentially missing out on on game world-changing secrets. **Dr. Anesia:** And what exactly do you consider these secrets to be worth, Mister Ivanov? **Dr. Ivanov:** Think what the Foundation could do if it learned how this creature managed to erase the entire site. Not to mention that if it can really heal living organisms from anything this could bring about an age without...terminal illnesses. **Director Anesia:** I can see the potential here, doctor. I disagree with you that it's worth the risk though. We still don't know even half of it's capabilities. I refuse to simply throw bodies into a meat grinder. While you are here, do me a favor and stop lying. I can tell there's a more personal reason you want to go back there. Speak plainly. //Dr. Ivanov goes silent and takes a deep breath.// **Dr. Ivanov:** Fine. I want to know if this...thing can really bring them back. **Director Anesia:** There will be no disciplinary action, if you're worried about that, but I am going to be assigning you a psychiatrist  and three years of paid leave. **Dr. Ivanov:** If four years weren't enough, why do you think three would make a difference? There are wounds time and help just can't heal, ma'am. **Director Anesia:** I am not letting you toss your life away for a fool's hope. There's a reason we don't use anomalies for therapy or medicine. You are vulnerable and being lured into a potential flytrap. **Dr. Ivanov:** If this fool's hope kills me so be it. I am not asking you to understand. I don't want you to understand what it's like to lose a loved one, but have a heart and try to understand. Living with your better half gone. That's not a life worth living. **Director Anesia:** I may not have a family, but don't think I don't know what it's like to lose people you value. I had parents. I have employees. You are asking me to put my head in the bag so you can beg a creature we don't know anything about to do something we can't be sure it can actually do. //Director Anesia breaths in deeply.// **Director Anesia:** Why do you think I am gone at least one day of the week, Alex? **Dr. Ivanov:** Why? //Director Anesia points to her cupboards. Every one of them is stacked with photos of her with other people dressed in black in front of a newly dug grave. Dr. Ivanov goes silent.// **Director Anesia:** Every week it's another. Every time it's worse. Jess was so young, Mihail's twins had their eleventh birthday just a week prior. I refuse to lose any more people than I have to. **Dr. Ivanov:** I'm sorry you endure all of that. I am sorry I might be asking you to bury me. I am sorry I need to ask you this. If you really know what it's like, please, help a grieving man get his closure once and for all. //Director Anesia closes her eyes, breathes deeply and stamps Dr. Ivanov's request to continue his work with "approved".// **Director Anesia:** Not a word of this to anyone. It's an interview for information and nothing more. [[/div]] **Addendum-9230-3:** [[div class="blockquote"]]] The following is a transcript of an interview of POI-9230-1, carried out by Dr. Alexander Ivanov. **Date:** 27.05.2025 **Time:** 11:30pm **Interviewer:** Dr Alexander Ivanov **Interviewee:** POI-9230-1 ----- **Dr. Ivanov:** Hello again Magdalena. Sorry for how our last meeting went. **POI-9230-1:** No need for apologies, doctor. You have come to meet her, yes? //Dr. Ivanov nods.// **POI-9230-1:** It's not the longest walk. I take it you need something from her? **Dr. Ivanov:** I need some hope and closure **POI-9230-1:** Everybody needs those things. **Dr. Ivanov:** Think your deity will be cross with me fo- **POI-9230-1:** No. Her wrath is only given to the greatest of monsters. I've gotten to know you aren't one of them. **Dr. Ivanov:** That's reassuring. I never really got to ask, but what exactly can I expect? **POI-9230-1:** She is hard to describe. Imagine being in the presence of the world itself. Every river, mountain and star is right there, listening. You think it would be terrifying, but it isn't. There is no need to be something you aren't. You cannot be something you aren't near her. She sees through you: knows your thoughts, your life, your struggles, your sorrows, your joys. Despite this she never judges, only comforts. **Dr. Ivanov:** What do you want to do in life? //POI-9230-1 turns to Dr. Ivanov, eyebrow raised.// **Dr. Ivanov:** I've gotten to know your goddess and culture better than I know you. **POI-9230-1:** Did you read the book I gave you? **Dr. Ivanov:** Sorry, but no. Been busy begging my boss and people are still testing to see if it's safe. **POI-9230-1:** I want to see our home restored. I want to see The Lady outside The Lake. I want to walk upon The Moonlit Sea, learn to capture moonlight in gem, see the Abyss King rise from the depths and make the sky purple. I want to see pain go away forever with all the agony our creators gave to us. //POI-9230-1 and Dr. Ivanov walk in silence for several minutes.// **POI-9230-1:** Why do you need closure if you don't mind? **Dr. Ivanov:** I lost two things I can't live without. //Dr. Ivanov pulls out a photo from his coat. He, a woman and a child are at the beach smiling.// **POI-9230-1:** They look wonderful. **Dr. Ivanov:** They were. My gremlin and my guardian angel. She hated that nickname so much. I pestered her with it for a month after I got out of the hospital. **POI-9230-1:** The hospital? **Dr. Ivanov:** I was playing with that little imp when she was at work once, knights and bandits. I made the mistake of letting my guard down and that little goblin jammed a plastic sword into my eye. I yelled at him not to call the ambulance. but the little shit was already on the phone and it turned out the paramedics were the least of my worries. He had called his mother. **POI-9230-1:** I take it you had a very protective guardian angel. **Dr. Ivanov:** Protective doesn't cut it. She argued with the doctor in the hospital until security kicked her out, then started calling until they blocked all ten of her phone numbers. In the end I pulled some strings so she could come. She and that gremlin were there, eight hours a day, every day of the week, serving me home-cooked food instead of the garbage the doctors had and making sure I was never bored. //POI-9230-1 goes silent. Dr. Ivanov sheds several tears.// **POI-9230-1:** Remember when I told you about how we visit the Lady as children and swear a vow of secrecy? **Dr. Ivanov:** Yeah? **POI-9230-1:** When I visited her, she asked me what I want more than anything. Those were the worst days of my life. My parents had chosen to leave the world a week prior. I told her that I wanted my mother and father back, if for just a little while longer. She took me by the hand and lifted me into the sky. The world grew smaller and smaller. I saw it was but a small island in an endless ocean. Then I saw a group of people sitting and talking in that ocean. She brought me down to them and there were my parents. They hugged me so tightly. I didn't wanna let go "The world needs you, my dear.", said my mother "Our part is done. We need to rest now.", my father chimed in "How can I live without you?" I asked "You are never without them, my child. Would you rather they see you broken and withered from grief as you come back to them, or tired and relieved with stories, memories and lessons to share? Would you rather they shed tears of mourning for a lost daughter, or of joy for a child returned home from a long journey?" said The Lady. //POI-9230-1 wipes the tears from her eyes.// **POI-9230-1:** So I will finish the journey, even if I must crawl on my chin to the final stretch. //Dr. Ivanov and POI-9230-1 reach the edge of SCP-9230.// **POI-9230:** Now it's your time to receive a gift. //POI-9230-1 walks away. A bright light envelopes the screen and the recording is cut off.// [[/div]] **Addendum-9230-4:** [[div class="blockquote"]]] The following is a transcript of an interview of SCP-9230-1, carried out by Dr. Alexander Ivanov. **Date:** 27.05.2025 Time: 12:00 am **Interviewer:** Dr Alexander Ivanov **Interviewee:** SCP-9230-1 ----- **SCP-9230-1:** Greetings, my child. I must say I anticipated your arrival sooner. **Dr. Ivanov:** Yeah, my superiors were quite concerned after what you did last month and I didn't exactly help myself on that front. You'd be shocked at the amount of paperwork I had to go through after that. Not to mention the lectures! Well, now I'm finally here. Seeing that book people compiled of your stories, I'll assume you enjoy chatting. **SCP-9230-1:** You assume correct, dear. **Dr. Ivanov:** What exactly are you? Goddess is a bit of a broad term. **SCP-9230-1:** That is up to you to decide, but please refrain from labeling me that. **Dr. Ivanov:** What's the problem with "goddess", if you don't mind? **SCP-9230-1:** The greatest monsters I have seen coveted it like a jewel. I am no fear mongerer. I do not wish for any gifts. A mother does not take from her own children. **Dr. Ivanov:** How old are you? Who are these monsters? **SCP-9230-1:** I cannot answer your first question, my child, for you speak in terms and concepts that do not apply to me. Time started at the dawn of existence, yet I was ancient before it was even a single, dying spark, dancing in the nothingness. I will not answer your second question, for you have already met my enemies. Worms and maggots who believe themselves to be kings, yet cower the moment one greater than them challenges their right to treat their creations as toys. A great pity that some of you still yearn for the love of beings that will never find you worthy of it. **Dr. Ivanov:** You mean like the Sarkic cults and the Church of the Broken God? **SCP-9230-1:** Indeed. The Broken Goddess, The Great Dragon and all the rest look upon you and see a future where you exist as nothing more than toy solders in needless war. A future me and my husband swore, would never come to pass. **Dr. Ivanov:** How do you feel about people worshipping them? Also who is your husband? **SCP-9230-1:** How would you feel about Simion being kidnapped and brainwashed into becoming a solder for the Foundation? What would you do in that case? //Dr. Ivanov goes silent.// **Dr. Ivanov:** ...I'd break him out of there with my bare hands. Try my luck with the O5s if I get the chance. **SCP-9230-1:** And you are here now to bring him and Maria out of my realm. To take from the one to whom you owe your very soul and life. To claim that which belongs to death herself. //Dr. Ivanov takes a deep breath and looks straight into SCP-9230-1's eyes without flinching.// **Dr. Ivanov:** If you really are better than others of your caliber, you will do this for me. //SCP-9230-1 closes its eyes.// **SCP-9230-1:** I would, but I have a question for you first. Did you ever ask yourself what they wanted? **Dr. Ivanov:** Wha-tha-what do you mean? I risked my hide at every turn to save them. I personally cu- **SCP-9230-1:** I am not denying you tried to save them, but did you ever consider that they didn't want to keep on living? **Dr. Ivanov:** I-nobody woul-certainly not her. She loved life so much, she wouldn't just- and he- **SCP-9230-1:** If you were in her place, would you want to live? Would you want to stay a prisoner in your own body, always burning with the sensation of your own being turning on itself and being rent open with a scalpel? **Dr. Ivanov:** No, but I wouldn't be so selfish as to give up, knowing how much my death would hurt. I'd rather have her ill, but here than gone from my life. **SCP-9230-1:** Truly? Then it brought you less pain seeing her in tears, begging for me than it does knowing she is in peace?! Perhaps she made a mistake devoting herself to such a cruel, egotistical man. Did you ever love her, or did you merely desire her? **Dr. Ivanov:** I-no. It didn't bring me joy, but I could have healed her! I could have figured something out! I could have- **SCP-9230-1:** You could not have. //SCP-9230-1 puts a hand on Dr. Ivanov's shoulder.// **SCP-9230-1:** Your efforts were beyond commendable, but hear the words of one that gave her own life to bring forth seven new ones. No matter how hard and nobly you fight, there are things you cannot defeat, events you cannot prevent. **Dr. Ivanov:** I refuse to accept that the only thing I can do is roll over and accept that she is gone. **SCP-9230-1:** Good, because it's not. You are a master of your own faith and mark my words, you will see them again. Much, much sooner than you think. //A tear falls from Dr. Ivanov's eye.// **Dr. Ivanov:** Thank you. If you don't mind, what caused you to...become like this? //SCP-9230-1 laughs, several tears falling from it's face.// **SCP-9230-1:** A story for another time, my child. Right now I have a task for you. Try to better yourself for your reunion. Maria and Simion would be disappointed to see their husband and father like this. **Dr. Ivanov:** Yeah. I guess I need some alone time. Can't believe I claimed to love her, yet effectively tortured her. **SCP-9230-1:** The only unforgivable crime, my child, is one for which forgiveness is not sought. **Dr. Ivanov:** Thank you. For the advice and...everything. **SCP-9230-1:** You are most welcome and do visit me again one day. Or don't. All of you will come back to my embrace one day. //Dr. Ivanov turns off the recording.// [[/div]] **Incident Report-9230-2:** [[div class="blockquote"]] **Date:** 11:06:2025 **Location:** Dr. Alexander Ivanov's residence Anomalous events were captured via Dr. Ivanov's security system. Suspected link to SCP-9230-1. ----- **11:00pm:** Dr. Ivanov is seen working on his computer. Light fluctuations in Hume level. **11:10pm:** The moon's glow intensifies drastically.  Hume levels on rapid descent. **11:15pm:** Mobile task force Lambda-5 dispatched to location. **11:20pm:** Connection with mobile task force Lambda-5 is lost. **11:30pm:** Substance believed to be water starts flowing from the ground outside the house. **11:40pm:** Dr. Ivanov's yard is fully submerged. **11:50pm:**  Two humanoid beings emerge from the water. One is noticeably taller and guides the other. **11:52pm:** The taller entity rings the doorbell. **11:53pm:** Dr. Ivanov opens the door. Dr. Ivanov smiles and embraces Entity-9230-1 and 2, openly crying. **Dr. Ivanov:** There you are...I was beginning to think she lied. //Entities embrace Dr. Ivanov back, luminescent fluid dripping from their eyes.// **Entity-9230-2:** Dad! I missed you! **Entity-9230-1:** May we come in, dear? **Dr. Ivanov:** Of course. //Entity-9230-1 and 2 enter the house and sit on the couch. Dr. Ivanov brings three cups of chocolate.// **Dr. Ivanov:** You can still drink as spirits right? **Entity-9230-1:** You'd think no, but- **Entity-9230-2:** Hey that's from the really good one! You had promised to get some of it for my birthday before... //Entity-9230-1 rubs 2's back.// **Entity-9230-1:** We are here to spend time with your father, not dwell on long gone unpleasantries. **Dr. Ivanov:** Sorry, but we do need to talk about that. I owe both of you an apology. I was so focused on saving you, that I didn't even notice how badly I had mutilated both of you. //Entity-9230-2 looks visibly scared. 1 looks deeply uneasy.// **Entity-9230-1:** Alex, please. This isn't something I want to talk about. **Dr. Ivanov:** Nor do I, but it's not something that can be put off. I want to tell you that I am sorry. Deeply sorry. I maimed you worse than that illness ever could. I didn't act like a surgeon, I acted like  a butcher. **Entity-9230-1:** I cannot forgive you, Alexander. //Dr. Ivanov looks down, clearly ashamed. Entity-9230-1 hugs him.// **Entity-9230-1:** I was never mad at you to begin with. You don't need forgiveness for trying to save us. Please, can we just enjoy our time together? **Dr. Ivanov:** Of course. Say how has it been like in the afterlife. **Entity-9230-2:** It's amazing. Everyone is so nice. Even that grumpy old man is nice. He makes candy out of thin air! I asked him to teach me and look. //Entity-9230-2 creates a short sword, seemingly out of light.// **Entity-9230-2:** Hey can we play bandits and knights again later? //Entity-9230-1 laughs.// **Entity-9230-1:** Now, now my dear. Your father's bones could barely keep up with your plastic sword. Let's not drag him back with us. He deserves a few more decades free from our tyranny. **Dr. Ivanov:** Yeah, your old man has gotten even older. Tell me though, does your mother have powers of her own. //Entity-9230-1 visibly blushes.// **Entity-9230-1:** No- **Entity-9230-2:** Yes. You should see her when she grows those long wings. She can fly so fast and looks so- **Entity-9230-1:** Simion! I told you not to mention it in front of him! **Dr. Ivanov:** So you're now my official guardian angel? //Entity-9230-1 sighs and smiles.// **Entity-9230-1:** I told you to stop calling me that. //Dr. Ivanov pulls both entities into a tight embrace.// **Dr. Ivanov:** I told you no other words do you justice. **Entity-9230-1:** ...Fine, you win. But we are doing it outside. I wanna stretch. **Dr. Ivanov:** I wouldn't mind my pillow getting some divine feathers on it. Could bring me some good luck and better sleep. //Entity-9230-1 laughs and walks outside with -2 and Dr Ivanov. Footage cuts off.// Note: MTF Lambda-5 returned an hour later with no memory of transpired events. All anomalous activity in the area ceased at 1:00am. [[/div]] Dr. Ivanov has not been seen since. The following note was found in his residence: [[div class="blockquote"]] "If you love someone, you're gonna let them go." At first I hated that saying. It's only now that I understand how true it is. Letting go may be hard, but the alternative is torture the one you claim to love. I made this mistake and was forgiven, though I did not deserve it. To any on a similar road to mine, please: learn to let go. I know how terrifying it is to think that this may be the last you see of one to whom you have devoted your life, but I am here to tell you that it is not so. No separation lasts forever. The ones who would seek to bring such torment upon us are too weak to do so. Take solace in knowing that after the fire comes the water, after baking summer comes peaceful winter, after the brutal day comes the gentle night, after The Scarlet King comes the Moonlit Queen. I will see all of you at the Moonlit Sea. -Alexander Ivanov. Item #: SCP-9231

Object Class: Neutralized

Special Containment Procedures: Containment of SCP-9231 is unnecessary, as there have been no formal reports of SCP-9231 being utilized among anomalous communities, and all efforts to replicate SCP-9231's effect by Foundation researchers have been unsuccessful. All gathered SCP-9231 instances have been rendered inert.

Containment Schematics for SCP-9231.

Description: SCP-9231 was the designation given to now defunct phenomena wherein memetically-augmented sestinas1 were anomalously imbued with the essence of a particular concept. The imbued concept, designated as SCP-9231-A, would always appear as one of the repeating words within the sestina. When was interpreted in either written or spoken form, the essence of the instance's SCP-9231-A would reflect upon the interpreter, causing them to manifest properties associated with the concept for a period of time.2 The resulting anomalous impact depended heavily on the interpreter's personal understanding of the concept, with particularly complex concepts generally resulting in significantly different results from interpreter to interpreter.

Addendum: SCP-9231-Omega Series

Following the conclusion of Różewicz v The Global Occult Coalition3 in the Esterberg Supreme Summer Court, the Foundation was able to obtain a number of documents related to anartistic works seized by GOC officers. Among this documentation is a series of SCP-9231 instances, hereafter referred to as the SCP-9231-Omega series, written as correspondences between two unidentified reality benders during the first years of the Ichabod Campaign. This series of SCP-9231 instances was reportedly discovered on the persons of a reality bender whose remains could not be identified due to excessive charring. The full series has been transcribed in full below, with their associated SCP-9231-A concepts denoted in bold:

just a moment to chat. I thought my tremulous hands would betray me, my Swallowtail, (3)
that each held breath would give me away. His sober (6)
eyes tell me to run, as his words remark on the aesthetics of a town emptied of its wealth (2)

by his raiders. He reassures me that things are improving in the shadow of members of the community whose missing wealth (2)
of kindness and spirit ring hollower than the morning breeze through the burnt-out car wreck (4)
of the hopeful. I mask myself in inebriation; only fear controls me while sober, (6)
and a misdelivered comment can be turned silver (5)
by the hints of oak or hops they're carried on. I stare at my ceiling and dream of what-ifs, my Swallowtail. (3)
What is worth trading for more time? How is it worth it to just… continue to exist? (1)

May you face the world with a more sober (6) demeanor, sister. A wealth (2)
of knowledge, of the world that may exist (1), breathes beyond this wreck. (4)

End words: "voice", "bear", "flesh", "dim", "vultures", "sun";

Sister, though I always cherish your parchment words, there is little I would not give to now hear your voice. (1)
Alas, there is little left for a dreamer like me to give. I feel like a mother bear, (2)
mourning the loss of her cubs who she did not know. The smell of putrefying flesh (3)
and burnt hair greets me in all my dreams. Even when I escape, it lingers, dim, (4)

rises, I see and smell what they have done to our kin. I hear it with the setting sun. (6)

the fact I lived. Why not the young painter I met, who's eyes went dim (4)
when a bullet pierced his skull? He barely had time to learn of all the wonders of this world, before becoming a flesh (3)

pile, and I live still. I do not wish to die, sister, but why was I chosen to live when their flesh (3)
now rots in the maws of scavengers? Why did I live to see the sun (6)
rise again, when so many others burnt that night? The world feels more dim (4)
without their songs and dreams. At night, I hear the collective voice (1)
of that camp scream out like a dying animal, all that needless suffering. I cannot bear (2)

who sent them to an early grave. I don't think they would begrudge me, but I feel like one of the vultures. (5)
As though my chance survival is evidence of a betrayal of my flesh (3)
and blood, like there is no difference between a coward and an enemy. When they began to bear (2)

of a hero behind me, gathering dreamers to protect dreamers, as the dim (4)

evening erupted in screaming fire. When the violence had begun to dim, (4)

and stomping boots. Would things have been different if I had stayed? Could my voice (1)

growing larger, as the days began to slim. I envy him; The bear knows the dim (4)
of the world will return to vibrancy soon. I cannot say the same. As I glimpse the sun (6)

Every day, with the setting sun (6), the losses become harder to bear. (2)
The warmth in my voice (1) is gone, my senses grow duller. (4)
The calls of vultures (5) will soon find their home by my flesh. (3)

are only real in drafts of missives and sepia photographs, a shadow (2)

The date on the envelope containing SCP-9231-Omega-5 indicates this is the newest instance of SCP-9231 within Foundation files. It is possible that SCP-9231-Omega-5 was the final instance of SCP-9231 created, given that sources agree that all SCP-9231 instances lost their anomalous properties some time in the early 1970s. Dr. Luca Armaros has theorized that the collective trauma inflicted during the Ichabod Campaign may have caused the authors of the SCP-9231-Omega series to unintentionally use their reality bending capacities to remove SCP-9231's anomalous effects; While potentially possible, this hypothesis remains untestable.

Footnotes
1. A poetic form consisting of six stanzas of six lines each, with six repeating end words at the end of each line. This is often followed by a three-line envoi, oftentimes a dedication or summation of the poem, containing the six words in a (6 2) (1 4) (5 3) pattern.
2. While it is believed that the strength and duration of SCP-9231's effect was determined by an interpreter's reality-bending capabilities, and the interpersonal familiarity between creator and interpreter, this was never empirically confirmed.
3. A legal case which concluded that members of Esterberg's anomalous community had the right to access certain documentation related to the Ichabod Campaign.

SCP-9239.raw_content:
SCP-9239-A is not to be informed of SCP-239’s status as an uncontained anomaly.

SCP-9239, formerly Containment Unit 428-B.

Item #: SCP-9239

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: Two Scranton Reality Anchors are to be present on the left and right sides of the entrance to SCP-9239 respectively to prevent any dimensional intrusions to baseline reality. SCP-9239-A is to be kept in Containment Unit 428-A at Site-17, and is to be provided standard amenities typical for humanoid anomalies.

SCP-9239-A is not to be informed of SCP-239’s status as an uncontained anomaly.

Description: SCP-9239 is an extradimensional space created through ontokinetic manipulation. It takes the form of a realm consisting of creatures and objects similar to those depicted in common fairy tales. The entrance to this realm is currently located in the area formerly designated as Containment Unit 428-B,1 which has replaced the steel doors with a door of a design typically seen in medieval fortresses. Entering through this door will lead to a dense forest with trees as tall as 60 meters, and mythical creatures such as unicorns and ogres. These creatures are usually docile, and will not attack personnel unless provoked.

SCP-9239-A refers to itself as Sir Reynold the Great, who is the only human being present in SCP-9239. It claims to be the protector of SCP-239, and it wants to reunite with it for unclear purposes. SCP-9239-A is impervious to any and all forms of damage, but otherwise is typical of a standard non-anomalous human, wearing nondescript armor from the medieval period and wielding a broadsword for close combat.

Discovery: SCP-9239 was discovered on 2019/03/08 when the door to Containment Unit 428-B suddenly transfigured into its current form. SCP-9239-A proceeded to open the entrance from the other side to enter baseline reality. It expressed confusion about its surroundings before being detained by security personnel. Initial intake interviews provided little information, as SCP-9239-A demanded to see SCP-239. After being informed that this would not be possible,2 it proceeded to draw its sword and attempt to attack personnel, and was subsequently sedated.

Addendum 9239.01: Interview 9239-A.06

The following is a transcript of the sixth interview between SCP-9239-A and Dr. Glass, conducted on 2019/06/10.

<Begin Log>

Glass: So, could you explain to me again why you’re looking for “Princess Siggy?”

Dr. Glass is sitting in his chair, holding his clipboard and writing on a piece of paper. SCP-9239-A is currently leaning against a wall, attempting to look unconcerned. Its left hand is resting on its sword’s sheath.

SCP-9239-A: Why certainly, good sir! You see, we’ve been the best of companions since we were but wee lads and lasses, and we’ve traveled afar in that little world of hers. She has such imagination, with a will that can topple a mountain with just a thought. Isn’t that magnificent?

Glass: Well, yes, it is quite a destructive ability.

SCP-9239-A: You must be her caretakers, then?

Glass: You could say that.

SCP-9239-A: I am saying it.

Glass sighs.

Glass: I can tell. But there’s a reason why we keep her here, Reynold. She can make a man disappear in the blink of an eye. In fact, we know she has done that at least once.

SCP-9239-A steps away from the wall, and moves toward Dr. Glass, speaking to him in a stern voice.

SCP-9239-A: She was only a child.

Glass: A child with the ability to do whatever she wanted. We couldn’t have sent her out into the world. With that kind of power combined with her naivety, it would’ve hurt her and who knows how many other people.

SCP-9239-A: But now she’s grown, and she knows better. I need to see her. Please, good sir, you must take me to her!

Glass rubs his forehead in exasperation.

Glass: You know I can’t allow that, Reynold. There’s too many risks with having separate anomalies interact with each other, especially with ones that have been recently formed.

Reynold slams a fist on the table.

SCP-9239-A: I am not those aberrations that you speak of! I am a knight, bounded by oath to protect the fair maiden Siggy, and I will not be taking orders from knaves like you!

SCP-9239-A proceeds to attempt to exit the chamber, before being stopped and subdued by the guards stationed outside. Dr. Glass takes a sip of his coffee, seemingly unfazed.

Agent Adams enters the room, smirking at Dr. Glass, who rolls his eyes.

Adams: ‘Nother loon on the loose, huh?

Glass: I’m not bothered by it. He never makes it far.

Adams: A bit pathetic for a knight, don’t you think?

Dr. Glass folds his arms and stares at her expectantly.

Glass: What’s your business for being here?

Adams: Well, I got good news! We may have found 239’s hiding spot.

Dr. Glass leans in a bit closer.

Glass: Really?

Adams: Yeah, some place in the middle of bumfuck Ohio. Chillicothe, I think. The nerds found some pretty damn strong levels of reality going sideways.

Glass: How close is it to hers, though?

Adams: Almost an exact match.

Glass pauses, and considers something for a moment. Then he reaches for the phone on his desk.

Glass: I need to make a call.

Adams: What for?

Glass: Someone who can help us reach out to her. I know just the person for the job, and luckily for us, he’s in the right place and hopefully the right time.

<End Log>

Addendum 9239.02: Communication with SCP-239

On 2019/06/13, Dr. Michael Prescott, head of Psychology & Parapsychology at Site-35, requested to meet with SCP-239 through a message sent by a contact from the Wanderer’s Library. The request was initially refused, however through a series of correspondences Dr. Prescott eventually convinced SCP-239 to meet with it in a public location alone with no surveillance. After deliberation, this proposition was accepted, and Dr. Prescott went to a local café in Chillicothe for this purpose.

<Begin Log>

Dr. Prescott makes his way to the outdoor patio of the café, before spotting SCP-239 sitting alone at a table away from the people around it. It is wearing sunglasses and a baseball cap, attempting to keep itself inconspicuous.

Dr. Prescott sits across from it, and reaches out his hand as a gesture of introducing himself. SCP-239 reluctantly shakes his hand.

Prescott: Pleasure to make your acquaintance. You may call me Michael.

SCP-239 pauses.

SCP-239: Are you expecting me to tell you my name, or what?

Prescott: Well, I was just introducing myself. It’s courtesy.

SCP-239: Did someone up top forget that I’ve been on-the-run from you all for the past 13 years now?

Prescott: It’s at least better than calling you by your numbers. That never rolls off the tongue well. ‘Hey ess see pee two three nine, how have you been feeling lately?’ See what I mean?

SCP-239: And it’s dehumanizing.

Prescott: That too, yes.

SCP-239: If you want a name, you can use my fake name for now. Shelby.

Prescott: That will suffice. Thank you, Shelby.

He breaks off eye contact with SCP-239, and begins to watch passing cars at the road ahead of them.

Prescott: If I may ask, how did you manage to stay away from us for so long? We certainly don’t have the best technology to track reality benders like the GOC does, but we would have noticed something eventually.

SCP-239 smiles, and gleefully points at its hat and sunglasses.

SCP-239: You mean these, right? That’s my go-to.

Prescott: Your go-to disguise is a baseball cap and sunglasses?

It shrugs.

SCP-239: The Clark Kent method does work under the right circumstances. Only you guys know me as 239, and if everyone else knows me as Shelby, as long as I don’t use my magic, it’s all good! No one would be able to tell the difference.

Prescott: Besides recently, since we caught you doing just that.

SCP-239: Come on, can’t a girl have a little bit of fun and whimsy in her life? Or at least go five seconds without being watched?

SCP-239 points at the traffic camera across the street recording them.

SCP-239: I thought we agreed on no surveillance.

Prescott: I can’t speak for my superiors, but since we have access to the majority of surveillance systems around the world, it technically doesn’t violate our agreement since it’s always being monitored 24/7.

SCP-239: Wow, that makes me feel so much better.

It sighs.

SCP-239: Can’t catch a fucking break. Why are you even here, anyway?

Prescott: I was first sent to request assistance from you, but the question of your recent activity is something significant to the people who first took you under their care.

SCP-239: Right, those assholes at 17. If they want to know something, it was for a friend’s birthday party. That’s all you’re getting. And why do you need my help?

Dr. Prescott turns his attention back to SCP-239.

Prescott: They first spotted something unusual at the containment unit where you once resided. A door to another realm, full of magical creatures. They thought it linked back to you.

SCP-239: So? That can mean anything. You have to deal with stuff like that all the time.

Prescott: That is true, but the first thing they encountered once the door opened was a knight with the name Reynold the Great, supposedly. Does that ring a bell to you?

SCP-239 stands up quickly and suddenly, eyes open wide in shock.

SCP-239: You’ve got to be shitting me.

Dr. Prescott stands up as well, pushing his chair in.

Prescott: You do know something about this.

SCP-239: I thought he wouldn’t come back. Like all of the others. How is he here?

Prescott: That’s what we’re trying to figure out.

SCP-239 begins to pace back and forth, muttering to itself.

SCP-239: How is this possible? He can’t be out here. I specifically made it that way. That can’t be right. No, that can’t be right at all. How—

Prescott: Are you alright, Shelby?

SCP-239 stops in its tracks, and turns to face Dr. Prescott.

SCP-239: You don’t need my help.

Prescott: And why is that?

SCP-239: I need to pull the weed by its roots. Then we can forget this all happened and you won’t have to worry about me again. ‘Kay? ‘Kay.

SCP-239’s eyes flash a bright green color. Dr. Prescott rushes over to it, and as it completes the thaumaturgical incantation for instant translocation, he puts a hand on its shoulder, adding himself to the thaumaturgical rite being cast, and causing both of them to disappear from view.

<End Log>

Addendum 9239.03: Exploration of SCP-9239

The following is a transcript of Dr. Prescott and SCP-239’s impromptu exploration of SCP-9239, taken from Dr. Prescott’s personal cell phone camera.

<Begin Log>

Camera activates. Dr. Prescott holds the camera, and spots himself and SCP-239 in a dense forest, with trees that have low-hanging branches and knotted and tangled roots, thick enough to be unable to see past their immediate surroundings. The trees are large enough to block out the sun, making the whole forest feel shaded and enormous. Small pink lights appear to maneuver through the forest, bouncing up and down in a rhythmic manner.

SCP-239 stares at Dr. Prescott and crosses its arms.

SCP-239: Did you really need to do that?

Prescott: I thought I could be of some help.

SCP-239: I don’t need anybody’s help. I can handle myself.

Prescott: I apologize if I came across that way, but this is an uncharted anomaly with unknown properties. I’ve learned by now that it’s never a good idea to go to a place like this alone.

SCP-239: And yet you’re holding a camera and recording me. Oh wait, I get it now, you’re here so that they can track you and catch up to me. And then you’ll put me right back in my cage! No thanks.

SCP-239 begins to advance forward. Dr. Prescott follows behind it.

Prescott: That was not my intention. I’m recording us in case no one is able to contact us again. It’s standard protocol.

SCP-239: Of course. You people and your protocols.

Prescott: Until we find a way out of this place, you’re stuck with me unfortunately.

SCP-239 turns to look at him.

SCP-239: Okay? Just don’t mess with what I’m doing, like that stunt you pulled earlier. I need to get this done.

It turns back and keeps going. Dr. Prescott takes a second before catching up to it.

Prescott: Am I able to ask what you are planning to accomplish here?

SCP-239: No.

Prescott: Why not?

SCP-239: Because you keep asking me these inane questions! Aren’t you supposed to be good at reading people?

Prescott: Not in a casual conversation, no. But that’s how my brain is wired, so I’ll have to live with it.

It shakes its head.

SCP-239: At least you were able to figure out why you are that way, right? Lucky you. The only good thing I ever got was being put in a coma.

Prescott: Because you finally felt free.

SCP-239: In an ironic way, yes. What those researchers at 17 didn’t know was that I was able to immerse myself in my imagination, creating entire worlds that became my sandbox. I did what I pleased, and acted out fantasies that I never got to do otherwise.

Prescott: I assume that’s how this place was formed, then?

SCP-239: Well, not like this, but yeah. When I was in my coma, this was all in my mindscape, and not as real as this. Not sure why it’s all real now.

SCP-239 produces a flame by snapping its fingers, before snuffing it out by closing its palm.

SCP-239: Your people made me, you know. You told me I was a witch, you gave me that spell book and told me what I should be, you put that idea in my head and then told me stories of princes fighting dragons for the princesses that they loved. They all lived happily ever after, because that’s how it’s supposed to go. Riding off into the sunset with your partner, because that’s the point that everyone is supposed to reach in life. All roads lead to love.

Prescott: I think I see where you’re going with this.

SCP-239: You think? This is how it’s been for the past thirteen goddamn years.

It huffs, and exerts its ability to lift a tree from its roots, pulling the tree towards itself. It headbutts the tree, splitting it in half.

SCP-239: I can literally do whatever the hell I want, and yet this shit is stopping me. Isn’t that embarrassing?

Prescott: I’ve had clients with similar experiences to yours. Trying to navigate a world actively hostile to the idea of your orientation is quite a difficult task.

SCP-239: Especially when it goes unnoticed most of the time. The kind of stuff that I have to deal with, it’s almost never discussed. I’ve had people look at me like I’ve said an unknown language just because I wanted to stay single. Not my fault they’re trying to dig into my supposed love life!

Prescott: Have there been any difficulties with your social life because of this?

SCP-239: Thankfully, no. I found friends. Well, it’s more like they found me, but I’ve got some by my side, and I wouldn’t have dreamt of anything better.

SCP-239 sits in front of the tree that it split and leans back against it. Dr. Prescott sits next to it.

SCP-239: They don’t know how much I care about them. How much they mean to me. I can go all day praising the shit out of every single one of them. The things I’ve done with them, the memories we made together, it’s just special, you know? It’s special.

Prescott: I understand.

SCP-239: I don’t think partnering with anyone is a bad thing. That’s special for the people who want that, it’s got that deep connection and a commitment that’ll last a lifetime. But that’s not me. My friends are my life. Nothing can ever replace what we have.

Prescott: Until they marry someone else.

It sighs.

SCP-239: Yeah. I’m prepared for that, but it’s still not going to make it hurt less.

Prescott: Like you're less valued.

SCP-239: And it reminds me that, in the end, I’m alone. I never really escaped that cage, did I?

Prescott: If your friends are really your friends, they’d find a way to include you. They’d know well enough to never leave you behind. And if they mean that much to you, then there’s surely a chance that you mean that much to them. You have to share your feelings, and you have to sort it out together.

SCP-239 turns to look at him.

SCP-239: You think it’s as simple as that?

Prescott: Communication is a complicated process for me, but there’s nothing more effective than telling people how you feel, and working through it with them.

SCP-239: I hope so. I really do.

They both stand up, and resume their trek through the forest.

Prescott: I’m surprised you haven’t kicked me out yet.

SCP-239: You’re a good listener. Which means you know when to shut up. And you’re not those morons from 17.

Prescott: Fair enough.

A screech can be heard from up above. A flaming phoenix is seen flying through the trees, starting a controlled fire in some patches of the forest.

Prescott: Now can I ask what you’re planning to achieve?

SCP-239 smiles.

SCP-239: I’m here to bury my past, and make sure it stays dead.

<End Log>

Addendum 9239.03: Incident 9239.01

Immediately after SCP-239 and Dr. Prescott’s apportation to SCP-9239, the following events took place during the latest interview between Dr. Glass and SCP-9239-A.

<Begin Log>

Glass: Why are you so invested in 239?

SCP-9239-A is sitting in a chair across from Dr. Glass. It stares at him with a look of confusion.

SCP-9239-A: Isn’t it obvious? I love her dearly, ever since I first laid my eyes on her. She came down from the heavens and proclaimed me as her protector, to stand guard against any foe cowardly enough to attack a fair maiden like her. That was the oath we built together, one that I shall not shatter.

Glass: Have you considered that she might not feel the same way about you now?

SCP-9239 laughs with an inauthentic tone of voice.

SCP-9239-A: What jokes you have, good sir! If she no longer wished to see me again, then why would I be here, standing before you?

Glass: That’s what’s not making any sense to me. From what we know, 239 has completely refused to bother with any fantastical things of any sort, ever since she’s escaped from us. Unless it was from a subconscious decision…

There is a short pause, before SCP-9239-A stands up suddenly, and enthusiastically points at Dr. Glass.

SCP-9239-A: Aha! That’s it! You, my friend, have just solved the conundrum we’re in.

Glass: Care to explain what you mean by that?

SCP-9239-A: I never knew if it was true, but I’m still there in her heart. Now is my chance to prove that I’m still worthy!

Glass: Alright, hang on, slow down. Why do you need to prove that you’re ‘worthy?’

SCP-9239-A: Worthy to be her guiding light until the end. To be her companion, and perhaps even more. Together we shined brighter than the stars themselves. Don’t you understand how special that is?

Glass: If that’s the case, then why hasn’t she talked to you yet? Surely from what you're saying about her there wouldn’t be an issue with that.

SCP-9239-A: Well, it has certainly been ages. How many years has it been since you last saw her?

Glass: Thirteen, to be exact.

SCP-9239-A begins to consider something for a moment.

SCP-9239-A: If it has been that long, then she must have been reminiscing about me. There’s no other explanation.

Glass: You can’t assume that she wants to see you based on a hunch, Reynold.

SCP-9239-A: But I can see if she does, if you let me see her.

Dr. Glass collects himself, attempting to quell his burgeoning frustration.

Glass: I’ve told you multiple times that we can’t allow that to happen. It’s against protocol, and it’s not my decision to make regardless. As long as you accept that, then there won’t be any problems.

SCP-9239-A shakes his head.

SCP-9239-A: You are no honorable man, Sir Glass. I can see it in your very spirit.

The door slams open, and two guards enter the room, one of them rushing over to Dr. Glass.

Guard: We have a problem.

Dr. Glass stands up, knocking his nameplate off the table.

Glass: What’s going on?

Guard: Your colleague and 239 have somehow disappeared from the café. We suspect she’s taken him someplace else.

A look of recognition appears on SCP-9239-A’s face.

SCP-9239-A: I know where she is.

The remaining personnel in the room turn to face the anomaly.

Glass: You mean the forest?

SCP-9239-A: Indeed. And I will not let some foulish cur take her from me. This is my chance, friends, my chance to bring her back to me! God wills me so!

SCP-9239-A vanishes from the room, startling the guards and Dr. Glass. They look at each other for a moment, stunned.

Guard: Well, uh, I think we might need to update the documentation.

Dr. Glass sighs deeply.

Glass: You can go ahead and tell the director, I’d rather not do it myself.

He moves to exit the chamber, ignoring the guards who attempt to continue conversing with him.

Glass: I really should’ve picked a different career.

He slams the door shut.

<End Log>

Addendum 9239.04: Confrontation between SCP-239 and SCP-9239-A

The following is a transcript of the continuation of SCP-239 and Dr. Prescott’s exploration of SCP-9239, and the former’s encounter with SCP-9239-A.

<Begin Log>

SCP-239 and Dr. Prescott are in a field, having left the dense forest. Around them are 3-meter-tall griffins who chase the deer grazing in the field. Once they capture the deer, they sink their claws into the deer’s skin and fly upwards, beginning to consume them in the sky above.

Prescott: Will you know when you’ll find what you’re looking for?

SCP-239 gazes into the horizon.

SCP-239: He’ll find me. I’m sure of it.

They stare at the field of animals ahead in silence.

Prescott: I was thinking about how they treated you.

SCP-239 turns to him and tilts its head.

SCP-239: What for?

Prescott: In my line of work, we’re trying a new form of how to handle anomalies. One that treats them not as a contained object, but instead in a way that humanizes them, providing a safe environment for them to be comfortable in.

SCP-239: And why does that matter to what I’ve been through?

Prescott: Instead of putting you through a fabrication that dictated your life and your actions, we could’ve taught you how to manage your powers, and we could’ve at least done something that made you comfortable to be you and express yourself without risking harm to others. It would’ve been exceedingly difficult since you were a child, but you were a child nonetheless.

SCP-239: It wasn’t that bad, really.

Prescott: How so?

SCP-239 gestures to the field around it.

SCP-239: I was able to make the worlds I was able to make. And that gave me the chance to, you know, escape from my cell and be free. If I wasn’t able to teach myself to be on my own, I wouldn’t have gotten myself out of that coma.

Dr. Prescott nods in understanding.

Prescott: That is fair.

SCP-239: Let me ask you something. Are you consulting with any of them at all?

Prescott: They’d want to escape.

SCP-239: Well, yeah, no shit.

SCP-239: The people you work for think they’re so confident that they have all the answers, that they know what’s best for people like me. But they never will. So if escape isn’t an option, then maybe you can at least try to put yourself in their shoes?

Prescott: I have been thinking about such things, but you have good points there. I could potentially—

Dr. Prescott is grabbed by a claw, but not of the griffins. He is taken higher and higher by a massive, gold-and-black scaled dragon, on the back of which is SCP-9239-A. It waves its sword in the air, as if to greet SCP-239.

The griffins and deer scamper away from the presence of the dragon. Dr. Prescott attempts to free himself from the dragon’s claws and calls out to SCP-239.

SCP-9239-A: My dear Siggy! It is a great honor to meet you once again!

SCP-239: Not to me, it isn’t.

Both the dragon and SCP-9239-A tilt their heads in unison.

SCP-9239-A: Why do you look so grim?

SCP-239: I think you can take a pretty good guess.

SCP-9239-A: Am I not worthy to travel together alongside you again? I promise you, I am still the same as I ever was.

SCP-239: Exactly. That’s the problem.

SCP-239 begins to levitate itself until it faces the dragon in front of it.

SCP-239: We’re not going to travel together again. I’ve changed, Reynold. Changed for the better, because I’m doing what’s best for myself. I think you should consider that, and try to do what’s best for you.

SCP-9239-A: But what has always been the most important thing to me is you, my dear.

SCP-239 rolls its eyes.

SCP-239: Have you always been this saccharine? Oh wait, I guess you have.

SCP-9239-A: Now that is very unlike a lady such as yourself. Have your manners gone as well?

SCP-239: Look, man, I’ve moved on from you. I moved on from those fantasies because that wasn’t who I really was. All I ever wanted was to be reminded that I was still a human person for fuck’s sake, because I never got a chance to feel like anything in that cage. And when I read those fairy tales, that connection we made together fulfilled that and made me feel whole. Problem was, it wasn’t the connection I was actually thinking of.

SCP-9239-A: What fulfills you now?

SCP-239: My friends. They are the light of my life, Reynold. I’d give them my everything if I could. But I can’t. I can’t because of people like you.

There is a short pause.

SCP-9239-A: You reject that which you are? You reject the very foundation of what drives us, the very thing that makes us human?

SCP-239: What makes us human is our ability to define and express ourselves. There’s also, like, a million other things that make us human but that one’s the big one.

The dragon pulls Dr. Prescott up so that SCP-9239-A can see him. He scoffs at him with disdain.

SCP-9239-A: So this is your new companion, I see.

SCP-239: Wha— no? We barely just met? What are you even talking about?

SCP-9239-A: This filth is feeding you lies, isn’t he? Trying to convince you to run off with him, I bet!

SCP-239: I know what I am, Reynold. No one else can tell me otherwise.

SCP-9239-A: Was that what you thought when your captors took you in, eh?

It points its sword at Dr. Prescott.

SCP-9239-A: How about I vanquish this foe of ours, and we can run off into the sunset once more?

SCP-239: What is wrong with you? You’re not supposed to harm anyone!

SCP-9239-A: I am meant to be your guardian to protect you from harm. And since this devil has already begun its tricks, I’ll have to make this quick.

SCP-9239-A raises its sword, before being stopped by an imperceptible force. Dr. Prescott is apportated away from the dragon’s grasp, and is now seen floating next to SCP-239. He is disoriented, and is having difficulty with moving in the air.

Prescott: Let’s hope that’s the last time I have to be kidnapped by a dragon.

SCP-239: You’ll be fine. Let me handle this.

Dr. Prescott is again apportated, this time to the ground below. SCP-239 floats closer to the dragon.

SCP-9239-A: You dare defy me?

SCP-239: I can make my own decisions. You were not supposed to, since you were an NPC, but I guess that’s changed. What gives?

SCP-9239-A: Well, it’s quite simple, really. Ever since you left, I realized that since this place and I were made by the same thing, that being your imagination, then I could finally make myself be the protector that you dreamt of me to be. And now, I am one with the forest. I control all of what you see here.

SCP-239: That— that’s not possible. It can’t be.

SCP-9239-A: It has been so long, my dear. Any longer and I would have gone mad.

The dragon huffs, smoke shooting out of its nostrils.

SCP-9239-A: If you insist.

SCP-9239-A raises it sword to point at SCP-239.

SCP-9239-A: My dear, if you wish to spar, then we shall spar. You win, and you can take that devil back with you. I win, and we shall begin our partnership as it was always meant to be. Have I made myself clear?

SCP-239 balls its hands into fists.

SCP-239: You’re more than clear. Bring it.

SCP-9239-A nods, and taps one of the dragon’s horns to signal a command. The dragon springs into action, and before SCP-239 has time to react, it grabs the anomaly and plummets to the field below, colliding with the dirt and dragging SCP-239 through it.

The dragon roars in SCP-239’s face, and begins to prepare to expel fire from its throat. Before this occurs, SCP-239 pushes out a bright green circle of ontokinetic energy in front of itself. Its eyes glow with the same color, and it grunts in pain as it exerts its ability, blocking the fire from reaching it.

SCP-9239-A: And I thought you would be more of a challenge. Is your strength as weak as your heart?

SCP-239: Oh, I’m just getting started.

SCP-239 pushes its hands forward, causing SCP-9239-A to be knocked off balance and fall off the dragon, and the dragon itself is pushed back 10 meters.

SCP-239 then gestures to the dragon to move closer.

SCP-239: Come on big guy, hit me with your best shot.

The dragon grins, and flies down to make its second attack, with SCP-239 ascending to meet up with it.

They trade blows, with the dragon attempting to use its claws and jaw to injure its opponent, while SCP-239 conjures medieval shields made out of ontokinetic energy to block its attacks.

Seeing that SCP-239 is distracted, the dragon then whips its tail around to strike the anomaly. It cries out in pain, and blood flows from a cut on the left side of its face, almost reaching the eye. The dragon’s grin grows wider.

SCP-239 covers its injury with one hand, and points at the dragon with the other.

SCP-239: Alright, that one was good, I’ll give you that. But honestly, you’re a pretty boring fighter for a dragon. I was expecting more pizazz, you know? Now I have to end this early.

A hammer that is about half the height of the dragon is conjured directly above the dragon’s head. SCP-239 snaps its fingers, and the dragon is struck with the weapon, knocking it unconscious. It plummets to the ground once more, however, SCP-239 uses its ability to cushion the fall.

It apportates down to where the dragon landed. While it bends down to check to see if the creature is breathing, it uses its other hand to instantly heal its own injury. Once it is done and the dragon is confirmed to be stable, it gets back up and looks around to attempt to locate SCP-9239-A’s location.

SCP-239: Glad you’re safe, big guy. Already got enough blood on my hands.

SCP-9239-A: And you shall spill more if you take another step further.

SCP-239 turns around, to see SCP-9239-A holding Dr. Prescott hostage, its sword being held against his neck.

SCP-239: You wouldn’t.

SCP-9239-A: You continue to impress me with how naive you are, my dear. Did you really think that I’d be as merciful as I was before you left me behind?

SCP-239: Says the bastard who thinks that I’m the same girl he met who was led to believe something that she wasn’t.

SCP-9239-A: Am I led to believe otherwise?

SCP-239: You don’t get to decide who I’m meant to be. What I feel is real, Reynold.

SCP-9239-A: I know what you are. You doubt yourself. You’re doubting yourself even now. Your heart is telling me everything. You feel that deep ache in your soul, that sense of longing of something that you will never have. I see it now. You need me. You need a man to mend your heart and make you feel whole.

Tears begin to fall down SCP-239’s face, no matter how hard it tries to restrain itself.

SCP-239: Stop. Please.

SCP-9239-A: I will never cease until my dear Siggy returns to my side. Let me end this madness, so we can go back to how things used to be.

SCP-239 clenches its left hand to form a fist, its body shaking heavily.

SCP-239: No.

The sword holding Dr. Prescott dematerializes, causing him to drop to the floor. He sighs in relief.

SCP-9239-A: You’re trying to end this spar by cheating, eh? You can’t hide from yourself forever.

SCP-9239-A raises its hand, and another sword materializes for it to wield.3 The anomaly attempts to bring the sword down onto Dr. Prescott, before being stopped by SCP-239’s ability. The two are locked in a standstill, with neither SCP-9239-A being able to make progress nor SCP-239 to stop it completely.

Prescott: Shelby, you need to listen to me—

SCP-9239-A: Quiet, you devil. No more lies.

SCP-239: At least let him speak.

SCP-9239-A: And have you run from me again? I think not.

SCP-239: I said, let him speak.

SCP-9239-A continues to open its mouth, but no sound comes out. SCP-239 begins to hyperventilate, and openly sob.

Prescott: Shelby, I know this may seem dire, but you can’t let him win.

SCP-239: I’m not strong enough. I can’t do it.

Prescott: You are stronger than him. You are stronger than anyone can ever claim.

SCP-239: I have to kill him if I want to save you. I promised myself that I’d never hurt anyone again, Michael. I can’t do this.

Prescott: You can, because this is not the knight that you knew. This is something within you, beckoning you to let it take control. You cannot let it overcome you.

The sword slowly begins to inch its way to Dr. Prescott’s throat, as SCP-9239-A gains the upper hand.

SCP-239: I guess I still am that girl who doesn’t know what the world is like. I can’t live like this, I can’t live knowing that I’ll never be as happy as my friends are with the people they love, I can’t love, I can’t love at all, I can’t—

Prescott: Shelby, it’s alright. Take deep breaths. You’re not incapable of love. You don’t have to love like they do. There are other paths to take, there are other ways you can live.

SCP-239: But I can’t live like myself. I can’t live without any of you fuckers finding me again, or having my friends turn their backs on me, or—

Prescott: You don’t have to hide who you are. You don’t have to pretend to be someone you’re not. You have to prove them all wrong. You have to live. Even if you have to crawl your way out with your bare hands, you have to live.

SCP-9239-A eventually realizes that it is not vocalizing, and shakes its head, glaring at SCP-239.

SCP-9239-A: A clever trick on your part, my dear. But not enough. It’s time I take back what’s rightfully mine.

It raises its sword for another strike.

SCP-239: I was never yours to take. You were never real to me to begin with.

SCP-239 thrusts its hand forward, causing SCP-9239-A to spontaneously combust, disintegrating into ash. SCP-239 then falls onto its knees and weeps.

Dr. Prescott slowly begins to crawl his way over to the anomaly, before eventually reaching it and laying down next to it, grunting in pain. He waits until SCP-239 lets its emotions out before sitting up and turning to look at it.

Prescott: You okay?

SCP-239 sniffles.

SCP-239: No, but I needed that. I really needed that. Thank you.

Prescott: It’s what I do.

They both stare at the horizon ahead of them, seeing the sun set.

SCP-239: It shouldn’t have to be as complicated as this. Why do I need to prove my love more by tying the rest of my life to someone else? I can bend the world with a thought, and yet I still feel like I don’t belong anywhere.

Prescott: It’s not only your fight. We’re always doubting ourselves, always questioning if we’re right about what we think we are, but no matter what you or I or what anyone else says, what we feel is real. It’s what gives the world all of its beauty.

SCP-239 smiles.

SCP-239: Why are you always so goddamn reasonable?

Prescott: Well, everyone deserves the chance to have their voices heard, right?

SCP-239: I guess so.

Prescott: We may see you as an anomaly, but in truth, the deep affection you have for everyone you know is intrinsic to reality itself.

SCP-239 stands up, and so does Dr. Prescott.

SCP-239: I can feel them coming.

Prescott: It would be best if you leave me, then.

SCP-239: What about you? Aren’t you supposed to take me in?

Prescott: As long as you're safe, that’s all that matters. I’ll be fine.

Dr. Prescott pulls out a white ring from his left middle finger, and presents it to SCP-239.

Prescott: I think you should have this. It’s a symbol of solidarity, to show others like me that they are never alone. I don’t need it anymore as much as you do.

SCP-239 takes it, and stares at it for a moment, before realizing the significance of it.

SCP-239: Wait…

Prescott: I might have exaggerated a bit when I said that I had clients like you. It was more like I was the client, really.

SCP-239 attempts to prevent its tears from returning, but fails and weeps once more.

SCP-239: I don’t know what to say. Thank you.

It turns to look at Dr. Prescott’s left hand, and considers something for a moment. Then it snaps its fingers, and a ring exactly identical to the one given to it is manifested to fit his left middle finger. Dr. Prescott looks down towards his hand, and looks back up at the anomaly in disbelief.

SCP-239: It should be the same composition with the material, but I had to guess, so…

It shrugs.

Prescott: Now I don’t know what to say.

SCP-239: Hey, I’m full of surprises!

Dr. Prescott looks toward the tree line, and looks back at SCP-239.

Prescott: We’re still using Shelby, correct?

SCP-239: Yeah, I think that’s who I’m going to be from now on. Wouldn’t be well for me to dwell on the past.

He nods.

Prescott: Stay safe, Shelby.

SCP-239: You too.

They wave goodbye, and SCP-239 apportates away to another location, while Dr. Prescott walks back toward the forest.

<End Log>

Dr. Prescott has been summoned to a disciplinary hearing to explain his actions, with Director Madeline Webb of Site-35 in attendance. SCP-9239-A’s reclassification to Neutralized pending approval.

Footnotes
1. Originally designed as the containment unit for SCP-239.
2. It was not informed of SCP-239’s status as a fugitive since its escape from containment in 2006.
3. Post-incident analysis confirms a faint ontokinetic signature resulting from this action that matches those emitted by SCP-239.
