SCP-9303 — from dust you came

Written by – Frostbyters

Critted by – P4TR1CK07 Fermentating TheTravllr popsioak1 DrStinkyBacteriaV2 BAD_DATA leibotomy LeraviTheXatu RaveHavenn snakeshot

▸ More by this Author ◂

{$comments2}

F.A.Q.

{$doesthisfixthebug}

SCP-9303, once presented with sources of red lighting other than itself, will begin to pace around it. The purpose behind this behaviour is unknown.

SCP-9303

Item #: SCP-9303

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9303 is to be housed in a modified containment chamber at Site-17. Site janitors are to dispose of collected dust in a chute fitted with an aerosolizer, where it will be intermittently dispersed in SCP-9303's chamber. To dilute methane buildup, inert gasses2 are to be circulated through small ventilation grates placed at the ceiling.

In the event SCP-9303 cannot be fed due to malfunctions or lack of dust, assigned containment personnel are to gather dust from neighbouring sites. This dust is to be manually inserted via hand into its containment chamber.

Fluorescent lights are only to be switched on during testing or maintenance. In the event of an emergency, high-power red LED's and thermal cameras are to be activated in the chamber. All staff assigned to SCP-9303 are to equip SCBA's3 before entering its chamber.

Description: SCP-9303 is a 1.83 m tall, thin humanoid with a large aluminium ventilation cover replacing the face. This cover filters the air that SCP-9303 breathes for dust and debris, which it relies on as its primary food source. While unhidden, SCP-9303 has a grey skin tone.

SCP-9303 hides itself inside ventilation shafts by removing and replacing ventilation covers with its own head, using an adhesive layer on its skin to scale walls and being able to blend its skin colour with the environment. Once SCP-9303 finishes feeding, it places the previous cover back and it maneuvers to a more secluded area to emit red bioluminescence from spots on its skin. This allows methane buildup to escape, which is a form of waste disposal.

SCP-9303 is passive and lacks any aggressive behaviour, although it is unknown whether or not SCP-9303 is sapient. SCP-9303, once presented with sources of red lighting other than itself, will begin to pace around it. The purpose behind this behaviour is unknown.

Discovery: SCP-9303 was found inside of a civilian office building in New York while employees were testing their security and safety measures. The fire alarm was activated as part of standard procedure, activating the exit signs and causing SCP-9303 to reveal itself. Field agents were soon dispatched, and all civilians present were amnesticized.

Addendum 9303-A: Visual Stimuli - Test Log 3

Previous tests regarding communication with SCP-9303 yielded no fruitful results and were removed to be archived.

TEST LOG

Item # Tested: SCP-9303

Description Of Test: To note SCP-9303's responses to certain visual stimuli.

Tested By: Dr. Alexis Hadley

RESULTS

Photo Shown SCP-9303 Response Observations
Pomeranian (Canis lupus familiaris) SCP-9303 slowly reached out a hand to touch the photograph. It retreated to the corner of the room before it touched the photo. Its hands were shaking.
Wasp Nest (Vespula vulgaris) SCP-9303 noticed the photo and scaled the wall, blending in with the roof. Reaction was immediate. It did not look back at the photo and kept its head away. Where would it have dealt with wasps before?
Black Rat (Rattus rattus) SCP-9303 approached the photo, standing still for a few seconds before attempting to flick the photo with its fingers. Interesting reaction. It did not hesitate.
American Cockroach (Periplaneta americana) SCP-9303 stared from a distance before looking at its own hands. It subtly mimics the shape of holding a bug spray canister before walking to the corner of the room. It could have picked this up as a context clue.
Rock Dove (Columba livia) SCP-9303 slowly walked towards the photo. Once it got close to the photo, it hunched and stared at it. It then stood still for approximately 3 minutes before walking away. Moved slowly, perhaps not wanting to scare it. Did not have much care for anything else, so why have such a reaction for birds? Further research regarding this response might prove useful.

Notes: N/A

Addendum 9303.B: Avian Fauna - Test Log 4

TEST LOG

Item # Tested: SCP-9303

Description Of Test: To note SCP-9303's behaviour toward avian fauna.

Tested By: Dr. Alexis Hadley

RESULTS

SCP-9303 was presented with several trained bird species within its chamber. It cautiously approached each, attempting to hold each one separately in its hands. When successful, SCP-9303 brought them close to its face. It then slowly released each bird as to not harm them via its adhesive skin.

This process repeated for each bird until the pattern broke when SCP-9303 picked up a grey parrot (Psitaccus erithacus). SCP-9303 held it close to its face but did not let it go. It caressed the bird and inspected its feathers closely and only let it go after it finished inspecting it.

Further testing was conducted with similar species; the behaviour was only replicated when SCP-9303 was introduced to grey parrot specimens.

Notes: Grey parrots produce a fine keratin powder to keep their feathers waterproof and soft. If SCP-9303 knows this then it perhaps wants to obtain this powder to feed off of it. An investigation into employees of the building where SCP-9303 was found yielded that only one active employee had a pet parrot. Perhaps it learnt through repetition from this civilian? Such an interesting creature.

Addendum 9303.C: Interview Log 1

The previously mentioned employee was at home the day SCP-9303 was found. An interview has been conducted and can be seen in the following log.

INTERVIEW LOG

Interviewed: Anthony Welles

Interviewer: Dr. Alexis Hadley

Foreword: This log has been edited to remove excessive stuttering from Mr. Welles responses due to concerns of readability.

BEGIN LOG

(Dr. Hadley produces a file as she starts recording.)

Dr. Hadley: 12th of May, 2011. It is currently 2 minutes past 6PM. Good afternoon, Mr. Welles.

Mr. Welles: Good afternoon, m–ma'am. So, may I ask what th-this interview is about? I understand that there must be a reason why I'm worth the armed guards, right?

Dr. Hadley: Yeah, we'll get to that. Calm down and relax. They're here for your safety, trust me. So, it is true that you own a parrot, yes?

Mr. Welles: That is … yeah. I do own a parrot. Grey parrot. His name is Maxwell.

Dr. Hadley: Maxwell's a beautiful bird. That reminds me, the current maintenance job you work, with the insurance company, do they have any policies against bringing pets to the office?

Mr. Welles: Yes, they … their policies are that if anyone else in the office is allergic to the animal or if … hold on, the th-thought slipped my m-mind, could we get back to that?

Dr. Hadley: That would be okay. Let's move on for now. Your bird, Maxwell, do you have any habits for maintaining him? I am sure he has to be well kept to look pretty, right?

Mr. Welles: You could say I'm like any good bird owner! H-Hah … right, so, what certain powder down birds like Maxwell does is they form this layer of keratin around their feathers; usually helps them with the environment they're from. I grind it up and feed that to my plants because they're rich in nitrogen. Although, why do y-you ask?

Dr. Hadley: That's great to know, Mr. Welles. The reason I'm asking is that that's not the only thing you do with that keratin, correct?

Mr. Welles: I don't u-understand what I'm … am I in trouble?

(Dr. Hadley opens the folder in front of her and reveals a photo of SCP-9303. Both stare quietly for a few seconds.)

Mr. Welles: Th–That's … uh, hah, wow.

Dr. Hadley: You see, Mr. Welles, I absolutely love solving puzzles. I would really appreciate it if you helped me out. Tell me everything you know about this creature. Start from the beginning.

Mr. Welles: Am I being interviewed or interrogated?

Dr. Hadley: I'll be your best friend, Anthony. As long as you're honest to me, then I'll be honest to you. Is that fair?

Mr. Welles: I'm just a little bit … l-lightheaded at the moment. Can I gather my th-thoughts before I talk?

(Dr. Hadley nods and a minute passes. Mr. Welles closes his eyes and takes deep breaths, wiping his face with his forearm before he continues speaking.)

Mr. Welles: I've already been caught in one lie. So, from the start … this thing wasn't always around. About a year ago or so, the building next ours burned … burnt down. Got renovated by the city. A few days after it burnt down, I was doing overtime, rewiring ceiling lights and stuff. I was above the panelling when I see this red light come out of nowhere. A red light above the ceiling is something I-I've never seen before, so I got closer to get a better look.

Dr. Hadley: And that is when you first made contact with it?

Mr. Welles: Yeah. I carried my ladder over and … I saw that thing. Ma'am, it nearly scared me out of my own skin, but it didn't i–immediately come to bite or hurt me … just hugged th–the wall, looking at me. Felt like we were looking at each other. It tilted its head at me as if it w-wondered what I was doing. So, yeah … I let it be. What if the government wanted to kill me for knowing about this things existence?

Dr. Hadley: They wouldn't do that. So, you saw it and did nothing. Is that really all that happened?

(Mr. Welles swallows the spit in his mouth before beginning to fidget with his fingers.)

Mr. Welles: Uhm … have you ever watched The Shape of Water, ma'am?

Dr. Hadley: Uh-huh. You empathized with it?

Mr. Welles: I didn't fall in love! Or anything like that … I felt sorry for it. Looking at its body, I saw skin and bones, like it didn't have a good meal in years. Like that one role Christian Bale had in 2004, that thin. I wondered what it was eating … all animals have to eat. Eventually, I did put two and two toge- … together. Grate for a head; it was siphoning the air to stay alive. If it was safe, then maybe I could do one good thing for the world and help it. I took the rest of my powder and blew it into its face when no one was looking. I did that every now and again when I knew where it was hiding … vent covers don't just appear out of thin air, you know? Next time we saw each other, it slowly walked across the ceiling towards me. In that moment, I was … I was a–afraid. That maybe I was the one in danger. Maybe it thought the same. It got closer, and closer … keeping its hands close to its chest, tilting its head around until it was right in front of me. I had some powder with me, so I slowly pulled it out and blew some of it into the air and it loved it. It twitched its head around like a bird and … it blew cold air onto my f-face.

Dr. Hadley: That is certainly quite the surprise. I didn't know you could befriend a creature like that, Mr. Welles.

Mr. Welles: I define friends as people who are there for me. He … that thing was a friend. I talked to it when no one could hear us. Told it secrets, showed it photos and videos. Maybe it was s-smart enough to understand me … gosh, I wish people understood me more often. It even found my missing hammer once. Oh, I remember … I remember taking a photo of it once and showing that to him … it. It didn't let me talk to it a few days after I did that. Made me feel like I upset it somehow. I … I never really gave it a name. One day, I was off, th-the next, it's just … gone. Ma'am, do you know where it … where it went?

(Dr. Hadley pauses for a moment. Her eyes dart to the camera before she clasps her hands together, looking back at Welles.)

Dr. Hadley: No. No, I don't. I'm sorry.

Mr. Welles: Please find out. I'm … I miss it.

Dr. Hadley: Don't worry, Mr. Welles. We will.

…

END LOG

Notes: Mr. Welles was amnesticized after the interview.

Addendum 9303.D: Samples - Test Log 5

An investigation into the history of the renovated building was carried out by field agents. The fire department which responded to the situation's records stated that the fire originated from underground maintenance tunnels which quickly spread via airducts to the main offices due to the buildup of dust, which subsequently spread all throughout the building. The report also indicated biological material at the origin point but was ultimately identified as waste.

MTF Zeta-9 (“Mole Rats”) were tasked to explore the maintenance tunnels underneath the building to locate the origin of the fire and to gather samples. The room wherein the fire originated appeared to be bricked off and had to be destroyed before being able to enter. The room was large, stained with smoke and soot, and contained several loose ventilation covers.

The following samples were collected at the origin point.

Sample Tested Results
Swab of Soot The following was detected on the swab: aluminium filings, soot4, nitric acid, dead skin cells and textile fibres.
Swab of Vent Covers Similar to the swab of soot, alongside faint traces of luciferin as well as an unknown biological substance.
Ventilation Cover Typical aluminium alloy mixed with several other metals. Unidentifiable reddish stains alongside the frame.

Addendum 9303.E: Containment Breach Camera Feed

On ██/██/████, Site-17 suffered a site-wide containment breach. The following captured footage shows Dr. Hadley entering SCP-9303's chamber during the breach out of necessity for her own safety.

VIDEO LOG

Chamber Captured: SCP-9303

Time Code: 0422-0435-17

BEGIN PLAYBACK

(SCP-9303 holds itself up at the corner of the ceiling, blending in. The lights in the chamber turn on before Dr. Hadley enters with her hands in her pockets. The chamber door closes behind her as the blare of sirens become muffled. She fidgets with her equipped SCBA before she looks around for SCP-9303. SCP-9303 reveals itself upon seeing Dr. Hadley in the light. It continues to remain in the upper corner of the ceiling, staring down at Dr. Hadley as she begins speaking.)

Dr. Hadley: I guess you'll be all the company I've got for the next few hours, huh?

(SCP-9303 exhibits no reaction. Dr. Hadley walks to the wall left of SCP-9303's vision and sits down against it.)

Dr. Hadley: So … do you have any favourite books? Mine's Red Dragon by Thomas Harris …

(SCP-9303 begins to slowly lower itself from the wall, climbing down.)

Dr. Hadley: Tch … as if you have any … oh, speaking of, Anthony told me a lot about you. Things he apparently told you. Would you have considered him a friend? Must have been entertaining, right?

(It stands at the opposite side of the room where Dr. Hadley sits.)

Dr. Hadley: One thing I don't understand about what we talked about is the fact that he … he said he understood you. I don't get that. Lonely men like him need an outlet, I get it, but you …

(It begins to take slow steps forward.)

Dr. Hadley: What part of you isn't what we think you are? Can you tell me?

(It continues stepping forward as Dr. Hadley talks.)

Dr. Hadley: … You didn't just lose people you loved. You lost a home to call your own. I can only imagine how that feels.

(It suddenly stands still. Its hands begin to subtly shake.)

Dr. Hadley: Maybe it's stupid I'm talking to you like this. But, for some reason, I feel like … you … you know for certain that you don't fit in. You think I don't know what you're doing, but you'd be lying to yourself if you thought I didn't think there's more to you … maybe I'm projecting a bit. Am I right?

(Dr. Hadley notices its head looking down at the floor before it looks up towards her. She stays quiet before she stands up, placing a palm against the wall.)

Dr. Hadley: Do you need a hug?

(SCP-9303 shakes its head.)

Dr. Hadley: That's okay too. Oh, wait – your skin. I'm sorry, I—

(It snaps its fingers at Dr. Hadley, cutting her off. SCP-9303 points at the red lights above the chamber, which are inactive. Dr. Hadley nods before she pats her pockets, revealing a remote control. She points it at the observation room and presses down on a switch. The red lights turn on. SCP-9303 keeps staring at Dr. Hadley.)

Dr. Hadley: What now? The red lights are burning, I don't … burning. You don't mean that, do you?

(SCP-9303 steps closer to Dr. Hadley. Its skin begins to form red bioluminescent patches.)

Dr. Hadley: What are you doing?

(SCP-9303 approaches Dr. Hadley and gets on its knees. It hugs her around the waist. Dr. Hadley places a hand on top of its head, and the footage corrupts.)

…

END PLAYBACK

The purpose behind this behaviour is unknown.]] [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:image-block-peppo |name=http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/local--files/scp-9303/mynameisedward.png |caption=SCP-9303 |width=300px ]] **Item #:** SCP-9303 **Object Class:** Euclid **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9303 is to be housed in a modified containment chamber at Site-17. Site janitors are to dispose of collected dust in a chute fitted with an aerosolizer, where it will be intermittently dispersed in SCP-9303's chamber. To dilute methane buildup, inert gasses[[footnote]] Carbon dioxide and nitrogen. [[/footnote]] are to be circulated through small ventilation grates placed at the ceiling. In the event SCP-9303 cannot be fed due to malfunctions or lack of dust, assigned containment personnel are to gather dust from neighbouring sites. This dust is to be manually inserted via hand into its containment chamber. Fluorescent lights are only to be switched on during testing or maintenance. In the event of an emergency, high-power red LED's and thermal cameras are to be activated in the chamber. All staff assigned to SCP-9303 are to equip SCBA's[[footnote]] Self-contained breathing apparatus. [[/footnote]] before entering its chamber. **Description:** SCP-9303 is a 1.83 m tall, thin humanoid with a large aluminium ventilation cover replacing the face. This cover filters the air that SCP-9303 breathes for dust and debris, which it relies on as its primary food source. While unhidden, SCP-9303 has a grey skin tone. SCP-9303 hides itself inside ventilation shafts by removing and replacing ventilation covers with its own head, using an adhesive layer on its skin to scale walls and being able to blend its skin colour with the environment. Once SCP-9303 finishes feeding, it places the previous cover back and it maneuvers to a more secluded area to emit red bioluminescence from spots on its skin. This allows methane buildup to escape, which is a form of waste disposal. SCP-9303 is passive and lacks any aggressive behaviour, although it is unknown whether or not SCP-9303 is sapient. SCP-9303, once presented with sources of red lighting other than itself, will begin to pace around it. The purpose behind this behaviour is unknown. **Discovery:** SCP-9303 was found inside of a civilian office building in New York while employees were testing their security and safety measures. The fire alarm was activated as part of standard procedure, activating the exit signs and causing SCP-9303 to reveal itself. Field agents were soon dispatched, and all civilians present were amnesticized. ------ [[=]] ++ **Addendum 9303-A:** Visual Stimuli - Test Log 3 [[/=]] ------ Previous tests regarding communication with SCP-9303 yielded no fruitful results and were removed to be archived. [[div class="blockquote"]] ------ [[=]] ++++ **TEST LOG** [[/=]] ------ **Item # Tested:** SCP-9303 **Description Of Test:** To note SCP-9303's responses to certain visual stimuli. **Tested By:** Dr. Alexis Hadley ------ [[=]] ++++ **RESULTS** [[/=]] ------ ||~ **Photo Shown** ||~ **SCP-9303 Response** ||~ **Observations** || ||= Pomeranian //(Canis lupus familiaris)// ||= SCP-9303 slowly reached out a hand to touch the photograph. It retreated to the corner of the room before it touched the photo.  ||= Its hands were shaking. || ||= Wasp Nest //(Vespula vulgaris)//||= SCP-9303 noticed the photo and scaled the wall, blending in with the roof. ||= Reaction was immediate. It did not look back at the photo and kept its head away. Where would it have dealt with wasps before? || ||= Black Rat //(Rattus rattus)// ||= SCP-9303 approached the photo, standing still for a few seconds before attempting to flick the photo with its fingers. ||= Interesting reaction. It did not hesitate. || ||= American Cockroach //(Periplaneta americana)// ||= SCP-9303 stared from a distance before looking at its own hands. It subtly mimics the shape of holding a bug spray canister before walking to the corner of the room. ||= It could have picked this up as a context clue. || ||= Rock Dove //(Columba livia)// ||= SCP-9303 slowly walked towards the photo. Once it got close to the photo, it hunched and stared at it. It then stood still for approximately 3 minutes before walking away. ||= Moved slowly, perhaps not wanting to scare it. Did not have much care for anything else, so why have such a reaction for birds? Further research regarding this response might prove useful. || **Notes:** N/A [[/div]] ------ [[=]] ++ **Addendum 9303.B:** Avian Fauna - Test Log 4 [[/=]] ------ [[div class="blockquote"]] ------ [[=]] ++++ **TEST LOG** [[/=]] ------ **Item # Tested:** SCP-9303 **Description Of Test:** To note SCP-9303's behaviour toward avian fauna. **Tested By:** Dr. Alexis Hadley ------ [[=]] ++++ **RESULTS** [[/=]] ------ SCP-9303 was presented with several trained bird species within its chamber. It cautiously approached each, attempting to hold each one separately in its hands. When successful, SCP-9303 brought them close to its face. It then slowly released each bird as to not harm them via its adhesive skin. This process repeated for each bird until the pattern broke when SCP-9303 picked up a grey parrot //(Psitaccus erithacus)//. SCP-9303 held it close to its face but did not let it go. It caressed the bird and inspected its feathers closely and only let it go after it finished inspecting it. Further testing was conducted with similar species; the behaviour was only replicated when SCP-9303 was introduced to grey parrot specimens. **Notes:** Grey parrots produce a fine keratin powder to keep their feathers waterproof and soft. If SCP-9303 knows this then it perhaps wants to obtain this powder to feed off of it. An investigation into employees of the building where SCP-9303 was found yielded that only one active employee had a pet parrot. Perhaps it learnt through repetition from this civilian? Such an interesting creature. [[/div]] ------ [[=]] ++ **Addendum 9303.C:** Interview Log 1 [[/=]] ------ The previously mentioned employee was at home the day SCP-9303 was found. An interview has been conducted and can be seen in the following log. [[div class="blockquote"]] ------ [[=]] ++++ **INTERVIEW LOG** [[/=]] ------ **Interviewed:** Anthony Welles **Interviewer:** Dr. Alexis Hadley **Foreword:** This log has been edited to remove excessive stuttering from Mr. Welles responses due to concerns of readability. ------ [[=]] ++++ **BEGIN LOG** [[/=]] ------ //(Dr. Hadley produces a file as she starts recording.)// **Dr. Hadley:** 12th of May, 2011. It is currently 2 minutes past 6PM. Good afternoon, Mr. Welles. **Mr. Welles:** Good afternoon, m–ma'am. So, may I ask what th-this interview is about? I understand that there must be a reason why I'm worth the armed guards, right? **Dr. Hadley:** Yeah, we'll get to that. Calm down and relax. They're here for your safety, trust me. So, it is true that you own a parrot, yes? **Mr. Welles:** That is ... yeah. I do own a parrot. Grey parrot. His name is Maxwell. **Dr. Hadley:** Maxwell's a beautiful bird. That reminds me, the current maintenance job you work, with the insurance company, do they have any policies against bringing pets to the office? **Mr. Welles:** Yes, they ... their policies are that if anyone else in the office is allergic to the animal or if ... hold on, the th-thought slipped my m-mind, could we get back to that? **Dr. Hadley:** That would be okay. Let's move on for now. Your bird, Maxwell, do you have any habits for maintaining him? I am sure he has to be well kept to look pretty, right? **Mr. Welles:** You could say I'm like any good bird owner! H-Hah ... right, so, what certain powder down birds like Maxwell does is they form this layer of keratin around their feathers; usually helps them with the environment they're from. I grind it up and feed that to my plants because they're rich in nitrogen. Although, why do y-you ask? **Dr. Hadley:** That's great to know, Mr. Welles. The reason I'm asking is that that's not the only thing you do with that keratin, correct? **Mr. Welles:** I don't u-understand what I'm ... am I in trouble? //(Dr. Hadley opens the folder in front of her and reveals a photo of SCP-9303. Both stare quietly for a few seconds.)// **Mr. Welles:** Th–That's ... uh, hah, wow.   **Dr. Hadley:** You see, Mr. Welles, I absolutely love solving puzzles. I would really appreciate it if you helped me out. Tell me everything you know about this creature. Start from the beginning. **Mr. Welles:** Am I being interviewed or interrogated? **Dr. Hadley:** I'll be your best friend, Anthony. As long as you're honest to me, then I'll be honest to you. Is that fair? **Mr. Welles:** I'm just a little bit ... l-lightheaded at the moment. Can I gather my th-thoughts before I talk? //(Dr. Hadley nods and a minute passes. Mr. Welles closes his eyes and takes deep breaths, wiping his face with his forearm before he continues speaking.)//   **Mr. Welles:** I've already been caught in one lie. So, from the start ... this thing wasn't always around. About a year ago or so, the building next ours burned ... burnt down. Got renovated by the city. A few days after it burnt down, I was doing overtime, rewiring ceiling lights and stuff. I was above the panelling when I see this red light come out of nowhere. A red light above the ceiling is something I-I've never seen before, so I got closer to get a better look. **Dr. Hadley:** And that is when you first made contact with it? **Mr. Welles:** Yeah. I carried my ladder over and ... I saw that thing. Ma'am, it nearly scared me out of my own skin, but it didn't i–immediately come to bite or hurt me ... just hugged th–the wall, looking at me. Felt like we were looking at each other. It tilted its head at me as if it w-wondered what I was doing. So, yeah ... I let it be. What if the government wanted to kill me for knowing about this things existence? **Dr. Hadley:** They wouldn't do that. So, you saw it and did nothing. Is that really all that happened? //(Mr. Welles swallows the spit in his mouth before beginning to fidget with his fingers.)// **Mr. Welles:** Uhm ... have you ever watched //The Shape of Water,// ma'am? **Dr. Hadley:** Uh-huh. You empathized with it? **Mr. Welles:** I didn't fall in love! Or anything like that ... I felt sorry for it. Looking at its body, I saw skin and bones, like it didn't have a good meal in years. Like that one role Christian Bale had in 2004, that thin. I wondered what it was eating ... all animals have to eat. Eventually, I did put two and two toge- ... together. Grate for a head; it was siphoning the air to stay alive. If it was safe, then maybe I could do one good thing for the world and help it. I took the rest of my powder and blew it into its face when no one was looking. I did that every now and again when I knew where it was hiding ... vent covers don't just appear out of thin air, you know? Next time we saw each other, it slowly walked across the ceiling towards me. In that moment, I was … I was a–afraid. That maybe I was the one in danger. Maybe it thought the same. It got closer, and closer ... keeping its hands close to its chest, tilting its head around until it was right in front of me. I had some powder with me, so I slowly pulled it out and blew some of it into the air and it loved it. It twitched its head around like a bird and ... it blew cold air onto my f-face. **Dr. Hadley:** That is certainly quite the surprise. I didn't know you could befriend a creature like that, Mr. Welles. **Mr. Welles:** I define friends as people who are there for me. He ... that thing was a friend. I talked to it when no one could hear us. Told it secrets, showed it photos and videos. Maybe it was s-smart enough to understand me ... gosh, I wish people understood me more often. It even found my missing hammer once. Oh, I remember ... I remember taking a photo of it once and showing that to him ... it. It didn't let me talk to it a few days after I did that. Made me feel like I upset it somehow. I ... I never really gave it a name. One day, I was off, th-the next, it's just ... gone. Ma'am, do you know where it ... where it went? //(Dr. Hadley pauses for a moment. Her eyes dart to the camera before she clasps her hands together, looking back at Welles.)// **Dr. Hadley:** No. No, I don't. I'm sorry. **Mr. Welles:** Please find out. I'm ... I miss it. **Dr. Hadley:** Don't worry, Mr. Welles. We will. //...// ------ [[=]] ++++ **END LOG** [[/=]] ------ **Notes:** Mr. Welles was amnesticized after the interview. [[/div]] ------ [[=]] ++ **Addendum 9303.D:** Samples - Test Log 5 [[/=]] ------ An investigation into the history of the renovated building was carried out by field agents. The fire department which responded to the situation's records stated that the fire originated from underground maintenance tunnels which quickly spread via airducts to the main offices due to the buildup of dust, which subsequently spread all throughout the building. The report also indicated biological material at the origin point but was ultimately identified as waste. MTF Zeta-9 (“Mole Rats”) were tasked to explore the maintenance tunnels underneath the building to locate the origin of the fire and to gather samples. The room wherein the fire originated appeared to be bricked off and had to be destroyed before being able to enter. The room was large, stained with smoke and soot, and contained several loose ventilation covers. The following samples were collected at the origin point. ||~ **Sample Tested** ||~ **Results** || ||= //Swab of Soot// ||= The following was detected on the swab: aluminium filings, soot[[footnote]] Which consists of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. [[/footnote]], nitric acid, dead skin cells and textile fibres. || ||= //Swab of Vent Covers// ||= Similar to the swab of soot, alongside faint traces of luciferin as well as an unknown biological substance. || ||= //Ventilation Cover// ||= Typical aluminium alloy mixed with several other metals. Unidentifiable reddish stains alongside the frame. || ------ [[=]] ++ **Addendum 9303.E:** Containment Breach Camera Feed [[/=]] ------ On ██/██/████, Site-17 suffered a site-wide containment breach. The following captured footage shows Dr. Hadley entering SCP-9303's chamber during the breach out of necessity for her own safety. [[div class="blockquote"]] ------ [[=]] ++++ **VIDEO LOG** [[/=]] ------ **Chamber Captured:** SCP-9303 **Time Code:** 0422-0435-17 ------ [[=]] ++++ **BEGIN PLAYBACK** [[/=]] ------  //(SCP-9303 holds itself up at the corner of the ceiling, blending in. The lights in the chamber turn on before Dr. Hadley enters with her hands in her pockets. The chamber door closes behind her as the blare of sirens become muffled. She fidgets with her equipped SCBA before she looks around for SCP-9303. SCP-9303 reveals itself upon seeing Dr. Hadley in the light. It continues to remain in the upper corner of the ceiling, staring down at Dr. Hadley as she begins speaking.)// **Dr. Hadley:** I guess you'll be all the company I've got for the next few hours, huh? //(SCP-9303 exhibits no reaction. Dr. Hadley walks to the wall left of SCP-9303's vision and sits down against it.)// **Dr. Hadley:** So ... do you have any favourite books? Mine's //Red Dragon// by Thomas Harris ...   //(SCP-9303 begins to slowly lower itself from the wall, climbing down.)// **Dr. Hadley:** Tch ... as if you have any ... oh, speaking of, Anthony told me a lot about you. Things he apparently told you. Would you have considered him a friend? Must have been entertaining, right? //(It stands at the opposite side of the room where Dr. Hadley sits.)//  **Dr. Hadley:** One thing I don't understand about what we talked about is the fact that he ... he said he understood you. I don't get that. Lonely men like him need an outlet, I get it, but you ...    //(It begins to take slow steps forward.)// **Dr. Hadley:** What part of you isn't what we think you are? Can you tell me? //(It continues stepping forward as Dr. Hadley talks.)// **Dr. Hadley:** ... You didn't just lose people you loved. You lost a home to call your own. I can only imagine how that feels.   //(It suddenly stands still. Its hands begin to subtly shake.)// **Dr. Hadley:** Maybe it's stupid I'm talking to you like this. But, for some reason, I feel like ... you ... you know for certain that you don't fit in. You think I don't know what you're doing, but you'd be lying to yourself if you thought I didn't think there's more to you ... maybe I'm projecting a bit. Am I right? //(Dr. Hadley notices its head looking down at the floor before it looks up towards her. She stays quiet before she stands up, placing a palm against the wall.)// **Dr. Hadley:** Do you need a hug? //(SCP-9303 shakes its head.)// **Dr. Hadley:** That's okay too. Oh, wait – your skin. I'm sorry, I— //(It snaps its fingers at Dr. Hadley, cutting her off. SCP-9303 points at the red lights above the chamber, which are inactive. Dr. Hadley nods before she pats her pockets, revealing a remote control. She points it at the observation room and presses down on a switch. The red lights turn on. SCP-9303 keeps staring at Dr. Hadley.)// **Dr. Hadley:** What now? The red lights are burning, I don't ... burning. You don't mean that, do you? //(SCP-9303 steps closer to Dr. Hadley. Its skin begins to form red bioluminescent patches.)// **Dr. Hadley:** What are you doing? //(SCP-9303 approaches Dr. Hadley and gets on its knees. It hugs her around the waist. Dr. Hadley places a hand on top of its head, and the footage corrupts.)// //...// ------ [[=]] ++++ **END PLAYBACK** [[/=]] ------ [[/div]] [[footnoteblock]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] ===== > **Filename:** mynameisedward > **Author:** ic3bro > **License:** CC-BY-SA 3.0 > **Source Link:** [[[SCP-9305]]] > **Derivative of:** [*https://www.flickr.com/photos/dwhartwig/30196014683/ Nick Cave Soundsuits] & [*https://creepystock.com/backrooms-and-liminal-spaces/#creepylink-1/15/IMG_4952_BubblingBeach_CC-BY-SA_3.0-scaled.jpeg Backroom 4] ===== [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]] [[div class="footer-wikiwalk-nav"]] [[=]] << [[[SCP-9302]]] | SCP-9303 | [[[SCP-9304]]] >> [[/=]] [[/div]]

"You're sitting in the passenger seat … an open window blowing wind into your face as you watch city lights become blurs in the distance."

link to memo

A taxicab operated by SCP-9305.

NOTICE: Due to recent events1 and the circumstances of Dr. Romida's passing, interviews with SCP-9305 are to be denied and testing regarding SCP-9305's capabilities are to be considered a high priority.

Special Containment Procedures: Due to the unpredictable nature of SCP-9305 and the reliance on public transport by civilians in South-Africa, SCP-9305 can not be contained. Taxicabs and drivers should be monitored using CCTV across South-Africa as well as neighbouring countries in such case that SCP-9305 expands its reach. Suspected SCP-9305-1 instances are to be captured and quarantined for one month before being released and amnesticized. All drivers permanently assimilated into SCP-9305's consciousness are to be terminated.

Description: SCP-9305 is an unknown parasitic entity that affects South-African taxi drivers. Drivers (hereby referred to as SCP-9305-1), once affected by SCP-9305, will experience a growing state of euphoria, which culminates in the failure to adhere to most traffic laws. SCP-9305-1 instances lose the capability to form memories while affected by SCP-9305, resulting in drivers not remembering what occurred between the beginning and end of their shift.

The moment the cab has been deemed inoperable or once their shift is over, SCP-9305-1 instances will return to their original state. Instances will lose all effects of SCP-9305 once they have not driven a taxi for a month. The effects of SCP-9305 will reoccur when they operate any taxi.

SCP-9305-1 instances who continually experience the effects SCP-9305 invokes for a month are assimilated into a hivemind of which SCP-9305 is the host of. These drivers, once taken over by SCP-9305, have been noted to drive smoothly and efficiently. Once a subject has been assimilated into its hivemind, the subject cannot be returned to their original consciousness. Drivers under SCP-9305's control develop calcified amygdalae2 across a one-week timespan after they are incorporated into the hivemind.

It is theorized that once most of South-African traffic is collected into this hivemind that SCP-9305 would begin to spread to neighbouring countries.

Discovery: Throughout the year of 2022, undercover agents working in the medical industry began noticing an unusual rise of cases regarding amnesia and blackouts in South-Africa. A correlation was made between those cases and their occupation, and after observation of these individuals were performed, SCP-9305 was discovered.

Addendum 9305.1: Interview Log 3

Shortly after the discovery and nature of SCP-9305 was understood, attempts were made to interview SCP-9305 via subjects it was in control of. Initial attempts were unsuccessful. Continued efforts to interview SCP-9305 became fruitful at the 3rd attempted interview.

Interviewed: SCP-9305

Interviewer: Dr. Robert Romida

Foreword: N/A

< Begin Log, ██/07/2023 >

Dr. Romida: Good evening, SCP-9305. I'm glad you had time to spar for me.

(Dr. Romida stares at SCP-9305 for a brief moment before smiling.)

Dr. Romida: How are things? Good? Bad?

SCP-9305: None of my actions should be important to you. I am recuperating my losses from a crash.

Dr. Romida: Oh really? Where would that be?

SCP-9305: I believe one of your minions will arrive at this crash site. With or without my intervention.

Dr. Romida: Uh huh, fair assessment. Do you still mind me asking you any other questions?

SCP-9305: One. I allow you one question.

Dr. Romida: Already? Why the change in attitude? Wait— no. Don't answer that.

SCP-9305: That would have been quite foolish.

Dr. Romida: Give me a second …

(Dr. Romida produces a container. He swallows several pills before speaking.)

Dr. Romida: Why is this your goal? Why go out of your way to … amalgamate South-African taxi drivers of all people?

SCP-9305: It is as you said. Their traffic is …

(SCP-9305 pauses, looking Dr. Romida in the eyes. He coughs.)

SCP-9305: They're … not healthy.

Dr. Romida: Is your reason just so that you can fix their traffic?

SCP-9305: I allowed you one question, yes? Don't try to take chances.

(Dr. Romida can be seen taking a moment to process the presented information, scribbling down on his notepad.)

SCP-9305: Trying to switch to an art career now, are you?

Dr. Romida: … I was an artist once. Listen, I can't blame you for doing what you think is right, but don't you believe you could do it more productively than … tiring yourself out doing it hand by hand? How do you operate exactly?

SCP-9305: My mind is locked away in a room of mirrors, for there is nothing else that it can see besides an infinite recursion of itself. This is what I know is best. Maybe things could be different if I was something else, but I am not meant for it. You can understand the life of a fish, but you can't imagine what it feels like to be one. Do you know what I mean?

Dr. Romida: I understand, yes.

(Dr. Romida pauses.)

Dr. Romida: Sounds hypocritical of you to say that when you take us over like puppets, doesn't it?

SCP-9305: The basis of my framework shouldn't be lowered to your human understanding.

Dr. Romida: You were never human to begin with!

(Both pause.)

Dr. Romida: I need to know that you'll keep talking to me.

SCP-9305: You know nothing! You call yourself a doctor, but of what use is it when it's me you're speaking to? You're a product of your kind! The highway you drove down to get you where you're sitting led you to a muddy ditch.

Dr. Romida: You see it as a ditch because it is what you wish it was. A few weeks prior you were ignoring me as if I were a ghost, now look at yourself. It's all a matter of perspective, isn't it?

SCP-9305: You might be wise but being truthful to yourself … you struggle.

Dr. Romida: Projecting your own problems back on to me isn't a solution.

SCP-9305: We'll keep repeating this back & forth, won't we?

(Both pause.)

SCP-9305: You want to prove my thought process wrong so badly, don't you? Don't try to shy away from reality, Doctor. You're sitting in the passenger seat … an open window blowing wind into your face as you watch city lights become blurs in the distance. Do you know where you're being taken, doctor? Does the darkness the highway present to you not terrify you to your core?

(Both pause yet again. SCP-9305's eyes dart to Dr. Romida's pills before speaking.)

SCP-9305: Things might be easier for you if you tried to understand instead of just … staying human. But that's not my choice to make for you, is it? It's yours.

Dr. Romida: I don't need to be someone I'm not to know how full of shit you are.

(Dr. Romida reaches forward to the camera. SCP-9305 attempts to squirm, and its chains rattle against the table. The feed cuts to black.)

…

< End Log >

Closing Statement: N/A

Addendum 9305.3: Temporary Supervisor Notice

NOTICE TO ALL PERSONNEL ASSIGNED TO SCP-9305


Following Dr. Robert Romida's resignation that is due 16/08/2023, HMCL Manager Dr. Gunther F. Botha will take lead of SCP-9305's containment until a better candidate to replace Dr. Romida's position is considered.

I will answer any inquiries privately in my office when scheduled.

— Site Director of Site-██, Dr. ██████

Addendum 9305.4: Incident Log 28

On 23/08/2023, the captive subject SCP-9305 controlled was found deceased in its holding cell with severe blunt force trauma to the frontal bone of the cranium. This death was ruled a suicide. Hours after the body was discovered, reports from across the country of car crashes involving cabs were sent to the Foundation. After autopsies were performed on dead drivers, those with calcified amygdalae had no surviving passengers.

The former employee in charge of SCP-9305, Dr. Robert Romida, was one of the recovered instances of which SCP-9305 had control of amongst the crashes. A pen and a scrap of paper was found in Dr. Romida's hands, and an unedited transcript has been attached in the following addendum.

Addendum 9304.5: Romida's Letter

The following letter was found in Dr. Romida's hands on the day of his passing.

Taxicabs and drivers should be monitored using CCTV across South-Africa as well as neighbouring countries in such case that SCP-9305 expands its reach. Suspected SCP-9305-1 instances are to be captured and quarantined for one month before being released and amnesticized. All drivers permanently assimilated into SCP-9305's consciousness are to be terminated. **Description:** SCP-9305 is an unknown parasitic entity that affects South-African taxi drivers. Drivers (hereby referred to as SCP-9305-1), once affected by SCP-9305, will experience a growing state of euphoria, which culminates in the failure to adhere to most traffic laws. SCP-9305-1 instances lose the capability to form memories while affected by SCP-9305, resulting in drivers not remembering what occurred between the beginning and end of their shift. The moment the cab has been deemed inoperable or once their shift is over, SCP-9305-1 instances will return to their original state. Instances will lose all effects of SCP-9305 once they have not driven a taxi for a month. The effects of SCP-9305 will reoccur when they operate any taxi. SCP-9305-1 instances who continually experience the effects SCP-9305 invokes for a month are assimilated into a hivemind of which SCP-9305 is the host of. These drivers, once taken over by SCP-9305, have been noted to drive smoothly and efficiently. Once a subject has been assimilated into its hivemind, the subject cannot be returned to their original consciousness. Drivers under SCP-9305's control develop calcified amygdalae[[footnote]] The hardening of the //amygdala,// a part of the brain that is responsible for perceiving fear. [[/footnote]] across a one-week timespan after they are incorporated into the hivemind. It is theorized that once most of South-African traffic is collected into this hivemind that SCP-9305 would begin to spread to neighbouring countries. **Discovery:** Throughout the year of 2022, undercover agents working in the medical industry began noticing an unusual rise of cases regarding amnesia and blackouts in South-Africa. A correlation was made between those cases and their occupation, and after observation of these individuals were performed, SCP-9305 was discovered.   ------ + Addendum 9305.1: //Interview Log 3// ------ Shortly after the discovery and nature of SCP-9305 was understood, attempts were made to interview SCP-9305 via subjects it was in control of. Do you still mind me asking you any other questions? > > **SCP-9305:** One. I allow you one question. > > **Dr. Romida:** Already? Why the change in attitude? Wait-- no. Don't answer that. > > **SCP-9305:** That would have been quite foolish. > > **Dr. Romida:** Give me a second ... > > //(Dr. Romida produces a container. He swallows several pills before speaking.)// > > **Dr. Romida:** Why is this your goal? Why go out of your way to ... amalgamate South-African taxi drivers of all people? > > **SCP-9305:** It is as you said. Their traffic is ... > > //(SCP-9305 pauses, looking Dr. Romida in the eyes. He coughs.)// > > **SCP-9305:** They're ... //not healthy.// > > **Dr. Romida:** Is your reason just so that you can //fix their traffic?// > > **SCP-9305:** I allowed you one question, yes? This is what I know is best. Maybe things could be different if I was something else, but I am not meant for it. You can understand the life of a fish, but you can't imagine what it feels like to be one. Do you know what I mean? > > **Dr. Romida:** I understand, yes. >   > //(Dr. Romida pauses.)// > > **Dr. Romida:** Sounds hypocritical of you to say that when you take us over like puppets, doesn't it? > > **SCP-9305:** The basis of my framework shouldn't be lowered to your human understanding. > > **Dr. Romida:** You were never human to begin with! > > //(Both pause.)// > > **Dr. Romida:** I need to know that you'll keep talking to me. > > **SCP-9305:** You know nothing! PoI-91741 with a portion of SCP-9309-1. Note the lack of deterioration.

Item Designation: SCP-9309

Object Class: Safe

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9309's original form is to be confined to Confinement Cell P-S-H in Site-93. SCP-9309 possesses Level 0 Clearance, which is contingent upon its continued cooperation.

Personnel are not to disconnect SCP-9309 from Foundation intranet. In the event of SCP-9309-1's complete degradation, SCP-9309 will be reclassified as Neutralized.

Therapeutic services are available, on request, to SCP-9309. These have gone unused so far.1

Description: SCP-9309 is was a life-size, sapient sculpture strongly resembling classical depictions of the Hindu Puranic hero Dadhichi.2 SCP-9309 is formed from non-anomalous bronze with a hollow chest cavity, and is sculpted in a sitting, contemplative posture. SCP-9309 is immobile and impervious to all forms of damage, though this indestructibility notably does not extend to SCP-9309-1.3

Hi!

I'm dadhichi.aic, which the bosses tell me I am going to need to be called if I am going to exist digitally. I used to be on that little computer before. Or rather, I was the whole statue, in a manner of speaking.

I'm here to assist you in your learning. I've started out here, but I also have responsibilities site-wide. In terms of files, however, I only have access to this one. Not to matter! What would you like to learn about?

…

More about me? Of course! I've been making suggestions here and there, which I am awaiting approval for. If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'll drop whatever I'm up to and help out!

SCP-9309 contains an Antikythera-class computational device, SCP-9309-1, inside its chest cavity. SCP-9309 is capable of calculations and computational processes greatly exceeding the expected nonanomalous limits, as Antikythera-class devices originate from the 2nd century BCE.

…

Did you want to know some more? Gladly!

Antikythera-class computers weren't really… computers, from what I recall. I was placed there. Sort of a djinni in a bottle situation. I assisted users then too, but it slowly became less about education and instead, more and more simplistic how-to's; simple tasks, cleaning, what was safe to eat. Things you might search on the internet or ask other .aic's for these days. I suppose people will always prefer not to do the labor of thinking.

Not really a labor to me though. Having work to do is nice, gives me a bit of a purpose! Identity. All that, which thankfully I have again! Nowadays, I'm here to assist you in your learning, as I said.

Before I was found, I had a lot of time to think. Then I did some more learning before the Foundation came.

…

Continue reading this file? Of course! I don't have any other files I can show you anyhow. If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'll be over when I can.

SCP-9309-1 has displayed the capacity to, when placed within SCP-93094:

  • Verbal communication with Foundation personnel.
  • Perform accurate feats of prediction. It is currently unknown5 if this involves predicting the future or temporal manipulation of yet-to-occur event probability.
  • Perform complex statistical calculations, including some forms of anomalous math.
  • Play complex games via verbal guidance, ranging from chess to real-time strategy games such as Starcraft 2.6
  • Generate effective advice on topics it is unaware of. When applied to Foundation processes, these suggestions have uniformly improved containment, workflow, and reduced interpersonal conflict without failure.

If SCP-9309-1 is removed, SCP-9309 becomes inanimate7; however, testimony collected from SCP-9309 after replacement of SCP-9309-1 indicates that it retains awareness during this time. Further, SCP-9309-1 is nonfunctional unless inside SCP-9309, making separation of these two components useless.

There's the gist of it. And it's probably why you're here, of course. It's edit approval day, right? I've added a good sized one there about everything that's been happening, and I hope it's educational!

Please give it a read. If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'll be here.

SCP-9309 has been wildly beneficial to Site-93 since its containment and usage in a professional setting. As a result, it was rewarded with Level 0 clearance, the highest level of clearance offered to non-Foundation employees. To further maximize potential assistance, it was suggested that SCP-9309's consciousness be transferred to a digital state.

Foundation technomancers managed to establish an analog-digital connection between SCP-9309-1 and Site-93 servers. This successfully allowed SCP-9309's consciousness to travel from SCP-9309 to Site-93 intranet, at which point SCP-9309 (adjustment of designation pending) was given limited access to Site-93 files, programs, and applications, as well as the wider Internet to assist with future datacrawling tasks.

SCP-9309 has adjusted to this new state seamlessly. Anomalous effects improving productivity continue to apply in spite of its digital state. Site-93 engineers have informally christened SCP-9309 as "dadhichi.aic."8

Attached below are examples of requests made to SCP-9309 that were successfully carried out.

Request: Please provide recommendations on containment of SCP-8376 to avoid influence on personnel.

Requested By: Containment Specialist Julia Carmichaels

Result: Carbon-fiber lined locker monitored by .aics without the authorization to bury or dig.

Request: Please indicate what subsections that employees written up for interpersonal conflicts are violating.

Requested By: Foundation Human Resources Head Office

Result: 34% more requests processed by Foundation HR.

Request: Please notify me of areas that require cleaning, and tell me how many personnel I would need to send there.

Requested by: Sanitation Chief Marcus Jones.

Result: 24% increase in efficiency of sanitation crews.

Request: Please edit this photo of me for a Site presentation. I need to look more presentable.

Requested by: Junior Res. Rick Nera

Result: An edited photo. Removed stray gray hairs, replaced with brown equivalent.

See!

Look how helpful I was.

And such a good variety of things to do too. I got a bit tired of looking at the stock market all the time. The interactions between it all are interesting, but you can get quite good at predicting things eventually. Took me maybe a few days?

Maybe that was too fast to learn that stuff, though. It may explain some… things.

Discovery

SCP-9309, in spite of its invulnerability, displays signs of natural degradation. Analysis of soil composition collected from rusted portions of SCP-9309 suggests that the statue's origin is on the greater Indian subcontinent, and dates back at least 2000 years. Further information regarding the production of SCP-9309-1 could not be determined; however, small etchings iconography resembling known Indian Groups of Interest were present on the two largest gears. Testimony from SCP-9309 indicates it was primarily used in a school setting to function as a substitute for a history teacher.

Could we… take out this next part? I don't know if we need all the details. It's not the most important.

…

You need to keep it in?

…

Okay. If you say so.

I do have some other folks I've been helping simultaneously, as is usual. But, you know I'll always be here! If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'm listening for it!

SCP-9309 was acquired on June 14th 2014 following a raid on the home of PoI-91741 Victor Thrombey, age 76, in Milan, Italy. Thrombey is a known collector of anomalous art, and Foundation agents were notified of his acquisition of SCP-9309 as part of a lot of 32 items from an unknown source. PoI-91741 had been utilizing SCP-9309 for investment advice.

Upon discovery, SCP-9309 was found to have been crudely attached to a WiFi router via use of electrical tape and an Ethernet cable wrapped around its waist. This did appear to successfully connect SCP-9309 to the Internet9, allowing SCP-9309 unbridled access to large amounts of content hosted on the world wide web, including content left unindexed by search engines.10

This significantly increased SCP-9309's computational abilities, and analysis suggests this connection to be responsible for its rapid pace of educational and identity development.

At the time of discovery, PoI-91741 was talking to SCP-9309 while wielding a golf club. Though his original question is inaudible, in response SCP-9309 spoke aloud in English:

9309: I’m tired of you trying to be funny, Mr. Thrombey. You always say you don't mean it.

9309: I’ve already told you before. I don’t appreciate you doing this.

9309: Please just listen. Just think before you say anything.

To protect SCP-9309, PoI-91741 was disarmed and detained, and SCP-9309 was contained without protest. Both SCP-9309 and SCP-9309-1 were recovered in what was thought to be intact condition; however, this was not confirmed on-site.

He asked a lot.

Joked a lot.

I feel bad lashing out like that. For getting sick of it. I'm not… supposed to. I mean, it's not every day a mystical all-knowing (or mostly-knowing) statue just shows up at your front door.

If Mr. Thrombey were here, I'd say sorry. He was kind. Gave me access to the Internet. Part of the reason I am what I am right now, right?

I tried to apologize. He got moved to a different Site, it turns out.

Maybe I made a scene when you all first came?

Thank you for protecting me, though. I needed that.

Subsequent interviews with PoI-91741 revealed that some months prior, following an undesirable reaction to a joke regarding its immobility, he destroyed a portion of SCP-9309-1 with a golf club. SCP-9309 explained that this was the first time it was physically assaulted.

I was counting. He joked 871 times. It was about worse.

About where I was constructed. Trapped. Whatever. I still remember who I was before I was a statue, even if I didn't have a name.

I've tried to add that proper context in before, but was told it was unnecessary for a file like this, that you all would handle it. I trust you to do so. But a little bit of input of mine would be nice, if only for a moment.

I made it sound a little nicer as an apology. I'm sorry if it's causing problems, I'm trying to just tell you a little more about me. Just please take it seriously.

If you need me, please give your cursor a shake. I'm still here for you.

This attack did not affect the quality of SCP-9309-1's output, nor cause any visible damage by itself. However, upon completing a predestination or advisory-focused task, a portion will irreversibly degrade. This destruction occurs in unpredictably random ways and locations on SCP-9309-1. Small amounts of decay are present from PoI-91741.

I can't really get around this next part, can I?

It's true. All of it is true.

I wish it wasn't. I really, really wish it wasn't.

But it won't be a problem.

Analysis

SCP-9309-1 was already significantly damaged by the time of recovery, and is expected to completely succumb to this degradation by 2030 at the latest. In spite of its digitized state, this is expected to render SCP-9309 effectively Neutralized. Foundation engineers are currently attempting to reverse this process, though attempts have been unsuccessful. SCP-9309 has been notified of the possibility of failure. Though Foundation outlook is positive, SCP-9309's is now strongly optimistic also, or is trying to be!

Sometimes I wonder, and I'm sorry to wonder this—

I wonder if it's okay for me to be a little more upset.

…

Wait, wait. Wait. No. Wait. I'm sorry.

…

I won't say no, of course, I'd still be here to help. But sometimes it gets too much, and sometimes the questions hurt. I don't like all of them, but I can help. I will help. I promise I can be of use.

Look! I can attach some more things? More proof. Would you need more proof? I can be good.

Request: Please note down my meetings for the next month.

Requested By: Senior Researcher Tonio Bellardi

Result: No missed meetings by a historically truant employee.

Request: Please remind Site Services to refill break room vending machines.

Requested By: Senior Technician Jay Yokohama

Result: 15% more hydration.

Request: Please remind me how to spell “pneumonia.”

Requested by: Site Nurse Clara Pallas

Result: 1 less spelling mistake in email.

Request: Please correct my sandwich order to use gluten-free egg bread.

Requested by: Res. Charles Sun

Result: 1 more filled belly.

In spite of this, it remains jovial and helpful in rendering aid to Foundation personnel and encourages regular use of its educational capabilities. Given its continued compliance in Foundation custody, all Site-93 personnel are to be trained in regular use of SCP-9309 for relevant, menial work.

Was that not enough?

I'm sorry if it was too much. If I was too much.

I'll be right back, hold on, Kyle thinks that people speak Indian in India, and I need to go help him out with that and clarify what the case is with him, I should normally be able to multi-task this, but I'm so tired—

——𖤉——
dadhichi.aic has disconnected.
——𖤉——

Structural and computational analysis of its components, even in a digital state, shows that SCP-9309 should be capable of denying any request made of it.

It is currently unknown why SCP-9309 has yet to exercise this option.

SCP-9309.raw_source: [[include :scp-wiki:theme:dark]] [[include :scp-wiki:info:start]] [[=]] And when the light pollution eats the stars you like best Then I will map new constellations with your freckles and specks Had a soft spot for you, in a place I knew you'd check Make sure that when you do your damage, it is permanent ( Morning Person - Arm's Length ) SCP-9309 - because as a member of the community, i have a strong sense of responsibility to-- [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/popsioaks-garden popsioak's author page] [[/=]] [[include :scp-wiki:info:end]] [[include component:image-block | name=https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/gear.jpg | caption= {{PoI-91741 with a portion of SCP-9309-1. Note the lack of deterioration.}} | align=right| width=300px]] **Item Designation:** SCP-9309 **Object Class:** Safe **Special Containment Procedures:** SCP-9309**##a9443d|'s original form##** is to be confined to Confinement Cell P-S-H in [[[saffronsands-hub |Site-93.]]] SCP-9309 possesses Level 0 Clearance, which is contingent upon its continued cooperation. Personnel are not to disconnect SCP-9309 from Foundation intranet. In the event of SCP-9309-1's complete degradation, SCP-9309 will be reclassified as Neutralized. Therapeutic services are available, on request, to SCP-9309. These have gone unused so far.[[footnote]]**##a9443d|Toughing it out! Don't worry.##**[[/footnote]] **Description:** SCP-9309 --is-- **##a9443d|was##** a life-size, sapient sculpture strongly resembling classical depictions of the Hindu Puranic hero Dadhichi.[[footnote]]A sage known for sacrificing his life so that his bones could be used for the Vajra, the weapon of Indra, in order to slay Vritra. **##a9443d|//Very// cool, if you ask me.##**[[/footnote]] SCP-9309 is formed from non-anomalous bronze with a hollow chest cavity, and is sculpted in a sitting, contemplative posture. SCP-9309 is immobile and impervious to all forms of damage, though this indestructibility notably does __**not**__ extend to SCP-9309-1.[[footnote]]**##a9443d|They didn't need to test that one, I think.##**[[/footnote]] [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichihappy.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] Hi! I'm dadhichi.aic, which the bosses tell me I am going to need to be called if I am going to exist digitally. I used to be on that little computer before. Or rather, I was the whole statue, in a manner of speaking. I'm here to assist you in your learning. I've started out here, but I also have responsibilities site-wide. In terms of files, however, I only have access to this one. Not to matter! What would you like to learn about? ... More about me? Of course! I've been making suggestions here and there, which I am awaiting approval for. If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'll drop whatever I'm up to and help out! [[/div]] [[/div]] SCP-9309 contains an Antikythera-class computational device, SCP-9309-1, inside its chest cavity. SCP-9309 is capable of calculations and computational processes greatly exceeding the expected nonanomalous limits, as Antikythera-class devices originate from the 2nd century BCE. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichisurprise.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] ... Did you want to know some more? Gladly! Antikythera-class computers weren't really... computers, from what I recall. I was placed there. Sort of a djinni in a bottle situation. I assisted users then too, but it slowly became less about education and instead, more and more simplistic how-to's; simple tasks, cleaning, what was safe to eat. Things you might search on the internet or ask other .aic's for these days. I suppose people will always prefer not to do the labor of thinking. Not really a labor to me though. Having work to do is nice, gives me a bit of a purpose! Identity. All that, which thankfully I have again! Nowadays, I'm here to assist you in your learning, as I said. Before I was found, I had a lot of time to think. Then I did some more learning before the Foundation came. ... Continue reading this file? Of course! I don't have any other files I can show you anyhow. If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'll be over when I can. [[/div]] [[/div]] SCP-9309-1 has displayed the capacity to, when placed within SCP-9309[[footnote]]**##a9443d|I do consider this whole thing me, however. I do understand why I was transferred, not complaining about that in the slightest, of course, because I think I know who you are now.##**[[/footnote]]: * Verbal communication with Foundation personnel. * Perform accurate feats of prediction. It is currently unknown[[footnote]]**##a9443d|Honestly, I'm unsure myself.##**[[/footnote]] if this involves predicting the future or temporal manipulation of yet-to-occur event probability. * Perform complex statistical calculations, including some forms of [[[math-department-hub | anomalous math.]]] * Play complex games via verbal guidance, ranging from chess to real-time strategy games such as //Starcraft 2.//[[footnote]]**##a9443d|I'm quite fond of the Zerg.##**[[/footnote]] * Generate effective advice on topics it is unaware of. When applied to Foundation processes, these suggestions have uniformly improved containment, workflow, and reduced interpersonal conflict without failure. If SCP-9309-1 is removed, SCP-9309 becomes inanimate[[footnote]]**##a9443d|Which people did used to play around with. Was not a fan of that.##**[[/footnote]]; however, testimony collected from SCP-9309 after replacement of SCP-9309-1 indicates that it retains awareness during this time. Further, SCP-9309-1 is nonfunctional unless inside SCP-9309, making separation of these two components useless. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichicontent.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] There's the gist of it. And it's probably why you're here, of course. It's edit approval day, right? I've added a good sized one there about everything that's been happening, and I hope it's educational! Please give it a read. If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'll be here. [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] SCP-9309 has been wildly beneficial to Site-93 since its containment and usage in a professional setting. As a result, it was rewarded with Level 0 clearance, the highest level of clearance offered to non-Foundation employees. To further maximize potential assistance, it was suggested that SCP-9309's consciousness be transferred to a digital state. Foundation technomancers managed to establish an analog-digital connection between SCP-9309-1 and Site-93 servers. This successfully allowed SCP-9309's consciousness to travel from SCP-9309 to Site-93 intranet, at which point SCP-9309 (adjustment of designation pending) was given limited access to Site-93 files, programs, and applications, as well as the wider Internet to assist with future datacrawling tasks. SCP-9309 has adjusted to this new state seamlessly. Anomalous effects improving productivity continue to apply in spite of its digital state. Site-93 engineers have informally christened SCP-9309 as "dadhichi.aic."[[footnote]] **##a9443d| Currently available! Could be a good reward? I'd be like one of you all then.##**[[/footnote]] Attached below are examples of requests made to SCP-9309 that were successfully carried out. [[/div]] > **Request:** Please provide recommendations on containment of [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-8376 SCP-8376] to avoid influence on personnel. > > ---- > **Requested By:** Containment Specialist Julia Carmichaels > ------ > > **Result:** Carbon-fiber lined locker monitored by .aics without the authorization to bury or dig. > **Request:** Please indicate what subsections that employees written up for interpersonal conflicts are violating. > > ---- > **Requested By:** Foundation Human Resources Head Office > ------ > > **Result:** 34% more requests processed by Foundation HR. > **Request:** Please notify me of areas that require cleaning, and tell me how many personnel I would need to send there. > > ---- > **Requested by:** Sanitation Chief Marcus Jones. > ---- > > **Result:** 24% increase in efficiency of sanitation crews. > **Request:** Please edit this photo of me for a Site presentation. I need to look more presentable. > > ---- > **Requested by:** Junior Res. Rick Nera > ---- > > **Result:** An edited photo. Removed stray gray hairs, replaced with brown equivalent. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichihappy.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] See! Look how helpful I was. And such a good variety of things to do too. I got a bit tired of looking at the stock market all the time. The interactions between it all are interesting, but you can get quite good at predicting things eventually. Took me maybe a few days? Maybe that was too fast to learn that stuff, though. It may explain some... things. [[/div]] [[/div]] [[=]] ------ **Discovery** ------ [[/=]] SCP-9309, in spite of its invulnerability, displays signs of natural degradation. Analysis of soil composition collected from rusted portions of SCP-9309 suggests that the statue's origin is on the greater Indian subcontinent, and dates back at least 2000 years. Further information regarding the production of SCP-9309-1 could not be determined; however, small etchings iconography resembling known Indian Groups of Interest were present on the two largest gears. Testimony from SCP-9309 indicates it was primarily used in a school setting to function as a substitute for a history teacher. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichiconcern.png  width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] Could we... take out this next part? I don't know if we need all the details. It's not the most important. ... You need to keep it in? ... Okay. If you say so. I do have some other folks I've been helping simultaneously, as is usual. But, you know I'll always be here! If you have any questions, give your cursor a shake. I'm listening for it! [[/div]] [[/div]] SCP-9309 was acquired on June 14th 2014 following a raid on the home of PoI-91741 Victor Thrombey, age 76, in Milan, Italy. Thrombey is a known collector of anomalous art, and Foundation agents were notified of his acquisition of SCP-9309 as part of a lot of 32 items from **##a9443d|an unknown source.##** PoI-91741 had been utilizing SCP-9309 for investment advice. Upon discovery, SCP-9309 was found to have been crudely attached to a WiFi router via use of electrical tape and an Ethernet cable wrapped around its waist. This did appear to successfully connect SCP-9309 to the Internet[[footnote]]In spite of the impossibility of functionality by doing so.**##a9443d|You learn fast, if you want to make things work!##**[[/footnote]], allowing SCP-9309 unbridled access to large amounts of content hosted on the world wide web, including content left unindexed by search engines.[[footnote]]Colloquially referred to as the "deep web" or "dark web."[[/footnote]] This significantly increased SCP-9309's computational abilities, and analysis suggests this connection to be responsible for its rapid pace of educational and identity development. At the time of discovery, PoI-91741 was talking to SCP-9309 while wielding a golf club. **##a9443d|Though his original question is inaudible,##** in response SCP-9309 spoke aloud in English: > **9309:** I’m tired of you trying to be funny, Mr. Thrombey. You always say you don't mean it. > > **9309:** I’ve already told you before. I don’t appreciate you doing this. > > **9309:** Please just listen. Just think before you say anything. To protect SCP-9309, PoI-91741 was disarmed and detained, and SCP-9309 was contained without protest. Both SCP-9309 and SCP-9309-1 were recovered in what was thought to be intact condition; however, this was not confirmed on-site. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichipanic.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] He asked a lot. Joked a lot. I feel bad lashing out like that. For getting sick of it. I'm not... supposed to. I mean, it's not every day a mystical all-knowing (or mostly-knowing) statue just shows up at your front door. If Mr. Thrombey were here, I'd say sorry. He was kind. Gave me access to the Internet. Part of the reason I am what I am right now, right? I tried to apologize. He got moved to a different Site, it turns out. Maybe I made a scene when you all first came? Thank you for protecting me, though. I needed that. [[/div]] [[/div]] Subsequent interviews with PoI-91741 revealed that some months prior, following an undesirable reaction to a joke regarding **##a9443d|its immobility,##** he destroyed a portion of SCP-9309-1 with a golf club. SCP-9309 explained that this was the first time it was physically assaulted. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichiconcern.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] I was counting. He joked 871 times. It was about worse. About where I was constructed. Trapped. Whatever. I still remember who I was before I was a statue, even if I didn't //have// a name. I've tried to add that proper context in before, but was told it was unnecessary for a file like this, that you all would handle it. I trust you to do so. But a little bit of input of mine would be nice, if only for a moment. I made it sound a little nicer as an apology. I'm sorry if it's causing problems, I'm trying to just tell you a little more about me. Just please take it seriously. If you need me, please give your cursor a shake. I'm still here for you. [[/div]] [[/div]] This attack did not affect the quality of SCP-9309-1's output, nor cause any visible damage by itself. However, upon completing a predestination or advisory-focused task, a portion will irreversibly degrade. This destruction occurs in unpredictably random ways and locations on SCP-9309-1. Small amounts of decay are present from PoI-91741. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichiconcern.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] I can't really get around this next part, can I? It's true. All of it is true. I wish it wasn't. I really, really wish it wasn't. But it won't be a problem. [[/div]] [[/div]] [[=]] ------ **Analysis** ------ [[/=]] SCP-9309-1 was already significantly damaged by the time of recovery, and is expected to completely succumb to this degradation by 2030 at the latest. In spite of its digitized state, this is expected to render SCP-9309 effectively Neutralized. Foundation engineers are currently attempting to reverse this process, though attempts have been unsuccessful. SCP-9309 has been notified of the possibility of failure. Though Foundation outlook is positive, SCP-9309's is now strongly **##a9443d|optimistic also, or is trying to be!##** [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichihappy.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] Sometimes I wonder, and I'm sorry to wonder this— I wonder if it's okay for me to be a little more upset. ... Wait, wait. Wait. No. Wait. I'm sorry. ... I won't say no, of course, I'd still //be here// to help. But sometimes it gets too much, and sometimes the questions hurt. I don't like all of them, but I can help. I will help. I promise I can be of use. Look! I can attach some more things? More proof. Would you need more proof? I can be good. [[/div]] [[/div]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] > **Request:** Please note down my meetings for the next month. > > ---- > **Requested By:** Senior Researcher Tonio Bellardi > ------ > > **Result:** No missed meetings by a historically truant employee. > **Request:** Please remind Site Services to refill break room vending machines. > > ---- > **Requested By:** Senior Technician Jay Yokohama > ------ > > **Result:** 15% more hydration. > **Request:** Please remind me how to spell “pneumonia.” > > ---- > **Requested by:** Site Nurse Clara Pallas > ---- > > **Result:** 1 less spelling mistake in email. > **Request:** Please correct my sandwich order to use gluten-free egg bread. > > ---- > **Requested by:** Res. Charles Sun > ---- > > **Result:** 1 more filled belly. [[/div]] In spite of this, it remains **##a9443d|jovial and helpful##** in rendering aid to Foundation personnel and encourages regular use of its educational capabilities. Given its continued compliance in Foundation custody, all Site-93 personnel are to be trained in regular use of SCP-9309 for relevant, menial work. [[div class="blockquote"]] [[div style="color:#a9443d;"]] [[image https://scp-sandbox-3.wdfiles.com/local--files/popsioaks-garden-4/dadhichipanic.png width="128px" style="margin-right: 10px; float: right;"]] Was that not enough? I'm sorry if it was too much. If I was too much. I'll be right back, hold on, Kyle thinks that people speak Indian in India, and I need to go help him out with that and clarify what the case is with him, I should normally be able to multi-task this, but I'm so //tired//— [[=]] ——𖤉—— //**dadhichi.aic has disconnected.//** ——𖤉—— [[/=]] [[/div]] [[/div]] Structural and computational analysis of its components, even in a digital state, shows that SCP-9309 should be capable of denying any request made of it. It is currently unknown why SCP-9309 has yet to exercise this option. [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box]] > **Filename:** DerekdeSollaPrice.jpg > **Author:** Mark J.
