SCP-9310.raw_content:
Altar outside the gate of SCP-9310.

Item #: SCP-9310
Object Class: Euclid
Special Containment Procedures: MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”) is authorized to operate full-time within SCP-9310. This task force is also designated as the primary unit responsible for preventing civilian access to SCP-9310 by any means.

Any authorized personnel intending to conduct work, research, or exploration within SCP-9310 must be accompanied by at least one member of MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”) at all times to ensure safety and compliance with current protocols.

The operational headquarters of MTF Sigma-50 is located along the western perimeter of SCP-9310, where facilities supporting rapid response and anomalous containment measures are maintained.

Special Notice: Personnel are strongly advised to avoid entering SCP-9310 on Halloween, as anomalous activity and uncontrolled incidents have been observed to increase significantly on this date.
Description:

SCP-9310 is an anomalous village of thaumaturgical origin located deep within a forested area of Val Poschiavo, Switzerland. According to historical records and testimonies provided by internal entities, SCP-9310 is believed to have been established during the 15th century, coinciding with the escalation of witch hunts across Europe.

SCP-9310 is entirely enveloped by a large-scale thaumaturgical concealment field, which functions as both a visual and perceptual obfuscation mechanism, rendering the village undetectable to unaided observation and modern surveillance technologies. As a result, SCP-9310 effectively does not exist to unauthorized individuals.

The inhabitants of SCP-9310 are collectively designated SCP-9310-A. SCP-9310-A entities are humanoid in appearance and possess advanced proficiency in the application of thaumatology. However, the thaumaturgical methodologies employed by SCP-9310-A are fundamentally distinct from and incompatible with the systems of modern thaumaturgical practice documented by the Foundation.

All SCP-9310-A entities are classified as Wielder-class entities, demonstrating the ability to channel and manipulate anomalous energies directly through their physical forms. Additionally, SCP-9310 contains six (6) entities designated SCP-9310-B, which function as the ruling council and primary authority within the village. SCP-9310-B entities are classified as Gifted-class entities, exhibiting significantly higher levels of thaumaturgical capability and influence than standard SCP-9310-A instances.

SCP-9310-B entities typically manifest as elderly humans; however, multiple instances of voluntary morphological alteration have been documented, allowing these entities to assume significantly younger appearances. The estimated biological ages of entities residing within SCP-9310 range between 550 and 650 years, achieved through sustained thaumaturgical practices intended to prolong lifespan.

Despite their anomalous characteristics, the daily lives of SCP-9310-A and SCP-9310-B entities closely resemble those of baseline humans. Entities require regular consumption of food and water, sleep cycles, and physical activity to maintain physiological stability.

Notably, SCP-9310 entities possess full awareness that witch hunts no longer occur in the outside world. Nevertheless, they have elected to continue residing within SCP-9310 as a closed and self-governing community. Select SCP-9310-A entities are periodically permitted to exit SCP-9310 for limited durations to procure supplies from nearby civilian settlements.

It has been confirmed that SCP-9310 maintains a functioning electrical infrastructure, though the origin and long-term sustainability of its power source remain undetermined.

Addendum 9310-1: Hunting period

Grand Elder Lilly (4/6).

Interviewed: SCP-9310-B-04 (“Grand Elder Lilly”)
Interviewer: Agent Rigid
Location: SCP-9310, Western Perimeter Facility

Physical Description:
Grand Elder Lilly is a humanoid female entity measuring approximately 1.49 meters in height. Postural deformation is present; estimated height without spinal curvature is approximately 1.60 meters. The entity wears a tall, sharply pointed wizard’s hat and consistently carries a crooked wooden staff. Clothing consists of brightly colored garments, predominantly white with accents of warm colors.

Grand Elder Lilly is consistently observed in a state of mild intoxication. A flask is attached to the entity’s waist at all times. Records indicate the flask formerly contained a universal medicinal compound; it is currently used exclusively to store alcoholic beverages.

<Begin Log>

Agent Rigid: Good day, Grand Elder. Thank you for taking the time to meet with me.

(Grand Elder Lilly leans on her staff before sitting down, resting it against the table.)

Grand Elder Lilly: Oh, my poor bones… they ache so terribly.

Agent Rigid: Would you like some assistance?

Grand Elder Lilly: No, no. Just the usual troubles of old age, nothing more.

(Grand Elder Lilly’s voice is raspy and low. It becomes difficult to hear her clearly when ambient noise increases.)

Agent Rigid: Ma’am—your flask stopper seems to be missing. It’s leaking.

Grand Elder Lilly: Oh, that’s quite all right. That flask lost its stopper a long time ago.

(The entity takes a long drink from the flask.)

Agent Rigid: What is that liquid?

Grand Elder Lilly: Alcohol. Much better these days than when I was young. I keep it in this medicine flask and carry it with me.

Agent Rigid: I see… Grand Elder, may I ask when this village was founded?

Grand Elder Lilly: (Frowns) This old mind of mine… let me think… around October 31 , 1450, if I recall correctly. We built this village and concealed it with magic to hide from the authorities. We’ve lived here for a very long time.

Agent Rigid: How did you feel at the time? I apologize—this may bring back unpleasant memories.

Grand Elder Lilly: Time dulls even the deepest wounds. I regret only that I did not stand and protect those I loved. I fled with the others, ran far away. Back then, all I felt was hatred, deep in my core. But… yes, I was childish. They could never live as long as I would.

Agent Rigid: That sounds… terrible. I’m sorry.

Grand Elder Lilly: Have I ever told you? In the past, they even used captured witches to hunt other witches. Ah, you won’t find that in your history books. I and the others erased it from history.

Agent Rigid: Do you mean torture—forcing witches to confess and betray others?

Grand Elder Lilly: No. Far worse. They used some kind of dark art. They removed the witches’ brains and bound each one to a raven. Ravens filled the skies—each bird was one of their eyes.

Agent Rigid: So they used witches to control ravens for hunting. That’s horrifying.

Grand Elder Lilly: They are only echoes of an old age. We live happily here now. Four thousand three hundred and eighty-one witches live in this village. We survived that dark era. We live on for those who did not.

Agent Rigid: I understand. A truly dark period.

Grand Elder Lilly: Indeed. Oh, my spine… I believe I must visit the clinic today.

Agent Rigid: Would you like me to assist you?

Grand Elder Lilly: No, no need. Thank you for your kindness, child.

(Grand Elder Lilly mounts her staff and levitates away from the area.)

<End Log>

Addendum 9310-2: MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”)

MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”) was initially established as an exploration and reconnaissance task force assigned to investigate SCP-9310. Following successful infiltration and extended observation of SCP-9310, Foundation command determined that a permanent, integrated presence would be more effective than conventional containment measures.

As a result, MTF Sigma-50 was reassigned to embed within the SCP-9310 community. Due to the notably cooperative and non-hostile disposition of SCP-9310-A and SCP-9310-B entities, the integration process was completed with minimal resistance or incident.

Prolonged cohabitation with highly skilled thaumaturgical practitioners resulted in a significant anomalous development among Sigma-50 personnel. Over time, multiple members began to manifest thaumaturgical abilities consistent with the operational paradigm of SCP-9310-A and SCP-9310-B entities, rather than modern Foundation-documented systems.

At present, all active members of MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”) are classified as Scholar-type Thaumatologists. Ongoing research efforts are focused on identifying the anomalous mechanisms that allow a significant proportion of SCP-9310-A entities to advance into the Wielder-class.

The following section summarizes the recorded observations regarding thaumaturgical practices employed within SCP-9310, as documented and analyzed by MTF Sigma-50.

Thaumaturgical Practices of SCP-9310-A Entities

Thaumaturgy utilized by SCP-9310-A and SCP-9310-B entities adheres closely to pre-modern European ritualistic traditions, differing fundamentally from contemporary thaumaturgical methodologies recognized by the Foundation.

Through this system, SCP-9310-A entities have demonstrated access to a wide array of abilities traditionally associated with folkloric witchcraft, including but not limited to:

Potion brewing

Curse application

Hexes and maledictions

Divination and prophetic rituals

Alchemy

Conditional invulnerability when subjected to bladed attacks

Directed dream traversal into designated targets

Notably, these abilities require minimal long-term training. Proficiency is primarily dependent on understanding functional principles and activation conditions. Examples include:

Curse rituals requiring a physical component belonging to the target

Potion creation involving extensive and variable formula sets

Talisman construction requiring animal blood, with effectiveness dependent on species-specific properties

Advanced Thaumaturgy of SCP-9310-B

Thaumaturgical application by SCP-9310-B entities follows the same foundational framework as SCP-9310-A; however, it is heavily influenced by subjective interpretation and individual perception.

For example, while SCP-9310-A entities require specific material components (e.g., blood) to create talismans, SCP-9310-B entities may disregard such requirements entirely, focusing instead on symbolic elements such as engraved patterns. Despite bypassing traditional conditions, SCP-9310-B entities consistently produce talismans of greater potency than those created by SCP-9310-A.

In multiple documented cases, SCP-9310-B entities have demonstrated the ability to omit individual steps—or entire ritual procedures—altogether. Manifestation of thaumaturgical effects appears to occur immediately upon conceptual intent, without observable activation conditions.

Thaumaturgy employed by SCP-9310-B is therefore assessed as perception-driven and condition-independent, operating according to the entity’s internal logic rather than external constraints.

As a result, each SCP-9310-B entity possesses at least one unique, high-yield thaumaturgical ability, characterized by extreme effectiveness but infrequent usage. Some SCP-9310-B entities are believed to possess multiple such abilities, though full documentation remains incomplete.

Addendum 9310-3: Halloween Festival at SCP-9310

Halloween festival poster at SCP-9310.

Within SCP-9310, Halloween is regarded as one of the most significant annual celebrations, as it coincides with the anniversary of the village’s founding. Preparations typically begin ten (10) days prior to the event. During this period, SCP-9310-A entities display heightened enthusiasm, decorating structures with Halloween-themed posters and conducting frequent excursions outside SCP-9310 to acquire supplies. The atmosphere within the village becomes notably vibrant and anticipatory.

On the night of the festival, a synchronized countdown ritual is observed throughout SCP-9310.

“9”
“8”
“7”
All residential lights are extinguished simultaneously.

“6”
“5”
Fully matured pumpkins, previously harvested, are gathered at the village center.

“4”
“3”
“2”
Logs are stacked vertically into a tall, conical pyre.

“1”
“0”


At the conclusion of the countdown, the pyre is ignited. The flames rapidly rise, flickering violently as every dwelling within SCP-9310 illuminates at once. A dense fog settles low across the ground, producing a distinctly unsettling atmosphere beneath the firelight.

Despite this, loud laughter and cheerful conversation are recorded among entities whose lifespans exceed five centuries. At approximately 22:00 local time, SCP-9310-A and SCP-9310-B entities gather around the bonfire in a communal assembly. At this point, a male entity ascends the raised platform adjacent to the pyre, signaling the beginning of the central ceremonial proceedings.

Grand Elder Aphex (2/6).

“Thank you all for gathering here today.”

(Grand Elder Aphex, exhibiting pronounced spinal curvature, steps forward while gripping his staff tightly.)

“Time will continue to flow. One by one, we shall eventually abandon this fragile mortal realm and pass into a quieter, more peaceful world beyond. This year, we bear sorrowful news: Grand Elder Carmen (1/6) has passed away. Her loss is a profound one for us all.”

“However, we must not allow grief to bind us for too long. Regard this moment as bitterness—an unkind jest played by fate itself. We endure, as we always have.”

“Now, I hereby declare the Halloween Festival of this year officially begun.”

(Grand Elder Aphex’s cloak suddenly expands, enveloping his entire body. From within the cloak, a large number of white doves emerge and take flight. Upon dissipation of the cloak, Grand Elder Aphex is no longer present.)

Addendum 9310-4: God

Grand Elder Dorothy (5/6).

“We fled. We ran. We abandoned those hellish lands drenched in death and came here. Yes… no. We were never strong enough to create a great concealment barrier like this. Such a thing was impossible with the power we possessed at the time.

The skies behind us were blackened by the King’s ravens. They lurked within the forests, and we prayed that the flocks would fail to find us. But how could anyone ever escape them, when those ravens could merge into a single, unified swarm?

Then came the King’s hunting hounds.

Liam descended upon us.

The King maintained an entire pack of hunters tasked with eliminating any threat he believed might endanger his rule. Liam was the most infamous among them. He wielded an enchanted blade imbued with freezing magic. He moved through forest after forest, killing indiscriminately. One… ten… fifty lives were taken by his hand. It was only a matter of time before he reached us.

Carmen knew this.

As we fled, she whispered continuously—murmuring a chant I had never heard before, a spell unknown even to us. When he finally drew close, preparing to strike me down, Carmen descended from above. Her left hand twisted unnaturally, poised for a single snap.

Snap.

His body was crushed flat against the ground, reduced to ruin in an instant. Without hesitation, she seized his sword and severed his head.

I tell you this not to glorify the past. Our generation is nearing the end of its long life. You—the younger ones—now carry burdens heavier than we ever did. You shall become the new flame that guides humanity forward.”

—Grand Elder Dorothy

Throughout the ongoing investigation into the unusually high concentration of Wielder-class entities within SCP-9310, the Foundation has conducted extensive interviews and informal interactions with SCP-9310 residents. To date, the statement provided by Grand Elder Dorothy (5/6) remains the sole consistent and actionable lead.

Personnel exposed to or actively utilizing the thaumaturgical systems practiced within SCP-9310 consistently report a distinct psychological response. This response is characterized by an intense sensation of anger, resentment, and suppressed rage. These effects have been independently verified by MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”).

Notably, this phenomenon is not limited to direct practitioners. Any individual who is the target or recipient of thaumaturgical effects originating from SCP-9310 methodologies has reported similar emotional feedback, regardless of prior thaumaturgical sensitivity.

A prevailing hypothesis has been proposed identifying Grand Elder Carmen (1/6) as the potential origin of this effect. According to Grand Elder Dorothy’s testimony, prolonged incantation duration directly correlates with spell potency. Based on this principle, it is theorized that Grand Elder Carmen conducted an extended, large-scale thaumaturgical invocation during the period of persecution described in historical accounts.

Foundation researchers now hypothesize that Grand Elder Carmen intentionally created a secondary anomalous construct to serve as a power framework for SCP-9310-A and SCP-9310-B entities. The substance used to condense and stabilize this construct is believed to be the accumulated hatred and anguish of witches killed during the European witch hunts.

This construct—while not directly observable—may function as a collective thaumaturgical reservoir, amplifying emotional resonance and lowering the threshold required for SCP-9310 entities to ascend into the Wielder-class.

Further investigation into this hypothesis is ongoing.

SCP-9310.raw_source: [[include :scp-wiki:theme:halloween]] [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] [[include component:image-block | name=Witches'_Stone_between_Ried_and_the_Falkensteinkirche,_225928.jpg | caption=Altar outside the gate of SCP-9310.]] **Item #:** SCP-9310 **Object Class:** Euclid **Special Containment Procedures:** MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”) is authorized to operate full-time within SCP-9310. This task force is also designated as the primary unit responsible for preventing civilian access to SCP-9310 by any means. Any authorized personnel intending to conduct work, research, or exploration within SCP-9310 must be accompanied by at least one member of MTF Sigma-50 (“Witch Apprentices”) at all times to ensure safety and compliance with current protocols. The operational headquarters of MTF Sigma-50 is located along the western perimeter of SCP-9310, where facilities supporting rapid response and anomalous containment measures are maintained. **Special Notice:** Personnel are strongly advised to avoid entering SCP-9310 on Halloween, as anomalous activity and uncontrolled incidents have been observed to increase significantly on this date. **Description:** SCP-9310 is an anomalous village of thaumaturgical origin located deep within a forested area of Val Poschiavo, Switzerland. According to historical records and testimonies provided by internal entities, SCP-9310 is believed to have been established during the 15th century, coinciding with the escalation of witch hunts across Europe. SCP-9310 is entirely enveloped by a large-scale thaumaturgical concealment field, which functions as both a visual and perceptual obfuscation mechanism, rendering the village undetectable to unaided observation and modern surveillance technologies. As a result, SCP-9310 effectively does not exist to unauthorized individuals. The inhabitants of SCP-9310 are collectively designated SCP-9310-A. SCP-9310-A entities are humanoid in appearance and possess advanced proficiency in the application of thaumatology. However, the thaumaturgical methodologies employed by SCP-9310-A are fundamentally distinct from and incompatible with the systems of [[[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/goc-supplemental-thaumatology | modern thaumaturgical practice documented by the Foundation.]]] All SCP-9310-A entities are classified as Wielder-class entities, demonstrating the ability to channel and manipulate anomalous energies directly through their physical forms. Additionally, SCP-9310 contains six (6) entities designated SCP-9310-B, which function as the ruling council and primary authority within the village. SCP-9310-B entities are classified as Gifted-class entities, exhibiting significantly higher levels of thaumaturgical capability and influence than standard SCP-9310-A instances. SCP-9310-B entities typically manifest as elderly humans; however, multiple instances of voluntary morphological alteration have been documented, allowing these entities to assume significantly younger appearances. The estimated biological ages of entities residing within SCP-9310 range between 550 and 650 years, achieved through sustained thaumaturgical practices intended to prolong lifespan. Despite their anomalous characteristics, the daily lives of SCP-9310-A and SCP-9310-B entities closely resemble those of baseline humans. Entities require regular consumption of food and water, sleep cycles, and physical activity to maintain physiological stability. Notably, SCP-9310 entities possess full awareness that witch hunts no longer occur in the outside world. Nevertheless, they have elected to continue residing within SCP-9310 as a closed and self-governing community. Select SCP-9310-A entities are periodically permitted to exit SCP-9310 for limited durations to procure supplies from nearby civilian settlements. It has been confirmed that SCP-9310 maintains a functioning electrical infrastructure, though the origin and long-term sustainability of its power source remain undetermined. ------ [[=]] ++ Addendum 9310-1: Hunting period [[/=]] ------ [[div class="blockquote"]] [[include component:image-block | name=Wicked_Witch_of_the_East.png | caption=Grand Elder Lilly (4/6).]] Interviewed: SCP-9310-B-04 (“Grand Elder Lilly”) Interviewer: Agent Rigid Location: SCP-9310, Western Perimeter Facility Physical Description: Grand Elder Lilly is a humanoid female entity measuring approximately 1.49 meters in height. Postural deformation is present; estimated height without spinal curvature is approximately 1.60 meters. The entity wears a tall, sharply pointed wizard’s hat and consistently carries a crooked wooden staff. Clothing consists of brightly colored garments, predominantly white with accents of warm colors. Grand Elder Lilly is consistently observed in a state of mild intoxication. A flask is attached to the entity’s waist at all times. Records indicate the flask formerly contained a universal medicinal compound; it is currently used exclusively to store alcoholic beverages. ---- Agent Rigid: Good day, Grand Elder. Thank you for taking the time to meet with me. (Grand Elder Lilly leans on her staff before sitting down, resting it against the table.) Grand Elder Lilly: Oh, my poor bones… they ache so terribly. Agent Rigid: Would you like some assistance? Grand Elder Lilly: No, no. Just the usual troubles of old age, nothing more. (Grand Elder Lilly’s voice is raspy and low. It becomes difficult to hear her clearly when ambient noise increases.) Agent Rigid: Ma’am—your flask stopper seems to be missing. It’s leaking. Grand Elder Lilly: Oh, that’s quite all right. That flask lost its stopper a long time ago. (The entity takes a long drink from the flask.) Agent Rigid: What is that liquid? Grand Elder Lilly: Alcohol. Much better these days than when I was young. I keep it in this medicine flask and carry it with me. Agent Rigid: I see… Grand Elder, may I ask when this village was founded? Grand Elder Lilly: (Frowns) This old mind of mine… let me think… around October 31 , 1450, if I recall correctly. We built this village and concealed it with magic to hide from the authorities. We’ve lived here for a very long time. Agent Rigid: How did you feel at the time? I apologize—this may bring back unpleasant memories. Grand Elder Lilly: Time dulls even the deepest wounds. I regret only that I did not stand and protect those I loved. I fled with the others, ran far away. Back then, all I felt was hatred, deep in my core. But… yes, I was childish. They could never live as long as I would. Agent Rigid: That sounds… terrible. I’m sorry. Grand Elder Lilly: Have I ever told you? In the past, they even used captured witches to hunt other witches. Ah, you won’t find that in your history books. I and the others erased it from history. Agent Rigid: Do you mean torture—forcing witches to confess and betray others? Grand Elder Lilly: No. Far worse. They used some kind of dark art. They removed the witches’ brains and bound each one to a raven. Ravens filled the skies—each bird was one of their eyes. Agent Rigid: So they used witches to control ravens for hunting. That’s horrifying. Grand Elder Lilly: They are only echoes of an old age. We live happily here now. Four thousand three hundred and eighty-one witches live in this village. We survived that dark era. We live on for those who did not. Agent Rigid: I understand. A truly dark period. Grand Elder Lilly: Indeed. Oh, my spine… I believe I must visit the clinic today. Agent Rigid: Would you like me to assist you? Grand Elder Lilly: No, no need. Thank you for your kindness, child. (Grand Elder Lilly mounts her staff and levitates away from the area.) Proficiency is primarily dependent on understanding functional principles and activation conditions. Examples include: > Curse rituals requiring a physical component belonging to the target > Potion creation involving extensive and variable formula sets > Talisman construction requiring animal blood, with effectiveness dependent on species-specific properties [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Advanced Thaumaturgy of SCP-9310-B** Thaumaturgical application by SCP-9310-B entities follows the same foundational framework as SCP-9310-A; however, it is heavily influenced by subjective interpretation and individual perception. For example, while SCP-9310-A entities require specific material components (e.g., blood) to create talismans, SCP-9310-B entities may disregard such requirements entirely, focusing instead on symbolic elements such as engraved patterns. Despite bypassing traditional conditions, SCP-9310-B entities consistently produce talismans of greater potency than those created by SCP-9310-A. In multiple documented cases, SCP-9310-B entities have demonstrated the ability to omit individual steps—or entire ritual procedures—altogether. Manifestation of thaumaturgical effects appears to occur immediately upon conceptual intent, without observable activation conditions. Thaumaturgy employed by SCP-9310-B is therefore assessed as perception-driven and condition-independent, operating according to the entity’s internal logic rather than external constraints. As a result, each SCP-9310-B entity possesses at least one unique, high-yield thaumaturgical ability, characterized by extreme effectiveness but infrequent usage. Some SCP-9310-B entities are believed to possess multiple such abilities, though full documentation remains incomplete. #top-bar .open-menu a {
        position: fixed;
        top: 0.5em;
        left: 0.5em;
        z-index: 5;
        font-family: 'Lucida Sans Unicode','Lucida Grande','Lucida Sans','Times New Roman',Helvetica,Roboto,sans-serif;
        font-size: 30px;
        font-weight: 700;
        width: 30px;

        border: 0.2em solid #888;
        background-color: #fff;
        border-radius: 3em;
        color: #888;
        pointer-events: auto;

@media not all and (max-width: 767px) {
 
    #top-bar .mobile-top-bar {
        display: block;
        pointer-events: none;
    }
 
    #top-bar .mobile-top-bar li {
        display: none;
    }
 
    #main-content {
        max-width: 44.5rem;
        margin: 0 auto;
        padding: 0;
        transition: max-width 0.2s ease-in-out;
    }
 
    #side-bar {
        display: block;
        position: fixed;
        top: 0;
        left: -18rem;
        width: 15.25rem;
        height: 100%;
        margin: 0;
        overflow-x: hidden;
        overflow-y: auto;
        z-index: 10;
        padding: 1em 1em 0 1em;
        background-color: rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
        transition: left 0.4s ease-in-out;
 
        scrollbar-width: thin;
    }
 
    #side-bar:target {
        left: 0;
    }
    #side-bar:focus-within {
        left: 0;
    }
 
    #side-bar:target .close-menu {
        display: block;
        position: fixed;
        width: 100%;
        height: 100%;
        top: 0;
        left: 0;
        margin-left: 17rem;
        opacity: 0;
        z-index: -1;
        visibility: visible;
    }
    #side-bar:not(:target) .close-menu { display: none; }
 
    #top-bar .open-menu a:hover {
        text-decoration: none;
    }

The "Hintze Hall" of SCP-9316.

Special Containment Procedures: Due to the nature of its location, SCP-9316 is partially contained alongside the rest of SCP-1678. A reinforced electric fence has been constructed along the boarders of SCP-9316 to prevent potential tampering. A line of properties across the "Cromwell Road" district have been converted into Area-9316, where SCP-9316 is remotely monitored from.

Following recent events, all exploration into SCP-9316 is forbidden.

The exterior of SCP-9316.

Description: SCP-9316 is an approximation of the London Natural History Museum, located exactly 1km below the original. Whilst originally regarded as part of SCP-1678, recent findings have warranted for it to receive its own item number.

SCP-9316 follows the same general floor plan as its surface-level counterpart. It is a two-story building, comprised of rooms arranged in a vaguely circular formation. The interior of SCP-9316 is noticeably more ornate than that of the real Natural History Museum; monolithic marble structures are used in place of the more traditional stone bricks. The infrastructure is decorated with intricate carvings and silver inlays. Interestingly, matriarchal imagery is common throughout the structure.

Notably, some sections of SCP-9316 are more homely in design, with carpeted floors and open chandeliers in place of the typical gas lamps. Similar to the rest of SCP-1678, lighting within the museum is unreliable; how it is supplied with a stable flow of oxygen and gas is unknown.

The primary difference between SCP-9316 and the real Natural History Museum is the exhibits. Whilst architecturally similar, they vary wildly in subject matter. In place of the traditional scenes of nature, displays within the museum refer to a variety of creatures, plants, figures and events not recognized by the general public.1 The most notable exhibit within the museum is “The Fall of Man”, a collection of displays centring on an ambiguous “apocalypse”.

Addendum 9316.1: Exploration

Recovered ground-floor map of SCP-9316.

SCP-9316 was discovered alongside the rest of SCP-1678 on 8/16/1998. The site was quickly marked as a point of interest, however due to the hostile nature of its surroundings exploration was limited.

The first manned expedition into SCP-9316 was lead by MTF Alpha-5 ("Paranaughts") on 3/3/2006. Initial entry proved difficult due to an unusually high density of SCP-1678-A instances throughout the grounds, with the team only able to enter the building after almost an hour of combat.

Once inside the team performed a basic sweep of the structure, noting several discrepancies between the structure and its surface counterpart; a partial list of which can be read below:

Section # Surface Equivalent Observed Differences
Sect-9316-1 Garden In place of the fossilized tree trunk, a large copper statue of an unknown male stands in the front grounds.
Sect-9316-3 Hintze Hall In place of the famed blue whale, the skeleton of an unidentified, significantly larger aquatic creature is hung from the ceiling.
Sect-9316-4 Central Café There are no kitchens or counters at which to buy food. The space is taken up by a single large canteen, with numerous SCP-1678-D dispensers scattered throughout.
Sect-9316-9 Earth Hall Rather than the randomly-assorted metal plating, the globe features a detailed world map. Whilst similar, the landmasses shown on the globe are not entirely accurate to surface geography.
Sect-9316-14 Darwin Centre Glass cases throughout display the taxidermied remains of a number of unknown species, including previously unknown links between species.
Sect-9316-17 Lower Basement [See Addendum 9316.3]

A total of 24 manned expeditions were made into SCP-9316. Future missions were planned, with the goal of eventually converting the museum into a Foundation site. However, these have all since been aborted.

Addendum 9316.2: Exhibits

Over the many excursions into SCP-9316, researchers have been able to study its various exhibitions in great detail. A list outlining each of the primary exhibits can be read below:

E-9316-1

Taxidermy of an unknown creature, often depicted alongside instances of SCP-1678-A.

AKA: "UnNature"

Description: The purpose of E-9316-1 seems to be showcasing different wildlife found throughout SCP-1678 and possibly beyond. At the entrance there are models of a number of recorded entities, including variants of SCP-1678-A in different uniforms, as well as instances of SCP-1678-B in varying states of decay.

Certain bodily features have been shown to be common amongst different species, regardless of kingdom. These include faded colours, emaciated appearances and lack of facial features; it is as if they had adapted to live off minimal amounts of light or nutrients.

One display, labelled "Cortex Worms: Hidden Killers", is comprised of several glass cases, containing a number of rouge-pink slugs. A series of diagrams depict the slugs entering through a person's ear and burrowing inside their brain. Upon inspection, one of the cases was found to be empty.

At its far end, the hall connects to an aquarium-like area, labelled "It Came from the Channel!". Three of the room's walls were comprised of large interconnected fish tanks, host to a variety of aquatic lifeforms. The largest recorded was a seal-like creature with a notably humanoid body plan. It watched Foundation personnel through the glass for several minutes before swimming deeper into the enclosure and out of sight.

E-9316-2

Recovered daguerreotype. The words "T.T.B. Cira 1850" are written on the back.

AKA: "Natural Oddities"

Description: E-9316-2 is decorated with depictions of nature, with various species of plants (some known, some unknown) set up in displays throughout. The taxidermied body of a large ape-like creature, with shaggy fur and a hairless face, is stood amongst a group of potted bushes near the entrance.

The exhibit showcases a number of ecofacts with supposed connections to mythological creatures. In one area a complete set of jawbones, roughly 55 inches high, are on display; a plaque on the podium below claims them as having belonged to "The Last Feathered Chinese Dragon."

Several exhibits throughout the museum are noted as having been donated by outside benefactors, however little information is given on the identities of these individuals.

E-9316-3

The automaton in its dormant state.

AKA: "Fossil Animalia"

Description: As the name suggests, E-9316-3 is almost entirely made up of various animal fossils, many of which are accompanied by model reconstructions. These reconstructions are far more accurate than what would have been achievable in the Victorian era, possessing a number of features that would not be proposed until years later.

In an adjoining room, there stands a life-sized automaton, resembling antiquated depictions of the tyrannosaurus rex. The mechanism within is almost entirely worn down. The only recorded movement has been in the eyes, which are known to follow any individuals that enter the room. There have also been reports of it emitting low growling sounds. Examination revealed its outer layer to be organic in origin, possessing several genetic markers found at other anomalous sites.

E-9316-4

AKA: "Ancient Wonders"

Description: E-9316-4 features a substantial lack of organic displays, compared to other exhibits. Instead, visitors are presented with a variety of artefacts, accompanied by descriptions and images depicting their relation to nature. In one corner there is an array of simple, yet well crafted tools laid out on a table; a painting on the wall above shows group of hooded figures using said tools to tend to various plants, shaped like human body parts.

Marble bust located near the described display. The words "The Final Face of the Mournful Bride" are carved into the podium below.

In another corner there stands a suit of armour, ornately decorated with patterns of gold and silver. The make does not resemble those of any known culture. Several additional pieces of metal are arranged behind the main body, positioned as if meant to cover two extra appendages sprouting from the wearer's back. An information board beside the case reads the following:

Once worn by the Archangel Ariel during her last stand against the Scarlet Hordes, this armour was crafted with a level of power and complexity unachievable by the hands of mortal men. It is said that the Eviscerator himself was blinded by its radiance as she plunged her flaming pike deep into the heart of one of his devourers. However, the Legion's ruthless might proved too great even for one as magnificent as her, and she too eventually fell to the blade of the dreaded Guardian of the Gates.

- E.P.B

E-9316-5

AKA: "The Fall of Man"

Description: Unlike the other exhibits within SCP-9316, E-9316-5 does not correlate to any existing areas of the museum above. Instead it is located within a large subbasement, accessible only via a staircase near the back of the building.

A tall square platform stands in the middle of the room, with various displays organised around it. Atop the platform is a large marble statue of a humanoid figure. The figure is depicted as being in the foetal position, with their wrists and ankles cuffed and chained to the platform.

On the wall left of the entryway, there is a framed charcoal sketch of a giant humanoid entity, regurgitating black liquid over a village as screaming residents flee. Beside it is an oil painting depicting a pillar of red liquid reaching into the sky, with several human bodies levitating around it.

On the wall to the right of the entrance is a collection of clockwork devices of various sizes. Each of their mechanisms are clogged-up with an unidentified organic substance. Artworks on the wall above depict scenes of colossal war machines, battling emorphous entities of flesh and bone, as well as tall creatures with spiked skin and several sets of eyes.

The far wall is entirely taken up by a single large mural. The mural depicts thousands of people, many with visible injuries, crossing a barren landscape. On the edges of the mural are sins of ruined cities of the silhouettes of large entities looming over them. The crowds all join at the center, surrounding the base of a single tall pillar. An individual stands at the top of the pillar, with their arms outstretched that's the people below reach up towards them.

Addendum 9316.3: Incident-9316-A

On 14/09/2021, as researchers were analysing the structure's foundations for potential expansion, a piece of false panelling was disturbed in the floor of SCP-9316's lower basement. Underneath, there was discovered to be a stairwell, connecting the basement to a series of interconnected chambers appearing to predate SCP-9316. MTF Zeta-9 (“Mole Rats”) were soon gathered to investigate and a copy of their exploration log can be read below:

Exploration Log

Date: 16/09/2021

Foreword: MTF Zeta-9 were employed to explore a series of previously undocumented chambers underneath SCP-9316. They are accompanied by two members of Area-9316's research staff.

Exploration Team:

  • Zeta-9-1 - Captain/Team Lead
  • Zeta-9-2
  • Zeta-9-3
  • Zeta-9-4
  • Dr. Sokov - Resident Parahistorian
  • Junior Researcher Mariner - Dr. Sokov's Assistant

[Begin Log]

(The team descend down the stairwell in a single-file line, with Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 at the front, Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 at the back and Dr. Sokov and Jr. Researcher Mariner in the middle. As they move further from the entrance shaft, they rely on the flashlights mounted to their firearms to navigate.)

Jr. Researcher Mariner: …So how far down is this place, anyway?

Zeta-9-1: Brief said about sixty metres, so it shouldn't be that much further. There, see that?

(The stairwell empties out into a large stone chamber. Six pillars, arranged in two rows of three, reach from the ground to the ceiling, each covered in intricate series of carvings. The chamber is otherwise completely featureless.)

(The MTF members assume standard defensive positions as they scope out the area. Dr. Sokov breaks away from the group to inspect one of the pillars.)

Zeta-9-1: Careful, doctor. I wouldn't advise wandering off until we know for sure this place is empty. How are things looking guys?

Zeta-9-3: All clear on my end.

Zeta-9-2: Clear.

Zeta-9-4: Yep, clear for me too.

Dr. Sokov: My apologies madame captain, it's just that these carvings are… Could I get some more light please?

(Zeta-9-3 aims his flashlight at the pillar, illuminating the carvings.)

Dr. Sokov: Remarkable… James, come look.

(Jr. Researcher Mariner moves to stand beside Dr. Sokov.)

Jr. Researcher Mariner: Wow, it's a whole story! And these symbols are so complex, Daevite?

Dr. Sokov: I don't think so. Here, run your hand along the grooves.

Zeta-9-4: What is that supposed to prove?

Dr. Sokov: You can tell a lot about a people from the state of their carvings, miss. Here, see this? Look at the shallow indent, the course texture around the edges…

Jr. Researcher Mariner: You're right, these weren't done with metal tools. They'd had to have used just regular rocks.

Dr. Sokov: Exactly! These people, whomever they were, carved out these pillars, most likely the entire complex. It would have taken them years, decades maybe, working practically by hand. That's how much they cared, cared about… whatever's down here.

(For the next ten minutes Dr. Sokov and Jr. Researcher Mariner analyse each individual pillar, as the Zeta-9 members take photos. Logs cut for brevity.)

(Eventually the team gather around a rectangular doorway on the far side of the chamber.)

Zeta-9-1: Everyone here? Good, heading in.

(The second chamber is nearly identical to the first, however instead of pillars there is a large cylindrical platform in the centre of the space.)

Zeta-9-2: Looks like some kind of ritual chamber.

Dr. Sokov: It is, and that means there must be… Yes, over there!

(Dr. Sokov gestures to the right. Zeta-9-2 moves his flashlight in the same direction, casting light onto a small square podium. Dr. Sokov, Jr. Researcher Mariner, Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 walk over, as Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 inspect the platform.)

Dr. Sokov: I was right, look at these.

(An array of what appear to be rudimentary tools are laid out across the podium. Dr. Sokov inspects one, before handing it to Zeta-9-2.)

Zeta-9-1: Just a sharpened rock.

Jr. Researcher Mariner: I just don't understand, how could they have done all of this if they didn't even have proper tools? And what does any of this have to do with the museum?

Dr. Sokov: My boy, the first rule of being a historian is that you have to get used to not having all the answers. However in this instance, I think it's safe to say there may be other forces at work.

Zeta-9-3: Captain, take a look at this.

(Zeta-9-1 walks over to where Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 are standing, with the other three following behind. Zeta-9-4 points her flashlight down, illuminating a series of lines, carved along the edge of the platform.)

Zeta-9-1: Thaumaturgy?

Zeta-9-3: Looks like it, but our scanners aren't picking up on any residual energy. Doctor, any thoughts?

Dr. Sokov: It's… interesting. It's the right layout, but far too simple for any branch I know of. Unless…

Zeta-9-4: Unless what?

Dr. Sokov: Well, location can often be just as important as iconography.

Jr. Researcher Mariner: You think being so far underground might have had something to do with it?

Dr. Sokov: That's the working theory at least.

(The team continue to inspect the platform for another 12 minutes, before moving on to the next chamber. The third chamber is similar to the other two, however beyond the entrance are two thin cylindrical posts. The tops of each post are divided into three separate plates.)

Zeta-9-1: Okay, that's interesting.

(Zeta-9-1 reaches out to feel one of the posts. She puts more force onto one of the plates, causing it to rotate.)

Zeta-9-1: Looks like some kind of puzzle, but for what?

Zeta-9-4: Uh, I think it's for that.

(Zeta-9-4 points her flashlight across the room. Like the previous chambers, there is a doorway on the far wall, however it is blocked by two large stone panels.)

Zeta-9-2: Hold on, there's something on here.

(Zeta-9-2 crouches to inspect the plates.)

Zeta-9-2: Little symbols, carved into the sides.

Zeta-9-1: So maybe if we line them all up it'll open?

Zeta-9-2: That's the idea.

(Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 rotate the plates on their respective posts. The doors remain shut.)

Zeta-9-2: Hmm, maybe we're meant to do it at the same time?

(Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 pull the top plates back.)

Zeta-9-1: Alright. Three, two, one…

(Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 slot the plates back into place at the same time. A low grinding noise can be heard as the stone panels slowly begin to pull back.)

(Dr. Sokov begins to approach the opening doors.)

Dr. Sokov: Incredible! This kind of engineering… It challenges everything we know about past technology!

Zeta-9-1: Look doctor, I get your enthusiasm but I think it would be best if you let us scope it out first.

Dr. Sokov: Don't worry captain, I'm simply admiring the craftsmansh-

(As the doors reach their fully opened state, a series of loud clicking noises can be heard emanating from the chamber beyond.)

Zeta-9-1: Don't love that.

(As the noises continue, a long object can be seen coming through the doorway, slowly sliding across the floor. It resembles a large insect leg, approximately 60cm in diameter with black leathery skin and several joints along its length. At the end of the appendage is a large curved point, resembling a claw or a stinger.)

Zeta-9-1: What in the-

(A second identical appendage suddenly comes out of the darkness, slamming on the ground. Vision is briefly obscured by the resultant dust cloud.)

Dr. Sokov: Oh-!

(Dr. Sokov attempts to back away, however the first appendage rapidly moves, impaling him in the chest and lifting him into the air.)

Jr. Researcher Mariner: DOCTOR SOKOV!

(Jr. Researcher Mariner suddenly dashes forward. Before another team member can pull him back, the second appendage springs up and hits him in the side at high speed, knocking him into the air. A lock cracking noise can be heard as he impacts the wall, before collapsing limp on the ground.)

Zeta-9-1: Goddamn it! Open fire!

(All members of Zeta-9 open fire, with minimal effect. The first appendage is drawn back into the chamber, still carrying Dr. Sokov's limp body. Two more emerge in its place, with all three beginning to swipe at the team.)

Zeta-9-4: Our bullets are barely doing anything!

Zeta-9-1: If in doubt, use a flash!

(Zeta-9-1 takes a flash grenade from off her harness and throws it towards the doorway. Upon detonation, high-pitched screeching noises can be heard as the appendages begin to move more erratically, seemingly in distress.)

Zeta-9-1: That did something! Alright, everyone on my mark!

(Zeta-9-1 throws another flash grenade. On detonation, the team once again opens fire. More screeching can be heard, as the appendages quickly retreat back through the doorway. Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 rush to rearrange the plates on the posts, resealing the doorway.)

Zeta-9-3: Alright!

Zeta-9-2: Captain, we're losing this guy!

Zeta-9-1: Ah shit, hang in there kid!

[End Log]

Following extraction, Junior Researcher Mariner was rushed to receive medical attention at Site-44 and is currently in stable condition. Dr. Sokov's body is yet to be recovered.

[[include component:image-block name=outside.jpg|caption=The exterior of SCP-9316.]] **Description:** SCP-9316 is an approximation of the London Natural History Museum, located exactly 1km below the original. [[/div]] **Addendum 9316.3:** Incident-9316-A On 14/09/2021, as researchers were analysing the structure's foundations for potential expansion, a piece of false panelling was disturbed in the floor of SCP-9316's lower basement. Underneath, there was discovered to be a stairwell, connecting the basement to a series of interconnected chambers appearing to predate SCP-9316. MTF Zeta-9 (“Mole Rats”) were soon gathered to investigate and a copy of their exploration log can be read below: [[div class="blockquote"]] **Exploration Log** **Date:** 16/09/2021 **Foreword:** MTF Zeta-9 were employed to explore a series of previously undocumented chambers underneath SCP-9316. They are accompanied by two members of Area-9316's research staff. **Exploration Team:** * Zeta-9-1 - Captain/Team Lead * Zeta-9-2 * Zeta-9-3 * Zeta-9-4 * Dr. Sokov - Resident Parahistorian * Junior Researcher Mariner - Dr. Sokov's Assistant ------ [Begin Log] //(The team descend down the stairwell in a single-file line, with Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 at the front, Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 at the back and Dr. Sokov and Jr. Researcher Mariner in the middle. As they move further from the entrance shaft, they rely on the flashlights mounted to their firearms to navigate.)// **Jr. Researcher Mariner:** ...So how far down is this place, anyway? **Zeta-9-1:** Brief said about sixty metres, so it shouldn't be that much further. There, see that? //(The stairwell empties out into a large stone chamber. Six pillars, arranged in two rows of three, reach from the ground to the ceiling, each covered in intricate series of carvings. The chamber is otherwise completely featureless.)// //(The MTF members assume standard defensive positions as they scope out the area. Dr. Sokov breaks away from the group to inspect one of the pillars.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Careful, doctor. I wouldn't advise wandering off until we know for sure this place is empty. How are things looking guys? **Zeta-9-3:** All clear on my end. **Zeta-9-2:** Clear. **Zeta-9-4:** Yep, clear for me too. **Dr. Sokov:** My apologies madame captain, it's just that these carvings are... Could I get some more light please? //(Zeta-9-3 aims his flashlight at the pillar, illuminating the carvings.)// **Dr. Sokov:** Remarkable... James, come look. //(Jr. Researcher Mariner moves to stand beside Dr. Sokov.)// **Jr. Researcher Mariner:** Wow, it's a whole story! And these symbols are so complex, Daevite? **Dr. Sokov:** I don't think so. Here, run your hand along the grooves. **Zeta-9-4:** What is that supposed to prove? **Dr. Sokov:** You can tell a lot about a people from the state of their carvings, miss. Here, see this? Look at the shallow indent, the course texture around the edges... **Jr. Researcher Mariner:** You're right, these weren't done with metal tools. They'd had to have used just regular rocks. **Dr. Sokov:** Exactly! These people, whomever they were, carved out these pillars, most likely the entire complex. It would have taken them years, decades maybe, working practically by hand. That's how much they cared, cared about... whatever's down here. //(For the next ten minutes Dr. Sokov and Jr. Researcher Mariner analyse each individual pillar, as the Zeta-9 members take photos. Logs cut for brevity.)// //(Eventually the team gather around a rectangular doorway on the far side of the chamber.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Everyone here? Good, heading in. //(The second chamber is nearly identical to the first, however instead of pillars there is a large cylindrical platform in the centre of the space.)// **Zeta-9-2:** Looks like some kind of ritual chamber. **Dr. Sokov:** It is, and that means there must be... Yes, over there! //(Dr. Sokov gestures to the right. Zeta-9-2 moves his flashlight in the same direction, casting light onto a small square podium. Dr. Sokov, Jr. Researcher Mariner, Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 walk over, as Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 inspect the platform.)// **Dr. Sokov:** I was right, look at these. //(An array of what appear to be rudimentary tools are laid out across the podium. Dr. Sokov inspects one, before handing it to Zeta-9-2.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Just a sharpened rock. **Jr. Researcher Mariner:** I just don't understand, how could they have done all of this if they didn't even have proper tools? And what does any of this have to do with the museum? **Dr. Sokov:** My boy, the first rule of being a historian is that you have to get used to not having all the answers. However in this instance, I think it's safe to say there may be other forces at work. **Zeta-9-3:** Captain, take a look at this. (Zeta-9-1 walks over to where Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 are standing, with the other three following behind. Zeta-9-4 points her flashlight down, illuminating a series of lines, carved along the edge of the platform.) **Zeta-9-1:** Thaumaturgy? **Zeta-9-3:** Looks like it, but our scanners aren't picking up on any residual energy. Doctor, any thoughts? **Dr. Sokov:** It's... interesting. It's the right layout, but far too simple for any branch I know of. Unless... **Zeta-9-4:** Unless what? **Dr. Sokov:** Well, location can often be just as important as iconography. **Jr. Researcher Mariner:** You think being so far underground might have had something to do with it? **Dr. Sokov:** That's the working theory at least. //(The team continue to inspect the platform for another 12 minutes, before moving on to the next chamber. The third chamber is similar to the other two, however beyond the entrance are two thin cylindrical posts. The tops of each post are divided into three separate plates.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Okay, that's interesting. //(Zeta-9-1 reaches out to feel one of the posts. She puts more force onto one of the plates, causing it to rotate.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Looks like some kind of puzzle, but for what? **Zeta-9-4:** Uh, I think it's for that. //(Zeta-9-4 points her flashlight across the room. Like the previous chambers, there is a doorway on the far wall, however it is blocked by two large stone panels.)// **Zeta-9-2:** Hold on, there's something on here. //(Zeta-9-2 crouches to inspect the plates.)// **Zeta-9-2:** Little symbols, carved into the sides. **Zeta-9-1:** So maybe if we line them all up it'll open? **Zeta-9-2:** That's the idea. //(Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 rotate the plates on their respective posts. The doors remain shut.)// **Zeta-9-2:** Hmm, maybe we're meant to do it at the same time? //(Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 pull the top plates back.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Alright. Three, two, one... //(Zeta-9-1 and Zeta-9-2 slot the plates back into place at the same time. A low grinding noise can be heard as the stone panels slowly begin to pull back.)// //(Dr. Sokov begins to approach the opening doors.)// **Dr. Sokov:** Incredible! This kind of engineering... It challenges everything we know  about past technology! **Zeta-9-1:** Look doctor, I get your enthusiasm but I think it would be best if you let us scope it out first. **Dr. Sokov:** Don't worry captain, I'm simply admiring the craftsmansh- //(As the doors reach their fully opened state, a series of loud clicking noises can be heard emanating from the chamber beyond.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Don't love that. //(As the noises continue, a long object can be seen coming through the doorway, slowly sliding across the floor. It resembles a large insect leg, approximately 60cm in diameter with black leathery skin and several joints along its length. At the end of the appendage is a large curved point, resembling a claw or a stinger.)// **Zeta-9-1:** What in the- //(A second identical appendage suddenly comes out of the darkness, slamming on the ground. Vision is briefly obscured by the resultant dust cloud.)// **Dr. Sokov:** Oh-! //(Dr. Sokov attempts to back away, however the first appendage rapidly moves, impaling him in the chest and lifting him into the air.)// **Jr. Researcher Mariner:** DOCTOR SOKOV! //(Jr. Researcher Mariner suddenly dashes forward. Before another team member can pull him back, the second appendage springs up and hits him in the side at high speed, knocking him into the air. A lock cracking noise can be heard as he impacts the wall, before collapsing limp on the ground.)// **Zeta-9-1:** Goddamn it! Open fire! //(All members of Zeta-9 open fire, with minimal effect. The first appendage is drawn back into the chamber, still carrying Dr. Sokov's limp body. Two more emerge in its place, with all three beginning to swipe at the team.)// **Zeta-9-4:** Our bullets are barely doing anything! **Zeta-9-1:** If in doubt, use a flash! //(Zeta-9-1 takes a flash grenade from off her harness and throws it towards the doorway. Upon detonation, high-pitched screeching noises can be heard as the appendages begin to move more erratically, seemingly in distress.)// **Zeta-9-1:** That did something! Alright, everyone on my mark! //(Zeta-9-1 throws another flash grenade. On detonation, the team once again opens fire. More screeching can be heard, as the appendages quickly retreat back through the doorway. Zeta-9-3 and Zeta-9-4 rush to rearrange the plates on the posts, resealing the doorway.)// **Zeta-9-3:** Alright! **Zeta-9-2:** Captain, we're losing this guy! **Zeta-9-1:** Ah shit, hang in there kid! [End Log] [[/div]] Following extraction, Junior Researcher Mariner was rushed to receive medical attention at Site-44 and is currently in stable condition. Dr. Sokov's body is yet to be recovered. ACT I

RISE FROM THE DEPTHS



The Villains Of The Story

"We've been here before. We'll always have been here. That makes this okay."

Rainer Kingsley looked up at the portrait of great suffering hanging above his bed. It was a magnificent rendition of a scene of a long dead culture. It depicted what probably would’ve been an enviably common sight in their world: A giant magnificent aristocratic warrior, leading a vicious looking army, all clad in leather and bone and entrails, marching their way through town, looked up at by a crowd of onlookers.

Beneath their heels lies the rape and brutalization of an entire class of people.

Small people. Weak people. Tiny people.

"Do not touch with bare flesh."

Oh, Rainer Kingsley fancied himself a collector, and his bedroom was littered with curios related to his interest in that dead old world. Preserved scrolls, millenias old, were plastered on his walls. A replica of an old warrior's helmet crafted by Erikeshan mystics hung from the ceiling. On his bedside, a glass box holding a rock pulsing red, said to have been touched by a goddess. But his most prized acquisition was the painting.

He must’ve spent ages staring at it everyday, at the rightness of it all. Hours of admiration and contemplation, hours of self-absorbed narcissistic mental masturbation at the sight of it. He savored the details. He loved it.

But today, today is different. He mustn’t take too long. No, no, today is a glorious one. Today, oh, today, he won’t just be watching. He’ll be the great ur-warrior, the great smiter, and his sword is righteous, and his sword is just.

He changed into his best red suit, and out he walked to the sound of uproaring applause from a crowd of people in ceremonial garbs and robes and blood-scars and military uniforms and much more. The great, grand Machine whirring like an engine, dragging this world to one made in his image. All is right in his world.

Endless boardroom meetings, a lifetime of indignities, of being sneered at. All those weekend nights, pretending to laugh at Adrian Green's braindead attempts at comedy just to secure the right contracts and deals. All of it is about to be worth it.

He gets on the stage, and began addressing the crowd.

“My father told me about the Daevites when I was 6,” he says. “I’m sure most of you know them, but… for those who don’t, they were the first civilization… and they were the greatest. They valued traditions… hierarchies. They valued strength. And with these values as the core tenets of their society, they ruled their world with an iron fist for centuries… and it was only when they forwent these values that they did fall. Sound familiar?”

The crowd watched raptly as he paced the room, “My father, he instilled in me the lessons of the Daevites. To never let go of those old ways. And I never forgot. And for generations, men like me, good, decent, old-stock men… we’ve tried to keep the dream, haven’t we? And what have we gotten in return? Hunted. Hunted to near extinction.”

He paused, and looked at the crowd. They were all staring at him now. All of them in the room, only hundreds now, the last of the followers of the Scarlet truth. The last shreds of a dying empire, but not for long. Not for long at all.

“And that’s our shared pain today, isn’t it, friends?” he says, stretching his arms out. “The pain of the hunted! Over the years, the Foundation, the Coalition, the Hand, the Initiative, they’ve butchered us! Murdered us for their New World Order! But they didn’t finish the job! And now, today, their reckoning begins! Their judgement! Cheers, my friends, cheers!”

The crowd cheers as Kingsley bends towards the great machine. It has been whirring since last night, all of his technicians had been working around the clock to get it up, just for this moment, just a few more minutes…

“This day is yours as much as it is mine, my friends! This day is a fruit of all of our labors, years of work, countless billions spent on placing people into the media, the government, the military, all for this moment!” he shouts to the jubilated audience, “Today, we rise from the depths! We overtake their defenses, mutilate their souls! We shall never, ever, show mercy!”

He does not notice his dimensional separators rusting. He does not notice the decay of the engraved runes on the ceiling. He does not notice because he was never told that it would happen.

“Today begins the blessed cleansing! The blessed-” Kingsley almost reaches the crescendo when it finally happens. A deafening roar and quake takes out the lights as the machine activates, as everyone in the room feels the red right hand of god squeezing their hearts. The room is bathed in an unholy red glow.

There is silence, and then applause - hooting and hollering from the red-bathed crowd. The effect was undeniably effective, but Kingsley Rainer can only stand in shocked silence. This was not how this was supposed to go, he thinks to himself, because now he hears the creaking noises, the sound of metal liquefying, shouting from the rooms in the back as his technicians dashes to fix a situation that was never accounted for.

And in the red glow of the room, a special kind of fear grips him as he hears the main door being blown open. And that’s when Foundation agents started flooding the room, and the real mess finally began.

This is not what I was told, he thinks. This is not what I was promised.

Selection

"Death is just an open door."

It’s Tuesday (or Monday, or maybe Wednesday) evening, and Hannah Xob wakes up in her room in her Foundation On-Site apartment. As always, a familiar panic jolts through her body as she realizes she did not set the alarm for today (she never does) followed by a familiar calm as she glances at her wall clock to find that it is only 1:43 PM. There is no way to immediately tell the time - her apartment has no windows.

In her mind, the rest of her day’s routine was already laid out for her. She’d go back to sleep, wake up again in a few hours, order one of the three things she’s always ordered from the Site cafeteria (clam rice, cup hotpot, or fried noodles) and take a 10-minute walk to the main lobby of Site-252. She’d spend 6 hours there mostly doing nothing aside from spending about half an hour writing reports on some dead anomalous plants, then she walks back to her apartment and then goes to sleep again until the next day.

This has been her daily routine for the last 2 years, and it has not deviated considerably in ages. It does not matter if she arrives late, or if she doesn’t hit her quota. Little matters at Site-252 - Building 5 of the Department Of Thanatology. It was one of those posts that were considered just essential enough to require someone for the position, but buried so deeply into the Foundation’s bureaucracy that it can't be said to be of any actual importance.

The building is small. The apartments are shabby. The site - situated in the desert in the middle of nowhere - reeks of death and decay, with fresh bodies and dead plants being brought in everyday, and vatfuls of compost leaving every night. Many say that employment here was a depressing existence. Hannah is fine with that.

And she’s been fine with it everyday, for the last 2 years, tucked away in the little forgotten corners of the Foundation’s ledgers. And she’d be fine with it everyday forward, too, if it wasn’t for the fact that something new seems to have entered her world today.

She didn’t notice at first, but her attention slowly drifted to her phone, which had been gathering dust in the corner for a while (no one calls, and the news only serves to depress her further) but was now emitting little tinny noises. The telltale sign of an urgent Foundation notification.

Surprised but annoyed, she retrieves the phone, and opened up her nearly-empty SCiPnet account. A new message, sent a few hours ago.

[URGENT] MTF NOTICE: You have been PERSONALLY selected for a high-priority Foundation Project, Foundation Agent Hannah Xob. The following is…

She groans. It seems it was another exploration-slash-archeology mission. She didn’t particularly care for that kind of work, and she didn’t care for Foundation missions at all nowadays, period. She’d already configured it so that every mission notice directly went to the trash. The fact that it says she was “personally selected” and that it was an urgent notice was new, though. Was it a new tactic? Was she finally getting in trouble because someone had finally realized that her current position wasn’t much of an actual job?

She read on. Most of the message was the usual Foundation jargon, but the pay… it was a lot of money compared to the usual Foundation job. A lot of money. She scrolled through it again, and a sentence caught her eye.

…selected for your personal involvement in prior projects involving [GoI-586], [Exploration Fieldwork], [Multi-Day Fieldwork],…

Memories started flooding back. Feelings that she never thought she’d feel again, and her heart felt like it was beating faster than it has in ages. The calmness, the monotony, the routine was broken, but it still wasn’t enough yet, her hand was still hovering on the “delete” button. Urgent or not, the Foundation wasn’t going to personally drag her out of her apartment for it, she wasn’t that important, and it wasn’t enough until she scrolled to the very end…

…Ethical Disclosure: High-Risk Mission, Rate Of Fatality Is High. Usual Foundation Insurance Policies applies as covered under Goldbaker-Reinz…

She blinked.

Then, she pressed “Accept.”

I Thought You Died Alone

"It's as comfortable as it looks."

Room D74 of Site-19’s hospital Wing D was a room full of stragglers.

The latest batch of patients arrived here long ago, and most of them have either healed to go back to broken, traumatized lives, or passed, either in pain or in peace.

The Foundation does not send new patients here. The opening of the more well-equipped Wing F took care of most medical needs nowadays, and Wing D was becoming more of a storage facility everyday. Room D74 remains, possibly because everyone who knows about it is just waiting for all the patients to finally die.

At the very end of the room, in the western corner is a man who the Foundation believes will never wake up. He has no brain activity, but due to bureaucratic inertia, or perhaps his former title, the Foundation has allowed him to remain alive.

Opposite him is a man with an almost completely shattered spine, who is believed to be comatose. It is a miracle that he remains alive, and if he was awake, he’d have no use for anything aside from perhaps being able to look around.

The other people in the room aren’t faring better. They too will probably never awaken. The doctors consider this a mercy.

Every week or so, someone arrives to change the filters on the bed’s integrated feeding and waste systems, refill the nutrients and liquids for each patient, and maybe wipe some dust off the ventilators. They don’t stay in the room for long, and never do. The Foundation’s technological superiority compared to the rest of the world had eliminated much of the human-required maintenance for these patients.

For the last year or so, every week, Agent Ulrich, lying in the bed in the corner with only the ability to twitch his eyes, had been trying to signal to any soul who might care that he was conscious. No one’s noticed thus far.

There is no differentiating one day from the next. There is no differentiating one moment to the next, and part of Ulrich wonders why he hasn’t gone insane yet, or if he already has. And all of this torment could just end, if just one person, just one person could just look, look at him one time…

But the moment never comes. He occasionally wonders if anyone else in the room was awake in the same way that he was, and he prayed for it to not be so. But most of all, he prayed for release.

One night, it came. He didn’t register it at first, but there it was again - something emerging from the night, a rustling from the other side of the room. And suddenly, he was acutely aware of the absence of the beeps of one singular heart monitor. Something crashes and falls. Shaky flesh on floor tiles. Then, a gaunt shadow looms over him, one with bloodshot eyes.

He recognized those eyes. He recognized the familiar grey temples, but he never saw him after the injury. The large, deep, jagged scar on the front of his head was a new, unsettling sight.

“Ulrich,” it said, in a gaspy, rattling voice. A throat that hadn’t produced sounds in ages. “Ulrich… are you there?”

And the man asked him questions, familiar phrases and names, and Ulrich wished he could answer, but nothing came out. Eventually, the man realized his situation, and he realized Ulrich’s situation, and for a second, for just a second, he stared into Ulrich’s eyes…

It’s time.

Please, he thought. Please, you know what this means. Please…

And the man did understand, recognizing the patterns as they repeated. Ulrich’s final wishes. The man read, and he shuddered, and leaned back away from view. A brief moment of despair followed by bliss unlike any as a crackling sound is heard, signalling the destruction of several vital components of the infernal system keeping him alive.

Ulrich wished he could’ve told the man how much he appreciated it, that he was glad for this final reunion, but as he drifted off into the depths, he simply wondered why anyone would want to leave its warm embrace in the first place.

Foundation Lieutenant Colonel Lucas Conley walked out of Room D74, legs trembling from years of disuse while hands shook from their most recent use, but there was so much to do, and even though he knew the Site like the backside of his hand, he had to move quick. There was only so much time.

But as he walked towards the exit of Wing D, something compelled him to pause and walk the other way, towards the mail room.

Obviously, he needed to check if he had mail.
