SCP-9321.raw_content:
But let it be known: we are keeping the building. Fair and square.

If you give us ownership of the building, we will gladly keep it away from you.

NOTICE



BY ORDER OF THE ETHICS COMMITTEE

Due to recent circumstances, the following SCP has been neutralized. Unauthorized editing of the following document is forbidden.

9321

Item#: SCP-9321
Level3
Containment Class:
neutralized
Secondary Class:
none
Disruption Class:
{$disruption-class}
Risk Class:
{$risk-class}
link to memo

Special Containment Procedures: Following a vote, SCP-9321 has been terminated. Personnel and Endling Inc. (GOI-8327) are not to interfere with MC&D's constructions. Endling Inc. will receive compensation for any losses incurred following SCP-9321's disassembly.

Description: SCP-9321 is an abandoned Khrushchevka apartment, located in Корлики (Korliki), that displays anomalous properties akin to the physiology and behaviour of plants.

SCP-9321-1 consisted of a series of rusted pipes and wires displayed and interconnected within SCP-9321. These components functioned as SCP-9321's symbiotic mycelium. The pipes stored water and removed waste, while the wires transferred electricity as nutrients. SCP-9321-1 stabilised SCP-9321's trellis.

Tetrapods on Graciosa Island, Azores, which are typically spotted on shore

SCP-9321-2 were a cluster of tetrapods (wave-dissipating concrete blocks) surrounding SCP-9321. The cluster acted as a barrier to wildlife and litter atop it. The cluster also blocked out the sun, keeping the ground underneath moist for the wires, which could be found along the damp ground. It also prevented erosion on the ground surrounding SCP-9321. Observation revealed that the adolescent tetrapods, from birth, can grow to their usual adult size within 10 weeks.

Each structure of SCP-9321 exhibited a symbiotic relationship akin to the Three Sisters1. Birds also inhabited SCP-9321, feeding off bugs and pests infested in SCP-9321-1.

Addendum 9321.01: Discovery

When the nearest town reported unusual and illegal alterations to SCP-9321 to the authorities, MTF Psi-7 (“Home Improvement”) was sent to Russia to set up a perimeter and investigate.

After a few hours, MTF Psi-7 returned with samples from the dried red fluids from the cracked walls. MTF P7-3 reported feeling heat emanating from the centre of SCP-9321. Recordings from MTF Psi-7 picked up continuous moaning-like sounds and birds pecking one member of the team.

Researchers at Site-16 analysed the dried samples and video recordings. They discovered the samples were blood, and DNA analysis revealed the process of photosynthesis in the blood. Six researchers went to Корлики to personally study SCP-9321 after seeing these recordings.

Addendum 9321.02: Meeting

One week after the containment, MC&D's (Marshall2, Carter, & Dark) agent gave one of the perimeter guards a cease and desist letter.

Dear Foundation,

We must inform you that your building is on the land owned by the MC&D organization. The land we picked for development has the perfect environment that our investors wanted. It will be an amazing property: a hotel/museum hybrid that will house all our items for affluent visitors to see and explore, all for $100 guaranteed! As opposed to that useless, ugly building you tried to preserve.

Foundation, before we discuss ethics, let’s talk about ownership. Since the building was part of the land we purchased, it would make sense for us to keep it. We have seen your personnel exploring and setting up perimeters around the apartment. If you give us ownership of the building, we will gladly keep it away from you. We would also renovate the building to prevent it from decaying.

If you want more answers, we can schedule a virtual meeting in two days at 1 PM to discuss what needs to be done. If you don't use Zoom calls, please send us a link to whatever program you use to discuss things. Here is our email address: [REDACTED].

Don't forget.

From,
Bill N. Smith

Interviewed: Bill N. Smith

Interviewer: Dr. Michael Russo

Foreword: The meeting began two days after the Foundation sent a link to the private Foundation-owned video chat IFVC (Instant Foundation Voice-Chat). Dr. Michael Russo represented the Foundation while interviewing Bill N. Smith, a representative and business partner of MC&D.

<Begin Log, [1:20]>

Dr. Russo: Hello? Can you hear me?

Smith: I can hear you loud and clear!

Dr. Russo: Good. Sorry, the internet here can be real rough sometimes.

Smith: No worries, it wouldn't bother us at all.

Dr. Russo: Right. So about the land rights.

Smith: Why yes! About the building you contained?

Dr. Russo: Well, I wanted to understand the ownership of the building.

Smith: Well, Dr. Russo, I just so happened to have created a PowerPoint for this.

Dr. Russo: Okay, go ahead then.

5 pages presented from the powerpoint (note that the actual number of pages is 40)

Smith: Well? What do you think?

(Dr. Russo was seen sleeping during half of the presentation before waking up.)

Dr. Russo: Huh? Oh, I..understand where you're coming from.

Smith: So, Dr. Russo, do you understand?

Dr. Russo: About the building ownership?

Smith: Yes, that.

Dr. Russo: I'm not sure. Can't we just split it by 50/50?

Smith: I beg your pardon?

Dr. Russo: I mean, in terms of-

Smith: I'm not sure you understand this, doctor. I never said anything about 50/50 custody. This is about the full-custody arrangement for the building. We bought this land, we own everything built on it. Sure, maybe you can visit it for research or something. But let it be known: we are keeping the building. Fair and square.

(Pause)

Smith: Don't worry though. We will maintain it by any means necessary. We might renovate and restructure it to keep it pretty for costumers to wander around as much as their hearts desire. So what do you say?

Dr. Russo: We're still not sure about this deal though.

Smith: Just think about it later after this, okay? If not with the request, then lawsuit will be inevitable. I can hardly wait for your agreement. Until then, I think we have enough for today. Thank you so much, Dr. Russo!

Dr. Russo: Thank you, Mr Smith.

<End Log, [3:34]>

Closing Statement: After the interview, Dr Russo requested more interviews with Smith to convince Bill further to offer better solutions from the initial settlement, which were pending.

Addendum 9321.03: Conflicts

One week after the meeting, a letter by an activist group, Endling Inc., was sent via physically to the agent, Marcie Coulson.

Dear Foundation,

This is Amanda Rue, contacting you on behalf of Endling Inc. Our partners informed us of MC&D's development plans, so we're in the nearest town to check what they're up to.

We're here to help you protect the structure from MC&D and maintain its longevity. Here is what it would look like:

  • Setting up camp or living inside the apartment
  • Declutter all the litter from the tetrapods
  • Secure the building with your guards around the perimeter
  • Sabotaging MC&D's equipment and progress

Endling Inc. is serious about protecting beautiful anomalies from those who would exploit or revamp them. For me, where some see cracks and rust from the apartment, I see history that has gone unnoticed. I see the small animals that have taken refuge from the storms. There is beauty that cannot and should not be replaced with cheap gold or artificial luxuries.

We know MC&D will do anything to prevent you from taking what's yours. The lawsuits for this will be detrimental to your finances.

We can discuss this at Quiet Rose Espresso Bar downtown. We'll be there.

From,
Endling Inc.

The same agent was sent to the town to meet with Amanda Rue about Endling Inc.'s role in the operation. The Foundation agreed to let Endling Inc. handle the health and safety of SCP-9321, complete with decluttering the litter present in SCP-9321-2. The Foundation guards were to safeguard against MC&D's attempted damage control, including providing false perception of Endling Inc. to the town.

Amanda Rue even attempted to meet up with Bill N. Smith to discuss Endling Inc.'s perspective, which only ended with a short riot. It ended with both parties successfully separated by Foundation guards.

Addendum 9321.04: Agreements

Three months after the dispute between the Foundation, MC&D, and Endling Inc., the Foundation made multiple treaties with MC&D and Endling Inc. The treaties for MC&D includes providing equipment, some leeway regarding Foundation control, etc.

Endling Inc. were persuaded by the Foundation to sign the treaties to preserve SCP-9321 as a third-party watchdog, though they are not to interfere with MC&D's progress. The Foundation had provided Endling Inc. some equipment needed for routine operations. After some consideration from both parties, the proposal and the treaties were made.

To: The Foundation
From: Bill N. Smith, Marshall, Carter, & Dark.
Subject: Regarding Our Treaties

Dear Foundation,

After much consideration of your proposal, we and our investors have unanimously agreed to take your treaties to heart. We promise to be careful about going around the building as you suggested, though we hesitate about Endling Inc.'s contribution to spying on us. That is so absurd, but hey, a deal is a deal.

However, we're still considering our previous options. It's not like we're planning on something big or anything; I'm just saying.

Also, thank you so much for assisting us with such troubles. We will give you back someday, somehow. So we hope you actually visit the place, in any case. We will be grateful for it.

From,
Smith

Dear Foundation,

We're expressing our concern over this new arrangement. We're still processing it since we're still having difficulty from MC&D, especially from our new proposal. Even then, we still don't trust them. We know how much they'll do anything for a stash of money.

We're still looking forward to seeing the development though. Let's hope this works.

From,
Endling Inc.

Addendum 9321.05: Requests

The Ethics Committee suggested that MC&D decide on the visitation rights to avoid unnecessary conflicts and legal troubles with the schedule and treaties. Personnel are required to make a formal request on printed paper. Agent Marcie Coulson has a required visitation rights to visit and inspect SCP-9321.

Request: Ever since Coulson began to do room inspections of SCP-9321 for further analysis on SCP-9321's health, she noted how the original paints are slowly getting dull and coming off which were painted over with new colors. We decided we will do some inspections around SCP-9321 just in case.

Submitted: Dr. Michael Russo

Status: Denied

Request: We're worried about the state of the birds due to your renovation on the anomaly. Actually, Coulson stated that she saw some pesticide brands coming from the truck. Are you trying to get rid of the pests all the while harming the birds inside? How about we go there to instruct you on a safer alternative to the situation?

Submitted: Amanda Rue

Status: Denied

Request: Today, I arrived at the perimeter only to be told that I was not allowed on your property anymore. When I ask why, you told me that my presence seems to be attracting unwanted attention from the Foundation and Endling Inc. I was in disbelief, I need to inspect SCP-9321 like I have to. Can you please reconsider your option?

Submission: Agent Marcie Coulson

Status: Denied

Request: This is ridiculous! Now you're rounding up the tetrapods, crushing most of them up and use them as gravel for the parking space. You didn't even consult us with such actions. You're just using the anomaly's property to charge up shit! At least let us visit the anomaly, please!

Submission: Amanda Rue

Status: Denied

Request: Please…

Submitted by: Amanda Rue

Status: Denied

Addendum 9321.06: Incident

A year after the initial renovation, the grand opening was revealed. At least five visitors were coming to SCP-9321. It soon collapsed when one of them stepped into SCP-9321's lobby. No injuries or deaths have occurred. MC&D had to refund the visitors for collateral damages and safety violations.

To: The Foundation
From: Bill N. Smith, Marshall, Carter, & Dark.
Subject: Regarding Our Treaties

Dear Foundation,

We're deeply sorry about the destructive aftermath of the SCP. We'll take full responsibility for our action.

We know you tried your best with that treaties. This thing was bound to happened. We know you tried so, so hard with that treaties. We know you did everything, absolutely everything you could. But please don’t blame yourself.

From,
Smith

Addendum 9321.07: Aftermath

Due to the extensive damage to SCP-9321-2, which will cause the whole structure to be damaged further, the Ethics Committee voted on whether SCP-9321 should be neutralised due to the circumstances.

Yes No
Ethics Committee3 4 3

It was decided that SCP-9321 would be neutralised. MTF Psi-7 (“Home Improvement”) and the demolition crew arrived to demolish the remains of SCP-9321, whilst Endling Inc. is in charge of handling euthanising SCP-9321 humanely. MC&D will be starting the new construction next month.

Hello Foundation,

We know it's not your fault. Actually, it would be easy to place the blame on us. At least, we are partially blaming ourselves for letting MC&D damage the building to the point of no return

We can't blame your decision to destroy the remains, humanely at least. We knew it was for the best for the long term, though we're still bitter at the fact that MC&D are able to do the construction as planned.

We're sorry.

From,
Endling Inc.

Footnotes
1. A traditional agricultural technique using maize, climbing beans and squash together.
2. The position was vacant during the time of post.
3. At the time of the vote, the Ethics Committee members were greatly reduced due to [REDACTED]. Only 7 members were active at the time.

SCP-9323.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9323
Object Class: Safe Euclid (see Incident 023)

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9323 is to be contained in a 230m2 containment chamber in Site-33, walls being two (2) feet thick and preferably made of titanium to halt any of SCP-9323's attempts at breaching containment.

SCP-9323 is allowed to spend an allocated amount of time in each week within the Foundation front race track Speed, Control, Power. This race track is to employed with only Foundation agents.

A photograph of SCP-9323 prior to containment.

Description: SCP-9323 is a 5.1 meters long clown car, with style that is indicative of a vintage car, of which is capable of fitting up to 58 adult persons and 77 individual adolescents without coming to a complete stop, though is certainly able to fit more than this limit when immobile. Regardless of how feeble SCP-9323 may appear, it has strength on par with a modern off-road terrain automobile and is capable of breaking through walls of its own volition. SCP-9323 functions like a regular automobile despite its structure. SCP-9323 produces a quiet, idle melody from an unknown source.

SCP-9323 has an immense desire to drive on roads of all variety, this is likely to spread its primary effects. SCP-9323 has a cognitohazardous allure that only affects oneself when in direct contact with the object. This lure makes affected subjects have the insurmountable urge to enter the object. With each subject within SCP-9323, it grows more and more uncomfortable. It is noted that if the amount of persons within SCP-9323 surpasses 30 individuals, SCP-9323 will gradually slow down until reaching a complete stop at 58 persons or 77 adolescents. It is capable of fitting more than this limit.

SCP-9323 exhibits properties that leads Foundation staff into believing that the object has some form of sapience. One (1) member of the research team assigned to SCP-9323, Dr. Charlie; who is effectively fluent in morse code, has taken up the mantle to training SCP-9323 morse code via its headlights.

Addendum:

+ Open Incident 001
+ Close Incident 001

On March 21st, 2013, SCP-9323 was found in a rural area in Canada with at least 62 persons within the vehicle, all of varying age. All persons within SCP-9323 were identified to be from the nearby city of Edmonton and had gone at most 4 days without food and water. Foundation staff only intervened when the amount of persons inside of the vehicle was discovered, which was deemed 'physically impossible' by law enforcement. All individuals involved in the case were amnesticised, and SCP-9323 was brought into Foundation containment with little resistance.

+ Open Incident 023
+ Close Incident 023

On October 28th, 2017, SCP-9323 expressed heightened levels of aggression after not being allowed to drive in a large space for a three (3) day period. Camera footage revealed SCP-9323 repeatedly slamming itself into the concrete walls of its chambers, causing major structural damage as it eventually broke through completely.

SCP-9323 was seen driving through the hallways at a walking pace, purposefully avoiding Foundation staff until it broke through the site's main entrance. MTF squads and on-site security were unable to stop SCP-9323 before it fled the facility. MTF Delta-4 was able to erect a barricade in order to halt SCP-9323 in its tracks and return it to a new holding cell.

Site staff decided to move SCP-9323 to a holding cell with heightened security, with its classification being updated from Safe to Euclid. Its holding cell was to be fitted with titanium walls two (2) feet thick.

+ Open Incident 055
+ Close Incident 055

Following a breakthrough in Dr. Charlie's attempts to teach SCP-9323 morse code, Dr. Charlie initiated an interview with SCP-9323. The following is an exact transcript of this interview.

Dr. Charlie: Hello, SCP-9323.
SCP-9323: Hi.
Dr. Charlie: How are you feeling today?
SCP-9323: Tired. I want to ride, man.
Dr. Charlie: Mhm, unfortunately you know you can't do that.
SCP-9323: It fucking sucks. It feels equally horrible to be stuck here and to have them all inside of me.
Dr. Charlie: SCP-9323, where exactly do you want to go?
SCP-9323: Man, I don't even know. Maybe Brazil, I heard Australia was a neat place.
Dr. Charlie: …from whom did you hear this from?
SCP-9323: Word of mouth, you know. I can hear everyone while they're inside of me, too. Some kid wanted to go to Brazil.
Dr. Charlie: Noted. Do you have any idea where Brazil or Australia are exactly?
SCP-9323: I don't really know what the world looks like. I couldn't really point it to you on a map.
Dr. Charlie attempts to make a joke.
Dr. Charlie: Is it because of the lack of hands and fingers?
SCP-9323: Yeah. Sure.
Dr. Charlie: I have one more question: is this allure you produce purposeful?
SCP-9323: Oh, Gods no. Every time another dude enters me it feels like hell. It feels like hell until they leave and oh God, are they stubborn. Even when I break down they don't bother to walk out, I've got to sort of scramble about before they get flung out of my doors.
Dr. Charlie: I see. I'll talk to you again, later. Thank you for your time SCP-9323.
SCP-9323: Yeah. Thanks, doc.

Further testing of SCP-9323 is authorized.

    SCP-9325 - The New Colossus Is Dead

    popsioak's author page

Designation: SCP-9325

Object Class: Keter

In-flight photo of SCP-9325.

Special Containment Procedures: References to a ghost Fly-Saf Airlines Flight 8400 are to be scrubbed from digital and print media. Aerial reality anchors are currently in use to return SCP-9325 to this reality. Observers of SCP-9325 instances are to be given misinformation and/or amnesticized as appropriate.

Any public evidence of SCP-9325-1 having been in SCP-9325 is to be destroyed. Personnel have been deployed to monitoring SCP-9325-1 for potential development of anomalous characteristics.

Under no circumstance will SCP-9325 be allowed to land.

Description: SCP-9325 is a Boeing 777-300ER, intended to fly as Fly-Saf Airlines Flight 8400, which has been trapped since 12/12/2024 in a spatial anomaly of unknown cause. As a result, once daily at 0800 hours local time, SCP-9325 spontaneously manifests and de-manifests above random portions of American airspace. It is currently unknown how SCP-9325 remains actively airborne; only one untrained passenger is aboard, designated SCP-9325-1.

SCP-9325 typically spontaneously manifests at a cruising speed in the upper atmosphere, fifteen to thirty kilometers from its target airport, before initiating a sharp, uncontrolled nosedive aimed at the center of the largest runway. This has never resulted in contact with the ground, with SCP-9325 de-manifesting seconds before initial impact. Rarely, SCP-9325 may cruise without a nosedive. Observed flight patterns are not consistent with professional piloting; landing gear improperly deploys, SCP-9325 jettisons fuel, and moves wingflaps in erratic patterns.

Previous attempts to impede SCP-9325 through weaponry or physical blockades have proven ineffective, due to intangibility to sources of potential damage. Currently, the only response that has shown any degree of success has been the use of aerial Scranton Reality Anchors that initiate temporary locks to increase tethering to this reality.

Discovery: The exact origin of SCP-9325 is unknown. Fly-Saf Airlines Flight 8400 was stationed at Indira Gandhi International Airport in Delhi, India. At approximately 0600 hours local time, SCP-9325 taxied to the runway and took off while airport employees were performing standard pre-flight checks and refueling procedures.1 At the time of departure, no one had entered the cabin.

Foundation authorities were unable to physically prevent SCP-9325's initial de-manifestation due to a lack of resources in the Indian subcontinent. As a result, Site-93 personnel were tasked with providing a cover story through Indian government contacts. This involved a non-existent rogue pilot, who was forced to return to Delhi by Indian and American armed forces over the Atlantic Ocean.

As a part of this cover story, a replacement Boeing 777-300ER was acquired to stand in for SCP-9325. Pre-flight checks for anomalous markers showed no significant results, and multiple Foundation agents were added to the passenger list to respond in the event of a repeat scenario. The new Flight 8400 took off for San Francisco International Airport with no issues.

SCP-9325-1 was a stowaway in SCP-9325's front wheel-well, identified as Armaan Saini, age 23. SCP-9325-1 had no anomalous abilities of its own that may have explained SCP-9325's existence. Changes in SCP-9325-1's appearance were observed between manifestations. These consisted of injuries acquired from falling or jumping out of SCP-9325, significant amounts of frostbite, and a lack of typical physical needs. Notable are signs of accelerated healing, proof of which is suggested by a notable series of falls from cruising altitude that each resulted in SCP-9325-1's death. SCP-9325-1 was observed alive in subsequent manifestations.

Beginning in 27/1/2016 and prior to its entanglement with SCP-9325, SCP-9325-1 had unsuccessfully applied seven times for asylum to the United States following extrajudicial threats on its life in Punjab, India. Documents seized from U.S. Border Patrol list multiple reasons for being denied entry. These include improperly filed paperwork, language barriers, and utilizing smugglers2 to reach the southern border near Tijuana, framing SCP-9325-1 as a potential criminal. Following multiple attempts at unauthorized border crossings, SCP-9325-1 was deemed permanently inadmissible.

On 12/6/2025, aerial SRAs matched ambient Hume levels to a level consistent with SCP-9325’s manipulation during a manifestation above Los Angeles International Airport. SCP-9325 attempted a nosedive before demanifesting. SRA intervention appeared to successfully decouple solely SCP-9325-1; it was left behind in midair, suffering a twenty foot fall with major injuries. How SCP-9325-1 came to be entangled with SCP-9325 is currently unknown. In spite of personal protest, the former SCP-9325-1 was found to be in violation of good-faith asylum requirements, amnesticized, and deported.

SCP-9325 manifestations then paused for three months. On 13/9/2025, a young male exhibiting phenotypes consistent with individuals originating from the Pakistani-Afghani region was observed inside a re-manifesting SCP-9325’s front wheel-well. It has been designated SCP-9325-2. Efforts to detain SCP-9325-2 continue.

SCP-9330.raw_content:
Intercedent

Author: Intercedent

Author Page

If you liked this, you would like:

FALLOUT: The United States Federal Government and the SCP Foundation go to war.

Item #: SCP-9330

Object Class: Keter

Special Containment Procedures:

Site-███ industrial reservoir, primary drainage channel.

SCP-9330 is currently suspended in Lower Maintenance Subpassage 7X-IVB. A five-hundred meter WHITE zone has been established around the corridor and surrounding passageways. Hallways, ventilation shafts, and pipework connecting to subpassage 7X-IVB have been destroyed and sealed as necessary, with the exception of the Primary Access Route. Portions of Site-███ falling within this zone are considered lost. Retrieval of documentation and personnel missing within the zone at the time of containment is ongoing.

Redundant surveillance systems are to be installed and maintained within subpassage 7X-IVB, monitored on a continuous basis by the attendant containment liaison. Deviations in the structural integrity of subpassage 7X-IVB or in the surveillance system itself are to be reported to the attendant HMCL supervisor. Changes in the flow rate, physical appearance, or composition of SCP-9330 and SCP-9330-1 are to be reported to Site Director Valdez under flag PRIORITY ORPHEON GREEN.

Bimonthly, an authorized maintenance patrol will enter the WHITE zone to conduct necessary mechanical and structural maintenance. Equipment that has come into contact with the interior of the WHITE zone is to be scuttled after exfiltration. All other entry into the WHITE zone is forbidden barring extraordinary authorization per ADMIN-HCV-2029-9330.

HMCL supervisors are encouraged to refer to the appended video file for an overview of conditions inside of the WHITE zone and general hazard mitigation practices.

Loading 9330-MAINPAT47.vid…

The acetylene torch smokes in your hand, spitting hatefully. Sparks sputter and die, drowned by the wet, clawed into splinters by the damp. Your neck itches, throbbing beneath the duct-tape that seals your fume hood flush against your coveralls. Aching breaths hiss fitful and fast through the filter.

It’s always wet here. Always soaking. Rotting plaster and rust. The muck that settles to the bottom of turbid, waist-high tide-locked pools of scum. Oily and soft and sharp with bits of broken stone and shell. The cold, from your balls to your chin, the cold.

At the tips of your fingers when you make the ascent, feeling your gut writhe and boil. Sliding down the back of your neck when you pull off the undersuit in the showers, sticky and slick. Beneath your fingernails, between your toes. It gets in bed with you and wakes you in the morning. Your breath curdles in the morning mist like spoiled milk.

Tomorrow you’ll scrape muddy brown stains in streaking arcs across your dinky steel mirror and wipe your face until it bleeds. You’ve been told it does little for the stench.

The Foundation is to maintain the continued circulation of freshwater in the Danube river basin by any means necessary. In the event of cascading containment failure, the WHITE zone perimeter is to be expanded to ███████, ████████, adjusted for seasonal rainfall.

Foundation-wide recall and destruction of amnestics products has been implemented under FLAG WONDERLAND ZERO. Further action pending.

Description:

SCP-9330 is the corpse of Vladimír Smutný, formerly a practicing amnesthesiologist employed at Site-███. SCP-9330 displays an advanced degree of decomposition consistent with long-term water exposure. Although the nature of SCP-9330 renders precise observation difficult, no measurable progression in its state of decomposition has been observed since 2023-██-██ Samples of SCP-9330 have proven resistant to conventional putrefactive agents and solvents.

SCP-9330 continually extrudes a clear fluid chemically identical to unprocessed █████ from its orifices, extremities, and clothing at a rate of 0.56 L/s, hereafter designated SCP-9330-1. Samples of skin, muscle, cloth, and nylon demonstrate identical anomalous properties; laboratory analysis has evidenced that discrete samples of less than 1.77 * 10^-11 mg in mass continue to produce SCP-9330-1, albeit at a dramatically reduced rate of flow.

Humans contacting or ingesting SCP-9330-1 who subsequently come into significant physical or sensory contact with water have a chance1 of undergoing a ZODIAC EVENT.

A ZODIAC EVENT consists of spontaneous spatial displacement into SCP-9330-2.The mechanism for this displacement is unknown. Attempts to delay or negate this displacement utilizing external mechanisms have proven to be unilaterally unsuccessful.2

SCP-9330-2 is an extradimensional space centered on the Site-███ industrial reservoir. The interior of SCP-9330-2 presents as a large cavern system entirely filled with water. The topology of SCP-9330-2 is variable. To this date, all attempts at comprehensive mapping utilizing navigational data and topographic imagery collected by exploration teams have failed.

While egress from SCP-9330-2 is possible, its total area is unknown and potentially infinite.

Addendum: Compiled SCP-9330 Exploration Task Group After Action Reports

Date: 2030-██-██

ETG personnel manifest: D-349959-9330, attendant research team

Equipment manifest: One (1) standard Hazardous Environment Exclusion suit with attached air supply. One (1) Autonomous Baryometric Probe. One (1) Xyank-Stanford Reality Shunt Harness.

Summary: D-349959-9330 imbibed 1 liter SCP-9330-1 solution at 96% concentration. The subject was subsequently fully immersed in Lake █████. Prior to immersion, D-349959-9330 was fitted with a Xyank-Stanford Reality Shunt, designed to transport the subject back to baseline reality upon either cessation of life functions or 30 minutes of subjective time elapsing. ZODIAC EVENT commenced immediately upon full immersion.

Subject remainfested in baseline reality 10 seconds after conclusion of the ZODIAC EVENT due to postmortem Xyank-Stanford Reality Shunt activation. Autopsy concluded the cause of death was massive deep-tissue trauma due to extreme fluid pressure. Equipment heavily damaged, minimal data salvaged.

ETG-9330-2 AAR

Date: 2030-██-██

ETG personnel manifest: Beta-7 Juliana Valdez, Beta-7 Jayden Rodriguez, Beta-7 Kyle Reese, Beta-7 Victoria Timmons, Beta-7 George Chang, attendant research team

Equipment manifest: Five (5) Deep Ocean Hardened Exploration Chassis. Six (6) Xyank-Stanford Reality Shunt Harness. One (1) Sophont-class autonomous deep-sea navigation vehicle, SCPS Viola.

Summary: The task package consisted of MTF Beta-7 E Company, exploration squad 3, and SCPS Viola. Task force members were tethered to the SCPS Viola, which served as secondary oversight on operation of Xyank-Stanford Reality Shunts as well as general data collection and communications relay. After systems check, the task package fully submerged in Site-███ industrial resevoir. ZODIAC EVENT commenced for all task package members within 4 minutes of full immersion.

Task package remanifested two hours, thirty two minutes, and twenty seconds after the conclusion of the ZODIAC EVENT due to automated Xyank-Stanford Reality Shunt activation.

ETG-9330-2 AAR initial insertion.


Loading 9330-ETG2.vid…

Descend.

Control confirms ready-screen, condition delta green, clear for ignite.

Reactors burn coruscant bubbles into the midnight churn as the spin starts, the almighty cycle, the shuddering thrum that builds and boils and burns in your chest like a laugh. The mask interlock seals over your face. Plastic packets inserted antiseptic beneath your ribcage flow blue with kinetic gel. Hyperoxygenated blood runs cherry-lipstick red.

Dive.

The display floods crystalline. Your face is a wild mass of piping and metal and plastic tubes and your breath is engine fumes scattered across obsidian water. Outside the pressure builds, presses against carbon-fiber and titanium, impossibly heavy. Chambers flush, counterflood. By the time your boots hit the silty ground, you’ve reached equilibrium.

Drown.

The squeeze happens in an instant. The optics flash white, sizzling. Silt gives away to nothing. The gyroscopic compass nestled in your chest ticks in arrhythmic syncopy. Breathe, breathe, soothe your furnace-heart, breathe, breathe as down the rabbit hole you go, spinning like a shot.

Darkness upon darkness returns to the deep.

One two three four five headlamps flash into the abyssal black. Above, Viola shines like an orphan star. Radar sprints into the dim and sonar sings a sad soliloquy, call without response. The gyrocomp spins a gentle lie.

Up, the machine ticks, is behind you. Downwards, lies before.

Egress behind. Ingress below.

One two three four five the lonely lights sink into the night, tethers trailing behind like sundered bowels. One two three four five, ad maiora.

The water, you realize, is not clear. Flakes of milk-white film drift mercurially into the beam of your headlamp, casting shadow on shadow. There’s already a slick layer of slimy deposit forming at the edge of your visor’s exterior wipers. Periodically, Viola’s active sonar thrums through the dim, a bassy tremble that shakes the condensed gunk from top to bottom as it vibrates through your suit and down into your bones.

The depth meter spins in languid circles and the barometer fritzes sublime.

Nothing marks motion except for the steady, gentle sway of the tethers. Nothing marks direction except the gyrocomp’s polite fictions. Nothing marks progress at all. There is only the black, the hiss of static on the ready line, and the gnawing churn in your bowels.

Your body remembers descent. It’s ground into your bones, the turgid pulse of your hyperoxygenated blood, the touch of feathers crawling up from your stomach and into your throat, an interminable itch at the apex of thought.

We come into the world falling, screaming and freezing. Most leave the same way.

You fall for a long time.

Descend.

Dive.

Drown.

You feel it before Viola chimes warning into the corner of your eye, before Timmons barks a static report into the squadnet on all hands, before your headlamps flicker on one by one as a circle of shivering candles.

The cone of your headlamp fuzzes with marine snow, a blizzard of filth. The murky water swirls as one, pale sediment dancing windwards. The dark writhes and pulls.

There is a current. It wasn’t there before.

You stay silent as the squad confers, assenting or dissenting with spare twitches of the suit’s digitigrade controls. The debate is perfunctory, an idiot dance.

There’s really only one way these things ever go.

The gyrocomp spins another gentle lie.

Up, the machine ticks, is against the current. Downwards is the pull.

Egress behind. Ingress below.

Viola, that orphan star, flickers uneasily. Here, the sediment coalesces into thick strata, filaments like galactic clouds drifting quiet through dead space. Your faceplate fogs the color of cobwebs and curdled milk, visibility gone to nil. The wiper squeaks along in steady futility.

In the fish-bowl refraction of your faceplate you see the haggard guise of a familiar corpse.

Egress behind. Ingress below.

When you were a boy you sat on the hot earth beneath the temple at the center of your parent’s hometown. Dark stunted siheyuan clustered in stolid silence with wet timber stacked against their crumbling walls like the corded baskets bending the backs of the petitioners come all around to pray.

The monks called out the sutra with foreheads pressed seamless against the floor and as they rose with dust clinging to leather-wrapped bones you fancied the movement of carrion beetles wriggling beneath skin, through dead chasms and eyeless caverns. Nothing looked back.

Another vaporous fold elapses beneath your drifting boots and then the debris is gone, your faceplate clear.

You crane your head to follow the trail of your tether, up to where it disappears from the cone of your headlamp, up into the overhead plume, into the cloud of filth as it glimmers, glows, and then blazes with pale light.

Viola descends from the murk, ethereal.

The current is stronger here, purposeful. The squad hangs in place, thrusters straining. Nothing on the net except ragged breathing.

At once, all at once, you look down.

The perfect dark stretches glass-flat beneath your boots. It’s like ink splashed into your eyes, so sudden the dissolution, so absolute again the abyss. Your fingers tighten in their gauntlets.

You feel it before Viola chimes into your earpiece, before the sediment pours as a great river of rot downwards, with incredible force, downwards and downwards into the black, rattling your tethers, subsuming Viola, roaring in a great plume down, down, down, you feel it before your turbines short and the descent turns into a fall, you feel it before Timmons barks panic into the squadnet and one by one the tin men are yanked back into the toybox.

You are standing above a hole.

You are standing at the edge of a hole.

Rodriguez is beside you, Viola above.

Reese is dead.

The squeeze came while he was standing half-submerged in the gray water off the dockside ramp, still going through the pre-mission checklist in that anal, droning way of his, calibrating hydraulics and triple-checking reactor readings, all buttoned up but for his helmet and gorget. Red mist in the water, now.

Slime oozes above your knees, the same rancid muck drifting above like invisible nebulae, a spreading undersky the color of running pus. Periodically, great plumes of the stuff spiral down, caught in the same currents that bore your descent, swirling into the pit in a cloud a hundred stories high. Exhalation, inhalation, breathe in time.

And around, all around the edges, the dead come to pray.

You thumb the emergency release. The tether drops away, red light blinking on your HUD. Rodriguez does the same. You move closer, closer, at the very precipice of the drop. Small rivulets of silt continuously erode, flowing into the deepest dark like waterfalls.

There’s really only one way these things ever go.

One after the other, you step off the edge.


You drift downwards, gaze held up to Viola's dimming embers. Your tether trails above, a severed umbilical.

Rodriguez faces you, silhouette haloed. His legs are crossed as he descends. His breathing on the squadnet is steady, even.

You watch him raise his hands to his helmet interlock. You watch him twist.

His headlamp vanishes. The squadnet is silent.

You fall for a long time.

Corpses carpet the bottom of the world so thick their entangled limbs hang over quiet waters like mangrove roots. From their eyes and mouths dissolution seeps, the Karanodaka, the primordial undersea from which all rivers flow.

They, the unnumbered. They, the transcendent. They, the sacrosanct dead.

Hollow yourself, penitent. Digest well. Mouth the sutra from throats long empty. Reach gauntleted hands for the seal at the back of your helmet. Unclasp it.

It is a black worm wriggling primeval beneath the skin of thought. Recalcitrance.

It is a dream of falling. Remittance.

It is a light in the hole at the floor of eternity.

Addendum: Strategic Containment Concerns

Long-term observation demonstrates that the range of actions potentially causative of ZODIAC EVENTS increases over time according to an as-of-yet undefined model of semantic decay. See attachment for aggregate observational timeline.

Timeline

Day 1-30: Full ingress into bodies of natural water.

Day 30-66: Full bodily immersion in water, regardless of origin. Partial ingress into bodies of natural water.

Day 66-155: Partial immersion in water, regardless of origin. Close physical proximity with river currents.

Day 155-██: Partial immersion in water, regardless of origin. Physical proximity with bodies of natural water. Auditory and visual contact with bodies of natural water.

Day ██-███: Partial immersion in water, regardless of origin. Auditory proximity to running water, regardless of origin. Exposure to rainfall.

Day ███-███: Oral consumption of water. Proximity to stagnant water, regardless of origin. Remembering snowfall. Dreaming a dream of spring.

Day ███-████: Unknown. Presumably irrelevant.

Dilution of SCP-9330-1 has proven successful at reducing the probability of ZODIAC EVENTS occurring post-contact, although not the true range of sensory triggers. Based on current estimates, minimum necessary dilution is █ liters SCP-9330-1 per ███████ liters water to reduce ZODIAC EVENT occurrence to tolerable rates3 within the general population.

Strategic containment initiatives are primarily focused on damage mitigation.

Bratislava, Slovakia, 0745 UTC, 2033-██-██.

Aching breaths hiss fitful and fast through the filter. It’s always wet here. Always soaking. Rotting plaster and rust. The muck that settles to the bottom of turbid, waist-high tide-locked pools of scum. Oily and soft and sharp with bits of broken stone and shell. The cold, from your balls to your chin, the cold. At the tips of your fingers when you make the ascent, feeling your gut writhe and boil. Sliding down the back of your neck when you pull off the undersuit in the showers, sticky and slick. Further action pending. **Description:** SCP-9330 is the corpse of Vladimír Smutný, formerly a practicing amnesthesiologist employed at Site-███. SCP-9330 displays an advanced degree of decomposition consistent with long-term water exposure. Although the nature of SCP-9330 renders precise observation difficult, no measurable progression in its state of decomposition has been observed since 2023-██-██ Samples of SCP-9330 have proven resistant to conventional putrefactive agents and solvents. SCP-9330 continually extrudes a clear fluid chemically identical to unprocessed █████ from its orifices, extremities, and clothing at a rate of 0.56 L/s, hereafter designated SCP-9330-1. Samples of skin, muscle, cloth, and nylon demonstrate identical anomalous properties; laboratory analysis has evidenced that discrete samples of less than 1.77 * 10^-11 mg  in mass continue to produce SCP-9330-1, albeit at a dramatically reduced rate of flow. Humans contacting or ingesting SCP-9330-1 who subsequently come into significant physical or sensory contact with water have a chance [[footnote]] Observational range of 0.001% to ██% depending on severity of initial contact and dilution of SCP-9330-1 sample.[[/footnote]] of undergoing a ZODIAC EVENT. A ZODIAC EVENT consists of spontaneous spatial displacement into SCP-9330-2.The mechanism for this displacement is unknown. Attempts to delay or negate this displacement utilizing external mechanisms have proven to be unilaterally unsuccessful. Item#: 9331
Level1
Containment Class:
safe
Secondary Class:
none
Disruption Class:
dark
Risk Class:
notice
link to memo

Special Containment Procedures: No nonanomalous copy of SCP-9331 is to circulate or be available to the public. Maynard.aic is to track and prevent all attempts of piracy and/or debugging involving SCP-9331. Online rumors regarding SCP-9331's features have been deemed a negligible loss.

Description: SCP-9331 is a single-player 64-bit roleplaying videogame titled “I Believe in the End of the Tunnel”, solely developed by Hannah Ullman under the online pseudonym “punkrockqueen”. SCP-9331 is currently downloadable on online independent videogame hosting platform itch.io for free, although it was priced at 2 USD up until October 2014; attempts to remove SCP-9331 from the store have resulted in devices overheating and crashing, invariably. When downloaded regularly, SCP-9331 will showcase a consistent series of bugs, all of which possess no discernible cause upon inspecting its source code. Pirated copies of SCP-9331, despite being identical in programming, will function normally and won’t experience any bug during playtime.

SCP-9331 displays a turns-based combat system, a medieval-inspired aesthetic and follows a roughly linear structure composed of minute town environments and dungeon sections. The story follows a presumably female character whose name is chosen by the player, questing to retrieve an unknown object hidden within the underground castle section composing SCP-9331's final stage. Other characters are under the player's control and will aid SCP-9331's protagonist through enemy encounters as well as dialogues of encouraging nature. After one last dialogue heavy portion, the player is supposed to fight SCP-9331's final boss to unlock the ending. Upon completion, SCP-9331 is programmed to restart from its beginning whereas the player's character's sprite is modified to display more feminine features. These last events are unobtainable in an anomalous copy of SCP-9331.

The bugs affecting SCP-9331 will manifest as follows:

SCP-9331's starting menu.

  • The soundtrack playing at the starting menu won’t loop upon ending.
  • Despite the presence of a “Save” button within the pause menu, this is not functioning, preventing players from saving progress and completing SCP-9331 in more than one sitting.
  • Character name select is locked upon “Hannah”.
  • The in-game day and night cycle is deactivated.
  • A number of indoor environments the player will have access to appear as identical copies of SCP-9331's starting area, the protagonist's house.
  • Numerous nonplayer characters’ sprites won’t appear on screen, although they can still be interacted with.
  • Although limited, various nonplayer character’s dialogue options are unresponsive. This leads the aforementioned characters to repeat their first-encounter dialogue throughout SCP-9331.
  • Party members will not accept healing items in any point of gameplay.
  • Enemies often have their sprites replaced with other sprites present in the game, including the player’s character’s.
  • Blood sprites will generate thrice as many times as they’re supposedly programmed to appear.
  • Combat sequences lack any soundtrack.
  • The last stage’s background is glitched out, appearing as static.
  • Party members won’t respond to any input during the last stage.
  • No dialogue will appear on screen during the “Self Acceptance” scene preceding the final boss fight.
  • All text from the final boss’s dialogue is replaced with the astrological symbols for Mars and Venus.
  • SCP-9331 will crash upon defeating the final boss, only to reboot shortly after. After rebooting, the starting menu will lack any and all text or user interface option. Only the background image, a view of sunlight coming from the end of a cave, will appear, only to fade to black. This event will repeat at each attempt to restart SCP-9331.

Analyzing online discussion surrounding SCP-9331, it is estimated it first displayed anomalous behavior somewhat around early 2014. Patch notes spread through the source code indicate constant updates of SCP-9331 were planned by its programmer but were never applied after launch.

Discovery: SCP-9331 first came to Foundation attention on 12/07/2016, when Researcher Ruggiero of Site-77 privately downloaded the executable to later encounter the bugs described above. When inspecting SCP-9331’s source she failed to locate any coding errors, prompting her to research forums and discover SCP-9331’s oddities to have been relatively well known to the public since 2014. Official investigation into SCP-9331 properties was initially dismissed until Researcher Ruggiero damaged a Foundation issue office computer in an unauthorized attempt to remove SCP-9331 from its digital platform. Site-15 was officially tasked with researching the anomaly and enforce preemptive information control.

Addendum-9331-1: Interview with Hannah Ullman.

Online research allowed assigned personnel to track down Hannah Ullman in her apartment in Montréal, Québec. Researcher Kazumi Oshima first approached her through email under the guise of an interviewer for videogame journalism outlet Polygon. Later, on July the 2nd, Researcher Kazumi was able to schedule a meeting with Ms. Ullman in her habitation.

Interview begins

The two are seated on the opposing ends of a round wooden table. Ullman rests her hands on her lap, whereas Kazumi is gripping his graphite pen and notebook.

Rs. Kazumi: I don't really have a say in how much of this interview will actually make it on the page. We'll be lucky if the article gets published in the first place.

Ullman: Got it.

Rs. Kazumi: Just so you don't keep on refreshing our website looking for this interview. I think I explained that a little bit in the email already.

Ullman: T'was crystal clear.

Rs. Kazumi: (Clears his voice.) If I'm here in the first place it's because we value your perspective on this. You began your career in programming from an early age through independent development and now you're a programmer for a big software house. How do you look back on your earliest pieces? Frogrock, CaterPrimia and Bone Digger to name a few. Not excluding your most ambitious project, I Believe in the End of the Tunnel.

Ullman: (Chuckles.) That piece of garbage?

Researcher Kazumi reports being startled.

Ullman: Did that come out too harsh? I'm sorry, so deep in French I'm losing my English language filter. I look back at those works with fondness, minus Tunnel. I've grown to find it embarrassing.

Rs. Kazumi: Why so?

Ullman: It just screams amateur through each pixel. To be frank, all of my early portfolio does and I'd never be so judgmental to programmers who are just starting out. But Tunnel, I feel like it deserves to be held to a different standard, it was my most ambitious game after all.

Rs. Kazumi: Are there any aspects you'd like to pick out?

Ullman: Uhm, sure. Starting from most obvious, the music. I sucked and still suck at composing, good thing my husband's a musician. (Pause.) Am I getting off track? Ok, semi-catchy 16-bit music was the best I could achieve, still I pushed myself to make a whole soundtrack just to put my name on it. Quite literally.

Rs. Kazumi: By this you mean?

Ullman: You've seen the credits, right? Beyond the guy who shot the CC photo for the menu it's all just me, all over the place. I had just picked up Hannah and really wanted to parade it around.

Rs. Kazumi: Any more nitpicks?

Ullman: I'd be here all day. Plot was generic. Dialogue was corny. The protagonist was visibly drawn in my image but it doesn't stop at that, everyone, from partymates to enemies was a real person's sona. That's something a professional could never pull. On top of this, as much as I was a hardcore player myself, I didn't have a strong sense of what made a game challenging at the time, so all encounters played out the same and final boss was a damage sponge.

Rs. Kazumi That's quite the list.

Ullman: Guess I was multitasking everything but quality control.

Both laugh.

Ullman: Ok, jokes aside. There is one issue I noticed from early on. No replay factor.

Rs. Kazumi: That is something I experienced myself. The player's character's sprite acquires major visual upgrades in new game +, but there are no other meaningful changes. Was this unfinished game content?

Ullman: Kinda. When I made the game I wasn't really going outside that often, it definitly gave me a huge boost in productivity but I discovered I had a breaking point too. Most of the game was finished and I decided to leave that in, a snippet of sort. I was confident I'd get to add more content in the future. That never came to happen.

Rs. Kazumi: I figure you'd be more willing to discuss other aspects of your career rather than this one. Can we clutch a few more questions before moving on to better subjects?

Ullman: Sure. Hit me up.

Rs. Kazumi: Given your previous experience solely consisted of platformers and gimmick games. What has pushed you to take on such a task?

Ullman is visibly uncomfortable.

Ullman: I wasn't going out much, I've told you already.

Rs. Kazumi: I'm sorry, I didn't mean to—

Ullman: It's ok. If you want an answer that might look good in an article, I'll say this.

Ullman is now visibly more relaxed.

Ullman: I was always an RPG nerd, and when I thought, stress on thought, I was experienced enough to make my own, I carried through it with this "kid me would've loved this" mindset. What's ironic is that kid me would have never asked for money but I put so much effort in the thing that compensation felt earned. Overall, it might've been what motivated me to do the jump to professional game development. There's a solid chance I wouldn't be here right now without it. So that's something adult me loves about it, I guess.

Rs. Kazumi: Didn't think I'd hear you say that. Not after all the complaints.

Ullman: That makes two of us.

Rs. Kazumi: To wrap things up before moving on. How do you relate to I Believe in the End of the Tunnel's internet fame?

Ullman: It's famous?

Rs. Kazumi: Mostly for being a bugged mess.

Ullman: (Suppresses a giggle.) Should've seen that coming.

Rs. Kazumi: So you never look back at the game. Never tried to add new features or the like?

Ullman: I returned a few years ago, actually. Switched it to free download. I've seen quite a bunch of angry reviews on the way but nothing concerning bugs.

Rs. Kazumi: That was a question I decided to gloss over. But now that we're at it, could you explain this choice?

Ullman: I'd maybe say it's because I didn't need the money anymore. I considered deleting it altogether, but I thought that maybe there's someone out there who'll enjoy it even if I don't anymore.

Rs. Kazumi: All this talk of sentimentalism and you still resent the game?

Ullman: Resent is a strong word, it's not that. It's something else… How can I phrase it?

Ullman starts looking around in her chair. She grabs an object on a shelf behind her and places it in front of Researcher Kazumi.

Rs. Kazumi: It's a toddler's chewing toy, a very worn out one at that.

Ullman: It's my son's. You used one of these?

Rs. Kazumi: I don't have children.

Ullman: What I meant is, you used one yourself at some point in life?

Rs. Kazumi: Of course I did.

Ullman: Why aren't you sporting it like a medal then?

Rs. Kazumi: 'Cause it's a toy, I don't need it anymore.

Ullman: Didn't it help you grow teeth? Why are you so ungrateful to your old toy?

Rs. Kazumi: No. Like, I take care of my teeth regularly. Isn't that enough gratitude already? Just because it played a huge role, it's not like I have to remind myself what I've went through every day.

Ullman: Those are the words I was looking for.

Rs. Kazumi: Huh. Before moving on to the next topic. What do you think is the ultimate reason you never returned to update I Believe in the End of the Tunnel?

Ullman: I think the answer to that is right in the title.

The remainder of the interview has been cut.

Following this interview, researchers discovered SCP-9331's anomalous properties to have severely diminished. Currently, all bugs not relating to the end of game reboot no longer manifest, rendering SCP-9331 near indistinguishable from nonanomalous copies. The sole remaining bug has experienced a slight variation: upon reloading after reboot, the menu screen won't fade to black, getting increasingly brighter instead.

SCP-9333.raw_content:
█████████ Castle ruins, one place of SCP-9333 manifestation held in Foundation safekeeping.

Item #: SCP-9333

Object Class: Keter

Special Containment Procedures: The privately owned “Society for the Preservation of Castles” Foundation front has been established to ensure guardianship of locations associated with SCP-9333 manifestation. A dedicated fund has been allocated to the SCP-9333 project for tasks such as grounds upkeep and misinformation campaigns. As of currently, the Foundation has been entrusted with information pertaining to two sites confirmed to be consistently used for the ritual. The current agreement with local anomalous communities is that access will be granted to further locations depending on the success of current responsibilities.

Foundation personnel assigned to SCP-9333 are to maintain close communication with regional associates of the Serpent’s Hand Group of Interest. During leap years, a roster of past and present flitch claimant couples, as well as the outcome of their trials, is to be maintained and updated on a monthly basis. Any further documentation or update of such regarding SCP-9333, including this file, must be reviewed and approved by Serpent’s Hand associates before it may be added to official records of the anomaly.

Description: SCP-9333 is an anomalous variant of the “flitch of bacon custom”, which originated in 13th century Little Dunmow, a village in rural Essex, England. The non-anomalous tradition, practiced in Britain and once in the United States of America, involves a wedded couple convincing a ceremonial jury that they have not regretted their marriage for a year; successful claimants swear a specific “flitch oath” and are awarded a flitch of bacon (hence the name “flitch trials”). Modern variants involve more public spectacle, including a procession, traditional outfits, and successful petitioners being carried on a chair around the village.

The ritual to invoke SCP-9333 differs from the Dunmow custom in the following ways:

  • Rather than taking place in a human settlement, SCP-9333 only manifests in forested areas in close proximity to castles or castle-like structures that have stood1 for at least seven centuries.
  • SCP-9333 trials can be invoked at any time during a leap year, so long as both partners in the couple and three non-jury witnesses are present in a location suitable for the ritual.
  • The jury that judges claimants is composed of seven members, all of whom are members of high standing in the local anomalous community.
  • SCP-9333 is begun with both wedded members swearing a portion2 of the traditional flitch oath, rather than concluding the event with the oath.
  • Successful claimants do not receive a portion of bacon, but rather a large slab of wood upon which assorted high-value edible fungi3 are actively growing.

Addendum SCP-9333-1: Following Foundation intervention to preserve historical sites where SCP-9333 instances have previously been held, Serpent’s Hand ambassadors permitted researchers assigned to SCP-9333 to conduct an informal interview involving three interviewees from the anomalous community. This quick session was held in the interest of helping SCP-9333 custodians to better understand the background of the custom.

All interviewees were confirmed to have undergone the SCP-9333 trial at least once, and all had only agreed to provide testimony if their responses were transcribed from memory at the conclusion of the interview, not recorded live in any manner. Due to this condition, a different interviewer was assigned to ask each question in the interview, and all interviewee responses have been recorded by hand from the respective interviewer’s recollection.

Interviewer 1: Have you ever successfully claimed a flitch from the trial?

Respondent SCP-9333-A: Three times as we were growing, then we stopped the going. Let the younger generations have a turn at celebrations.
Respondent SCP-9333-B: No.
Respondent SCP-9333-C: Just the one. We’ve been hoping to go again. Now that you’ve become involved, we might be able to make that happen, eh?

Interviewer 2: Are you still married to the partner you stood with for the first flitch trial?

Respondent SCP-9333-A: Married yes, happy yes, at least most days that is my guess.
Respondent SCP-9333-B: No.
Respondent SCP-9333-C: [laughs] Thankfully, I am!

Interviewer 3: Do you think you learned anything from undergoing the trial?

Respondent SCP-9333-A: A juror told us something nice, soon as we had gone there thrice. We were prepared for lifetime shared, they made it true with numbers paired. Mortal born, spirit begot, the differences now matter not. Our years and days now perfect matched, until the day death is dispatched.
Respondent SCP-9333-B: Clean the clutter, abundance will flow in. I need a partner who respects my space, if any partner at all.
Respondent SCP-9333-C: My extended family used to call it “rich witch flitch trials”. Ha! Turns out most of the participants these days aren’t witches at all, or even rich! Still a lot of powerfully talented mums and nans out there, though. Can’t tell you how relieved my wife was to get the flitch. Some couples immediately call it quits if the jury turns ’em down, see? And the more failures, the more the whispers that love is fading, the magic’s fading.

Interviewer 4: Do you think the flitch trials should be preserved?

Respondent SCP-9333-A: Like to keep it as is, but not a thing I’d miss. Convincing me depends on whether we someday get something better.
Respondent SCP-9333-B: Is it our duty to prove to other people we are capable of a year’s love? Used to be a high courts only practice. Still hard for commonfolk to sit a flitch jury. There’s more meaningful ways to honor a bond.
Respondent SCP-9333-C: Why shouldn’t we try to keep alive a tradition that rejoices in a love that lasts?

Interviewer 5: Why did you and your partner decide to participate in the trials?

Respondent SCP-9333-A: For the feelings, for the fun, just to say that it was done. Sometimes the timing’s right, sometimes the timing’s shite. Love is, love was, love does.
Respondent SCP-9333-B: It’s what Mother wanted.
Respondent SCP-9333-C: Why not give it a go? Not just for those getting the flitch, but those giving as well. The world’s changed much and it’s more and more a question of will you love at all, rather than will you lose your love. Flitches are still handed out, even if it’s just at one tree, the one castle. Someone somewhere out there, thousands of years in, still waits and lives in hope they may be on the jury more time and hear just one more love story.

Addendum SCP-9333-2: While the SCP-9333 trial has traditionally been undertaken by individuals of high standing, significant wealth, and/or notable accomplishment in the anomalous community, more recent accounts indicate a growing number of couples successfully claiming the fungal flitch despite one or both partners having no familial relation to such persons. As such, in the interest of preserving the SCP-9333 ritual, the Foundation has petitioned the Serpent’s Hand for consideration of allowing research employees to participate in the flitch trials.

Permission was eventually granted for three Foundation-designated couples and their witnesses to participate at known SCP-9333 protected sites per trial year. However, it was brought to attention that of the partners and witnesses selected, the majority of the personnel present were unable to physically see4 the jurors judging them. In these cases, even when a flitch was awarded, the monetary value of the fungus granted was noted to be significantly less5 than those given to couples who were able to perceive all members of the SCP-9333 jury.

The SCP-9333 research team will continue to revise the questionnaires for determining trial eligibility, in the interest of maintaining the invitation to send attendees to SCP-9333 invocations.

Addendum SCP-9333-3: It has not yet been officially determined whether the fungus flitch granted to successful couples should be fully allocated to the claimants, or surrendered to the research team for analysis. Up to this point, the SCP-9333 team has been handling the matter on a case-by-case basis.

Footnotes
1. It is believed that castle ruins will still suffice for this condition. Communication from the Serpent’s Hand indicates that “so long as there’s a jury willing, and somewhere for the jury to sit”, the trial can be initiated, including in countries that are outside the European and North American continents.
2. “In a twelve month and a day / Repented not in thought in any way.”
3. Primarily truffles, in addition to mushrooms such as matsutake and morels. As it is highly unusual for such species to grow together, it is believed the flitch of wood is anomalous.
4. Serpent’s Hand associates note that this is not the first time such an occurrence happened, given that even prominent magic practitioners have married outside of the anomalous community before. However, this is the first time such an instance was related to an increase in trial participation, not a decrease.
5. In rare cases, a lower-quality flitch provided through SCP-9333 included the fungus growing on clearly defined halves of the wooden slab, rather than a continuous mass more difficult to portion out between two separate individuals.

    SCP-9339: Shrewtamer
    Author: whenwerewe
    Here's my page!

The tongue of a post-recovery penitent. Note the nodular formations and thickened tissue.

Item #: SCP-9339

Object Class: Keter

Special Containment Procedures: The sanctity of marriage is to be reinforced at regular intervals through the use of broad-spectrum media saturation campaigns. Particular attention is to be paid to messaging towards youth demographics, which are disproportionately disciplined by SCP-9339. Images of SCP-9339 penitents are to be displayed prominently on regular programming, with a particular focus on the surgical complications arising during recovery.

SCP-9339 penitents of class BETH penitents are to be appropriately surgically separated and chastised thereafter.

Description: SCP-9339 are the consequences of a declaration made by the Bishop of Rome, Vicar of Jesus Christ, Successor of the Prince of Apostles, Supreme Pontiff of the One Most Holy Apostolic and Catholic Church, Innocent XI, as concerns the novel practice of “going steady”, i.e. engaging in romantic relations outside of marriage (or indeed even as its intended predecessor). This practice had been growing in popularity among new adults in the West, especially those in the Union State of America, since around 1995.

Innocent’s condemnation of the practice at the Fifth Council of the Vatican was followed by the appearance of a halo of celestial light around him, one of only five confirmed miracles in the twenty-first century. Further consultation with the archangel Gabriel at Sinai confirmed that this condemnation had been made ex cathedra, and should be understood as a true expression of heavenly will.

Afterwards, it was found that the act of kissing between unmarried individuals would result, in about 0.5% of cases, in the permanent bonding of the involved organs. The epidermis of the two involved individuals will shift to allow the underlying muscle to fuse, and capillaries will often knit so that blood is carried between the penitents. Although this occasionally affects more innocent acts, it has been extremely effective in curbing the practice of unmarried concupiscence, and so the condemnation has remained in force despite the protests of various Marian groups in favour of expressions of maternal love.

SCP-9339 involving only the mucosal tissues are often trivial to rectify, with a simple surgical procedure separating the involved penitents. It has become customary to seek pilgrimage to Rome in order to purge one’s sin after such humiliation, but Foundation interference in these cases is not necessary. These are referred to as ALEPH cases.

However, of particular note are SCP-9339 cases that involve the tongues of the penitents, known as BETH cases. Within the first hour, fusion typically extends deeper than the mucosa, as lingual muscle fibres interweave. Small blood vessels cross the interface early, and one penitent attempting to speak or swallow will trigger mirrored motion in the other, due to engagement of the nervous system. Ultimately, the tongues behave as a single, thickened organ. At this point, the only treatment possible is for surgeons to gain access to the female penitent’s lingual roots through a controlled mandibular opening. Surgeons isolate the root, clamp the aberrant vessels feeding in from the other penitent, and incise the deadened tissue.

Typically, enough tissue is left to the male penitent that further surgery can restore oral function and eventually even speech. After surgery, female penitents are often considered prized brides.

SCP-9341.raw_content:
You walk a split path: Gate-A, the facility intact, D-9341 contained. Gate-B, nothing remains. All has been buried in a labyrinth of clearance, be it the Containment Breach, or Project Spiral Gestalt.

by Ethagon

Surroundings of Site-CB

Special Containment Procedures: The Clearance System of SCP-9341 and its associated files are not to be modified without O5 approval.

In order to prevent cross-contamination, utilisation of Gates A and B to enter the facility is to be mutually exclusive for all personnel.

A small outpost has been established to process documents regularly released from Gate A. Processing consists of filing documents for potential future utilisation.

Entering Gate-B requires a radiation-resistant hazmat suit.

More specific Containment Procedures are available to relevant personnel.

Description: SCP-9341 is Site-CB,1 a facility subordinate to Site-19. Site-CB was originally a research facility, but had to take up containment duties past its expected limits as a response to the Fracturing Raids. After an incident further elaborated in this file's sub-documentation, it turned into SCP-9341.

SCP-9341 is causally inconsistent. The state of the facility is dependent on both specific "trigger" actions by personnel and on an as of yet poorly understood process. The primary trigger for the anomaly is interaction with the gate entryways to the facility. Site-CB will remain intact when entering from Gate-A and appears destroyed when entering from Gate-B.

For all intents and purposes, SCP-9341 serves as two separate but interconnected locations. Each has been assigned a distinct purpose, per O5 instructions.

SCP-9341-A is Benjamin Oliver Walker, formerly designated as D-9341. SCP-9341-A is a focal point of SCP-9341's anomaly.

Further information related to entering SCP-9341 through its respective gates has been archived on site or is available at Clearance 5/General request.

» Gate-A «

Archival of documents about the investigation of the incident that required reclassification as SCP-9341.

» Gate-B «

Archival of documents about the aftermath of the incident and SCP-9341's future.

Footnotes
1. Temporary designation. Original designation lost.

SCP-9342.raw_content:
Item: 9342

Containment Protocols (Updated 15/07/2007): Item 9342 must be completely and irreversibly sealed.

The chains affixed to Item 9342 must be constantly monitored and replaced if failure is imminent. At no time can there be less than 49 chains attached to the Item for any reason.

The sigils throughout Item 9342/A must be routinely checked, maintained, and repaired as necessary. Proposed additions must be reviewed and approved by at least three Level 4 or above Department of Thaumaturgy personnel.

Description: Item 9342 is an ironstone slab obstructing a 90cm by 200cm doorway in the central chamber of Item 9342/A, a semi-artificial subterranean network south-west of Stuttgart, Germany.

Item 9342 is engraved with the word ‘RETRACTARE’1 and was formerly connected to the wall opposite it by seven chains comprised of an anomalous alloy; three were broken on discovery and the remaining four were visibly failing, indicating Item 9342 was being pulled outward by a constant, steady force. All chains were replaced with non-anomalous approximations.

The surfaces throughout Item 9342/A are engraved with dormant thaumaturgic sigils; if activated, the sigils are predicted to pull Item 9342 shut with a force of approximately 1072 Joules.2

Attempts to non-invasively image the area behind Item 9342 fail to receive any data passing through a plane 20cm behind the front surface, or otherwise depict the Item as coterminous with the surrounding stone. There is insufficient clearance to insert probes between the Item and doorframe without damaging either.

Addendum 1: Item 9342 was discovered during investigations into a Young Codex Text passage, partially reconstructed from the following:

There are two great sources called Abenet and Muasada; their water is endless, but bitter and harsh. When mixed they are sweet, and give might to all that drinks; where the sources mix they become the river Unuthoth. Ages ago the water of Unuthoth flowed endlessly into […]

— Damaged phonograph recording of an Unendamubi oral legend (1916).

BANQUO
A potter’s jar with bitter water seal’d,
and tale’d wandering through lands of old.
A ruse; a fount of Erthot concealed
by king, but found and water drawn unmixed.
So bitter taste ‘til other found to add
and temper both.

ANTONIO
And pray he thinks not ask for both?

BANQUO
The one you have, but he with wellspring jar
spoke not of where it was nor offered it.
To seek is foolish; for guard bizarre
bids none to find the fount unless the taste
of waters mixed they know before the act.

— The Tradgedie of Antonio, Psuedo-Shakespeare (1704), Act III Scene 6.

[…] stopping was not yet fast; and as Evö went it came undone, and the waters of Urthothr spilled once again.

There the land bowed, lest the sweet waters spill north into the Great River and swept into the North Ocean; lest they spill south upon the bones of Ymir, and they grow yet mightier in size; lest they spill west into the forest of Abnoba, and give might to the vengeful jötunn within.

The land bowed to cradle the waters of Urthothr; and it became strong and long-lasting, and ever after yields luscious crops and fruitful vine.

— ‘The Tale Of Evö’, Norse Legends: A Comprehensive Guide To Viking Mythology, (2018), 3rd edn.

[…] the cork was bound with seven bindings. Many other rare and powerful marvels are there hidden in the Ertoth, and the cask is with them. For ages and ages they have not been found, and will not be; not unless the watch lessens, and the bindings break, and the cork is removed; only then the casked Ertoth will be found.

Those who want Ertoth to flow will find their joy beyond the cork; those who want to master it will have their golden sword;3 those who drink of it will want nothing else.

— Direct translation of the Young Codex Text by Francesco Kircher (1653); accuracy is dubious.4

Addendum 2:
On 07/07/2007, a test was conducted to open Item 93425 under controlled conditions.

VIDEO LOG

00:00: Footage begins; Item 9342 is centre frame. Researchers move about checking equipment.

02:16: All staff exit view. Four winches attached to one side activate, slowly opening the Item away from the camera.

05:32: The winches stop. A figure wearing a tethered harness approaches, aiming a handheld camera at the opening.


Hover to enlarge.


06:12: The winches resume.


08:23: The gap widens enough for the handheld camera to see through unobstructed.


Hover to enlarge.

12:08: The winches stop, leaving a half-metre gap.

Researcher (off-screen): Get the camera in there so we can see.

12:56: The figure complies, activating the handheld camera’s flashlight and reaching through the gap with it. Excluding Item 9342 and its doorway – which are not attached to a surface on this side – nothing is illuminated or visible.


Hover to enlarge.

13:17, Researcher (off-screen): Wait, go back.

13:22: The figure slowly reverses the movement of the camera.

13:31, Researcher (off-screen): Stop, there.


Hover to enlarge.

13:37, Researcher (off-screen): Is that a –

13:38: A faint pop. The footage abruptly darkens, redshifts, and distorts toward the opening. Loose objects and personnel, including the perspective camera, are sucked toward the opening; the figure is pulled completely through.

13:40: The camera stops, jerking around on the end of its cord; several overexposed, blue-shifted frames show humanoids rapidly moving in the area behind it before the camera comes to rest facing toward the threshold. Airborne objects and personnel exponentially slow as they approach the opening, becoming physically and conceptually warped; they are indistinguishable, spaghettified, and functionally motionless at the threshold. Nothing is audible over the rushing wind.

13:41 – 40:06: The Item is gradually closed over half an hour, crushing all obstructions.

40:07: The gap closes. All visual and temporal distortions cease; the camera topples to the floor as the Item slams shut. All equipment and furnishings remain deformed toward the Item, and difficult to identify; movement, retching, and screaming is audible.

Afterword: Due to temporal dilation, the events of this log occurred over a 72-hour period relative to baseline.

The sigils throughout Item 9342/A activated in response to the phenomena, and closed Item 9342; the sigils have remained active since.

All entities within the central chamber were declared incompatible with life. Average hume and chronon readings have reduced by 3% globally since this event.

Addendum 3: On 22/09/2007, the sigils throughout Item 9342/A returned to dormancy. All personnel in the area reported a succession of brief, intrusive feelings consisting of, in order:

  • Imminent, life-threatening danger;
  • Uncertainty with recent decisions, requiring reconsideration;
  • Intuitive certainty a significant object was secure;6
  • Mutual comradery and solidarity with others.
Footnotes
1. Latin, either a second-person imperative (‘You must [reconsider / withdraw / refuse / retract / undertake again]’), or first-person declaration (‘I am [reconsidering / withdrawing / refusing / retracting]’).
2. For comparison, the known universe contains approximately 1071 Joules across all forms of matter and energy.
3. A recuring phrase throughout the Young Codex Text of unknown meaning.
4. Translations by Francesco are known to be heavily interpretive; documents show they believed ‘Ertoth’ to be a Greco-Roman wine.
5. Before current protocols were enacted.
6. Interviewed personnel generally correlated the sensation with knowing their residence’s front door was properly locked.

[[/div]] The sigils throughout Item 9342/A activated in response to the phenomena, and closed Item 9342; the sigils have remained active since. All entities within the central chamber were declared incompatible with life. Average hume and chronon readings have reduced by 3% globally since this event. **Addendum 3:** On 22/09/2007, the sigils throughout Item 9342/A returned to dormancy. All personnel in the area reported a succession of brief, intrusive feelings consisting of, in order: * Imminent, life-threatening danger; * Uncertainty with recent decisions, requiring reconsideration; * Intuitive certainty a significant object was secure;[[footnote]]Interviewed personnel generally correlated the sensation with knowing their residence’s front door was properly locked.[[/footnote]] * Mutual comradery and solidarity with others.
