    background-color: rgb(var(--basalt-primary-color));     border: solid 0.2rem rgb(var(--general-border-color));     color: rgb(var(--basalt-main-text-color)); } [[/module]] [[>]] [[module Rate]] [[/>]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:author-label-source start=-- |name=Dino--Draws, Rosyfox2002]] [[=]] ~3.2k words, ~15 minute read **Written by [[*user Dino--Draws]] and [[*user Rosyfox2002]]** **[https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/dinodraws-author-page View my other works here!]** [[/=]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:author-label-source end=--]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:anomaly-class-bar-source |item-number= 9404 |clearance= 2 |container-class= keter |secondary-class= none |secondary-icon= none |disruption-class= vlam |risk-class= warning ]] ------ [[div class="grid-item"]] [[include component:image-block name= tree.jpg |caption= Recovered photograph of claw marks believed to be left by an SCP-9404 instance. |width=350px|align= right]] [[/div]] **Special Containment Procedures:** The Site-898 Cryptozoology Sector is to continue their pursuit in information pertaining to SCP-9404, as well their attempts at capturing a living instance for proper analysis and study. The discovery or reports of disemboweled corpses within the Northern Appalachian mountains are to be attributed to bears, cougars, and coyotes if local news reports do not assume this automatically. SCP-9404's own properties are otherwise considered self-concealing. **Description:** SCP-9404 is the designation given to a species of anomalous predatory animals from North American folklore, simply referred to as "hidebehinds," that are believed to exist throughout the forests of the Appalachia region. Utilizing both folktales relating to these entities, and sparse eyewitness accounts from various newspapers, the following has been gathered: * SCP-9404 instances are exceedingly difficult to observe directly; * SCP-9404 instances are keenly aware of attempts at observation, and will hide behind the nearest object[[footnote]] Typically trees.[[/footnote]] to avoid detection. The mechanics in which it achieves this are presently unknown; * SCP-9404 instances utilize this property in hunting -- stalking prey within the woods for extended periods of time, while remaining completely unseen -- before striking. * The appearance of these animals is unknown, though they are reported as making "hissing" or "clacking" sounds. Additionally, SCP-9404 instances are rumored to predate primarily on people who wander the woods alone. ------ **Containment Efforts:** The following details the efforts by Site-898's Cryptozoology Sector to discover and capture an instance of SCP-9404 for the purpose of further research. World's End State Park, due to its proximity to Site-898, was chosen for investigation. [[div class="blockquote"]] **Interview Log 9404** **Interviewers:** Dr. Fate Hargroves,[[footnote]] Cryptozoology Lead; cryptozoologist and tactical theologian.[[/footnote]] Dr. Atticus Rune[[footnote]] Cryptozoologist, folklorist.[[/footnote]] **Interviewee:** Officer Micah Eardwulf **Foreword:** On 12/05/1975, Drs. Hargroves and Rune departed Site-898 to meet with Officer Eardwulf, a local game warden of the Pennsylvania Game Commission, in an attempt to garner information relating to SCP-9404. ------ //Dr. Hargroves and Dr. Rune are walking along a forest trail at dusk. Dr. Rune is holding the camcorder as the two of them walk towards a small, dirt lot. A patrol vehicle is sitting parked there with a large, bearded man sat atop its hood. He turns his head as the two of them approach.// **Eardwulf:** Aha! You the lot that wanted to talk? **Dr. Rune:** Yes sir-ree. Thanks for agreein’ to speak with us. //Dr. Rune makes a flagrant hand gesture sideways.// **Dr. Rune:** I know it’s all a bit strange, but I reckon you’re someone who sees the strange all the time, out here. Off the record, of course. //Eardwulf gives a hearty laugh.// **Eardwulf:** What ain't strange out here, ey? I've seen plenty, in these woods. Guess it comes with the territory a' the name. **Dr. Hargroves:** It's hardly a subtle one. I almost thought my friend here was playing a prank on me until I saw the State Park's welcome sign. //Dr. Rune scoffs.// **Dr. Rune:** Told ya. It’s fun, if a little ominous. Anyhow, we were wonderin’ if you’ve gotten any reports of people feeling watched out there? We think something’s hiding ‘round the trees in the area, but good info is scarce. Sightings even scarcer. **Eardwulf:** Ah, people say that all the time. I hear it from my buds, too. Some folk are just running into mountain lions, but hunters round these parts do talk a' more fantastical things. **Dr. Hargroves:** Have you ever heard of a "hidebehind," sir? **Eardwulf:** Indeed I have. **Dr. Rune:** Curious bit of folklore, but every story’s usually got a bit of truth to it. Have you ever met one? You look like you’ve got some interesting stories. **Eardwulf:** You don't exactly //meet// 'em. Most people don't know it, if they do. It's in the name. They'll stalk folks from outta sight, hissin' and gigglin' all the while. I haven't gotten the honor to meet one of them hunter of hunters myself, though. **Dr. Hargroves:** Hunter of hunters? //Eardwulf shifts a bit, sliding off his car's hood to walk closer to the pair of doctors.// **Eardwulf:** Aye. Huntsmen are the folk who are out in these woods the most. Them and lumberjacks. It's said a hidebehind will feast when men walk the woods alone. **Dr. Rune:** Checks out. No one would be there to watch their back. //Dr. Rune pauses and leans against a tree.// **Dr. Rune:** Well, you got any favorites? Stories, I mean. Any specifics will help, really. We got time, and I like a good yarn.   **Eardwulf:** //[He chuckles]// A few. They make for good campfire talk. //The game warden folds his arms over his chest, and taps a finger in consideration as he thinks. Dr. Hargroves chooses a rock to sit on.// **Eardwulf:** There's this one 'bout a lumberjack. A young fellow, who had a bit too much to drink with his buddies out in the trees. Went for a walk, probably to find a place to piss. //[He barks a laugh]// Got more than he bargained for, with it! **Dr. Hargroves:** Oh? **Eardwulf:** He was being followed, of course. Not by his buds, but by one of those beasts. He heard the footsteps, called out "Now you better not be playing any games with me!" in a drunken slurry. His eyes were down on the dirt, trying not to trip in the dark, so he was unaware of the hulking thing creeping up. **Dr. Rune:** //[Under his breath]// Poor bastard. **Eardwulf:** //Lucky// bastard, cause there's something you should know about hidebehinds. They can't //stand// the taste a' booze. The things favorite treat is munchin' on your intestines, but if you got alcohol in your system? They'll turn up their nose to ya. They hate it! So when that hidebehind sunk its fangs into his arm only to smell booze on his breath? Nasty shock for the critter! //Dr. Rune opens his mouth and raises his eyebrows, momentarily at a loss for words.// **Dr. Rune:** Well... duly noted. Guess now I’ve got a good excuse to drink booze. **Eardwulf:** That's what I'm saying! The thing spat him out and scampered off back where it came. So some folk take to making sure they got a pint in them before going for a walk. //[He laughs]// Though some people say that it's just an excuse. **Dr. Hargroves:** What do you think, in regards to that? **Eardwulf:** Eh, I don't care as long as they don't leave the bottles in my park. **Dr. Hargroves:** ...Are there rumors of hidebehinds here? **Eardwulf:** Hm... I think I've heard talk of strange things stalkin' round the Rock Garden by Canyon Vista? Heavily wooded and full of big rocks 'n cliffs, folks say they like being in those sorts of cracks and caves. //Dr. Rune playfully nudges Dr. Hargroves.// **Dr. Rune:** Looks like we’ll have to stop by a state store ‘n check it out, sometime. //Dr. Hargroves laughs.// **Dr. Hargroves:** A lead is a lead! //Eardwulf tilts his head and smiles.// **Eardwulf:** You two fancy yourself cryptid hunters? //Dr. Rune glances at Dr. Hargroves, who smiles and shrugs.// **Dr. Hargroves:** I suppose we do. **Eardwulf:** Then it's good luck, to you both. Pairs are good, in these woods. Keep eyes on each other's backs. //Dr. Rune gives a humorous salute to the man.// **Dr. Rune:** Yes sir. If we aren’t found dead in a ditch somewhere, you’ll know we made it.   **Eardwulf:** Ha! Stay alive, keep my job easy. //He gives the two a good natured smile and wink. Dr. Hargroves shakes her head with a light chuckle.// **Dr. Hargroves:** Loud and clear. [[/div]] [[div class="grid-item"]] [[include component:image-block name= 11.png |caption= Transcription of symbol, "hidebehind." |width=250px|align= right]] [[/div]] On 13/05/1975, the personnel of the Cryptozoology Sector began scouting World's End State Park in the area that Officer Eardwulf had recommended. During the exploration, a new [https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-8411 SCP-8411] symbol was discovered etched onto a tree. Members of the team were immediately receptive to its memetic meaning, determining that it was representative of "hidebehind." In addition, the symbol for "stay alert"[[footnote]] An eye.[[/footnote]] accompanied it. It is unclear whether or not Officer Eardwulf was aware of the symbol's existence. Nearby, personnel would find a small overhang in a rocky hill, with clear traces of animal activity within the cave. Most notably, various scratches and scattered bones.[[footnote]] Later identified to be a mix of small animals, deer, and human.[[/footnote]] In conjunction with the SCP-8411 symbol, it was concluded that this area was actively inhabited by an SCP-9404 instance. The location was marked on the team's map, and containment efforts began. Below is a truncated list of containment attempts for SCP-9404. [[div class="jotting"]] **Containment Attempt #:** 1 ------ **Method:** A video camera was mounted near the cave in attempts to film SCP-9404 to gain information on its physiology as to fine-tune containment attempts. **Result:** Failure. After a two day period of no activity, the camera was found destroyed. [[>]] //I suppose video counts as being watched. -- Dr. Rune// [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="jotting"]] **Containment Attempt #:** 2 ------ **Method:** A trip-wire and bola trap was constructed at the mouth of the cave. **Result:** While the subject was successfully ensnared, it escaped and vanished from sight upon being spotted by approaching personnel. The only information gleamed is that the SCP-9404 instance had dark and shaggy fur. [[/div]] [[div class="jotting"]] **Containment Attempt #:** 3 ------ **Method:** A deer carcass is placed outside of the cave. Its digestive tract has been filled with sedatives. **Result:** Failure. Remains untouched. [[>]] //Perhaps the rumors of them preferring the meat of men is true. -- Dr. Hargroves// [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="jotting"]] **Containment Attempt #:** 4 ------ **Method:** A visual memetic stun agent was placed within the cave. **Result:** Failure. Despite evidence of multiple returns to the cavern by the SCP-9404 instance, it appears to have not reacted to the agent. [[>]] //Fascinating! -- Dr. Viceroy// [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="jotting"]] **Containment Attempt #:** 5 ------ **Method:** A weighted net trap was rigged within the trees surrounding the overhang where tracks indicate the SCP-9404 instance typically passes through. **Result:** Failure. Trap was triggered, but the netting was shredded by the instance. [[>]] //We need to stop booby-trapping its den. If it runs off, we'll never find it. -- Dr. Warren// [[/>]] [[/div]] [[div class="blockquote"]] **Archived Recording 9404** **Personnel Present:** Dr. Fate Hargroves, Dr. Atticus Rune, Dr. Murphy Warren,[[footnote]] Cryptozoologist, wildlife photographer.[[/footnote]] Dr. Amanda Viceroy,[[footnote]] Wildlife biologist, memeticist.[[/footnote]] Captain Rudy Weller[[footnote]] Captain of MTF Gamma-89 ("Rock and a Hard Place")[[/footnote]] **Foreword:** An impromptu meeting within the Cryptozoology Sector between members of staff. ------ //Dr. Hargroves heaves a sigh. She braces both hands on the table, and leans towards the team. Drs. Rune, Warren and Viceroy are sitting with her. Cpt. Weller leans against the wall.// **Dr. Hargroves:** We're going to need to try from a different angle. **Dr. Rune:** Clearly. //Dr. Warren shifts on his feet.// **Dr. Warren:** It is, ah, a bit difficult to catch an animal when we barely know anything of its physiology. The best I've been able to gather is from its footprints. It's bigger than your average bear. **Dr. Viceroy:** Maybe we need to beef up our efforts then? What do they use to catch polar bears? **Cpt. Rudy:** Tranquilizers, if I had to guess. Polar bears don't //disappear// when you look at them. **Dr. Hargroves:** I think our biggest issue is that we don't have an effective way of luring it anywhere. We can't exactly bait an animal whose preferred diet is human intestines. //Dr. Viceroy scrunches up her face.// **Dr. Viceroy:** Well, I mean, we //could// but--- **Cpt. Weller:** Anyone we send out there would be //eviscerated.// Body armor can only do so much. //Dr. Hargroves pauses, squints.// **Dr. Hargroves:** ...there might be a different type of defense though. **Dr. Rune:** Oh no. **Dr. Hargroves:** The game warden we spoke to mentioned one way to make sure that a hidebehind doesn't eat you. **Dr. Warren:** Yeah? **Dr. Hargroves:** Alcohol.   //There's a pause.// **Dr. Viceroy:** Like rubbing alcohol or-- **Dr. Rune:** Booze. She talkin' booze. //Cpt. Rudy barks a laugh.// **Cpt. Rudy:** They allergic or something? **Dr. Hargroves:** I don't know. He said they have a severe aversion to it, that they wouldn't eat someone who's got it in their system. Something about the taste and smell pains them.   **Cpt. Rudy:** Are you suggesting we get someone wasted in the woods as a backwards sort of //bait?// **Dr. Hargroves:** It sounds asinine when said that way, but yes. In theory, it would prevent it from harming them. If we can lure it into striking, only for its target to be drenched in a scent that would repel it, it would be open to counter-attack. **Dr. Rune:** For an incredibly tight window of time. **Dr. Warren:** And it would be the world's most horrific game of chicken. //Cpt. Weller taps a finger against his arm.// **Cpt. Weller:** You'd need it to spring a tripwire, a heavy bola to knock it down. Some folks layin' in wait with darts. **Dr. Warren:** We tried to bola it before, though. It just vanished the moment we got close enough to see it. **Dr. Viceroy:** You could blindfold the tranq team. **Dr. Warren:** ...blindfold the people who need to shoot at it? **Cpt. Weller:** The only person in this Site that I'd trust to quite literally fire blind is the Chief. **Dr. Viceroy:** Is she busy? **Cpt. Weller:** I could find out. **Dr. Warren:** This is actually insane. You people are insane. **Dr. Rune:** I mean, if we got people on stand-by, it'd be easy to abort the attempt and make it go away. The biggest risk here is trustin' the whole alcohol bit -- but I'm willin' to believe it. //Dr. Warren bites his lip, but Dr. Viceroy nods eagerly.// **Dr. Hargroves:** So, we'd also need alcohol. Which we… don’t have a lot of, huh? Unless we take a few hour drive to civilization to hit a liquor store. //Dr. Warren looks confused, Dr. Rune sighs.// **Dr. Rune:** Director Eden refuses to add anything more than some shitty draft to the shipments. Probably so no one gets in a drunken fight with a not-deer. So we don’t have much and what we have tastes like ass. **Cpt. Weller:** Actually, I know a guy. **Dr. Hargroves:** You… know a guy? **Dr. Warren:** //[Murmuring]// This site doesn't even have 100 people, don’t you know everyone? **Cpt. Weller:** Hold on, hold on. I’ll be right back. //Ten minutes of extraneous footage removed.// //Cpt. Weller places a mason jar of dark purple-red liquid on the table with a heavy thunk. Dr. Rune raises an eyebrow, interested.// **Dr. Rune:** What the hell is that? **Cpt. Weller:** Some actually good booze. //Dr. Hargroves pinches her nose.// **Dr. Hargroves:** Eden is gonna kill you. **Cpt. Weller:** Bah! He can thump a Bible about it. Not that he knows. **Dr. Warren:** //We're literally recording--// //Dr. Viceroy nudges past Dr. Warren.// **Dr. Viceroy:** Who’s the bootlegger? **Cpt. Weller:** Do I //look// like a snitch? //Dr. Viceroy giggles. Dr. Warren puts a hand to his forehead as Dr. Rune leans forward.// **Dr. Rune:** Do I get to know what’s in that or is it a trade secret? **Cpt. Weller:** It’s a blueberry mead. Made from some shit in the swamp and doctored with a little extra, this’ll knock you off your ass faster than you can shake a tail at. //Cpt. Weller grins widely.// **Cpt. Weller:** A bit of behind-the-back brewing to catch a hidebehind. [[/div]] On 28/05/1975, the Cryptozoology Sector determined a revised plan to catch the SCP-9404 instance. Despite the unorthodox proposal, the plan was approved for execution by Chief Zoe Miranda[[footnote]] Chief of Security and Containment.[[/footnote]] and the attempt was undergone the next day. [[div class="modal"]] **Containment Attempt After-Action Report** **Officer of Record:** Director Julian Eden ------ [[div class="notation"]] **Dr. Hargroves:** We think the mechanics behind its ability to "hide behind" things is a form of observational teleportation. **Dir. Eden:** Mhm. **Dr. Hargroves:** When observed, they vanish into the shadows or behind things where they are unseen. It's not that they're incredibly fast on their feet, I'd reckon they're probably as fast as your average bear, it's a dematerialization.   **Dir. Eden:** So this meant you had to blindfold the people wielding rifles? **Dr. Hargroves:** In our defense, it is incredibly difficult to try and catch a creature -- in an open forest -- that you cannot look at. We had to get creative in terms of baiting it into an open spot to be tranq'd. **Dir. Eden:** And the other part of your "creativity" was to get drunk?   [[/div]] [[div class="notation"]] **Dr. Rune:** It was a tad risky, but I've long learned to trust the words of folk out here when it comes to warding. We did some cross-referencing after talking to that game warden. Turns out it was a consistency we missed in our first diggin', and consistencies in folktales are always important. **Dir. Eden:** Risky is not how I would've described it. I have never heard of alcohol as any sort of ward. **Dr. Rune:** Ya could call it a ward 'gainst bacteria. //Dir. Eden pauses.// **Dir. Eden:** I... suppose? **Dr. Rune:** We did actually find out //why// it's so adverse to alcohol, too. **Dir. Eden:** Oh? [[/div]] [[div class="notation"]] **Dr. Viceroy:** It's an incredibly fascinating animal! Like a polar bear, almost, in the way it sees -- well, mostly smells -- people as viable prey. **Dir. Eden:** People are its //preferred// prey, are they not? **Dr. Viceroy:** They'll eat the guts of anything alone in the woods, but it seems to prefer people, yeah. Which is why we had Warren stand out there as bait! **Dir. Eden:** Oh my God you made Murphy do it. **Dr. Viceroy:** Hey, if we messed up, it's not like he would've been hurt! //Silence on recording.// **Dr. Viceroy:** ...much. [[/div]] [[div class="notation"]] //Dr. Warren is sitting with his head in his hands. Dir. Eden is sitting next to him, worried.// **Dr. Warren:** Please don't let them talk me into that again. Oh my god I drank too much. I didn't even //know// I was a confident drunk. **Dir. Eden:** I'm not letting them do that again. **Dr. Warren:** It was so big. Did you //see// how big it was? I bet it's 4 meters on its hind legs. //Dir. Eden pats him on the back.// **Dr. Warren:** It nearly touched me when the bola downed it. I felt its CLAWS whiff the air behind my head! Or maybe that was one of the darts. I can't tell which one of those is the worse option. //He pauses.// **Dr. Warren:** I'm not in trouble, right, sir? **Dir. Eden:** No. **Dr. Warren:** Are any of us in trouble? **Dir. Eden:** I'm debating it. [[/div]] [[div class="notation"]] **Dir. Eden:** And you wonder why I don’t add more alcohol to the shipment list. **Cpt. Weller:** That crap is barely 5 proof! **Dir. Eden:** And yet you still found a way to get drunk on it. //Cpt. Weller pauses. Dir. Eden is regarding him tiredly.// **Cpt. Weller:** …Yup. [[/div]] [[div class="notation"]] **Dir. Eden:** What in God’s name made you think this was a good idea? **Chief Miranda:** I mean… //She clicks her tongue.// **Chief Miranda:** It worked. [[/div]] [[/div]] The SCP-9404 instance has since been successfully transported to Site-898 and placed within one of the Cryptozoology Sector's outdoor containment units. The entity's containment procedures and upkeep have been established as the following: * All cameras within Outdoor Containment Unit B are to be deactivated; a series of motion sensors are to take their place as to more effectively monitor SCP-9404's activity. * SCP-9404 is to be fed deer viscera on a twice-daily feeding schedule. * In the event that the instance needs to be subdued -- whether for medical examination or containment cleaning purposes -- it is to be sedated via its food. While the SCP-9404 instance was tranquilized and transported to containment, members of staff were able to examine the anomaly's physiology in-full. See below. 1/9405 LEVEL 1/9405
CLASSIFIED
Item #: SCP-9405
Argus

Semi-legendary depiction of SCP-9405-α in the Emblemata

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9405 is contained.

Foundation surveillance assets are to maintain an alert for sightings of SCP-9405-β or reports of infiltration of the SCP-9405 caverns by civilians. If these occur too frequently, Foundation agents are to seize control of SCP-9405 by any and all means, including force majeure, and evacuate the environs. However, for the moment, SCP-9405 is classified as Argus1.

Description: SCP-9405 is a mausoleum, and attendant subterranean residence complex2, located in a cave system beneath the women's quarters of the Paliani Monastery, in the Heraklion municipality of Greece. The tomb therein, dating to ca. 400 BC, is believed to be that of Lais of Corinth, a historically noteworthy hetaira3. She is remembered primarily for her beauty by figures including Plato and Antipater of Sidon, otherwise appearing only sparsely in the historical record. No document mentions her presence on Crete (or anywhere else outside Corinth), and her identity can only be verified using esoteric methods.

The anomalous history of the complex can be divided into two broad phases: Between the 4th and 1st centuries BC, the complex served as a residence for between 50 and 100 women and some small number of transient men, drawn from across Crete. During this period, the community was not enormously wealthy but displayed a strikingly common use of the written word, implying high literacy rates. Between the 1st century BC and the 1st century AD, it experienced considerable upheaval, likely related to the advance of the Roman Republic across the island, and was depopulated.

Afterwards, it was rendered essentially mundane, and was inhabited only by vagrants until the foundation of the Paliani monastery ca. 400 AD. The founding members are known to have been aware of the existence of the complex, but did not have detailed knowledge of its history or properties. At its construction, SCP-9405 exhibited a variety of attendant anomalies, which are documented in the supplementary material. Today, two of these anomalies remain extant.

SCP-9405-α is a carved marble catafalque4 positioned by the western wall of the tomb, in the deepest sublevel of SCP-9405. On its eastern side, facing the room's entrance, is what appears to be a stylisation of a lioness chasing a ram. The lioness' facial features have been disfigured beyond recognition, and the ram's horns have been chipped away, apparently in a gradual process. Otherwise, the carvings do not show signs of weathering or decay. The upper surface of SCP-9405-α is deeply cracked, and no body is present.

Certain individuals experience a painful sensation akin to a powerful shock upon contact with SCP-9405-α. It is unknown what, precisely, causes this effect, but it is reported disproportionately often in male personnel and security specialists.

SCP-9405-β is an animate marble lioness, originally identical in form to that pictured on SCP-9405-α, which has suffered considerable damage. Most notably, its right foreleg has been broken off, with the shoulder shattered at the joint. It also displays numerous hairline fractures and chips, presumably inflicted during close combat. Finally, large portions of the face and flanks display pitting and spalling due to musket-fire.

This damage has rendered SCP-9405-β slow, but not weak, and it is capable of exerting well in excess of 20 kilonewtons of force with its limbs. It behaves aggressively towards precisely those individuals which trigger the injurious effect of SCP-9405-α, and will act in a territorial manner to keep them from entering SCP-9405's grounds. However, it displays affection and obedience to the inhabitants of SCP-9405 (currently the sisters of the monastery) and will allow all personnel to pass on their instruction.

Discovery: During the Cretan War of 1645, raiding Ottoman forces struck at the monastery, which was known not to be well-defended. Despite this, their first advance was repulsed. Records indicate the presence of "ferocious beasts" which fought on behalf of the monastery, giving its members time to escape before the next wave seized the building. These accounts caught the interest of the Foundation Historical Annex, who alerted the Department of Archaeology. Beginning on 18/05/2022, the Department carried out a survey of the site with permission of the contemporary residents5, and discovered SCP-9405.

Prior to the unearthing of the main entrance, SCP-9405-β had been able to enter and exit the complex through a circuitous route of tunnels and caverns. The residents of the monastery maintained a wealth of folklore concerning SCP-9405-β, which they referred to as μικρή αδελφή6.

Over the two years following the initial dig, personnel uncovered many further parahistorical artefacts, which are catalogued below.

Artefacts:

Note that the below is not an exhaustive list of artefacts. Many of the discovered objects are of extremely minor anomalous effect or historical interest, and are standard for the period. For example, a great number of amulets to Mithras have been found in and especially around the complex, many of which display elevated Akiva emissions, as would be expected. For a complete catalogue, consult RAISA Reliquary 9405-3507.

  • Graves & Grave-Goods
  • Statuary Artefacts
  • Miscellanea

Bodies believed to be from the period SCP-9405 was inhabited are interred exclusively on the plain the monastery overlooks. These include both remains of the residents of SCP-9405 and other burials carried out by its inhabitants. A brief list:

— Around 600 remains arranged in a roughly orderly manner across the better part of the plain. ca. 550 are female, and 50 male. Remarkably, no infant remains can be found among them. Most deaths appear to have been from natural causes. A few apparently incidental injuries are present, but all have healed exceptionally well. Many are buried with simple personal effects: small sherds of ceramic, simple jewellery, or copper beads. Dated roughly uniformly between 400 and 100 BC.

Damaged weapons recovered among remains. These are the only valuable items present.

— ~20 male remains, piled densely in a single region. These bear signs of serious injury, commonly including shattered ribcages and skulls, and have been arranged apparently without much care. Few material artefacts are buried with them. Dated to around 80 BC.

— A single set of remains that has been thoroughly pulverised. Although only belonging to a single individual, no single bone fragment measures more than three square centimetres in area. The region in which these remains are buried is distant from the rest, and the earth over them is barren. Dated to around 80 BC.

— 15 remains, 13 female and 2 male, buried haphazardly, and with no grave-goods. All show signs of traumatic deaths. Dated to around 60 BC.

— Remains belonging to 5 individuals, occupying a distinct position on the plain. Though gross morphology is subtly different between instances, all are genetically identical. Four seem to have died peacefully, but the fifth bears a compound fracture across the skull. Burial sites also contain trace amounts of precious metals and signs of reburial, implying the looting of more extensive goods at some point. Dated evenly through the years between 400 and 80 BC.

Sketch of instance by Salvator Rosa, who was related a description secondhand. The significance of the other skull is unknown.

Throughout the site, various instances of sculpture can be found, primarily formed of marble. Many of these are mundane in nature, but of particular interest are several which, due to their unusual construction and notable placement within the complex, are believed to have been previously animate. The Department believes these to be decommissioned SCP-9405-β instances. These are:

The front half of a marble cow, bisected cleanly by unknown means. Its flesh ends at the neck, and its head is simply a bovine skull. The tips of its horns have been broken off, and a thunderbolt has been etched into its flank. Though weathered, flecks of dried organic matter can be found on its head, neck, and hooves, originating from at least 12 distinct persons. Found in the lower chambers of SCP-9405.

An owl, embedded into the rock of the cave system. Physical contact with the instance produces a sense of reassurance. Found in what was a common residence area. The stones of the room are covered in simplistic sketches of various faces, at around waist-level.

Department-commissioned reconstruction of cervine statue, complete with curved antlers

Various fragments of a cervine statue scattered across multiple chambers. They display unusual warping and melting inconsistent with mechanical breakage alone, and some pieces bear a glassy surface texture. The antlers occupy a central position in a shrine (see Miscellania). Found distributed throughout the upper residential levels of SCP-9405. Only about three-fifths of the whole statue has been recovered to date.

A statue of a newborn lamb, found atop a ridge overlooking the valley, entirely undamaged. It is depicted curled up, as if only momentarily resting, and ready to wake.

Aside from the previous two categories, the Department has discovered a variety of artefacts and desiderata that do not occur in a common enough pattern to have their own dedicated category. The most notable of these are below.

Graffiti is found in many of the upper chambers of SCP-9405, which have been used as impromptu quarters for soldiers repeatedly throughout the last two thousand years. These include:

  • Damn these hills, original text in German.
  • Mustafa was here and This frost is too much, original text in Arabic.
  • LEGIO VII AUGUSTA7 and, below it, CITY OF WHORES, original text in Latin.
  • Even now, I dream of this. It is nearly time. Across the years, sisters—, text cuts off abruptly due to damage to the surface, originally in Doric Greek.

It is unknown how the relatively impoverished residents of SCP-9405 were able to produce the dyes needed for this fresco.

A collection of shrines to various classical Hellenic divinities, such as Athena, Demeter, and Hestia, is assembled throughout the caves. These are unlike their typical depictions, as each bears the same facial features: dark curled hair, an aquiline nose, and blue eyes. One shrine breaks from typical religious forms: instead of statuary or imagery, at its centre are a pair of marble antlers, which have shattered and then been tied together with twine (see Statuary Artefacts). It was dedicated to Artemis; water poured over the antlers will vanish before it hits the ground, and the next projectile aimed by supplicants will always hit its target.

The lowermost chamber of the cave system is filled with an underground body of water. Within it are four sets of synthetic material, which resemble sets of sloughed human skin. Chemical analysis does not conclusively identify the substance, though it contains complex proteins or protein-analogues. It has an iridescent appearance, and is strikingly coloured, with patterns resembling those found on a peacock's feathers.

Addendum 9405-1: After the conclusion of the survey, Department staff noted that SCP-9405 was deeply embedded in both the physical structure and the culture of the nuns, and full containment would necessitate a large-scale amnesticisation campaign. Today, the monastery is a moderately popular tourist destination, and its surface levels are almost perpetually occupied.

Consequently, it was determined impossible to simply keep the nuns in place while erasing knowledge of the complex and SCP-9405-β. In fact, full containment would necessitate evacuation of all current inhabitants, and a large-scale disinformation scheme across Heraklion and indeed much of wider Greece.

Since the monastery had historically been able to avoid the spread of information outside its bounds, and had not allowed outsiders access to the grounds until the Foundation's active intrusion, it was decided that simply reinforcing its natural isolationist tendencies would be sufficient. It has been declared a protected historical site, and monasterial officials have agreed to disallow further study of the area.

Today, SCP-9405 remains under the effective containment and control of the sisters of the Paliani Monastery.

Addendum 9405-2: During the dig, Department analysts discovered several fragmentary texts. These were not meaningfully translatable in themselves. However, after comparison with manuscripts in the monastery's collection, researchers were able to identify common threads and motifs, hypothesising that perhaps they were both descended from the same text. After thorough interpolation by retrocognitive techniques, they were able to reconstruct a few small passages, likely written by the residents during SCP-9405's inhabited period. The translations are necessarily uncertain, but are presented below for completeness. These represent the final artefacts collected from the SCP-9405 dig site.

[…] came up from Knossos, bearing [marks?/scars?]. I took her hands and […] no man would [pursue/find?] her here. […] beneath the earth, born […] waits. Women, all, who […] the [huntress/maiden?] was completed by […] have taken a new face. […] twenty women at last […] who did not yesterday. This is the work.

[…] Each woman who arrives broken leaves whole, or […] but remains […] The guardians stand […] Sister, and Old Mother. […] The steel of [soldiers/raiders?] is […] flesh from their bones with the tomb's fire, if necessary. […] be glad. Their [oars/hulls?]8 shall not [reach?] […] the young grow old […]

They hunted the child with […] perhaps more. [Seeking?/Demanding?] return of stolen […] Elder Sister met them […] fell before she broke. Only three […] I, myself […] for the [augur/priest?]. What was left […] wind spread him far. […] will not accept his bones.

The students of the sun […] killing light. And [Mithras?/The sky-father?] […] spiteful, and cruel. They fear […] see hope in the East. What is […] My guardians fall […] Little Sister still waits. She […] and struck, but fights on. […] worse each year. I must speak with [the consul?] […]

The lady was […] cowardly scheme. Creticus9 will be […] has not [risen/woken?] from the lake. We prepare to mourn […] Lais, you were ours. How long shall […] In the hills, a lamb [surprises/appears?] […] wait, and be ready.

[…] what was here. For generations […] lived without shame […] my mother, and her mother's mother died in [peace/silence?]. Their swords cannot take that […] day is coming when their gods […] forgiven. Lais promised a new […] dais is broken. Death shall [flee/surrender?] […] Whatever they say, we were not […] what we made […] enough. Across the years, sisters, I salute you.

SCP-9406.raw_content:
Item #: SCP-9406

Object Class: Keter Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9406-1 is currently contained at Site-██ in the Humanoid Containment Wing.

SCP-9406-1 is to be contained in a 10x10x10 meters room, furnished with Class 4 amenities, with rounded corners and minimal straight lines. Any other amenity requests by personnel or SCP-9406-1 are to be reviewed and approved by the Lead Researcher for SCP-9406 (currently Dr. Lacan). The room in itself must have walls that connect to the ground in a smooth curve, mitigating SCP-9406 from triggering.

Any contact with SCP-9406-1 must be reviewed and accepted by at least two Level 4 Researchers. The only authorized personnel for such contact are Level 3 or above Researchers, who must previously have been briefed on SCP-9406.

Every wall of the containment must have a white Light-Emitting Diode capable of producing concentrated light flashes of, at minimum, 200,000 candelas in case of the SCP perceiving a geometric shape.

Refer to SCP-9406-1's latest Medical Log for any new information.

Description: SCP-9406 is the designation of the anomaly affecting SCP-9406-1.

SCP-9406-1 is a Caucasian male, formerly named Albert Carrel. At the time of this report, it is 34 years old, 1.91 meters tall and weighs approximately 89 kg. SCP-9406-1 has brown short hair and green eyes. SCP-9406-1 knows English, but prefers talking in French.

SCP-9406 manifests when SCP-9406-1 visually and consciously perceives one or multiple shapes1. When it does, the anomalous reaction linked to the shape manifests in a certain radius.

This radius, called SCP-9406-2, is a sphere, with the center being SCP-9406-1. SCP-9406-2's size seems to be based on the size of the shape that SCP-9406-1 perceived.

The following are the shapes currently known by the Foundation2 and their corresponding effects when viewed by SCP-9406-1:

Associated Shape Designation Effect(s)
Circle SCP-9406-A A specific ongoing process in SCP-9406-2 is abruptly stopped (processes include, but are not limited to: conversations, thinking, walking, or mechanical processes like motors or gears turning). The process will be stopped for as little as 11 seconds and as long as 2 hours and 16 seconds.
Rectangles SCP-9406-B A specific object or phenomena in SCP-9406-2 is now bound by a new random rule, tied to the environment in SCP-9406-2. For example, in a forest, it could add "Everyone must walk on leaves", or in a Site's corridor, it could add "Anyone walking past a door must have previously opened it". Rules created by SCP-9406-1 cannot be broken and last forever in the affected area.
Triangle SCP-9406-C An existing pattern or sequence in SCP-9406-2 is forced to rapidly and exponentially expand or accelerate. This could lead to tiny cracks on a wall becoming a crevasse, or a tiny electrical output becoming a lightning bolt. This effect lasts around 1 minute.
Rhombus SCP-9406-D For a brief period, the intended purpose of an object in SCP-9406-2 is inverted. For example, a chair might be uncomfortable to sit upon, but very comfortable to stand on, or a ceiling might let rain and light go through it while still being opaque. This usually lasts around 1 minute.
Five-Pointed Star SCP-9406-E All individuals within SCP-9406-2 temporarily share a unified consciousness, like thoughts and emotions, in a single, unstopped stream. This usually lasts around 20 seconds.
Four-Pointed Star SCP-9406-F A random object or concept in SCP-9406-2 is temporarily split in two different states. For example, a room's temperature could be split in "cold" and "hot", making anyone inside feel both, or a door could become opened and closed at the same time. This is, of course, normally impossible, and as such often results to the creation of a cognitohazard. This usually lasts around 30 seconds.
Oval SCP-9406-G A random event or process in SCP-9406-2 is stretched, causing it to take far longer to finish than it would normally. For example, a quick discussion could turn into a three hours talk, or a door that should open in a few seconds could take days to be opened. The effect lasts until the stretched event or process is finished.
Arrow SCP-9406-H Any moving objects and individual in SCP-9406-2 suddenly start moving in the same direction as the perceived arrow is pointing. The effect usually lasts 1 minute.
Spiral3 SCP-9406-I A gravitational event manifests in SCP-9406-2: gravity seems to "turn", at around 1 degree per second. The axis of rotation depends on the axis of the spiral SCP-9406-1 perceived. This effect lasts exactly 6 minutes. If someone leaves the affected area before the end, their gravity will be changed forever.



Addendum 9406-A: Obtainment of SCP-9406

SCP-9406-1 was found in October of 2022, in the city of Nice, France, after a lot of bizarre events occurred in the same city in a single night. Reports included the stop of every vehicles on a road segment in the night, caused by SCP-9406-1 after it looked at the moon, triggering SCP-9406-A; then the locking of every doors, that could only be opened when reciting the entire Notice of the vehicle, caused by SCP-9406-1 when it looked at a car's window after the sudden stop of all the cars around it, triggering SCP-9406-B; and finally the lights that suddently stopped producing light, caused by SCP-9406-1 seeing the logo of a car brand, including a rhombus, triggering SCP-9406-D, making every light in the area instead reduce the amount of light in front of them.

SCP-9406-1 was then captured without incidents. Since then, SCP-9406-1 has been very cooperative with the Foundation, only protesting when researchers wanted to test SCP-9406-E, due to the distress it causes.



Interview Log 9406-A:

Interviewer: Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan
Interviewee: SCP-9406-1

Foreword: This Interview took place 6 hours after SCP-9406-1 was captured.

<Begin Log>

Dr. Lacan: Hello, SCP-9406-1.

[SCP-9406-1 doesn't seem to have heard Dr. Lacan.]

Dr. Lacan: SCP-9406-1? Can you hear me?

SCP-9406-1: [SCP-9406-1's head shoots up.] Wha- Ohh… You… uh… you were talking to me?

Dr. Lacan: No worries. I'm only here to ask you some questions about your… particular ability.

SCP-9406-1: Oh… Well, I… I understood you weren't classic police, with your guys grabbing me out of nowhere and putting me in a… cell. Okay, so… [SCP-9406-1 pauses for 5 seconds.] I started having this weird… thing… around 5 days before you got me. You know, I… I really liked drawing in my spare time, but whenever I drew some… basic things, my eyes started hurting a little.

Dr. Lacan: Was this the only effect that manifested when looking at shapes?

SCP-9406-1: For the four next days… I'd say it was… But it started hurting more and more as days went on… On the day you captured me, my eyes had started… er… hurting a bit too much. So, I decided to go outside for a small break. A bit of… fresh air, you know? And that's when hell broke loose.

Dr. Lacan: I see… Do you have any ideas what could have caused you to get those properties?

SCP-9406-1: Uuh, not at all. It was just a… normal day. Worked, drew, slept. Not much of an exciting life… Well except the drawing part, heh…

Dr. Lacan: Very well. Thank you for your cooperation. We will work on our side to make your stay here as pleasant as we can.

<End Log>



Test Log 9406-A:

Goal: To determine what triggers SCP-9406.

Shape Shown Effect(s) Note
Square To open the testing chamber's door, subjects had to say "Open Sesame" out loud. A keycard wasn't needed anymore. -B's effects seem to be able to change multiple things at the same time, like here, where it changed how the door and the keycard reader worked. - Dr. Lacan
Square with small rounded corners Anyone around walls had to put their hand on the closest wall when moving. We are currently trying to see if changing the shapes by distorting them could negate the effects. Maybe this one wasn't distorted enough? - Dr. Lacan
Same as before, more rounded corners None As I hypothesized, heavily distorted shapes do not trigger SCP-9406. - Dr. Lacan
Square with curved sides None We had to try this one multiple times, as having the sides too curved triggered -A, and if they weren't curved enough it triggered -B. - Dr. Lacan



Addendum 9406-B: Project Sermau:

After 17 days of being in Foundation custody, SCP-9406-1 is starting to show some mental weaknesses. As such, I, Dr. Lacan, have started Project Sermau to prevent it from becoming uncooperative. The goal is as follows:

1. Find a language that doesn't require any shape to be written and understood.

2. If no language has been found, create a new writing system ourselves, without any shapes that could trigger SCP-9406.

Here is a list of languages/writing systems that cannot be used for Project Sermau:

  • Any language using the Roman Alphabet: multiple letters contain a circle (o), oval (a) or spiral (s) in them.
  • Chinese: multiple symbols like the ones for "moon" (月), "stone" (石) or "room" (间) contain one or multiple rectangles.
  • Japanese: multiple symbols like the ones for "su" (す), "nu" (ぬ) or "ro" (ロ) contain rectangles, circles or ovals.
  • Korean: multiple symbols like the ones for "milk" (우유), "m" (ㅁ) or "b" (ㅂ) contain one or multiple rectangles or circles.



Incident Log 9406-A:

On November of 2022, during the weekly interview between SCP-9406-1 and Dr. Lacan, SCP-9406-1 inadvertently looked at the interviewer's face, triggering SCP-9406-A, -B, -C and -G at the same time. -B made the two people in the room unable to sit up unless they held each other's hand, -A stopped the light from generating any light, -C made any soundwave grow in volume the more they went through the air, and -G stretched the time it took for SCP-9406-1 to close its eyes, instead taking 174 minutes to close them.

After -A's effects were discovered and both Dr. Lacan and SCP-9406-1 finally stood up, site security quickly arrived and escorted SCP-9406-1 back to its containment chamber, only for it to see an arrow on the floor pointing forward, making all of the guard walk in the same direction for 1 minute, eventually hitting the wall in front of them.

While walking into the wall, SCP-9406-1 looked up and saw a rhombus on a guard's uniform. This shape triggered SCP-9406-D, making everyone able to walk through closed doors and unable to go through opened doors, leading to a minor breach. SCP-9406-1 was then blindfolded and taken back to its containment chamber, and the aforementioned breach got resolved simply by inverting the doors' system (having them opened at all time and closing them when someone wants to go through).



Note from Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan:

Though it probably did not make any of this on purpose, it still constitutes a great security risk. As such, all further Interviews will be via microphones, despite the damage it may cause to SCP-9406-1's mental state.



Interview Log 9406-B:

Interviewer: Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan
Interviewee: SCP-9406-1

Foreword: This Interview took place the day after Incident 9406-A, with SCP-9406-1 still in its chamber, talking by microphone to Dr. Lacan.

<Begin Log>

Dr. Lacan: Hello again, SCP-9406-1.

SCP-9406-1: Hello…

Dr. Lacan: You don't seem really happy to see me.

[SCP-9406-1 sighs]

SCP-9406-1: Well… seeing all the things I did yesterday, I… I can't really be happy about anything. With all the problems I caused…

Dr. Lacan: Hmm, let's say it could have been worse.

SCP-9406-1: And now, I can't even talk to you in person? It's just… quite a lot.

Dr. Lacan: At least I hope you understand why we put measures like this. It's to prevent the exact problems that happened yesterday.

SCP-9406-1: I see… I guess I should be thankful?

Dr. Lacan: Moving on. I came here to ask about how you felt in the Foundation.

SCP-9406-1: What do you mean by that?

Dr. Lacan: Well, we need to know how you feel, to then give you a better stay here.

SCP-9406-1: Well… Even if I didn't live here, it wouldn't be good for me, right? Like, at least here I can… walk around, look around my room, sleep knowing I haven't caused too much problems, all that… If I instead lived outside, I would need to be… blindfolded to do anything, and being blind for the rest of my life… isn't really something I wanna do.

Dr. Lacan: Do you have any goals then? Anything you'd really want?

SCP-9406-1: Er… [SCP-9406-1 pauses for a few seconds.] Well, what I'd like the most would be being able to draw again. Drawing… drawing really was what anchored me in the world before you… captured me… and before all the weird things happened. I… I could draw hours on end and still feel rested at the end of the day… But now… now I can't really. That… was probably the things I loved the most, so… not being able to do it is rough. Can't do anything about it anyways, right?

Dr. Lacan: That is, sadly, exact. Drawing is, and will probably forever be, something that you cannot do without triggering SCP-9406.

SCP-9406-1: It was more of a rethorical question… Anyways, that's why I'm really excited about that… "Project" you talked about. Reading will at least allow me to do something else other than think about my past life… or about all the things I've done here.

<End Log>

Note from Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan:

I'd suggest trying to speed up Project Sermau, but being one of the researchers assigned to it, I know we are already overworking ourselves, as we rarely have time to work on it. I simply hope SCP-9406-1 can hold until there.



Incident Log 9406-B:

Five days after Incident 9406-A, when giving SCP-9406-1 its meal, Junior Researcher L████ also gave it utensiles, once again triggering SCP-9406. The following is the camera footage recovered from one of the cameras in SCP-9406-1's cell:

<Begin Log>

<12:01:05> [The door to the cell opens, Dr. L████ going entering the cell.]

<12:01:12> [SCP-9406-1 looks at the plate, triggering -A.]]

<12:01:20> [Dr. L████ drops dead. It is later confirmed that -A stopped Dr. L████'s heart. SCP-9406-1's eyes widen while it slowly walks to the wall at the opposite side of the door.]]

<12:01:26> [Tears can be seen pouring from SCP-9406-1's eyes.]

<12:01:35> [SCP-9406-1 notices a knife that fell from the plate. SCP-9406-1 approaches it.]

<12:01:45> [After taking the knife, SCP-9406-1 looks at it, triggering -C. It is later confirmed that it massively enlarged a spider web outside its containment cell.]

<12:02:03> [SCP-9406-1 slowly aligns the knife to put it towards its right eye. SCP-9406-1 can be seen shaking.]

<12:02:31> [Dr. Lacan enters the room with three security agents behind him.]

<Dr. Lacan (12:02:35)> SCP-9406-1, please lower this knife.

<12:02:38> [SCP-9406-1 doesn't seem to answer, instead lowering its eyes, preventing itself from looking towards Dr. Lacan]

<Dr. Lacan (12:02:42)> Please, SCP-9406-1. We are not entirely sure why you want to do this, bu-

<SCP-9406-1 (12:02:56)> You really… don't understand why? Why I'd pierce my eye? Why I'd risk killing myself? Just look on the ground in front of you. It's a human being. Someone that was doing their job. And they are dead now. Because of me. Because of this… thing that I have and that I didn't ask for. Is THAT enough of a reason?

<Dr. Lacan (12:03:26)> While I do understand your motive, it still isn't a solution. Do you really think the only way to redeem yourself from killing someone is hurting yourself?

<SCP-9406-1 (12:03:39)> So you didn't understand what I just said. I don't want do redeem myself. I… I just don't want… to have this thing anymore. It just seems childish, or even "normal", but… I ju-… I just don't want to kill anyone. And I just did. I thought I could have that thing in me and still live a life I'm somewhat proud of. But this is the event I specifically didn't want to happen because of me. I… I just can't. I can't take it anymore.

<12:04:21> [As SCP-9406-1 was tightening its grip on the knife still in its hands, one of the three security agents fired a sleeping dart, while another one quickly grabbed the knife.]



Note from Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan:

This incident should serve as example of why we don't send Junior Researchers to new and dangerous SCPs. I updated SCP-9406's file to only allow personnel at or above Clearance Level 3. Only later did I find out that L████ was sent by the Agent that was supposed to feed SCP-9406-1, because "they felt that this would be valuable experience for Dr. L████".
We should also note that SCP-9406-1's mental state is rapidly deteriorating. Despite all of this, Project Sermau is finally almost finished. It should hopefully improve its mental state.



Incident Log 9406-C:

Two days after Project Sermau had finished and SCP-9406-1 had started taking classes to learn the new language, SCP-9406-1 got its first book. However, the paper was too thin, and caused the letters at the front and the back to merge. This created multiple shapes, triggering multiple times SCP-9406. In those shapes, 3 circles, 2 triangle, 2 spirals, 2 rhombuses and 1 square were created and perceived by SCP-9406-1. The following is the camera footage recovered from cameras around the Site:

<Begin Log>

<17:26:08> [SCP-9406-1 looks at the pages, triggering SCP-9406 multiple times.]

<17:26:13> [SCP-9406-1 notices it, and runs to the door while the walls are shaking, gravity is spinning and light gets divided between light and darkness. As the room crumbles, the door bends forward, up until breaking and being sent outwards. SCP-9406-1 gets out of its containment chamber this way.]

<17:26:29> [After waiting 8 seconds outside of its cell, SCP-9406-1 looks around and runs into a corridor, towards the Site's exit.]

<17:26:42> [Site security finally arrive at SCP-9406-1 location, but are stopped by SCP-9406-1 making shapes with its hands. It first does a circle, triggering -A, stopping anyone around it from walking or running. Then, it does a rhombus, triggering -D, making bullets heal wound instead of penetrating skin. This allows SCP-9406-1 to continue running while another security team is arriving.]

<17:26:59> [As SCP-9406-1 arrives at the checkpoint to get out of Heavy Containment, the reinforcements arrive, but SCP-9406-1 again creates shapes with its hands, the first one being an oval, triggering -G, making firing a gun around 20 times slower, then doing a triangle, amplifying any vibration to the extreme.]

<17:27:05> [Dr. Lacan arrives too while the site's security agents are still trying to fire their guns. Most of the agents have their ears covered in blood as any sound destroys their eardrums.]

<Dr. Lacan (17:27:07)> [Dr. Lacan is trying to talk above the many sounds in the room.] SCP-9406-1! Please stop whatever you are doing right now!

<SCP-9406-1 (17:27:16)> And why… why should I? I just want… I just want to be free… Am I asking too much??

<Dr. Lacan (17:27:24)> Wha- Of course you are! We are trying to keep you out of the public's eye! Please… At least get back here!

<17:27:32> [Cracks are seen forming on the walls.]

<Dr. Lacan (17:27:48)> Get back here! You're gonna get crushed if you stay there!

<SCP-9406-1 (17:27:24)> And what makes you think I don't want that? I can't bear this any longer… This curse… It's just… too much for me… Do you know how hard it is to not even be able to look at myself, or anyone for that matter? Do you know how hard it is to not be able to do what I loved before? Do even know… Do you even know what it is to have a "before"? I ju-

<17:28:09> [The room's ceiling falls, crushing SCP-9406-1 and five other security agents.]



Medical Log 9406-A:

After Incident 9406-C, SCP-9406-1 was found, still alive, even after almost half of its body was crushed by heavy concrete blocks. Below is a list of its injuries and overall medical problems:

  • Complete loss of its right forearm, and partial loss of control over its right shoulder;
  • Complete loss of control over its right leg, and its patella, tibia and fibula are broken;
  • Severe auditory loss;
  • Complete loss of taste and smell;
  • Partial visual loss for its right eye;
  • Severe nerve damage, inflicting pain for any kind of movement;
  • Falls asleep around every 2 hours, going up to 5 hours and 56 minutes, and down to 31 minutes.

As such, SCP-9406-1 must be sustained through IV. This also means SCP-9406-1 cannot move, so any interviews must be done inside of its chamber. The personnel inside its chamber must write down the time when SCP-9406-1 falls asleep, and checks must be done if 3 hours of sleep are exceeded.



Interview Log 9406-C:

Interviewer: Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan
Interviewee: SCP-9406-1

Foreword: This Interview took place 8 days after Incident 9406-C, and was the first Interview since the Incident. During the whole Interview, SCP-9406-1 was looking at the ceiling.

<Begin Log>

Dr. Lacan: Hello SCP-9406-1.

SCP-9406-1: Hello Doc.

Dr. Lacan: Seems like you've gotten a bit more talkative since last time.

SCP-9406-1: Yeah. I've just… gotten to peace with myself.

Dr. Lacan: Oh really?

SCP-9406-1: Well, I've just been thinking since the last incident… and I found that… trying to hope that something will change in me and that this curse will be lifted somehow is just futile. The only thing I can really do is… accepting it.

Dr. Lacan: So you're saying you are accepting your current condition?

SCP-9406-1: It's a peculiar one, but yeah, I do. What can I do anyways? I can't get out of this bed without my entire body screaming in pain, half of my body is already destroyed, and I still have this thing. All I can do is to just… embrace what I currently have.

Dr. Lacan: About that, I may have a little surprise…

<End Log>



Addendum 9406-C: End of Project Sermau:

I, Lead Researcher Lacan, officially and happily say that Project Sermau is finished, as the team created to make a new writing system has finally created one without any shape that could trigger SCP-9406, as the last one also had imperfections, other than having the paper too thin.
After nearly three weeks of teaching, SCP-9406-1 has learned to easily and fluently read this new writing system.
Below is a transcript of SCP-9406-1's first writing with it:

Translation: "HELLO, THIS IS SCP-9406-1. I HOPE YOU CAN READ THIS. THIS IS REALLY COOL! I CAN FINALLY READ AND WRITE THINGS!!"




Footnotes
1. For example, if the shape is in the corner of its view and it doesn't notice it, it won't create any effect.
2. Note that there could be more that have yet to be discovered.
3. Has been tested with one, two and four branches spirals. Square-shaped spirals also seem to trigger this effect.

**SCP-9406-1:** //[SCP-9406-1's head shoots up.]// Wha- Ohh... You... uh... you were talking to me?



**Dr. Lacan:** No worries. I'm only here to ask you some questions about your... //particular// ability.



**SCP-9406-1:** Oh... Well, I... I understood you weren't classic police, with your guys grabbing me out of nowhere and putting me in a... cell. Okay, so... //[SCP-9406-1 pauses for 5 seconds.]// I started having this weird... //thing//... around 5 days before you got me. You know, I... I really liked drawing in my spare time, but whenever I drew some... basic things, my eyes started hurting a little.



**Dr. Lacan:** Was this the only effect that manifested when looking at shapes?



**SCP-9406-1:** For the four next days... I'd say it was... But it started hurting more and more as days went on... On the day you captured me, my eyes had started... er... hurting //a bit// too much. So, I decided to go outside for a small break. A bit of... fresh air, you know? And that's when hell broke loose.



**Dr. Lacan:** I see... Do you have any ideas what could have caused you to get those properties?



**SCP-9406-1:** Uuh, not at all. It was just a... normal day. Worked, drew, slept. Not much of an exciting life... Well except the drawing part, heh...



**Dr. Lacan:** Very well. Thank you for your cooperation. We will work on our side to make your stay here as pleasant as we can.



**<End Log>**

[[/div]]



 _



**Test Log 9406-A:**



**Goal:** To determine what triggers SCP-9406.



||~ Shape Shown ||~ Effect(s) ||~ Note ||

|| Square || To open the testing chamber's door, subjects had to say "Open Sesame" out loud. A keycard wasn't needed anymore. || -B's effects seem to be able to change multiple things at the same time, like here, where it changed how the door and the keycard reader worked. //- Dr. Lacan// ||

|| Square with small rounded corners || Anyone around walls had to put their hand on the closest wall when moving. || We are currently trying to see if changing the shapes by distorting them could negate the effects. Maybe this one wasn't distorted enough? //- Dr. Lacan// ||

|| Same as before, more rounded corners ||= None || As I hypothesized, heavily distorted shapes do not trigger SCP-9406. //- Dr. Lacan// ||

|| Square with curved sides ||= None || We had to try this one multiple times, as having the sides too curved triggered -A, and if they weren't curved enough it triggered -B. //- Dr. Lacan// ||



 _



**Addendum 9406-B: Project Sermau:**



[[div class="blockquote"]]



After 17 days of being in Foundation custody, SCP-9406-1 is starting to show some mental weaknesses. As such, I, Dr. Lacan, have started Project Sermau to prevent it from becoming uncooperative. The goal is as follows:



**1.** Find a language that doesn't require any shape to be written and understood.



**2.** If no language has been found, create a new writing system ourselves, without any shapes that could trigger SCP-9406.



Here is a list of languages/writing systems that **cannot** be used for Project Sermau:



* Any language using the Roman Alphabet: multiple letters contain a circle (o), oval (a) or spiral (s) in them.

* Chinese: multiple symbols like the ones for "moon" (月), "stone" (石) or "room" (间) contain one or multiple rectangles.

* Japanese: multiple symbols like the ones for "su" (す), "nu" (ぬ) or "ro" (ロ) contain rectangles, circles or ovals.

* Korean: multiple symbols like the ones for "milk" (우유), "m" (ㅁ) or "b" (ㅂ) contain one or multiple rectangles or circles.

[[/div]]



 _



**Incident Log 9406-A:**



On November of 2022, during the weekly interview between SCP-9406-1 and Dr. Lacan, SCP-9406-1 inadvertently looked at the interviewer's face, triggering SCP-9406-A, -B, -C and -G at the same time. -B made the two people in the room unable to sit up unless they held each other's hand, -A stopped the light from generating any light, -C made any soundwave grow in volume the more they went through the air, and -G stretched the time it took for SCP-9406-1 to close its eyes, instead taking 174 minutes to close them.



After -A's effects were discovered and both Dr. Lacan and SCP-9406-1 finally stood up, site security quickly arrived and escorted SCP-9406-1 back to its containment chamber, only for it to see an arrow on the floor pointing forward, making all of the guard walk in the same direction for 1 minute, eventually hitting the wall in front of them. 



While walking into the wall, SCP-9406-1 looked up and saw a rhombus on a guard's uniform. This shape triggered SCP-9406-D, making everyone able to walk through closed doors and unable to go through opened doors, leading to a minor breach. SCP-9406-1 was then blindfolded and taken back to its containment chamber, and the aforementioned breach got resolved simply by inverting the doors' system (having them opened at all time and closing them when someone wants to go through).



 _



**Note from Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan:**



[[div class="blockquote" style="background-color:#FFF6D3"]]



 //Though it probably did not make any of this on purpose, it still constitutes a great security risk. As such, all further Interviews will be via microphones, despite the damage it may cause to SCP-9406-1's mental state.//



[[/div]]



 _



**Interview Log 9406-B:**



**Interviewer:** Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan

**Interviewee:** SCP-9406-1



**Foreword:** This Interview took place the day after Incident 9406-A, with SCP-9406-1 still in its chamber, talking by microphone to Dr. Lacan.



[[div class="blockquote"]]

**<Begin Log>**



**Dr. Lacan:** Hello again, SCP-9406-1.



**SCP-9406-1:** Hello...



**Dr. Lacan:** You don't seem really happy to see me.



//[SCP-9406-1 sighs]//



**SCP-9406-1:** Well... seeing all the things I did yesterday, I... I can't really be happy about anything. With all the problems I caused...



**Dr. Lacan:** Hmm, let's say it could have been worse.



**SCP-9406-1:** And now, I can't even talk to you in person? It's just... quite a lot.



**Dr. Lacan:** At least I hope you understand why we put measures like this. It's to prevent the exact problems that happened yesterday.



**SCP-9406-1:** I see... I guess I should be thankful?



**Dr. Lacan:** Moving on. I came here to ask about how you felt in the Foundation.



**SCP-9406-1:** What do you mean by that?



**Dr. Lacan:** Well, we need to know how you feel, to then give you a better stay here.



**SCP-9406-1:** Well... Even if I didn't live here, it wouldn't be good for me, right? Like, at least here I can... walk around, look around my room, sleep knowing I haven't caused //too// much problems, all that... If I instead lived outside, I would need to be... blindfolded to do anything, and being blind for the rest of my life... isn't really something I wanna do.



**Dr. Lacan:** Do you have any goals then? Anything you'd really want?



**SCP-9406-1:** Er... //[SCP-9406-1 pauses for a few seconds.]// Well, what I'd like the most would be being able to draw again. Drawing... drawing really was what anchored me in the world before you... captured me... and before all the weird things happened. I... I could draw hours on end and still feel rested at the end of the day... But now... now I can't really. That... was probably the things I loved the most, so... not being able to do it is rough. Can't do anything about it anyways, right?



**Dr. Lacan:** That is, sadly, exact. Drawing is, and will probably forever be, something that you cannot do without triggering SCP-9406.



**SCP-9406-1:** It was more of a rethorical question... Anyways, that's why I'm really excited about that... "Project" you talked about. Reading will //at least// allow me to do something else other than think about my past life... or about all the things I've done here.



**<End Log>**

[[/div]]



**Note from Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan:**



[[div class="blockquote" style="background-color:#FFF6D3"]]



 //I'd suggest trying to speed up Project Sermau, but being one of the researchers assigned to it, I know we are already overworking ourselves, as we rarely have time to work on it. I simply hope SCP-9406-1 can hold until there.//



[[/div]]



 _



**Incident Log 9406-B:**



Five days after Incident 9406-A, when giving SCP-9406-1 its meal, Junior Researcher L████ also gave it utensiles, once again triggering SCP-9406. The following is the camera footage recovered from one of the cameras in SCP-9406-1's cell:



[[div class="blockquote"]]



**<Begin Log>**



**<12:01:05>** //[The door to the cell opens, Dr. L████ going entering the cell.]//



**<12:01:12>** //[SCP-9406-1 looks at the plate, triggering -A.]]//



**<12:01:20>** //[Dr. L████ drops dead. It is later confirmed that -A stopped Dr. L████'s heart. SCP-9406-1's eyes widen while it slowly walks to the wall at the opposite side of the door.]]//



**<12:01:26>** //[Tears can be seen pouring from SCP-9406-1's eyes.]//



**<12:01:35>** //[SCP-9406-1 notices a knife that fell from the plate. SCP-9406-1 approaches it.]//



**<12:01:45>** //[After taking the knife, SCP-9406-1 looks at it, triggering -C. It is later confirmed that it massively enlarged a spider web outside its containment cell.]//



**<12:02:03>** //[SCP-9406-1 slowly aligns the knife to put it towards its right eye. SCP-9406-1 can be seen shaking.]//



**<12:02:31>** //[Dr. Lacan enters the room with three security agents behind him.]//



**<Dr. Lacan (12:02:35)>** SCP-9406-1, please lower this knife.



**<12:02:38>** //[SCP-9406-1 doesn't seem to answer, instead lowering its eyes, preventing itself from looking towards Dr. Lacan]//



**<Dr. Lacan (12:02:42)>** Please, SCP-9406-1. We are not entirely sure why you want to do //this//, bu-



**<SCP-9406-1 (12:02:56)>** You really... don't understand why? Why I'd pierce my eye? Why I'd risk killing myself? Just look on the ground in front of you. It's a human being. Someone that was doing their job. And they are dead now. Because of me. Because of this... //thing// that I have and that I didn't ask for. Is THAT enough of a reason?



**<Dr. Lacan (12:03:26)>** While I do understand your motive, it still isn't a solution. Do you really think the only way to redeem yourself from killing someone is hurting yourself?



**<SCP-9406-1 (12:03:39)>** So you //didn't// understand what I just said. I don't want do //redeem// myself. I... I just don't want... to have this thing anymore. It just seems childish, or even "normal", but... I ju-... I just don't want to kill anyone. And I just did. I thought I could have that //thing// in me and still live a life I'm somewhat proud of. But this is the event I specifically didn't want to happen because of me. I... I just can't. I can't take it anymore.



**<12:04:21>** //[As SCP-9406-1 was tightening its grip on the knife still in its hands, one of the three security agents fired a sleeping dart, while another one quickly grabbed the knife.]//



[[/div]]



 _



**Note from Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan:**



[[div class="blockquote" style="background-color:#FFF6D3"]]



//This incident should serve as example of why we don't send Junior Researchers to new and dangerous SCPs. I updated SCP-9406's file to only allow personnel at or above Clearance Level 3. Only later did I find out that L████ was sent by the Agent that was supposed to feed SCP-9406-1, because "they felt that this would be valuable experience for Dr. L████".

We should also note that SCP-9406-1's mental state is rapidly deteriorating. Despite all of this, Project Sermau is finally almost finished. It should hopefully improve its mental state.//



[[/div]]



 _



**Incident Log 9406-C:**



Two days after Project Sermau had finished and SCP-9406-1 had started taking classes to learn the new language, SCP-9406-1 got its first book. However, the paper was too thin, and caused the letters at the front and the back to merge. This created multiple shapes, triggering multiple times SCP-9406. In those shapes, 3 circles, 2 triangle, 2 spirals, 2 rhombuses and 1 square were created and perceived by SCP-9406-1. The following is the camera footage recovered from cameras around the Site:



[[div class="blockquote"]]



**<Begin Log>**



**<17:26:08>** //[SCP-9406-1 looks at the pages, triggering SCP-9406 multiple times.]//



**<17:26:13>** //[SCP-9406-1 notices it, and runs to the door while the walls are shaking, gravity is spinning and light gets divided between light and darkness. As the room crumbles, the door bends forward, up until breaking and being sent outwards. SCP-9406-1 gets out of its containment chamber this way.]//



**<17:26:29>** //[After waiting 8 seconds outside of its cell, SCP-9406-1 looks around and runs into a corridor, towards the Site's exit.]//



**<17:26:42>** //[Site security finally arrive at SCP-9406-1 location, but are stopped by SCP-9406-1 making shapes with its hands. It first does a circle, triggering -A, stopping anyone around it from walking or running. Then, it does a rhombus, triggering -D, making bullets heal wound instead of penetrating skin. This allows SCP-9406-1 to continue running while another security team is arriving.]//



**<17:26:59>** //[As SCP-9406-1 arrives at the checkpoint to get out of Heavy Containment, the reinforcements arrive, but SCP-9406-1 again creates shapes with its hands, the first one being an oval, triggering -G, making firing a gun around 20 times slower, then doing a triangle, amplifying any vibration to the extreme.]//



**<17:27:05>** //[Dr. Lacan arrives too while the site's security agents are still trying to fire their guns. Most of the agents have their ears covered in blood as any sound destroys their eardrums.]//



**<Dr. Lacan (17:27:07)>** //[Dr. Lacan is trying to talk above the many sounds in the room.]// **SCP-9406-1! Please stop whatever you are doing right now!**



**<SCP-9406-1 (17:27:16)>** **And why... why should I? I just want...** I just want to be free... **Am I asking too much??**



**<Dr. Lacan (17:27:24)>** Wha- **Of course you are! We are trying to keep you out of the public's eye! Please... At least get back here!**



**<17:27:32>** //[Cracks are seen forming on the walls.]//



**<Dr. Lacan (17:27:48)>** **Get back here! You're gonna get crushed if you stay there!**



**<SCP-9406-1 (17:27:24)>** **And what makes you think I don't want that? I can't bear this any longer... This curse... It's just...** too much for me... **Do you know how hard it is to not even be able to look at myself, or anyone for that matter? Do you know how hard it is to not be able to do what I loved before? Do even know...** Do you even know what it is to have a "before"? I ju-



**<17:28:09>** //[The room's ceiling falls, crushing SCP-9406-1 and five other security agents.]//



[[/div]]



 _



**Medical Log 9406-A:**





[[div class="blockquote"]]



After Incident 9406-C, SCP-9406-1 was found, still alive, even after almost half of its body was crushed by heavy concrete blocks. Below is a list of its injuries and overall medical problems:



* Complete loss of its right forearm, and partial loss of control over its right shoulder;

* Complete loss of control over its right leg, and its patella, tibia and fibula are broken;

* Severe auditory loss;

* Complete loss of taste and smell;

* Partial visual loss for its right eye;

* Severe nerve damage, inflicting pain for any kind of movement;

* Falls asleep around every 2 hours, going up to 5 hours and 56 minutes, and down to 31 minutes.



As such, SCP-9406-1 must be sustained through IV. This also means SCP-9406-1 cannot move, so any interviews must be done inside of its chamber. The personnel inside its chamber must write down the time when SCP-9406-1 falls asleep, and checks must be done if 3 hours of sleep are exceeded.



[[/div]]



 _



**Interview Log 9406-C:**



**Interviewer:** Lead Researcher Dr. Lacan

**Interviewee:** SCP-9406-1



**Foreword:** This Interview took place 8 days after Incident 9406-C, and was the first Interview since the Incident. During the whole Interview, SCP-9406-1 was looking at the ceiling.



[[div class="blockquote"]]

**<Begin Log>**



**Dr. Lacan:** Hello SCP-9406-1.



**SCP-9406-1:** Hello Doc.



**Dr. Lacan:** Seems like you've gotten a bit more talkative since last time.



**SCP-9406-1:** Yeah. I've just... gotten to peace with myself.



**Dr. Lacan:** Oh really?



**SCP-9406-1:** Well, I've just been thinking since the last //incident//... and I found that... trying to hope that something will change in me and that this curse will be lifted somehow is just futile. The only thing I can really do is... accepting it.



**Dr. Lacan:** So you're saying you are accepting your current condition?



**SCP-9406-1:** It's a peculiar one, but yeah, I do. What can I do anyways? I can't get out of this bed without my entire body screaming in pain, half of my body is already destroyed, and I still have this //thing//. All I can do is to just... embrace what I currently have.



**Dr. Lacan:** About that, I may have a little surprise...



**<End Log>**

[[/div]]



 _



**Addendum 9406-C: End of Project Sermau:**



[[div class="blockquote"]]



I, Lead Researcher Lacan, officially and happily say that Project Sermau is finished, as the team created to make a new writing system has finally created one without any shape that could trigger SCP-9406, as the last one also had imperfections, other than having the paper too thin.

After nearly three weeks of teaching, SCP-9406-1 has learned to easily and fluently read this new writing system.

Below is a transcript of SCP-9406-1's first writing with it:

SCP-9408.raw_content:
There's only one story to tell. Tell it with corpses.

NOTICE FROM THE FOUNDATION RECORDS AND INFORMATION SECURITY ADMINISTRATION

This document details a CORPSEBALL related anomaly. For those who are currently unaware, CORPSEBALL is a multiversal sport that connects every Foundation together in a yearly tournament. It is played via two teams of three people, each with a dismembered torso at their "home base", fighting over the limbs and head for their corpse. There are almost no rules, except for reality-bending the corpse. Everything else is fair game.

We organize at least 542 Dimensional Foundation Treaties during these yearly tournaments.

Our home team is Sigma-68. Go CorpseBallers!

— Laila Mahmoud, Head of CORPSEBALL Recordkeeping

Item#: #9408
Level5
Containment Class:
apollyon
Secondary Class:
none

none
