Its progress can only be impeded through maintained but steady use of SCP-9445-1. High mitigation opportunities are to be considered top priorities, however actions and/or events that result in low or medium amounts of mitigation are to be pursued as well. Foundation fronts posing as relevant governmental and non-governmental organizations are to be maintained at all times in order to ensure mitigation levels remain consistent. Memetic, infohazardous, and cognitohazardous triggers are to be disseminated throughout both Foundation personnel unaware of SCP-9445's existence, and the general civilian populace. Additionally, Foundation personnel posing as public or political figures are to attempt to spread the influence of SCP-9445-1 and are permitted to utilize anomalous methods in order to gain more attention and/or supporters.   ---- **Description:** SCP-9445 is the current designation for a violent noospheric phenomenon existing within approximately 60% of the collective human consciousness. Although projections indicate that if SCP-9445 were to be left uncontained, that number could increase to 80%. SCP-9445 is a persistent desire, often unknown to the subject, to accelerate human extinction. Actions taken by affected individuals are typically banal, although still harmful. These can include anything from acts of verbal abuse, to physically harming other individuals, which typically, although not always, spreads the effects of SCP-9445. Analysis conducted by the Department Regulating Engrams and Amnestic Management in 2023 determined that early humans did not actually suffer from any characteristic associated with SCP-9445. It was also determined that initially, humanity was found to almost exclusively cooperate or otherwise take actions that did not hinder each other. The first known appearance of SCP-9445 did not occur until somewhere around 2700 BCE. Although the origins of SCP-9445 are as of yet it unknown, it is currently believed that SCP-9445 does not typically manifest until an individual is around five years of age. Furthermore, an approximated 30% of all affected individuals will commit more severe actions, such as advocating for, or actually attempting to carry out, the termination of large numbers of people, typically through means such as, mass murder, ideological warfare, or by attempts to convince the general populace of perceived threats. It is currently believed that individuals are more susceptible to developing the phenomena by living in high population density areas, interacting, either digitally or physically, with other humans, and by following common social practices regardless of if they harm the collective population or not. Due to the prevalence of both the anomaly, and the actions taken by the population, it is currently believed that humanity will cease to exist within 50 to 100 years. All previous attempts to contain SCP-9445 can be found below: ---- [[div class="rmpostcontainer"]] @@ @@ @@ @@ [[div class="rmpostcontent"]] By the grace of God, Divinely Appointed Lord of the Spiritual Cleanliness Protectorate, protector of the English Empire and all her territories. The following edict, scribed in the year of Lord, 1300, is only to be observed by those a part of the Spiritual Cleanliness Protectorate: Those who read this edict without express consent of any current member of our sacred Foundation are to be executed. Amen. Although we predicted success of our endeavor within the last century, we did not fully comprehend its magnitude. Nevertheless, not only have we been able to prevent a widespread panic, but due to the success of our agent, Aquinas, we have managed to successfully liberate the minds of the educated from this curse. The educated in turn, have spread their teachings to the serfs, who in turn spread these throughout the land. The reduction in overall violence and panic has led our scryers to believe that we may have pushed back our judgement by a number of years. Now, there are two factors that remain constant: our own faith, and the nature of all wars. Should a war soon occur, it is extremely likely that what progress we have made shall be lost. What panic was prevented shall return. Our rinascita[[footnote]] An Italian word meaning "rebirth," or "revival." [[/footnote]], a contingency to attempt to rectify this, is still at least a few hundred years away. Should Man fall victim to sin, it is unlikely that any plans laid will be carried out. We perish in the darkness so that we might serve His light. This our foundation we hold dear. [[/div]] [[/div]] ---- [[include :scp-wiki:component:pages | medium=vintage-book | style= css | contents= 1787 - The following ledger is only to be viewed by members of the Scientific Confederacy of Progress, who have been deemed privy to receiving the following knowledge. If it is determined that he who does not posses proper permission has read this text, he is to be hanged by the neck until dead. Despite our initial success in publishing and disseminating the theory of social contracts from our allied man, who at this time shall only be known as R, we have seen little success in preventing widespread conflicts or the loss of human life. Further, despite our projected losses from the revolutionary period being higher than the number of people killed, we are still cursed by our own nature, and despite the teachings of R, members of the general public are still fully expectant to keep human beings as chattel. Our men, Publius and L, attempted to rectify this during the conflict. However due to the latter's death, and the former's growing unpopularity in our congress and public, it seems unlikely that this barbaric practice will end in the near future. In addition to this failure, we have learned from several trusted sources in France, including but not limited to our men, Babeuf, Chaumette, and the one who wishes to only be known as R The Jacobian, have informed us of growing tensions across the country. Whether or not our country, which is nary past its fetal state, becomes involved remains unclear at present, although it has been determined that any action in France will result in a displacement that will render our current predictions for the end of times, inaccurate at best and completely unfeasible at worst. We must not lose sight of what remains important, our dying in the dark means that man can achieve his Enlightenment. ]] ---- > **1860** > > ---- > > Society for Cruelty Prevention memo. Those who view, reproduce, or read this memo without the express permission of their superior are to be subject to trepanation and/or nullification. > > It has come to light that certain members of our congress are unhappy with changes being made to our constitution and way of life. Although this would not usually be a cause for concern, the belligerents have threatened to leave our fragile union. > > While we cannot abide by their values of allowing human beings to become property, we cannot risk them leaving our country either. Our scholars have theorized that such an action would result in a conflict that would delay our attempts prolonging the inevitable by such a period that the event would instead accelerate. > > This is not the most optimal outcome, nor is it one we can easily recover from. Due to this we have drafted a proposal to maintain what order we have. We did not make this decision lightly, and it sickens us to protect the status quo, but we have come to the conclusion that Lincoln is a threat to our peace. It has been determined that the most efficient method of preventing him from gaining authority is by usurping his seat in the upcoming election. > > Actions are to be taken to ensure the victory of either Douglas, Breckenridge, or Bell. In order to slow the spread of our demise, we are not to pursue violent measures in our venture. Such attempts would likely result in the hastening of our own misery. Additionally propaganda that discredits Lincoln is to be disseminated among the masses. > > Our actions, though extreme, are for the good of all man. We let ourselves die in the dark so that they may live in all light. ---- > **1919:** - interview excerpt.[[footnote]] This interview was initially recorded by means of wax cylinder. Due to the natural degradation of this medium, much of the recorded audio has been lost. What remains has been transcribed. [[/footnote]] > > ---- > > **Dr. Cathcart:** Can you describe experiencing the effects of mustard gas for the first time? > > **PVC Bratton:** I-I was in a trench with around two-dozen other men, I was only on the fringe so I didn't get burned too bad, but I saw the worst of it. People were... coughing up blood, and phlegm, and I think bits of their own guts. I saw a man, his skin was sloughing off his face like wax melting down the side of a candle, crying out with lungs filled with blood. > > There was a boy, maybe only seventeen years, his skin was covered in these awful boils and sores. I seen a man be gangrenous once, but this was so much worse. He cried out for his mama until he could do nothing but cough. Some put their masks on in time, but that didn't help too much, but it did keep it out of their lungs long enough for them to place their guns under their chins. > > When it touched me, my skin was on fire. I had a jacket on, a heavy sort made of canvas, it ate through that like it was paper. I tried to put on my mask but my fingers couldn't hold it. One of my hands still doesn't work right when it gets cold. > > I only survived because someone dragged me away, and took me into a tunnel underneath where the gas wasn't. Even then I could see the other men shambling, bodies decaying before my eyes, barely coherently begging to be killed. > > **Dr. Cathcart:** And yet you lobbed a canister of mustard gas into a Bolshevik trench? Why? > > ---- > > End Log ---- > **1939.** > > ---- > > One recovered film reel found in the basement of a destroyed east German synagogue. > > Film possesses the minor anomalous effects of causing the subject to cry profusely upon completion of the viewing. > > **Film Length:** 40 minutes. > > **Film Contents:** The film opens with a man identified only as Proloff, who is seen chatting with the owner of a small bookstore. Proloff purchases a book but does not read it immediately, nor does he remove the ribbon binding it closed. After exiting the bookstore, a man dressed in brown approaches Proloff and offers him a flyer with a Nordic rune on it before scoffing at the bookshop. The man, although brusque, is friendly to Proloff and offers him a second flyer. Throughout the rest of the film, Proloff visits the bookstore somewhat frequently, and has encounters with similarly dressed men, until one them eventually manages to convince him to attend a meeting with him. > > At the meeting, a tall handsome man in brown explains several concepts to the members, and when he sees that Proloff has not visited before, he invites him onto the stage and offers him a leather-bound book with the same Nordic rune on its cover. Proloff accepts, although his body language suggests that he is uncomfortable with the interaction. > > Proloff later begins to read the book somewhat sporadically, while the book he purchased earlier remains untouched. Soon, he begins attending more meetings while visiting the bookstore less often. His body language throughout these scenes suggest he is becoming increasingly at ease with the interactions. Eventually Proloff stops visiting the bookstore completely, and attends the meetings frequently. > > A posse of the men in brown, including Proloff, organize at night and begin to throw bricks through the windows of several shops and residencies throughout the city. Proloff, is shown to be hesitant about this action and initially refuses to take part in it. This is until the posse reaches the bookstore, Proloff is handed a brick and instructed to throw it. He once again hesitates and is struck across the face. Proloff raises the brick and aims it at the man who struck him, before the camera focuses on the Nordic rune on the man's jacket, which Proloff is now wearing on his clothing. Proloff grips the brick tighter, but instead of striking his attacker with it, he throws it through the window of the bookstore. > > The final scene of the film is of the posse and several additional men throwing books into a large fire. Proloff is holding the book he bought at the start of the film and immediately throws it into the fire. The final shot of the film is the book beginning to burn before the camera centers on Proloff. Proloff is grinning. > ---- > **1966** > > ---- > > Recovered diary entry from US Marine. Name unknown. > > ---- > > We found them hiding in a straw hut, the kind you might see in a Nat Geo film. They were scared, young. Fuck, I think one of them was barely out of his teens. They begged in a language I didn't understand. I didn't want to do it, but I marched them out of the hut and lined them in the village center. Me and everyone else. > > My commander, real sonnuva bitch named Walther, he asked them if they were pink? Their response was to sob profusely. I had as much idea of what they were saying, as I do of what the surface of Mars looks like. But I knew from their tone, the way they clasped their hands together, and those awful ragged sobs that they were praying. For my mercy? Walther's? God's? I guess it doesn't matter now. > > Walther looked at all of us and then told us to "do it." O'Hannigan was first, scrawny kid from the Bronx with glasses pushed up to his nose. Last night he was showing me a Superman comic his folks sent him. At the time I thought he was a likable sort if not a bit spacey. Now, he was pressing the barrel of his rifle against an old man's head and making eye contact as he fired. > > Noakes was next. This Black man who shared a bunk with me, nice guy honestly, shares his smokes. He had this tattoo on his arm, kept it hidden but I saw it in the showers, three arrows in a circle in a weird sort of triangle shape, I asked him about and he said it was just a fraternity from college, and he got defensive when I pushed it further. Still he's a pretty groovy man, he taught me his "unbreakable" poker strategy. Now he was breaking a young woman's skull open like a ripe pumpkin. > > The two other men, I didn't know their names, that doesn't matter. One seemed distant, like he didn't want to do it, but did it anyway. The other? I think the bastard might've been grinning. > > When it was my turn, I put my rifle down and closed my eyes. I felt Walther grip my shoulder, not in a fatherly way either, he barked in my face that either I put a bullet between the commie's eyes or he would do it to me. I looked at O'Hannigan but he pretended to not see me. Noakes tried to say something, but Walther barked at him that if he didn't have to listen to him in the States, he didn't have to listen to him here. Walther turned to me, he said, "You have one chance before I do it for you." > > I pressed my rifle against the young man's head, he wasn't much older than me, maybe a couple years... he didn't scream. He didn't beg. He didn't yell that I was gonna burn for this. That was the worst part, he didn't say anything. He just looked down at the ground and let his tears run down his face. Walther shouted at me to fire. I'm so sorry mama, your little boy is going to Hell. > ---- > **1974**[[footnote]] NOTE: Portions of this text were heavily redacted, crudely, but completely scratched out, or were otherwise illegible. What remains has been transcribed. [[/footnote]] > > ---- > > SCP Foundation Department of Abnormalities. > > Best intentions. > > Underground. > > Bill and Bernadine no longer take orders. > > No peace. Only violence. > > Extinction nears. ---- > **1988** > > Diary page found in the ruins of a house. > > Text has been translated from Arabic. > > ---- > It was Aaliyah's idea, of course it was her idea, it's always her idea. > > She woke me up early this morning and said she wanted candy. She showed me the money she had hidden in her purse, lots of coins that she found around the house, or by running errands for the neighbors. > > I told her to go back to bed and Father or Uncle could take us to the market when they wake up. She shook her head and told me that she didn't want to go to the market, she wanted to go to the city. > > I called her a fool and said that we weren't allowed in the city, at least not without Father. She told me that she was not a fool, and that if I didn't go with her then she would go alone and tell Father that I let her go alone. I asked her what if we got caught or encountered the oppressors? She said she had a plan for the oppressors but wouldn't tell me what she meant. > > That did it, I said I would go with her. It was stupid, but I didn't know what else to do. We made it out of the village easy enough, Naeem gave us a ride out in his car. We told him that we needed to run an errand in the city for our parents. He told us that to be very careful and that soldiers that worked for "them" were patrolling earlier. > > We walked through the city but most people paid us no mind, it was easy, at first. We made it to the candy store, and the owner scoffed at us and asked if we had money. Aaliyah said that we did. He said fine, but to keep our hands out of our pockets and that if we stole even one piece he'd tell the authorities. > > Aaliyah wanted to call him a name, but I told her to be quiet, we were close to getting our candy, the one thing we left the village for. She agreed and picked out what she wanted, a couple of lollipops, some boiled sweets, and a chocolate bar. She poured her coins out on the counter, and the man told her she didn't have enough for the chocolate bar, and that she needed one more coin. She said that she heard children say that they didn't need to pay full price, he said that those children followed different rules because they weren't... "dirty". > > Aaliyah got that look on her face that she wanted to do something, but I squeezed her arm and she sighed and paid for what candy she could afford instead. We left, and walked through the streets, Aaliyah's purse now filled with the candy she bought, yet she struggled with it as if it weighed more than a car. I didn't know why at the time. > > We walked to the city center where I still had a coin so that we could use the phone to call Naeem. As I was about to enter the phone booth, a hand grabbed my shoulder and turned me around. I saw three men wearing green uniforms, with their flag on the arms. Two were around Uncle's age, but the other couldn't have been older than Cousin Rashid was when he left for university. That one smiled at us, and tried to look reassuring. > > The soldiers led us away from the phone booth and into an alley. They started by asking our names, and Aaliyah was too scared to answer, but I answered for her. They asked how old we were? I said that I was 10, and that Aaliyah was 7. They asked what we were doing alone? Aaliyah mumbled something, and one of the men told her to speak up. I answered for her that we were buying candy. They laughed at this, but the younger one said that he believed us. > > They asked us if anyone knew we were here alone? I lied and said that Father, Uncle, and Naeem did. One of them jabbed the younger man in the side, and he asked us what Father, Uncle, and Naeem did as jobs? I said that Father is a builder, Uncle is also a builder, and Naeem is a driver. They asked if anyone told us to deliver any packages anywhere and I said no. The younger man said that we were okay, and told the other two that they should leave. > > I thought we were clear... until the lead one asked to see in Aaliyah's purse. She didn't want to hand it over, but I told her to give it to them. There was nothing in there but her school supplies, and her candy. > > The man reached in and rustled around in there before he removed an object that I had only seen a couple times at home: Father's gun. > > I looked to the younger man but he now had an expression of disgust and looked away from me, mumbling about how we were all rotten. > > The man with the purse asked Aaliyah what she intended to do with it? I tried to answer for her, to tell him that I didn't know that it was in there, that Father never even keeps it loaded, but he barked at me to be quiet before I could say anything, and scowled at me when I tried to speak again. He asked her again what she was going to do with it? Aaliyah said that she was going to use it on "bad men." The man's face grew dark, and he asked her what a bad man was? She said that Father said that the bad men were the men who would always take, and beat people, and murder. Oppressors. People like him. > > He started by taking the gun from her. Then he started beating her. She cried for me, and I tried to run to her, but the man behind me held me back and threatened to beat me too. She screamed, but nobody came. I tried to look away, but they pushed my head forward. I looked past her instead, past the crowd that didn't care, and into the building across the street. From one the windows, I saw two people watching. They were wearing the white coats of doctors, but the coats had this strange shape on them, these three arrows in a circle all pointing inwards. All they did was watch. > > It felt like hours before the man stopped, then they left, and didn't even stop to look at us. I was terrified, but still I ran to her. She was bleeding everywhere, and wasn't moving. She didn't make any noise, but I could still see her breathing. I picked her up, my knees straining, she was so heavy, so limp. > > I called Naeem to take us home, and told him what happened. He looked so sick. He told us we did nothing wrong, we couldn't have known this would happen. He put Aaliyah in the back, and let her lie down as he drove us home. She was still by the time we reached our house. I have never seen Father cry before.    ---- > **1997** > >  Note Found on Foundation Junior Researcher's Desk. > > ---- > > Oslo was a mess. > > What made us think we could solve the issue? > > What made us think it could solve any issue? > > Don't know when it's gonna happen. > > Drown my sorrows before it drowns me. > > I did my best, Aaliyah, I'm sorry. ---- > **2010** - O5-4's suicide note. > > ----- > > New York, 2001. > > Moscow, 2002. > > Morocco, 2003. > > London, 2005. > > Mumbai, 2008. > > Nigeria, 2009. > > We are beasts, and we are fucked. ---- **Addendum:** On 10/12/24, following projections of SCP-9445's current model, both the O5-Council and Ethics Committee voted to institute the Rousseau Protocol, henceforth designated SCP-9445-1, which is intended to slow the spread of SCP-9445 and possibly even neutralize it, should the overall situation permit it. SCP-9445-1 has currently gone into effect both throughout Foundation facilities, and the civilian populace. As per the protocol's mandate, memetic triggers and images have been implanted into various pieces of media, popular culture, and advertisements. Additionally, several Foundation created fictional works and/or characters have been subconsciously implanted in key members of the populace in order to maintain levels congruent with SCP-9445-1 projections. A brief excerpt from SCP-9445-1's mandate can be found below. > **Rousseau Protocol: Page 16/40** > >As outlined on page 12, in order to maintain full control of the population, Foundation officials have been ordered to fabricate, either through amnestic or otherwise anomalous means, fictitious events that facilitate rapid production of dopamine and/or serotonin. Such events are not to consist of more than 100 individuals and are to appear repeatable should the population desire to enact them. > > Additionally cognitohazardous phrases and triggers that encourage reciprocity and actions in opposition to animus are to be implanted naturally within civilian populations in excess of 50,000 individuals. To this end, mitigation percentages gained from this that range between 5-8% are to be considered both valid and successful. > > Measures to prevent small to medium scale conflicts are detailed more extensively on page 17, however, personnel should note that conflicts of this nature are not to be avoided, and memetic messages which are in line with the Jus In Bello theory, in addition to the Geneva Protocol, are to be propagated throughout both non-Foundation civilian and military personnel.   > > Although armed conflicts involving anomalous means are still a concern, negotiations involving the Serpent's Hand, the Horizon Initiative, and the Global Occult Coalition are on-going in order to prevent and/or mitigate this. Full descriptions of this can be found on page 18. > >Furthermore, logs are to be maintained at all times in order to accurately gauge the amount of mitigation generated and actions taken that result in positive mitigation. Due to the nature of the anomaly personnel are instructed to write their logs in the first person and are to allow other personnel to read them in order to ascertain opportunists for mitigation, and to formally adjudicate fellow personnel. > > __**NOTICE:**__ All actions taken by Foundation personnel in line with the Rousseau Protocol are to be conducted with genuine intent. Performative actions and/or actions intended to generate discussion without sufficient societal alternations, are not to be attempted as they do not result in mitigation, and are thus a misuse of time and resources. > > [[size 60%]]Primary Writer: Nicholas Klaus, Ethics Committee Member. Foundation Site: 029.  Date: January 5th, 2025.[[/size]] ---- [[collapsible show=" SCP-9445-1 Rousseau Protocol Logs" hide="- Close"]] > **Subject:** Researcher Sunderland. > > **Mitigation Percentage:** 0.5% > > **Estimated SCP-9445 Delayment:** one minute > > **Method:** "When Researcher Woods thought everyone forgot her birthday, and I surprised her with a cake." ---- > **Subject:** Dr. Stanhope. > > **Mitigation Percentage:** 0.09% > > **Estimated SCP-9445 Delayment:** One second > > **Method:** "My son had the flu, so I stayed home from work and read Wizard of Oz and Percy Jackson to him until he fell asleep." ---- > **Subject:** Dr. Ibrahim Abadi. > > **Mitigation Percentage:** 1% > > **Estimated SCP-9445 Deylayment:** Five minutes > > **Method:** "My wife asked me if I had thought of a name to give our daughter? I said I wanted to name her Aaliyah." ---- > **Subject:** Ethics Committee Liaison Zarah Chang. >   > **Mitigation Percentage:** 1.5% > > **Estimated SCP-9445 Delayment:** seven minutes > > **Method:** "When Kathy needed help with her makeup for the first time, and smiled when I showed her how to zip her fancy dress." > ---- > **Subject:** Ethics Committee Member Kristine Klaus. > > **Mitigation Percentage:** 0.9% > > **Estimated SCP-9445 Delayment:** One and a quarter minutes > > **Method:** "The night I visited my daughter at work and brought her flowers. She and I got dinner at TGI Friday's, we talked, and then I cried." [[/collapsible]] ---- **Addendum II:** It is currently believed that at the current rate of mitigation SCP-9445's effects will be delayed by approximately one year. However projections indicate that with continued success of the Rousseau Protocol, SCP-9445's effects could be delayed by up to 100 years. In order to achieve this, personnel are instructed to continue to act with forbearance and benignity. Liberal projections from the Rousseau Protocol indicate that should this appear as a global pattern, SCP-9445's effects could be delayed by at least 1000 years. ---- [[footnoteblock]] [[div class="footer-wikiwalk-nav"]] [[=]] << [[[SCP-9444]]] | SCP-9445| [[[SCP-9446]]] >> [[/=]] [[/div]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box |author= Y0ssarian]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]] ----

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9448 is to be kept in its containment chamber at all times. The door to the chamber must be locked to prevent access to the active D-Class being restrained, as well as to SCP-9448 itself. The door to the chamber is to be locked behind a keycard door that can only be accessed by a member with, at minimum, restricted access.

There are to be no light sources in the containment room other than SCP-9448. There are also to be no windows into the adjacent observation room. There is to be one camera placed in the far corner of the room, facing the wall opposite the active D-Class, monitoring the active light level from a camera feed in the adjacent observation room.

Attached to the host is a tube from the ceiling running along the wall to the restraint for the host. Running through the tube is sustenance for the active D-Class to maintain the necessary physical and mental state. The access point for the tube can be accessed from the observation room.

After the light level in the room drops below the specified threshold, expiration of the active D-Class (signified "host") is imminent. At this time, the security detail is to be prepped for the transfer protocol.

Under the guidance of Dr. Maxwell, two guards will retrieve the next selected D-Class (signified "replacement") and transport them to the outside of the chamber. The guards provided will be trained with 100 hours of simulation within a replica room to conduct this transfer without sight. On retrieval of the replacement, a device forcing their eyes to remain open will be fastened to their head, a central IV line will be inserted, and an NG tube will be placed. The replacement will have their hands and feet bound to prevent attempts at escaping. The guards will be blindfolded with three layers of cloth and a blackout helmet placed onto their heads to prevent any possibility of sight during host replacement.

Upon bringing the replacement into the chamber, they will seat the replacement in the provided chair next to the host. The guards will latch and restrain the replacement into the chair, connecting the tube from the ceiling to their NG tube, permanently sealing the replacement to their chair. On completion of restraining the replacement, the guards will await instruction from the control room that the room has gone completely dark, signifying the completion of SCP-9448 cycle. During this time, the host will scream and thrash with agony, with varied additional reactions that vary among the hosts, such as hallucinations, verbal interactions with an invisible entity, or severe psychosis related symptoms. With acknowledgement of total darkness and cessation of signs of life from the host, the guards will unhook and remove the now deceased host from their restraints and remove them from the room, locking the replacement within the confines of the chamber.

The guards will be administered short-term amnestics for mental stability due to the psychological impact of the death of the host during the transfer. This procedure will be documented as a success upon observation of light within the room from SCP-9448 at sunrise the following day, signifying the completion of containment. With successful containment, the replacement is classified as the host, replacing the previous host; continue to monitor the host’s state until the light level drops below the specified threshold again.

Description: SCP-9448 is an orange, tall taper candle. It burns with a scent of strong vanilla, which resides in a white porcelain candlestick, housed at Site-811. When first reformed, the anomaly stands at 30.48 cm upon reforming and relighting, and burns at a rate of .3463 cm daily when not being observed by the host, rounded to .35 cm for ease, lasting exactly 88 days.

When the host is observing the anomaly, it slows its burning rate significantly. If the host does nothing but observe the anomaly, it would burn for one full year from the day it is relit. Under natural conditions, however, it would be impossible to achieve this number due to human bodily functions, as well as the anomalous effects of SCP-9448 prior to the host's death.

SCP-9448 has no outwardly anomalous effects except on the host, other than its extremely slow burning rate and inability to be extinguished through various means; further descriptions of these attempts are listed in the addenda 9448-4. It can only affect one person at a time, deemed “the host” of the anomaly. The host is determined by the person who actively observes it as it goes out. Upon sunrise, the following morning, the wax of SCP-9448 will reform into its original shape and relight, starting the timer for the new host.

Upon completion of the cycle, signified by the anomaly completely burning out, the active host will die; the means of their death is determined by the amount of time the host observed the candle to slow its rate of burning. The longer the host observed the anomaly, the more graphic and anomalous the deaths become.

  • Not observing the anomaly at all/fleeting glances toward the anomaly
    • Stage 1 - Duration of burning: 88 days
  • The host becomes highly exhausted to the point of an inability to remain awake and falls into a state of comatose, starting 10 hours before the completion of SCP-9448's cycle. Within their coma, they suffer a sudden and irreversible cardiac event that ceases all function of their heart, leading to instantaneous death.
  • Observing the anomaly irregularly
    • Stage 2 - Duration of burning: Extended to 3-6 months
  • The host will suddenly go blind 5 minutes before the completion of SCP-9448’s cycle. The host will also lose all mechanical function and begin to convulse as they fall into a seizure. During which they will foam at the mouth before falling into a motionless state. At this time, their lungs will rapidly fill with blood and foam, suffocating the host.
  • Observing SCP-9448 regularly/devoting time to observing it burn
    • Stage 3 - Duration of burning: Extended to 6-9 months
  • At 24 hours before the completion of SCP-9448’s cycle, the host will complain of hearing voices and seeing shadows move out of the corner of their eyes. When asked to describe, the host specified that the voices are largely incoherent, and the shadows can never be viewed directly, but are always just out of sight. At 10 minutes to the completion of SCP-9448's cycle, the host will become entirely catatonic, unable to move, as the object's anomalous effects cause the host’s body to enter an intense hyperactive state, wherein the host’s body will begin to cannibalize its muscles and skin. Active brain scans of the host show that while catatonic, they are entirely aware and alive throughout this process. In the host's final moments, the catatonia will cease, and their motor function will be briefly regained, starting at their vocal cords. The host will scream in agony, followed by a plea to what is described as a shadow forming in the center of their vision. Descriptions of the shadow vary from host to host. From pleas of the host, the shadow is presumed to speak one final time, and upon hearing its words, the host will immediately cease all cerebral function as their brain stem is instantaneously severed by an unknown force. All attempts at forcing the D-Class into relaying those final words have been met with failure. No shadows or alterations in light level are recorded within the chamber.
  • Observing the anomaly from ignition to completion
    • Stage 4 - Duration of burning extended to 1 year.
  • Stage 4.1 - After one full week of doing nothing but observing the anomaly burn, the host will develop an extreme desire to divert or close their eyes to cease all contact with it. After one month, hallucinations begin pulling at the edges of their vision, described as yelling in an attempt to pull the host's attention away from the anomaly.
  • Stage 4.2 - Nearing 3 months, the hallucinations worsen, beginning to manifest visually within the host’s field of view, making futile attempts at pulling the host's vision away from the object. They are described as reaching out to physically pull the host's eyes away from it. Observations from active brain scans, however, do indicate there is no physical interaction on the host while these manifestations occur.
  • Stage 4.3 - Nearing 6 months, the host develops a form of fascination with the anomaly. The muscular function of any appendage below the neck entirely ceases; subsequently, any ticks, nervous coping mechanisms, or self-soothing exercises the host was able to perform in their restraints cease. Active brain scans show that the host's brain is in a constant state of hyperactivity, coupled with a lack of sleep, which causes the brain to begin consuming itself in a form of “relief.” Note this level of self-consumption would be entirely life-altering to the point of comatose or death, but it appears that at this level, SCP-9448 keeps the host not only alive, but aware and functioning enough to be able to speak ,and to some degree, think. According to the host, the hallucinations are now able to interact with the environment and communicate with one another. Supposedly casting shadows within the room. Observations of the wall where the camera in the room is angled to see show no significant change in light level that a shadow in the room would cause. Cerebral function begins to show signs of deterioration at this time, due to the host's brain's self-consumption, manifesting in incessant rambling, speaking directly to the hallucinations, dementia, perceptual reality shifts, and extreme depersonalization.
  • Stage 4.4 - Nearing 9 months, hallucinations end, and the anomaly now “speaks to” the host. The host regains sudden and immediate full cerebral function, but only to hold “conversations” with the anomaly itself. In between the “conversations,” the host continues to rapidly digress mentally: their only moments of lucidity are when “conversing” with the anomaly, now no longer having any desire to look away from it. These “conversations” seem to start by ranging from topics that one would hold with friends, lovers, parents, rivals, or those that the Foundation has identified from the host's past.
  • Stage 4.5 - Nearing 1 year, the “conversations” evolve into deep, philosophical questions upon the meaning of life, the purpose of humans in our relation to all life on Earth, how we fit in the universe, and if our existence is a burden to “the light that burns inside all living beings.” It is worth noting that the previous phrase is consistent between all hosts that make it to this point. Any following “conversations” with SCP-9448 exclusively surround the topic of time. The time they wasted, what they could have done instead, running through a seemingly infinite amount of possibilities, at the end of every string of thoughts, the host seemingly waits for a response back from SCP-9448. There is no noise coming from the room when the host is not talking, except for labored breathing from the host, and there is no noticeable change in light level in the room that could be interpreted as a response.
  • Stage 4.6 - On the 51st week, the hallucinations seem to brutally return, as the host seemingly argues with multiple invisible shadows and SCP-9448 itself. No arguments from this point on are coherent, and any attempts at deciphering meaning from them are fruitless. The host begins to fear for their life, pleading to the anomaly. Their pleas include things like the argument that “they have done everything right” and “What more do you want from me?” The host’s emotional state is constantly fluctuating between panic, mania, and severe depression up to their final day. On the final day, the host enters a catatonic state, sitting motionless, blankly staring at the flame of the anomaly. This state of catatonia remains until the final minute of the host's life, and subsequently the final minute of the cycle. During this final minute, every symptom possible seems to hit the patient at once. Violent seizures occur, and even though the host is restrained, they tense and thrash with enough force to tear their muscles, tendons, and bones. The host’s internal organs rapidly fail and break down at a cellular level. Causing the epithelial lining protecting the esophagus, stomach, and intestines to deteriorate, its acidic contents rapidly dissolve the gastrointestinal tract. This leads to severe and intense vomiting and bloody diarrhea. The object seems to enhance the acidic quality of the host during this event anomalously, causing further erosion of all internal organs, including the skin, melting the host from the inside. These effects anomalously only alter the patient from the neck down, allowing their head, brain, and eyes to remain transfixed on the flame. The host screams in agony as they begin to "melt." Through this grueling process, the host is awake and conscious, and making every effort not to lose sight of the anomaly at any point. The host finally passes as their brain ruptures from within their skulls, ending their life. It is in these final moments of the host’s suffering that the camera inside the chamber of SCP-9448, discrepancies can be seen in the form of shadows cast upon the wall. These alterations are slight and hardly noticeable; it is unclear if they are caused by the flickering of the now-dying flame or are some anomalous force cast by the anomaly. Despite the trauma, the host’s eyes remain perfectly intact throughout this event.

Autopsies: Autopsies on what’s left of the now deceased hosts show a seared, inverted engraving of SCP-9448’s flame on the back of their eyes. The engraving chars through the host’s optic nerves and macula, permanently scarring the detached eye.

It is unclear to the Foundation what exactly the anomalous side effects of SCP-9448 are, what side effects are caused by the extreme isolation, prolonged viewing of one object, and the lack of sensations other than the strong smell of vanilla. It is noted that the constant viewing of SCP-9448 allows the host to survive largely unaffected by the normal effects of extreme, extended sleep deprivation, but only when consistently viewing SCP-9448.

The researchers tasked with managing the containment of SCP-9448 understand the barbarity of the current containment procedures, but have deemed it to be the most effective method of containing it currently. Efforts to find an alternative are being considered, but due to more pressing concerns, have been pushed to the back of the list of priorities in Site-81.

Initial Recovery
Initial Recovery

On June 26th, 2007, the Foundation got notice of a supposed “crazed cult leader” that had been detained by local law enforcement. The reports claimed that an “off-the-map” village had been discovered when the "cult leader" eventually stumbled into the nearest town. Supposedly, the cult, with the exception of the leader, had all been wiped out and buried in a mass grave with bodies dating back to 1990.

The Foundation took notice of the reports as the “cult leader” claimed that the deaths had all been caused by “the candle.” He claimed “The Candle” had betrayed him and his people, and that "they had done everything right", yet "The Candle" would still take him. Upon reaching the site of the village, a small collection of seemingly poorly built houses and a church, the Foundation discovered the mass grave, where they were able to make a count of 62 bodies buried at the location, some seeming to be as recent as the past 3 months, with potential remains of others scattered near the mass burial.

Upon exploring the worn-down church in the village, the Foundation came across what they believed the cult leader was referencing by “The Candle.” On the pulpit of the church was a standard pillar-style candle. It had a deep red coloration and was seated upon a golden offering plate, likely used while the church was still in commission. It had about .18 cm of wax left and was burning at what appeared to be a significantly slow pace.

The recovery team members took the offering plate and SCP-9448 out of the building and were attempting to lock it in the back of a mock patrol car for transportation to the nearest Foundation site when one of the members of the recovery team, who was actively securing it in the back, claimed the candle ran out of wax and burned out entirely. It was later determined that at this exact time, the “cult leader,” who had moments prior gone catatonic, died in the custody of police by “rapid muscle deterioration”, screams, pleas to an entity not visible to the officers on scene, and finally followed by an instantaneous severing of his brain stem. (This death would now be classified as a stage 3 death from the anomaly) SCP-9448 was brought to Site-81 for further inspection. The police were administered amnestics, and the foundation wiped all records of the cult leader’s arrest as well as the village as a whole.

Once in a containment room at Site-81, a camera was placed in the room to observe the anomaly for further surveillance, and the retrieval team member who witnessed the candle go out was tested for potential anomalous effects, where none were found. Upon sunrise the following day, June 23, the anomaly was observed through the security camera to reform, the wax in the offering plate re-shaping into the original pillar-style candle before it had burned out. The anomaly was now burning at what appeared to be a fairly slow pace once again.

Initial Recovery

.

Incident Report - Dr. Simon
Incident Report - Dr. Simon

On the morning of September 19, 2007, exactly 88 days after the initial relighting of the anomaly, Dr.Simon was observing the candle as it was nearing burning out. After about thirty minutes of observing the candle through the camera placed in the room and taking notes on its state every 5 minutes through audio recordings, the candle simply burned out. Its wax pooled at the bottom of the offering plate as the flame died out. Dr. Simon waited in the observation room for another 26 minutes to see if it would have any additional reaction; the only noted change was a hardening of the wax as it cooled.

After waiting in the room for a bit longer, two other researchers entered the room to speak with Dr. Simon, informing him that the transportation unit member who originally witnessed the flame extinguish had passed out and then died due to a heart attack in his unconscious state while on temporary leave due to recent lightheadedness. (Now classified as a stage 1 death from the anomaly)

At this point, Dr.Simon, as well as the other researchers, concluded via consistencies surrounding the deaths of the “cult leader” and the containment team agent related to the anomaly time of completion. Realizing that observing it as it goes out is what links a person to it, and subsequently, had placed a timer on Dr. Simon's life. After taking a week off to think, Dr. Simon requested the use of amnestics to forget about the incident entirely and was placed on indefinite leave to spend time with his family.

Incident Report - Dr. Simon

Initial Containment
Initial Containment

Over the next two months, the Foundation prepped for a D-Class to take the place as the next host of the anomaly following Dr. Simons' death. On the day of Dr. Simons' 88th day, a D-Class was sent into the containment room and instructed to observe the candle as it burned out.

The Foundation would allow the D-Class access to entertainment in the room as well as three meals a day. The D-Class would not be allowed to directly interact with the anomaly, as it was placed on a podium in the corner of the room. Once SCP-9448 was nearing its cycle completion and the D-Class was soon to die, security personnel would escort them out of the room and into a private room. At this same time, another set of security personnel would send a new D-Class into the room to observe the candle as it burned out. Upon the re-ignition of the candle the following sunrise, containment was considered a success.

Initial Containment

.

Testing
Testing

The foundation attempted multiple tests on SCP-9448 over the course of the next few cycles. These tests would be run over its “safe period.” Attempts were made to alter its shape, size, burn rate, or even extinguish it entirely. Some attempts to attempt to alter the relationship between the host and the anomaly were also made.

Test 9448-1
Subject SCP-9448
Protocol Researchers will attempt to extinguish the flame using various methods, such as a spray bottle, pouring water from a large container onto the anomaly, and fully submerging the anomaly.
Results Despite the various attempts from researchers, the anomaly did not seem to be affected by any form of dousing the flame. Whether it was sprayed, doused, or submerged, it would simply continue burning. Even while fully submerged, the flame did not alter in size, shape, or change the rate of the burn, even when submerged for 24 hours.
Test 9448-2
Subject SCP-9448
Protocol Researchers will attempt to completely cut off oxygen to the anomaly by placing it in a vacuum chamber on site. After placing it in the vacuum chamber, it is to be sealed and monitored through a camera also in the chamber, as well as checked for any alterations once removed.
Results Despite being placed in the vacuum chamber and having all oxygen stripped from its container, it continued to burn. Its flame once again did not change in size or shape, and there was no alteration in the rate of burn, whether while in the vacuum chamber or once removed.
Test 9448-3
Subject SCP-9448
Protocol Researchers will attempt to extinguish the anomaly by various methods, such as blowing on it, using an industrial fan to attempt to blow it out, and finally placing it where natural wind would cause it to extinguish.
Results Despite researchers blowing on the object, placing it in front of an industrial fan, and even allowing it to be placed outside, all in an attempt to extinguish the anomaly before the 88 days of its natural cycle, these attempts were all met with failure. There was once again no change in size and shape, and there was no alteration in burn speed.
Test 9448-4
Subject SCP-9448's host
Protocol Researchers will give amnestics to the new host of the anomaly; they will also prepare a new D-Class to take their place on the 88th day should the anomalous properties continue.
Results Once the host had been established, they were given amnestics to forget about the anomaly entirely. They were barred from interacting with any other testing and were monitored for 88 days, during which no anomalous effects were observed. Regular health and mental checks were conducted on the host, to which no noticeable changes were observed. On the 88th day at the end of the cycle, the host experienced a class 1 death, and a new D-Class was prepped and observed the anomaly burning out in the event that the anomalous properties continue. Upon sunrise the next day, SCP-9448 relit, and the cycle continued as normal.
Test 9448-5
Subject SCP-9448
Protocol Researchers will attempt to cut pieces from the wax body of the anomaly using a scalpel, use a metal sheet to completely sever it wax body both horizontally and vertically, and finally use a D-Class to simply touch the anomaly with their hands.
Results In researchers' attempts to use a scalpel to slice small pieces off of the anomaly's wax body, the anomaly would seem to form around the scalpel. Researchers documented that there was zero friction, as if they were not cutting through anything at all. Once a cut was made, that should have taken a piece off, there would simply be no change in it. Upping the measures, researchers took a larger metal sheet and attempted to completely sever the anomaly in half, both vertically and horizontally. Both of these attempts were met with a similar result to the scalpel; there was no friction, and despite being visually completely severed, the candle continued to burn as normal, and the wax body seemed to ignore the metal sheet entirely. Finally, when a D-Class was ordered to touch the object gently, having no knowledge of what it was and simply believing it to be a candle, the D-Class was actually able to touch and interact with it somewhat normally. He gently touched its waxy body, and it would rock in its place. When instructed to knock it over, however, the D-Class's hand phased through it, similar to the scalpel and sheet of metal. When the D-Class was instructed to pick it up gently, they were able to; however, when instructed to attempt to crush it in their hand, it then phased through the D-Class's hand, falling to the ground, unharmed and unaltered.
These results seem to indicate that the anomaly has some inherent knowledge of the intent of the interactions it has. If the intent is not to harm or alter it in any way, it will allow itself to be touched, moved, or even held. However, if the intent changes to attempt to alter it, it then seems to act defensively and makes whatever is going to cause the change simply phase through it.
Test 9448-6
Subject SCP-9448's host
Protocol Researchers will take a class IV D-Class that has been made host, and subject them to lethal injection, prepping another
D-Class to take their place as the next host in the event of
the anomaly extinguishes early upon the death of the host.
Results The researchers had the potential new host observe the anomaly as the final, lethal dose was given to the active host. The candle burned normally until around 2 seconds before the brain death of the host. Reported by the new host watching the anomaly, it was in these two seconds that the flame grew in size significantly, to the point that the new host referred to it as a "fireball." The flame was large enough and hot enough to melt the rest of the unburned wax in the final 2 seconds prior to the active host's brain death.
Test 9448-7
Subject SCP-9448's replacement
Protocol Researchers will attempt to tie the "host" status to a nonsentient creature; in the case of the tests, this was a stray cat and a stray dog. This will be performed in tandem with standard containment procedures to prevent potential risks of failure leading to a containment breach.
Results During the designation of a new host, another group of personnel held a stray cat up to also observe the anomaly as it extinguished. By measuring the burning rate of the candle when the cat observed it afterwards, it was deemed not to be the host, and the host had been transferred to the D-Class who observed it extinguish instead. During the next cycle, this test was repeated with a stray dog to see if the anomaly simply "chose" the person instead of the cat during the first test; however, the same results were obtained. Researchers deemed it was possible that SCP-9448 happened to "choose" the person as the host both times, and this test could result in a transfer of the host to a non-sentient animal; it was deemed unnecessary to continue trying.
Testing

.

Inconsistencies
Inconsistencies

Over the next cycles of SCP-9448, a few inconsistencies were noted by research staff, specifically with the length of time that it burned before burning out.

After instructing the active host to observe the anomaly for 20 minutes daily. This resulted in it burning at a slower rate while being actively observed by the host. When another D-class was sent into the room and instructed to observe the anomaly, no change in burning rate was observed.

Since this discovery, the host was instructed to continue observing the anomaly actively for 20 minutes a day, eventually pushing his life span to 142 days. The host’s death, however, was now less peaceful, being classed as stage 2, as shown above.

Inconsistencies

.

False Positives
False Positives

After more cycles of SCP-9448, the Foundation continued to instruct the host to observe the candle more and more per day. The foundation managed to extend the candle and subsequently, the host's lifespan up to 232 days, which resulted in a death classified as stage 3, specified above.

The D-Class that was able to reach this length of time by becoming what appeared to be obsessed with the anomaly to some extent, actively ignoring and arguing with the visions it saw in favor of continuing to observe it. The obsession did not reach the point of ignoring meals or other human functions to observe the anomaly.

Due to the nature of D-Class being death row inmates, often of which means violent criminals, they can be hazardous to work with, which can lead to complications. While transferring an active host out of the room and transferring in the new D-Class to take their place, the D-Class lashed out and fought with the armed personnel to the point of forced submission by the security detail. It was at this point that the host had died, and SCP-9448 burned out, without a new host.

Researchers continued to closely monitor the now burnt-out SCP-9448 in an attempt to diagnose any new anomalous effects, but none appeared. The following sunrise, when the anomaly would normally reform and re-ignite, it failed to. The wax stayed pooled at the bottom, now entirely cooled on the offering plate.

After waiting for the next sunrise and continuing testing and observation of the anomaly, the Foundation had deemed this as an "accidental success,” and then changed SCP-XXXX’s classification to “neutralized.”

False Positives

.

Bloodline
Bloodline

On October 19, 2011, the Foundation received a report from one of its watchdog programs about an old woman who was placed into a psychological facility for the elderly in ███████. The woman was found in her home by a neighbor, mumbling incoherently about “a candle.” Her family all lived together in the home and had all died within 3 months of each other by what appeared to be heart attacks, even those that were otherwise entirely healthy. The list of dead family members included:

  • The woman’s husband
  • The woman's only child, her daughter
  • The woman’s son-in-law

The woman claimed that a candle in her home was the cause as it kept coming back, even when she knew it should’ve burned out by then, and do to the mental stress of her family's untimely death, and the proximity of them all, she was placed into the care of ███████. Once the Foundation got wind of the event, they went to the elderly facility and provided the woman with amnestics, as well as sending a recovery team to the woman's house to retrieve the new instance of SCP-9448.

SCP-9448 now takes the form of a new candle, the orange, tall taper candle from the description. The previous instance of SCP-9448 was now disposed of as common waste, as it was confirmed to show no more anomalous effects.

Bloodline

.

Procedure
Procedure

It was at this point that researchers began implementing stricter rules on the host. It started with the host being instructed to observe the anomaly far more frequently throughout the day, from half an hour to multiple hours a day. If the host failed to comply, they were punished by various means, such as skipped meals, stripping of the little furniture in the room, and then the stripping of entertainment.

This was met with backlash and rebellion from the hosts. Due to this rebellion, as well as the anomalous effects prior to the death of the host during a stage 3 instance, researchers decided it would be easier to simply restrain the hosts and force them to observe the anomaly, in order to delay the amount of time between hosts, subsequently lowering the amount of D-Class that would die due to SCP-9448.

The restrictions and protocol continued to progress and advance until you have the active containment procedures listed above. The Foundation has had zero incidents since implementing the most recent containment procedures.

Barbarism
Barbarism

The following is an audio recording between the lead researcher for SCP-9448, Dr. Ian Maxwell and his second, Dr. Olivia Kolumn.

Proof of Diagnostics Before Host Transition Process for SCP-9448

Date: January 12, 2021

Subject: Ethics of SCP-9448 host transition

Team Lead: Dr. Ian Maxwell

Team Members: Dr. Olivia Kolumn

[BEGIN AUDIO LOG]

Dr. Maxwell: Tapes rolling Kolumn, this is Dr. Ian Maxwell head of research and containment of SCP-9448. This audio log is proof of final diagnostic checks before the transition of hosts for SCP-9448. Kolumn, hand me that paper, would you?

(A few seconds pass with no answer from Kolumn.)

Dr. Maxwell: Doctor Kolumn.

Dr. Kolumn: Sorry, excuse me sir.

Dr. Maxwell: The diagnostics paper Kolumn.

Dr. Kolumn: Yes, sorry.

(Papers rustle seemingly between the two)

Dr. Maxwell: It's okay Kolumn. (Sigh) Vitals?

Dr. Kolumn: Stable.

Dr. Maxwell: IV, NG?

Dr. Kolumn: Disconnected due to impending transition.

Dr. Maxwell: Good. Light level?

(No response from Dr. Kolumn.)

Dr. Maxwell: Doctor Kolumn, light level please.

Dr. Kolumn: I'm sorry Doctor, this is just hard, I mean it's fucking barbaric, they're still people.

Dr. Maxwell: This is your sixth host transition Kolumn, you have to get used to it. They were death row inmates, they were going to die anyway.

Dr. Kolumn: By lethal injection, a quick painless death. Now what, they go sit and stare at that, (The sound of Dr. Kolumn choking on her words can be heard) that thing. They're gonna sit in that chair for the next year of their life, suffering the whole time, then they die so cruelly that we have to give the damn guards amnestics afterwards.

Dr. Maxwell: I don't enjoy it either Kolumn, but it's just us on the research team now; it's up to us to find a new way and we aren't gonna get any help. The Foundation is perfectly happy to keep throwing one D-Class a year at the thing for eternity. You saw what happens when we were more lax.

Dr. Kolumn: I know, that poor woman.

Dr. Maxwell: Exactly. Look, we've got about two hours before we have to have one ready to go for the team, we'll look through the files and pick one with some real heinous shit, okay?

Dr. Kolumn: Does it make a difference?

Dr. Maxwell: Does it feel like it does?

Dr. Kolumn: I think so.

Dr. Maxwell: Then it does. Alright, light levels please Kolumn?

Dr. Kolumn: Diminishing, estimated time till completion, four hours. Time to completion based off of reigniton, four hours.

Dr. Maxwell: Thank you Doctor, ending the log.

[END AUDIO LOG]
