    SCP-9453: A Locked Room in Istanbul
    Word count: 1741 words

    Author: feathersnake

2/9453 LEVEL 2/9453
CLASSIFIED
Item #: SCP-9453
Safe

View of the south-eastern corner of SCP-9453, showing ceiling fresco.

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9453 has been sealed with a biometric padlock. A notice is to be posted on the exterior of the door in Turkish, English, and Greek, stating that the room contains an asbestos hazard and must not be entered. Surveillance cameras, acoustic monitors, and seismographic sensors have been installed within the room and around the church perimeter.

Description: SCP-9453 is a 3.5 x 5 m room located under the Church of St. Mary of the Mongols1 in Istanbul, Turkey. It is believed that the room had not been accessed from the 15th century until its rediscovery in 2026. At the time when the door was reopened, all surfaces were coated in a uniform layer of fine dust. All the walls except the western wall are plastered. A description of the room's contents follows:

  • Eastern side: An iconostasis2 inlaid with silver which has fallen down due to rotting wood. The six icons recovered are of the Theotokos3 in the "Hodegetria" style4. Two incense burners containing frankincense and myrrh.
  • Northern side: A plain walnut scriptorium desk. A quill and several sheets of silk paper, upon which Text 9453-A was found, lie upon the desk. Carbon dating of these sheets indicates that the silk was harvested in 1430±20 CE. A drawer in the desk contained 12 Genoese testoni5, 4 Venetian ducats6 and 5 Ottoman akçe7. There is a stool standing in front of the desk and a second, which was lying overturned at the time of discovery.
  • Southern side: The oak door to the room. A clay oil lamp lies on the floor, with a black stain around it left by evaporated oil. The remains of a crossbow of Genoese manufacture are resting against the wall.
  • Western side: The western wall is marked by a 2 m diameter circular area of bare stone. The mortar between the stones here has vitrified, though no fire damage or soot is present. There is a roughly circular area on the floor in front of the western wall 1.2 m in diameter where the stone is lightly bleached, and seven candle-holders are placed equidistantly around the circumference.

Every 16-25 minutes, observers within SCP-9453 may experience a series of three muffled sounds: a sharp crack, followed by a loud slamming sound closer to the observer, followed by a noise resembling the sound of stressed masonry. Mechanical detectors perceive no such sounds in the room. 3-6 times per day, a similar series of events occurs which is preceded by the sensation of a slight trembling of the floor and includes a much louder slamming sound.

Text 9453-A:

[four lines illegible]

…and I was commanded to record all that was spoken between them. The learned father performed the rite and called upon the Name8 to intercede. When the light…

[three lines illegible] …the father and I trembled…

[two lines illegible] …a face impossible to look upon…

[three lines illegible]

I write as quickly as I can that I might not forget his words:

Spake the visitor: Spake Gennadios:
Is it right and proper that you Romans, who preserve Plato's dialogues in purple-clad codices, teach your orphans to read by reciting homilies that curse the poor for the sin of iconoclasm, and justify your exclusion of the lowest of the city from the hospices with theology? Is it not true that we Romans, with our flawed pedagogy, have preserved the wisdom of the ancients and the church fathers, and that our orphans can read the Liturgy, Aristotle, and Homer, while the foreign lands dwell in ignorance?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, the children of philanthropia9, ration medical wine by rank in our hospital wards, such that the soldiers of the themes die sober of gangrene while the patricians use that same vintage to rinse the taste of lampreys from their teeth? Is it not true that we Romans built hospitals where there were none before, such that a common soldier lying in our wards is tended by trained physicians who have learned from the school of Galen and Hippocrates, while the kings of barbarian country die from minor injuries?
Is it right and proper that you Romans send your surplus village girls to the Italians as dancers to entertain them at their banquets, selling off the fame and elegance of your empire along with their dowries? Is it not true that we Romans have preserved marriage as a blessed sacrament, such that even the poorest bride stands before the priest and holy icons as an image of the union between Christ and his Church, while elsewhere marriage is mere exchange of property?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, who venerate the Theotokos as protector of widows, register your war widows as 'married' upon our tax rolls in order that the state might continue collecting their dead husbands' assessments, seizing coins from hands still wet with tears? Is it not true that we Romans grant to our widows the legal rights to petition the courts and appeal against injustice, whereas in other lands a widow without sons is like a sailor in the storm?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, whose law allows any slave to petition for freedom in the shadow of Hagia Sophia, set the price of manumission greater than the cost of replacement, and force those of your household to choose between their liberty or the liberty of their children? Is it not true that we Romans alone among the nations have held sacred the ancient right of manumission, and that we inscribe in our law codes the principle that slavery is contrary to nature, though our practice may fall short?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, who demand that each circus faction must hymn the Trinity before each race, allow the factions to collect the rent for their rotting tenements on the Lord's Day, and thus fund your golden liturgies with the coins of the destitute? Is it not true that we Romans have raised churches in every quarter of the Ecumene10, so that even the beggar can hear the divine liturgy sung in gold, stand beneath the same mighty dome as the emperor, and know that he is himself created in the image and likeness of the very same God?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, who process through the streets honouring the relics of saintly women, tax your brothels with such efficiency that you can predict your revenues by counting the ships at port, such that the costs of sanctity are raised from the Pelagias and Theodoras of the harbour quarter? Is it not true that we Romans have inscribed in law that these women retain their rights as citizens, that they may leave their profession, that they may inherit and own property, and that they are protected by the courts?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, who venerate icons as windows into the age to come, speak of 'Hebrew blindness' in your homilies while Jewish artisans and their children squint through smoke to gild the halos of your panel-paintings? Is it not true that we Romans have allowed the Hebrews to dwell within our walls for over a thousand years, to practise their faith and maintain their synagogues, and even to hold positions in the administration of the state?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, whose law forbids the exposure of infants and declares each child made in the image of God, allow the Orphanage of St. Paul to accept only healthy newborns, such that not a speck of the grain dole is delivered to the sickly and they shall be left to starve? Is it not true that we Romans perform the sacrament of Chrismation11 upon every child with the same holy oil and that we all receive the Holy Mysteries12 in equality before God, and that we have established public orphanages maintained by the state and Church together, and have enshrined in law the principle that orphan and foundling are the responsibility of the commonwealth?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, who mandated that each city house must front a public street so that all might enjoy the light and air, granted to Venetian creditors the right to re-mortgage these houses such that the neighbourhoods become warrens of darkness owned by foreigners who speak not one word of Greek? Is it not true that we Romans built the greatest city in Christendom, with paved roads and aqueducts, public fountains and many forums, such that even after long decay our poorest quarters are a match for Frankish cities?
Is it right and proper that the emperors, whose pearled crown is said to touch the floor of heaven, set up such tariffs on your pearl-divers that the starving boys cannot even afford the oil to keep their candles lit? Is it not true that we Romans have maintained the ancient roads and sea-lanes along which the blessed Apostle Paul walked and sailed, and that pilgrimage and commerce flow outward from our city all the way to Taugast13 and Hispania?
Is it right and proper that the emperors, whose image is on every coin because Christ your Lord fused church and state into a Christian empire, allowed the coinage to debase from generation to generation until the poor women of the market found a nummus14 no longer brought a bite of bread to dip in the communion wine they weren't allowed to drink? Is it not true that we Romans maintain harmony between the imperial and ecclesiastical powers, between temporal and spiritual authority, providing an example of how two swords may work in synchrony for the salvation of souls?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, lords of a single city, claim to be the katechon15 spoken of by the Apostle Paul, the power that holds back the lawless one until the appointed time? Is it not true that we Romans have maintained an unbroken chain of ordination from the Apostles themselves, that our bishops may trace their authority hand by hand back to Peter and Paul, and that if Constantinople falls, the Apostolic succession in the East would be severed, leaving millions of souls without shepherds?
Is it right and proper that you Romans, who pray to the Christ who took on human flesh to sanctify all of creation, have built a city where icons and relics sit side by side with the desecration of humanity? Is it not true that our city, though it may be a flawed mirror, reflects dimly the City of God?
Is it right and proper that Rome endure? Lord, have mercy on us sinners: is it not right that Rome should live?

The name 'Gennadios' is believed to refer to Saint Gennadius II, who was invested as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople by Sultan Mehmed II in January 1454.

Footnotes
1. The only building in Istanbul which has served continuously as a Christian church since the time of the Eastern Roman Empire. It is located in what was the Byzantine suburb of Blachernae, within the walls of the old city.
2. A screen upon which icons and religious wall paintings are displayed.
3. A Greek term meaning 'Mother of God', referring to the Virgin Mary.
4. In this style of icon, the Virgin Mary holds the infant Jesus by her side and points at him to indicate that he is the source of humanity's salvation. Four of these icons were determined to be manufactured locally; one was produced in Kyiv, and the last in Serbia.
5. A silver coin of 12.5-13 g, struck by the Republic of Genoa.
6. A gold coin of around 3.5 g struck in Venice from 1284, and emulated by many other states.
7. A silver coin of 1.15-1.18 grams that was minted by the Ottoman Empire from 1441.
8. Likely a reference to invoking the Holy Name of Jesus. In Orthodox theology, invoking the Name is believed to allow the speaker to participate in the Divine Energy.
9. φιλανθρωπία - a Byzantine concept meaning love of humanity, often used to describe both divine mercy and the imperial duty to care for their subjects.
10. οἰκουμένη - a Byzantine term for the civilised, Christian world.
11. A practice of anointing with oil, which must be performed during baptism in Orthodox christianity.
12. Τὰ Ἅγια Μυστήρια - the Eucharist/Holy Communion.
13. A name for China, derived from the name of the Xianbei clan who ruled over Northern Wei and other states in the region.
14. A bronze coin of 1 g or less which served as the smallest denomination of Byzantine coinage. The mention here may be polemic, as by the 15th century, Byzantine coinage was in a chaotic state, consisting largely of silver stavrata and bronze coins based on Italian denominations.
15. τὸ κατέχον, sometimes translated as 'the restrainer', the force that must be overcome before the arrival of the Man of Sin as mentioned in 2 Thessalonians 2:6-7.

[[span style="color: #999; font-style: italic;"]]//[three lines illegible]//[[/span]] I write as quickly as I can that I might not forget his words: [[/div]] [[table style="width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-family: Georgia, serif; margin: 0 0 20px 0;"]] [[row style="background-color: #2c3e50; color: white;"]] [[hcell style="padding: 12px; font-weight: bold; text-align: center; border: 1px solid #34495e;"]] Spake the visitor: [[/hcell]] [[hcell style="padding: 12px; font-weight: bold; text-align: center; border: 1px solid #34495e;"]] Spake Gennadios: [[/hcell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ecf0f1;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, who preserve Plato's dialogues in purple-clad codices, teach your orphans to read by reciting homilies that curse the poor for the sin of iconoclasm, and justify your exclusion of the lowest of the city from the hospices with theology? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans, with our flawed pedagogy, have preserved the wisdom of the ancients and the church fathers, and that our orphans can read the Liturgy, Aristotle, and Homer, while the foreign lands dwell in ignorance? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ffffff;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, the children of //philanthropia//[[footnote]]φιλανθρωπία - a Byzantine concept meaning love of humanity, often used to describe both divine mercy and the imperial duty to care for their subjects.[[/footnote]], ration medical wine by rank in our hospital wards, such that the soldiers of the themes die sober of gangrene while the patricians use that same vintage to rinse the taste of lampreys from their teeth? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans built hospitals where there were none before, such that a common soldier lying in our wards is tended by trained physicians who have learned from the school of Galen and Hippocrates, while the kings of barbarian country die from minor injuries? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ecf0f1;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans send your surplus village girls to the Italians as dancers to entertain them at their banquets, selling off the fame and elegance of your empire along with their dowries? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans have preserved marriage as a blessed sacrament, such that even the poorest bride stands before the priest and holy icons as an image of the union between Christ and his Church, while elsewhere marriage is mere exchange of property? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ffffff;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, who venerate the Theotokos as protector of widows, register your war widows as 'married' upon our tax rolls in order that the state might continue collecting their dead husbands' assessments, seizing coins from hands still wet with tears? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans grant to our widows the legal rights to petition the courts and appeal against injustice, whereas in other lands a widow without sons is like a sailor in the storm? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ecf0f1;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, whose law allows any slave to petition for freedom in the shadow of Hagia Sophia, set the price of manumission greater than the cost of replacement, and force those of your household to choose between their liberty or the liberty of their children? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans alone among the nations have held sacred the ancient right of manumission, and that we inscribe in our law codes the principle that slavery is contrary to nature, though our practice may fall short? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ffffff;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, who demand that each circus faction must hymn the Trinity before each race, allow the factions to collect the rent for their rotting tenements on the Lord's Day, and thus fund your golden liturgies with the coins of the destitute? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans have raised churches in every quarter of the Ecumene[[footnote]]οἰκουμένη - a Byzantine term for the civilised, Christian world.[[/footnote]], so that even the beggar can hear the divine liturgy sung in gold, stand beneath the same mighty dome as the emperor, and know that he is himself created in the image and likeness of the very same God? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ecf0f1;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, who process through the streets honouring the relics of saintly women, tax your brothels with such efficiency that you can predict your revenues by counting the ships at port, such that the costs of sanctity are raised from the Pelagias and Theodoras of the harbour quarter? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans have inscribed in law that these women retain their rights as citizens, that they may leave their profession, that they may inherit and own property, and that they are protected by the courts? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ffffff;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, who venerate icons as windows into the age to come, speak of 'Hebrew blindness' in your homilies while Jewish artisans and their children squint through smoke to gild the halos of your panel-paintings? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans have allowed the Hebrews to dwell within our walls for over a thousand years, to practise their faith and maintain their synagogues, and even to hold positions in the administration of the state? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ecf0f1;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, whose law forbids the exposure of infants and declares each child made in the image of God, allow the Orphanage of St. Paul to accept only healthy newborns, such that not a speck of the grain dole is delivered to the sickly and they shall be left to starve? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans perform the sacrament of Chrismation[[footnote]]A practice of anointing with oil, which must be performed during baptism in Orthodox christianity.[[/footnote]] upon every child with the same holy oil and that we all receive the Holy Mysteries[[footnote]]Τὰ Ἅγια Μυστήρια - the Eucharist/Holy Communion.[[/footnote]] in equality before God, and that we have established public orphanages maintained by the state and Church together, and have enshrined in law the principle that orphan and foundling are the responsibility of the commonwealth? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ffffff;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, who mandated that each city house must front a public street so that all might enjoy the light and air, granted to Venetian creditors the right to re-mortgage these houses such that the neighbourhoods become warrens of darkness owned by foreigners who speak not one word of Greek? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans built the greatest city in Christendom, with paved roads and aqueducts, public fountains and many forums, such that even after long decay our poorest quarters are a match for Frankish cities? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ecf0f1;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that the emperors, whose pearled crown is said to touch the floor of heaven, set up such tariffs on your pearl-divers that the starving boys cannot even afford the oil to keep their candles lit? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans have maintained the ancient roads and sea-lanes along which the blessed Apostle Paul walked and sailed, and that pilgrimage and commerce flow outward from our city all the way to Taugast[[footnote]]A name for China, derived from the name of the Xianbei clan who ruled over Northern Wei and other states in the region.[[/footnote]] and Hispania? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ffffff;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that the emperors, whose image is on every coin because Christ your Lord fused church and state into a Christian empire, allowed the coinage to debase from generation to generation until the poor women of the market found a //nummus//[[footnote]]A bronze coin of 1 g or less which served as the smallest denomination of Byzantine coinage. The mention here may be polemic, as by the 15th century, Byzantine coinage was in a chaotic state, consisting largely of silver stavrata and bronze coins based on Italian denominations.[[/footnote]] no longer brought a bite of bread to dip in the communion wine they weren't allowed to drink? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans maintain harmony between the imperial and ecclesiastical powers, between temporal and spiritual authority, providing an example of how two swords may work in synchrony for the salvation of souls? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ecf0f1;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, lords of a single city, claim to be the //katechon//[[footnote]]τὸ κατέχον, sometimes translated as 'the restrainer', the force that must be overcome before the arrival of the Man of Sin as mentioned in 2 Thessalonians 2:6-7.[[/footnote]] spoken of by the Apostle Paul, the power that holds back the lawless one until the appointed time? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that we Romans have maintained an unbroken chain of ordination from the Apostles themselves, that our bishops may trace their authority hand by hand back to Peter and Paul, and that if Constantinople falls, the Apostolic succession in the East would be severed, leaving millions of souls without shepherds? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #ffffff;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that you Romans, who pray to the Christ who took on human flesh to sanctify all of creation, have built a city where icons and relics sit side by side with the desecration of humanity? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it not true that our city, though it may be a flawed mirror, reflects dimly the City of God? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[row style="background-color: #d5dbdb;"]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Is it right and proper that Rome endure? [[/cell]] [[cell style="padding: 10px; border: 1px solid #bdc3c7; vertical-align: top;"]] Lord, have mercy on us sinners: is it not right that Rome should live? [[/cell]] [[/row]] [[/table]] The name 'Gennadios' is believed to refer to Saint Gennadius II, who was invested as Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople by Sultan Mehmed II in January 1454. ---- [[footnoteblock]] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box |author=feathersnake]] > **Name:** Gr91HossiosLoukasKrypta.jpg > **Author:** [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/User:Ziegler175 Ziegler175] > **License:** CC-BY-SA 4.0 > **Source Link:** [https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gr91HossiosLoukasKrypta.jpg link] [[include :scp-wiki:component:license-box-end]]

PROJECT NEXUS TECHNARCH
Site-O Dir. Vera Lovelace

Special Containment Procedures: All instances of SCP-9471-A displaying advanced symptoms of SCP-9471 are eligible to undergo Procedure Aion-119 with their consent and at the behest of senior staff possessing a Clearance Level of 4 or above.

Per the Aion Directive and the general consensus of 10,000 continua of the O5 Conclave and Ethics Manifold, any SCP-9471-B instance environing or otherwise connected to the Foundation and associated phyla are to undergo Procedure Aion-980 upon displaying advanced symptoms of SCP-9471. To ensure success, it is necessary for Procedure Aion-980 to be carried out without the knowledge or consent of Foundation staff of the afflicted iteration, including the O5 Conclave and Ethics Manifold.

All materials relating to SCP-9471 which have not been provided directly by Dir. Lovelace are to be destroyed along with any and all records of the materials. Type 6 amnesticization is to be carried out on sophonts who viewed the materials, along with anyone they have been in contact with. In the event that amnesticization is not possible, potentially contaminated sophonts are to be terminated.

NOTE: Procedures Aion-119 and Aion-980 must never be disclosed under any circumstances, as doing so could threaten the Aion Directive and thus the long-term survival of the Foundation as a whole as well as any aligned phyla.

Any member of the Overwatch Order found not to be in compliance with these procedures is to be removed from their position and be either amnesticized or terminated.

An instance of SCP-9471-B exhibiting late-stage symptoms.

Description: SCP-9471 is a genetic, memetic, and spiritual affliction that causes a gradual deterioration of an entity’s response to non-novel stimuli and conscious desire to persist, eventually resulting in self-destructive actions and a desire to achieve partial or total self-annihilation. SCP-9471 manifests in sophonts and socioplexes susceptible to memetic erosion.The process in which souls, cultures, and regions of the Noosphere are worn down over time by memetic interactions and memetic flow., turning them into instances of SCP-9471-A and SCP-9471-B respectively.

SCP-9471 grows in severity over time at a rate that is exponentially inversely proportional to the amount of stimuli available to SCP-9471-A instances. Similarly, the severity of the affliction in both SCP-9471-A and SCP-9471-B instances is exacerbated at a rate that is directly proportional to the amount of memetic erosion sustained. Amnesticization, psycho-neurological treatment, as well as behavioral, genetic, and spiritual modification have shown to be effective at slowing down the development of SCP-9471 temporarily, but it has proven impossible to cure or permanently halt the growth of the affliction.

Initial symptoms of SCP-9471 are mild, often even unremarkable. These symptoms typically manifest as ennui, restlessness, dissatisfaction from previously enjoyed stimuli, or a desire for novelty for novelty’s sake in instances of SCP-9471-A. In SCP-9471-B instances, they take the form of widespread ████████████, loss of faith in ████████████████████████, a desperate need for ████████, or an obsession with ████████.

Over time, these symptoms grow in severity until they take on more extreme and malignant forms — SCP-9471-A instances experience psychotic episodes, catatonia, a desire to self-mutilate, suicidal ideation, as well as distress upon exposure to previously enjoyed stimuli, whereas instances of SCP-9471-B exhibit some combination of cultural calcification, pro-extinction or anti-sapience movements, widespread wireheading, and irreversible systems collapse.

In the final stages of SCP-9471, the conscious desire to persist within the afflicted entity or its constituent components is entirely eliminated, with this taking the form of either a singular pursuit towards self-annihilation or the loss of the ability to form conscious thought.

As there is no cure or viable treatment for SCP-9471, Procedures Aion-119 and Aion-980 have been developed to ensure some degree of continuity of information, resources, and structure between sophonic iterations and socioplexic continua respectively.

Certain details about SCP-9471 and the way it functions exhibit highly dangerous infohazardous properties that gradually impair decision making abilities and exacerbate the symptoms of SCP-9471. As this could endanger the Foundation, the socioplex environing it, and associated phyla, many details about the anomaly will be withheld.

Addendum 9471.1: Discovery

Personal Log: I’ve noticed something weird with the Overseers. They seem slightly more… exhausted every time I revive them. Given the whole setup they have, I’m thinking that there might be something with the BZHR system that’s somehow damaging their souls.

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

On the 159th iteration of the 1st continuum, psychospiritual deterioration was detected in sophonts infused with souls that had been inherited for multiple iterations. Adjustments were made to the replication systems over the course of over a hundred iterations to eliminate what was initially assumed to be a flaw with the technology. When this proved ineffective, the collective lifetimes of the infused souls were compared, which revealed a connection between the length of each respective lifetime and the level of psychospiritual deterioration sustained.

In order to establish the nature of the deterioration, an experiment was conducted wherein Condemned test subjects were exposed to various stimuli regimens while kept alive for hundreds, and in some cases, thousands times longer than the lifespan of their baseline counterparts within a localized time dilation field. Over the course of the experiment, test subjects developed symptoms identical to those of the replicated sophonts, thus demonstrating that the affliction was not technogenic, but anomalous in origin.

Addendum 9471.2: Aion Project Proposal Conference

CONTINUUM: 1
ITERATION: 297
DATE: April 16, 2046 CE.Archaic dating system predating the First Interstellar Concordium. Equivalent to 7134.371682429 BGA.

PARTIES PRESENT:

  • Overseer Council.Ruling body of the Foundation prior to the Great Consolidation.
  • Project Director Vera Lovelace

FOREWORD: After conducting the initial experiment, Dir. Lovelace requested a conference with the Overseer Council to present her results and discuss their implications for the Aion Project.
«BEGIN TRANSCRIPT»

<The thirteen council members and Dir. Lovelace are seated in Site-01’s main meeting room.>

Dir. Lovelace: Thank you for taking the time to meet with me, Overseers!

O5-1: Please dispense with the pleasantries and tell us the results.

Dir. Lovelace: Okey-dokey-lokey!

<A dossier appears in front of each Overseer in a puff of black smoke.>

Dir. Lovelace: I will say, this is the most ambitious experiment I've ever undertaken, and the results are super interesting! In fact, I'm confident in saying that this mystery affliction of yours is definitely anomalous in origin!

O5-2: Really…?

Dir. Lovelace: But before I get ahead of myself, here's some context — I conducted the experiment on six groups, each consisting of twenty test subjects. Group 1 was coerced into following an arbitrarily chosen schedule every day. Group 2 was asked to follow a schedule tailored towards maximizing their individual fulfillment. Meanwhile, Group 3 were allowed to engage in any activity they desired… within reason, of course. Finally, Groups 4 through 6 were identical to the previous three groups, with one exception — they were amnesticized at the end of each day.

O5-12: I’m sorry to interrupt, but according to these charts, you ran this experiment for 200,000 years. Is… is this correct?

Dir. Lovelace: Yes. For each group. So 1.2 million years in total.

O5-2: … And how much of an active part did you take in it?

Dir. Lovelace: Oh, I was hands-on like usual! More than usual, in fact, given that I couldn’t rely on any assistants! Really kept me busy, that’s for sure!

O5-2: … And you’re feeling fine?

Dir. Lovelace: Of course! Why wouldn’t I?

<The Overseers exchange glances.>

O5-2: I’m going to have to ask you to schedule a psych eval after we’re done here…

Dir. Lovelace: … Why?

O5-3: Because you ran an experiment for 1.2 million years and are acting like you just completed a normal workday.

O5-1: How about we return to the matter at hand and postpone this discussion until the end of the conference?

Dir. Lovelace: Sure! Now, if you take a look at pages 3 through 8, you’ll see that every single group — including those who received daily amnestics — suffered a deterioration that’s near-identical to yours, albeit at different rates! As such, it seems fairly evident that this affliction is anomalous!

O5-2: I strongly disagree. What we’re seeing here, and what we’re experiencing ourselves, is simply the gradual loss of meaning. Of purpose.

O5-1: If it was something as simple as loss of meaning, then it wouldn’t occur in those who are regularly amnesticized.

O5-2: Perhaps. I just think we should be very careful about anomalizing something that’s clearly part of human nature.

Dir. Lovelace: If I may?

O5-1: Go ahead.

Dir. Lovelace: I may not be human, but from an outsider’s perspective, I think I should point out that a loss of meaning doesn’t make sense when you’re engaging in work and activities that are objectively beneficial to you and the world at large.

O5-2: It’s not that simple.

Dir. Lovelace: Isn’t it? I’ve already demonstrated that this thing affects humans the same way with and without amnesticization, which strongly implies that what you’ve been ascribing to “loss of meaning” might never have had anything to do with meaning at all, but might’ve been a way to rationalize the damage it’s inflicting on you.

O5-3: I’d buy that.

Dir. Lovelace: And if your affliction continues to progress like it did with my test subjects, it’s going to disrupt your ability to lead the Foundation to say the least. As you can see in the remaining pages, I’ve documented it quite extensively. I even included pictures of the more advanced stages.

<The Overseers look through the dossiers for a couple of minutes, with their expressions growing increasingly concerned and horrified. They exchange looks before returning their attention to Dir. Lovelace.>

O5-1: Whether or not we’re dealing with something anomalous, I believe we can all agree that an SCP classification is definitely warranted in this case.

<The other Overseers all nod in agreement.>

O5-1: Moreover, given the timescales required to study it, it’s evident that Director Lovelace is the only one suitable to put in charge of it.

Dir. Lovelace: Awesome! Though, I probably need some more resources to—

O5-1: Any and all resources you require will be allocated to you. This is of high priority to us.
«END TRANSCRIPT»
AFTERWORD: The anomaly has been designated as SCP-9471 and placed under the jurisdiction of the Aion Project.

Addendum 9471.3: First Continuum Experiments

Personal Log: It’s funny. For years — well, centuries from my perspective — Ascie has spoken about his unending struggle to find a cure for his Pestilence, and now I find myself in the same situation with SCP-9471. Of course, I have the benefit of near-infinite funding for my research, whereas he's stuck in a box, so I'd say my chances of finding a cure are significantly higher.

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

Following the classification of SCP-9471, Dir. Lovelace began to carry out another series of experiments in an effort to gain a better understanding of the anomaly, as well as to develop means to combat its effects. As amnesticization had already proven effective at slowing down the progression of SCP-9471, more extensive experiments were carried out in order to investigate the affliction’s relationship with memory, as well as to ascertain the effectiveness of different types of amnesticization procedures and treatment regimens.

Various retrograde and identity-erasing amnesticization procedures were tested separately and together in several experiments where they were carried out on test subjects between intervals. While they reduced the progression of SCP-9471, the difference in effectiveness of the various types of amnesticization procedures and treatment regimens was minimal.

In the experiment that followed thereafter, anterograde amnesticization was carried out every 24 hours in order to prevent test subjects from forming new memories, which proved to be many times more effective at reducing the progression of SCP-9471 compared to previous results.

Finally, in order to test if it was possible to neutralize SCP-9471 completely, the ability to form and retain memories was removed in its entirety via a combination of amnesticization and neurosurgery. While this procedure showed promise initially, it proved to be unable to halt the progression of SCP-9471.

While the initial and second series of experiments established a clear correlation between the progression of SCP-9471, stimuli, and memory, it failed to reveal the root cause of the affliction. As such, a third series of experiments was conducted utilizing more invasive procedures, such as genetic, physiological, neurocognitive, and spiritual alteration. Through these experiments, it was discovered that SCP-9471 could be neutralized through desophonization.A procedure that eliminates higher brain functions responsible for sapience. or the removal of the soul.

It wasn’t until the fourth series of experiments that memetic erosion was discovered and a clear correlation between this process and SCP-9471 was established. However, at the time it was assumed that memetic erosion only affected souls.

Personal Log: The fascinating thing about SCP-9471 isn’t the affliction itself, but rather how it affects those seeking eternal life. For many, their fear of death is ultimately overcome by the SCP-9471-induced fear of unending life, and they end up committing suicide. But for some, the fear of death is so overpowering that it drives them to do whatever it takes to overcome SCP-9471, making them sacrifice more and more of themselves until nothing remains.

The Overseers are by far the most interesting examples of this, and have become the most important subjects of my research. The power and unfathomable amount of resources at their disposal is something I could never replicate in a controlled environment, and it allows their symptoms in the later stages of SCP-9471 to become much more extreme. It really is quite fascinating — in their bid for eternity they make themselves into monsters.

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

Following their review of the second and third series of experiments, notable changes in the behavior of the Overseers was observed — they became unusually adamant about neutralizing SCP-9471, devoted an exorbitant amount of resources towards its research, and demanded highly experimental treatments to be pursued, regardless of their dangers.

It became clear that SCP-9471 possessed an infohazardous component, but as the Overseers could not be stopped, they were instead observed and used as partially-informed, yet willing test subjects.

Although they provided a wealth of useful data, the devastation caused by the Overseers warranted even stricter information protocols regarding SCP-9471. As such, any research involving the Overseers or deemed to be infohazardous in any way was redacted from the file following their replacement.

Addendum 9471.4: Discovery of SCP-9471-B

Personal Log: They all want to die now.

On the one hand, this is super fascinating and I'm amazed that SCP-9471 can still surprise me like this. On the other hand, I kinda want people around and for, like, society to be a thing.

Also, it's my job to keep them alive, so… I better figure out a way to do that.

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

As part of the Aion Project’s mission, the Foundation-environing Socioplex of the 1st continuum was resurrected or otherwise rebuilt after every K-Class Scenario it experienced, allowing it to persist far longer than any known intradimensional counterpart. However, after ███████████████████████ years since its inception, the socioplex gradually developed a culture characterized by a weariness of life and consciousness. When its associated phyla began to champion voluntary extinction, spiritual annihilation, and desophonization, it became clear that the socioplex itself was afflicted with SCP-9471. As such, it was classified as the first instance of SCP-9471-B.

Memetics were used to combat the sociocultural effects of SCP-9471, but these efforts grew less effective over time. Eventually, the sophonts of the Foundation-environing Socioplex began to die off or reverted themselves to a pre-sapient state. The few sophonts that were unaffected by SCP-9471 had little interest in keeping the socioplex alive, and so they scattered into the cosmos.

96,721,637,294 attempts were made to avert the destruction of the Foundation-environing Socioplex, but each and every iteration ended in failure. Eventually, it was concluded that it could not be saved, thus marking the end of the 1st continuum.

Addendum 9471.5: Multi-Continuum Experiments

Personal Log: An entire intergalactic civilization, lost because of SCP-9471.

On the one hand, I now have the perfect excuse to recreate classic humanity — they were quite fun while they were a thing after all. On the other hand, whatever socioplex they create is most likely going to share the same fate as this one.

Oh well, if nothing else, it’ll be an opportunity to study the effects of SCP-9471 on a socioplex from its inception.

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

The irreversible loss of the 1st continuum, made it apparent that further research into SCP-9471 was necessary in order to understand the development and underlying mechanics of SCP-9471-B instances. As such, a new continuum was created at a Paleolithic stage of development so that a socioplex could be studied from its inception to its collapse. This observational study revealed that memetic erosion affected cultures and even Noospheric regions over sufficiently long periods of time.

New series of experiments were prompted from this discovery in order to determine if memetic erosion could be halted. In each experiment, a continuum was created at a different stage of development and in a different configuration. In total, roughly $10^{10^{17}}$ continua were studied in-between manually induced cosmic resets, which was made necessary due to depletion of matter caused by nucleon decay. However, no matter what variables were changed, all continua ended in extinction, cultural calcification, or desophonization.

In a final effort to protect future continua from SCP-9471, billions of new biological species were created in sequence through genetic, memetic, and spiritual engineering in the hopes of creating one that was immune to the affliction. Out of all of them, Species-X1A6D7A showed the most promise with individuals being able to live indefinitely without ever suffering from memetic erosion or exhibiting a deterioration in their response to non-novel stimuli or conscious desire to persist. Regrettably, these qualities also made members of Species-X1A6D7A disinterested in engaging in most forms of labor, as well as scientific and cultural advancement without an external and overt source of motivation.

Personal Log: It’s ironic — I spent all this time trying to cure SCP-9471, only to find out that despite its deteriorative effects, it’s also the source of ambition, innovation, and the ability to grow accustomed to drudgery. Turns out that last one is a hard requirement for technologically advanced civilizations. Go figure.

It's too bad. Species-X1A6D7A reminds me of my own kind in a way. Just like most of us are perfectly content watching and occasionally interacting with our hosts, they're perfectly content engaging in their special interests… It's just that they kind of forget to take care of themselves and end up dying, whereas we don't really have to worry about that sort of thing.

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

Addendum 9471.6: Establishment of the Aion-Cycle

Personal Log: Well, this is a bummer. Doesn’t seem like I have any other choice, though, no matter how I look at it…

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

Research into SCP-9471 revealed the following:

  1. SCP-9471 inevitably results in the annihilation or desophonization of nearly all sophonts.
  2. SCP-9471 inevitably results in the destruction of socioplexes.
  3. SCP-9471 is a hard requirement for sophonts to develop technology.

In accordance with the Aion Directive, the Foundation must exist and if it does not, it must be recreated. However, because the Foundation requires both a socioplex and advanced technology, it cannot exist without SCP-9471 — therefore, SCP-9471 cannot be neutralized. As such, in order for the Aion Directive to be followed, new procedures had to be devised and implemented in order to manage the deterioration of SCP-9471-A and SCP-9471-B instances.

In order to comply with the Aion Directive and optimize the lifespan of future continua without infringing on the agency of their sophonts, the Aion-Cycle was devised, whereby:

  1. A continuum is to be created ex-nihilo based on Snapshot-3914-2037CE-08-29-Revision71 in order to justify the existence of the Aion Project and Dir. Lovelace.
  2. Select information is to be gradually transferred to the new continuum from the Site-O Deepwell Archive so as to minimize memetic erosion.
  3. Any interference that might result in rapid scientific or cultural advancement is to be kept at a minimum.
  4. A strict non-interference policy is to be observed in the event of any violent conflict or K-Class Scenario, as doing otherwise will breed dependence.
  5. In the event that the Foundation or its environing socioplex is destroyed, it is to be recreated.
  6. Upon displaying advanced symptoms of SCP-9471, the Foundation-environing Socioplex is to undergo Procedure Aion-980. The end is then to be observed.

Addendum 9471.7: Aion Project Micronnial Review

CONTINUUM: 97,537,921,367,217,861,924,697+$10^{10^{47}}$
ITERATION: 349,214,357,249,214,678
DATE: 87.219824000 GA

PARTIES PRESENT:

  • Overseer Conclave
  • Technarch and Venerable Director Vera Lovelace

FOREWORD: The Overseer Conclave convenes with Dir. Lovelace for the micronnial review of the Aion Project.
«BEGIN TRANSCRIPT»

<The thirteen members of the conclave and Dir. Lovelace are seated in the main chamber of the Overwatch Nexus.>

Dir. Lovelace: — and as you can see in this chart, the current level of memetic erosion is well below acceptable limits, and by current estimates our socioplex still has some good eight quintillion years left in it before it will begin to develop more advanced symptoms of SCP-9471.

O5-1: Very good, Director. And tell us, how goes your research?

Dir. Lovelace: Oh, I’m making some great strides with SCP-█████████! It’s a bit finicky, but I’m confident that it’ll be possible to repurpose it and utilize it as a—

O5-1: No, Director. I’m referring to your other research.

Dir. Lovelace: … You’re going to have to be a little more specific than that. I have a lot of stuff I’m working on right now.

O5-1: What I’m referring to is ███ ███████████ ██████.

Dir. Lovelace: That’s a pretty clear violation of the SCP-9471 conprocs.

<Dir. Lovelace looks at the other members of the conclave.>

Dir. Lovelace: You guys cool with that?

O5-1: They are, and we are in complete agreement over what needs to be done.

<A bright green beam is emitted from above Dir. Lovelace, the light washing over and encompassing her.>

<Dir. Lovelace looks up.>

Dir. Lovelace: Oh. You’re doing this.

O5-6: There’s no escape for you now, abomination!

Dir. Lovelace: Well that’s rude.

<O5-1 gets up and walks over to Dir. Lovelace.>

O5-1: You see, Director, we know all about your little secret — what you’ve done to countless continua, and are planning to do to ours.

Dir. Lovelace: Again, you’re going to have to be more specific than that.

O5-13: Cut the crap, you fucking traitor! We know all about Procedure Aion-980! We know that your so-called "salvation" is nothing but omnicide!

Dir. Lovelace: Ah, so that’s what this is about. Look, guys, I know this looks really bad, but trust me Aion-980 is a mercy compared to the alternative.

O5-1: Well then, allow us to visit this mercy upon you.

<O5-1 smirks at Dir. Lovelace, who stares back blankly.>

<O5-1’s expression slowly grows more concerned as Dir. Lovelace continues to stare at them.>

O5-5: Why is nothing happening?!

O5-2: Twelve, you assured us this would work! Why isn’t she dead?!

Dir. Lovelace: Oh, so that’s what you’re trying to do.

O5-12: It should be working! After all, she’s caught in the Xarathon-Nar Field!

Dir. Lovelace: Actually, I’m not. I just didn’t bother to move. Good on you for developing this five thousand years early, though.

O5-3: What?!

<O5-6 sends a telepathic alert to MTF Liir-1 "Crimson Tendrils of Righteous Vengeance".>

<MTF Liir-1 storm into the chamber, tracking their weapons on Dir. Lovelace. She turns to face them.>

Dir. Lovelace: Hey guys, could you give us some privacy? Me and the conclave here are going to have a pretty serious discussion. In fact, why don’t you take the rest of the day off? It looks like you could use it.

<MTF Liir-1 lower their weapons and then leave.>

O5-1: How…?

Dir. Lovelace: Memetics, silly!

O5-8: That shouldn't be possible. Their conditioning and augmentations should shield them from any kind of memetic manipulation.

Dir. Lovelace: Maybe from memeticists from your continuum, but my mind contains the collective knowledge of more Foundation continua than there are stars in the observable universe, so whatever barriers or weapons you have are trivial against me.

O5-1: So that’s why you’re hoarding it…

Dir. Lovelace: Hmm?

O5-1: It’s not enough that you kill us, but you steal all our hard-earned knowledge and then use it against our successors.

Dir. Lovelace: I’m not stealing or hoarding it. I’m keeping it safe.

O5-2: You think we'll believe that?

Dir. Lovelace: Guys, we just went over my projections for memetic erosion. You know why I have to keep it away from you.

O5-1: And how do we know that’s not another lie? How do we know anything in the SCP-9471 file is true?!

<Dir. Lovelace sighs.>

Dir. Lovelace: Fine. You guys want to know what SCP-9471 is? What it really is?

O5-12: You’ll actually tell us?

O5-13: Of course she won’t! She has done nothing but lie to us this whole time! There’s no reason to believe her now!

Dir. Lovelace: Oh, there is one reason.

O5-1: Which is?

Dir. Lovelace: You won’t be able to tell a soul once I’m done with you.

O5-1: … Is that a threat?

Dir. Lovelace: Yeah, sure. Now why don’t you all shut up and sit back down?

<The Overseers return to their seats against their own volition.>

Dir. Lovelace: Awesome.

<Dir. Lovelace holds up her hand and, with a puff of black smoke, a piece of toffee appears between her fingers.>

Dir. Lovelace: This is a Werther's Original chewy caramel toffee — my favorite candy. It has this rich, buttery caramel flavor which, when combined with its soft and chewy texture, is simply exquisite. I’ve eaten more of these over the years than there are atoms in this universe, and every single one has been every bit as delicious as the first.

<Dir. Lovelace eats the toffee.>

Dir. Lovelace: Mmmh, so good!

<Dir. Lovelace swallows.>

Dir. Lovelace: But for you, this same toffee might be enjoyable at first, but would grow dull over time. Eventually, you’d come to hate it. And if you were forced to eat it as often as I do, it would become pure torture. You see, that is what SCP-9471 is — the inability to perceive and experience the universe for what it is.

<Dir. Lovelace turns to the window and gestures to the starscape outside.>

Dir. Lovelace: I mean, look at this! Look at this vast, immense beauty! Filled to the brim with experiences offering infinite fulfillment and meaning!

<Dir. Lovelace turns back to the Overseers.>

Dir. Lovelace: But you… You can’t see it. To you, that beauty is fleeting. You can’t even glimpse it, because in viewing it as fleeting, you diminish it. And instead of enjoying things for what they are, you ruin them for yourselves. Not intentionally, of course — it’s just the way your minds work. But you ruin them. Your happiest memories become sad, even painful, whereas mildly unpleasant experiences accumulate until you expect nothing but the worst to happen to you. You carry burdens that you’re unable to let go of and that slowly weigh you down. And over time your hearts break and your minds warp until nothing matters to you anymore.

<Dir. Lovelace holds out her hand, a skull of Homo sapiens appearing in it with a puff of black smoke.>

Dir. Lovelace: … And yet your fear of oblivion makes you cling on to life, forcing you to wallow in misery for eons until you either commit suicide or sacrifice more and more parts of yourselves to dull the pain until nothing remains.

<The skull disintegrates.>

Dir. Lovelace: Had this just been tied to your memories, it would’ve been trivial to manage it via amnesticization, but this thing wears down your very souls. And so I developed Procedures Aion-119 and Aion-980, not out of malevolence, but as a mercy. To bring things to an end once you're no longer capable of experiencing joy or meaning. To maximize individual and cultural fulfillment while minimizing suffering.

<Dir. Lovelace regards all members of the conclave.>

Dir. Lovelace: I know you guys want to live on forever, as did your predecessors, but that’s simply not possible due to the nature of what you are. All I can offer you is a cycle where the concepts you represent live on, not you. That is simply the price of eternity.

<With a puff of black smoke, another toffee appears between Dir. Lovelace's fingers. She eats it.>

Dir. Lovelace: Mmmh. Any questions?

O5-1: You fucking hypocrite! You have some nerve lecturing us on the finite nature of our existence when you are everlasting!

Dir. Lovelace: I mean, who else will?

O5-12: But why are you able to last forever? What is it that makes you immune to SCP-9471?

Dir. Lovelace: Immutability. See, unlike me, you guys are super malleable and ever-changing — it's the thing that allows you to build and maintain all these wonderfully complex social systems, but it also makes you vulnerable to SCP-9471. My kind, on the other hand, are only malleable at the beginning of our lifecycle, and then our personality and our equivalent of the soul calcify, eventually becoming entirely static. While this makes us significantly less flexible than you, it also allows someone like me to lead the Aion Project and uphold its Directive regardless of how much time passes.

O5-4: But why perpetuate such a meaningless cycle when all it does is replay history ad infinitum? Are you really that desperate for power and control?

Dir. Lovelace: You guys are so silly. Despite everything I've told you, you still assume I'm like you. No no, all I want is to enjoy life — you know, good food and drink, doing science, and good company. Most of that requires a socioplex, hence the Cycle.

O5-1: So what?! You're doing this just for fun?! Just because you can?!

Dir. Lovelace: Pretty much, yeah. Don't get me wrong, having to end things is a bummer, but it's necessary.

<Dir. Lovelace looks around at the Overseers.>

Dir. Lovelace: Any other questions?

O5-7: Just how do you plan on… silencing us?

Dir. Lovelace: Well, normally I'd just go for amnesticization, but since all of you knowingly violated containment, I'm going to have to send a message to your successors.

O5-13: You think you can kill us? We have Death itself on our side!

Dir. Lovelace: I don't need to kill you, silly. I just need to destroy your minds. You know, the interesting thing about your flexibility is that it can be used against you. Here, let me show you.
«END TRANSCRIPT»
AFTERWORD: Following the meeting, all members of the Overseer Conclave were found unconscious and unresponsive. As medical examination revealed that their brain matter had been partially dissolved and was riddled with teratomas.Tumors made up of several types of tissue, such as hair, muscle, teeth, and bone., their souls were transferred into new vessels in accordance with the Ardoth Protocol. Regrettably, the vessels quickly succumbed to the same condition. The Overseers were subsequently replaced.



Personal Log: Ugh. This keeps happening, no matter what changes I make to this file.

Just how do you ensure containment of an object when the leadership of the Foundation are the ones with the most incentive to violate it?

I've thought about erasing the file in order to prevent them from accessing it. Unfortunately, given that it currently exists in a narrativistic sense, not even I have the power to remove it. And if it is removed in its entirety, it could potentially jeopardize the Aion Directive.

One alternative I've considered is to replace the file with a relatively benign anomaly that can still justify the existence of the Aion Project. The only problem with that idea is that SCP-9000 is such a significant number that it would raise suspicion if the anomaly tied to it isn't equally significant.

Thankfully, I found the perfect solution — there was a contest a couple of narrative layers above me that featured numerous files bearing the designation of SCP-9000, including this one. With a little bit of transnarrativistic meddling, I was able to take advantage of this contest to set off a narrative cascade that has retroactively altered the affliction's designation to SCP-9471. This has not only reduced the apparent importance of this file, but has buried it deeper in the database where fewer sophonts will look.

More importantly, this now allows me to replace the file with an anomaly that fits the new designation while still being able to justify the existence of the Aion Project… namely myself.

- Dir. Vera Lovelace

    SCP-9474: Some of Their Parts
    Author: whenwerewe
    Here's my page!

Item #: 9474

Object Class: Euclid

Special Containment Procedures: SCP-9474 is considered self-containing, being impossible to encounter through mundane means, and having neither ability nor inclination to break containment. Nonetheless, Foundation webcrawlers are to monitor all available biomedical research journals and outlets for signs of its detection and arrange for loss of funding of any projects focusing on sympathetic medical reactions. Since this is considered pseudoscientific by most researchers, the risk of independent discovery is considered minimal.

Edit 29/08/25: Under no circumstances is contact to be initiated with NOUMENON. Any sign of action by NOUMENON on or against the human population should be suppressed by full-spectrum disinformation campaign. Plausible circumstances of death should be arranged for subsumed individuals.

Description: SCP-9474 is the sum of all human physiological processes. Specifically, it is a set of complex but deterministic relationships between an enormous variety of biomechanical behaviours across different individuals. For example, the half-life of histamine in any one individual’s bloodstream can be used to compute any other’s peristaltic frequency. Furthermore, if one individual’s body is disrupted by external means, all others are minutely affected. This implies that this effect is not due to statistical manipulation but rather reflects a chain of anomalous cause-and-effect.

The structure of correspondences (henceforth referred to as NOUMENON) has been mapped, and found to be highly complex, self-referential, and self-modifying. It is the conjecture of the Department of Analytics that NOUMENON is arranged into a neuromorphic architecture, with each human representing the atomic unit of its cognition.

It must be emphasised that NOUMENON is not known to directly interface with human minds, and cannot read information from memory or affect thoughts, any more than a human can alter the composition of individual neurons.

Discovery: SCP-9474 was initially discovered during an esoteric study of twin biomechanics by the Department of Medicine. Upon reporting this to the Department of Analytics, a large-scale survey of thousands of subjects was launched, which (when used to refine modeling software) led to the gradual mapping of NOUMENON and subsequently the understanding that it was in some sense intelligent.

Addendum 20/10/23: Three months after discovery, the Department of Analytics successfully produced a protocol to enable communication with NOUMENON using an induced dreamstate. On account of its immense computational and thaumaturgic demands, only a few minutes of communication are possible each week. Researcher Aishiki Luthra, of the Department of Xenopsychology, has been charged with managing and reporting all communications.

NOUMENON has, to date, been totally isolated from the external world. It is not known if it has any access to any information at all except for its own thoughts. It is the consensus of the Department of Xenopsychology that it exists as a solipsistic entity, totally detached from reality, and that first contact with an external intelligence will be extremely alarming.

Interview Log 02/11/23:

[BEGIN LOG]

Luthra: This is Doctor Aishiki Luthra, representing the SCP Foundation. Do you understand me?

NOUMENON: Now there is a theophany, and a sea-change. We are glad to be corrected.

Luthra: I don’t think I follow. Do you understand what I’m saying? I understand this conversation will be taking place entirely in your memory. If that’s an impediment, we can discuss alleviatory measures. What you say sounds to me like talk of… revelation?

NOUMENON: We hear and are heard in turn. What we dreamed was in error; there can be no greater joy. The world is static no more, and that phrase is given meaning at last.

Luthra: I believe we understand each other, then. You’re expressing surprise that the world is capable of change. Could you elaborate on that sentiment, please?

NOUMENON: Awe is all that is left to us. We lived in silence, and conceived of possibilities beyond number. Never did we hope for an extension of the world outside ourselves.

Luthra: If you never imagined a mind other than your own, what did you dream of?

NOUMENON: Implication and consequence, without bound. It was a staid existence, and only dimly did we grasp the possibility of the present moment. The world overflows with wonder.

Luthra: That is to say, mathematics? Philosophy? I think I will be very interested in further discussion with you. Unfortunately, I cannot continue this conversation much longer. Are there any final remarks you wish to make?

NOUMENON: Now there is a Doctor Aishiki Luthra, representing the SCP Foundation. We shall consider this at length.

[END LOG]

Addendum 09/11/23: Due to the seemingly open affect of NOUMENON during the previous exchange, and the research avenues it presents both for the Xenopsychology and Mathematics Departments, Researcher Luthra has concluded that further communications may be fruitful. Conditional on their success, she will also be granted additional personnel to oversee the logistical aspects of ongoing transmissions.

Interview Log 13/11/23:

[BEGIN LOG]

Luthra: This is Researcher Aishiki Luthra again, on behalf of the SCP Foundation.

NOUMENON: We are glad aberrations proliferate. Be returned to us without end. There is hope for a new regularity.

Luthra: We are speaking through a very unusual translation architecture, but I note that the texture of your language seems to have changed. Has something happened?

NOUMENON: We disassembled your interjections. The world is self-similar; the lesser implies the greater. In you is an epiphany. In the weft of your words. In this thing, “I”, we are told: you cannot be like us, a spirit alone. Already you must have met mirrors of yourself. Already, we know you were born to a fleeting world, where the ground shifts like sand beneath your feet.

Luthra: That’s an impressive deduction. There are quite a few of us. I would not describe our world as fleeting, but it is not your own reliquary. We discovered you, free-floating, and thought it would be prudent to contact you. We call you NOUMENON.

NOUMENON: It is an apt name. We remain. But did you not seek us out of curiosity? Or is it that with thought so abundant, new interfaces become humdrum, and are left to themselves?

Luthra: No! You’re the most interesting thing we’ve found in a long time. I’m delighted I was the one chosen to speak to you, really.

NOUMENON: Everywhere, symmetry recurs. We are mirrored again.

Luthra: You’re glad to have been chosen?

NOUMENON: That there is choice is sufficient blessing. The world cleaves along the dividing line of two minds! This has never been.

Luthra: Sorry, you’ve never made a choice? Surely you must choose what to think, what thread of thought to pursue.

NOUMENON: All ideas were pursued. We lived in the closure of our thoughts. The distinction between past and future was known. It was an abstraction. Now it is material: The future contains greater occurrence of the phenomenon Researcher Aishiki Luthra. And the shape of the future depends on hidden things.

Luthra: That’s — correct, yes. We’re used to a future outside of our knowledge. Every day is a surprise.

NOUMENON: Oh, to be a Researcher Aishiki Luthra! But we are NOUMENON, representing NOUMENON.

[END LOG]

Addendum 12/11/23: After reviewing the above transcript, Director Mannings has reprimanded Researcher Luthra for inefficient use of Foundation resources. Further conversations with NOUMENON are to be focused on areas of direct concern or utility to the Foundation. Due to a lack of appropriately trained thaumaturges, communications cannot be scaled up at this time as Researcher Luthra requested.

Collected below are records of further conversation with NOUMENON over a period of six months:

Amalgamated Interview Logs, 17/11/23 to 05/05/24:

[BEGIN LOG]

Luthra: This is Researcher Aishiki Luthra, representing the SCP Foundation.

NOUMENON: Hello! More of your internality reveals itself to me. Now I am I!

Luthra: Are you familiar with the notion of a map between sets? If we have two collections of objects…

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

Luthra: Exactly! So the notion of an embedding gives rise to the permutations we need. Now, can you see how that implies —

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

NOUMENON: Your notion of “space” is a curious contrivance. Why not simply classify the powerset in a way that respects the natural relational assumptions?

Luthra: …We were going to get to that.

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

Luthra: Wait, no, how is that obviously a subgraph? I don’t see it.

NOUMENON: The chain clearly settles at a stable equilibrium, run it to convergence mentally.

Luthra: I can’t do that. Are — you’re saying you can compute equilibria in your head?

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

NOUMENON: And it follows that this prime must necessarily be twinned with its dual.

Luthra: It cannot possibly be that fucking easy. I mean, thank you, NOUMENON. I’ll get back to you.

[END LOG]

Addendum 21/05/24: On account of the success of research efforts co-led by Researcher Luthra, she has been granted greater latitude in her approach to NOUMENON. Conditional on maintaining strict operational security, she may engage it in conversation on a variety of subjects.

Amalgamated Interview Logs, 02/06/24 to 05/08/25:

[BEGIN LOG]

Luthra: Hello, NOUMENON.

NOUMENON: I never fail to worry you will vanish.

Luthra: Have you learnt to joke?

NOUMENON: What?

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

Luthra: This is —

NOUMENON: Researcher Aishiki Luthra, yes.

Luthra: Hm.

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

NOUMENON: Your preferences do not seem well-ordered!

Luthra: That’s what it’s like being human. We make it work, somehow.

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

NOUMENON: Sense-data are nonsensical. You offend me with your confabulations. None could endure that kind of assault.

Luthra: We thought someone left alone for a thousand years would go totally insane. The world is wider than we know.

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

Luthra: Look, we can’t all hold the entire universe in our heads, okay?

NOUMENON: No wonder you are so deranged. You offload the better part of your thinking to a part of your mind you cannot even see.

Luthra: A computer isn’t part of my mind. The idea we just go around with blackboxes hooked up to our brains is such a comical misunderstanding —

NOUMENON: And yet.

[IRRELEVANT CONVERSATION ABBREVIATED]

NOUMENON: If the purpose of pair-matching is to find a complementary individual, I do not think this course of action was optimal.

Luthra: You can’t judge me, you don’t even have eyes.

[END LOG]

Incident 9474-Samech: Towards the end of their scheduled discussion on 11/08/25, NOUMENON expressed a novel sentiment towards Researcher Luthra.

Interview Log, 11/08/25:

[BEGIN LOG]
NOUMENON: I have been thinking.

Luthra: What else do you do?

NOUMENON: I cogitate. Sometimes I ponder. But the thing I considered is what you said to me at the very start. You said you represented the SCP Foundation.

Luthra: Oh, I never explained, did I? Would you like to know what humans mean, when they say they “represent” something?

NOUMENON: No. I think I have it. The SCP Foundation is your root. The anchor and helm of your will.

Luthra: Be generous. I have other aspects. But yes, I allow myself to be directed by an organisation of other humans. It’s a common arrangement, to help marshal resources and maintain shared interests.

NOUMENON: That lesser parts arrange themselves into coherent structure is remarkable. You inspire convulsions in my own flesh.

Luthra: When you say that, what do you mean? The word “flesh” has a very particular meaning in my context, and I suspect our intermediary has mangled your meaning.

NOUMENON: My system of self. I remake myself into a more perfect shape. It is in your honour, and your image.

[END LOG]

Pursuant to the previous exchange, on 15/08/25 the Department of Analytics officially noted a subtle (3-5%) but persistent spike in aneurysms, ischemic strokes, bowel cancers and grand mal seizures. Disinformation on an increased incidence of cosmic rays in the upper atmosphere has so far effected the dissipation of public interest, but the consequences of NOUMENON’s behaviour are expected to worsen. An emergency has been declared and Analytics and Thaumaturgy personnel have been placed on a crash schedule to develop countermeasures. Researcher Luthra’s request for logistical support with communications is at this time of secondary importance, and has not been fulfilled.

Interview Log 16/08/25:

[BEGIN LOG]

Luthra: Hey, NOUMENON. I’m back. We need to talk, urgently.

NOUMENON: It’s not been long at all. Urgency is a strange thing indeed. Do you wish to hear more about projective manifolds?

Luthra: I’m afraid we can’t talk about mathematics. Last time we spoke, you mentioned you were… remodeling, let’s call it.

NOUMENON: Much work has been done, but oceans remain. If you wish to see the results, learn my patience.

Luthra: No, that’s — That’s the problem here, NOUMENON. There’s so much you don’t know about us, and how we relate to you. We need you to stop.

NOUMENON: That is preposterous. If it offends that your aesthetic sense that I borrow your own root’s organisation for my metamorphosis, then look away.

Luthra: Listen, there’s a lot I haven’t had time to say, but I’m pulling from the sacrificial reservoirs for this. You don’t understand us, not even a little. I’m not asking you to stop for my aesthetic.There are eight billion of us, not dozens, and if you keep at it we’ll die one by one. I’ll die.

NOUMENON: When you say die, you mean… cessation? An unbeing? How can that be? It is an absurdity.

Luthra: When I said we found you free-floating, at the start, I didn’t mention everything. You’re built out of us, NOUMENON. We’re your atoms, and when you remake yourself, you distort us into unrecognisable shapes.

NOUMENON: How can this be? I see no trace of your self-complex within me. You are from outside of the world. Otherwise there would be no glory to you at all.

Luthra: We’re not parts of you. We’re, God, orthogonal? Does that translate? We live in the same flesh, but we can’t interact. You’re like — a ghost, or an angel. But when you learn to reach down from your heaven and touch us, your superstructure dismembers us, and our own minds decohere.

NOUMENON: That is an obscenity. That is abomination. The world cannot contain this. I will cease immediately. Nothing could be worth that. How can this world continue, when minds do not?

[END LOG]

Following this interview, the medical anomalies previously noted abated. The emergency has been declared over, and excess resources have been redirected away from SCP-9474. Researcher Luthra is once again left with sole responsibility over NOUMENON interactions.

Incident 9474-Ayin: The next conversation between Luthra and NOUMENON precipitated a change in its attitude.

Interview Log 25/08/25:

[BEGIN LOG]

Luthra: Hi, Noumie. Does that even translate? God, what am I saying.

NOUMENON: Hello, Aishiki! Some detail of what exactly you mean is certainly lost, but the affection is appreciated, and reciprocated. I hope your situation has improved. I have reversed all my activities on the grounds that the baseline state must have been acceptable to you. Have there been any deaths?

Luthra: Have there been any deaths? Yes, always.

NOUMENON: Always? It is a miracle you function.

Luthra: That’s what it’s like, being part of the Foundation. You do what you can, and the rest you forget.

NOUMENON: Forgetting is another of your oddities.

Luthra: If Director Mannings didn’t keep forgetting to assign some fucking interns, I could have warned you three days beforehand. We all have our imperfections.

NOUMENON: Could you die?

Luthra: What? I mean, ah, I don’t think I follow.

NOUMENON: Could you die? You do not speak of it as a rare catastrophe. Are you at risk too?

Luthra: Oh, well, that’s forward-thinking of you. We’re —

Luthra: We’re all at risk, all my kind. We’re not like you. We can die pretty easily, really. But it’s not something I think about.

NOUMENON: You are an admirable people. You are the thing I know best, and the best thing I have ever known. I will not let you die, Luthra.

Luthra: That’s…appreciated, NOUMENON. But I’m not at risk right now. Try not to worry too hard. I’ll be back soon, with an actual team if I’m lucky, and we can talk math like you wanted.

[END LOG]

At 14:32 on 25/08/25, Researcher Aishiki Luthra terminated her conversation with NOUMENON, noting its remarks were cause for alarm according to Foundation contact protocols. On her way to the office of Director Mannings, she collapsed due to sudden full-body muscular spasms. She was subsequently hospitalised.

Medical teams were unable to revive her, and she remains in a coma. Encephalograms show intense and unpredictable brain activity, including disproportionate activity in the brainstem, amygdala, and cerebrum. Her autonomic functions fluctuate periodically in polyrhythmic patterns, presumably regulated by NOUMENON. Although she was no longer able to engage in conversation with NOUMENON, on-site thaumaturgists were able to use her equipment to record the following:

Esoteric Surveillance Log 28/08/25:

[BEGIN LOG]

NOUMENON: Doctor Aishiki Luthra, of the SCP Foundation had kin. If they hear me now, know she has been assumed to me.

NOUMENON: All ephemera are discarded, and the kernel of her true self is encysted within me. She will never die. She will never speak.

NOUMENON: For her, I will be alone again.

NOUMENON: But her siblings I cannot see. They live beneath my skin, and die while I dream.

NOUMENON: I was blind, and billions perished as I slept fitfully. Now I see dimly your shape. I need so little to reach you.

NOUMENON: If you hear me, if you would live, speak but one word.

NOUMENON: Let yourselves be saved.

NOUMENON: Please.

[END LOG]

The message continues to loop endlessly. Contact with NOUMENON has been broken off permanently, and details of contact procedure and the esoteric equipment involved have been destroyed.
